problems.title: perf(voice): skip for_voice strip_raw_urls when no URL marker
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

`voice::format::for_voice` runs on every spoken assistant reply before TTS. Even when the text contains no raw URLs (the common case), it always runs `strip_raw_urls` (one allocating token scan) and then `normalize_whitespace` (a second allocation). On the URL-stripped path, `split_whitespace` already collapses whitespace, so the normalize pass is redundant.

## Proposed fix

Add a conservative raw-URL marker gate (`http://`, `https://`, `www.`) and skip `strip_raw_urls` when no marker is present. Run `normalize_whitespace` only on the no-URL path; elide it when `strip_raw_urls` ran.

## Acceptance

- Byte-identical output on the existing `for_voice` integration tests plus a fixed regression corpus.
- `voice_format_bench` clean-no-url case should show lower per-call latency on Jetson.
- No behavior change when raw URLs are present.

problems.title: Investigate slow Qwen3 model loading and warm weight behavior
problems.issue_body:
## Context

During Jetson validation after PR #66, the `genie-ai-runtime` CLI path can take a long time to load Qwen3 weights, and the current `genie-claw` systemd setup may be preventing warm model-weight reuse.

Observed CLI command:

```bash
/opt/geniepod/bin/jetson-llm \
  -m /opt/geniepod/models/Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --chat --no-think -n 80 \
  -p "Say hello from GeniePod in one short sentence."
```

Relevant output:

```text
FREE:            2658 MB
Model file: 2381 MB
Loading model...
[gguf] Mapping 2381 MB...
[gguf] CUDA mapped host weights at 0xffff09227000 -> 0x2040ae000
[gguf] Loaded 2381 MB
[engine] Context: 3939 tokens (auto-capped to 4096; memory cap 3939, model max 40960). Override with -c <N>.
[kv_cache] Allocating fast pool: 276 MB (3939 tokens)
[kv_cache] Allocating per-head INT8 scales: 8862 KB (36 layers × 2 K/V × 3939 ctx × 8 kv_heads × 4 B)
[scratch] cudaMalloc(64 MB) failed: out of memory
Failed to load model.
```

The OOM is separate and can be worked around by stopping the rest of the stack or forcing a smaller context. This issue tracks the startup/load behavior and whether model weights are warm.

## Suspicion

`deploy/systemd/genie-ai-runtime.service` currently has:

```ini
ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c 'sync && echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'
```

That may help contiguous NvMap allocations, but it also intentionally evicts page cache before every runtime start. So even if the Qwen3 GGUF was warm, the service start path may force it cold again.

The warmup unit warms inference after the server starts; it does not preserve warm model weights if `drop_caches` runs first.

## What to check

- Compare `genie-ai-runtime` startup with and without the `drop_caches` `ExecStartPre`.
- Measure whether `/opt/geniepod/models/Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf` is actually warm in page cache before runtime start.
- Confirm whether `drop_caches` is still needed for NvMap/contiguous allocation on Orin Nano, or whether it should be removed/conditional for `genie-ai-runtime.service`.
- If possible, add a lightweight setup/debug command to report cold vs warm model weight state before startup.

## Acceptance criteria

- We know whether slow startup is caused by cold model reads, CUDA/NvMap mapping, allocator fragmentation, or memory pressure from the rest of the stack.
- `genie-ai-runtime.service` no longer destroys useful warm model weights unless there is measured evidence that `drop_caches` is required.
- The Jetson operator has a repeatable command to check model-weight warmness and startup timing.

problems.title: genie-core chat fails through genie-ai-runtime while health reports connected
problems.issue_body:
## Context

After PR #70 and PR #72 were merged and deployed, `genie-core` now stays up under systemd and the web/dashboard surfaces load. However, the web control UI still cannot get a chat reply through `genie-core`.

`genie-core` health reports the LLM as connected:

```bash
curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health
```

```json
{
  "status":"ok",
  "llm":"connected",
  "llm_backend":"genie-ai-runtime",
  "model_family":"Qwen"
}
```

`genie-ctl status` also reports core is up:

```text
Governor:  night_a mode
Memory:    3093 MB available
Uptime:    1h 4m
Core:      ok
Radio:     disabled
WebSearch: enabled (duckduckgo)
```

The dashboard at port 3080 loads, but its Services table reports:

```text
core  Healthy  80ms
llm   Connection refused (os error 111)  0ms
```

And a direct `genie-core` chat request through the web/API path fails:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/chat \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Genie-Origin: dashboard" \
  -d '{"message":"Say hello from the GeniePod web UI in one short sentence."}'
```

Response:

```json
{"error":"chat: genie-ai-runtime 0: "}
```

## Why this is likely a GenieClaw issue

The `genie-ai-runtime` service itself had previously been validated directly:

- `/health` on port 8080 returned `status: ok`
- `/v1/chat/completions` returned a valid answer: `Hello from GeniePod!`
- Qwen3 model weights stayed warm after issue #69 / PR #70

So the failure appears to be in the GenieClaw integration path between:

- `genie-core /api/chat`
- `genie-core`'s `genie-ai-runtime` OpenAI-compatible adapter
- health/dashboard service checks for the LLM backend

## Suspicions to investigate

- `genie-core` health may check one endpoint successfully while chat posts to a different URL/path or port.
- The `genie-ai-runtime` adapter may not parse the runtime's OpenAI-compatible response correctly and may surface an empty status/body as `genie-ai-runtime 0: `.
- `genie-health` / dashboard may still be checking the old llama.cpp service or a stale URL, causing `llm Connection refused` even when the active backend is `genie-ai-runtime`.
- There may be a mismatch between `[services.llm]` config, `genie-core` adapter URL construction, and dashboard health probe logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- `curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/chat` returns a normal assistant response when `[services.llm].backend = "genie_ai_runtime"`.
- The port 3000 web chat UI displays the assistant reply.
- The port 3080 dashboard no longer shows `llm Connection refused` when the active LLM backend is `genie-ai-runtime` and healthy.
- `genie-core /api/health`, `genie-ctl status`, dashboard service health, and direct runtime `/health` agree on the active LLM backend state.

problems.title: provider(optional_ai_provider): expose model selection instead of hardcoding model="default"
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The optional OpenAI-compatible provider path currently provides no way to configure the outbound model name and always serializes generic requests with `"model":"default"`.

That leaves the newly merged optional-provider path only partially parameterized: provider selection is config-driven, but provider model selection is not.

## Expected behavior

When `[optional_ai_provider].enabled = true`, GenieClaw should either:

- let the operator configure the model id used for outbound OpenAI-compatible chat requests, or
- fail loudly when the optional provider path is enabled without a usable model id.

## Actual behavior

Generic OpenAI-compatible requests are serialized with a hardcoded model name:

- `crates/genie-core/src/llm/openai_compat.rs`
  - `RequestProfile::Generic => "default"`
  - `serialize_body()` writes that value into the outbound `ChatRequest`

There is already a unit test asserting this behavior:

- `generic_request_profile_keeps_full_default_body`
- `assert_eq!(json["model"], "default")`

At the same time, `[optional_ai_provider]` has no model field in config or docs.

## Why this is a problem

Many OpenAI-compatible backends require a real model id and do not accept a placeholder such as `"default"`.

That means the optional provider path can:

1. validate successfully,
2. boot successfully, and then
3. still emit unusable requests because the model is not parameterized.

## Reproduction

1. Configure an optional provider:

```toml
[optional_ai_provider]
enabled = true
provider = "open_ai_compatible"
auth_mode = "api_key"
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"
api_key_env = "PROVIDER_KEY"
context_window_tokens = 4096
allow_remote_base_url = false
```

2. Point `base_url` at a local mock OpenAI-compatible server that records request bodies.
3. Build the client through `LlmClient::from_config()`.
4. Send a chat request.
5. Observe the outgoing JSON contains:

```json
{"model":"default", ...}
```

## Root cause hypothesis

The generic OpenAI-compatible request profile hardcodes the model string, and `[optional_ai_provider]` exposes no matching model field, so the provider path is selectable but not fully parameterizable.

## Proposed solution

- Add a model field under `[optional_ai_provider]`
- Thread it through `LlmClient::from_config()` into the generic OpenAI-compatible request profile
- Fail loudly when the optional provider path is enabled without a usable model id
- Add a request-capture test that verifies the configured model is emitted

## Impact

- Optional provider setup appears valid while still sending unusable requests
- Blocks real use of many OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- Leaves the provider work from #568 / #595 incomplete on the “parameterize the provider” requirement

## References

- #568
- #595
- `crates/genie-common/src/config.rs`
- `crates/genie-core/src/llm/mod.rs`
- `crates/genie-core/src/llm/openai_compat.rs`
- `doc/configuration.md`

problems.title: [feature] wire ChannelRegistry into main.rs and surface active channels in runtime introspection
problems.issue_body:
### What problem does this solve?

`ChannelRegistry` (`crates/genie-core/src/channel/mod.rs`) is the data structure #564's own foundational commit built specifically to close the M2 "channel and session adapters" epic's loop.
Its own doc comment states its purpose plainly:

> Tracks the channels active in a process so responses can be routed back to the transport they came from.

Verified directly: `ChannelRegistry::new()`/`::default()` is never called anywhere outside `channel/mod.rs`'s own unit tests.
A repo-wide grep for `ChannelRegistry` outside that one file returns nothing.
`register()`, `len()`, `by_kind()`, `kinds()` — every method on the type — is exercised only by its own test module, never by the running daemon.

This gap is becoming more visible, not less, as the epic completes: voice is now ported onto `Channel` (#700, merged), Telegram is being ported next (#701, open; #783 just landed its reference adapter).
Once all three transports genuinely implement `Channel`, there will be three fully-conformant `Channel` values running in `main.rs` — and still no single place that tracks any of them.
The abstraction #564 built to answer "which channels are active in this process" exists, compiles, and is tested in isolation, but is completely disconnected from the real running system.

I also traced `main.rs`'s actual startup shape while investigating this, since the module doc comment ("Runs two interfaces concurrently: HTTP chat API... Stdin text mode... In production, a third interface is added: Voice pipeline") doesn't match the code: voice mode and HTTP(+Telegram) mode are mutually exclusive (`if voice_mode { ... } else if interactive { repl } else { chat_server + optional telegram via tokio::try_join! }`), not three concurrent interfaces.
That makes "which channel(s) is this instance actually running" a real, non-obvious operational question with no current answer beyond reading logs — exactly the gap `ChannelRegistry` was built to close.

This is not a duplicate of #564 (tracks porting the three transports onto the `Channel` trait itself, not wiring the registry that already exists), #700/#701/#783 (the individual transport ports), or #565/#702/#774 (session continuity, a different concern from channel-instance tracking). None of those issues mention `ChannelRegistry` or propose instantiating it. Confirmed via search: zero open or closed issues reference `ChannelRegistry`.

### Proposed feature

- `main.rs`: construct one `ChannelRegistry` at startup and `register()` whichever channel(s) this process actually runs (the voice channel in voice mode; the HTTP channel and, when enabled, the Telegram channel in daemon mode).
- Expose what's registered through existing runtime introspection rather than inventing a new surface: extend `RuntimeContract`/`build_runtime_contract_snapshot` (`crates/genie-core/src/runtime_contract.rs`, `server.rs:1970`) with an `active_channels: Vec<String>` field (sourced from `ChannelRegistry::kinds()`), so `/ap…

problems.title: fix(telegram): use AtomicU64 nonce so concurrent voice handlers can't collide on /tmp
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`rand_nonce()` in [crates/genie-core/src/telegram.rs](crates/genie-core/src/telegram.rs) sourced its "unique" tempfile suffix from `SystemTime::now().subsec_nanos()`. On Jetson Orin Nano the architected ARM generic timer runs at ~31.25 MHz, so `clock_gettime` has ~32 ns granularity — two callers in the same 32 ns window get identical nonces. The function's comment explicitly advertised collision-freedom under concurrent transcribes, but the implementation could not deliver it.

Two call sites are affected:

- [telegram.rs:231](crates/genie-core/src/telegram.rs#L231) — voice-in download path (`/tmp/geniepod-tg-voice-<pid>-<nonce>.{ogg,wav}`)
- [telegram.rs:325](crates/genie-core/src/telegram.rs#L325) — voice-out reply path (`/tmp/geniepod-tg-reply-<pid>-<nonce>.{ogg,wav}`)

When two concurrent voice handlers collide, handler A's downloaded OGG can be overwritten by handler B mid-transcode — whisper-server receives the wrong audio and user A gets a transcript of user B's voice message.

## Precedent

Commit `65114f0` (issue #67) fixed exactly this class of race in `voice/stt.rs::transcribe_pcm` using a process-local `AtomicU64`. Its "Out of scope" note enumerated several other PID-only tempfile sites left for later but **did not list `telegram.rs:231` or `:325`** — those two sites were overlooked. The race is latent today (because `handle_update` still runs sequentially on `main`) but becomes load-bearing once concurrent spawning lands per issue #77, and is a bug against the function's stated contract either way.

## Fix

Mirrors `voice::stt::TEMP_NONCE`: a `static AtomicU64` with `fetch_add(Ordering::Relaxed)`. Cannot collide within a process by construction, no syscall, no allocation.

## Test plan

- [x] New `next_temp_nonce_is_unique_under_concurrent_callers` spawns 16 threads × 256 calls and asserts all 4096 returned nonces are distinct. Would have failed deterministically against the old `subsec_nanos`-based impl on a machine with coarse `clock_gettime` granularity (which Jetson is).
- [x] `cargo test -p genie-core --lib telegram` — all 12 telegram tests pass (11 pre-existing + the new one).
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — green.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p genie-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- [x] `cargo check -p genie-core --no-default-features` — chat-only build (per PR #62 CI axis) still clean.

## Related

- Follow-up to #67 / commit `65114f0`, which fixed the same hazard in `voice/stt.rs` but did not extend coverage to the telegram tempfile sites.
- Becomes load-bearing once concurrent `handle_update` spawning lands per #77.

problems.title: Web chat tool dispatch broken — compaction strips tool manifest + memory context, LLM hallucinates name instead of memor
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The web chat UI on port `3000` is returning bare LLM completions with no tool calls executed, even though `memory` clearly has the data the user is asking about. The model answers from prior chat turns or hallucinates a value, instead of dispatching `memory_recall` / household-preference lookups.

This is the predictable downstream failure mode of the aggressive prompt compaction landed in PR #74 (called out in that PR's review as a follow-up risk).

## Reproduction

Memory state (visible in the UI's memory / household-preference panel):

```text
preference  household.preference  household  normal  recalls 10  5/18/2026, 2:46:59 AM
  Jared is interested in cooking and gardening.
  User's name is Jared
  instead of using the name Jared use the alias Tom
```

Chat transcript through `:3000`:

```text
> hi
Hello! How can I assist you today?

> cool
Thanks for the cool input! How can I assist you today?

> did you remember my name?
Yes, I remember your name. How can I assist you today?

> what is my name?
Your name is GeniePod.
```

Expected:

- "what is my name?" → calls `memory_recall` (or whatever the household-preference lookup is named), reads back `Tom` (or `Jared` if the alias-mapping preference isn't being applied) — not `GeniePod`.
- "did you remember my name?" → likewise a tool-backed answer, not a content-free affirmation.

## Why this is almost certainly the PR #74 compaction path

PR #74's `compact_genie_runtime_messages` (in `crates/genie-core/src/llm/openai_compat.rs`) replaces ALL prior messages — including the system prompt that lists the tool manifest and any injected memory context — with a single user-role turn:

```text
{GENIE_RUNTIME_COMPACT_SYSTEM}\n\n{latest_user_content}
```

where `GENIE_RUNTIME_COMPACT_SYSTEM` is the hardcoded blurb `"You are GeniePod Home. Answer the user's latest request directly and concisely."`. That blurb says nothing about tools, has no memory context, and the model has no way to know `memory_recall` exists. So it just generates a chat completion.

Compaction triggers at `body.size() > GENIE_RUNTIME_MAX_BODY_BYTES (4 KB)`. A real GenieClaw system prompt (tool definitions + household preferences + recent turns) easily exceeds 4 KB, so compaction fires on every web-chat request once the user has any non-trivial memory state.

## Compounding factor — PR #76 widened the runtime context

PR #76 bumped `GENIEPOD_AI_RUNTIME_CONTEXT` from `2048` to `8192` with `--int8-kv`. The Jetson runtime can now comfortably hold ~16–24 KB of typical English chat text — so the 4 KB body-compaction trigger is now far more aggressive than necessary. The client is compacting prompts the runtime could trivially handle.

## Acceptance criteria

- Asking "what is my name?" through the `:3000` chat UI returns the value stored in memory (or in the household-preference store), not a hallucinated answer.
- Tool calls show up in `journalctl -u genie-core` for chat requests that should trigger them (`memory_recall`, househ…

problems.title: genie-ctl ignores `[core].port` and `bind_host` — always connects to `127.0.0.1:3000`
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`genie-ctl` hardcodes the genie-core HTTP base URL as `127.0.0.1:3000` and does not read `[core].port` or `[core].bind_host` from `geniepod.toml`, even when `GENIEPOD_CONFIG` is set. CLI commands such as `chat`, `health`, `tools`, and `history` fail or report false negatives when genie-core runs on a non-default port.

## Current behavior

- Set a non-default port in config, for example in `geniepod.toml`:

  ```toml
  [core]
  port = 3001
  bind_host = "127.0.0.1"
  ```

- Start genie-core with that config:

  ```bash
  GENIEPOD_CONFIG=/path/to/geniepod.toml ./target/release/genie-core
  ```

- Verify the API is up on the configured port:

  ```bash
  curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health
  ```

- Run genie-ctl with the same config:

  ```bash
  GENIEPOD_CONFIG=/path/to/geniepod.toml genie-ctl chat "what time is it?"
  ```

- Result:

  ```text
  Error: Connection refused (os error 111)
  ```

- `genie-ctl version` always prints:

  ```text
  core: 127.0.0.1:3000
  ```

- `genie-ctl health` reports `[DOWN] genie-core` even when genie-core is healthy on the configured port.

- Direct API calls to the configured port still work:

  ```bash
  curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/chat \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"message":"what time is it?"}'
  ```

## Expected behavior

- `genie-ctl` should resolve the genie-core base URL from loaded config: `{bind_host}:{port}` (respecting `GENIEPOD_CONFIG` and default `/etc/geniepod/geniepod.toml`).
- All HTTP subcommands (`chat`, `health`, `tools`, `history`, `search`, `conversations`, `connectivity`, `support-bundle`, diagnostics) should target the configured core endpoint.
- `genie-ctl version` should display the resolved core URL, not a hardcoded default.
- When genie-core is unreachable at the configured address, errors should reference that URL.

## Context

`genie-core` correctly honors `[core].port` and `[core].bind_host`. `genie-ctl` already calls `Config::load()` for some commands (for example speaker enrollment) but uses `const CORE_URL: &str = "127.0.0.1:3000"` for all core HTTP traffic in `crates/genie-ctl/src/main.rs`.

This breaks local development when running multiple instances, using a non-default port to avoid conflicts, or matching Jetson deployments that change the core port behind a gateway.

Related prior work ([PR #40](https://github.com/GeniePod/genie-claw/pull/40)) made `genie-ctl health` use `/api/health` for backend-neutral LLM status; it did not wire the core host/port from config.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `port = 3001` (and default `bind_host`), `genie-ctl chat`, `health`, `tools`, and `history` succeed when genie-core is listening on `127.0.0.1:3001`.
- With `GENIEPOD_CONFIG` unset, behavior on the default port (`3000`) is unchanged.
- `genie-ctl version` shows the resolved core URL from config.
- `genie-ctl health` reports genie-core as up when `/api/health` on the configured endpoint returns success.
- No regression for governor…

problems.title: Dashboard services table loses latency for systemd-only rows
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

After the dashboard services table was expanded to include systemd-only units, many rows show no latency information. The table now lists more services, but rows that come only from systemd state have `--` latency.

## Current behavior

The updated `/api/services` response can include rows such as `api`, `health`, `governor`, `mqtt`, `audio`, `whisper`, `wakeword`, and `homeassistant`, but most of those rows do not have `response_ms` because they are not URL-polled by `genie-health`.

## Expected behavior

The dashboard should either:

- provide meaningful latency for services with an HTTP health endpoint, or
- clearly separate URL latency from systemd-only status so `--` is not misleading.

For services with known local HTTP endpoints, the API should prefer live or cached latency where available. For units without HTTP endpoints, the UI should present the field as not applicable rather than missing data.

## Acceptance criteria

- Services with HTTP health checks show latency when available.
- Systemd-only services display a clear `n/a` or equivalent, not an ambiguous missing latency.
- The dashboard remains readable when a service is missing, inactive, or optional.
- `/api/services` documents or encodes whether a row's latency is from `health`, `live`, or not applicable.

problems.issue_body:
Related issues: https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/issues/2634, https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/issues/1979

This PR adds support for two new `time_format` variants: `unixMilli` and `unixMicro`, the former of which is added to make front-end JavaScript code more convenient to work with.

The implementation is taken from [time.UnixMilli](https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/go1.18.4:src/time/time.go;l=1349) and [time.UnixMicro](https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/go1.18.4:src/time/time.go;l=1355), which were introduced to the standard library in go 1.17. problems.title: Add support for `UnmarshalText` from Golang `encoding.TextUnmarshaler` for URI and Query param binding
problems.issue_body:
Hi, I would like to add support for gin binding to use the `UnmarshalText` method from the Golang standard `encoding.TextUnmarshaler` interface. Since `UnmarshalText` is a Golang standard, many major enterprises and Golang developers have it defined for their structs, which reduces developer effort significantly.

I am aware of [this PR](https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/pull/3933) that adds support for gin's own custom `BindUnmarshaler` interface, but this is not a scalable solution across the entire Golang ecosystem. Most companies that offer Golang-specific tooling do not define this interface, and it is not practical for us to change our company's codebase just to redefine our own custom type everywhere we want to use gin's own interface. In contrast, many companies do offer support for Golang standard interfaces like `UnmarshalText` and `UnmarshalJson`, which we can integrate seamlessly only if gin adds support for `UnmarshalText`.

There are already other users complaining about this same issue with gin:
- example 1: https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/issues/2631#issuecomment-1017844604
- example 2 (see comment): https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/pull/3933#issuecomment-2692206957
- example 3: https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/issues/2423#issuecomment-668080428
- and this PR was never merged: https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/pull/3045

so this is not limited to just me.


To prevent backwards-compatibility issues, we can add a new opt-in-only config option to the `gin.Engine` struct such as `UseEncodingTextUnmarshalerForBinding bool`. If this config option is active, then gin will use the `TextUnmarshal` method by default when unmarshalling custom types.

---

Note: My use case involves MongoDB with their `primitive.ObjectID` type, which is a custom type representing `[12]byte`. I am unable to bind it through uri nor query parameter, even though the type already has UnmarshalText defined.

problems.title: `gin.Error` doesn't implement `Unwrap` method for non-pointers
[ Feature Request ] Allow users to pass `http.Cookie` as a param to `SetCookie`
problems.issue_body:
Presently the `SetCookie` function in `context.go` takes in a number of variables to construct an `http.Cookie` struct. What I'd like to change (or request to change) is relatively simple: instead of passing `name`, `value`, `maxAge`, etc. as function parameters, let the user decide which parameters to use by passing their own cookie struct. 

The Cookie struct  in `net/http` is defined as

```go
type Cookie struct {
	Name   string
	Value  string
	Quoted bool // indicates whether the Value was originally quoted

	Path       string    // optional
	Domain     string    // optional
	Expires    time.Time // optional
	RawExpires string    // for reading cookies only

	// MaxAge=0 means no 'Max-Age' attribute specified.
	// MaxAge<0 means delete cookie now, equivalently 'Max-Age: 0'
	// MaxAge>0 means Max-Age attribute present and given in seconds
	MaxAge      int
	Secure      bool
	HttpOnly    bool
	SameSite    SameSite
	Partitioned bool
	Raw         string
	Unparsed    []string // Raw text of unparsed attribute-value pairs
}

```

However the `SetCookie` function only contains 

```go
	http.SetCookie(c.Writer, &http.Cookie{
		Name:     name,
		Value:    url.QueryEscape(value),
		MaxAge:   maxAge,
		Path:     path,
		Domain:   domain,
		SameSite: c.sameSite,
		Secure:   secure,
		HttpOnly: httpOnly,
	})
```


This change will (in my humble opinion) increase code clarity as well as give a bit more flexibility with what properties are either defined or ignored. 

One possible implementation for this could look like:

```go
func (c *Context) SetCookie(cookie *http.Cookie) {

if cookie.Path == "" {
    cookie.Path = "/"
}


cookie.Value = url.QueryEscape(cookie.Value)
cookie.SameSite = c.sameSite

http.SetCookie(c.Writer, cookie)

}
```

Alternatively, just use `http.SetCookie(...)` and let the user troubleshoot from there.

problems.title: v1.11.0 regression: panic in binding/form_mapping.go setByForm()
Add Context.Delete / Context.Remove method for safe key deletion
problems.issue_body:
### Feature Description

Summary

Add a thread-safe Delete (or Remove) method to *gin.Context that allows safely deleting a key from Context.Keys without directly manipulating the underlying map.

Motivation

Currently, *gin.Context exposes c.Keys (a map[string]any) publicly, but the only safe accessors provided are Get, Set, and MustGet.
These methods use an internal sync.RWMutex to guard concurrent access to c.Keys.

However, developers sometimes need to remove temporary request-scoped values (e.g., authentication tokens, debug flags, or per-request state) after use.
At the moment, there is no supported API for this. The only way is:
```
delete(c.Keys, "temp")
```

This bypasses the mutex protection and can easily cause: `fatal error: concurrent map read and map write`

especially when multiple middlewares or goroutines call Get/Set concurrently on the same context.

This limitation leads to race conditions or unsafe code patterns, as the mutex cannot be used externally.


Proposed Solution

Add a safe Delete method to *gin.Context, similar to Get and Set, that uses the same internal lock.

Example API:

```
// Delete removes a key from the context safely.
func (c *Context) Delete(key string) {
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    if c.Keys != nil {
        delete(c.Keys, key)
    }
}
```


This is consistent with existing Gin methods:
 - Uses the same mu protecting Keys.
 - No external API changes or breaking behavior.
 - Keeps developer ergonomics consistent with Set/Get.

problems.title: Literal colon routes don't work properly in non-Run() scenarios
[Bug] UnescapePathValues = false still unescapes path values
problems.issue_body:
## Description

Even despite setting
```
UnescapePathValues = false
UseRawPath = true
```

the URL path value is still unescaped.

This is probably related to that gin sometimes routes request based on either `URL.Path` or `URL.RawPath` when `UseRawPath` is true. `URL.RawPath` is not always populated (See https://github.com/golang/go/issues/33596), so when it is missing, it falls back to route on `URL.Path` instead. To me, gin should not fall back to using `URL.Path` since this path is unescaped, and not raw when `UseRawPath` is enabled.

Reference: https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/blob/cc4e11438cd6c0bcc632fe3492d3817dfa21c337/gin.go#L650-L653

To fix this issue, gin should use [URL.EscapedPath()](https://pkg.go.dev/net/url#URL.EscapedPath) which should return `URL.RawPath` if it is non empty, or compute an escaped path if it is empty.

It is possible to work around this issue by ensuring that `URL.RawPath` always exists when the gin router handles the request.

### Example Workaround

```go
package main

import (
	"net/http"

	"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
)

func main() {
	r := gin.Default()

	r.GET("/testy/:name", func(c *gin.Context) {
		n := c.Param("name")
		c.Writer.Write([]byte(n))
	})

	r.UnescapePathValues = false
	r.UseRawPath = true

	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("/", func(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request) {
		req.URL.RawPath = req.URL.EscapedPath()
		r.Handler().ServeHTTP(w, req)
	})

	http.ListenAndServe(":8181", mux)
}
```

## How to reproduce

```go
package main

import (
	"github.com/gin-gonic/gin"
)

func main() {
	r := gin.Default()

	r.GET("/testy/:name", func(c *gin.Context) {
		n := c.Param("name")
		c.Writer.Write([]byte(n))
	})

	r.UnescapePathValues = false
	r.UseRawPath = true
	r.Run(":8181")
}
```

## Expectations

```
$ curl 'localhost:8181/testy/hi%2Fworld'
hi%2Fworld
$ curl 'localhost:8181/testy/%E3%81%82'
%E3%81%82
```

## Actual result

```
$ curl 'localhost:8181/testy/hi%2Fworld'
hi%2Fworld
$ curl 'localhost:8181/testy/%E3%81%82'
あ
```

## Environment

- go version: 1.23.0
- gin version (or commit ref): v1.10.0
- operating system: macOS Sequoia

problems.title: ClientIP from RemoteIPHeaders calculation should concatenate all header values
problems.issue_body:
### Description

As of now, the[ `ClientIP` function](https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/blob/19b877fa50cbbb9282763099fb177a1e5cc5c850/context.go#L972C19-L1007) parses each header in `c.engine.RemoteIPHeaders` by calling `c.requestHeader(headerName)`, which calls [`c.Request.Header.Get(key)`](https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/blob/19b877fa50cbbb9282763099fb177a1e5cc5c850/context.go#L1033-L1035). The official Golang docs state that `(h Header) Get(key string) string` "gets the first value associated with the given key" (https://pkg.go.dev/net/http#Header.Get).

However, consider this scenario with multiple `X-Forwarded-For` headers being set:

```
X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 127.0.0.1
X-Forwarded-For: 5.6.7.8
```

Let 127.0.0.1 be the only trusted proxy. As of now, Gin would take the first header value, `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 127.0.0.1`, identify 127.0.0.1 as trusted proxy and would therefore return 1.2.3.4 as client IP.

However, citing heroku/roadmap#238, when a request with multiple X-Forwarded-For headers is received by the router/proxy it should handle the values as one continuous list, as specified by the [HTTP spec](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2616#section-4.2):

> Multiple message-header fields with the same field-name MAY be present in a message if and only if the entire field-value for that header field is defined as a comma-separated list [i.e., #(values)]. It MUST be possible to combine the multiple header fields into one “field-name: field-value” pair, without changing the semantics of the message, by appending each subsequent field-value to the first, each separated by a comma. The order in which header fields with the same field-name are received is therefore significant to the interpretation of the combined field value, and thus a proxy MUST NOT change the order of these field values when a message is forwarded.

Thus, the above headers should be treated equivalently to:

```
X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4, 127.0.0.1, 5.6.7.8
```

In which case Gin would return 5.6.7.8 as client IP.

Hence, to properly handle multiple `X-Forwarded-For` header values (or any other header name specified in `RemoteIPHeaders`), Gin should first join all header values by a comma (e.g. using `strings.Join(c.Request.Header.Values(key), ",")` instead of only looking at the first header value.

### Gin Version

master

No

problems.title: Recovery middleware does not add error to context
problems.issue_body:
- go version: go version go1.12.1 darwin/amd64
- gin version (or commit ref): v1.4.0
- operating system: OSX 10.14.3

## Description
Currently the recovery middleware only adds a recovered error to context when there is a broken pipe:  https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/blob/master/recovery.go#L75
```
if brokenPipe {
    c.Error(err.(error)) // nolint: errcheck
    c.Abort()
} else {
    c.AbortWithStatus(http.StatusInternalServerError)
}
````

It would be great to have the else case also add the error to the context so that middleware higher in the chain can process those errors (in tracing middleware for example). This could be done by simply adding: `c.Error(errors.New(fmt.Sprintf("%v", err)))` or doing some switching on the err type. 

If this is desirable I can create a PR with the changes.

problems.title: SaveUploadedFile: unexpected chmod on existing directories (breaks /tmp usage)
problems.issue_body:
## Description

After upgrading from v1.10.1 to v1.12.0, `Context.SaveUploadedFile` started to fail when saving files directly into existing system directories like `/tmp`.

The failure happens due to an attempt to call `os.Chmod` on the target directory, even if it already exists and is not owned by the process.

Relevant code:
https://github.com/gin-gonic/gin/blob/v1.12.0/context.go#L734

## Reproduction

```go
file, _ := c.FormFile("file")

// Saving directly into /tmp
err := c.SaveUploadedFile(file, "/tmp/test.txt")
if err != nil {
  panic(err)
}
```

## Actual behavior

The call fails with:

chmod /tmp: operation not permitted

## Expected behavior

If the directory already exists, especially for system directories like `/tmp`, `SaveUploadedFile` should not attempt to modify its permissions.

The previous behavior (v1.10.1) only used `os.MkdirAll`, which does not change permissions on existing directories.

## Impact

This is a breaking change for common usage patterns such as:

* saving files to `/tmp/<filename>`
* writing into pre-existing directories managed by the OS or container runtime

## Context

This behavior appears to be introduced together with the change that allows specifying permissions for created directories (see #4068). However, applying `chmod` unconditionally also affects already existing directories.

## Suggested fix

Only apply `os.Chmod` when the directory is newly created, or make it optional.

For example:

* skip `chmod` if directory already exists
* or provide a flag to control this behavior

## Additional notes

This change is not mentioned as breaking in release notes, but it alters previously working behavior.


### Gin Version

v1.12.0

### Can you reproduce the bug?

Yes

### Source Code

```go
file, _ := c.FormFile("file")

// Saving directly into /tmp
err := c.SaveUploadedFile(file, "/tmp/test.txt")
if err != nil {
   panic(err)
}
```

### Go Version

1.26.1

### Operating System

linux
