problems.title: fix: Weekly Brief safety/privacy note counts are always zero in production
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix `weekly-brief-lib.js`'s `itemFromEntry`/`newEntryReasons`/`sourceBackedReasons` so they use the already-correct `hasSafetyNotes(entry)`/`hasPrivacyNotes(entry)` fallback instead of reading `entry.safetyNotes`/`entry.privacyNotes` directly — those raw fields are always empty in the production directory index the brief actually runs against.

## Why this matters
The module's own comment (lines 145-148) explicitly warns about this exact trap: *"the slimmer directory index the brief actually runs against in production drops [safetyNotes/privacyNotes] and keeps only the `trustSignals.has*` booleans — read both so the signal isn't silently dead in prod."* `hasSafetyNotes()`/`hasPrivacyNotes()` and `trustScore()` correctly follow that warning. But `itemFromEntry()` — the function that builds every email-visible `BriefItem` — and `newEntryReasons()`/`sourceBackedReasons()` ignore it, reading the raw fields directly. Since `buildDirectoryEntries()` (the function that builds the production directory index) never emits `safetyNotes`/`privacyNotes` (only `trustSignals`), `safetyNotesCount`/`privacyNotesCount` are always `0` in every real Weekly Brief email, and the "safety notes"/"privacy notes" badge in `brief-email-lib.ts`'s `itemBadges` can never appear — even for entries that genuinely have safety notes — directly undermining the brief's own stated claim that "every entry is metadata-reviewed for source & safety."

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/weekly-brief-lib.js:216-217,228-229,235-236`:
```js
safetyNotesCount: list(entry.safetyNotes).length,
privacyNotesCount: list(entry.privacyNotes).length,
```
(and the same pattern in `newEntryReasons()`/`sourceBackedReasons()`). `buildDirectoryEntries()` (`packages/registry/src/artifacts-lib.js:294-338`) never emits `safetyNotes`/`privacyNotes`, only `trustSignals` (via `buildEntryTrustSignals`, which does compute `hasSafetyNotes`/`hasPrivacyNotes` booleans).

## Desired behavior
`itemFromEntry()`, `newEntryReasons()`, and `sourceBackedReasons()` all use `hasSafetyNotes(entry)`/`hasPrivacyNotes(entry)` (the module's own existing, correct helpers) instead of raw `list(entry.safetyNotes).length`/`list(entry.privacyNotes).length`, so the safety/privacy badges and reason text actually reflect real entry data in production.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/weekly-brief-lib.js
- focused tests: tests/weekly-brief-lib.test.ts

## Out of scope
- apps/web/src/lib/brief-email-lib.ts's itemBadges rendering logic itself (already correct, reference implementation — the bug is upstream data, not the badge logic)
- trustScore()'s existing correct usage of hasSafetyNotes/hasPrivacyNotes (already correct, do not modify)
- artifacts-lib.js's buildDirectoryEntries (already correct/intentional — the slim production index is by design; the fix belongs in the consumer, not the producer)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- itemFromEntry/newEntryReasons/sourceBackedReasons produce non-zero …

problems.title: fix: hashSearch/savedSearchSignature use unescaped delimiters, causing real cross-search hash collisions
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix `hashSearch`'s (and the same-pattern `savedSearchSignature`'s) unescaped-delimiter join so two different saved searches can no longer collide onto the same hash — the collision is real, reachable via a plain `/browse` URL, and causes cross-user newsletter alert-segment routing.

## Why this matters
`hashSearch`'s docstring claims "different searches (almost) always differ," but joining fields with a raw `|` delimiter means content shifted across a field boundary produces byte-identical input. Verified concretely: `{q:"foo", category:"bar|baz"}` and `{q:"foo|bar", category:"baz"}` both hash to `"8hrv9c"`. This is reachable in practice, not just theoretical — `/browse`'s `category` search param is validated as a plain `z.string()` with no enum restriction, and `saveCurrent()` copies it verbatim into the saved search, so a hand-edited or shared URL like `/browse?q=foo&category=bar%7Cbaz` produces a colliding saved search. `hashSearch` builds the newsletter alert-segment key `saved-search:${hashSearch(s)}` when a user enables email alerts — a collision means one user's saved-search alert segment can be shared with an unrelated user's saved search, so alert emails intended for one search can be delivered against a different search's segment. `savedSearchSignature` (`saved-search-signature-lib.ts`) has the identical unescaped-delimiter bug (verified: a tab character shifted from `label` into `q` produces the same signature) — lower real-world impact since it only gates a `useEffect` refetch, not actual alert matching, but the same fix applies.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/lib/saved-search-hash-lib.ts:12-17`:
```ts
export function hashSearch(s: SavedSearch): string {
  const raw = `${s.q}|${s.category ?? ""}|${s.trust ?? ""}|${s.source ?? ""}|${s.platform ?? ""}`;
  let h = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < raw.length; i++) h = (h * 31 + raw.charCodeAt(i)) | 0;
  return Math.abs(h).toString(36);
}
```
`apps/web/src/lib/saved-search-signature-lib.ts:12-28` joins fields with `\t` and entries with `\n`, same class of bug.

## Desired behavior
Both functions escape or unambiguously delimit fields before hashing/joining — e.g. JSON-encode the field array (`JSON.stringify([s.q, s.category, ...])`) or length-prefix each field — so two semantically different inputs can never produce the same hash/signature via a shifted delimiter.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/lib/saved-search-hash-lib.ts
- apps/web/src/lib/saved-search-signature-lib.ts
- focused tests: tests/saved-search-hash-lib.test.ts, tests/saved-search-signature-lib.test.ts

## Out of scope
- Any consumer of hashSearch/savedSearchSignature (saved-search-manager.tsx, watch.tsx) — no changes needed there, the fix is contained to the two hashing functions
- Changing the alert-segment key format itself beyond fixing the underlying collision

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- The two previously-colliding fixture pairs (documented above) now produce different hashes/signatures.
- Exi…

problems.title: feat(mcp): add workflow toolbox planner
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

HeyClaude MCP has strong primitives for search, related entries, copyable assets, comparison, trust explanations, and install guidance. A workflow planner tool can compose those primitives into a practical small toolbox for a user goal.

## Current state

- MCP tools include `search_registry`, `get_related_entries`, `compare_entries`, `get_copyable_asset`, and trust/safety helpers.
- Clients must manually chain those tools to build a recommended set of entries.
- There is no single read-only tool that turns a task like “set up Claude Code hooks and MCP docs search” into a curated candidate set.

## Desired behavior

- Add a read-only MCP tool that accepts a goal/query plus optional category/platform constraints.
- Return a bounded toolbox of recommended entries with reasons, caveats, trust metadata, and next-step copy/install actions.
- Prefer diverse categories when useful instead of returning only near-duplicates.
- Keep all output factual and metadata-derived.

## Implementation notes

- Build on shared ranked search and related-entry scoring if available.
- Include explicit reason codes like `query_match`, `same_platform`, `trusted_package`, `has_safety_notes`, or `complementary_category`.
- Keep limits small and validation strict.
- Do not call external services or create submissions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tool returns a bounded, deterministic toolbox for common workflow goals.
- Results include reason metadata and trust/safety reminders.
- Empty or weak matches return useful guidance rather than fabricated recommendations.
- Protocol tests cover happy path, constrained category/platform, and no-match behavior.

## Validation

- `pnpm test:mcp`
- `pnpm validate:mcp-package`
- Add or update focused unit tests for the touched API/helper surface.
- Run the narrow relevant validation command for the changed package or route.
- Run `git diff --check` before opening a PR.

problems.title: fix: inferStructuredFields' verifiedAt derivation isn't Date-guarded like normalizeDateAdded
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix `inferStructuredFields`'s `verifiedAt` derivation so it Date-guards `data.dateAdded` the same way `content-builder-lib.js`'s `normalizeDateAdded` already does, preventing a timezone-shifted, non-ISO `verifiedAt` value the moment a future skill entry's `dateAdded` is written unquoted in frontmatter.

## Why this matters
`content-builder-lib.js` has a dedicated `normalizeDateAdded` helper specifically because YAML/gray-matter coerces an unquoted date (`dateAdded: 2025-09-18`, no quotes) into a real JS `Date` object. But `inferStructuredFields`'s `verifiedAt` derivation for skills reads the same raw `data.dateAdded` without that guard, calling `String(data.dateAdded).trim()` directly. Verified against the real gray-matter parser with an unquoted date: the resulting `verifiedAt` is not just malformed, it's timezone-shifted to the wrong calendar day (e.g. `"Wed Sep 17 2025..."` instead of the intended `2025-09-18`). This value flows directly into the published entry's `verifiedAt` field with no gate, because `validateEntry` — the only place that would catch the bad format — is confirmed test-only (never called from `buildContentEntryFromMdx` or any build script). All 1,372 current `dateAdded:` values in `content/` happen to be quoted strings, so this hasn't fired yet — but it's a real, reproduced defect waiting on the first unquoted date, not a hypothetical.

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/content-schema-lib.js:574-581` (`inferStructuredFields`):
```js
const verifiedAt = category === "skills"
  ? data.verifiedAt ? String(data.verifiedAt).trim()
    : data.dateAdded ? String(data.dateAdded).trim()   // no Date guard
    : ""
  : "";
```
`packages/registry/src/content-builder-lib.js:52-61` (`normalizeDateAdded`, the correct reference pattern):
```js
export function normalizeDateAdded(value) {
  if (!value) return undefined;
  if (value instanceof Date && !Number.isNaN(value.getTime())) {
    return value.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  }
  ...
}
```

## Desired behavior
`inferStructuredFields`'s `verifiedAt` fallback uses the same Date-instance guard as `normalizeDateAdded` before stringifying `data.dateAdded`, so an unquoted-date frontmatter value produces the correct ISO calendar date instead of a timezone-shifted `Date.toString()` output.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/content-schema-lib.js
- focused tests: tests/content-schema-lib.test.ts

## Out of scope
- content-builder-lib.js's normalizeDateAdded itself (already correct, reference implementation — reuse it or its logic, don't modify it)
- Wiring validateEntry into the actual build path (a separate, larger concern — out of scope for this narrow fix; if the maintainer wants that too, it should be its own issue)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- inferStructuredFields produces a correct ISO-format verifiedAt when data.dateAdded is an unquoted YAML date (a real JS Date instance from gray-matter).
- Existing behavior for quoted-string dateAdded values …

problems.title: fix: githubRepoFromUrl/githubLoginFromUrl don't normalize www.github.com like isPublicGitHubHostUrl does
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Make `githubRepoFromUrl()` and `isPublicGitHubProfileUrl()`/`githubLoginFromUrl()` recognize `www.github.com` URLs the same way `isPublicGitHubHostUrl()` already does.

## Why this matters
`isPublicGitHubHostUrl()`'s own docstring says it strips `www.` before comparing hostnames; a sibling classifier `isPublicGitHubProfileUrl()` explicitly documents intending to "stay in sync" with the repo-URL parser via a shared reserved-name set, yet neither it nor `githubRepoFromUrl()` performs the same `www.` stripping. A submitted `https://www.github.com/owner/repo` source URL silently fails to register as a GitHub source trust signal and never calls `addGithubSourceRepo`, even though the package's own `isPublicGitHubHostUrl()` would classify it as a valid GitHub repo URL a few lines away.

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/submission-risk.js:292-303`'s `githubRepoFromUrl()` checks `url.hostname !== "github.com"` with no normalization. `packages/registry/src/source-url-lib.js:166-178`'s `isPublicGitHubHostUrl()` does `url.hostname.replace(/^www\./i, "").toLowerCase()` first. `isPublicGitHubProfileUrl()` (used by `githubLoginFromUrl`) has the same un-normalized `=== "github.com"` check.

## Desired behavior
`githubRepoFromUrl()` and `isPublicGitHubProfileUrl()` both strip a leading `www.` (case-insensitive) before comparing hostnames, either by duplicating the same one-line normalization or by routing through `isPublicGitHubHostUrl()` directly.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/submission-risk.js
- focused tests: tests/submission-risk-invariants.test.ts, tests/registry-source-url.test.ts

## Out of scope
- Any other hostname classifier not named above
- source-url-lib.js's isPublicGitHubHostUrl itself (already correct, reference implementation)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- A submitted https://www.github.com/owner/repo source URL is recognized as a GitHub repo the same way https://github.com/owner/repo is.
- Existing non-GitHub and non-www GitHub URL handling is unchanged.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- List the exact URL forms covered by the new/updated test cases (with and without www., mixed case).

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/submission-risk-invariants.test.ts tests/registry-source-url.test.ts
pnpm --filter web type-check

problems.title: fix: relationships-lib.js's sourceUrls() omits packageUrl, docsUrl, sourceUrl, repositoryUrl, and plural sourceUrls[]
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Add the four real, validated URL fields (`docsUrl`, `sourceUrl`, `packageUrl`, `repositoryUrl`, and the plural `sourceUrls[]`) that `relationships-lib.js`'s `sourceUrls()` currently omits, so entries that share these source links can actually be matched as related.

## Why this matters
`content-schema-lib.js` validates `docsUrl`, `sourceUrl`, `packageUrl`, `repositoryUrl`, and `sourceUrls[]` as first-class URL fields with the same treatment as `repoUrl`/`documentationUrl`, and `content-builder-lib.js` copies all of them onto every built entry. But `relationships-lib.js`'s `sourceUrls()` — whose entire job is gathering an entry's source links for relationship matching — never reads any of them, only `repoUrl`/`documentationUrl`/`websiteUrl`/`downloadUrl`/`retrievalSources`. `packageUrl` and plural `sourceUrls[]` are actively used in real content today (e.g. `content/tools/official-mcp-rust-sdk.mdx`'s `packageUrl`), so entries that share only these fields are invisible to relationship matching — verified with two realistic tool entries sharing only a `packageUrl` domain: they never score as related, because `candidatesFor` in `buildRegistryRelationGraph` indexes candidates off these same source-URL buckets, so such pairs may not even be considered as candidates at all.

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/relationships-lib.js:126-140`:
```js
export function sourceUrls(entry) {
  return unique(
    [
      entry.repoUrl,
      entry.documentationUrl,
      entry.websiteUrl,
      entry.downloadUrl && !String(entry.downloadUrl).startsWith("/") ? entry.downloadUrl : "",
      ...(Array.isArray(entry.retrievalSources) ? entry.retrievalSources : []),
    ].map(normalizeUrl).filter(Boolean),
  );
}
```

## Desired behavior
`sourceUrls()` additionally includes `entry.docsUrl`, `entry.sourceUrl`, `entry.packageUrl`, `entry.repositoryUrl`, and `...(entry.sourceUrls ?? [])`, so entries sharing any of these real, validated fields become visible to relationship candidate-building and scoring.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/relationships-lib.js
- focused tests: tests/relationships-lib.test.ts

## Out of scope
- candidatesFor's bucket-based optimization logic itself (already verified correct in a prior pass — only the input set (sourceUrls) needs to grow, not the bucketing algorithm)
- content-schema-lib.js's validation of these fields (already correct, reference implementation)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- Two entries sharing only a packageUrl (or docsUrl/sourceUrl/repositoryUrl/plural sourceUrls) domain now become candidates and can score as related.
- Existing relationship behavior driven by repoUrl/documentationUrl/websiteUrl/downloadUrl/retrievalSources is unchanged.
- A regression test locks in the previously-missed packageUrl-sharing case.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- Include a before/after: two fixture entries sharing only a packageUrl, showing they were not candidates befor…

problems.title: fix: commercial-lib.js's hasHttpsUrl accepts malformed/credential-embedded URLs that reach the public jobs board
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Replace `commercial-lib.js`'s weak `hasHttpsUrl` prefix-only check with the same `isPublicHttpsUrl` validator already used elsewhere in the same file, so job `applyUrl`/`sourceUrl` gating can't be bypassed with a malformed or credential-embedded URL.

## Why this matters
`hasHttpsUrl`/`isPublicHttpsUrl` are meant to validate the same concept ("a public https URL") for job listing fields in the same file, but they diverge: `hasHttpsUrl` is a naive `/^https:\/\//i` prefix test that accepts malformed URLs and URLs with embedded userinfo/credentials (`https://user:pass@evil.com/apply`), while `isPublicHttpsUrl` correctly rejects them. This isn't a theoretical gap — `validateJobPublicExposure` (gated by `hasHttpsUrl`) is the literal filter `apps/web/src/lib/jobs.ts:88` uses to decide which "active" jobs are shown on the public jobs page, and `apps/web/src/lib/job-admin-lib.ts:174` uses it in the admin gate too. A job with a malicious/malformed `applyUrl` can pass this check and reach the public jobs board.

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/commercial-lib.js:192-194`:
```js
export function hasHttpsUrl(value) {
  return /^https:\/\//i.test(textValue(value));
}
```
Used to gate `applyUrl`/`sourceUrl` in `validateJobPublicationQuality` (lines 267-269) and `validateJobPublicExposure` (lines 318-323). The same file already imports and uses the stricter `isPublicHttpsUrl` (from `source-url-lib.js`) for lead `websiteUrl`/`applyUrl` validation via `isPublicLeadHttpsUrl` (lines 97-101) — the correct pattern is already present in the file, just not applied here. Verified: `hasHttpsUrl('https://user:pass@evil.com/apply')` returns `true`, while `isPublicHttpsUrl` on the same input returns `false`, and `validateJobPublicExposure` with that `applyUrl` produces zero errors — a clean pass for a URL that should be rejected.

## Desired behavior
`hasHttpsUrl`'s callers use `isPublicHttpsUrl` (already imported in this file) instead, so job `applyUrl`/`sourceUrl` get the same rejection of malformed/credential-embedded URLs that lead validation already gets.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/commercial-lib.js
- focused tests: tests/commercial-lib.test.ts

## Out of scope
- source-url-lib.js's isPublicHttpsUrl itself (already correct, reference implementation)
- Lead validation (isPublicLeadHttpsUrl) — already correct, do not modify
- Any other job-validation field not related to applyUrl/sourceUrl's https-URL check

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- A job with a malformed or credential-embedded applyUrl/sourceUrl is now rejected by validateJobPublicationQuality/validateJobPublicExposure.
- Legitimate https applyUrl/sourceUrl values continue to pass.
- A regression test locks in the credential-embedded-URL rejection case.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- List the exact URL forms covered by the new/updated test cases (valid https, credential-embedded, malformed), with expected pass/fail for each.

## Vali…

problems.title: fix: command-safety-lib.js's REMOVE_PATTERN/CHMOD_PATTERN miss split and long-form flag variants
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix `command-safety-lib.js`'s `REMOVE_PATTERN` and `CHMOD_PATTERN` so they catch split, reversed, and long-form flag variants of `rm -rf` and `chmod -R 777`, not just one literal bundled-flag spelling.

## Why this matters
`REMOVE_PATTERN`/`CHMOD_PATTERN` back the shell-command safety scanner used by `apps/web/src/lib/skill-package-validator-lib.ts` and `trust-lib.ts` for skill-package/script safety scanning — a real, user-facing safety signal. Verified by direct testing that both patterns only match one specific flag spelling and silently miss equally common variants.

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/command-safety-lib.js:18-19`:
```js
export const REMOVE_PATTERN = /\brm\s+-[a-z]*r[a-z]*f|\brm\s+-[a-z]*f[a-z]*r/i;
export const CHMOD_PATTERN = /\bchmod\s+(?:-R\s+)?0?777\b/i;
```
Verified via direct execution:
- `REMOVE_PATTERN.test("rm -r -f /")` → **false** (missed — split flags)
- `REMOVE_PATTERN.test("rm --recursive --force /")` → **false** (missed — long-form)
- `CHMOD_PATTERN.test("chmod -Rv 777 f")` → **false** (missed — bundled extra flag alongside -R)
- `CHMOD_PATTERN.test("chmod -vR 777 f")` → **false** (missed — same, different position)
- `CHMOD_PATTERN.test("chmod --recursive 777 f")` → **false** (missed — long-form)
- `REMOVE_PATTERN.test("rm -rf /")` → true (correctly caught)

## Desired behavior
Both patterns (or a token-aware replacement) recognize split (`-r -f`), long-form (`--recursive --force`), and bundled-with-extra-flags (`-Rv`, `-vR`) variants — parsing `rm`/`chmod` flags token-by-token the same way this file already parses `sudo`/`env` prefixes elsewhere, rather than relying on a single monolithic regex expecting one exact bundled-flag token.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/command-safety-lib.js
- focused tests: tests/command-safety-lib.test.ts, tests/command-safety.test.ts, tests/command-safety-posix-shell.test.ts

## Out of scope
- packages/registry/src/submission-risk.js's separate, independent rm -rf check (tracked in a separate issue — different file, different consumer, do not conflate the two fixes)
- Any other pattern in command-safety-lib.js not named above

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- All previously-missed forms above (split flags, long-form flags, bundled-with-extra-flags) now match REMOVE_PATTERN/CHMOD_PATTERN as appropriate.
- Previously-caught forms remain caught.
- No new false positives on clearly benign commands (add at least one negative test case per pattern).

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- List every input string covered by the new/updated test cases, with expected true/false for each.

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/command-safety-lib.test.ts tests/command-safety.test.ts tests/command-safety-posix-shell.test.ts

problems.title: feat(mcp): expose jobs and trending resources
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The MCP server currently exposes registry directory/category/entry resources. Jobs and trending discovery are useful read-only surfaces too, and MCP clients should be able to inspect them without scraping web pages.

## Current state

- MCP resources include directory, category, and entry templates.
- Public jobs are exposed through `/api/jobs`.
- Trending exists internally through growth surfaces but does not yet have a public endpoint.

## Desired behavior

- Add MCP resources for active jobs and trending/recent discovery once the corresponding public API/artifact is stable.
- Keep outputs bounded and public-safe.
- Include source/freshness/trust metadata where available.

## Implementation notes

- Reuse public API/artifact payloads instead of database access from the MCP package.
- Keep the no-key read-only policy explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

- MCP resource listing includes jobs and discovery resources.
- Reading resources returns bounded JSON/markdown content.
- Resources degrade gracefully if dynamic state is unavailable.
- Tests cover resources over local MCP and remote HTTP route where practical.

## Validation

- `pnpm test:mcp`
- `pnpm validate:mcp-package`

problems.title: fix: source-repo-signals job makes unauthenticated GitHub API calls with no backoff for permanently-failing repos
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Add GitHub API authentication and basic error backoff to the scheduled source-repo-signals refresh job, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase for GitHub API calls.

## Why this matters
`fetchGitHubSourceSignal()` (the function the source-repo-signals scheduled job uses every 6 hours to refresh repo health signals for content entries) sends no `Authorization` header at all, subjecting every refresh to GitHub's unauthenticated 60 requests/hour limit — worse in practice on Cloudflare Workers' shared egress IPs, which are commonly already rate-limited by GitHub for anonymous traffic. The sibling route `apps/web/src/routes/api/github-stats.ts` already reads `GITHUB_TOKEN` and sets an `authorization` header — the pattern exists, it's just not applied here. Compounding this, a repo that legitimately errors (renamed/deleted/private/rate-limited) is unconditionally retried every run with no backoff, permanently competing for the same limited per-run refresh budget (default 25/run) as genuinely-stale-but-healthy repos, since repos are selected alphabetically with no prioritization between "stale" and "permanently broken." With ~1,392 content files in this directory, the resulting throughput can't keep the corpus fresh within its own staleness threshold once any repos start erroring.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/lib/source-repo-signals-fetch-lib.ts:60-83`'s `fetchGitHubSourceSignal()` makes unauthenticated requests. `shouldRefreshSourceRepoSignal()` (`source-repo-signals-lib.ts:141-146`) always returns true for `status: 'error'` rows, with no retry-count or backoff tracking. `refreshSourceRepoSignalsForEntries` (`source-repo-signals.server.ts:169-175`) takes the first N alphabetically from `collectSourceRepos()`, with no prioritization separating genuinely-stale-but-healthy repos from permanently-erroring ones.

## Desired behavior
`fetchGitHubSourceSignal()` sends an `Authorization` header using `GITHUB_TOKEN` when available (mirroring `github-stats.ts`'s pattern), raising the effective rate limit substantially. Repos in `status: 'error'` get basic backoff (e.g. a retry-count or last-attempted timestamp that delays re-attempting an errored repo for progressively longer, or at minimum deprioritizes them below genuinely-stale-but-healthy repos in the per-run selection) so a small number of permanently-broken repos can't starve the rest of the corpus of refresh budget.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/lib/source-repo-signals-fetch-lib.ts
- apps/web/src/lib/source-repo-signals-lib.ts
- apps/web/src/lib/source-repo-signals.server.ts (only the selection/prioritization logic in refreshSourceRepoSignalsForEntries)
- focused tests: tests/source-repo-signals-fetch-lib.test.ts, tests/source-repo-signals-lib.test.ts

## Out of scope
- apps/web/src/routes/api/github-stats.ts (already correct, reference implementation for the auth header pattern)
- Changing the default refreshLimit value itself (a separate tuning question, not part of this fi…

problems.title: fix: IndexNow's 48h window guarantees duplicate submission of every changed URL
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix `indexnow-scheduled.ts`'s change-detection window so it stops guaranteeing duplicate submission of essentially every changed URL, which directly contradicts the job's own anti-spam design comment.

## Why this matters
The job's own header comment states: *"We submit ONLY the URLs that changed recently... resubmitting unchanged URLs gives no benefit and reads as spam."* But the job runs daily (`DAILY_CRON = "0 5 * * *"`, 24h cadence) using a 48-hour change-detection window (`WINDOW_MS = 48 * 60 * 60 * 1000`) — exactly 2x the cadence. Traced the arithmetic: an entry updated shortly after one run has `age < 48h` at both the next run (24h later) and the run after that (48h later), so it's submitted twice before correctly aging out on the third run. This isn't an edge case — it's the guaranteed common case for essentially every changed URL, directly contradicting the "resubmitting reads as spam" rationale the comment itself states.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/plugins/indexnow-scheduled.ts:10,18,63-91` uses a 48h sliding window against a 24h run cadence, guaranteeing double submission of every changed URL under normal operation.

## Desired behavior
Either:
(a) shrink the window close to the actual cadence (e.g. 25-26h — just enough tolerance for one occasionally-missed daily run, without doubling submissions in the normal case), or
(b) track a persisted "last submitted" watermark (e.g. in KV or D1) instead of a pure sliding time window, so a URL is submitted exactly once per real change regardless of run timing.

Option (a) is the narrower fix; option (b) is more robust against missed/delayed runs but requires new persisted state — pick based on how much missed-run tolerance actually matters in practice.

## Scope
- apps/web/plugins/indexnow-scheduled.ts
- focused tests: tests/indexnow.test.ts, tests/indexnow-submit-args.test.ts

## Out of scope
- indexnow-hubs.test.ts / indexnow-normalize-site-url.test.ts's covered logic (unrelated to the window calculation)
- Any change to which URLs are eligible for submission beyond the window/watermark logic itself

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- A URL updated once is submitted exactly once across the normal daily run cadence (barring the explicitly-tolerated missed-run case, if choosing option (a)).
- The chosen fix's reasoning (window size chosen, or watermark design) is documented in a code comment, matching the file's existing comment style.
- A regression test proves a URL updated at T+ε is not submitted on both the T+24h and T+48h runs under the new logic.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- Include a before/after: trace of a URL's submission eligibility across 3 consecutive daily runs, showing double-submission before and single-submission after.

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/indexnow.test.ts tests/indexnow-submit-args.test.ts

problems.title: fix: brandLogoUrl never auto-resolves via Brandfetch, unlike brandIconUrl in the same function
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Give `brandLogoUrl` the same Brandfetch auto-resolution fallback that `brandIconUrl` already has in `buildBrandAssetMetadata`, instead of leaving it permanently empty unless an author manually supplies one.

## Why this matters
`brandAssetProxyUrl(domain, { kind })` explicitly supports `kind: "logo"`, and the runtime API route (`apps/web/src/routes/api/brand-assets/$kind/$domain.ts`) fully implements logo fetching — the capability exists end-to-end. But `buildBrandAssetMetadata` only ever calls the proxy with `kind: "icon"`, so every entry that auto-resolves an icon still leaves `brandLogoUrl` empty, despite `brandAssetSource: "brandfetch"` being recorded as if brand-asset resolution happened uniformly across both fields. This is an asymmetry between two fields meant to be handled the same way within the same function. (Currently inert/harmless in practice — nothing in the frontend renders `brandLogoUrl` today — but it's worth fixing now so the field isn't silently wrong if/when something starts consuming it, and so `brandAssetSource` accurately reflects what was actually resolved.)

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/brand-assets-lib.js:335-343,412-420`:
```js
const brandIconUrl =
    clean(data.brandIconUrl) ||
    (shouldUseBrandfetch
      ? brandAssetProxyUrl(brandDomain, { kind: "icon", siteUrl: ... })
      : "");
const brandLogoUrl = clean(data.brandLogoUrl);   // no fallback — ever
```

## Desired behavior
`brandLogoUrl` gets the same fallback treatment as `brandIconUrl`, calling `brandAssetProxyUrl(brandDomain, { kind: "logo", ... })` when `shouldUseBrandfetch` is true and no manual `brandLogoUrl` was supplied — mirroring the icon's fallback block exactly.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/brand-assets-lib.js
- focused tests: tests/brand-assets-lib.test.ts, tests/brand-assets.test.ts

## Out of scope
- Any frontend code that would render brandLogoUrl (none currently exists — this issue is scoped to making the data correct, not adding a new UI consumer)
- brandIconUrl's existing fallback logic (already correct, reference implementation)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- brandLogoUrl auto-resolves via the same Brandfetch proxy mechanism as brandIconUrl when shouldUseBrandfetch is true and no manual value was supplied.
- Manually-supplied brandLogoUrl values continue to take precedence over auto-resolution, matching brandIconUrl's existing precedence.
- A regression test locks in the new fallback behavior.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact (no current UI consumer).
- Include a before/after: a fixture entry with only brandDomain set, showing brandLogoUrl was empty before and resolves to the expected proxy URL after.

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/brand-assets-lib.test.ts tests/brand-assets.test.ts

problems.title: fix: MCP read-only tools throw unhandled exceptions instead of a clean error envelope on artifact load failure
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Make the local stdio MCP server's read-only tools return the codebase's own declared "clean error envelope" when a backing artifact fails to load, instead of throwing an unhandled exception that surfaces as a raw SDK transport error.

## Why this matters
The codebase already has the right pattern for this — `registry-response-lib.js`'s `unavailable()` is explicitly documented as "the standard 'unavailable' error envelope... so MCP clients can tell apart 'endpoint failed' from 'no such resource'" — and it's correctly used by the two HTTP-backed resource tools and independently reimplemented for the remote-proxy path. But the local stdio server's ~27 artifact-backed read-only tools (search, list, detail, related, etc. — the most heavily used entry point) never use it: a missing or corrupt artifact file (partial deploy, wrong `--data-dir`, bad JSON) throws a raw, unguarded `Error` all the way up through the MCP SDK's request handler, which also has no try/catch. This bypasses the tool's own declared `outputSchema` (which requires `{ok: boolean, ...}`) and turns a domain-level "data unavailable" case into an opaque transport-level failure for the MCP client.

## Current behavior
`packages/mcp/src/registry-artifact-loader-lib.js:47-67`'s `readJsonArtifact` does an unguarded `JSON.parse(await readTextArtifact(...))`. `packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js` has 16+ call sites of `readJsonArtifact(...)` with no `.catch` (e.g. lines 169, 202, 260, 306, 346, 376, 398, 544-545, 588, 679, 724, 839-840, 851, 867, 897) — only the `relation-graph.json` read at line 407 has `.catch(() => null)`. `callRegistryTool` (lines 987-1004) only wraps argument parsing in try/catch, not the `switch` dispatch to the actual tool implementations. `packages/mcp/src/server-lib.js:60-79`'s `CallToolRequestSchema` handler has no try/catch at all around `callRegistryTool`. Verified by direct execution: pointing `readJsonArtifact` at a nonexistent data directory throws a raw `Error: ENOENT...` that propagates unhandled through the entire call chain.

## Desired behavior
A missing/corrupt artifact during any read-only tool call returns the same `unavailable(...)` envelope already used by `listRegistryTrending`/`listJobsActive` and the remote-proxy path, matching the tool's own declared output schema, instead of throwing.

## Scope
- packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js
- packages/mcp/src/server-lib.js (only the CallToolRequestSchema handler's error boundary, if the fix is centralized there rather than per-call-site)

## Out of scope
- packages/mcp/src/registry-response-lib.js's unavailable() itself (already correct, reference implementation)
- The remote-proxy path (remote-proxy-lib.js) — already handles this correctly, do not modify
- Any change to the artifact files themselves or how they're generated

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- A missing or corrupt artifact file during any of the ~27 read-only tool calls returns …

problems.title: fix: browse decision-confidence/adoption-queue summaries divide a sampled numerator by the full population
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix decision-support summary text in `browse-decision-confidence-lib.ts` and `browse-adoption-queue-lib.ts` so the reported counts are computed from the same population as the reported total.

## Why this matters
These panels render user-facing text like "X/Y results are low-confidence" driven directly from `state.summary`. A mismatched numerator/denominator produces misleading guidance — e.g. the panel can report 0 low-confidence results when many actually exist — which undermines the whole point of a decision-support panel.

## Current behavior
`browseDecisionConfidenceState()` (`apps/web/src/lib/browse-decision-confidence-lib.ts:161-169,203-214`) sorts entries descending by `confidenceScore`, slices to `maxEntries` (default 8) as `mapped`, then calls `summary(mapped, entries.length)` where `entries.length` is the full unsliced browse result count. `summary()` counts `low`/`high` only from the 8-entry top-scored slice but labels the denominator as the full population.

`browseAdoptionQueueState()` (`apps/web/src/lib/browse-adoption-queue-lib.ts:188-196,229-239`) has the identical pattern for `hold`/`ready` counts.

Sibling modules `browse-freshness-distribution-lib.ts` and `browse-rollout-signals-lib.ts` avoid this bug by slicing first and reporting `scannedCount: scoped.length` from the same sliced population — that's the correct pattern to follow.

## Desired behavior
Both summary functions compute their numerator and denominator from the same population — either report counts scoped to the full population before slicing for display, or scope the reported denominator to the same sliced set used for the counts (matching `browse-freshness-distribution-lib.ts`/`browse-rollout-signals-lib.ts`).

## Scope
- apps/web/src/lib/browse-decision-confidence-lib.ts
- apps/web/src/lib/browse-adoption-queue-lib.ts
- focused tests: tests/browse-decision-confidence-lib.test.ts, tests/browse-adoption-queue-lib.test.ts

## Out of scope
- Changing browse-freshness-distribution-lib.ts or browse-rollout-signals-lib.ts (already correct)
- UI/component changes in browse-decision-confidence-panel.tsx / browse-adoption-queue-panel.tsx beyond what naturally follows from the corrected data
- Generated registry artifacts

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- Both summary helpers report a numerator and denominator drawn from the same population.
- Existing behavior for the correct sibling modules is unchanged.
- A regression test proves the previous bug (e.g. an all-low-confidence-except-top-8 fixture that previously reported "0 low-confidence" now reports the true count).

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- List the exact before/after summary text for a representative fixture.
- No visual impact expected (pure data-layer fix) — if the visible summary text on a real browse page changes, include a before/after screenshot of the panel.

problems.title: fix: entry.related sometimes includes a relation field and sometimes doesn't, for the same tool
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Make `entry.related`'s output shape consistent regardless of whether a pre-generated relation-graph row exists for the queried entry.

## Why this matters
The same tool, called on two different entries — or the same entry before/after the next artifact rebuild — currently returns entries with a `relation` field in one code path and without it in the other. That's a real, callable-today output-shape inconsistency that isn't caught by any schema check (the tool's output schema is loose/generic here), and a client depending on `relation` for classification will silently break for the fallback case.

## Current behavior
`packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js:393-448`'s `getRelatedEntries` has two paths:
- **Graph path** (a `relation-graph.json` row exists): `resolveGraphRelatedEntries` (`registry-handlers-lib.js:178-200`) includes `relation: relation.relation`, and the response (`buildRelatedEntriesGraphResponse`, `registry-handlers-lib.js:156-167`) sets `relationGraph: true`.
- **Fallback path** (no graph row): `scoreRelatedEntry` (`registry-projection-lib.js:59-97`) returns only `{score, reasons}` — no relation-type classification — and the handler (`buildRelatedEntriesScoredResponse`, `registry-handlers-lib.js:169-176`) omits both `relation` and `relationGraph` entirely.

The relation-type classification logic exists elsewhere in the monorepo — `packages/registry/src/relationships-lib.js:216-244`'s `relationTypeFor` computes it from the same scoring evidence — but `packages/mcp`'s fallback scorer never calls it.

## Desired behavior
Either (a) the fallback path always includes `relationGraph: false` for symmetry with the graph path's `relationGraph: true`, and/or (b) the fallback path calls the same relation-type classification logic (porting or reusing `relationTypeFor`-equivalent logic) so `relation` is present in both paths' output. Prefer (b) if it can be done narrowly, since it gives callers a consistently useful field rather than just a consistent "absence" signal.

## Scope
- packages/mcp/src/registry-handlers-lib.js
- packages/mcp/src/registry-projection-lib.js
- focused tests: tests/mcp-registry-projection-lib.test.ts

## Out of scope
- Regenerating or modifying relation-graph.json itself
- packages/registry/src/relationships-lib.js's relationTypeFor (read-only reference, or port narrowly — do not restructure it)
- Any other MCP tool's response shape

## Acceptance criteria

problems.title: fix: submission-risk.js is missing two risk checks that scripts/ci/validate-content-policy.mjs already blocks on
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Port the `affiliate_referral_url` and `mutable_script_install_source` risk-detection heuristics from `scripts/ci/validate-content-policy.mjs` into `packages/registry/src/submission-risk.js`, which the codebase's own comments say is meant to stay in sync with the CI script.

`submission-risk.js`'s `addContentRiskSignals()` backs the risk report shown to maintainers on both the issue-intake/preflight path and the direct-PR risk-report comment (`scripts/analyze-submission-risk.mjs`). Right now a submission that installs via a cloned local script pinned to a mutable ref — a `critical`-severity check the real CI gate already blocks on — can show "risk tier: medium, 0 blocking flags" in the human-readable risk report maintainers actually read, while CI silently fails it for an entirely different reason. This is a real trust gap between what the automation tells a maintainer and what actually blocks a PR.

## Current behavior
`scripts/ci/validate-content-policy.mjs` has two detection heuristics never ported to the registry package:
- `affiliate_referral_url` (severity "high", lines 913-920)
- `mutable_script_install_source` (severity "critical", lines 993-1005)

Backed by helper functions (`isLikelyAffiliateUrl`, `referencesClonedLocalScriptInstall`, `hasBoundImmutableGithubScriptEvidence`, `isMutableGithubSourceUrl`, `githubSourceRef`, `collectGitCloneRepos`, `checkoutCommitIndex`, all in `validate-content-policy.mjs:439-646`) that exist only in that CI script — confirmed absent from `packages/registry/src/submission-risk.js` by name search. `submission-risk.js`'s comments (e.g. around line 79-86) explicitly describe other `*_PATTERN` constants as "intentionally duplicated" and meant to mirror the CI script, but these two checks were never ported.

problems.title: fix: submission-risk.js's rm -rf detector misses bare-root/tilde targets and non-standard flag ordering
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix the `unsafe_install_pipeline` "critical" destructive-command check in `submission-risk.js` so it actually catches the most classic `rm -rf` destructive-command forms — bare-root/tilde/`$HOME` targets and non-`-rf`-ordered flags — instead of silently missing them.

## Why this matters
This is a "critical"-severity content-risk check meant to catch destructive install commands in submitted content. Verified by direct testing that the regex misses the single most classic destructive command (`rm -rf /`, with nothing appended after the target) plus several trivial flag-ordering variants — the exact forms most likely to appear in an actually-malicious submission, since they're the shortest/most literal way to write "delete everything."

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/submission-risk.js:971` (part of the `unsafe_install_pipeline` critical flag, lines 970-987):
```js
/rm\s+-rf\s+(\/|~|\$home)\b/i.test(installText)
```
Verified via direct execution:
- `"rm -rf /"` → **false** (missed — the `\b` word-boundary after the bare target `/`/`~`/`$HOME` requires a following word character, which a bare target doesn't have)
- `"rm -rf ~"` → **false** (missed, same reason)
- `"rm -r -f /"` → **false** (missed — split flags)
- `"rm -fr /"` → **false** (missed — reversed flag order)
- `"rm --recursive --force /"` → **false** (missed — long-form flags)
- `"rm -rf /etc"` → true (correctly caught — has a trailing word character after the target)

## Desired behavior
The check catches `rm -rf /`, `rm -rf ~`, `rm -rf $HOME` with nothing appended, and recognizes split (`-r -f`), reversed (`-fr`), and long-form (`--recursive --force`) flag variants — not just the single literal `-rf` token.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/submission-risk.js
- focused tests: tests/submission-risk-invariants.test.ts

## Out of scope
- packages/registry/src/command-safety-lib.js's separate REMOVE_PATTERN/CHMOD_PATTERN (tracked in a separate issue — different file, different consumer, do not conflate the two fixes)
- Any other risk check in submission-risk.js not part of unsafe_install_pipeline's destructive-command detection

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- All 5 previously-missed forms above (bare `/`, bare `~`, split flags, reversed flags, long-form flags) now trigger the unsafe_install_pipeline critical flag.
- Previously-caught forms (e.g. `rm -rf /etc`) remain caught.
- No new false positives on clearly benign install text (add at least one negative test case).

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- List every input string covered by the new/updated test cases, with expected true/false for each.

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/submission-risk-invariants.test.ts

problems.title: feat: registry.list can't filter by trust signals like registry.search can

Give the `registry.list` MCP tool the same trust-signal filters (`hasSafetyNotes`, `hasPrivacyNotes`, `downloadTrust`, `claimStatus`, `sourceStatus`) that `registry.search` already supports over the same underlying data.

`registry.list` is the paginated browse tool — the natural fit for a query like "show me all first-party-package MCP servers with safety notes, paginated" — but today only `registry.search` (unpaginated) can filter by trust signals. ## Desired behavior
`ListCategoryEntriesInputSchema` accepts the same 5 trust fields as `SearchRegistryInputSchema`, and `listCategoryEntries` applies `entryMatchesTrustFilters(entry, parsedTrustArgs(args))` the same way `searchRegistry` does, before pagination.

## Scope

- packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js

## Out of scope

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- registry.list accepts hasSafetyNotes, hasPrivacyNotes, downloadTrust, claimStatus, sourceStatus and filters results by them before pagination.
- registry.search's behavior and schema are unchanged.

problems.title: fix: resolveMcpInstallConfig rejects valid multi-server configSnippets, giving them zero install targets
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix (or explicitly document as intentional) `resolveMcpInstallConfig`'s hard rejection of any `configSnippet` declaring more than one server — real, valid multi-server MCP registry entries currently get zero one-click install targets as a result.

## Why this matters
`content/mcp/ai-aliengiraffe-spotdb-mcp-server.mdx` is a real, valid, currently-published registry entry whose `configSnippet` legitimately declares two servers (`spotdb-sse`, `spotdb-streamable`) under `mcpServers` — a normal, valid MCP config shape. Running `resolveMcpInstallConfig` against its actual `configSnippet` returns `null`, so this entry (and any future multi-server MCP bundle) gets zero one-click install targets, even though every individual server config inside it is otherwise valid on its own. There's no comment in the code explaining single-server-only as a deliberate product constraint, so this may be an oversight rather than a design decision.

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/mcp-install-config-lib.js:134-143` (`singleServerFromMap`):
```js
function singleServerFromMap(value) {
  if (!isRecord(value)) return null;
  const servers = Object.entries(value).filter(([, config]) => isRecord(config));
  if (servers.length !== 1) return null;   // hard-rejects anything but exactly 1
  ...
}

Make the admin jobs list surface (or filter by) the same visibility rules the public jobs list applies (`expires_at` cutoff and `validateJobPublicExposure` quality gate), so an admin filtering to `status=active` doesn't see jobs that are simultaneously invisible on the public `/jobs` page with no indication of the discrepancy.

`queryActiveJobs` (the public path, `apps/web/src/lib/jobs.ts:33-98`) filters on `status = 'active' AND (expires_at IS NULL OR datetime(expires_at) >= datetime('now'))`, then further filters through `validateJobPublicExposure()`. `queryAdminJobs` (`apps/web/src/lib/job-admin-lib.ts:234-276`) only filters on `status`/`tier`/`source`/`sourceKind` — no expiry cutoff and no exposure/quality gate at all. problems.title: fix: admin listing-leads status PATCH has a lost-update race with no conflict detection
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix a lost-update race in the admin listing-leads status PATCH — two concurrent status-change requests on the same lead can silently overwrite each other with no conflict detection.

## Why this matters
`nextStatus` is computed from a `status` value read in a separate prior `SELECT`, but the subsequent `UPDATE`'s `WHERE` clause only matches on `id`, not on the status the transition was actually derived from. Two concurrent PATCH calls on the same lead (e.g. `action=approve` and `action=reject`, both valid from `pending_review`) can both read the same starting status, both compute a different valid `nextStatus`, and both unconditionally write — last write wins, silently. The losing request still returns `{ ok: true, status: nextStatus }` and logs an audit event with a `from/to` pair that no longer reflects the actually-persisted row, which is a real data-integrity and audit-trail problem for an admin moderation action.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/routes/api/admin/listing-leads.ts:122-138`:
```ts
const current = await db.prepare("SELECT id, status FROM listing_leads WHERE id = ?").bind(id).first();
...
const nextStatus = nextLeadStatus(current.status, action);
if (nextStatus === current.status) return apiError("invalid_transition", 400, { requestId });

await db.prepare("UPDATE listing_leads SET status = ?, updated_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = ?").bind(nextStatus, id).run();
```
No check of `result.meta.changes` after the UPDATE, and no `status = ?` condition tying the write to the status that was read. Compare to `updateAdminJobState`, which at least checks `meta.changes` to detect a no-op after its UPDATE.

## Desired behavior
The UPDATE includes `AND status = ?` bound to `current.status`, making the write conditional on the row not having changed since it was read. If `meta.changes === 0` after that conditional UPDATE, the route returns a `409` conflict (the lead's status changed between read and write) instead of assuming success.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/routes/api/admin/listing-leads.ts

## Out of scope
- nextLeadStatus's transition table itself (packages/registry/src/commercial-lib.js — already correct, reference implementation)
- apps/web/src/lib/job-admin-lib.ts's own concurrency handling (a separate, lower-confidence finding tracked in a different issue if the maintainer wants it addressed)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- The UPDATE is conditioned on the status value that was read, not just the id.
- A conflicting concurrent write (status changed between read and write) returns a 409, not a silent false-success.
- A regression test simulates the race (two sequential updates where the second's expected prior status no longer matches) and confirms the second call gets a 409.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- List invariants: confirm the audit-log event for the conflicting request is either not emitted or clearly marked as a conflict, not a successful transition.

problems.title: fix: /api/public/npm/$ has zero rate limiting, unlike every comparable public proxy endpoint
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Add rate limiting (and confirm origin-check policy) to `/api/public/npm/$` — an open, unauthenticated proxy endpoint that currently has neither, unlike every other comparable public data-proxy endpoint in this app.

## Why this matters
`/api/public/npm/$` takes an arbitrary npm package name from the URL path and fans out to **three** upstream fetch calls (`registry.npmjs.org/.../latest`, `api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/...`, `registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>`) per uncached request, with only a per-isolate in-memory cache that's trivially bypassed by varying the package-name path segment (the accepting regex is broad enough to match many non-real package-shaped strings, so a request doesn't even need a real package to trigger the fan-out). This is a real, currently-live amplification/cost vector: an unauthenticated caller can drive unbounded upstream request volume against npmjs.org through this app's own edge, with no rate limit anywhere in the request path. Every other comparable public proxy/dynamic-data endpoint in this app (`githubStats.read`, `brandAsset.read`, `publicFeeds.health`, `publicAlerts.read`) has a rate-limit scope; this one doesn't.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/routes/api/public/npm/$.ts` is not registered in `apiRouteDefinitions` (no `rateLimit`, no `originCheck`) and never calls `isRateLimited`/`enforceApiRateLimit`/`isAllowedOrigin` anywhere in the file.

## Desired behavior
`/api/public/npm/$` is registered in `apiRouteDefinitions` with a `rateLimit.binding` matching the pattern used by `githubStats.read`/`brandAsset.read` (a Cloudflare `RateLimit` binding via `enforceApiRateLimit`, not just an in-memory check), and applies it before the upstream fan-out. If an origin check is appropriate for this endpoint's actual usage (confirm by checking how it's called — client-side fetch vs. server-to-server), add that too, matching sibling public endpoints.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/routes/api/public/npm/$.ts
- apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts (register the route's rate-limit binding)
- apps/web/wrangler.jsonc (only if a new RateLimit binding needs provisioning — check first, an existing binding like API_DYNAMIC_RATE_LIMIT may already fit)

## Out of scope
- apps/web/src/routes/api/github-stats.ts or brand-asset equivalents (already correct, reference implementations)
- Changing the npm proxy's actual data-fetching/caching logic beyond adding the rate limit
- Any other public API endpoint's rate-limit configuration

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- /api/public/npm/$ enforces a real Cloudflare RateLimit binding before making any upstream fetch call, matching the pattern used by githubStats.read/brandAsset.read.
- Existing successful-path behavior (response shape, caching) is unchanged.
- apiRouteDefinitions includes a rateLimit.binding entry for this route.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- List invariants and backward-compatibility notes: confirm the chosen rate li…

problems.title: fix: /api/public/newsletter/unsubscribe skips the durable Cloudflare rate limiter its sibling endpoints use
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Route `/api/public/newsletter/unsubscribe` through the same durable Cloudflare rate limiter its sibling newsletter endpoints (`subscribe`, `confirm`, `webhook`) already use, instead of its own hand-rolled, per-isolate in-memory limiter.

## Why this matters
`subscribe`, `confirm`, and `webhook` all go through `createApiHandler`/`enforceRateLimit`, which tries the real Cloudflare `RateLimit` binding (`API_STRICT_RATE_LIMIT`) first and only falls back to an in-memory limiter in development/preview/binding-miss cases. `unsubscribe.ts` bypasses that entirely and hand-rolls its own check using only the weak in-memory limiter — in production this means it never gets the durable, cross-isolate rate limit its siblings get, making it trivially bypassable by hitting different Cloudflare edge isolates. It's also absent from `apiRouteDefinitions`, so it's excluded from the OpenAPI security contract that documents route-level rate limits for public endpoints.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/routes/api/public/newsletter/unsubscribe.ts`:
```ts
const RATE_LIMIT = { scope: "newsletter-unsubscribe", limit: 15, windowMs: 60_000 } as const;
...
if (isRateLimited({ request, ...RATE_LIMIT })) { ... }
```
It calls `isRateLimited()` directly, never `enforceRateLimit`/`enforceApiRateLimit`, and isn't registered in `apiRouteDefinitions` with a `rateLimit.binding`, unlike `apps/web/src/routes/api/newsletter/subscribe.ts` and `apps/web/src/routes/api/public/newsletter/confirm.ts`.

## Desired behavior
`unsubscribe.ts` routes through `createApiHandler`/`enforceRateLimit` and is registered in `apiRouteDefinitions` with a `rateLimit.binding` (e.g. `API_STRICT_RATE_LIMIT`, matching its siblings), so it gets the same durable, distributed rate limiting in production.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/routes/api/public/newsletter/unsubscribe.ts
- apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts (register the route's rate-limit binding, matching subscribe/confirm)

## Out of scope
- apps/web/src/routes/api/newsletter/subscribe.ts, apps/web/src/routes/api/public/newsletter/confirm.ts (already correct, reference implementations)
- Any other public API endpoint's rate-limit configuration

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- unsubscribe.ts uses createApiHandler/enforceRateLimit with a real Cloudflare RateLimit binding in production, matching subscribe/confirm's pattern.
- Existing unsubscribe behavior (the actual unsubscribe logic, response shape) is unchanged — only the rate-limiting mechanism changes.
- apiRouteDefinitions includes a rateLimit.binding entry for this route.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- List invariants and backward-compatibility notes: confirm the existing rate limit (15/60s) is preserved or intentionally adjusted to match the sibling endpoints' limits, and note which.

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/newsletter-unsubscribe-route.test.ts tests/api-contracts.test.ts

problems.title: fix: Raycast Has Safety/Privacy Notes filters always return zero results when browsing locally
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix the Raycast extension's "Has Safety Notes"/"Has Privacy Notes" advanced filters so they actually match entries when browsing locally (empty search box), instead of always returning zero results.

## Why this matters
This is a live, reproducible bug: selecting "Has Safety Notes" or "Has Privacy Notes" from the advanced-filter dropdown in any search command, without typing a query, always returns zero entries — even for entries that genuinely have safety/privacy notes in HeyClaude. The same root cause also permanently disables the safety/privacy accessory badge for locally-browsed entries. The filters only work when the user types a search query, because that path hits the server-side `/api/registry/search` endpoint, which does populate the needed fields — the local-browse path silently doesn't.

## Current behavior
`buildRaycastEntries` (`packages/registry/src/artifacts-lib.js:898-924`) never includes `trustSignals`, `safetyNotes`, or `privacyNotes` in the entries written to `raycast-index.json` — those fields are only populated in `buildRaycastDetail` (via `buildEntryTrustSignals`/`buildEntryNoteFields`) and in `buildSearchEntries`/`buildDirectoryEntries` (used by the server-side `/api/registry/search` endpoint), not in the feed the client caches and browses locally.

`integrations/raycast/src/feed.ts`'s `normalizeRaycastEntry` therefore always produces `entry.trustSignals === undefined`, `entry.safetyNotes === []`, `entry.privacyNotes === []` for feed-loaded entries.

`integrations/raycast/src/registry-command.tsx:283-336` (`entryMatchesResolvedFilter`, used whenever the search box is empty — `canUseServerSearch` requires non-empty search text, confirmed at lines 454, 603-612):
```ts
if (resolved.search.hasSafetyNotes === "true" &&
    !entry.trustSignals?.hasSafetyNotes && !entry.safetyNotes?.length) return false;
if (resolved.search.hasPrivacyNotes === "true" &&
    !entry.trustSignals?.hasPrivacyNotes && !entry.privacyNotes?.length) return false;
```
Both right-hand conditions are always true (fields always empty/undefined) for feed entries, so both filters always exclude every entry when browsing without a search query. The same missing data also defeats the safety/privacy `ExclamationMark` accessory badge in `metadataAccessories()` (`registry-command.tsx:219-229`) for local browsing.

## Desired behavior
`buildRaycastEntries` includes enough trust-signal data (at minimum `hasSafetyNotes`/`hasPrivacyNotes` booleans, or the full `trustSignals` object, mirroring what `buildSearchEntries` already does) so both the local-filter logic and the accessory badge work correctly whether or not the user has typed a search query.

problems.title: fix: heyclaude://category/{category} MCP resource has no pagination limit
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Add bounded pagination (offset/limit) to the `heyclaude://category/{category}` MCP resource, matching every other listing surface in the MCP server.

## Why this matters
`buildCategoryResourcePayload` (`packages/mcp/src/registry-handlers-lib.js`) filters the full search index by category and returns every matching summary with no limit at all. Every other listing surface in this package is bounded — `registry.list`'s own description promises "bounded pagination," and `DISCOVERY_RESOURCE_LIMIT = 25` caps the `heyclaude://registry/recent`/`trending`/`jobs` resources. But `content/mcp` alone currently has 481 entries, so reading `heyclaude://category/mcp` returns hundreds of full entry summaries in a single MCP resource response — an unbounded payload that defeats the token-efficiency goal the rest of the resource surface was designed around.

## Current behavior
`packages/mcp/src/registry-handlers-lib.js` (`buildCategoryResourcePayload`):
```js
export function buildCategoryResourcePayload(category, entries, toEntrySummary) {
  const summaries = entries
    .filter((entry) => entry.category === category)
    .map(toEntrySummary);
  return { ok: true, category, total: summaries.length, entries: summaries };
}
```
Called unconditionally from `packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js` wherever `parsed.hostname === "category"`, with no offset/limit parsing from the resource URI.

## Desired behavior
`buildCategoryResourcePayload` accepts `offset`/`limit` parameters (default `limit` to `DISCOVERY_RESOURCE_LIMIT`, same constant already used elsewhere in this file), slices the filtered summaries accordingly, and reports `total` (full count) alongside the returned page — mirroring how `registry.list` already exposes total vs. returned count. The category resource URI should accept `offset`/`limit` query params the same way other paginated resources in this file do.

## Scope
- packages/mcp/src/registry-handlers-lib.js (`buildCategoryResourcePayload`)
- packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js (the `category` resource-URI branch that calls it)
- packages/mcp/src/*.test.js covering this resource (add/update as needed)

## Out of scope
- Any other MCP resource or tool (`registry.list`, `registry.search`, other `heyclaude://` resources) — those are already bounded
- Changing the search index artifact itself

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- `heyclaude://category/{category}` reads accept offset/limit and cap the returned `entries` array at the effective limit (default `DISCOVERY_RESOURCE_LIMIT`).
- `total` in the response still reflects the full unfiltered count for that category, so a client can tell there's more to page through.
- Existing callers relying on the current unbounded shape (if any) are updated in the same PR.
