problems.title: fix: saved-search alerts never fire for removed registry entries
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix saved-search alerts so a "removed" registry event can actually surface as an alert, instead of being silently dropped before the match logic runs.

## Why this matters
`buildSavedSearchAlerts` (`apps/web/src/lib/saved-search-alerts-lib.ts`) explicitly models a `"warning"` severity for `action === "removed"` (line ~202), but that branch is structurally unreachable: it only evaluates events already present in `entriesByRef`, which `loadEventEntries` (`apps/web/src/lib/watch.tsx`) builds by fetching each event's *current* detail JSON (`entryDetailUrl`, `/data/entries/{category}/{slug}.json`). When an entry is removed, that JSON no longer exists, the fetch 404s, `loadEventEntries` returns `null` for it, and it's filtered out of the map entirely — so `buildSavedSearchAlerts`'s `if (!entry) continue;` skips every removed entry before checking whether it matched any saved search. A user with a saved search will never be told a matching entry was removed, even though the direct-watch path (`apps/web/src/lib/watch-alert-lib.ts`, `eventToAlert`) correctly surfaces "removed" today because it doesn't need a live entry fetch.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/lib/saved-search-alerts-lib.ts`:
```ts
const entry = entriesByRef.get(ref);
if (!entry) continue;
```
`apps/web/src/lib/watch.tsx` (`loadEventEntries`):
```ts
const response = await fetch(href, { headers: { accept: "application/json" } });
if (!response.ok) return null; // true for a removed entry — 404
```

## Desired behavior
Saved-search matching for a "removed" event uses the event's own carried fields (`event.title` and whatever entry fields the event payload already includes) instead of requiring a live entry fetch, so a removed entry can still be matched against active saved searches and produce the existing `severity: "warning"` alert. The direct-watch path already proves enough event data exists to avoid the live fetch for this case.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/lib/saved-search-alerts-lib.ts (`buildSavedSearchAlerts`)
- apps/web/src/lib/watch.tsx (`loadEventEntries`, only if the fix requires exposing the raw event alongside the fetched entry)

## Out of scope
- The direct-watch alert path (`watch-alert-lib.ts`) — already correct
- Any change to how "added"/"updated" events are matched — those already have live entry data

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- A saved search matching a since-removed entry produces a `SavedSearchAlert` with `severity: "warning"`, not silence.
- Existing "added"/"updated" saved-search alert behavior is unchanged.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact (logic-only fix, verified via a focused test).
- List invariants: a removed entry that matched an active saved search must still produce exactly one alert with `severity: "warning"`.

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/saved-search-alerts-lib.test.ts tests/saved-search-alerts.test.ts

problems.title: fix: jobs page "Up next" duplicates the current spotlight when only one job qualifies
problems.issue_body: ## Goal Fix `pickDailySpotlight` so the "Up next" job is never the same job as the currently spotlighted one. ## Why this matters `pickDailySpotlight` (`apps/web/src/lib/jobs-utils-lib.ts`) picks `current = pool[i]` and `next = pool[(i+1) % pool.length]` from the pool of high-signal jobs. When exactly one job qualifies (`pool.length === 1`), `(i+1) % 1` always equals `i`, so `next` becomes an alias of `current`. `jobs.index.tsx` renders "Up next: {spotlight.next.title}" whenever `spotlight.next` is truthy, with no check against `current` — so on any day where only one job scores high enough for the spotlight pool, the jobs page tells visitors the same job is both "currently spotlighted" and "up next," which is confusing and visibly wrong. ## Current behavior `apps/web/src/lib/jobs-utils-lib.ts` (`pickDailySpotlight`): ```ts const i = ((dayIndex % pool.length) + pool.length) % pool.length; const j = (i + 1) % pool.length; return { current: pool[i] ?? null, next: pool[j] ?? null }; ``` `apps/web/src/routes/jobs.index.tsx`: ```tsx {spotlight.next && ( Up next: {spotlight.next.title} )} ``` ## Desired behavior When `pool.length <= 1`, `pickDailySpotlight` returns `next: null` (no "up next" job exists if there's nothing else to rotate to), so the UI simply omits the "Up next" line instead of duplicating the current job. ## Scope - apps/web/src/lib/jobs-utils-lib.ts (`pickDailySpotlight`) ## Out of scope - The spotlight scoring logic (`spotlightScore`) itself - Any rendering change to jobs.index.tsx beyond what naturally follows from `next` being `null` ## Acceptance criteria - PR includes `Closes #`. - When the qualifying pool has exactly one job, `pickDailySpotlight` returns `{ current: , next: null }`. - When the pool has 2+ jobs, rotation behavior (`current`/`next` picks) is unchanged from today. ## Quality evidence required in the PR - No visual impact beyond the "Up next" line correctly disappearing for a single-job pool — a screenshot of the jobs page in that state is nice-to-have but not required given the existing test coverage path. - List invariants: `next` is never `=== current` for any pool size. ## Validation pnpm exec vitest run tests/jobs-utils-lib.test.ts

problems.title: fix: /api/submissions/preflight honeypot response doesn't match its declared response schema
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix `/api/submissions/preflight`'s published OpenAPI response contract so it accurately reflects the honeypot short-circuit response, which currently doesn't match its declared `responseSchema`.

## Why this matters
The route is registered with `responseSchema: submissionPreflightResponseSchema`, requiring fields like `category`, `slug`, `schema`, `risk`, `expectedNotes`, `blockers`, `warnings`, `duplicates`, `nextAction`, and a `routeSuggestion` enum. But the honeypot path — a real, intentional, permanent code path (confirmed by `tests/submission-api.test.ts`, "silently discards honeypot submissions without queueing anything") — returns `{ ok: true, valid: false, queued: false }`, which has none of the required fields and includes a `queued` field that isn't in the schema at all. Any API consumer or codegen tool relying on the published OpenAPI contract for this endpoint gets an inaccurate picture of what a real response can look like.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/routes/api/submissions/preflight.ts`:
```ts
if (String(payload.honeypot ?? "").trim()) {
  return apiJson({ ok: true, valid: false, queued: false }, ...);
}
```
`submissionPreflightResponseSchema` (`apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts:565-613`) is a union of two variants, both requiring the full field set above, with the non-PR-ready variant `.strict()`.

## Desired behavior
`submissionPreflightResponseSchema` becomes a union that includes the honeypot response shape as a distinct, documented variant (or the honeypot response is reshaped to satisfy the existing schema without breaking its intentional "discard silently" behavior) — whichever preserves the honeypot's actual security purpose (not revealing to a bot that it was caught) while making the published contract accurate.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts (submissionPreflightResponseSchema)
- apps/web/src/routes/api/submissions/preflight.ts (only if the response shape itself needs adjusting, not the honeypot logic)

## Out of scope
- The honeypot detection/discard logic itself (already correct, intentional security behavior — do not change what triggers it or remove the short-circuit)
- Any other submission-flow endpoint's contract

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- The published OpenAPI contract for /api/submissions/preflight accurately includes the honeypot response shape as a valid documented response.
- The honeypot's actual runtime behavior (silent discard, no queueing, no information leak to the caller about being detected) is unchanged.
- tests/submission-api.test.ts continues to pass unmodified in its honeypot assertion (or is updated only if the response shape itself changes, not the behavior).

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- List invariants: confirm the honeypot response still gives no signal distinguishing "caught as a bot" from other benign early-exit responses, if that's a deliberate security property worth preserving.

## Validation…

problems.title: fix: admin listing-leads list/CSV export has no pagination — leads beyond 100 are permanently unreachable
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Add pagination (`offset`) to the admin listing-leads list/CSV export — leads beyond the most recent 100 are currently permanently unreachable through this endpoint, with no error or indication of truncation.

## Why this matters
`adminListingLeadsQuerySchema` has `limit` (capped at 100) but no `offset` field, unlike `adminJobsQuerySchema`, which has both and is actually paginated by `scripts/check-d1-job-sources.mjs` via `offset += pageSize`. Since the router's `parseRequest` uses a non-`.strict()` zod schema (confirmed via `apps/web/src/lib/api/router-lib.ts`), an unrecognized query key like `?offset=100` is silently dropped before the handler ever sees it — appending it has zero effect. Once `listing_leads` accumulates more than 100 rows, every lead older than the newest 100 becomes permanently inaccessible through both the JSON list and the CSV export, with no error and no indication truncation happened. For a moderation/leads-review tool, this silently hides older leads from any admin trying to review the full backlog.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts:678-686` (`adminListingLeadsQuerySchema`):
```ts
export const adminListingLeadsQuerySchema = z.object({
  kind: ...,
  status: ...,
  limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).optional().default(50),
  format: ...,
});
```
No `offset`. `apps/web/src/routes/api/admin/listing-leads.ts:23-98` builds `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT ?` with only `limit`, for both the JSON list and CSV export paths.

## Desired behavior
`adminListingLeadsQuerySchema` gains an `offset` field (matching `adminJobsQuerySchema`'s pattern), and the query includes `OFFSET ?` bound to it, for both the JSON list and CSV export code paths.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts (adminListingLeadsQuerySchema)
- apps/web/src/routes/api/admin/listing-leads.ts
- focused tests: tests/listing-leads-csv-lib.test.ts

## Out of scope
- adminJobsQuerySchema/queryAdminJobs's existing pagination (already correct, reference implementation)
- Any change to the default limit value or MAX_LIMIT cap

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- offset is accepted and applied to both the JSON list and CSV export queries.
- A lead beyond the first 100 (by created_at DESC) is reachable via offset.
- Existing default (no offset supplied) behavior is unchanged.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- Include a before/after: with >100 leads in a fixture/test DB, confirm lead #101 is unreachable before and reachable with offset=100 after.

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/listing-leads-csv-lib.test.ts

problems.title: feat: jobs empty state should suggest which filter to relax, like browse does
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Give the jobs board's zero-results empty state the same actionable, per-filter guidance that `browse.tsx`'s equivalent empty state already provides.

## Why this matters
Jobs supports 6 independent filter dimensions (tier, remote, type, freshOnly, featuredOnly, free-text query) that can combine into a zero-result state with only a static "No roles match these filters." message — no indication of which filter is causing the empty result or what to relax. `browse.tsx`'s empty state solves the identical problem with contextual "relax a filter" suggestions and live match counts, materially reducing dead-end visits.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/routes/jobs.index.tsx:457-459` renders a static sentence with no per-filter suggestion when `filtered` (computed at lines 161-174) is empty. A generic "Clear" button exists in the filter bar (`jobs.index.tsx:421-430`, gated on `hasFilters`), but the empty-state message itself gives no guidance and doesn't surface which specific filter is producing zero results. Compare `apps/web/src/routes/browse.tsx:1280-1330`, which shows per-filter suggestions with live counts plus a fallback link when no suggestions exist.

## Desired behavior
The jobs empty state lists the currently active filters with per-filter "remove" affordances and/or live suggested-relaxation counts (reusing the existing `countForFilters()` helper already present at `jobs.index.tsx:216` for other UI), at minimum surfacing the existing `onClearFilters` action inline in the empty-state message itself rather than only in the separate filter bar.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/routes/jobs.index.tsx
- focused tests: tests/jobs-utils-lib.test.ts, or a new tests/jobs-empty-state-lib.test.ts if logic is extracted into a pure function

## Out of scope
- Redesigning the jobs filter bar itself
- browse.tsx's empty state (already correct, do not modify)
- Any backend/API changes to job listing data

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- The zero-result state surfaces at least one actionable per-filter suggestion or an inline clear-filters action, using the existing `countForFilters()` helper where practical.
- Existing filter-bar "Clear" button behavior is unchanged.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- Desktop and mobile screenshots of the new empty state with multiple filters applied, or a clear "No visual impact" note if not applicable.
- List expected behavior and edge cases covered: zero active filters (should not show this enhanced state), one filter applied, multiple filters combined.

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/jobs-utils-lib.test.ts
pnpm --filter web build
pnpm --filter web type-check

problems.title: fix: Raycast Create Install/Config Snippet actions never render (feed omits the fields the check depends on)
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix the Raycast extension's "Create Install Snippet"/"Create Config Snippet" actions (and the "Copy Install Command"/"Copy Config" actions in Trending/Recent Updates) so they actually appear for entries that have an install command or config snippet, instead of never rendering at all.

## Why this matters
This is a live, reproducible bug in the shipped Raycast extension, not a hypothetical. The feed generator only puts a compact subset of fields (`installable`, `hasInstallCommand`, `hasConfigSnippet`, `mcpInstallTargets`) into the cached/fetched `raycast-index.json` feed — the actual `installCommand`/`configSnippet` text only exists in the per-entry detail payload. But the client code that decides whether to show these actions reads `entry.installCommand`/`entry.configSnippet` directly off the feed entry, which is always an empty string, so the check always evaluates false.

## Current behavior
`buildCompactInstallFields()` (`packages/registry/src/artifacts-lib.js:552-568`, used by `buildRaycastEntries`, lines 898-924) never includes the raw `installCommand`/`configSnippet` text in feed entries. The client's `normalizeRaycastEntry` (`integrations/raycast/src/feed.ts:621-622`) sets `installCommand`/`configSnippet` via `optionalRawString(value.installCommand)`, which returns `""` when the field is `undefined` (`integrations/raycast/src/utils.ts:11-13`) — so every feed-loaded entry has `entry.installCommand === ""` and `entry.configSnippet === ""` regardless of whether the real entry has one.

Two consumers are broken by this:
- `integrations/raycast/src/discovery-command.tsx:389-390` (used by both `trending.tsx` and `recent-updates.tsx`) computes `hasInstallCommand = Boolean(entry.installCommand.trim())` / `hasConfig = Boolean(entry.configSnippet.trim())` — always `false`, so "Copy Install Command", "Copy Config", "Create Install Snippet", and "Create Config Snippet" (lines 430-513) never render in Trending or Recent Updates, for any entry.
- `integrations/raycast/src/registry-command.tsx:1110,1120` (used by `search.tsx` and every `search-*.tsx` command) gates `Action.CreateSnippet` for install/config directly on `entry.installCommand.trim()`/`entry.configSnippet.trim()` — same bug, so these two actions never appear in any of the 11 search commands.

Notably, the same file (`registry-command.tsx`) already has the correct pattern elsewhere: its "Use" / copy-to-clipboard section (lines 683-706, 941-944) correctly checks `entry.hasInstallCommand`/`entry.hasConfigSnippet` and fetches the detail payload via `loadEntryDetail` before copying — proving the right approach is already known and used in the same file, just not applied to the "Create Snippet" actions.

## Desired behavior
"Create Install Snippet"/"Create Config Snippet" (and Trending/Recent Updates' "Copy Install Command"/"Copy Config") gate on the boolean feed fields (`entry.hasInstallCommand`/`entry.hasConfigSnippet`) and fetch the entry detail payload (matching the existing `loadEntr…

problems.title: fix: /api/og is fully documented and tested but always returns a hardcoded 1x1 transparent PNG
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix `/api/og` so it actually generates a social-preview image from its documented query parameters, instead of always returning a hardcoded 1×1 transparent PNG regardless of input.

## Why this matters
`/api/og` is fully documented in the published OpenAPI spec (`apps/web/public/openapi.json`) with 5 real query parameters (`title`, `description`, `label`, `kind`, `badge`) and a summary of "Generate social preview image," and is exercised by `tests/api-contracts.test.ts`. Any API consumer calling it per its documented contract gets a static transparent pixel back no matter what they pass, with cache headers implying real per-query image generation. This is a fully-documented, tested endpoint that does nothing its own contract claims.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/routes/api/og.ts`:
```ts
export const GET = createApiHandler("og.render", async () => {
  return new Response(PNG_1X1_TRANSPARENT, {
    headers: {
      "content-type": "image/png",
      "cache-control": "public, max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400",
    },
  });
});
```
The handler never destructures `query` at all. Its route contract (`apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts:1461-1475`) declares `querySchema: ogQuerySchema`. The site's actual working OG image generator lives at `/og` (`apps/web/src/routes/og.index.ts`), whose own comment explains it: *"Lives on the crawlable /og namespace (NOT /api/og, which robots disallows)."* — `/api/og` appears to be an orphaned stub left behind after the real generator moved to `/og`.

## Desired behavior
Either:
(a) `/api/og` is wired to the same rendering logic `/og` uses (`renderOgPng`/`resolveOgQueryFields`), so it actually honors its documented query parameters, or
(b) if `/api/og` is intentionally deprecated in favor of `/og`, it's removed from `apiRouteDefinitions`/the OpenAPI contract and `tests/api-contracts.test.ts`, rather than left published and tested as if it works.

Pick whichever the maintainer confirms is the intended direction — comment on this issue with a decision before starting the PR if it's not obvious from context, since this is a scope choice (implement vs. deprecate), not a pure bug fix.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/routes/api/og.ts
- apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts (only the /api/og contract entry, if choosing to remove it)
- tests/api-contracts.test.ts (only the /api/og-related assertions)

## Out of scope
- apps/web/src/routes/og.index.ts (the real, working generator — reference implementation, do not modify unless extracting shared logic for reuse)
- Any other API route's OG/social-preview behavior

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- Either /api/og generates a real image reflecting its query parameters, or it's cleanly removed from the published contract with no dangling references.
- tests/api-contracts.test.ts accurately reflects the chosen outcome.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- If implementing: include a before/after — a sample /api/og?title=...&kind=entry re…

problems.title: fix: Raycast copyText/copyTextTruncated is validated and typed but never generated by the artifact builder
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Implement the `copyText`/`copyTextTruncated` fields that the Raycast feed validator, the shared type definitions, and the Raycast extension UI all already assume exist, but that the artifact generator never actually produces.

## Why this matters
This is a feature that's wired up end-to-end except for the one piece that matters: `scripts/validate-raycast-feed.mjs` validates `copyText`/`copyTextTruncated` fields, the Raycast extension client (`integrations/raycast/src/feed.ts`) has a fallback specifically written because the server never sends `copyText`, and `raycast-ui.tsx` renders a "Copy payload: Loaded on demand" label gated on `copyTextTruncated` — but the artifact generator that's the only source of these JSON files never sets either field, so every one of those consumers is running against a value that's permanently `undefined`.

## Current behavior
`buildRaycastEntries` (`packages/registry/src/artifacts-lib.js:898`) and `buildRaycastDetail` (`packages/registry/src/artifacts-lib.js:953`) — the only code producing `apps/web/public/data/raycast-index.json` and `raycast/<category>/<slug>.json` — never set `copyText` or `copyTextTruncated`, even though `RAYCAST_COPY_PREVIEW_LIMIT = 800` (`artifacts-lib.js:35`) already exists and is exported for exactly this purpose (currently only referenced from tests). Because `entry.copyText` is always `undefined` in real generated feeds, all four `copyText`-related checks in `scripts/validate-raycast-feed.mjs:203-211,239-258` are permanently inert (`entry.copyText !== undefined` is always false) — they have never exercised real data. Separately, `validate-raycast-feed.mjs:256` calls `detail.copyText.length` without guarding for `detail.copyText` being undefined, even though the line right above it (`:245`) explicitly allows that case — a latent `TypeError` waiting to fire the moment real data starts flowing through.

## Desired behavior
`buildRaycastEntries`/`buildRaycastDetail` generate a real `copyText` (using the existing exported `truncateText` helper + `RAYCAST_COPY_PREVIEW_LIMIT`) and set `copyTextTruncated: true` when truncation actually occurred, so the validator's existing checks start exercising real data and the Raycast extension's "load full copy text on demand" UI actually has something to load. The validator's unguarded `detail.copyText.length` access at line 256 must also be made defensive so it can't throw a raw `TypeError` instead of a clean validation failure message.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/artifacts-lib.js
- scripts/validate-raycast-feed.mjs
- focused tests: tests/artifacts-lib.test.ts, or a new fixture-based test covering copyText/copyTextTruncated generation

## Out of scope
- integrations/raycast/src/feed.ts's client-side fallback logic itself (it can stay as a defensive fallback; this issue is about making the server-side data real, not removing the client fallback)
- Any other Raycast feed field not related to copyText/copyTextTruncated
- Changing RAYCAST_COPY_PRE…

problems.title: perf(raycast): add signature-aware feed refresh
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Raycast currently fetches the full registry feed whenever it refreshes. The registry already exposes generated timestamps and changelog/signature-style artifacts, so the extension can avoid unnecessary full-feed work when nothing changed.

## Current state

- `fetchFreshFeed` requests `/data/raycast-index.json` directly and writes the full response into Raycast `Cache`.
- `loadEntryDetail` caches details by entry key/feed URL but does not know whether the feed snapshot changed.
- The web API exposes registry diff/changelog concepts separately.

## Desired behavior

- Store feed signature or generatedAt metadata with the cached feed.
- Check a lightweight manifest/diff endpoint before replacing the full feed when feasible.
- Invalidate detail cache only when the relevant snapshot changes.
- Keep manual refresh behavior clear and reliable.

## Implementation notes

- Use `registry-manifest.json`, `registry-changelog.json`, or `/api/registry/diff` depending on the smallest stable contract.
- Avoid adding hidden background work that makes Store review harder.
- Keep stale cache usable if the signature check fails.

## Acceptance criteria

- Freshness checks can determine no-change states without reparsing the full feed.
- Manual refresh still fetches current data when there are changes.
- Detail cache does not serve stale copy text after a snapshot change.
- Tests cover no-change, changed, and failed-check paths.

## Validation

- `npm test` from the Raycast extension directory
- `npm run lint` from the Raycast extension directory
- `npm run build` from the Raycast extension directory
- Add or update focused unit tests for the touched API/helper surface.
- Run the narrow relevant validation command for the changed package or route.
- Run `git diff --check` before opening a PR.

problems.title: feat: registry.updates can't filter by platform, unlike registry.search and registry.list
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Add a `platform` filter to the `registry.updates` MCP tool, matching the `platform` filter `registry.search` and `registry.list` already have.

## Why this matters
`registry.search` (`SearchRegistryInputSchema`) and `registry.list` (`ListCategoryEntriesInputSchema`) both accept a `platform` parameter to restrict results to entries compatible with a given platform/client (e.g. `claude-desktop`, `cursor`). `registry.updates` (`RecentUpdatesInputSchema`) — the "what's recently changed" discovery tool — only accepts `category`/`since`/`limit`, with no way to scope recent updates to a specific platform. An agent that only cares about, say, Claude Desktop-compatible updates has no way to ask for that directly from this tool, unlike the other two list-style tools.

## Current behavior
`packages/mcp/src/schemas-lib.js:289-310` (`RecentUpdatesInputSchema`) — fields are `category`, `since`, `limit`; no `platform`.

Compare `packages/mcp/src/schemas-lib.js:117-120` (`SearchRegistryInputSchema.platform`) and `:231-233` (`ListCategoryEntriesInputSchema.platform`).

## Desired behavior
`RecentUpdatesInputSchema` gains an optional `platform` field (same `platform` Zod primitive and description style already used by the other two schemas), and `buildDiscoveryRecentResponse`/its caller in `registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js` applies the same platform-compatibility filtering `registry.search`/`registry.list` already use, before slicing to `limit`.

## Scope
- packages/mcp/src/schemas-lib.js (`RecentUpdatesInputSchema`)
- packages/mcp/src/registry-handlers-lib.js (`buildDiscoveryRecentResponse`) and/or `registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js` (wherever `registry.updates` is dispatched) to apply the new filter
- packages/mcp/src/schemas.d.ts / registry.d.ts (if the input schema's shape needs a corresponding type update)

## Out of scope
- `registry.search`/`registry.list`'s existing platform filtering (already correct, reference implementation)
- Any other field on `RecentUpdatesInputSchema` (`category`/`since`/`limit` — already correct)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- `registry.updates` accepts an optional `platform` parameter and only returns entries compatible with it when provided.
- Omitting `platform` preserves today's behavior exactly (no regression for existing callers).

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact (MCP tool schema/response only).
- List the invariant: how platform-compatibility is determined for this tool (should match `registry.search`/`registry.list`'s existing logic, not a new one), plus a test covering a platform-filtered `registry.updates` call.

## Validation
pnpm test:mcp
pnpm build
git diff --check

problems.title: fix: MCP resources/list and resources/read lack the artifact-read error boundary tools/call already has
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Give the MCP server's `resources/list` and `resources/read` handlers the same error boundary `tools/call` already has, so a missing or corrupt registry artifact returns a clean error response instead of crashing the request.

## Why this matters
`packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js:1022-1037` (`callRegistryTool`, used by the `tools/call` handler) wraps its dispatch in a `try/catch` with a comment explaining exactly why: "Artifact reads (missing file, wrong --data-dir, corrupt JSON) throw from deep inside the handlers. Without this boundary they escape through the SDK request handler as a raw transport error." It converts that failure into a clean `unavailable` envelope. `listRegistryResources` (line 680-689) and `readRegistryResource` (line 691-) call `readJsonArtifact(...)` directly — the exact same artifact-read call the comment warns about — with no equivalent try/catch. The same failure mode the `tools/call` path was explicitly hardened against is still open on the `resources/list`/`resources/read` path.

## Current behavior
- `packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js:680-689` (`listRegistryResources`) — calls `readJsonArtifact("registry-manifest.json", options)` with no try/catch.
- `packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js:691-` (`readRegistryResource`) — the only try/catch present wraps `new URL(uri)` parsing; the `readJsonArtifact(...)` calls inside its dispatch branches (e.g. line 717) are unguarded.
- Compare `callRegistryTool` (lines 1022-1037) — the reference implementation for this exact failure mode.

## Desired behavior
`listRegistryResources` and `readRegistryResource` wrap their `readJsonArtifact(...)` calls in the same kind of boundary `callRegistryTool` uses, returning the existing `unavailable(...)` envelope (via `withPublicPolicy`) on failure instead of letting the exception escape as a raw transport error.

## Scope
- packages/mcp/src/registry-tool-orchestration-lib.js (`listRegistryResources` and `readRegistryResource` functions)

## Out of scope
- `callRegistryTool` (already correct, reference implementation)
- `packages/mcp/src/server-lib.js`'s request-handler registration (no change needed there — the fix belongs in the orchestration functions themselves, consistent with where `callRegistryTool`'s boundary lives)
- Any other MCP request handler (`ListToolsRequestSchema`, `ListPromptsRequestSchema`, etc. — not artifact-reading, not in scope)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- A missing/corrupt registry artifact during `resources/list` or `resources/read` returns the existing `unavailable` envelope instead of throwing an unhandled exception.
- Existing successful-path behavior for both functions is unchanged.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact (server-side only).
- List the invariant: what response shape callers now get on artifact-read failure for each of the two handlers, and confirm it matches the `unavailable` envelope shape `…

problems.title: fix: inferSource/presentation-lib/artifacts-lib treat the always-present self-referential githubUrl as proof of a real e
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Make every call site that checks "does this entry have an external source" exclude the always-present, self-referential `entry.githubUrl`, the way `packages/registry/src/quality-lib.js`'s `buildSourceProvenance` already correctly does — instead of naively treating `entry.repoUrl || entry.githubUrl` as proof of a real external source.

## Why this matters
`entry.githubUrl` is not the tool's own repository — `packages/registry/src/content-builder-lib.js:414` sets it unconditionally, for every single content entry, to `buildGitHubUrl(filePath, repoRoot)`: a link to that entry's own `.mdx` file inside `github.com/JSONbored/awesome-claude` (this directory's own repo). `packages/registry/src/llms-lib.js:168` labels it explicitly as `` `Directory source: ${entry.githubUrl}` ``, distinct from `` `Repository: ${entry.repoUrl}` ``. The codebase already has one place that handles this correctly — `quality-lib.js`'s `buildSourceProvenance` explicitly filters out any URL containing `github.com/JSONbored/awesome-claude` before counting something as an `externalSourceUrl`, and treats a `githubUrl`-only entry as the lowest real tier (`"local-editorial-source"`), below `repo`/`docs`/`first-party`. But several other places check `entry.repoUrl || entry.githubUrl` (or equivalent) with no such filtering — since `githubUrl` is always truthy, these checks are effectively unconditional and can never distinguish "has a real external source" from "has none."

## Current behavior
- `apps/web/src/lib/entry-normalize-lib.ts:278` (`inferSource`) — `if (entry.repoUrl || entry.githubUrl || entry.trustSignals?.sourceStatus === "available") return "source-backed";` always matches via `githubUrl`, so entries with no real repo still get classified `"source-backed"` instead of falling through to `"external"`/`"unverified"`.

problems.title: fix: resolve-pr-preview-url's GitHub API fetch has no timeout, undermining its own poll deadline
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Give `resolve-pr-preview-url.mjs`'s GitHub API fetch call a request timeout, so a hung request can't silently defeat the script's own poll/wait deadline design.

## Why this matters
`resolveFromGithubDeployments` (and the broader preview-URL resolution flow) polls the GitHub API in a loop with an explicit `deadline = Date.now() + waitSeconds * 1000` and checks `Date.now() >= deadline` between attempts. But the underlying `githubJson()` helper's `fetch()` call has no timeout or `AbortController` — if a single request to the GitHub API hangs (network stall, slow TLS handshake, GitHub having a bad day), that one `await fetch(...)` can block far longer than the script's own intended wait budget, since the deadline is only checked *between* poll attempts, not during one. In a CI context this risks the whole job running past its own designed wait window instead of failing fast.

## Current behavior
`scripts/resolve-pr-preview-url.mjs:96` (`githubJson`) — `const response = await fetch(...)` with no `signal`/timeout.

## Desired behavior
`githubJson()`'s fetch call uses an `AbortController` (or `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`) with a reasonable timeout (shorter than the overall poll deadline, so it fails fast and the poll loop can retry or exit cleanly), so a single hung request can't exceed the script's own designed wait budget.

## Scope
- scripts/resolve-pr-preview-url.mjs (the `githubJson` function, ~line 89-100)

## Out of scope
- The poll loop's own `deadline`/`waitSeconds` logic (already correct, just needs the fetch itself bounded)
- `deploymentQueries`/`resolveFromGithubDeployments`'s query-building logic (unrelated)
- Any other script's fetch calls (out of scope unless the maintainer wants this pattern applied more broadly — flag it as a comment, don't expand scope)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- `githubJson()`'s fetch call has a bounded timeout; a hung request fails within that bound instead of blocking indefinitely.
- Normal, fast GitHub API responses are unaffected.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact (CI script only).
- State the chosen timeout value and why it's shorter than the poll loop's own deadline.

## Validation
pnpm build
git diff --check

problems.title: fix: jobs Salary sort compares $210k against $120,000 on incompatible scales
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Fix the "Salary" sort on `/jobs` so it compares compensation values on the same scale, instead of comparing raw digit strings that mix thousands and full-dollar figures.

## Why this matters
Jobs list compensation as free text like `"$210k"` or `"$120,000"`. The Salary sort's value extractor pulls the leading digit run but ignores the trailing `k` multiplier, so `"$210k"` (really $210,000) sorts as the number `210`, while `"$120,000"` (also written out in full) sorts as `120000` — meaning a job paying $210,000/year sorts *below* one paying $120,000/year whenever the higher-paying listing happens to use the `"210k"` shorthand. The sort is silently wrong for exactly the mixed-format compensation strings this site actually has.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/routes/jobs.index.tsx:201-207`:
```js
const sval = (j: JobListing) => {
  if (!j.compensation) return -1;
  const m = j.compensation.match(/\$?(\d[\d,]*)k?/i);
  return m ? parseInt(m[1].replace(/,/g, ""), 10) : 0;
};
return [...filtered].sort((a, b) => sval(b) - sval(a));
```
The `k?` in the regex matches a trailing "k" but it's outside the captured group, so it's discarded — `"$210k"` and `"$210,000"` produce the same captured digits (`"210"`) despite representing values 1000x apart.

## Desired behavior
`sval` multiplies by 1000 when the string ends in `k`/`K`, so `"$210k"` sorts as `210000` and `"$120,000"` sorts as `120000` — both on the same real-dollar scale.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/routes/jobs.index.tsx (the `sval` function inside the `salary` sort branch, ~lines 201-207)

## Out of scope
- The `"newest"`/default sort modes (unaffected, already correct)
- Any change to how `compensation` is authored/stored (free text, out of scope)
- The sort dropdown UI itself

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- Sorting by Salary correctly ranks `"$210k"` above `"$120,000"`.
- Jobs with unparseable or missing compensation still sort last (unchanged fallback behavior).

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact — screenshot showing the jobs list correctly ordered by salary with a mix of `"$XXXk"` and `"$XXX,XXX"` listings, or a "No visual impact" note plus a unit test covering both formats.

## Validation
pnpm build
git diff --check

problems.title: fix: MCP package's isPublicGitHubProfileUrl mirror is missing the registry's RESERVED_OWNERS exclusion
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
`packages/mcp/src/public-url-lib.js`'s `isPublicGitHubProfileUrl` should reject GitHub product/marketing pages (`github.com/features`, `/sponsors`, `/about`, `/apps`, etc.) the same way the canonical `packages/registry/src/source-url-lib.js` version does, instead of accepting them as valid GitHub profile URLs.

## Why this matters
`packages/mcp/src/public-url-lib.js`'s own header comment says it "Mirrors the registry source-url userinfo guards without importing @heyclaude/registry, so packed tarballs stay self-contained" — it's meant to stay behaviorally in sync with `packages/registry/src/source-url-lib.js`. It has drifted: the registry version's `isPublicGitHubProfileUrl` excludes `RESERVED_OWNERS` (github.com/about, /features, /sponsors, /apps, /collections, /contact, /dashboard, /education, and more — reserved GitHub product pages, not user accounts), but the MCP package's copy has no such exclusion.

`isPublicGitHubProfileUrl` is not dead code — `packages/mcp/src/submissions-lib.js`'s `isPublicContact` calls it directly to validate a submitter's `contact` field for the MCP-driven submission-preparation tools. Concretely: submitting `https://github.com/features` as a contact URL through the MCP tools passes validation as a "public GitHub profile," while the same value would correctly fail the canonical registry-side validator used elsewhere in the submission pipeline — an inconsistency between the two entry points for the same submission data.

## Current behavior
`packages/mcp/src/public-url-lib.js` lines 34-45:
```js
export function isPublicGitHubProfileUrl(value) {
  const url = parseUrl(value);
  if (!url) return false;
  const hostname = url.hostname.replace(/^www\./i, "").toLowerCase();
  return (
    url.protocol === "https:" &&
    url.username === "" &&
    url.password === "" &&
    hostname === "github.com" &&
    url.pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean).length === 1
  );
}
```
No check against reserved single-segment paths.

Compare `packages/registry/src/source-url-lib.js` lines 142-155, which adds `!RESERVED_OWNERS.has(segments[0].toLowerCase())` (importing `RESERVED_OWNERS` from `./source-repo-lib.js`).

## Desired behavior
The MCP package's `isPublicGitHubProfileUrl` rejects the same reserved single-segment paths as the registry version. Since this file is deliberately dependency-free (no `@heyclaude/registry` import, per its own header comment), inline a local copy of the `RESERVED_OWNERS` set (or the minimal subset relevant to profile-vs-product-page disambiguation) rather than importing across packages — matching how the file already re-implements the userinfo/protocol guards locally instead of importing them.

## Scope
- `packages/mcp/src/public-url-lib.js` — `isPublicGitHubProfileUrl` only, plus a local `RESERVED_OWNERS` (or equivalently-named) constant.

problems.title: fix: embedded_secret detector misses Anthropic's own sk-ant-... and OpenAI's sk-proj-... key formats
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Make `submission-risk.js`'s `embedded_secret` detector catch real Anthropic (`sk-ant-...`) and OpenAI (`sk-proj-...`) API key formats, which it currently misses entirely.

## Why this matters
The `embedded_secret` check flags submissions that appear to contain a real secret/API token. Its `sk-` alternative is `sk-[a-z0-9]{20,}` — it requires 20+ alphanumeric characters *immediately* after `sk-`, with no hyphens allowed in that run. Real Anthropic keys (`sk-ant-api03-...`) and OpenAI keys (`sk-proj-...`) both insert a hyphenated segment right after `sk-`, which breaks the match before it can reach 20 characters. Verified empirically: `/\b(ghp_[a-z0-9_]{20,}|github_pat_[a-z0-9_]{40,}|sk-[a-z0-9]{20,}|akia[0-9a-z]{16}|xq_[a-f0-9]{40,})\b/i.test("sk-ant-api03-...")` returns `false`, and likewise for `sk-proj-...`, while a plain `sk-<alnum>` key does match. For a directory site specifically about Claude/Anthropic tooling, missing Anthropic's own key format is a notable gap in exactly the check meant to catch this class of accidental credential leak.

## Current behavior
`packages/registry/src/submission-risk.js:1204` — the `sk-` alternative in the `embedded_secret` regex is `sk-[a-z0-9]{20,}`, which cannot match `sk-ant-...` or `sk-proj-...` formatted keys.

## Desired behavior
The regex's `sk-` alternative (or an added alternative) matches real Anthropic/OpenAI key shapes, e.g. something like `sk-(?:ant-|proj-)?[a-z0-9-]{20,}` (allowing the optional hyphenated prefix and permitting hyphens within the trailing segment, since both real formats use them), while still catching the plain `sk-<alnum>` case it already handles.

## Scope
- packages/registry/src/submission-risk.js (the `embedded_secret` regex, ~line 1204)

## Out of scope
- The other alternatives in the same regex (`ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `akia`, `xq_` — already correct, not in scope unless trivially adjacent)
- Any other risk-detection pattern in this file
- Adding brand-new secret-format detectors beyond fixing the existing `sk-` alternative's known miss

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- The regex matches realistic `sk-ant-api03-...` and `sk-proj-...` strings.
- The regex still matches the plain `sk-<20+ alnum>` case and does not introduce false positives on ordinary prose containing "sk-" (spot-check a few benign strings).

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- Include the exact before/after regex test results for both key formats (a short script or test snippet is fine) in the PR description.

## Validation
pnpm exec vitest run tests/submission-risk-invariants.test.ts
pnpm build
git diff --check

problems.issue_body:
## Goal
A saved search's trust-signal filter (`signal`, e.g. "checksums" or "source-backed") should survive both when the saved search is reopened in `/browse` and when its RSS feed is generated — the same way `q`, `category`, `trust`, `source`, and `platform` already do.

## Why this matters
`/browse` has a first-class "signal" filter axis (`apps/web/src/routes/browse.tsx`, backed by `SearchFilters.signal` in `apps/web/src/data/search.ts`) for narrowing to entries with a specific trust signal (safety-notes, privacy-notes, source-backed, trusted-package, reviewed, checksums). `SavedSearch` (in `apps/web/src/lib/recents-types-lib.ts`) already has a `signal?: string` field, so it IS captured when a user saves a search with that filter active. But nothing ever reads it back:

- Reopening a saved search from the saved-search list restores every other filter but not `signal` — the user gets a broader result set than what they saved.
- The saved search's RSS feed (`/feeds/saved.xml`) drops `signal` entirely, so a subscriber who saved e.g. "MCP servers with checksums" gets fed every MCP server, checksummed or not.

This is a silent user-facing correctness bug: the app captures the filter faithfully but forgets it everywhere it's read back out.

## Current behavior
- `apps/web/src/lib/saved-search-nav-lib.ts`'s `applyToBrowseSearch(s: SavedSearch)` maps `q`, `category`, `trust`, `source`, `platform`, `sort` back onto `/browse` search params — no `signal`.

- None of the three existing test files (`tests/saved-search-nav-lib.test.ts`, `tests/saved-search-feed-url-lib.test.ts`, `tests/saved-search-query-lib.test.ts`) mention `signal` at all — confirming it was never wired in, not deliberately left out.

## Desired behavior

1. `applyToBrowseSearch` includes `signal: s.signal ?? ""`.
2. `savedFeedUrl` appends `signal` as a query param when set (and updates its docstring's field list).
3. `savedSearchQueryFromParams` parses `signal` from the URL.
4. `SavedSearchQuery` gains a `signal?: string` field, and `applySavedSearch` passes it through to `filterSearchEntries` as `signal: q.signal ?? undefined`.

problems.title: fix: /og and /og/$category/$slug have no rate limiting, unlike the identical /api/og render
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Add rate limiting to the two crawlable OG image routes (`/og` and `/og/$category/$slug`) so they can't be used to run unbounded expensive Satori PNG renders, matching the protection `/api/og` already has for the identical render work.

## Why this matters
`/api/og` is deliberately rate-limited (`"og.render"` contract: 90 req/min via `API_STRICT_RATE_LIMIT`) precisely because Satori rendering is expensive. `/og` and `/og/$category/$slug` call the exact same `renderOgPng()` renderer, but they are the routes deliberately left *crawlable* (robots disallows `/api/*`, so `/og` is the one surface social scrapers and Google actually hit) — meaning they see more real, and more spoofable, traffic than the rate-limited API twin, yet have no rate limit at all.

## Current behavior
- `apps/web/src/routes/og.index.ts` — plain `createFileRoute` `GET` handler, no rate-limit check, calls `renderOgPng()` directly with user-controlled query params (`resolveOgQueryFields`).
- `apps/web/src/routes/og.$category.$slug.ts` — same pattern, no rate-limit check, calls `renderOgPng()` per request.
- Compare: `apps/web/src/routes/api/og.ts` routes through `createApiHandler("og.render", ...)`, which enforces the `rateLimit` block defined at `apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts:1536-1541` (`scope: "og-image"`, `limit: 90`, `windowMs: 60_000`, `binding: "API_STRICT_RATE_LIMIT"`).

## Desired behavior
`/og` and `/og/$category/$slug` enforce a rate limit on the same `API_STRICT_RATE_LIMIT` Cloudflare binding (or a dedicated scope with a sane limit for crawlable/public traffic) before calling `renderOgPng()`, returning a `429` past the limit instead of rendering unconditionally. Legitimate crawler traffic (Googlebot, social-card scrapers) should not be blocked by a reasonably generous limit — this is about closing an unbounded-render surface, not throttling normal crawl traffic.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/routes/og.index.ts
- apps/web/src/routes/og.$category.$slug.ts
- apps/web/src/lib/api/contracts-lib.ts (only if a new rate-limit scope/entry is needed)

## Out of scope
- Changing `/api/og`'s existing rate limit (already correct, reference implementation)
- Any change to `renderOgPng()` itself or the Satori rendering pipeline
- Blocking or otherwise identifying crawlers by user-agent (out of scope — this issue is about a request-rate ceiling, not bot detection)

## Acceptance criteria
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- Both `/og` and `/og/$category/$slug` reject requests past a defined per-minute ceiling with a `429` response, using the existing rate-limit infrastructure (`API_STRICT_RATE_LIMIT` binding or equivalent).
- Normal single-request crawler/scraper fetches are unaffected.

## Quality evidence required in the PR
- No visual impact.
- List the exact rate-limit scope/limit/window chosen for each route and why, plus how a request past the limit is verified to return 429 (e.g. a test or a documented manual check).

fix: for.$platform hub route has no thin-content noindex/sitemap guard, unlike its own child route
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
`for.$platform.tsx` (the platform hub route) should noindex itself and be excluded from the sitemap when its platform has fewer than 2 entries, the same way its sibling routes `for.$platform.$category.tsx` and `tags.$tag.tsx` already do for thin pages.

## Why this matters
Two structurally parallel "hub" routes already implement a "thin content → `noindex` + excluded from sitemap" policy: `tags.$tag.tsx` and `for.$platform.$category.tsx` (the platform-hub's own child route) both add `{ name: "robots", content: "noindex, follow" }` when `entries.length < 2`, and `sitemap[.]xml.ts` mirrors that by only advertising tag groups via `getIndexableTagGroups()` (which filters thin ones). The platform hub itself (`for.$platform.tsx`) — the parent of the route that documents this exact policy — implements neither the noindex guard nor the sitemap filter. `PLATFORM_LABEL` includes platforms like `aider`, `zed`, and `continue` that plausibly have very few compatible entries, so a platform with 0-1 entries currently gets a fully indexed, sitemap-advertised page with no content-count safety net, unlike every other thin-content surface in the app.

## Current behavior
`apps/web/src/routes/for.$platform.tsx`, `head()` (lines ~41-70): builds meta/JSON-LD unconditionally from `entries = platformEntries(params.platform)`, with no `entries.length` check anywhere.

Compare `apps/web/src/routes/for.$platform.$category.tsx` (~lines 83-85):
```js
...(entries.length < 2 ? [{ name: "robots", content: "noindex, follow" }] : []),
```
and `apps/web/src/routes/tags.$tag.tsx` (~lines 60-62), same pattern with a comment: `// Single-entry tag pages are thin and excluded from the sitemap; keep them usable for in-page tag links but out of the index to match the sitemap policy.`

`apps/web/src/routes/sitemap[.]xml.ts` line 116 filters tags via `getIndexableTagGroups()`, but line 117 lists every platform unconditionally:
```js
...Object.keys(PLATFORM_LABEL).map((platform) => urlItem(`/for/${platform}`, "0.6")),
```

## Desired behavior
- `for.$platform.tsx`'s `head()` adds the same `entries.length < 2` noindex meta as its sibling routes.
- `sitemap[.]xml.ts`'s platform-hub URL list is filtered to platforms with 2+ entries, matching how `getIndexableTagGroups()` filters tags.

## Scope

- `apps/web/src/routes/sitemap[.]xml.ts`
- focused tests in `tests/web-platform-pages.test.ts` and/or `tests/sitemap-policy.test.ts`

## Out of scope

- Any change to what counts as an "entry" for a platform, or to `PLATFORM_LABEL` itself.

## Acceptance criteria

problems.title: fix: sitemapEntryLastModified is fully tested but unused — the real sitemap route uses a weaker inline derivation
problems.issue_body:
## Goal
Wire `sitemapEntryLastModified` into the actual sitemap route, or remove it — it's fully unit-tested but has zero real callers, and the live sitemap route reimplements a weaker inline version instead.

## Why this matters
`apps/web/src/lib/sitemap-policy-lib.ts:24-27` (`sitemapEntryLastModified`) derives an entry's sitemap `lastmod` from `entry.contentUpdatedAt || entry.repoUpdatedAt || entry.verifiedAt || entry.dateAdded` — a real content-update-aware fallback chain, and it's covered by tests (`tests/sitemap-policy.test.ts`, `tests/sitemap-policy-lib.test.ts`). But it has no callers anywhere in the app. The actual `apps/web/src/routes/sitemap[.]xml.ts` route computes `lastmod` inline instead, using `entry.reviewedAt ?? entry.dateAdded` (line ~127) — a strictly weaker derivation that ignores `contentUpdatedAt`/`repoUpdatedAt`/`verifiedAt` entirely, meaning the sitemap can report a stale `lastmod` for entries whose content or repo stats changed more recently than their `reviewedAt`/`dateAdded`.

## Current behavior
- `apps/web/src/lib/sitemap-policy-lib.ts:24-27` — `sitemapEntryLastModified`, unused, unit-tested.
- `apps/web/src/routes/sitemap[.]xml.ts:127` (inside the `urlItem` call for entries) — `entry.reviewedAt ?? entry.dateAdded`, the actual logic in production.

## Desired behavior
`sitemap[.]xml.ts` calls `sitemapEntryLastModified(entry)` instead of its own inline `entry.reviewedAt ?? entry.dateAdded`, so the sitemap's `lastmod` reflects real content-update signals, matching what the already-tested helper was built to do.

## Scope
- apps/web/src/routes/sitemap[.]xml.ts (the entry `urlItem` call, ~line 123-128)

## Out of scope
- `sitemapEntryLastModified`/`safeSitemapDate` themselves (already correct)
- Any other `urlItem` call in this route (hub pages, comparisons, etc. — different `lastmod` derivations by design, not in scope)
- `isSitemapIndexableEntry` filtering (tracked separately, unrelated)

## Acceptance criteria

problems.title: fix(d1-votes): vote sync never prunes orphaned D1 rows; verify ignores surplus keys
problems.issue_body:
### Goal

D1 vote storage (`votes_entries`, `votes_by_client`) must stay aligned with the live catalog in `content/`. After an entry is deleted or its slug changes, sync and verify must detect and remove orphan keys (or migrate votes), so community vote totals are not stranded on dead `category:slug` keys.

### Why this matters

HeyClaude keys votes as `category:slug` derived from MDX frontmatter. Maintainers rename slugs and remove entries during normal content maintenance. Today:

- `sync-votes-to-d1.mjs` only runs `INSERT OR IGNORE` for current catalog keys — it never deletes stale rows.
- `verify-d1-votes.mjs` only fails when D1 has **fewer** rows than the catalog (`totalRows < totalExpected`), not when D1 has **extra** orphan rows.

After a slug rename, votes remain on the old key; the new key starts at zero. Trending and `/api/votes/query` only read keys for live catalog entries, so accumulated community votes appear lost. Orphan `votes_by_client` rows also accumulate because `ON DELETE CASCADE` never runs unless `votes_entries` rows are deleted.

This is a must-fix **data-integrity / ops pipeline** issue. Fixing it requires coordinated changes across sync, verify, shared key enumeration, tests, and docs — not UI work.

### Current behavior

**Sync is insert-only** (`scripts/sync-votes-to-d1.mjs`):

```41:43:scripts/sync-votes-to-d1.mjs
    statements.push(
      `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO votes_entries (entry_key, upvote_count, updated_at) VALUES ('${safeKey}', 0, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);`,
    );
```

No `DELETE`, no diff, no prune mode.

**Verify checks missing rows only** (`scripts/verify-d1-votes.mjs`):

```98:105:scripts/verify-d1-votes.mjs
  if (
    result.missing.length > 0 ||
    result.negativeCounts.length > 0 ||
    result.totalRows < result.totalExpected
  ) {
    failed = true;
  }
```

There is no check for keys in D1 that are not in the catalog. When `totalRows > totalExpected`, verify exits 0.

**Runtime reads only live catalog keys** — e.g. `growth-surfaces.ts` builds keys from `getDirectoryEntries()`; orphan D1 keys are never queried.

### Desired behavior

- `pnpm sync:votes:d1` reconciles D1 to the current catalog: ensure rows exist for all live keys and **remove** (or migrate) rows for keys no longer in `content/`.
- `pnpm verify:votes:d1` fails when orphan keys exist (`totalRows !== totalExpected` or explicit orphan list).
- Shared `enumerateContentVoteKeys()` used by both scripts (today duplicated).
- Optional: `reconcileVoteKeys({ from, to })` in `apps/web/src/lib/votes.ts` for slug-rename migrations instead of blind delete.
- Vitest coverage for sync/verify pure logic (no UI).

### Scope

- `scripts/sync-votes-to-d1.mjs` — add prune/reconcile (e.g. `--prune`, default on in CI)
- `scripts/verify-d1-votes.mjs` — fail on orphan keys
- `apps/web/src/lib/votes.ts` — shared key enumeration / optional migration helper
- `tests/d1-vote-sync.test.ts` (new) and/or extend `tests/d1-dynamic-state.test.ts`
- `package.json` script docs;…

problems.issue_body:
## Goal

Make both GitHub-URL parsers accept `www.github.com` URLs so an entry whose `repoUrl` uses the `www.` host still resolves its `owner`/`repo` (and therefore its repo signals and dedup key).

## Why this matters

`https://www.github.com/owner/repo` is a valid, commonly-shared GitHub URL. Today both parsers reject it, so any content entry submitted with a `www.` repo URL silently loses its derived repo signals (stars/forks) on the website and its registry dedup key — degrading discovery quality and risking duplicate entries for the same repo.

## Current behavior

- `packages/registry/src/content-builder.js` → `parseGitHubRepo`: `if (url.hostname !== "github.com") return null;` rejects `www.github.com`.
- `apps/web/src/lib/source-repo-signals.server.ts` → `parseGitHubRepoUrl`: `if (parsed.hostname.toLowerCase() !== "github.com") return null;` rejects `www.github.com`.
- Result: a valid `www.github.com` repo URL yields `null` → no repo signals, no dedup key.

## Desired behavior

Both parsers treat `github.com` and its `www.github.com` alias as the same host and return the parsed result. No other accepted input changes — purely additive.

## Scope

- `packages/registry/src/content-builder.js` (`parseGitHubRepo`)
- `apps/web/src/lib/source-repo-signals.server.ts` (`parseGitHubRepoUrl`)
- focused tests

## Out of scope

- Changing dedup-key case semantics or owner/repo validation rules
- Generated registry artifacts (`apps/web/public/data/**`, `apps/web/src/generated/**`)
- Content imports
- CI / automation behavior
- Any unrelated parser rewrite

## Acceptance criteria

- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.
- `parseGitHubRepo` and `parseGitHubRepoUrl` return the same `owner`/`repo`/`key` for `https://www.github.com/owner/repo` as for the bare `github.com` form.
- Non-GitHub hosts and malformed paths still return `null`.
- Existing `github.com` behavior (`.git` suffix, deep paths) is unchanged.

## Quality evidence required in the PR

- `No visual impact` (parser / server-lib + tests only; no UI).

problems.title: feat: normalize "." path segments so ./ skill references are not flagged missing
problems.issue_body:
### Goal

Normalize `.` path segments in skill-package path handling so a resource reference written as `./scripts/foo.sh` resolves to the same path as `scripts/foo.sh` and is not falsely reported as missing.

### Why this matters

`validateSkillPackageFiles` validates community skill packages and blocks them when a referenced resource is missing. Authors commonly write relative links with a leading `./`; those currently fail validation even when the file is present, producing false "Referenced resource is missing" errors in a maintained intake path.

### Current behavior

In `apps/web/src/lib/skill-package-validator.ts`, `normalizePackagePath` (around lines 42–49) splits on `/` and filters falsy segments but keeps `.`. So `resolveRelativeReference("myskill/SKILL.md", "./scripts/build.sh")` returns `"myskill/./scripts/build.sh"`, which does not match the actual file path `"myskill/scripts/build.sh"` in `pathSet`, and the resource is reported missing. Verified:

- ref `"scripts/build.sh"` → `"myskill/scripts/build.sh"` (matches)
- ref `"./scripts/build.sh"` → `"myskill/./scripts/build.sh"` (does NOT match → false "missing")

### Desired behavior

`.` segments are dropped during normalization so `./scripts/build.sh` resolves to `myskill/scripts/build.sh` and matches. Plain `scripts/build.sh` is unchanged. `..` traversal continues to be treated as unsafe (it already is, via the existing `includes("..")` path check).

### Scope

- `apps/web/src/lib/skill-package-validator.ts` (`normalizePackagePath` / `resolveRelativeReference`)
- Focused tests in `tests/skill-package-validator.test.ts`

### Out of scope

- Changing the unsafe-path (`..`) rejection policy
- Reworking the reference regex or entrypoint discovery
- Generated artifacts
- CI or automation behavior

### Acceptance criteria

- A SKILL.md referencing `./scripts/build.sh` with the file present passes (no missing-resource error).
- `scripts/build.sh` (no `./`) still resolves correctly.
- `..` segments remain treated as unsafe (no traversal regression).
- PR includes `Closes #<issue>`.

### Quality evidence required in the PR

- State that the `..` unsafe-path guard is preserved.

problems.title: [Bug]: penalty label multipliers (<1) are floored to 1 and never applied
problems.issue_body:
# [Bug]: penalty label multipliers (< 1) are silently floored to 1 and never applied — over-rewards low-value PRs

## Summary

`selectLabelMultiplier` computes the per-PR label multiplier as
`Math.max(fallback || 1, ...matchedMultipliers)`. Because the neutral fallback is
always `>= 1`, any configured **penalty** label multiplier below 1 (e.g.
`refactor: 0.5`, `docs: 0.3`) is clamped back up to 1 and never applied. Only
**bonus** multipliers (`>= 1`) ever take effect. A maintainer who configures
penalty labels to dampen low-value PRs gets them silently ignored, and the
contributor's token score / merged-PR estimate is **inflated** by the dropped
penalty.

The product clearly intends sub-1 multipliers to work: the registry schema allows
any number, the upstream registry sync parses `label_multipliers` verbatim, the
ruleset treats `labelMultipliers` as first-class scoreability config — and the
codebase's own scoring fixture ships `refactor: 0.5`.

## Evidence

```ts
// src/scoring/preview.ts:736
function selectLabelMultiplier(labels: string[], multipliers: Record<string, number>, fallback: number): number {
  const normalized = new Set(labels.map((label) => label.toLowerCase()));
  return Math.max(
    fallback || 1,                                                              // floor is always >= 1
    ...Object.entries(multipliers).flatMap(([label, multiplier]) => (normalized.has(label.toLowerCase()) ? [multiplier] : [])),
  );
}
```

The result multiplies the base score:

```ts
// src/scoring/preview.ts:320 + :353
const labelMultiplier = selectLabelMultiplier(input.labels ?? [], config?.labelMultipliers ?? {}, config?.defaultLabelMultiplier ?? 1);
...
baseScore * labelMultiplier * issueMultiplier * credibilityMultiplier * reviewPenaltyMultiplier * openPrMultiplier * openIssueMultiplier * timeDecayMultiplier
```

Verified by executing the exact logic against the config `{ bug: 1.2, refactor: 0.5, docs: 0.3 }`, fallback 1:

| Labels | Intended multiplier | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `["refactor"]` | 0.5 | **1** |
| `["docs"]` | 0.3 | **1** |
| `["bug", "refactor"]` | (penalty present) | **1.2** (0.5 dropped) |
| `["bug"]` | 1.2 | 1.2 ✓ |
| `["feature"]` (no match) | 1 | 1 ✓ |

So a `refactor` PR that should score `baseScore * 0.5` instead scores
`baseScore * 1` — **2× the intended reward**; a `docs` PR at `0.3` scores **~3.3×**.

The schema imposes no lower bound (so the config is valid):

```ts
// src/openapi/schemas.ts:40
labelMultipliers: z.record(z.string(), z.number()),
```

## Reachability

Fully reachable from the public scoring surface. `labelMultipliers` is synced from
the upstream registry per repo (`src/registry/normalize.ts`, `src/upstream/ruleset.ts:573`),
and `input.labels` is caller-supplied to `buildScorePreview` via the MCP
`score_preview` tool and the score-preview/explain-breakdown routes. Any repo whose
registry config sets a penalty label multiplier gets it silently dropped on every
score preview/breakdown for a PR carryi…

problems.title: [Bug]: open-PR monitor's local isTestPath misses Python/Ruby test files (foo_test.py, bar_test.rb, baz_spec.rb), wrongly
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`missingTestsFromFiles` in `src/signals/contributor-open-pr-monitor.ts` decides whether an open PR ships tests using a **module-local** `isTestPath` helper that is a drifted, narrower copy of the canonical `isTestPath` exported from `src/signals/test-evidence.ts`. The local copy only recognizes Go's `*_test.go` convention and the dotted `.test.`/`.spec.` form; it does **not** recognize the bare `*_test.py`, `*_test.rb`, or `*_spec.rb` conventions that the canonical matcher (and the rest of the signal layer, e.g. `slop.ts`) already handle. As a result, a PR that genuinely adds Python/Ruby tests outside a `test/`/`spec/` directory is classified as having no tests, and the contributor is wrongly told to "Add or update tests".

This affects the open-PR work classification and the next-step guidance shown to contributors.

## Area

Signal logic

## Expected behavior

A PR whose changed files include a conventional Python/Ruby test file (`service_test.py`, `models/widget_test.rb`, `widget_spec.rb`) should be recognized as containing tests, so `missingTestsFromFiles` returns `false` and the PR is not classified `missing_tests`.

## Actual behavior

The local `isTestPath` (src/signals/contributor-open-pr-monitor.ts) only matches:

```ts
/(^|\/)(test|tests|spec|__tests__)\//i
/\.(test|spec)\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|py|go|rs)$/i
/(^|\/)[^/]+_test\.go$/i
```

The canonical `isTestPath` (src/signals/test-evidence.ts) additionally matches `*_test.py`, `*_test.rb`, `*_spec.rb`, and `src/test/`:

```ts
/(^|\/)[^/]+_test\.(go|py|rb)$/i
/(^|\/)[^/]+_spec\.rb$/i
/(^|\/)src\/test\//i
```

For a PR with changed files `service.py` + `service_test.py`:
- `codeFiles = [service.py, service_test.py]` (both fail the local matcher), `testFiles = []`
- `missingTestsFromFiles` returns `codeFiles.length > 0 && testFiles.length === 0` = **true** (wrong)
- Downstream, `mapPendingClassToWorkClassification` turns this into `"missing_tests"` and `buildNextStepPacket` emits "Add or update tests" guidance.

The same happens for `models/widget_test.rb` and `widget_spec.rb`.

## Reproduction

Unit-level: call the internal `missingTestsFromFiles` (exposed via `__contributorOpenPrMonitorInternals`) with `[{ path: "service.py" }, { path: "service_test.py" }]`. It returns `true` today; it should return `false`.

## Validation

The divergence is between two helpers in the same `src/signals` package. The canonical `isTestPath` is already reused by `src/signals/slop.ts`, so the maintainer-intended behavior is unambiguous; the local copy is accidental drift. Fix is to delete the local copy and import the canonical one. A regression test belongs in the existing `test/unit/contributor-open-pr-monitor.test.ts`.

## Public-safety check

- [x] I removed secrets, tokens, wallet details, private keys, local paths, and private scoring output.

problems.title: [Bug]: classifyMergeFailure treats the transient "Base branch was modified" 405 as terminal, holding a benign TOCTOU mer
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`classifyMergeFailure` in `src/services/merge-failure.ts` classifies **every** HTTP 405 from the merge mutation as terminal (`terminal: true` → the PR is immediately held for a human via `markPullRequestMergeBlocked`). But GitHub's "Merge a pull request" REST endpoint returns **405 with the message "Base branch was modified. Review and try the merge again."** when the base branch advances between the merge plan and the merge attempt — a benign TOCTOU race that succeeds on a simple retry. The file's own header comment explicitly names this exact case as the POSSIBLY-transient one that should be retried up to `MERGE_RETRY_CAP`, not held.

## Area

GitHub App

## Expected behavior

A 405 whose message is "Base branch was modified. Review and try the merge again." should be classified `terminal: false` so the executor retries it (up to `MERGE_RETRY_CAP`) against the settled base, where it typically merges cleanly. Genuine policy 405s (e.g. required reviews/checks forbidding an automated merge) should remain `terminal: true`.

## Actual behavior

`classifyMergeFailure` checks status codes before inspecting the message:

```ts
if (status === 405) return { terminal: true, reason: `merge not allowed (405 ...): ${message}` };
...
if (isMergeConflictMessage(message)) return { terminal: true, ... };
```

Because the 405 arm `return`s first, the "Base branch was modified" message is never distinguished — the first such race immediately marks the PR terminally merge-blocked and holds it for a human, instead of retrying.

This directly contradicts the file's own header comment (lines 13-15):

> A failure that matches none of these is treated as POSSIBLY transient (e.g. "Base branch was modified" — a benign TOCTOU race that a re-attempt against the new base resolves), so the executor retries it up to MERGE_RETRY_CAP before escalating.

The comment describes the intended behavior, but the code path makes it unreachable for a 405.

## Reproduction

Unit-level: `classifyMergeFailure({ status: 405, message: "Base branch was modified. Review and try the merge again." })` returns `{ terminal: true, ... }` today; it should return `{ terminal: false, ... }`. A 405 with a policy message (e.g. "Required status check ... is expected") and plain 403/409 should still be terminal.

## Validation

problems.title: [Bug]: score preview matches labelMultipliers keys exactly, but the validator matches them as fnmatch globs
problems.issue_body:
### Summary

The score preview's label-multiplier resolution matches a repo's configured `labelMultipliers` keys by **exact string equality**, but the upstream gittensor validator matches them as **`fnmatch` glob patterns**. Any repo that configures a wildcard trusted-label key (e.g. `type:*`, `kind/*`, `priority:?`) has those labels silently scored at the neutral default in the preview, so `estimatedMergedScore` diverges from the score the validator actually awards.

### Area

Signal logic

### Expected behavior

`selectLabelMultiplier` should mirror upstream `gittensor/validator/oss_contributions/label_resolution.py`, where `get_label_multiplier` matches each configured key with `fnmatch(label.lower(), pattern.lower())` and returns the highest matching multiplier. A configured key `type:*` should match a PR label `type:bug-fix`; `kind/*` should match `kind/bug`; `priority:?` should match `priority:1`. Upstream explicitly tests these patterns (`kind/*` -> `kind/bug`, `type:*` -> `type:bug-fix`, `*-dev` -> `backend-dev`, `3.*/feature` -> `3.0/feature`).

### Actual behavior

`src/scoring/preview.ts` builds a `Set` of the literal lowercase label keys and checks membership, so a wildcard key never matches any real label and the PR falls back to `defaultLabelMultiplier`. A repo with `{ "type:*": 1.5 }` and a PR labeled `type:bug-fix` is previewed at multiplier `1.0` instead of `1.5` — a 33% under-estimate of the merged-score projection (and the inverse error whenever the default is a penalty).

### Reproduction

`buildScorePreview` with `registryConfig.labelMultipliers = { "type:*": 1.5 }` and `input.labels = ["type:bug-fix"]` returns `scoreEstimate.labelMultiplier === 1` (expected `1.5`).

### Validation

A unit test drives `buildScorePreview` with wildcard (`*`, `?`, `[seq]`, `[!seq]`), unclosed-bracket, regex-metacharacter, multi-match, and literal label keys, asserting parity with upstream `fnmatch` semantics. Literal keys remain exact-match, so existing configs score identically (no regression).

### Public-safety check

- [x] I removed secrets, tokens, wallet details, private keys, local paths, and private scoring output.

problems.title: feat(scoring): model (or explicitly scope out) the issue-discovery / issue-spam dimension
problems.issue_body:

10 of 27 upstream constants are parsed/stored but **never read by any scoring logic** (model.ts:18-24): MIN_VALID_SOLVED_ISSUES, MIN_ISSUE_CREDIBILITY, MIN_TOKEN_SCORE_FOR_VALID_ISSUE, OPEN_ISSUE_SPAM_BASE_THRESHOLD, OPEN_ISSUE_SPAM_TOKEN_SCORE_PER_SLOT, MAX_OPEN_ISSUE_THRESHOLD, ISSUE_TREASURY_EMISSION_SHARE, PR_LOOKBACK_DAYS, TEST_FILE_CONTRIBUTION_WEIGHT, MIN_VALID_MERGED_PRS. These cover the **issue-discovery / issue-spam / mirror-validity** lane — gittensory ingests them but does not model their effect, so issue-lane planning/outcomes are incomplete.

## Deliverable

The issue-discovery lane (a real gittensor reward channel) is correctly scored — affects miner planning #544 and the conversion hook accuracy. Milestone M1.

problems.title: [Bug]: command-authorization lookup is case-sensitive but policy keys are normalized lowercase (over-permissioning)
problems.issue_body:
### Summary

`commandAuthorizationAllowedRoles` and the maintainer-only guard in `evaluateCommandAuthorization` look up a command name against the per-repo policy using the **raw** name, but `normalizeCommandAuthorizationPolicy` stores every command key **trimmed and lowercased**. A mixed-case or whitespace-padded command name therefore misses its restrictive override and falls through to the permissive `default` roles — and also skips the maintainer-only denial — so the authorization preview under-states the restriction (an over-permissioning report).

### Area

Auth/session

### Expected behavior

A command name should resolve to the same policy entry regardless of case/whitespace, matching how the policy keys are normalized (and how the live GitHub-webhook command parser already lowercases names). `Gate-Override` must resolve to the maintainer/collaborator-only override, not the permissive default.

### Actual behavior

`commandAuthorizationAllowedRoles(policy, "Gate-Override")` returns the default `["maintainer","collaborator","confirmed_miner"]` instead of `["maintainer","collaborator"]`, because `Object.hasOwn(commands, "Gate-Override")` is false (the stored key is `gate-override`). Likewise `MAINTAINER_ONLY_DEFAULT_COMMANDS.has("Gate-Override")` is false, so `evaluateCommandAuthorization` skips the `maintainer_command_requires_maintainer` denial. The maintainer settings preview (which trims but does not lowercase the sampled command name) thus reports a maintainer-only command as more permissive than it is.

### Reproduction

`commandAuthorizationAllowedRoles(undefined, "Gate-Override")` returns `["maintainer","collaborator","confirmed_miner"]` (expected `["maintainer","collaborator"]`).

### Validation

Unit test added asserting case/whitespace-insensitive resolution for `commandAuthorizationAllowedRoles`, `evaluateCommandAuthorization` (a PR author using a mixed-case maintainer-only command is still denied), and `commandAuthorizationNeedsMinerDetection`. Lowercase names are unaffected (existing behavior preserved).

### Public-safety check

- [x] I removed secrets, tokens, wallet details, private keys, local paths, and private scoring output.

problems.title: [Bug]: registry snapshot repoCount/totalEmissionShare double-count case-variant repo names
problems.issue_body:
### Summary

`normalizeRegistryPayload` computes `repoCount`, `totalEmissionShare`, and `repositories` directly from the raw payload entries without deduping case-variant repo names. But the persist layer (`registry/sync.ts`) collapses case-variant names ("Owner/Repo" vs "owner/repo") onto a single canonical row. So when a registry payload contains two case-variants of the same repo, the snapshot reports two repos and the summed emission share, while only one row is actually stored — the snapshot's headline totals are inflated and inconsistent with the persisted state.

### Area

Registry sync

### Expected behavior

The snapshot's `repoCount`/`totalEmissionShare`/`repositories` should dedupe case-variant names the same way persist does, so the reported totals match what lands in the database.

### Actual behavior

For a payload of `{ "Owner/Repo": { emission_share: 0.02 }, "owner/repo": { emission_share: 0.03 } }`, the snapshot reports `repoCount: 2` and `totalEmissionShare: 0.05`, while `persistRegistrySnapshot` collapses it to one row (already asserted by the existing "collapses case-variant duplicates within a single snapshot to one row" test).

### Reproduction

`normalizeRegistryPayload({ "Owner/Repo": { emission_share: 0.02 }, "owner/repo": { emission_share: 0.03 } }, ...)` returns `repoCount === 2` / `totalEmissionShare === 0.05` (expected `1` / `0.03`).

### Validation

Unit test added asserting the deduped snapshot reports one repo with the last-wins emission share, matching the single persisted row.

### Public-safety check

- [x] I removed secrets, tokens, wallet details, private keys, local paths, and private scoring output.

problems.title: feat(planning): fold upstream-inspired advisor/scan ideas into gittensory miner planning
problems.issue_body:
Inspiration from upstream gittensor issue #1460 (see #813) — **our own implementation, not a copy of any command.** Three ideas worth folding into gittensory's native miner planning:

## Deliverables
- [ ] **Severity-grouped advice** — layer a CRITICAL / WARNING / TIP / INFO taxonomy onto our existing reward-risk + decision-pack output: CRITICAL = eligibility blockers, WARNING = active penalties (open-PR spam, time-decay past midpoint, review penalty), TIP = multiplier opportunities (missing issue link, unused label multiplier, issue-discovery = 0), INFO = planning context (decay trajectory, diversification). Makes the advice scannable + action-first.
- [ ] **Explicit opportunity factors** — surface `competition_factor` (competing open PRs — reuse our collision/duplicate detection) and `freshness_factor` (issue age) as named components of the reward-risk opportunity score, alongside emission_share × label × issue multipliers we already model.
- [ ] **Eligibility-gap view** — a cross-repo 'repos within N PRs of eligibility unlock' surface, built on our scenario projections + cross-repo federation (#479). Tells a miner where a few PRs flip a repo to eligible.

## Context
src/signals/reward-risk.ts, src/services/decision-pack.ts, src/scoring/preview.ts (scenario previews). Relates #544 (miner intelligence), #479 (federation), #805 (PMF funnel — sharper advice helps onboarding).

## Outcome

problems.title: feat(mcp): expose the repo label-policy audit via gittensory_get_label_audit
problems.issue_body:
## Context

The deterministic label audit (`buildLabelAudit`, `src/signals/engine.ts`) reports whether a repo's **configured** label set (`.gittensory.yml` / dashboard) matches the **live** GitHub labels and is trustworthy for label-multiplier scoring — surfacing **missing** configured labels, **suspicious** status/source-style labels, and the overall **trusted-label-pipeline readiness**.

## Proposal

- No new REST route, migration, or auth-policy change — purely additive to the MCP surface (reuses `requireRepoAccess`).
- Output is the same public-safe audit already served in the repo-intelligence response.

## Value

Maintainers of owned repos can verify — from an agent/CLI, not just the dashboard — that their label pipeline is correctly configured and trustworthy for label-multiplier scoring, catching missing/suspicious labels before they distort contributor scoring.
