problems.title: fix(health): reliability badge weights latency mean by total probes, not healthy readings
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`loadReliabilityAggregate` in [`src/health-serving.mjs`](src/health-serving.mjs#L1014) — the live D1 loader behind the **public reliability badge** — computes the window latency mean by weighting each day's `avg_latency_ms` by the day's **total probe count (`samples`)** instead of the day's **healthy-reading count (`latency_samples`)**.

Because `surface_uptime_daily.avg_latency_ms` is a *success-only* mean (it averages latency over healthy probes only), re-aggregating those daily means must weight by `latency_samples`. Every other re-aggregation path in the codebase already does this; `loadReliabilityAggregate` is the one place still on the old, incorrect weighting. The result is an **inflated average latency** that silently docks the public badge score (and can drop a letter grade), with the error growing in proportion to how much downtime a subnet had.

This is a leftover oversight from #1331 ("success-only latency with tail percentiles and sample counts"), which introduced the correct healthy-weighted helper and fixed the sibling call sites but did not update this hand-rolled query.

## Where

[`src/health-serving.mjs:1036-1041`](src/health-serving.mjs#L1036-L1041), inside `loadReliabilityAggregate`:

```sql
CASE
  WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN avg_latency_ms IS NOT NULL THEN samples ELSE 0 END) > 0
    THEN SUM(CASE WHEN avg_latency_ms IS NOT NULL THEN avg_latency_ms * samples ELSE 0 END) /
         SUM(CASE WHEN avg_latency_ms IS NOT NULL THEN samples ELSE 0 END)
  ELSE NULL
END AS avg_latency_ms
```

The weight here is `samples` — total probes for the day, **including failed ones**.

## Why it's wrong

`surface_uptime_daily.avg_latency_ms` is written by the daily rollup as a healthy-only mean, and `surface_uptime_daily.latency_samples` records exactly how many healthy probes backed that mean (migration `0007_latency_percentiles.sql`). The canonical re-aggregation helper weights by that count, falling back to total samples only for legacy rows that predate the column:

[`src/health-sql.mjs:68-76`](src/health-sql.mjs#L68-L76) — `dailyLatencyColumns()`:

```js
const weight = `CASE WHEN avg_latency_ms IS NOT NULL THEN COALESCE(latency_samples, samples) ELSE 0 END`;
const denom  = `SUM(${weight})`;
const mean   = `SUM(CASE WHEN avg_latency_ms IS NOT NULL THEN avg_latency_ms * COALESCE(latency_samples, samples) ELSE 0 END) / ${denom}`;
```

The JS aggregator does the same — [`src/reliability.mjs:81-95`](src/reliability.mjs#L81-L95) weights `latency * latencyCount` where `latencyCount = row.latency_samples ?? samples`. And `loadSubnetReliability` (the per-subnet `/uptime` path) already routes through `dailyLatencyColumns()` + `computeReliability` ([`src/health-serving.mjs:991`](src/health-serving.mjs#L991)).

So for the **same subnet and window**, the per-surface `/uptime` reliability and the badge score are computed from two different latency means — and only the badge's is wrong.

## Concrete reproduction

Two days for one surface, both with 9…

problems.title: fix(mcp): find_subnet_for_task drops callable subnets — filters callability after truncating the rank pool
fix(scripts): README netuid affinity matches a netuid as the prefix of a longer number
problems.issue_body:
### Component

scripts / registry curation (README discovery)

### Description

`hasNetuidAffinity` in `scripts/lib.mjs` decides whether a README link "belongs to" a given subnet. After two correct boundary-aware regexes, it falls back to an **unbounded substring** check:

```js
const compactValue = compactReadmeValue(value);   // strips ALL non-alphanumerics
return (
  compactValue.includes(`sn${netuid}`) ||
  compactValue.includes(`subnet${netuid}`) ||
  compactValue.includes(`subnets${netuid}`)
);
```

Because `compactReadmeValue` removes every separator and the check is a bare `includes()`, a **short netuid matches as the prefix of a longer number**. For netuid `1`, `compactValue.includes("sn1")` is true for `sn123`, `subnets1000`, etc. The boundary-aware regexes just above (`(^|[^a-z0-9])sn[-_ ]?1([^a-z0-9]|$)`) correctly reject `sn123` for netuid 1 — but this compact fallback then matches it anyway.

#### Where

`scripts/lib.mjs`, `hasNetuidAffinity` (the compact fallback after the two regex patterns). Reached via `isReviewableReadmeLink` → `hasReadmeProjectAffinity` → `hasNetuidAffinity`, called by `selectReviewableReadmeLinks` in `scripts/discover-candidates.mjs`.

#### Concrete trigger

A source repo for **subnet 1** whose README contains an unrelated link such as `https://vendor-portal.example/sn123` (a reference to subnet 123). `isReviewableReadmeLink(link, { netuid: 1, repo })`:

- regex paths: no match (the digit `2` follows `1`).
- compact fallback: `"…sn123…".includes("sn1")` → **true**.

So the unrelated link passes the affinity gate and is emitted as a candidate **for subnet 1**.

#### Why it matters

Wrong-subnet README links get written into `registry/candidates/generated/public-sources.json` — the served candidate bundle. **Low netuids (1, 2, 3 …) are the most exposed**, because almost any `sn1xx` / `subnets1xxx` path in any project README is slurped in and mis-attributed. This pollutes the candidate/review queue with wrong-subnet evidence.

#### Proposed fix

Keep the compact fallback (it legitimately catches netuid references separated by characters the regexes don't list, e.g. `sn.1`, `sn:1`), but bound its **trailing** edge so the netuid isn't matched as the prefix of a longer number. The leading edge can't be enforced on the compacted value (compaction strips the separators that would delimit it — `example.com/sn1` → `examplecomsn1`), so guard only the digit boundary after the netuid:

```js
const compactValue = compactReadmeValue(value);
return new RegExp(`(sn|subnets?)${escaped}(?![0-9])`).test(compactValue);
```

(`escaped` is the already-computed regex-escaped netuid.) Add a regression test asserting netuid 1 does not match `sn123` while still matching `sn1`.

### Reproduction / evidence

`isReviewableReadmeLink({ classification: { kind: "docs" }, url: "https://vendor-portal.example/sn123" }, { netuid: 1, repo: { owner: "acme", repo: "widget" } })` returns `true` today; it should return `false` (it is a subnet-123 ref…

problems.title: fix(graphql): depth/complexity limits are bypassed by named fragments
problems.issue_body:
### Component

workers / GraphQL API (`src/graphql.mjs`)

### Description

The GraphQL endpoint enforces two DoS guards — `maxDepthRule(GRAPHQL_MAX_DEPTH=7)` and `maxComplexityRule(GRAPHQL_MAX_COMPLEXITY=50)` — but both are **fully bypassed by named fragments**. `selectionDepth` and `selectionComplexity` only recurse into `sel.selectionSet`; a `FragmentSpread` node has no `selectionSet`, so the traversal never follows it. A client can move the entire expensive selection into a fragment, and the operation's own selection set is then a single transparent spread:

```graphql
query { ...Big }
fragment Big on Query { t0: __typename t1: __typename  ...  t999: __typename }
```

- **Complexity** counted: `1` (just `...Big`), regardless of how many fields `Big` contains → the limit of 50 is defeated entirely.
- **Depth**: nesting hidden inside a fragment counts as `0` from the operation's perspective.

#### Where

`src/graphql.mjs` — `selectionComplexity` (counts `count += 1` per selection, recurses only into `sel.selectionSet`) and `selectionDepth` (same), invoked by `maxComplexityRule` / `maxDepthRule` over each `OperationDefinition`. Neither follows `FragmentSpread`.

#### Trigger / impact

This is a **public, unauthenticated** endpoint (`POST /api/v1/graphql`, CORS `*`). An attacker wraps an arbitrarily large/aliased selection in a fragment; the validator scores it at complexity 1 / depth 0 and lets it through to `execute()`, which fans out the real work (R2 artifact reads per resolver). The complexity guard — the primary protection against amplification on this endpoint — provides no protection at all in its current form. (The depth guard is less exploitable because the schema is shallow, but it is equally blind to fragments.)

#### Reproduction

A query whose fields live in a fragment (`query { ...Big } fragment Big on Query { t0: __typename … t50: __typename }`, 51 fields) returns `200 OK` today; it should be rejected with `COMPLEXITY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

#### Proposed fix

Follow named fragment spreads when computing depth/complexity: build a name→`FragmentDefinition` map from the document and, on a `FragmentSpread`, recurse into the referenced fragment's selection set (transparently — a spread adds no depth level, and its fields are counted at the spread site). Guard against fragment cycles with a `visited` set so the rules can't recurse infinitely (validate() reports cycles but our custom rules run in the same pass).

### Public-safety confirmation

This report does not include secrets, credentialed flows, private dashboards, or validator-sensitive data.

problems.title: fix(api): error responses are publicly cacheable — stale 404s and transient 5xx get cached at the edge
problems.issue_body:
### Component

workers / HTTP response layer (`workers/http.mjs`)

### Description

The canonical error envelope `errorResponse` builds its headers with `apiHeaders("short")`, which sets `cache-control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300`, and never overrides it. So **every** error response — `400`, `404`, `500`, `503`, `504` — is publicly cacheable for 60s with a 300s stale-while-revalidate window.

This contradicts the rest of the codebase, where dynamic and error responses are explicitly `no-store`:

- `dataResponse` (`workers/responses.mjs`) → `cache-control: no-store`
- og-image total-failure `503` (`tests/og-image.test.mjs`) → `no-store`
- webhook responses (`tests/webhooks-worker.test.mjs`) → `no-store`

#### Where

`workers/http.mjs`, `errorResponse`: `const headers = apiHeaders("short")` with no cache-control override. `CACHE_SECONDS.short = 60`.

#### Why it matters

A shared/edge cache (Cloudflare) stores the error and serves it to all clients for up to ~60s + 300s SWR:

- A transient `504`/`503` (e.g. an R2 timeout) becomes a multi-minute outage at the edge — a one-off blip is amplified into sustained downtime.
- A `404` for a subnet/surface that is published moments later is served stale, so newly-available resources appear missing until the cache expires.

#### Reproduction

`errorResponse("subnet_not_found", "…", 404)` returns `cache-control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300`. It should be `no-store`.

#### Proposed fix

Override caching in `errorResponse` so errors are never stored by shared caches, mirroring `dataResponse`:

```js
const headers = apiHeaders("short");
headers.set("cache-control", "no-store");
headers.set("x-metagraph-cache-profile", "no-store");
```

Add a regression test asserting `errorResponse` is `no-store` across 4xx and 5xx.

### Public-safety confirmation

This report does not include secrets, credentialed flows, private dashboards, or validator-sensitive data.

problems.title: GraphQL depth/complexity over-count inline fragments (reject valid queries)
problems.issue_body:
### Summary

The GraphQL `maxDepthRule` / `maxComplexityRule` (`src/graphql.mjs`) follow named fragment spreads **transparently** (so a spread can't bypass the limits — #1403), but they do **not** treat **inline fragments** (`... on Type { … }`, or a bare `... @include(if:) { … }`) the same way. An inline fragment falls into the generic field branch and is counted as an extra nesting level (depth +1) and an extra field (complexity +1). A query measures **larger** than its semantically-identical inlined or named-fragment form and is wrongly rejected.

### Where

- `src/graphql.mjs` — `selectionComplexity()` (the `count += 1; if (sel.selectionSet)` path catches `InlineFragment`).
- `src/graphql.mjs` — `selectionDepth()` (the `else if (sel.selectionSet)` path catches `InlineFragment` and recurses with `depth + 1`).

Named spreads are handled transparently; inline fragments are not — an inconsistency, since both are just groupings, not fields.

### Reproduction (complexity, limit = 50)

```
POST /api/v1/graphql
# 50 aliased scalar fields — complexity 50, exactly at the limit
{ "query": "query { a0: __typename a1: __typename … a49: __typename } }"
# -> 200 OK

# the SAME 50 fields wrapped in a no-op type condition
{ "query": "query { ... on Query { a0: __typename … a49: __typename } } " }
# -> 400  "Query complexity 51 exceeds the limit of 50."
```

The inline fragment adds 1, so a valid query identical to its inlined form is rejected. The equivalent named-fragment form (`query { ...F } fragment F on Query { …50 fields }`) is correctly counted as 50 — proving the inconsistency.

`selectionDepth` has the same over-count (an inline fragment adds a depth level); it's only masked today because this schema's deepest valid query is shallow, but the rule is still wrong and would mis-reject under a deeper schema.

### Expected

Inline fragments are transparent for both depth and complexity, exactly like named fragment spreads: count the contained fields, not the type condition itself.

problems.title: fix(feeds): clamp() splits a surrogate pair, producing malformed RSS/Atom XML
fix(api): per-subnet /health/trends accepts unsupported query params (200 instead of 400)
problems.issue_body:
### Component

workers / analytics API (`workers/api.mjs`)

### Description

`handleHealthTrends` (the per-subnet `/api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/health/trends` route) takes no `url` argument and never calls `validateQueryParams`, so it returns **200** for any unsupported query param. Every sibling analytics route returns **400 `invalid_query`** instead:

- `handleHealthPercentiles`, `handleHealthIncidents`, `handleUptime`, `handleTrajectory` all `validateQueryParams(...)` and `return analyticsQueryError(...)`.
- Even the **bulk** `/api/v1/health/trends` route (`handleBulkHealthTrends`) rejects stray params.

Only the per-subnet trends route is missing the guard.

#### Where

`workers/api.mjs` — dispatch `return handleHealthTrends(request, env, Number(trendsMatch[1]));` (no `url` passed) and `async function handleHealthTrends(request, env, netuid)` (no validation).

#### Concrete trigger

- `GET /api/v1/subnets/7/health/trends?bogus=x` → **200** (BUG; the param is silently ignored)
- `GET /api/v1/subnets/7/health/percentiles?bogus=x` → 400
- `GET /api/v1/subnets/7/trajectory?x=random` → 400
- `GET /api/v1/health/trends?bogus=x` (bulk) → 400

#### Impact

Inconsistent API contract: a client with a typo'd or unsupported param on this one route gets a silent 200 (and the param ignored) instead of the loud 400 the rest of the analytics surface guarantees. The route takes no params (it always returns all configured windows), so any param is unsupported.

#### Proposed fix

Thread the resolved `url` into the handler and validate against an empty allow-list, mirroring the bulk route:

```js
return handleHealthTrends(request, env, Number(trendsMatch[1]), resolved.url);
// ...
async function handleHealthTrends(request, env, netuid, url) {
  const validationError = validateQueryParams(url, []);
  if (validationError) return analyticsQueryError(validationError);
  ...
```

Add the route to the analytics non-canonical-query rejection test (`?bogus=x` → 400 `invalid_query`).

### Public-safety confirmation

This report does not include secrets, credentialed flows, private dashboards, or validator-sensitive data.

problems.title: fix(feeds): coverage-delta item renders undefined for a partial delta
fix(api): event ingest reports validated rows as inserted (ignores INSERT OR IGNORE dedup)
vectorId measures UTF-16 length, not the documented 64-byte cap (multi-byte ids exceed Vectorize limit)
parseBlockNumber returns NaN for malformed numeric headers instead of null
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
`parseBlockNumber()` in `src/health-probe-core.mjs` is documented and unit-tested to return either a numeric block height or `null` for any unusable input. Its own tests assert `null` for non-string/non-number `number` fields and for the bare string `"nope"`. But for a *string* `number` that fails to parse - the bare hex prefix `"0x"`, a malformed hex like `"0xZZ"`, or an empty string - it returns `NaN` instead of `null`. The plain-number branch likewise passes a `NaN`/non-integer `number` straight through.

## Location
`src/health-probe-core.mjs`, lines 696-700:

```js
if (typeof value === "string") {
  return value.startsWith("0x")
    ? Number.parseInt(value, 16)
    : Number.parseInt(value, 10);
}
```

## Why it's wrong
`Number.parseInt("0x", 16) === NaN` and `Number.parseInt("0xZZ", 16) === NaN`. An RPC node whose `chain_getHeader` result carries `number: "0x"` (or any unparseable string) therefore yields `latest_block: NaN` out of `summarizeRpcProbe`. `NaN` defeats the `??` fallbacks downstream - e.g. `live.latest_block ?? endpoint.latest_block ?? null` in `overlayRpcPoolEligibility` keeps the `NaN`, since `NaN` is neither `null` nor `undefined` - so the value relies entirely on `safeRpcBlockNumber()` scrubbing it later. The parser itself silently breaks its number-or-null contract.

## Expected
Return `null` for any value that does not parse to a real (finite, non-negative integer) block number, consistent with the function's existing tests and its other branches.

## Repro
```js
parseBlockNumber({ number: "0x" })    // => NaN  (expected: null)
parseBlockNumber({ number: "0xZZ" })  // => NaN  (expected: null)
parseBlockNumber({ number: NaN })     // => NaN  (expected: null)
```

problems.title: GraphQL paginate clamps limit:0 (and negatives) up to 1 instead of the default page (inconsistent with clampLimit)
problems.issue_body:
### What

The GraphQL list resolvers (`subnets`, `providers`) clamp the page size with:

```js
// src/graphql.mjs
function paginate(items, limit, cursor, keyFn) {
  const safeLimit = Math.min(Math.max(1, limit ?? 20), 100);
```

`Math.max(1, limit)` clamps an explicit `limit: 0` (or any negative) **up to 1**, so the query returns a single item instead of the default page.

### Why it is wrong

The codebase already established the opposite convention and documents exactly why. From `src/mcp-server.mjs` `clampLimit`:

> A missing/blank/<1 limit falls back to the default — it must NOT clamp UP to 1. `Math.max(1, …)` would return a single result, which reads to an agent as "this registry knows one subnet" (see the same fix in `src/ai-search.mjs`).

The GraphQL layer is an agent-facing read API with the same failure mode, but it still uses the `Math.max(1, …)` anti-pattern that `clampLimit` / `ai-search` were fixed to avoid.

### Repro

```graphql
{ subnets(limit: 0) { items { netuid } total } }
```
With 3 subnets in the artifact, `items` has length **1** (wrong). `limit: -5` likewise returns 1.

### Expected

A non-finite / `< 1` limit falls back to the default page size (20), consistent with `clampLimit` and `ai-search`. A valid limit is still upper-clamped to 100.

problems.title: internal-ingest body-size guards measure UTF-16 code units, not the documented byte cap
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
Three internal-ingest handlers in `workers/api.mjs` enforce their request-body size cap with `raw.length`, which counts UTF-16 code units, even though the caps (and the 413 error message) are defined in **bytes**. For any non-ASCII body the UTF-8 byte length exceeds the UTF-16 code-unit count, so the guard silently admits bodies larger than the intended byte ceiling.

## Locations
`workers/api.mjs`:
- line 649: `if (raw.length > MAX_EVENTS_INGEST_BODY_BYTES)` (events ingest, cap 262144)
- line 737: `if (raw.length > MAX_BACKFILL_INGEST_BODY_BYTES)` (history backfill, cap 1048576)
- line 825: `if (raw.length > MAX_BACKFILL_INGEST_BODY_BYTES)` (history backfill, cap 1048576)

```js
const raw = await request.text();
if (raw.length > MAX_EVENTS_INGEST_BODY_BYTES) {
  return errorResponse("payload_too_large", `Body exceeds ${MAX_EVENTS_INGEST_BODY_BYTES} bytes.`, 413);
}
```

## Why it is wrong
`raw` is a JS string, so `raw.length` is the UTF-16 code-unit count, not bytes. A 3-byte UTF-8 character counts as 1 code unit; a 4-byte astral character counts as 2. A body of 262,144 three-byte characters has `raw.length` ~262144 (passes) but is ~786,432 bytes, about 3x the cap the guard exists to enforce before parsing/buffering.

This is the file own outlier: every other size guard counts bytes correctly via the in-file `utf8Bytes` helper (line 349, `new TextEncoder().encode(value)`) -- e.g. the staged-neuron string guard at line 390 (`utf8Bytes(value).length > MAX_STAGED_NEURON_STRING_BYTES`) and the byte-accurate `readBoundedRequestText` used by `/api/v1/ask`.

## Expected
Measure the body in UTF-8 bytes so the cap matches its name and message:

```js
if (utf8Bytes(raw).length > MAX_EVENTS_INGEST_BODY_BYTES) { ... }
```

applied at all three sites.

problems.title: degraded /health 503 is edge-cacheable (public, max-age=60) — a recovered service keeps reporting 503 for ~6 min
problems.issue_body:
### What

`handleHealthRequest` (workers/api.mjs) returns the degraded branch as HTTP **503** but with `apiHeaders("short")`:

```
cache-control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300
```

### Why it is wrong

A 503 that carries explicit freshness is **cacheable per RFC 7234** (a stored response with an explicit `max-age` is reusable regardless of status). So a shared/edge cache (or a browser/proxy) can keep serving the degraded `503` for up to `max-age + stale-while-revalidate` (~6 min) after the underlying data has already recovered — pinning a transient blip into a multi-minute outage for every health consumer behind that cache.

This is exactly the failure `errorResponse` (workers/http.mjs) already guards against, with a documented comment:

> Errors must never be cached by shared/edge caches: a transient 5xx ... would otherwise be served stale for up to max-age + stale-while-revalidate, turning a blip into a multi-minute edge outage.

`/health` degraded is precisely such a transient 5xx, but it skips that guard.

### Fix

Set `cache-control: no-store` on the degraded (stale → 503) branch, mirroring `errorResponse`. Keep the healthy 200 path on the short edge-cache profile for load relief.

### Repro

Stale latest pointer -> GET /api/v1/health -> 503 with `cache-control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` (should be `no-store`).

problems.title: integration-snippets drops ALL snippets for a query-auth surface when the credential value has a space (default "Bearer
problems.issue_body:
### What

`generateServiceSnippets` interpolates a **query**-location credential straight into the URL without URL-encoding:

```js
// src/integration-snippets.mjs
const requestUrl =
  auth?.location === "query"
    ? `${url}${url.includes("?") ? "&" : "?"}${auth.name}=${auth.value}`
    : url;
if (!isSnippetSafeUrl(requestUrl)) return null;
```

`authFromDetail` deliberately allows spaces in `name`/`value` (it only rejects `['"`\n\\` so a placeholder can't break snippet quoting). That is fine for the **header** branch, but for the query branch the raw value lands in the URL — and `isSnippetSafeUrl` rejects any URL containing whitespace (`/['"`\\\s]/`). So the whole function bails to `return null` and the surface gets **zero** integration snippets.

### Why it is wrong

A space (or other URL-reserved char) in a query credential is normal, not a quoting hazard:

- The built-in default for a `{ scheme: "bearer", location: "query" }` auth resolves `value` to `"Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"` — the space alone trips the guard.
- A curated/spec `value_format` like `"<your api key>"` (a perfectly valid human-readable placeholder) does the same.

The file's stated philosophy (and its existing "unsafe placeholder → fall back to a plain GET, never injected" test) is that a problematic credential should **degrade gracefully**, not nuke the entire snippet set. Here a whole class of valid query-auth surfaces silently produces no curl/python/typescript snippets in the agent-catalog. Values with `+`/`&` would also corrupt the query string rather than be escaped.

### Repro

```js
generateServiceSnippets({
  base_url: "https://api.example.com/v1",
  auth_required: true,
  auth: { scheme: "api-key", location: "query", name: "api_key", value_format: "<your api key>" },
});
// → null  (no snippets at all)
```

Same `null` result for `{ scheme: "bearer", location: "query" }` (default value `"Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"`).

### Expected

The query credential is percent-encoded (`encodeURIComponent` on `name` and `value`) so the URL is well-formed and passes `isSnippetSafeUrl`, yielding a usable snippet, e.g.:

```
curl -sS 'https://api.example.com/v1?api_key=%3Cyour%20api%20key%3E'
```

Safe values such as `YOUR_API_KEY` / `api_key` are unchanged by encoding, so existing snippets are unaffected. The header branch keeps its current quote/backtick/backslash guard.

problems.title: feat(mcp): let list_subnets sort by readiness/netuid/name
problems.issue_body:
### Problem

The `list_subnets` MCP tool filters and paginates in raw registry source order. An agent that wants "the most integration-ready subnets" — the most common discovery need — has to pull every page and sort client-side.

### Proposal

Add two optional, backward-compatible args:

- `sort`: `netuid` | `integration_readiness` | `surface_count` | `name`
- `order`: `asc` | `desc` (default `asc`)

Order the (filtered) list before paging. Unscored subnets sort last regardless of direction; ties break by netuid for a stable page; the response echoes the applied `sort`/`order`. Additive MCP tool-surface change → minor server-version bump.

problems.title: feat(api): numeric range filters (min_/max_) on list endpoints
problems.issue_body:
### Problem

The list-query engine (`workers/list-query.mjs`) supports exact-equality, CSV-membership, and array-membership filters, plus sort and `q` search — but **no numeric range filtering**. Yet the collections sort by many numeric fields (`surface_count`, `candidate_count`, `participant_count`, `tempo`, …), so an agent or dashboard can *order* by them but can't *filter* by them. The MCP `list_subnets` tool even hand-rolls a one-off `min_readiness` because the generic capability is missing.

There's no way to ask, over REST:
- "subnets with at least 5 callable surfaces" (`?min_surface_count=5`)
- "subnets within a tempo band" (`?min_tempo=100&max_tempo=360`)

### Proposal

Add a generic, declarative **numeric range filter** to the list-query engine: a collection lists the numeric fields that support ranges, and each field `F` then accepts inclusive `min_F` / `max_F` query params (`row[F] >= n` / `row[F] <= n`). Wire it to the `subnets` collection first (`surface_count`, `probed_surface_count`, `candidate_count`, `participant_count`, `mechanism_count`, `tempo`, `block`); the mechanism is collection-agnostic and reusable.

Backward-compatible, auto-documented in OpenAPI (params generated from the collection config like the existing filters), validated (non-numeric bound → a query error), and a row whose field is absent/non-numeric is excluded once a bound on that field is set.

problems.title: fetch-events lag alert fires every run when EVENTS_WINDOW >= EVENTS_PRUNE_HORIZON (threshold goes <= 0)
problems.issue_body:
### What

`_emit_lag_alert` in `scripts/fetch-events.py` decides whether to warn (and POST to `METAGRAPH_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`) that the chain-event poller is falling behind:

```python
lag = head_bn - cursor
if lag < PRUNE_HORIZON - WINDOW:
    return
# ... emit ::warning:: + webhook ...
```

`WINDOW` (`EVENTS_WINDOW`, default 256) and `PRUNE_HORIZON` (`EVENTS_PRUNE_HORIZON`, default 300) are independent env-configurable knobs.

### Why it is wrong

The threshold `PRUNE_HORIZON - WINDOW` is used unclamped. If an operator sets `EVENTS_WINDOW >= EVENTS_PRUNE_HORIZON` (e.g. `WINDOW=300`), the threshold becomes `0` (or negative), so `lag < 0` is never true → the guard never returns → the alert fires on **every run, even at lag 0**, including a real webhook POST. That is precisely the configuration where the overlap window already covers the entire prune horizon, so blocks can never age out unseen and there is *nothing to alert about* — the opposite of the intended behavior.

### Repro

```
EVENTS_WINDOW=300 EVENTS_PRUNE_HORIZON=300   # window covers the whole horizon
# poller perfectly caught up (lag 0) → still emits a "poller lagging" warning + webhook every run
```

### Expected

When `PRUNE_HORIZON - WINDOW <= 0` the overlap fully covers the horizon, so never alert. Otherwise alert only when `lag >= PRUNE_HORIZON - WINDOW`. (Note a bare `max(0, …)` clamp is insufficient — it would still fire at lag 0; the `<= 0` case must short-circuit to no-alert.)

problems.title: readme-links registrableDomain over-collapses multi-label public suffixes (drops distinct tenant links in dedupe)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
`registrableDomain` in `scripts/lib/readme-links.mjs` computes the registrable domain as the last two labels (`parts.slice(-2)`). Under a multi-label public suffix that is wrong: every subdomain collapses to the bare suffix, so `readmeDedupeKey` treats two genuinely distinct sites as the same and `selectReviewableReadmeLinks` drops the second.

## Trigger
A subnet README links to two distinct tenants on the same multi-tenant host (or two distinct second-level ccTLD domains), same link kind:

- `https://exampleproject-a.pages.dev` and `https://exampleproject-b.pages.dev`
- `https://foo.co.uk` and `https://bar.co.uk`

Both reduce to `pages.dev` / `co.uk`, so the dedupe key `kind:pages.dev` matches and the second link is discarded even though the per-kind cap (e.g. `subnet-api`: 2) would have allowed it. A distinct, reviewable candidate link is silently lost during discovery.

## Location
`scripts/lib/readme-links.mjs`:

```js
function registrableDomain(hostname) {
  const parts = normalizeHost(hostname).split(".").filter(Boolean);
  return parts.slice(-2).join(".");
}
```

## Expected
When the last two labels form a known multi-label public suffix (multi-tenant platform host like `pages.dev`/`github.io`/`vercel.app`, or a second-level ccTLD like `co.uk`), the registrable unit is the last three labels, so distinct tenants stay distinct. Plain-TLD subdomains (e.g. `docs.foo.com` vs `api.foo.com`) should still collapse to one site as today. This mirrors the suffix handling already in `scripts/lib.mjs` (`MULTI_TENANT_HOST_SUFFIXES` + `CLUSTER_CCTLD_SUFFIXES`).

problems.title: neuron_daily archive+prune sample Date.now() independently — a day-boundary cron tick can delete an un-archived day
problems.issue_body:
### What

The `NEURON_HISTORY_ROLLUP_CRON` branch of `handleScheduled` (workers/api.mjs) runs the daily neuron_daily archive-before-prune:

```js
const archivedPrunable = await archivePrunableNeuronDaily(env).catch(() => ({ archived: false }));
const pruned = archived.archived && archivedPrunable.archived
  ? await pruneNeuronDaily(env).catch(() => ({ pruned: false }))
  : { pruned: false, reason: "archive-not-confirmed" };
```

### Why it is wrong

`archivePrunableNeuronDaily` and `pruneNeuronDaily` each default `now = Date.now()` internally and derive their retention cutoff via `neuronDailyRetentionCutoff(now)` = `new Date(now - 400*86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0,10)`, used with `snapshot_date < cutoff`. They are called WITHOUT a shared `now`, so each samples `Date.now()` at its own call time.

The backlog archive does ~33k-row R2 work (one gzip put per subnet per prunable day) and can run for seconds. If that work straddles a UTC midnight, `pruneNeuronDaily`'s `Date.now()` lands on the next day, so its cutoff is **one day larger** than the archive's. The prune then deletes a `snapshot_date` from D1 that was never written to R2 — the exact archive-before-prune data-loss gap the code's own docstring says it closes ("a day is never dropped from D1 before it exists in R2").

### Repro

- Archive runs `2026-06-21T23:59:59.7Z` → cutoff `2025-05-08`, archives days `< 2025-05-08`.
- R2 puts take ~1s; prune runs `2026-06-22T00:00:00.3Z` → cutoff `2025-05-09`, deletes days `< 2025-05-09`.
- Day `2025-05-08` is deleted from D1 although the archive never wrote it to R2 → permanent loss of one day of neuron_daily history.

### Expected

Compute `now` once in `handleScheduled` and pass `{ now }` to both `archivePrunableNeuronDaily` and `pruneNeuronDaily` (both already accept it), so they share one retention cutoff and the prune can only delete days the archive confirmed.

problems.title: Non-BMP string handling: embedding-input truncation splits surrogate pairs; badge under-sizes wide glyphs
problems.issue_body:
Two small, related correctness gaps in serve-time string handling for non-BMP (astral) characters. Both are follow-ups to already-merged code-point/byte-safety work.

### 1. `src/ai-search.mjs` — `embeddingText` truncates by UTF-16 units
`embeddingText` caps the embedding input with `.slice(0, 1500)`, counting UTF-16 code units. A non-BMP character (e.g. an emoji in a subnet title) straddling index 1500 is severed into a lone high surrogate, leaving a string that is **not well-formed UTF-16**. When UTF-8-encoded for the embedding model, the trailing token becomes a `U+FFFD` replacement — corrupting the text the cap was meant to preserve.

This is the byte-truthful sibling of the `vectorId()` cap directly below it, which was already made byte-correct (#1458). Repro: `embeddingText({ title: "a".repeat(1499) + "😀" }).isWellFormed()` returns `false`.

### 2. `src/badge.mjs` — `textWidth` under-sizes non-BMP / non-ASCII glyphs
`textWidth` is documented as "a safe overestimate so text never overflows its segment", but every non-ASCII code point falls through to the 6.5px lowercase default — narrower than the 8px of a capital letter. Since `sanitizeLabel` deliberately admits emoji in `?label=` (#1438), an emoji or CJK label is sized smaller than a capital `W` and clips its own segment. Repro: badge width is 38 for an emoji label vs 39 for `W`.

### Fix
Truncate embedding text by code point, and size astral/CJK glyphs as a safe over-estimate. Each with a regression test. ASCII paths unchanged.

problems.title: List sort places rows missing the sort field first in ascending order
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

List endpoints sort with `sortRows` in `workers/list-query.mjs`:

`[...rows].sort((a, b) => compareValues(a[key], b[key]) * direction)`

`compareValues` coerces a missing value to `String(value ?? "")`, so a row that lacks the sort field compares as the empty string `""`. In **ascending** order that sorts *smallest*, so the least-complete rows (e.g. a subnet with no `tempo` / `surface_count` yet) land at the **top** of the list. Flip to `order=desc` and those same gap rows jump to the bottom — so simply toggling direction shuffles incomplete rows in and out of the most-visible position.

## Expected

Rows missing the sort field should consistently sort **last**, in both directions — incomplete data shouldn't lead an ascending list, and its position shouldn't depend on the sort direction.

## Proposed fix

In `sortRows`, partition rows whose sort value is `null`/`undefined` out of the comparison and append them after the ordered rows. Present values sort exactly as before; missing rows always trail. Runtime-only — no schema/OpenAPI change.

problems.title: computeReliability buckets per-surface stats by unstable surface_id, inflating reliability surface_count across renames
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`computeReliability` in `src/reliability.mjs` aggregates per-surface uptime stats keyed on `row.surface_id`, not the stable `surface_key` introduced by the surface-identity rename model (#1005). When a surface is renamed within the scoring window, its history spans **one** `surface_key` but **two** `surface_id` values — so it splits into two buckets, inflating `surface_count` and fragmenting the per-surface reliability score.

## Where

`src/reliability.mjs` — `computeReliability()`:

```js
const surface = bySurface.get(row.surface_id) || { ... };
// ...
bySurface.set(row.surface_id, surface);
// ...
surface_count: bySurface.size,
```

## Impact

- **`loadSubnetReliability()` (`src/health-serving.mjs`) — live bug, no workaround.** Its query does `GROUP BY COALESCE(surface_key, surface_id), day` and emits `MAX(surface_id) AS surface_id` per group, so a surface renamed mid-window produces rows with one stable `surface_key` but a different `surface_id` on each side of the rename. `computeReliability` then double-counts it, and `subnet.surface_count` reports 2 for what is one physical surface. This value is served on the subnet reliability surface.
- **`formatUptime()` (`src/health-serving.mjs`) — already masked.** It works around the root cause by pre-rewriting each row's `surface_id` to the stable key before calling `computeReliability`:

```js
const reliabilityRows = (rows || []).map((row) => ({
  ...row,
  surface_id: surfaceLookupKey(row),
}));
```

This is a fragile band-aid that hides the defect from one caller while the other still trips on it.

## Expected

`computeReliability` should key per-surface aggregation on the stable `surface_key` (falling back to `surface_id` for legacy rows that predate it), so a renamed surface stays one bucket. The `formatUptime` workaround then becomes unnecessary.

## Repro (unit)

Call `computeReliability` (or `loadSubnetReliability`) with two rows sharing one `surface_key` but different `surface_id` values across days → today `subnet.surface_count === 2`; it should be `1`.

## Scope

Self-contained: `src/reliability.mjs` + remove the dead workaround in `src/health-serving.mjs`, with unit tests. No schema/contract regeneration; the served contract is unchanged.

problems.title: summarizeRows reports subnet health as ok when all surface statuses are unrecognized
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`summarizeRows` (`src/health-serving.mjs`) and the prober's `summarizeGroup` (`src/health-prober.mjs`) bucket surface rows by the raw `row.status` string. When a status is **outside** the canonical probe set (`ok` / `degraded` / `failed` / `unknown`), it lands in a dynamic key (e.g. `weird: 2`) that `rollupSubnetStatus` never sees.

Because `failed === 0 && degraded === 0`, the subnet rollup returns **`"ok"`** even when **every** surface has an unrecognized or missing status — a false healthy signal on live health overlays and the 15-minute cron KV snapshot.

## Where

```js
// health-serving.mjs + health-prober.mjs (identical pattern)
counts[row.status] = (counts[row.status] || 0) + 1;
// ...
status: rollupSubnetStatus({ ...counts, total: rows.length }),
```

`rollupSubnetStatus` (`src/health-probe-core.mjs`) only reads the four canonical buckets. Unrecognized strings bypass all of them.

## Impact

- **`overlaySubnetHealth` / live D1 health** — subnet badge can show `ok` while no surface is actually ok.
- **`runHealthProber` KV `health:current`** — per-subnet rollup written every 15 minutes can report `ok` with `ok_count: 0`.
- Forward-compat / corrupted rows (null status, typo, future enum value) all hit this path.

## Expected

Unrecognized / null / missing status values should normalize to **`unknown`** before counting, so an all-unrecognized subnet rolls up to **`unknown`**, not **`ok`**.

## Repro (unit)

```js
summarizeRows([{ status: "weird" }, { status: "weird" }])
// today: { status: "ok", ok_count: 0, unknown_count: 0 }
// expected: { status: "unknown", unknown_count: 2 }
```

## Scope

Self-contained: add `normalizeProbeStatus` next to `rollupSubnetStatus` in `health-probe-core.mjs`, use it in both aggregators, fix the existing test that documents the wrong behavior. No schema/contract regeneration.

problems.title: Uptime badge renders 100% for a sub-perfect uptime ratio (scoreFromStats rounds 0.99996 up to 1)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The reliability uptime badge renders `100%` for a subnet whose uptime is not actually perfect (e.g. 99.996%). `scoreFromStats` in `src/reliability.mjs` rounds the displayed `uptime_ratio` to 4 decimals with `Number(uptimeRatio.toFixed(4))`, and `(0.99996).toFixed(4) === "1.0000"`, so a sub-1 ratio is stored as an exact `1` before it ever reaches the formatter.

## Why the existing formatter guard does not catch it

The badge path is:

- `reliabilityContent` -> `loadReliability` (defaults to `loadReliabilityAggregate`, `src/health-serving.mjs:1168`) -> `scoreFromStats` (`src/reliability.mjs:30`) -> returns `uptime_ratio` (line 55)
- `src/badge.mjs:245`: `formatUptimePercent(rel.uptime_ratio)`

`formatUptimePercent` only demotes a value when `value < 1`. Because `scoreFromStats` has already collapsed `0.99996` to exactly `1`, the `value < 1` guard never fires and the badge prints `100%`. The rounding happens upstream of the formatter, so the information needed to demote is already lost by the time the formatter runs.

## Reproduction

`GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/badge.svg?metric=uptime` for a subnet whose 30-day rollup is `SUM(ok_count)=24999`, `SUM(samples)=25000` (uptime = 99.996%).

- Expected: badge text `99.99%` (sub-perfect uptime must not read as a perfect badge).
- Actual: badge text `100%`.

The same applies to the per-surface / per-subnet `uptime_ratio` that `computeReliability` exposes on the live health API: a 99.996% surface reports `uptime_ratio: 1`, overstating it as perfect.

## Expected

Only a genuine `okCount === samples` (exact `1`) should report `uptime_ratio: 1`. A sub-1 ratio that rounds up to `1` should clamp to the largest 4-decimal value below 1 (`0.9999`), so the badge reads `99.99%` and the health API does not claim a perfect ratio.

## Notes

- `score` / `grade` are unaffected (they are computed from the raw `uptimeRatio`, not the rounded display field).
- Health is computed live (never from a committed artifact), so the fix does not change any generated `public/` output.

problems.title: List ?q= only matches a contiguous phrase, so multi-word queries miss obvious results
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The list endpoints support a free-text `?q=` over each collection's searchable fields (added in #1631). The query is matched as **one contiguous substring** of the joined fields:

`workers/list-query.mjs` → `searchRows` does `haystack.includes(q.toLowerCase())`.

So `?q=` only finds rows where the terms appear together, in that exact order. A natural two-word query misses obvious matches:

- `/api/v1/subnets?q=gradients%20training` will **not** find a subnet named "Gradients" whose description is "decentralized training network", because the literal phrase "gradients training" never appears in a single field.

There is also a small edge: a **whitespace-only** `?q=%20` is truthy, so the lone-space needle matches every row whose joined fields contain a space — effectively a near-match-all instead of "no query".

## Expected

Multi-word discovery should match each term independently (order-independent AND) across the searchable fields, like typical search boxes — and a blank / whitespace-only query should mean "no search".

## Proposed fix

In `searchRows`, split `q` on whitespace into terms and keep a row only if **every** term is a substring of its joined searchable fields. A single term keeps the existing substring behaviour; an empty/whitespace-only `q` yields no terms and is treated as no search. Runtime-only — no schema/OpenAPI change.

problems.title: List range filters accept a contradictory min_ > max_ and return a silent empty 200
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The list endpoints accept inclusive numeric range bounds (min_<field> / max_<field>, e.g. `/api/v1/subnets?min_surface_count=…&max_surface_count=…`). Each bound is validated individually (must be a finite number, rejected if it overflows — #1655), but the **pair** is not checked against itself.

A request where the lower bound is greater than the upper bound on the same field, e.g.:

`/api/v1/subnets?min_surface_count=9&max_surface_count=2`

is schema-valid and returns `200` with an **always-empty** result set. The range can never select a row, so the response is silently empty with no signal that the query itself is contradictory.

## Expected

Consistent with how the API already rejects malformed and overflowing bounds (#1655) and unsupported `sort` fields, a contradictory range should be an explicit `400 invalid_query` naming the offending parameter, rather than a silent empty `200`.

## Proposed fix

In `validateListQuery` (`workers/list-query.mjs`), after confirming both bounds on a field are numbers, reject the request when `min_<field> > max_<field>` with parameter `min_<field>` and a clear message. Equal bounds stay valid (a single-value range). Runtime-only — no schema/OpenAPI change.

problems.title: refactor(build): extract build-readiness pure module + unit tests
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

`scripts/build-artifacts.mjs` is a ~7000-line build script excluded from vitest coverage. Integration readiness scoring (`subnetIntegrationReadiness`, `buildAgentReadiness`, `summarizeAgentReadinessBlockers`) and coverage-depth artifact derivation (`buildCoverageDepthArtifact` and helpers) are pure, deterministic functions buried inside the script with no direct unit tests.

Regressions in readiness tiers, blocker codes, coverage-depth tiers, or ranked-queue ordering only show up after a full `npm run build` + `artifacts.test.mjs` — slow and hard to bisect.

## Proposal

Follow the `scripts/lib/economics-artifacts.mjs` decomposition pattern:

1. Extract readiness + coverage-depth pure functions to `scripts/lib/build-readiness.mjs`
2. Re-import from `scripts/build-artifacts.mjs` (byte-identical artifact output)
3. Add `tests/build-readiness.test.mjs` with focused unit tests for:
   - `readinessTier` / `subnetIntegrationReadiness` score + tier matrix
   - `buildAgentReadiness` status, blocker_level, blocker codes
   - `summarizeAgentReadinessBlockers` aggregation
   - `coverageDepthTier`, gap sorting, priority scoring
   - `buildCoverageDepthArtifact` row shape, ranked_queue ordering, summary invariants

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/lib/build-readiness.mjs` exports all readiness/coverage-depth pure functions
- [ ] `npm run build` produces byte-identical readiness/coverage-depth artifacts
- [ ] New vitest file covers tier boundaries, blocker matrix, and queue ordering
- [ ] `npm test` passes

problems.title: refactor(api): extract deferred analytics handlers from api.mjs
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The deferred analytics handler cluster (trajectory, uptime, leaderboards, compare) still lives inline in `workers/api.mjs` (~480 lines), even though #1763 started modularizing request handlers into `workers/request-handlers/`.

Several of these handlers call `markD1FallbackResponse(envelopeResponse(...))` **without awaiting** `envelopeResponse`, so the WeakSet tags a `Promise` instead of a `Response` — the same #1760 bug class fixed elsewhere.

## Proposed fix

- Extract trajectory/uptime/leaderboards/compare (+ helpers) into `workers/request-handlers/analytics-routes.mjs`
- Wire `readHealthMetaKv` / `readEconomicsCurrentKv` via `configureAnalyticsRoutes` (same injection pattern as `configureAnalytics`)
- Fix missing `await` on `envelopeResponse` before `markD1FallbackResponse`
- Add direct unit tests mirroring #1904 (`tests/request-handlers-analytics-routes.test.mjs`)

## Acceptance

- `workers/api.mjs` dispatches imported handlers; no behavior change except the await fix
- Regression tests cover cold D1, query-param guards, and D1-fallback tagging

problems.title: feat(mcp): let semantic_search and ask filter results by type
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`semantic_search` advertises results across subnets, surfaces, and providers, but returns whatever the vector index ranks highest with no way to narrow to one kind. The keyword tools (`search_subnets`, `find_subnet_for_task`) already filter on `type`, while the semantic and grounded `ask` paths do not.

## Why it matters

An agent looking for "image generation APIs" often wants only callable subnets, or only provider records, and instead gets a mix. Without a server-side way to express that, the agent has to over-fetch and post-filter on its side, which wastes the `topK` budget whenever one type dominates the top matches.

## Proposed behavior

- Add an optional `type` argument to `semantic_search` (a single value or a list), validated against the known set: `subnet`, `surface`, `provider`.
- Honor the requested result count after filtering rather than before, so a scoped query still returns a full page.
- Thread the same option through the grounded `ask` path so the retrieved context can be scoped the same way.
- Return a clear error for an unknown type.

problems.title: health-serving: D1 fallback global status_counts skips normalizeProbeStatus
problems.issue_body:
### Summary

`health-probe-core.mjs` documents that aggregating callers must route probe statuses through `normalizeProbeStatus` so unrecognized / forward-compat strings fold into the four canonical buckets. `summarizeRows` already does this (line 113), but `liveFromD1Rows` - the D1 fallback path in `resolveLiveHealth` when KV is cold - still buckets raw `row.status` into the global `summary.status_counts`.

### Repro

When D1 `surface_status` carries a forward-compat status outside `ok|degraded|failed|unknown` (e.g. `throttled`), the fallback loop does:

```js
statusCounts[row.status] = (statusCounts[row.status] || 0) + 1;
```

That creates a phantom key (`status_counts.throttled`) and undercounts `unknown`, while per-subnet rollups in the same payload are normalized via `summarizeRows`.

### Expected

`summary.status_counts` should only expose the four canonical keys, with unrecognized statuses counted under `unknown` - matching `summarizeGroup` / `summarizeRows` and the contract in `normalizeProbeStatus`.

### Scope

- `src/health-serving.mjs` `liveFromD1Rows` global counter loop (~1251-1254)
- Unit test under the existing `resolveLiveHealth` D1-fallback tests

problems.title: health-serving: endpoint by_status histogram skips normalizeProbeStatus
problems.issue_body:
### Summary

When live probe health is overlaid onto endpoint artifacts (subnet detail, provider endpoints, `/api/v1/endpoints`), `overlayArtifactEndpoints` recomputes `summary.by_status` via `countEndpointStatuses`. That helper buckets raw `endpoint.status` values without `normalizeProbeStatus`, so an unrecognized live status creates a phantom histogram key instead of folding into `unknown`.

Per-subnet rollups elsewhere already normalize; this is the missed sibling for the endpoint overlay histogram.

### Repro

Live snapshot has `surfaces[0].status = \"throttled\"`. After overlay, `summary.by_status` contains `{ throttled: 1 }` instead of `{ unknown: 1 }`.

### Expected

`by_status` should only expose the four canonical keys (or absent keys with zero counts), matching the global `status_counts` contract.

### Scope

- `src/health-serving.mjs` `countEndpointStatuses` (~1540-1545)
- Regression test in `tests/health-serving.test.mjs` `overlayArtifactEndpoints` suite

problems.title: global summary status_counts skips normalizeProbeStatus (#1739 sibling): an unrecognized probe status adds a phantom key
problems.issue_body:
### Summary

`health-probe-core.mjs` documents an explicit contract on `normalizeProbeStatus`:

> Callers that aggregate rows into rollupSubnetStatus must normalize through
> normalizeProbeStatus first so unrecognized / forward-compat strings cannot
> bypass the four buckets and roll up to a false "ok".

PR #1739 applied this to the per-subnet rollup (`summarizeGroup`,
src/health-prober.mjs:353 uses `counts[normalizeProbeStatus(row.status)]`).
But the two GLOBAL summary counters were missed and still bucket the raw status:

- src/health-prober.mjs ~:497 (the `runHealthProber` return `counts`)
- src/health-prober.mjs ~:595 (the `persistToKv` served `status_counts`)

Both do:
```js
const counts = { ok: 0, degraded: 0, failed: 0, unknown: 0 };
for (const row of probed) counts[row.status] = (counts[row.status] || 0) + 1;
```

### Why it is observably wrong

The `counts` object from :595 is served verbatim as `summary.status_counts`
(KV health:current) and as `meta.status_counts` (KV health:meta). If a probe
yields a status outside the four canonical buckets (exactly the
"unrecognized / forward-compat" case normalizeProbeStatus exists to handle),
the bracket assignment CREATES A NEW KEY (e.g. `status_counts.throttled = 1`)
and leaves the `unknown` bucket undercounted. So the served status_counts has a
phantom key and its buckets don't fold the unrecognized status into `unknown` -
unlike the per-subnet rollup, which #1739 already normalized.

### Failing input

A probe row with `status: "throttled"` (or any value not in
ok|degraded|failed|unknown).
- Current: `status_counts = { ok:0, degraded:0, failed:0, unknown:0, throttled:1 }`.
- Correct: `status_counts = { ok:0, degraded:0, failed:0, unknown:1 }` (folded
  into `unknown`, no extra key) - matching `summarizeGroup`.

### Scope

`src/health-prober.mjs` only (the two global `counts` loops), routing both
through `normalizeProbeStatus` to mirror line 353; plus a unit test. No
schema/contract change.

problems.title: handleAccountBalance loses u128 rao precision via Number(BigInt(...)) before scaling
problems.issue_body:
## Context

`GET /accounts/{ss58}/balance` returns an account's TAO balance, computed by `handleAccountBalance` (`workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:516`). It reads `result.data.free` / `result.data.reserved`, which Bittensor returns as **hex-encoded `u128` rao values** (1 TAO = 1e9 rao). The comment at `entities.mjs:564` documents this contract.

## Problem

The conversion loses precision for large balances. At `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:565-573`:

```js
const freeRao =
  typeof data.free === "string" ? Number(BigInt(data.free)) : Number(data.free);
const reservedRao =
  typeof data.reserved === "string" ? Number(BigInt(data.reserved)) : Number(data.reserved ?? 0);
balanceTao = (freeRao + reservedRao) / 1e9;
```

`BigInt(data.free)` parses the hex `u128` exactly, but the immediate `Number(...)` cast collapses any magnitude above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (2^53 − 1 = 9,007,199,254,740,991 rao ≈ **9.007M TAO**) to the nearest double **before** the `/ 1e9` scale. The low-order rao digits are silently wrong for any account holding more than ~9M TAO — exactly the foundation / treasury / large-exchange wallets a balance API is most likely to be queried for.

Verified numerically: `Number(BigInt("9007199254740993"))` returns `9007199254740992` (trailing rao digit dropped).

### Test gap

`tests/account-balance.test.mjs` only exercises small values (line 27 numeric 2.5 TAO, line 156 hex ≈2 TAO, line 101 cached 99 TAO). No test feeds a value above the 2^53 rao threshold.

## Requirements

- Compute the balance entirely in BigInt space, converting to TAO only at the end:
  ```js
  const toRao = (v) => typeof v === "string" ? BigInt(v) : BigInt(Math.trunc(Number(v ?? 0)));
  const totalRao = toRao(data.free) + toRao(data.reserved);
  balanceTao = Number(totalRao / 1_000_000_000n) + Number(totalRao % 1_000_000_000n) / 1e9;
  ```
- Preserve current behavior for numeric inputs, hex-string inputs, and absent `reserved` (must still default to 0).
- Do not change the error path: a malformed `data.free` hex string must still throw inside the existing `try` (line 577) and leave `balance_tao: null` with a 200 response.

## Deliverables

- Fix the conversion at `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:565-573`.
- Add a test in `tests/account-balance.test.mjs` supplying a `free` value above 2^53 rao and asserting `balance_tao` matches the exact BigInt-derived TAO value.
- Keep existing small-value, hex-string, missing-`free`/`reserved`, RPC-failure, and cache tests green.

## Acceptance criteria

- For a `free` of `10_000_000_000_000_000` rao (10M TAO), `balance_tao` reflects the exact whole-TAO amount rather than a rounded double.
- A regression assertion proves `Number(BigInt(largeHex))` and the new path diverge, and the new path is correct.
- No change to the malformed-input → `balance_tao: null` behavior.

## References

- `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:516` (export), `:564` (u128 contract comment), `:565-573` (lossy conversion), `:577` (try/…

problems.title: feat(api): GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/concentration — stake & emission decentralization metrics
problems.issue_body:
## Problem / why it matters

Decentralization is the entire thesis of Bittensor, yet the registry has **no way to ask how concentrated a subnet's stake or emission actually is**. We serve the full per-UID metagraph (`/api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/metagraph`) and per-subnet history, but a consumer who wants "is this subnet captured by a few large holders, or is it broadly distributed?" has to pull every neuron row and compute the statistics client-side. Every serious chain explorer surfaces a concentration/Gini view; we already store the inputs.

## Current state (verified)

- The live `neurons` D1 tier carries, per UID per subnet, the absolute `stake_tao` and `emission_tao` columns (plus `validator_permit`) — `migrations/0007_neurons.sql`, exposed via `NEURON_COLUMNS` in `src/metagraph-neurons.mjs:7`.
- `loadSubnetMetagraph` already range-reads those rows for a netuid (`src/metagraph-neurons.mjs`), and `handleSubnetMetagraph` / `handleSubnetHistory` (`workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs`) are the established live-D1, null-safe (cold store → 200 empty, never 404) per-subnet route pattern.
- **No** concentration / Gini / HHI / Nakamoto endpoint exists anywhere (`src/contracts.mjs`, `workers/api.mjs`).

## Proposed addition

`GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/concentration` — computed live from the `neurons` tier, returning a concentration scorecard over the subnet's UID **stake** and **emission** distributions:

- **Gini coefficient** (0 = perfectly equal, 1 = fully concentrated)
- **HHI** (Herfindahl–Hirschman Index) + normalized HHI
- **Nakamoto coefficient** (minimum holders to exceed 50% of the total)
- **Top-percentile cumulative shares** (top 1% / 5% / 10% / 20% of holders)
- **Shannon entropy** + normalized entropy

…for each of `stake` and `emission`, plus `holders` and `total` context. Schema-stable: a cold/absent store or an empty subnet returns `stake: null` / `emission: null` with a 200, never a 404 (mirrors the sibling metagraph routes).

## Implementation sketch

- New pure module `src/concentration.mjs` — `computeConcentration(values)` (all the statistics, fully unit-testable) + `buildConcentration(rows, netuid)`.
- `handleSubnetConcentration` in `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs` (sibling to `handleSubnetHistory`), wired via a `SUBNET_CONCENTRATION_PATH_PATTERN` in `workers/config.mjs` + dispatch in `workers/api.mjs` with `withEdgeCache`.
- Register the live route in `src/contracts.mjs` (`artifact` + `route`), mark it computed (`R2_ONLY_PATTERNS` in `src/artifact-storage.mjs`, `COMPUTED_ARTIFACTS` in `scripts/validate-schemas.mjs`), add a `SubnetConcentrationArtifact` schema, and regenerate `openapi.json`/types via `npm run build`.

No new data collection, no new D1 tier, no static artifact — pure live aggregation over rows we already store.

problems.title: Per-subnet health incidents starve later surfaces under the global cap
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`/api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/health/incidents` can silently under-report downtime for some surfaces on busy subnets.

## Problem

Incident materialization uses a **global** row budget in two places:

1. **SQL** (`workers/request-handlers/analytics.mjs`): gap-island incidents are selected with `ORDER BY surface_id, started_at LIMIT 1000`.
2. **Formatter** (`src/health-serving.mjs` → `formatIncidents`): `maxIncidents` decrements a single global counter while iterating rows.

When one surface (especially an early `surface_id` in sort order) is flappy, it can consume the entire budget. Later surfaces in the same subnet still appear in the SLA table (`samples`, `uptime_ratio`) but return `incidents: []` and `incident_count: 0`, making SLA and incident lists inconsistent.

The per-subnet route is documented as the authoritative incident source for a subnet; a global cap that starves surfaces violates that contract.

## Expected behavior

- Each surface receives a fair share of the incident budget (e.g. per-surface cap with round-robin, or SQL that limits per `surface_key`).
- SLA uptime and incident lists remain consistent for every surface returned in the payload.

## Reproduction (conceptual)

Subnet with surfaces `a` (many gap-islands) and `z` (several incidents). Request:

`GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/health/incidents?window=7d`

Observe: `z` has non-zero SLA samples but zero incidents while `a` holds most of the cap.

## Scope

- `src/health-serving.mjs` (`formatIncidents`, possibly `formatGlobalIncidents`)
- `workers/request-handlers/analytics.mjs` (incident SQL if needed)
- Tests in `tests/analytics.test.mjs` and/or `tests/health-serving.test.mjs`

## References

- `docs/backend-artifact-contracts.md` — incidents are probe-derived, live from D1
- Comment in `analytics.mjs` claims the per-subnet route is authoritative; current cap behavior contradicts that for multi-surface subnets

problems.title: Cap semantic_search query length in shared semanticSearch (parity with ask's ASK_MAX_QUESTION_LENGTH)
problems.issue_body:
## Context

The AI search layer (`src/ai-search.mjs`) exposes two paths to the paid Workers AI embedding model: `semanticSearch` (used by REST `/api/v1/search/semantic`, MCP `semantic_search`, and MCP task-ranking) and `askQuestion`. `askQuestion` caps the embedding input; `semanticSearch` does not, despite both calling the same `embedQuery` → `env.AI.run(EMBED_MODEL, ...)`.

## Problem

`semanticSearch` (`:266-282`) trims and rejects only a **blank** query (`:268`), then passes the full string to `embedQuery` (`:274`) with no length cap. `askQuestion` enforces `ASK_MAX_QUESTION_LENGTH = 1000` (`:32`, `:353-360`). Documents are also capped (`EMBED_TEXT_MAX_CODE_POINTS = 1500`, `:103`/`:137`) — only the query side is unbounded.

Three uncapped callers funnel through `semanticSearch`: REST passes `q` unbounded (`workers/api.mjs:3136`); MCP `semantic_search` uses `requireString` (`src/mcp-server.mjs:1632`, `:399-408` — non-empty only); MCP task-ranking uses `requireString(args, "task")` (`:1696` → `:342`). The MCP body cap `MAX_MCP_BODY_BYTES = 64*1024` (`:163`) bounds the whole body but lets a ~64KB query reach the paid model; `withinRateLimit` bounds frequency, not size. Low severity (cost/abuse hardening).

## Requirements

- Add a shared query-length guard inside `semanticSearch` (covers all three callers), mirroring `askQuestion`. Reject (don't truncate) with `aiInputError(...)` so REST returns `400 invalid_query` (`workers/api.mjs:3141-3142`) and MCP surfaces an input error. Export `SEMANTIC_MAX_QUERY_LENGTH` near the other constants.

## Deliverables

- `src/ai-search.mjs`: add `export const SEMANTIC_MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = ...;` (~`:29-33`) and a guard after the blank-check (`:268`).
- Tests: an oversized-query case asserting `semanticSearch` throws `aiInputError` and `env.AI.run` is not called; REST → `400 invalid_query`; MCP → input error.

## Acceptance criteria

- A query over the cap throws before any `env.AI.run`/`embedQuery` for all three callers; at/below cap unchanged; REST returns 400 `invalid_query`; existing tests pass.

## References

- `src/ai-search.mjs:266-282`, `:238-245`, `:32`/`:353-360`, `:103`/`:137`; `workers/api.mjs:3136`/`:3141-3142`; `src/mcp-server.mjs:1632`/`:399-408`/`:342`/`:1696`/`:163`/`:2991`/`:2998`

problems.title: MCP and REST disagree on tie ordering for non-unique sort fields (sortSubnets has a netuid tie-break sortRows lacks)
problems.issue_body:
## Context

The subnet index is sorted by two surfaces meant to be the same logical query: **MCP** `sortSubnets` (`src/mcp-server.mjs:519-535`, fields `LIST_SUBNETS_SORT_FIELDS` `:488-493`) and **REST** `sortRows` (`workers/list-query.mjs:207-231`, the `subnets` collection's sort set at `src/contracts.mjs:560,579-593`). Both operate over the same in-memory index.

## Problem

The two paths order **ties differently** on non-unique fields. MCP ends with a deterministic tie-break (`:533`): `cmp !== 0 ? cmp * dir : a.netuid - b.netuid`. REST has **no** tie-break (`workers/list-query.mjs:229`): `compareValues(a[key], b[key]) * direction`, and `compareValues` returns 0 for equal values (`:233-238`), so V8's stable sort leaves ties in source order. So `sort=name` (duplicate names) or REST-only fields (`sort=status`/`coverage_level`) return ties in ascending-`netuid` order on MCP but arrival order on REST — same query, different page. Secondary: REST source order comes from the chain snapshot (`scripts/build-artifacts.mjs:156`), not guaranteed netuid-ordered, so REST tie ordering/cursor pages aren't stable across rebuilds.

The comment at `src/mcp-server.mjs:528-530` is scoped to the comparator (which does match `compareValues`); the tie-break is MCP-only (JSDoc `:510-513`), so the comment is incomplete/misleading, not strictly false.

## Requirements

Pick one:
1. **Preferred — make REST match MCP.** Add the `netuid` tie-break to `sortRows` (rows carry `netuid`; fall back/skip for collections without it).
2. **Minimum — fix the comment** if REST is intentionally tie-break-free.

## Deliverables

- Option 1: the tie-break + a test asserting REST `sortRows` orders ties on a non-unique field by ascending `netuid`. Option 2: the corrected comment.

## Acceptance criteria

- (Option 1) Sorting by a non-unique field yields the same order from MCP and REST; REST tie ordering is deterministic. No change to unique-field ordering or null-sink behavior. The `:528-530` comment accurately describes the relationship.

## References

- `src/mcp-server.mjs:519-535`, `:488-493`; `workers/list-query.mjs:207-238`; `src/contracts.mjs:560,579-593`; `scripts/build-artifacts.mjs:156,194,430`

problems.title: /health readiness probe runs an unconditional non-memoized D1 query per request, contradicting its no-I/O docstring
problems.issue_body:
## Context

`handleHealthRequest` (`workers/api.mjs:2648`) backs `/health`, the readiness probe in `run_worker_first` (`wrangler.jsonc:37`), hit on a fixed cadence from every colo plus ad-hoc LB checks. Its docstring (`:2646-2647`) claims it reports bindings "without touching R2/KV (no I/O, no cold-start cost)."

## Problem

The handler does I/O on every request, one piece un-memoized:

1. **Un-memoized D1 read per request.** When `bindings.health_db` is true, it runs (`:2707-2713`) a `SELECT ... FROM account_events ORDER BY observed_at DESC LIMIT 1` via `d1All` (`analytics.mjs:136-160`, no caching) — a billed D1 query per probe.
2. **Result does not gate status.** The comment (`:2700-2705`) is explicit: the chain-event heartbeat does NOT gate the HTTP status (computed only from KV pointer staleness). It is pure observability.
3. **HEAD pays too** — method only suppresses the body (`:2756`); the query runs unconditionally.
4. **Docstring is stale** — it also issues two KV reads (`:2679-2681`), though those ARE in-isolate memoized (`latestPointer` `storage.mjs:195-215`, `readHealthMetaKv` `api.mjs:1709-1721`). The D1 read is the one un-amortized per-request I/O.

Each call is cheap, but the volume (one query per probe, per colo, forever) plus the inaccurate docstring make it worth gating.

## Requirements

- Stop issuing a fresh D1 query per request; keep the `chain_events` field shape/semantics (best-effort, null on cold/unbound); don't let it gate status; fix the docstring.

## Deliverables

- Apply the established in-isolate memo pattern (`{ env, value, expiresAt }`, ~30-60s TTL, keyed on `env`, do not cache null) to the chain-event read — same shape as `readHealthMetaKv`/`latestPointer`/`readEconomicsCurrentKv`. (HEAD-skip or `?include=chain_events` opt-in are acceptable complements.)
- Update the docstring at `:2646-2647`.
- A test asserting the D1 read is collapsed across consecutive `/health` requests within the TTL on a warm isolate.

## Acceptance criteria

- Two `/health` requests within the TTL on one warm isolate result in at most one `account_events` query; `chain_events` body is equivalent to today; a stale pointer still yields 503; the docstring no longer claims "no I/O"; existing + new tests pass.

## References

- `workers/api.mjs:2646-2647`, `:2700-2722`, `:2756-2758`, `:1709-1721`; `workers/request-handlers/analytics.mjs:136-160`; `workers/storage.mjs:195-215`; `wrangler.jsonc:37`

problems.title: Homepage + api-catalog discovery responses lack ETag/304 (and api-catalog re-serializes per request)
problems.issue_body:
## Context

`workers/request-handlers/discovery.mjs` serves the agent/AI discovery surfaces. The most-advertised entrypoints are the homepage (`/`, `workers/api.mjs:962-963`) and the RFC 9727 API catalog (`/.well-known/api-catalog`, `:966-967`); the docstring (`discovery.mjs:224-225`) intends "an agent can bootstrap from a single HEAD of `/`." Every other discovery surface answers conditional requests with a cheap 304: `handleBadgeSvgRequest` (`:92-95`), `mcpServerCardResponse` (`:300-303`), `agentToolsResponse` (`:327-330`), each via `weakEtag(body)` + `ifNoneMatchSatisfied`.

## Problem

`homepageResponse` (`:226-232`) and `apiCatalogResponse` (`:238-271`) do neither — a conditional GET/HEAD always gets a full 200. Additionally `apiCatalogResponse` rebuilds the `linkset` object and runs `JSON.stringify(linkset, null, 2)` (`:240-270`) **per request**, though the document depends only on `PRIMARY_DOMAIN` (a module constant). (The homepage body `HOMEPAGE_HTML` is already a module constant, so only the missing 304 applies there.) Net: the two most-advertised entrypoints can never be revalidated cheaply, and the catalog re-allocates/re-stringifies an invariant document on the hot path. Note `weakEtag` is async (`workers/http.mjs:102-109`), so the catalog etag must be precomputed via top-level await or lazily memoized.

## Requirements

- Add `etag` + `ifNoneMatchSatisfied` → 304 to both handlers, matching the three siblings (including `*` and comma-separated weak validators).
- Build the api-catalog body **once** (module-level/lazy-memoized).
- HEAD still returns headers + etag with no body; shared discovery headers unchanged on all paths.

## Deliverables

- Hoist the catalog body to a precomputed string + precomputed `weakEtag`; add the 304 short-circuit to both handlers (with `HOMEPAGE_ETAG` over the static HTML).
- Extend `tests/discovery-conditional.test.mjs` to run `assertConditional` against `apiCatalogResponse` and `homepageResponse` (import `homepageResponse`, currently not imported), keeping the existing api-catalog HEAD/GET-body assertions.

## Acceptance criteria

- A matching `If-None-Match` to `/` and `/.well-known/api-catalog` returns 304 with the etag + headers, no body; a non-matching one returns the full 200; the catalog linkset is serialized once; new tests pass.

## References

- `discovery.mjs:226-232`, `:238-271`, `:92-95`/`:300-303`/`:327-330`; `workers/http.mjs:102-109`/`:119-127`; `workers/api.mjs:962-967`; `tests/discovery-conditional.test.mjs:16-33`/`:165-182`

problems.title: perf(api): complete keyset-cursor pagination across entity feeds
problems.issue_body:
Part of the performance/resource roadmap (parent: #2056).

## Context

The block-explorer / account entity feeds are live D1 routes recomputed on every edge-cache miss. The extrinsics feed already gained keyset (cursor) pagination in #1851 — a row-value seek on the PK — but the sibling feeds did not.

## Problem

The remaining entity feeds still use `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`, and the offset is clamped to **1,000,000** (`clampInt(..., 0, 0, 1_000_000)`), so a caller can request a deep page that makes SQLite scan-and-skip up to a million rows on large tables (`account_events`, `extrinsics`, `blocks`):

- `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:628` — `blocks` feed (`ORDER BY block_number DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`)
- `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:431` — account transfers
- `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:479` — per-subnet account events
- `src/account-events.mjs:456` — account event history
- `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:343` — account daily history

Offset cost is O(offset); keyset is O(limit).

## Requirements

- Extend the existing `encodeCursor` / `decodeCursor` row-value-seek pattern (already used by the extrinsics feed at `entities.mjs:844`) to the feeds above, using each feed's natural ordering key (e.g. `(block_number, event_index)` for events, `block_number` for blocks).
- Keep `offset` accepted as a deprecated fallback for back-compat; cursor takes precedence (mirror the extrinsics feed).
- Emit `next_cursor` in each feed envelope.

## Deliverables

- Keyset cursors on all listed feeds, mirroring `handleExtrinsicsFeed`.
- Tests: cursor round-trip, stable ordering across pages, malformed-cursor → ignored (falls back to first page).
- A note in the parent that offset is now legacy.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deep-page latency is flat (independent of page depth) on the cursor path.
- Existing offset callers keep working; contract/schema updated if `next_cursor` is newly added to a route.

## References

- Existing keyset impl: `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:841-862` (`decodeCursor`/`encodeCursor`, #1851)
- Offset sites: `entities.mjs:343,431,479,628`; `src/account-events.mjs:456`

problems.title: D1-backed live routes under `/testnet/` return artifact 404 instead of a mainnet-only error
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Multi-network routing (Phase 1) correctly blocks some mainnet-only routes under `/api/v1/testnet/…` (trends, compare, leaderboards, semantic search), but many **D1-backed live routes** still fall through to `handleApiRequest` and fail with a generic artifact `not_found`.

## Problem

`isMainnetOnlyApiPath` in `workers/api.mjs` covers analytics/AI routes but omits live entity routes already dispatched on bare mainnet in `handleRequest`, including:

- `/api/v1/blocks`, `/api/v1/blocks/{ref}`, sub-resources
- `/api/v1/extrinsics`, `/api/v1/extrinsics/{hash}`
- `/api/v1/accounts/{ss58}`, account tail routes
- `/api/v1/subnets/{n}/metagraph`, `/validators`, `/events`, `/history`, neuron routes
- `/api/v1/subnets/{n}/health` (live-only on mainnet)
- `/api/v1/health`, `/api/v1/incidents`, `/api/v1/rpc/usage`
- `/api/v1/chain/activity`, `/calls`, `/signers`, `/fees`

Under `/api/v1/testnet/…`, these hit `handleNetworkScopedRequest` → `handleApiRequest`, which looks for static artifacts like `/metagraph/testnet/blocks.json` and returns **404 `not_found`** without a clear mainnet-only signal.

This is inconsistent with the explicit message already returned for trends/compare:

> `{path} is only available on mainnet, not the testnet network.`

## Expected behavior

- Network-prefixed requests to D1-backed live routes return **404** with `meta.network` set and a clear mainnet-only message (same pattern as trends/compare).
- Registry artifact routes (`/subnets`, `/coverage`, `/providers`, etc.) remain network-partitioned and unchanged.

## Scope

- `workers/api.mjs` — extend `isMainnetOnlyApiPath` using existing path patterns from `workers/config.mjs`
- `tests/network-routing.test.mjs` — table-driven cases for blocks, accounts, metagraph, incidents, chain analytics

## References

- `tests/network-routing.test.mjs` — existing mainnet-only dynamic route test (trends, compare, leaderboards)
- `docs/backend-artifact-contracts.md` — blocks/accounts/metagraph schemas are live D1 routes, not partitioned artifacts

## Non-goals

- Serving mainnet D1 data under a testnet prefix
- Changing bare `/api/v1/…` mainnet dispatch

problems.title: feat(mcp): add live analytics tools for leaderboards, compare, uptime, and incidents
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Several REST analytics endpoints have no MCP parity:

- `/api/v1/registry/leaderboards` (live D1 + registry projections)
- `/api/v1/compare` (multi-subnet side-by-side)
- `/api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/uptime` (surface uptime history)
- `/api/v1/incidents` (global incident feed)

Agents can call `get_subnet_trajectory` and economic-only `find_subnet_opportunities`, but cannot access the full live leaderboards, compare view, uptime series, or cross-subnet incidents without falling back to REST.

## Proposed fix

- Extract shared live analytics loaders into `src/analytics-live.mjs` (move `composeCompareData` out of `workers/api.mjs`).
