problems.title: Incidents content feed always empty — reads a nonexistent static artifact
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`/api/v1/feeds/incidents` (RSS, Atom, JSON Feed) and per-subnet combined feeds merge incident items from `/metagraph/incidents.json`, but that artifact is **never built**. Live incident data is served only from D1 at `/api/v1/incidents`.

## Problem

`src/feeds.mjs` loads incidents via `readArtifact`:

```js
const incidents = await readData(readArtifact, env, "/metagraph/incidents.json");
```

`src/artifact-storage.mjs` and `src/contracts.mjs` document this path as a **live-only schema stub** — no static file is written during publish. `readData` returns `null`, so `incidentItems()` produces an empty list while the REST route may return real downtime rows.

## Expected behavior

- Feed endpoints surface the same live incident ledger as `GET /api/v1/incidents` (within feed item limits and formatting).
- Subnet combined feeds include probe-detected incidents for that netuid when D1 has data.

## Scope

- `src/feeds.mjs` — call the same D1 formatter as `handleGlobalIncidents` (or a shared helper)
- `tests/feeds.test.mjs` — assert non-empty feed when D1 returns rows; stop relying solely on injected static artifacts

## References

- `GET /api/v1/incidents` — `workers/request-handlers/analytics.mjs` → `handleGlobalIncidents`
- `#741` — content feeds feature

## Non-goals

- Committing a static `incidents.json` artifact
- Changing the REST incidents API shape

problems.title: feat(api): entity (coldkey) & validator concentration lenses on /subnets/{netuid}/concentration
problems.issue_body:
## Problem / why it matters

The new `GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/concentration` endpoint (#2106) measures stake/emission concentration **per UID**. But a single operator controls many hotkeys/UIDs under one **coldkey**, so a UID-level Gini *understates* real concentration: a whale that spreads its stake across 20 small UIDs reads as a broad, decentralized distribution when one entity actually controls it. Entity-level (coldkey-collapsed) concentration is the question Bittensor researchers actually ask — "is this subnet captured by a few entities?" (Sybil / consolidation). Separately, raw stake concentration says nothing about **consensus power**: validators (permit holders) set weights, so a subnet can have broad miner stake but a captured validator set.

## Current state (verified)

- The live `neurons` D1 tier already carries `coldkey` and `validator_permit` per UID (`NEURON_COLUMNS`, `src/metagraph-neurons.mjs`; `migrations/0007_neurons.sql`).
- `src/concentration.mjs` already exposes a pure `computeConcentration(values)` (Gini / HHI / Nakamoto / top-shares / entropy), merged in #2106 — so the statistics are a free reuse.
- The endpoint currently returns only `stake` and `emission` (per-UID); there is no entity or validator view anywhere in `src/contracts.mjs`.

## Proposed addition

Extend the existing response with three lenses over the same snapshot (additive, backward-compatible):

- **`entity_stake` / `entity_emission`** — collapse a coldkey's UIDs into one holder (true control distribution), plus **`entity_count`** and **`uids_per_entity`** (a Sybil/consolidation signal).
- **`validator_stake`** — concentration among only validator-permit UIDs (consensus/voting power).

All three reuse `computeConcentration`; the only new logic is a coldkey-grouping aggregation. Null-safe (cold store / empty subnet → null blocks, 200, never 404), consistent with the merged per-UID behavior.

problems.title: MCP `get_api_schema` / `get_fixture` ignore deprecated surface_id aliases
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

After a surface rename, agents can resolve and verify a deprecated `surface_id` via REST verify and MCP `verify_integration` (alias-aware `findSurface`), but MCP `get_api_schema` and `get_fixture` load artifacts using the raw id and 404.

## Problem

`get_api_schema` and `get_fixture` handlers call:

```js
loadArtifactData(ctx, `/metagraph/schemas/${surfaceId}.json`);
loadArtifactData(ctx, `/metagraph/fixtures/${surfaceId}.json`);
```

REST verify resolves aliases first:

```js
surface = findSurface(catalog.data?.surfaces, surfaceId, aliases.data);
```

Schema and fixture R2 keys are keyed by the **current** surface id. A deprecated alias that still verifies successfully cannot fetch its schema or captured fixture.

## Expected behavior

- Resolve deprecated `surface_id` → current id via `surface-aliases.json` before artifact lookup (same as verify).
- Return the schema/fixture for the canonical surface when the alias maps cleanly.

## Scope

- `src/mcp-server.mjs` — `get_api_schema`, `get_fixture` handlers
- `tests/mcp-server.test.mjs` or extend `tests/surface-aliases.test.mjs`

## References

- `#358` — verify-now + alias resolution on REST
- `#1005` — stable `surface_key` + alias artifact

## Non-goals

- Accepting arbitrary user-supplied URLs
- Changing alias artifact format

problems.title: feat(badge): add metric=apis — a callable-API-count badge
problems.issue_body: ### Problem The embeddable status badge (`/api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/badge.svg`) supports `metric=readiness`, `metric=uptime`/`reliability`, and `metric=grade`. There's no at-a-glance way to show **how many callable API surfaces a subnet exposes** — the core "is this subnet machine-integrable, and how much" signal that the registry exists to surface. ### Proposal Add `metric=apis`: a badge whose message is the count of the subnet's callable API surfaces — the machine-integration kinds `subnet-api`, `openapi`, `sse`, `data-artifact` (mirroring the build's callable-service set) — counted from the per-subnet `surfaces` artifact. - Message: `"3 apis"` (singular `"1 api"`), `"0 apis"` when none. - Color: shields-style informational blue (`#007ec6`) for >0, gray for 0, `"n/a"` (gray, 200) when there's no data — consistent with the other metrics, so an `` never breaks. - Providers: the sum across the provider's subnets (mirrors how `readiness`/`reliability` aggregate). problems.title: feat(api): concentration history — per-day decentralization trend on /subnets/{netuid}/concentration/history
problems.issue_body:
## Problem / why it matters

The `GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/concentration` endpoint (#2106) is a **point-in-time** snapshot of how concentrated a subnet's stake/emission is. But the question operators and delegators actually care about is the **direction**: is this subnet *centralizing* (a few holders accumulating) or *decentralizing* over time? A single Gini number can't answer that — you need the trend. There is no historical/trend view of concentration anywhere today.

## Current state (verified)

- The `neuron_daily` D1 rollup already stores per-UID `stake_tao` + `emission_tao` **per `snapshot_date`** (`migrations/0011_neuron_daily.sql`), with a 400-day retention and the `idx_neuron_daily_netuid_date` index — exactly the dated distribution a trend needs.
- `src/concentration.mjs` already exposes the pure `computeConcentration(values)` (Gini / Nakamoto / top-shares / …), merged in #2106 — so each day's metrics are a free reuse.
- The structural history route `handleSubnetHistory` (`entities.mjs`) is the established windowed `neuron_daily` read pattern, but it only `SUM`s per day — it can't produce a distribution metric like Gini.

## Proposed addition

`GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/concentration/history?window=7d|30d|90d` — a per-day concentration time series (newest first) from `neuron_daily`. Each point is flat + chartable: `stake_gini`, `stake_nakamoto_coefficient`, `stake_top_10pct_share`, the same three for emission, and `neuron_count`.

Because concentration needs each day's *full* distribution (not a cheap SQL `GROUP BY`), the read is the raw rows bounded by a row cap, with the window capped at 90d to keep it bounded; the builder drops a truncated oldest day so every point is a complete distribution. Reuses `computeConcentration`; null-safe (cold store → `points:[]`, 200, never 404).

problems.title: feat(api): GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/stake-flow, net staked vs unstaked over a window
problems.issue_body:
## Problem / why it matters

Stake is the capital signal in Bittensor, but the registry has no way to ask whether a subnet is gaining or losing stake over time. We serve the raw per-event feed (`/api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/events?kind=StakeAdded`) and validator churn (`/api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/turnover`), but a consumer who wants "is capital flowing into this subnet or draining out of it, and by how much?" has to page every StakeAdded and StakeRemoved row and sum them client-side. Turnover answers who entered or left the validator set; it does not answer how much TAO actually moved. Every capital tracker surfaces a net-flow view, and we already store every input.

## Current state (verified)

- The `account_events` D1 tier stores each stake event with an `amount_tao REAL` column (tao field / 1e9), per `migrations/0009_account_events.sql:21`. StakeAdded and StakeRemoved both carry it (`src/account-events.mjs`, EVENT_INSERT_COLUMNS plus the ingested-kinds set). `observed_at` is the block timestamp in epoch ms, and the tier keeps a rolling ~90-day hot window.
- `migrations/0024_account_events_kind_index.sql` indexes `account_events (netuid, event_kind, block_number)`, which is exactly the seek a per-subnet, per-kind aggregate needs.
- `handleSubnetEvents` (`workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:859`) is the established live-D1, null-safe per-subnet account_events reader (cold store returns 200 empty, never 404); `handleSubnetTurnover` (`entities.mjs:417`) plus the pure `src/turnover.mjs` module are the established compute-and-scorecard pattern.
- No stake-flow, inflow/outflow, or net-stake endpoint exists anywhere (`src/contracts.mjs`, `workers/api.mjs`).

## Proposed addition

`GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/stake-flow?window=7d|30d|90d` (default 30d), computed live from `account_events`, returning a stake-flow scorecard over the window:

- `total_staked_tao` (sum of StakeAdded amount_tao)
- `total_unstaked_tao` (sum of StakeRemoved amount_tao)
- `net_flow_tao` (staked minus unstaked, positive means net inflow)
- `stake_events` / `unstake_events` (counts)
- `window` and `netuid` context

All TAO sums rounded to rao precision (matches the rounding in `src/turnover.mjs`). The windows are 7d/30d/90d because `account_events` keeps a rolling ~90-day hot window, which is exactly the recent-capital-flow signal a flow view answers. Schema-stable: a cold or empty store returns zeroed totals with a 200, never a 404, mirroring the sibling routes.

## Implementation sketch

- New pure module `src/stake-flow.mjs`: `buildStakeFlow(rows, netuid, opts)` (the sums, net, and counts, fully unit-testable) plus `loadSubnetStakeFlow(d1, netuid, opts)`.
- `handleSubnetStakeFlow` in `workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs`, sibling to `handleSubnetTurnover`, one indexed `GROUP BY event_kind` read over `account_events` (`observed_at >= now - windowDays`) using `idx_account_events_netuid_kind`.
- A `SUBNET_STAKE_FLOW_PATH_PATTERN` in `workers/config.mjs` (next to `SUBNET_TURNOVER…

problems.title: feat(api): add GET /api/v1/chain/signers — windowed most-active-account leaderboard
problems.issue_body:
TITLE: feat(api): add GET /api/v1/chain/signers — windowed most-active-account leaderboard
REPO: metagraphed

## Problem

A premier developer block explorer needs a "who's most active on chain" view, but today we have no way to rank accounts by activity. Every per-account read we ship is keyed by a single ss58 the caller already has — `GET /api/v1/accounts/{ss58}/extrinsics` (`workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:366`), `/events`, `/transfers`. There is no *discovery* surface: the UI `accounts.index` route has nothing to list, so a user landing on "Accounts" has to already know an address. Indexers like Subscan/Taostats all front their accounts page with a most-active leaderboard; we should too.

We already store everything required — the `extrinsics` D1 tier carries `signer`, `fee_tao`, `tip_tao`, `block_number`, and `observed_at` per row. We just don't aggregate it. Let's expose a windowed signer leaderboard so the UI can populate its accounts landing page and agents can answer "top accounts by activity in the last 7d/30d".

## Current state (verified)

- **The data is there.** `migrations/0014_extrinsics.sql:29-46` defines `extrinsics(block_number, extrinsic_index, extrinsic_hash, signer, call_module, call_function, success, observed_at, PRIMARY KEY (block_number, extrinsic_index))`; `fee_tao` and `tip_tao` were added by `0016_extrinsic_fee_tao.sql` / `0019_extrinsic_tip_tao.sql` and are both in the load + read contract (`src/extrinsics.mjs:15` `EXTRINSIC_INSERT_COLUMNS`, `src/extrinsics.mjs:101` `EXTRINSIC_READ_COLUMNS`). `signer` is the ss58 of the signed extrinsic, null for inherents/unsigned (`migrations/0014_extrinsics.sql:33`).
- **No aggregation surface exists.** The only `signer`-keyed read is the per-account feed `handleAccountExtrinsics` — `SELECT … FROM extrinsics WHERE signer = ? ORDER BY block_number DESC, extrinsic_index DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` (`workers/request-handlers/entities.mjs:373`). Nothing does `GROUP BY signer`.
- **Index caveat — flag this loudly.** There is **no migration `0021`** in this tree (`migrations/` stops at `0020_account_events_alpha.sql`) and **no `idx_extrinsics_signer_order`**. The only signer index is the single-column `idx_extrinsics_signer ON extrinsics (signer)` from `migrations/0014_extrinsics.sql:44` (and a separate `idx_extrinsics_observed ON extrinsics (observed_at)` at `:46`). A `GROUP BY signer` with a `WHERE observed_at >= ?` window is served by neither single-column index well — it can't satisfy both the time filter and the grouping, forcing a scan + sort. This route needs a new composite index shipped in the same PR (see below).
- **Retention is 365 days, not 90.** `EXTRINSIC_RETENTION_MS = 365 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` (`src/extrinsics.mjs:10`). (The header comment in `migrations/0014_extrinsics.sql:12` still says "90-day" — stale prose; the code is authoritative.) So on data-retention grounds the largest *defensible* window is 365d — but see the next point: the *served* window set is narrower …

problems.title: feat(api): GET /api/v1/chain/fees — daily fee/tip aggregates + windowed top-fee-payers
problems.issue_body:
## Problem / why it matters

We index every extrinsic's `fee_tao` and `tip_tao` into the first-party `extrinsics` D1 tier (`src/extrinsics.mjs:24,28`, decoded from finney by `scripts/fetch-events.py`), but we surface those values *only* per-extrinsic. There is no way to ask "what did the chain spend on fees yesterday?", "is the fee market trending up?", or "who are the biggest fee payers this week?" without paginating the entire feed client-side. Every premier dev block explorer (Subscan, Etherscan) ships a fee/economics view; we already have the raw rows, we're just not aggregating them.

This is the natural fee-market companion to the chain-activity aggregate (the daily tx-count / event-volume rollup). The two compose: chain-activity answers *how many* extrinsics; `/chain/fees` answers *how much they cost*. Same `extrinsics` tier, same UTC-day buckets, same window param, so a dashboard can render activity and fee-burn on one shared time axis.

## Current state (verified)

- The `extrinsics` tier carries **both** fee columns: `EXTRINSIC_INSERT_COLUMNS` lists `"fee_tao"` (`src/extrinsics.mjs:24`) and `"tip_tao"` (`src/extrinsics.mjs:28`, the `TransactionFeePaid` priority tip — comment at `:25-26`: "most extrinsics tip 0. Nullable."). Both are TAO floats and **nullable** — `formatExtrinsic` passes them through as `row.fee_tao ?? null` / `row.tip_tao ?? null` (`src/extrinsics.mjs:125-126`), so any aggregate MUST treat NULL as "no fee", not zero-by-accident. `EXTRINSIC_READ_COLUMNS` (`src/extrinsics.mjs:101-102`) is the canonical SELECT list; `signer` is the single fee-paying key. Row timestamps are epoch-ms in `observed_at`.
- There is **no** `fee_tao_daily` rollup table — only the raw hot rows, bounded by 365-day retention (`EXTRINSIC_RETENTION_MS`, `src/extrinsics.mjs:10`; pruned by `pruneExtrinsics`, `:83`).

  - `d1All` (`analytics.mjs:136`) is the timeout-guarded reader that catches a D1 failure, logs it, and degrades to a marked empty result.
  - `markD1FallbackRows` (`:121`), `hasD1FallbackRows` (`:127`), and `markD1FallbackResponse` (`:131`) are the WeakSet bookkeeping that keeps a degraded payload out of the edge cache. **These are module-local, NOT exported today** (see wiring note below).
  - `validateQueryParams` (`:73`) and `analyticsWindow` (`:93`) handle the `?window` enum + unknown-param 400. `validateQueryParams` **is** already imported into `entities.mjs` (`entities.mjs:27-32`); `analyticsWindow` is **module-local, NOT exported**.
- `entities.mjs` currently imports `analyticsQueryError`, `d1All`, `d1Runner`, `validateQueryParams` from `analytics.mjs` (`entities.mjs…

problems.title: fix(account-events): coerce string-typed netuid and uid cells to Numbers in formatAccountEvent
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`formatAccountEvent` (`src/account-events.mjs`) projected the D1 `netuid` and `uid` cells directly into the API payload as `row.x ?? null`, while the sibling integer columns in the same function (`block_number`, `event_index`, `extrinsic_index`) already went through `toBlockNumber`. D1 can return an INTEGER column as a numeric string (`7` instead of `7`), so the bare pass-through silently leaked strings into the JSON response and broke any downstream arithmetic or comparison.

This routes `netuid` and `uid` through the same `toBlockNumber` helper that the other integer fields in this function already use â€” the same class of coercion applied to the sibling formatters `formatBlock` (#2435) and `formatExtrinsic` (#2439).

## What changed

- **`src/account-events.mjs`** â€” replaced the bare `?? null` pass-throughs on `netuid` and `uid` with `toBlockNumber(row.x)`. Missing, negative, or non-integer cells now fall back to `null`; string cells are coerced to their integer value.

- **`tests/account-events.test.mjs`** â€” added two cases: (1) string cells coerce to `number`; (2) negative / fractional / non-numeric cells fall back to `null`.

## Validation run

```
npx vitest run tests/account-events.test.mjs
# Test Files  1 passed (1)
# Tests       59 passed (59)

npx eslint src/account-events.mjs tests/account-events.test.mjs
# clean

npx prettier --check src/account-events.mjs tests/account-events.test.mjs
# All matched files use Prettier code style

npm run build
npm run validate
# Validated 129 native subnet(s), 129 curated overlay(s), 1213 surface(s), 125 provider(s), and 2037 candidate(s).
```

No schema/contract change â€” no schema edits, no `schemas/components/` changes, no client-version bump. The `npm run build` is run only to refresh local artifacts before `validate`; no regenerated artifacts are committed in this PR.

problems.title: 📊 Roadmap: subnet identity history — track + serve historical on-chain identity changes
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
A subnet's on-chain identity (`SubtensorModule.SubnetIdentitiesV3`: `subnet_name`, `symbol`, `description`, `github_repo`, `subnet_url`, `discord`, `logo_url`, contact) is **mutable** — owners rename, rebrand, and churn it over time. metagraphed currently captures only the **current, point-in-time** identity (the daily native snapshot), so all prior identities — and the fact that an identity changed at all — are lost.

This surfaced while migrating community surfaces:
- **SN86** churns its name constantly: `MIAO` (Apr 2025, sound-recognition AI) → `The Alpha Arena` (Oct 2025, financial-AI) → `ʕ•ᴥ•ʔ` → `¯\_(ツ)_/¯` → `___________` → `⚒` (current), with descriptions like *"We have not released a github. Cooks are cooking."* taostats keeps a full **Name History**; we keep nothing.
- **SN27** sits on the placeholder `Team TBC` while actually being **NI Compute** (Neural Internet).

## Why it's worth tracking
- **Provenance / "formerly known as":** an agent or dev researching a subnet should see it was previously `The Alpha Arena`, not just today's emoji.
- **Rebrand / instability / rug signal:** rapid identity churn is a real risk signal; change frequency is a derivable metric.
- **Disambiguation:** stealth + recycled names are common; history resolves "is this the same subnet I integrated last month?"
- Complements the `identity-placeholder` handling we just added (a nameless subnet today may have been named before / may be named later).

## Proposed scope
1. **Detect + record changes.** The daily `refresh-metagraph` already snapshots `SubnetIdentitiesV3`. Diff each refresh against the last recorded identity per netuid; on any field change, append a history row (block + observed_at + the changed identity fields + a content hash). No-op when unchanged (idempotent, dedup by hash).
2. **Storage (D1 tier).** New `subnet_identity_history` table — `(netuid, block, observed_at, subnet_name, symbol, description, github_repo, subnet_url, discord, logo_url, hash)` — append-only. Mirrors the metagraph-depth / blocks D1 tiering pattern (#1302, #1345).
3. **Serve.** `GET /api/v1/subnets/{netuid}/identity-history` (newest-first, paginated); add `previously_known_as` / alias hints on the subnet detail + agent-catalog; MCP tool `get_subnet_identity_history`.
4. **UI** (metagraphed-ui): a "Name history" panel on subnet detail (taostats-style timeline of name + description + block/date).
5. **Optional signal:** an identity-churn metric (changes per N days) for instability surfacing.

## Backfill (pre-tracking history)

problems.issue_body:
## Context

`apps/ui/src/routes/providers.index.tsx` defines `providersSearchSchema` with only one key — `view` (`grid`/`table`) — which is correctly read via `Route.useSearch()` and written via `navigate({ search: ... })` (lines 22-24, 46-48, 60-65). But the actual filter state — `q` (search text), `kind`, `authority`, and `sortKey` — lives in plain `useState` calls inside `ProvidersGrid` (lines 152-155) and is never round-tripped through the URL. A page refresh, back-navigation, or copy-pasted link silently drops whatever the user had filtered/sorted to, which is inconsistent with every other list route in the app (e.g. `endpoints.tsx`'s `q`/`category`/`provider`/`health`/`sort`/`order` are all schema-backed).

## Requirement

Move the Providers page's `q`, `kind`, `authority`, and `sortKey` state out of local `useState` and into the route's `validateSearch` schema, following the same `zodValidator` + `fallback().default()` + `Route.useSearch()`/`navigate()` pattern already used for `view` in this file (and for the full filter set in `endpoints.tsx`).

## Deliverable

- File to change: `apps/ui/src/routes/providers.index.tsx` — no other file needs to change for this issue.
- Exact anchor: extend `providersSearchSchema` (currently lines 22-24, `{ view }` only) to add `q` (string, default `""`), `kind` (string, default `""`), `authority` (string, default `""`), and `sort` (enum `["name", "surfaces", "endpoints", "subnets"]`, default `"name"` — matches the existing `SortKey` type at line 127). Then in `ProvidersGrid` (function starts line 129), delete the four `useState` calls at lines 152-155 and replace them with `Route.useSearch()` + a patch-based `setSearch` helper that calls `navigate({ search: (prev) => ({ ...prev, ...patch }), replace: true })`, mirroring `endpoints.tsx`'s `setSearch` (lines 378-398) — minus its page-reset logic, since this page has no pagination.
- Wire the three `Selector` calls (lines 248-261, `Kind`/`Authority`/`Sort`) and the search `<input>` (lines 240-247) to read from search state and call `setSearch({ ... })` instead of the local setters. Wire the `Clear` button (lines 262-274) to reset `q`/`kind`/`authority` (but not `view`) via one `setSearch` call instead of three `setState` calls.
- The `filtered` (lines 166-177) and `sorted` (lines 179-191) `useMemo`s keep their existing logic, just reading from `search.q`/`search.kind`/`search.authority`/`search.sort` instead of the deleted local state; `kinds`/`authorities` option derivation (lines 157-164) is unaffected.

problems.title: Add a polling auto-refresh hook for the latest block / freshness (refetchInterval)
problems.issue_body:
## Context

`apps/ui/src/routes/health.tsx` hand-rolls page-visibility-gated polling: a local `usePageVisible()` hook (lines 62-73) plus `HealthPage`'s own `enabled`/`intervalMs` state compute `effectiveInterval = enabled && visible ? intervalMs : false`, which is then threaded into five separate `useSuspenseQuery({ ..., refetchInterval: interval })` calls (lines 197-202, 359-360, 475, 541) alongside a bespoke `AutoRefreshControl` (interval `<select>`, pause/play, live countdown, aria-live announcements — lines 253-354). `apps/ui/src/routes/status.tsx` does the much thinner version of the same job: a bare hardcoded `const REFRESH_MS = 60_000` (line 23) fed straight into two `useSuspenseQuery` calls (lines 122, 250), with no visibility gating and no pause control at all. There is no shared hook capturing "compute an effective refetch interval, gated on tab visibility and an enabled flag" — the logic and its edge cases (tab hidden, paused) exist once, correctly, in `health.tsx`, and are simply absent in `status.tsx`.

## Requirement

Extract the page-visibility-gated polling logic into a reusable hook in `apps/ui/src/hooks/` (dedup, not a new UI surface) so both `health.tsx` and `status.tsx` compute their `refetchInterval` the same way instead of each route reimplementing (or omitting) the visibility gate.

## Deliverable

- New file: `apps/ui/src/hooks/use-refetch-interval.ts` — following the existing hook convention seen in `apps/ui/src/hooks/use-delayed-reveal.ts` (small exported pure functions + a thin hook wrapper), export:
  - `usePageVisible(): boolean` — lift the exact logic currently private to `health.tsx` lines 62-73 (`document.hidden` + `visibilitychange` listener, SSR-safe default `true`).
  - `useRefetchInterval(intervalMs: number, enabled = true): number | false` — encapsulate `enabled && visible ? intervalMs : false`, composing the lifted `usePageVisible()` internally so callers don't need to wire visibility themselves.
- New co-located test file: `apps/ui/src/hooks/use-refetch-interval.test.ts` — unit-test any pure helper(s) extracted alongside the hook (mirror the `use-delayed-reveal.test.ts` pattern: test the pure logic function directly rather than mounting the hook).
- Edit `apps/ui/src/routes/health.tsx`: delete the private `usePageVisible()` (lines 62-73) and replace `HealthPage`'s local `visible`/`effectiveInterval` derivation with the new shared hook; keep `enabled`/`intervalMs` as local `useState` (that's the interactive control's own state, not part of this hook) and keep `AutoRefreshControl` as-is — only the interval-computation plumbing moves.
- Edit `apps/ui/src/routes/status.tsx`: replace the hardcoded `REFRESH_MS = 60_000` passed directly into the two `useSuspenseQuery` calls (lines 122, 250) with `useRefetchInterval(60_000)`, so `status.tsx` gains the same tab-hidden pause behavior `health.tsx` already has, for free.

problems.title: Add absolute-timestamp tooltip to <TimeAgo> relative times
problems.issue_body: ## Context `TimeAgo` (`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/time-ago.tsx`) renders relative time ("2m ago") in a bare `{text}` with no `title` attribute, so there is no way to see the actual timestamp on hover — confirmed by reading the component (lines 21-25). This is the single most-used time component in the frontend (59 call sites across routes and components), so the gap is felt everywhere a relative time appears. The fix already has prior art: `apps/ui/src/lib/metagraphed/freshness.ts` exports `formatFreshnessAbsolute(updatedAt)`, a null-safe `new Date(x).toLocaleString()` helper, and five separate components (`methodology-callout.tsx`, `schema-drift-detail.tsx`, `charts/stat-with-spark.tsx` ×2, `charts/spark-legend.tsx`, `states/registry-empty.tsx`) each hand-wire `title={freshAbs ?? undefined}` around their own relative-time text using it. `panel-shell.tsx:82` goes further and puts a raw ISO string directly in `title={meta?.generatedAt}` on a wrapper `` around a nested `` — i.e. callers are already reaching for exactly this tooltip behavior by duplicating a wrapper around `TimeAgo`, rather than getting it from `TimeAgo` itself. ## Requirement Add an absolute-timestamp `title` tooltip directly to `` so every one of its 59 call sites gets hover-to-see-exact-time for free, using the existing `formatFreshnessAbsolute` helper instead of introducing a new formatter — this is a small, targeted enhancement to one shared component, not a new feature surface. ## Deliverable - File to change: `apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/time-ago.tsx` (the entire component is lines 1-26; the `` to add `title` to is lines 21-25). - Import `formatFreshnessAbsolute` from `@/lib/metagraphed/freshness` (same helper `methodology-callout.tsx`, `schema-drift-detail.tsx`, `stat-with-spark.tsx`, `spark-legend.tsx`, and `states/registry-empty.tsx` already import) and compute the tooltip value from the component's existing `at` prop. - Critical edge case to handle correctly: `formatFreshnessAbsolute` only checks `Number.isNaN(t.getTime())`, so on its own it renders the 1970-01-01 registry placeholder as a real (misleading) date like `"12/31/1969, 5:00:00 PM"` instead of suppressing it. `TimeAgo`'s visible text already suppresses the placeholder correctly because `formatRelative` internally gates on `isUsableTimestamp` (`> 2000-01-01`). The tooltip must use the same gate — e.g. only pass `title` when `isUsableTimestamp(at)` is true (or equivalently, skip the title whenever the visible `text` is the `"—"`/fallback case) — so a row that correctly shows "—" never shows a bogus 1969 date on hover. - What "done" looks like: the rendered `` gets a `title={...}` attribute holding the absolute local-time string (e.g. via `formatFreshnessAbsolute(at) ?? undefined`, gated as above) whenever `at` is a usable timestamp, and no `title` (or `undefined`) when `at` is missing, unparseable, or the 1970 placeholder — mirroring the existin…

problems.issue_body:
## Context
`IncidentTimeline` (`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/incident-timeline.tsx`, lines 15-22) defines a private `fmtDuration(ms?: number)` helper that hand-rolls the same "compact elapsed label" logic already centralized in `durationLabel(start?, end?)` in `apps/ui/src/lib/metagraphed/format.ts` (lines 88-94). `IncidentCard` (`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/incident-card.tsx`, line 27) already calls the shared `durationLabel(i.started_at, i.ended_at)` for the identical "incident duration" case, so `IncidentTimeline` is the odd one out — it's the only incident-duration renderer still computing its own ms diff and formatting it locally instead of reusing the shared helper.

## Requirement
Delete the local `fmtDuration` in `incident-timeline.tsx` and replace its call site with the shared `durationLabel` from `lib/metagraphed/format.ts`, matching the pattern already used by `IncidentCard`.

## Deliverable
- File to change: `apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/incident-timeline.tsx`
  - Remove the `fmtDuration` function (lines 15-22).
  - Add `durationLabel` to the existing `import { classNames } from "@/lib/metagraphed/format";` (line 7), e.g. `import { classNames, durationLabel } from "@/lib/metagraphed/format";`.
  - Replace the `duration` computation (lines 50-55) — currently `fmtDuration(inc.duration_ms ?? (inc.ended_at && inc.started_at ? new Date(inc.ended_at).getTime() - new Date(inc.started_at).getTime() : undefined))` — with a call to `durationLabel(inc.started_at, inc.ended_at)`. Note the signature difference: `durationLabel(start?: string | null, end?: string | null): string` takes ISO strings directly (which `FlatSurfaceIncident.started_at` / `.ended_at` already are — see `apps/ui/src/lib/metagraphed/types.ts` lines 646/648), so the manual `new Date(...).getTime()` diffing and the `inc.duration_ms` epoch-ms field become unnecessary for this call site.
  - Handle the behavioral difference deliberately: `fmtDuration` returns `null` (hiding the `· {duration}` span entirely, line 73) when there's no computable duration, whereas `durationLabel` always returns a string — `"—"` when `start` is missing, or a live "elapsed so far" label (computed against `Date.now()`) when `end` is omitted for an open incident. Decide and implement one consistent behavior: either keep suppressing the duration segment when `inc.started_at` is absent (guard on `inc.started_at` before rendering, not on the return value), or accept that open incidents now show a running duration instead of no duration — pick the option that matches `IncidentCard`'s existing "ongoing · {durationLabel}" convention (line 27 of `incident-card.tsx`) for consistency across both incident renderers.

`Sparkline` (`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/charts/sparkline.tsx`) renders its chart inside `<svg role="img" aria-label={ariaLabel} ...>`, and `ActivityHeatmap` (`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/charts/activity-heatmap.tsx`) wraps its grid in `<div role="img" aria-label={\`Registry activity heatmap for the last ${weeks} weeks\`}>` — both give the chart a real accessible name via the standard `role="img"` + `aria-label` pattern (the same pattern `MiniStack`/`DotRow`/`NoDataSpark` in `stat-with-spark.tsx` also use). `BarMini` (`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/charts/bar-mini.tsx`) renders a bare `<ul>` of label/bar/value rows with no `role` or `aria-label` anywhere on the list or its container, and `Donut` (`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/charts/donut.tsx`) marks its own `<svg>` `aria-hidden` and never puts an accessible name on the wrapping `<div>` — so a screen reader announces nothing for either chart. problems.title: Add a developer settings page for self-service webhook subscription management
problems.issue_body:
## Context

`POST/GET/DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions` is API-only today with no management UI (confirmed in `workers/api.mjs`'s `handleWebhookRequest`, `src/webhooks.mjs`, `tests/webhooks-worker.test.mjs`). There is no list-all route — a caller creates a subscription (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions`, which returns the `id` + a one-time `secret` + `filters`), then must hold onto that `id`/`secret` client-side to `GET` or `DELETE` `/api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/{id}` later. `apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/settings-popover.tsx` exists but is a display-preferences popover (theme/density/health-color palette) — there is no developer/API settings surface, and no route under `apps/ui/src/routes/` for one.

## Requirement

Add a `/settings` (or similarly-named) developer settings page that lets a visitor create a webhook subscription, paste in an existing subscription id to check its status/delivery health, and delete a subscription they hold the secret for — entirely client-side against the public subscription-management API, no server-side UI account model.

## Backend

- Endpoints:
  - `POST /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions` — create. Body: `{ url, filters?: { netuids?, kinds? }, secret? }`. Response (201): `{ id, url, filters, secret, active, created_at, delivery: {...} }` — **the `secret` is returned once here and never echoed back by GET.**
  - `GET /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/{id}` — read. Returns `publicSubscriptionView` (`id, url, filters, created_at, active` — no secret) plus a `delivery` health summary (`status: "ok"|"retrying"|"dead_letter"`, `pending`, `dead_letter`, `last_failure`).
  - `DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/{id}` — requires the matching secret (see `tests/webhooks-worker.test.mjs:347` "DELETE requires the matching secret" — confirm the exact required header/body shape by reading `deleteWebhookSubscription` in `workers/api.mjs` before wiring it).

- [ ] Since this is a pure refactor with no intended visual change (identical thresholds, just de-duplicated), no before/after screenshot is required — confirm via the PR diff that rendered tone/color for sample data is unchanged

Size: XS — keep this PR small (aim for ≤10 files / ≤1000 LOC).

Part of #2542.

problems.issue_body:
## Context

`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/nav-omnibox.tsx` renders a distinct "Go to" section (line 418-454) above the grouped search-hit list, but that section is populated only from `navTargets` — the direct-navigation regex matches for ss58 address / block number / 0x hash (lines 168-231). Search hits themselves are grouped by `kind` (lines 156-164, 472-509) with **no ranking at all**: they render in whatever order the `/api/v1/search` response returns, and there is no mechanism that lifts a strong subnet-name match (e.g. the query exactly matching a subnet's title) up into "Go to" the way a pasted address or block number does. Note the sibling file `command-palette-body.tsx` (the ⌘K modal) does have a `scoreHit()` function (line 181) and sorts hits by score, but only *within* each kind-grouped `CommandGroup` (line 254-263) — it never promotes a top hit into that file's own "Go to" group either, which stays reserved for `navigateTargets`. So the promotion behavior described here does not exist in either file today; it must be added.

## Requirement

Add ranking + promotion logic to `nav-omnibox.tsx` so that when the query strongly matches a subnet-kind hit (title equals the query, case-insensitively, at minimum), that single best subnet hit is prepended as an entry in the existing "Go to" section — not left buried in the grouped "Subnets" results below it.

problems.title: Surface loading/error states for signed-extrinsics and transfers on the account detail page
problems.issue_body:
## Context

`ValidAccountDetail` in `apps/ui/src/routes/accounts.$ss58.tsx` fetches signed extrinsics and native-TAO transfers via two non-blocking `useQuery` calls (lines 135-136: `accountExtrinsicsQuery` / `accountTransfersQuery`), but only ever reads `.data?.data ?? []` — no `isError`/`error` is destructured from either result. Both consumers, `AccountExtrinsicsSection` (line 356) and `AccountTransfersSection` (line 432), early-return `null` whenever `rows.length === 0`, so a genuine fetch failure renders byte-identical to a cold account with no extrinsics/transfers: nothing at all, no indication anything went wrong. The sibling `AccountHistoryChart` (`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/account-history-chart.tsx`, lines 149-164) already does this correctly — it destructures `isLoading`/`isError`/`error` from its `useQuery` and branches to `Skeleton` / `ErrorState` / `EmptyState` in that order.

## Requirement

Wire `isError`/`error` from the `accountExtrinsicsQuery` and `accountTransfersQuery` results in `ValidAccountDetail` through to `AccountExtrinsicsSection` and `AccountTransfersSection`, and render `ErrorState` (from `@/components/metagraphed/states`) instead of silently returning `null` when either query has failed.

## Deliverable

- File to change: `apps/ui/src/routes/accounts.$ss58.tsx` (only file expected in the diff for this fix).
- Exact anchor:
  - `ValidAccountDetail`, lines 135-136 — `useQuery(accountExtrinsicsQuery(...))` / `useQuery(accountTransfersQuery(...))` currently discard everything but `.data?.data`.
  - `AccountExtrinsicsSection`, line 356 — signature is `{ rows: Extrinsic[] }`, body is `if (rows.length === 0) return null;`.
  - `AccountTransfersSection`, line 432 — signature is `{ ss58: string; rows: Transfer[] }`, same `if (rows.length === 0) return null;` guard.
- What "done" looks like: keep the two queries non-blocking (do not switch them to `useSuspenseQuery` — that would defeat the documented "never stalls the summary" intent at lines 133-134), but pass `isError`/`error` down as props (or pass the whole query result) so each section can render:
  - `isError` → `<ErrorState error={error} context="signed extrinsics" />` / `<ErrorState error={error} context="transfers" />` respectively, using the same `import { ErrorState } from "@/components/metagraphed/states"` pattern `AccountHistoryChart` already uses — instead of the current unconditional `if (rows.length === 0) return null`.
  - Non-error empty (`rows.length === 0` and not `isError`) keeps its current behavior (render nothing) — this issue does not add empty-state copy to either section; only the failure case changes.
- Coordination note: this issue is scoped to the **error** branch only. The **loading** branch for these same two sections (currently `return null` while pending, no `Skeleton`) is already filed separately as #3420 ("Show a loading skeleton instead of silently hiding Signed Extrinsics and Transfers on the account page") — do not add `isPending`…

Follow the existing imperative-POST precedent already in this codebase: `apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/verify-surface-button.tsx`, which wraps a similar on-demand backend call in `useMutation` with `mutationFn: async () => { const res = await apiFetch<T>(path, ...); return res.data; }`, tracks `mutation.isPending`/`mutation.isError`/`mutation.data`, and special-cases `ApiError.status === 429` for a rate-limited message. Add the `AskAnswerData`/citation types to `apps/ui/src/lib/metagraphed/types.ts` alongside the schema's fields.

problems.title: feat(ui): add a registration-cost column to the subnets table view (#3364)
problems.issue_body:
Closes #3364

## Summary

Adds a right-aligned, sortable **Registration** column (`registration_cost_tao`, in τ) to the `/subnets` **table** view (`SubnetsTable`), between the Readiness and Health columns. The value is joined by `netuid` from the already-fetched `/api/v1/economics` artifact via `economicsQuery()` — **no new endpoint, no backend/schema change**. Missing values render `—`; `registration_allowed` drives a subtle cell tone + title (open/closed). Sorting works through the existing `SortHeader`/`sortBy` mechanism.

## What changed

- **`apps/ui/src/routes/subnets.index.tsx`** — new `useSuspenseQuery(economicsQuery())` + memoized `netuid → SubnetEconomics` map, folded into the same `all` memo alongside `joinHealth`/`joinCatalog` (dependency array updated). New `SortHeader label="Registration" field="registration_cost_tao"` `<th>` and a matching right-aligned `<td>` rendering `formatTao(...)`. `SubnetRow` extended with the two optional fields.
- **`apps/ui/src/lib/metagraphed/url-state.ts`** — new generic `joinEconomics()` helper next to `joinHealth()` (same shape: pure, allocation-light, non-matching rows pass through by reference so their cell renders `—`).
- **`apps/ui/src/lib/metagraphed/format.ts`** — extracted the tiered τ formatter `fmtTao` (previously duplicated in `economics-panel.tsx`) into a shared, documented `formatTao()`.
- **`apps/ui/src/components/metagraphed/economics-panel.tsx`** — now imports `formatTao` instead of defining a local copy (behaviour-preserving; the per-subnet Registration tile output is unchanged).

## Scope (matches the issue's acceptance criteria)

- [x] New "Registration" `<th>`/`<td>` in `SubnetsTable`, from `SubnetEconomics.registration_cost_tao` joined by `netuid`
- [x] Uses the existing `economicsQuery()` + `useSuspenseQuery` + memoized join (same as `healthMap`/`catalogMap`); no new fetch/endpoint
- [x] Sortable via the existing `SortHeader`/`onSort` (`?sort=registration_cost_tao&order=`) — `sortBy` reads the field off the row, no `tableSearchSchema` change
- [x] Null/missing renders `—` (never `undefined`/`NaN`/blank)
- [x] No `schemas/` / `registry/` / backend/Worker changes — frontend-only join of already-served data

- **Search/filter path:** the table's free-text filter is `matchesQuery([s.netuid, s.name, s.symbol], search.q)` — numeric joined fields (`service_count`, `integration_readiness`) are already excluded from that haystack, and `registration_cost_tao` follows the same rule (sort-only, not searched). problems.title: New chain-events Args column shows raw undecoded byte arrays, hard-clipped at the viewport edge with no way to read or c
problems.issue_body:
## Context

The new "Chain events" section on the block detail page (#3796) shows the Args column rendering values like `{"who":[[109,111,100,101,115,117,98,116,101,110,115,114,1,0,0,0,0,0,0,...}` instead of a decoded, human-readable representation (e.g. the actual SS58 address string this byte array almost certainly encodes). The text is not truncated with an ellipsis, not wrapped, and has no copy affordance — it runs straight to the right edge of the viewport and is cut off mid-array with no way to see the rest of the value. This affects most rows in the table (`Balances.Deposit`, `SubtensorModule.TimelockedWeightsRevealed`, etc.), making the new section's primary content column largely unreadable and useless as shipped. Every sibling hash/address column elsewhere in this codebase gets copy buttons and hover-cards per the existing, already-tracked backlog — this new column has neither truncation-with-affordance nor decoding.

## Requirement

The Args column must render a genuinely readable value for each row: decoded where the underlying type is recognizable (e.g. an account-id byte array becomes its SS58 string), and at minimum truncated with a copy-to-clipboard/expand affordance where full decoding isn't feasible for this issue's scope.

## Deliverable

- **File to change**: `apps/ui/src/routes/blocks.$ref.tsx`, the Chain events table's Args column (introduced in #3796).
- **What "done" looks like concretely**: for the common, decodable cases (account-id byte arrays → SS58, in particular), decode and display the human-readable form with a copy button, matching the pattern already used for hash/address cells elsewhere. For genuinely raw/undecodable arg shapes, truncate the JSON with an ellipsis and provide an expand-on-click or copy-full-value affordance, rather than letting the raw text run off the viewport edge uncontrolled.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `blocks.$ref.tsx` appears in the diff
- [ ] `Balances.Deposit` and `SubtensorModule.TimelockedWeightsRevealed` rows (or their current equivalents) show a decoded, human-readable value where the arg type is a recognizable account-id/address encoding
- [ ] No Args-column value overflows the viewport edge uncontrolled — every value is either fully visible, truncated with an expand affordance, or scrollable within its cell
- [ ] A copy-to-clipboard affordance exists for the (decoded or raw) value
- [ ] Includes a before/after screenshot table at desktop and mobile, both themes, per the repo's UI-PR requirement

## Non-goals

- Don't attempt to decode every possible pallet/call arg shape in this repo's type system — start with the account-id/address case that's clearly the common one in the sample data, and truncate-with-affordance for the rest; broader decoding coverage can be a follow-up.

## Size

Size: M — keep this PR small (aim for ≤10 files / ≤1000 LOC).

Part of #2542.

problems.title: Homepage KPI panels show "—" placeholders forever on both slow load and genuine failure, with no skeleton or error feedb
problems.issue_body:
## Context

In `apps/ui/src/routes/index.tsx`, `HeroKpis` (lines 322-414), `TrackedGrid` (lines 550-617), and `LivePerformance` (lines 619-668) all use plain `useQuery` (not `useSuspenseQuery`) with no `Suspense` wrapper and no `QueryErrorBoundary` around them. On slow load, they render the pre-fetch fallback ("—"/undefined values) with no skeleton shimmer; on a genuine fetch failure, they render the exact same "—" dashes. There is no way for a user to tell "still loading," "failed to load," and "value is legitimately unknown" apart — all three states look identical. This sits directly above sibling homepage sections that do handle this correctly.

## Requirement

problems.title: Three explorer.tsx leaderboard tables have no overflow wrapper — will force the page to scroll horizontally on mobile
problems.issue_body:
## Context

`apps/ui/src/routes/explorer.tsx` renders three `<table>` elements directly inside plain `<section className="rounded-lg border border-border bg-card p-5">` wrappers, with no `overflow-x-auto`/`overflow-x-clip` and no `ListShell` mediation at all: "Top fee payers" (line 424, 4 columns — Account/Fees/Tips/Txs), "Most active accounts" (line 477, 5 columns — Account/Txs/Fees/Tips/Last block), and the new "Stake-transfer leaderboard" (line 549, 4 columns — Subnet/Transfers/Distinct senders/Transfers per sender). Each uses `<table className="w-full text-left text-sm">` with no width constraint on the parent. A fourth table on the same page (chain-events, line 657) correctly routes through `ListShell` (`table={table}` at line 740-751) and doesn't have this problem. On any viewport narrower than the table's natural width — very plausible given the Account column shows a full monospace short-hash alongside 3-4 right-aligned numeric columns — these three tables will force the enclosing `<section>`, and with it the page body, to overflow horizontally rather than scroll internally.

## Requirement

All three tables must be contained within their own horizontally-scrollable wrapper so a narrow viewport scrolls the table, not the whole page.

## Deliverable

- **File to change**: `apps/ui/src/routes/explorer.tsx`, the three `<section>`/`<table>` blocks at lines 424, 477, and 549.
- **What "done" looks like concretely**: wrap each `<table>` in a `<div className="overflow-x-auto">` (matching the treatment the fourth, `ListShell`-based table already gets), so the table can scroll independently of the page at any viewport width. If `ListShell` itself is a better fit for these three tables (it already handles sort/pagination chrome consistently with the app's other list pages), migrating them to it is an acceptable alternative to a bare `overflow-x-auto` wrapper — reviewer's call based on how much of `ListShell`'s other machinery (sorting, mobile cards) these three tables would actually use.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `explorer.tsx` appears in the diff, covering all three tables (Top fee payers, Most active accounts, Stake-transfer leaderboard)
- [ ] At mobile widths (375px), none of the three tables forces the page body to scroll horizontally — each table scrolls independently within its own section
- [ ] The existing chain-events `ListShell` table on the same page is unaffected
- [ ] Includes a before/after screenshot table at mobile (375px), both themes, per the repo's UI-PR requirement

## Non-goals

- Don't add mobile-card variants for these three tables unless migrating to `ListShell` naturally brings that along — a working scroll container is the minimum bar here.
- Don't change any of the three tables' columns or data.

## Size

Size: S — keep this PR small (aim for ≤10 files / ≤1000 LOC).

problems.title: TypeScript SDK: retries, ETag caching, convenience methods
problems.issue_body:
Part of #740 · Phase 3 (SDK / DX).

## Context
The TS client (`packages/client`, npm `@jsonbored/metagraphed`) is fully typed from OpenAPI but lacks retries/backoff, response caching/ETag conditional requests, and ergonomic convenience methods.

## Scope
**In:** (1) opt-in **retries/backoff** on 429/5xx (honor Retry-After); (2) optional **ETag-based conditional caching** (→ 304); (3) convenience builders (`client.subnets({limit})` / `client.getSubnet(7)`) + `.fetchAll()`.
**Out:** Breaking the typed core; mandatory new deps.

## Completion requirements (a PR MUST satisfy ALL)
- [ ] Retries/backoff (opt-in) honoring Retry-After; tested
- [ ] ETag conditional-request caching (opt-in); tested
- [ ] Convenience methods + auto-pagination helper; types preserved
- [ ] Backward compatible + tree-shakeable; tests + typecheck pass
- [ ] README/examples updated; version bump + changelog
- [ ] Conventional Commit title

## Notes
The typed surface is generated from OpenAPI — don't hand-edit generated types.

problems.title: feat(api): add providers GraphQL list filters without breaking cursor contract (#7888)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
- Add REST/MCP list-query filters to `Query.providers` (`id`, `kind`, `authority`, `sort`, `order`, `fields`) by reusing `loadProvidersList` for validation + filter/sort.
- **Preserve the existing GraphQL contract** that caused LoopOver to reject #7920: opaque **string** id-keyset `cursor` / `next_cursor` (not REST’s integer offset), and cold/absent artifact → schema-stable **empty list** (not a GraphQL error).
- Invalid filter enums still surface as `BAD_USER_INPUT`.
- Rebased onto current `main` after [#7939](https://github.com/JSONbored/metagraphed/pull/7939) was closed for merge conflicts (`graphql.mjs` → `graphql.ts`, plus coexisting `#7886` rpc_endpoints import).

Closes #7888.
Supersedes #7914 / #7920 / #7927 / #7934 / #7939.

## What Changed
- `src/graphql.ts` — filter args on `providers`; shared-loader filter/sort + local string-keyset `paginate`.
- `tests/graphql.test.ts` — id/kind filters, authority/sort/order/fields (both id-prefix branches), string cursor follow, cold empty list, `BAD_USER_INPUT`.

## Why not full REST cursor parity?
LoopOver closed #7920 for changing `next_cursor: String→Int` and flipping cold-store from `{items:[],total:0}` to an error — breaking for existing GraphQL clients. This PR delivers the issue’s filter deliverables without that break.

## Registry Safety
- Links a tracked, currently-open issue (`Closes #7888`) — required.
- No secrets / private URLs.
- GraphQL SDL change only (additive filter args; cursor types unchanged).

## Validation
- `npx eslint src/graphql.ts` — clean
- `npx prettier --write` on touched files
- `npx vitest run tests/graphql.test.ts -t providers` — 9 passing

problems.title: Proxy middleware can panic when the balancer has no targets
problems.issue_body:
### Issue Description

`ProxyWithConfig` can panic when the balancer has no targets.

The built-in balancers return `nil` when their target list is empty. The proxy middleware then passes that nil target to `proxyHTTP` / `proxyRaw`, which can panic.

One way to hit this is to remove the last target with `RemoveTarget`.

I expected the middleware to return a proxy error, such as `502 Bad Gateway`, instead of panicking.

### Working code to debug

```go
targetURL, _ := url.Parse("http://127.0.0.1:8080")

balancer := middleware.NewRoundRobinBalancer([]*middleware.ProxyTarget{
	{Name: "target", URL: targetURL},
})

e := echo.New()
e.Use(middleware.Proxy(balancer))

// Later, from code that updates proxy targets at runtime:
balancer.RemoveTarget("target")

// The next proxied request can panic because the balancer returns nil.

### Version/commit
v4.15.x and v5.1.x

When `c.bind()` fails with a type error on POST'd form data the `inputfieldname` is not available
problems.issue_body:
### Issue Description

When using echo for a web application sending HTML and receiving MIMEApplicationForm POST requests, it seems very difficult / impossible to show helpful validation error messages to the user, when using `echo.context.bind()`. 

For any string data coming from the  MIMEApplicationForm submit which cannot be converted to the target type in the "DTO" struct provided, `echo.context.bind()`  returns a generic error that gives no information about which struct/form field failed validation. 

This makes it very difficult or impossible to render a helpful message to the user like "The `number` field should contain an integer". when the failed form is re-rendered in the browser. 

This issue is also discussed here:
https://stackoverflow.com/a/77712569/1087626

The issue apparently does not exist when dealing with JSON data rather than MIMEApplicationForm

### Checklist

- [x] Dependencies installed
- [x] No typos
- [x] Searched existing issues and docs

### Expected behaviour

For the error returned from `context.bind()` to return some information about which field failed type conversion

### Actual behaviour
The error returned from `context.bind()` contains no information about the form field which failed type conversion. 

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
server as below, then POST a non-integer to be bound into an integer field

$ curl localhost:8080/submit -d"number=10a"
code=400, message=strconv.ParseInt: parsing "10a": invalid syntax, internal=strconv.ParseInt: parsing "10a": invalid syntax
```

### Working code to debug

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/labstack/echo/v4"
)

type DTO struct {
	Number int     `form:"number"`
}

func main() {
	e := echo.New()
	e.POST("/submit", func(c echo.Context) error {
		dto := DTO{}
		if err := c.Bind(&dto); err != nil {
			return c.String(http.StatusBadRequest, err.Error() + "\n")
		}
		return c.String(http.StatusOK, fmt.Sprint(dto) + "\n")

	addr := "127.0.0.1:8080"

problems.title: static middleware: path ist unescaped twice for file names, leading to not downloadable content
problems.issue_body:
### Issue Description

Given a file on disk with a percent sign in its name, it is not possible to download it using echo's static middleware.

Given some file names:
- `100%.txt`
- `foo%20bar.txt` (this is really the name on disk)

It is not possible to download these files using the static middleware.

### Checklist

- [X] Dependencies installed
- [X] No typos
- [X] Searched existing issues and docs

### Expected behaviour

The standard way to download them would be using the folowing paths:

- `100%.txt` -> `GET /100%25.txt`
- `foo%20bar.txt` -> `GET /foo%2520bar.txt`


### Actual behaviour

- `100%.txt` -> `GET /100%25.txt`
  - echo error message: **`invalid URL escape "%.p`** (because of the double unescape and `.p` is no valid hex)
- `foo%20bar.txt` -> `GET /foo%2520bar.txt`
  - echo error message: **`path does not exist`** (because file `foo bar.txt` does not exist, only `foo%20bar.txt`)

Background is that url.Path in http.Request is already escaped (as the documentation for url.Path suggests), but echo is unescaping it again.

I tried to generate a fix. For the non-embedded case this is solved by simply removing the explicit url.PathUnescape call in static.go (see https://github.com/georgmu/echo/commit/852dedeca2a22a0b6967e71f69cbb0823959a198 which also contains some test cases). I haven't created a merge request yet, as the embedding using groups or path patterns is a bit more complicated (I haven't fully understand the case for the disablePathUnescaping toggle).

### Steps to reproduce / Working code to debug

See test cases in https://github.com/georgmu/echo/commit/852dedeca2a22a0b6967e71f69cbb0823959a198

### Version/commit

master ( commit fa70db8 )

problems.title: fix(static): reject encoded path separator to prevent route-level auth bypass
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Fixes an access-control bypass / static file disclosure where an **encoded slash (`%2F`) lets a request skip a protected route group yet still resolve the file on disk** (GHSA-vfp3-v2gw-7wfq, CWE-22).

The router matches routes against the raw, still-encoded request path, so `%2F` is **not** treated as a path separator — `/admin%2Fsecret.txt` is a single segment and never matches a protected `/admin/*` group. The request falls through to the static handler, which then `url.PathUnescape`d `%2F` back to `/` and resolved `admin/secret.txt` from disk. Router and file handler disagreed on what counts as a separator.

### Reproduction (before)
```
GET /admin/secret.txt    -> 403  (protected group fires)
GET /admin%2Fsecret.txt  -> 200  body="TOP-SECRET"   ← bypass + disclosure
```

Common affected pattern:
```go
adminGroup := e.Group("/admin", authMiddleware)
e.StaticFS("/", os.DirFS("public"))
```

## Fix

`StaticDirectoryHandler` now rejects a wildcard containing an encoded path separator (`%2F`/`%2f` or `%5C`/`%5c`) with `404` **before** unescaping, keeping the router and the file handler consistent. No real filename contains a path separator, so legitimate static requests are unaffected.

## Tests
- New `static_encoded_separator_test.go`: regression test for the bypass + unit test for the `%2F`/`%5C` detector (incl. lower-case hex and a benign `%25` case).
- Updated the existing `TestEcho_StaticFS` "open redirect" case: `…%2f..` now returns `404` with **no redirect emitted at all** (was a sanitized `301`), which closes that vector harder.
- `go test ./ ./middleware/` and `go vet ./` pass.

## Scope / notes
- This addresses the **static-disclosure** vector. The related report GHSA-xr3h-5475-xgqr (percent-encoded routing bypassing protected middleware on *non-static* routes) is a broader router-level decision and is intentionally **not** included here.
- Reported by @a-tt-om and @oran-gugu.
