problems.title: [Bug]: Predefined **Junk**, **Incubator**, and **Shard** tokens spawn without their printed activated abilities
problems.issue_body:
# Summary

`predefined_token_abilities` in `crates/engine/src/game/effects/token.rs` returns abilities for Food, Clue, Treasure, etc., but explicitly leaves **Junk**, **Incubator** (transform), and **Shard** as a TODO (`_ => vec![]`). Many cards create `Junk` tokens (Fallout / Universes Beyond); `known-tokens.toml` already defines Junk rules text, yet created tokens have **no** `{T}, Sacrifice…` ability on the battlefield.

# Impact

- **Cards broken:** Break Down, Boomer Scrapper, Crimson Caravaneer, Junktown, and other `CreatableToken::Junk` sources — tokens are inert artifacts.
- **Broader:** Incubator / Shard predefined tokens (Phyrexian / etc.) lack transform or sacrifice abilities until implemented.

# Steps to reproduce

1. In a test game or scenario, resolve an effect that creates a **Junk** token (e.g. **Break Down** destroying an artifact/enchantment).
2. Select the Junk token on the battlefield.
3. Attempt to activate `{T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Exile the top card…` (sorcery speed).

# Expected behavior

The token has the predefined activated ability from CR 111.10 / oracle text in `known-tokens.toml` (`rules_text` for subtype `Junk`), activatable at sorcery speed.

# Actual behavior

`predefined_token_abilities("Junk")` returns an empty vector; the token has no activated abilities. Same for Incubator/Shard until the TODO is implemented.

# Additional information

- **Suggested fix:** Add `junk_ability()`, incubator transform handling, and shard ability helpers; keep `predefined_token_abilities` and `predefined_token_rules_text` in sync (file comment requires paired edits).

problems.title: Engine: en-Kor damage redirection ('the next N damage that would be dealt to ~ … is dealt to target creature instead') i
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The en-Kor cycle's activated ability parses its effect clause to `Effect::Unimplemented`, so it doesn't function. The ability — `{0}: The next 1 damage that would be dealt to this creature this turn is dealt to target creature you control instead.` — is shared by all six en-Kor creatures.

## Affected cards

Nomads en-Kor, Lancers en-Kor, Outrider en-Kor, Shaman en-Kor, Spirit en-Kor, Warrior en-Kor (all six print the identical ability; Shaman en-Kor additionally has the already-supported active-voice variant).

## What the CR requires

CR 614.9: this is a one-shot damage *redirection* — the next 1 damage that would be dealt to the en-Kor creature is instead dealt to a chosen creature you control. The shield is consumed on its single use (CR 614.5) and expires at end of turn (CR 514.2).

## Current behavior

The `Effect::CreateDamageReplacement` infrastructure already exists (Soltari Guerrillas, Beacon of Destiny, Jade Monolith), but the parser only recognizes the active-voice `the next time [source] would deal damage …` framing. The en-Kor passive-voice `the next N damage that would be dealt to ~ … is dealt to [target] instead` framing isn't matched, so the clause falls to `Unimplemented`.

## Expected behavior

Resolving the ability creates a one-shot redirection shield on the en-Kor creature; the next damage dealt to it this turn is redirected to the chosen creature.

## Component

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_replacement.rs` (parser)
- `crates/engine/src/game/effects/create_damage_replacement.rs` (resolver — self recipient)

problems.title: [Bug]: `CantCrew` / "can't crew Vehicles" is never parsed or enforced in crew (and saddle) eligibility (CR 702.122c)
problems.issue_body:
# Summary

Auras and effects such as **Bound in Gold** grant `CantCrew` in `data/mtgish-cards.json`, but the engine has no `StaticMode::CantCrew`, no oracle parser for "can't crew Vehicles" (including the compound line "can't attack, block, or crew Vehicles"), and no filtering in `handle_crew_activation` / `handle_crew_announcement` (or saddle handlers). Enchanted creatures can still be tapped to crew a Vehicle.

# Impact

- **Rules correctness:** Violates CR 702.122c — creatures with "can't crew Vehicles" must not be legal crew costs.
- **Cards affected:** Bound in Gold, Intercessor's Arrest, Revoke Privileges, and any other card emitting `PermanentRule::CantCrew` in mtgish data.

# Steps to reproduce

1. Start a game with a Vehicle on the battlefield (e.g. **Smuggler's Copter**) and a creature with total power ≥ crew cost.
2. Enchant that creature with **Bound in Gold** (or apply equivalent `CantAttack` + `CantBlock` + `CantCrew` statics).
3. Activate the Vehicle's crew ability during your main phase with an empty stack.
4. Select the enchanted creature as a crew cost.

# Expected behavior

The enchanted creature is **not** offered as an eligible crew creature, and selecting it (if sent via `GameAction::CrewVehicle`) is rejected. Per Gatherer ruling on Bound in Gold: a creature that "can't crew Vehicles" can't be tapped to pay the crew cost.

# Actual behavior

`handle_crew_activation` only filters by controller, untapped, and creature type; a TODO at `crates/engine/src/game/engine.rs` (~5086) notes CR 702.122c is unimplemented. The enchanted creature remains eligible and can crew the Vehicle.

# Additional information

**Suggested fix areas:**
  - Add `StaticMode::CantCrew` and parse `"can't crew"` / `"cannot crew"` / `"or crew Vehicles"` compound fragments.
  - Filter `eligible_creatures` in `handle_crew_activation` and re-validate in `handle_crew_announcement` via `object_has_active_static` or dedicated helper.
  - Consider the same filter for `handle_saddle_activation` if saddle restrictions share wording on future cards.

problems.title: Engine: characteristic-defining P/T counting 'the chosen player' is unimplemented (Entropic Specter, Sewer Nemesis, Lost
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Several creatures with a characteristic-defining ability (CR 604.3) set their power and toughness equal to a count relative to **"the chosen player"** — the player chosen by an "As ~ enters the battlefield, choose a player" replacement. These P/T lines parse to `Effect::Unimplemented`, so the creatures have no defined P/T.

## Affected cards

- **Entropic Specter** — "~'s power and toughness are each equal to the number of cards in the chosen player's hand."
- **Sewer Nemesis** — "... the number of cards in the chosen player's graveyard."
- **Lost Order of Jarkeld** — "... 1 plus the number of creatures the chosen player controls."

(Skyshroud War Beast — "nonbasic lands the chosen player controls" — is blocked by a separate "nonbasic" type-phrase gap and is out of scope here.)

## What the CR requires

CR 604.3 / CR 613.1: the CDA continuously sets P/T to the count. "The chosen player" is the player persisted on the permanent via the ETB "choose a player" replacement — the same `ChosenAttribute::Player` mechanism that backs Siege protectors.

## Current behavior

The ETB choice already parses and persists the chosen player, and the dynamic-P/T effect (`SetDynamicPower` / `SetDynamicToughness`) already exists. But the quantity parser doesn't recognize "the chosen player controls" / "the chosen player's <zone>", so the P/T clause falls to `Unimplemented`.

## Component

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_nom/quantity.rs` (quantity parsing)
- `crates/engine/src/types/ability.rs` (`ControllerRef` / `PlayerScope`)
- `crates/engine/src/game/{filter,quantity}.rs` (resolution)

problems.title: [Bug]: "target creature attacks you this combat if able" (Alluring Siren class) forces the creature to attack ANY player
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Effects that force a creature to **attack a specific player** — "[target creature] attacks **you** this combat if able" (Alluring Siren, Dulcet Sirens, Public Enemy, …) — only require the creature to attack **something**, not the named player. The player target is recognized by the parser and then **thrown away**: the clause lowers to a generic `StaticMode::MustAttack`, so the affected creature satisfies the requirement by attacking a *different* player or planeswalker, dodging the lure entirely.

The parser even says so. `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_effect/imperative.rs` `try_parse_attack_if_able`:

```rust
/// Handles bare forms ("attacks this turn if able") and player-targeted forms
/// ("attacks you this turn if able", "attacks that opponent this combat if able",
/// "attacks target opponent this turn if able"). The player target is currently
/// not enforced at runtime — MustAttack forces the creature to attack if able,
/// but the specific-player constraint requires additional engine support.
```

This is the **attack-side analog** of the already-fixed forced-block bug (#1838 — "blocks ~ this turn if able" must block the *specific* attacker): the same "specific target dropped → generic requirement" defect, on the attack side.

## Cards (a class, not a one-off)

The source data carries `MustAttackPlayer` on **17 cards**, including:

- **Alluring Siren** — "{T}: Target creature an opponent controls attacks you this turn if able."
- **Dulcet Sirens** — "{2}, {T}: Target creature attacks [chosen player] this turn if able."
- **Public Enemy / A-Public Enemy**, **Knight Rampager**, **Ravener**, **City of the Daleks**, **Furygale Flocking**, … — "attacks [you / that player] this/each combat if able."

These are classic "lure into a bad attack" effects whose entire point is *which* player gets attacked.

## Expected

Per CR 508.1d, a creature with a "must attack [player] if able" requirement must, if able, be declared as an attacker **attacking that player** (or a planeswalker that player controls). If it can legally attack the named player but is declared attacking someone else — or not declared at all — the attack declaration is illegal. (This mirrors goad's "must attack a player other than the goading player" enforcement, but pins a *specific* player rather than "anyone but X".)

## Actual

The clause lowers to a bare `StaticMode::MustAttack` (`target: None`). Combat requires only that the creature attack *some* defender — so it can attack a different player/planeswalker, and Alluring Siren's lure does nothing meaningful.

## Root cause

### 1. The parser discards the player target

`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_effect/imperative.rs` — `try_parse_attack_if_able` strips the verb, *skips over the player phrase*, matches the duration suffix, and emits `must_attack_static_definition()` (a bare `StaticMode::MustAttack`) with `target: None`. Every branch (bare, player-targeted, scan-for-suffix) returns the same generic static; the "…

problems.title: A static "[subject] gets +N/+M and can't be blocked[…]" drops the evasion clause — the can't-be-blocked grant never pars
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

When a static ability pairs a P/T (or keyword) grant with a can't-be-blocked grant under one subject — "Enchanted creature gets +3/+0 **and can't be blocked by more than one creature**" — the static parser produces only the P/T grant and **silently drops the "and can't be blocked…" clause**.

`parse_static_line_multi_inner` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/shared.rs`) decomposes a grant followed by a second, structurally-different grant via dedicated splitters in `oracle_static/evasion.rs` — `try_split_and_can_attack_despite_defender`, `try_split_and_must_attack_block`, and `try_split_and_can_block_additional`. There is **no equivalent splitter for "and can't be blocked"**, so the compound line falls through to the single continuous-grant path, which merges/keeps the P/T modification and discards the evasion remainder. The standalone can't-be-blocked branches (grammar.rs / dispatch.rs) only fire when the predicate *begins* with "can't be blocked", so they are never reached for the compound form.

## Failure mode (concrete example)

**Madcap Skills** (Aura) — "Enchanted creature gets +3/+0 and can't be blocked by more than one creature."

`parse_static_line_multi("Enchanted creature gets +3/+0 and can't be blocked by more than one creature.")` returns a single `StaticDefinition`:

```
[ Continuous { affected: creature[EnchantedBy], mods: [AddPower(+3), AddToughness(0)] } ]
```

The `CantBeBlockedByMoreThan { max: 1 }` grant is absent. In-game, Madcap Skills gives +3/+0 but its enchanted creature can be blocked by any number of creatures — the evasion half of the card does nothing. The same drop affects the whole class "[subject] gets/has X and can't be blocked [by <filter> | except by <filter> | by more than N creatures]" (bare → `CantBeBlocked`, by → `CantBeBlockedBy`, except by → `CantBeBlockedExceptBy`).

(Distinct from #1840/#1861, which fixed the *standalone* "can't be blocked by more than N" enforcement. This is the *compound* line dropping the clause.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. `parse_static_line_multi("Enchanted creature gets +3/+0 and can't be blocked by more than one creature.")`.
2. Observe the result contains only the P/T `Continuous` def — no `CantBeBlocked*` static.

## Expected behavior

The line decomposes into two static definitions sharing the enchanted-creature affected set: the +3/+0 grant **and** a `StaticMode::CantBeBlockedByMoreThan { max: 1 }` grant (and the parallel `CantBeBlocked` / `CantBeBlockedBy` / `CantBeBlockedExceptBy` for the other tail shapes).

## Actual behavior

Only the P/T grant is produced; the evasion clause is dropped, so the creature gains no blocking restriction on its blockers.

## Suggested fix

Add a static-clause splitter `try_split_and_cant_be_blocked` (in `oracle_static/evasion.rs`), mirroring `try_split_and_can_block_additional`:

- Use `scan_preceded` to locate the "and can't be blocked …" conjunction at a word boundary; classify the tail into the right `StaticMode` (`CantBe…

problems.title: Conversion / Glaciers: "All Mountains are Plains" land type-change static is Unimplemented

## Summary

`parse_land_type_change_subject` in `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/type_change.rs` recognizes the land-type-change subjects `"nonbasic lands"` (Blood Moon), `"lands you control"` (Celestial Dawn), `"each land"` / `"all lands"`, and `"enchanted land"`, but **not** a subject filtered by a specific basic land subtype (`"All Mountains"`). So a global `"All <basic land type> are <basic land type>"` static fails the subject parse and produces no static ability.

`Conversion` / `Glaciers` — "All Mountains are Plains." `parse_land_type_change` splits on `" are "` → subject `"All Mountains"` → `parse_land_type_change_subject` returns `None` → the whole parser returns `None`, so the `SetBasicLandType` modification is never built and the card's `static_abilities` is empty.

## Expected behavior

"All Mountains are Plains" should produce a continuous static affecting every permanent with the **Mountain** basic land subtype (any controller), with modification `SetBasicLandType { land_type: Plains }` (CR 305.7) — the same shape as Blood Moon's "Nonbasic lands are Mountains", but with the subject filtered by basic land subtype instead of the nonbasic supertype. This is a building block for the whole "All `<basic land type>` are `<basic land type>`" class, not a single card.

## Component

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/type_change.rs` — `parse_land_type_change_subject`.

Unknown

When The Cyber-Controller enters, opponents mill X cards, but the creature cards milled this way are not all put onto the battlefield face down as 2/2 Cyberman artifact creatures.

problems.title: Reckless Cohort: 'attacks each combat if able unless you control X' rule-static is Unimplemented
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`parse_subject_rule_static` in `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/evasion.rs` strips the subject and classifies the remaining predicate with `parse_rule_static_predicate`. A trailing `"unless you control <X>"` clause makes that classification fail (the predicate is no longer a recognized rule-static), so the whole line falls through to `Unimplemented` — there is no path that attaches the "unless you control" rider as a condition.

## Failure mode

- `Reckless Cohort` — "This creature attacks each combat if able **unless you control another Ally**."
- `Marauding Maulhorn` — "This creature attacks each combat if able **unless you control a creature named Advocate of the Beast**."

The base `"attacks each combat if able"` is a `MustAttack` rule-static (Juggernaut parses fine), but the trailing `"unless you control <X>"` prevents the predicate from parsing, so `static_abilities` is empty.

## Expected behavior

`"<rule-static> unless you control <X>"` should produce the base rule-static (`MustAttack` here) with `condition = Not(you control <X>)`, so the requirement applies only while the controller does **not** control `<X>` (CR 508.1d / CR 604.1). This should generalize over any rule-static predicate carrying the same `"unless you control"` rider, reusing the existing control-presence condition parser — not a single card.

## Component

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/evasion.rs` — `parse_subject_rule_static`.

problems.title: [Bug]: "can't have or gain [keyword]" is dropped at parse time and never enforced — the Archetype cycle / Arcane Lightho
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The **"... and can't have or gain [keyword]"** clause — the *denial* half of the Theros **Archetype** cycle and **Arcane Lighthouse** — has no effect. The parser handles the "lose [keyword]" half (emits `RemoveKeyword`) but **drops** the "can't have or gain" half entirely, and the `StaticMode::CantHaveKeyword` variant that should model it is **never produced and never enforced**.

Net result: opponents *temporarily* lose the keyword, but can immediately **re-gain** it from any other source (an anthem, an aura, another grant), because the "can't have or gain" denial isn't applied. Archetype of Aggression is supposed to make it so your opponents' creatures **can't have trample at all** — currently a single other trample-granter undoes it.

## Cards (a played class)

- **Archetype of Aggression** — "Creatures you control have trample. Creatures your opponents control lose trample and **can't have or gain trample**." (and the full cycle):
- **Archetype of Courage** (first strike), **Archetype of Endurance** (hexproof), **Archetype of Finality** (deathtouch), **Archetype of Imagination** (flying) — a known Constructed/Commander cycle whose whole point is the denial.
- **Arcane Lighthouse** — "… creatures your opponents control lose hexproof and shroud and **can't have or be granted hexproof or shroud** until end of turn." (Commander staple).
- Other "can't gain [keyword/ability]" denial cards.

## Expected

Per **CR 613.1f** (Layer 6): "*Ability-adding effects, keyword counters, ability-removing effects, and effects that say an object **can't have an ability** are applied.*" A "can't have or gain [keyword]" effect is a layer-6 ability-denial: while it applies to an object, that object does not have the named keyword **even if another effect would grant it** — the grant is suppressed (and any keyword counters of that ability do nothing).

## Actual

The denial clause is discarded by the parser, and `CantHaveKeyword` is a dead static (produced nowhere, read nowhere). So the keyword is only removed at the instant the Archetype/Lighthouse applies its own `RemoveKeyword`; any concurrent or later grant re-adds it freely.

## Root cause

### 1. Parser drops the "can't have or gain" half

`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/keyword_grant.rs:542-549` — when it recognizes the "can't have or gain [keyword]" sub-clause it emits only the `RemoveKeyword` for the lose-half and leaves a literal TODO note instead of producing the static:

```rust
if let Some(kw) = map_keyword(kw_text.trim().trim_end_matches('.')) {
    modifications.push(ContinuousModification::RemoveKeyword { keyword: kw.clone() });
    // Note: CantHaveKeyword is a StaticMode variant, not a ContinuousModification.
    // It will be handled at the static definition level.   // <-- never actually happens
}
```

No `StaticMode::CantHaveKeyword` is ever constructed here (or anywhere in the parser).

### 2. `CantHaveKeyword` is never enforced

`crates/engine/src/types/statics.rs:926` defi…

When a static ability pairs a P/T grant with a can't-block restriction under one subject — "Equipped creature gets +2/+2 **and can't block**" — the static parser produces only the P/T grant and **silently drops the "and can't block" clause**.

problems.title: `StaticMode::CantBeTargeted` is parsed but never enforced — "can't be the target of spells or abilities" is a silent no-
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Permanents whose Oracle text says they **"can't be the target of spells or abilities"** (the descriptive, non-keyworded form of Shroud / Hexproof) currently do **nothing**. The parser recognizes the phrase and produces `StaticMode::CantBeTargeted`, but **no game code ever enforces that mode** — `can_target` checks Shroud, Hexproof, Hexproof-from, and protection, but never `CantBeTargeted`. The restriction is inert: opponents (and everyone else) can freely target the permanent.

There is a second, compounding defect: the parser **drops the targeting-source qualifier** ("…your opponents control", "…\[color] spells", etc.). Both production sites collapse every variant into a single bare, scope-less `CantBeTargeted`, so even if the mode *were* enforced it would model the wrong rule (blanket Shroud instead of opponent-only Hexproof).

This is the direct sibling of **#1929 / #1930** ("`StaticMode::IgnoreHexproof` is never produced/enforced by targeting, CR 702.11e"), which was accepted and fixed in `targeting.rs`.

## Evidence

**Parser produces it (two sites):**

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/dispatch.rs:1287` — `"~ can't be the target"` / `"~ can't be targeted"` → `StaticMode::CantBeTargeted` with `affected: TargetFilter::SelfRef`.
- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_effect/subject.rs:2653` — `"can't be the target of …"` → `StaticMode::CantBeTargeted` (the `of <scope>` tail is matched then discarded).

**Nothing enforces it.** `grep -rn "StaticMode::CantBeTargeted" crates/engine/src/game/` returns a single hit — the registry stub:

```
crates/engine/src/game/static_abilities.rs:61:  registry.insert(StaticMode::CantBeTargeted, handle_rule_mod);
```

`handle_rule_mod` is a no-op marker; the actual restriction is supposed to be enforced at the query site (`can_target`), exactly like Shroud/Hexproof. But `can_target` ([targeting.rs:1326-1367](crates/engine/src/game/targeting.rs#L1326-L1367)) never consults it:

```rust
fn can_target(obj, source_controller, source_id, state) -> bool {
    if obj.has_keyword(&Keyword::Shroud) { return false; }      // CR 702.18a
    // … Hexproof (702.11a), HexproofFrom (702.11d), protection …
    if is_protected_from(obj, source_id, state) { return false; }
    true   // <-- StaticMode::CantBeTargeted is never checked
}
```

So `obj.assigns…` aside, a card reading "Enchanted creature can't be the target of spells or abilities" parses to a typed, registered, inert static.

## Comprehensive Rules

- **CR 702.18a**: *"Shroud is a static ability. 'Shroud' means 'This permanent or player can't be the target of spells or abilities.'"* — the unqualified phrase **is, verbatim, the definition of Shroud.**
- **CR 702.11a / 702.11**: Hexproof — can't be the target of spells or abilities **opponents control** (the "…your opponents control" variant).
- **CR 702.11d**: "Hexproof from \[quality]" — can't be the target of \[quality] spells/abilities opponents control (the "…\[color] spells your opponents control" v…

problems.title: Afflict, Training, and Poisonous keywords are parsed but have no runtime trigger (silent no-op)
problems.issue_body:
### Summary
Three triggered-ability keywords are parsed and typed (so coverage reports them green) but have **no runtime trigger** — they are silent no-ops in actual games: **Afflict, Training, Poisonous**. `KeywordTriggerInstaller::triggers_for` falls through to `_ => Vec::new()` for each, so nothing is installed onto the card.

### Impact (~28 cards)
Afflict (~13), Training (~13), Poisonous (~2). On these cards the keyword does nothing — the defending player never loses life when an Afflict creature is blocked, a Training creature never grows when it attacks alongside a bigger creature, and a Poisonous creature deals combat damage without handing out poison counters.

### Expected behavior (CR)
- **Afflict N** (702.130a): whenever this creature becomes blocked, the defending player loses N life. Each instance triggers separately (702.130b).
- **Training** (702.149a): whenever this creature and at least one other creature with power greater than this creature's power attack, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature. Each instance triggers separately (702.149b).
- **Poisonous N** (702.70a): whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, that player gets N poison counters. Each instance triggers separately (702.70b).

### Actual behavior
No trigger fires. `triggers_for(&Keyword::Afflict(_) | &Keyword::Training | &Keyword::Poisonous(_))` returns an empty `Vec`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Put a creature with any of these keywords onto the battlefield.
2. Afflict: attack and have it blocked → defending player's life is unchanged. Training: attack alongside a higher-power creature → no +1/+1 counter is placed. Poisonous: deal combat damage to a player → that player gains no poison counters.

### Notes
Each should be synthesized in `synthesis.rs` mirroring the existing Bushido/Flanking/Mentor/Exalted synthesizers, reusing existing trigger modes (`BecomesBlocked` / `Attacks` / `DamageDone`+`CombatOnly`), the `LoseLife` / `PutCounter` / `GivePlayerCounter` effects, and the `DefendingPlayer` / `TriggeringPlayer` target filters — no new variants. Training's "higher-power co-attacker" gate is a one-field parameterization of the existing `MinCoAttackers` intervening-if condition (optional co-attacker `filter`), mirroring the sibling `AttackersDeclaredMin { minimum, filter }`.

### Component
- `crates/engine/src/database/synthesis.rs` (`triggers_for` / keyword trigger synthesizers)

problems.title: A static "[subject] gets +N/+M and can't attack" drops the can't-attack clause — the drawback never parses (Cagemail doe
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

When a static ability pairs a P/T (or keyword) grant with a plain attacking restriction under one subject — "Enchanted creature gets +2/+2 **and can't attack**" — the static parser produces only the P/T grant and **silently drops the "and can't attack" clause**.

`parse_static_line_multi_inner` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/shared.rs`) decomposes a grant followed by a structurally-different second clause via dedicated `try_split_and_*` splitters in `oracle_static/evasion.rs` (despite-defender, must-attack/block, can-block-an-additional-creature, can't-be-blocked, can't-block). There is **no splitter for "and can't attack"**, and the continuous-grant default (`grammar.rs` / `keyword_grant.rs::parse_continuous_modifications`) has no arm that maps "can't attack" to anything — `CantAttack` is a `StaticMode`, not a `ContinuousModification` — so the clause produces zero modifications and vanishes.

## Failure mode (concrete example)

**Cagemail** (Aura, Commander 2017) — "Enchanted creature gets +2/+2 and can't attack."

`parse_static_line_multi("Enchanted creature gets +2/+2 and can't attack.")` returns a single `StaticDefinition`:

```
[ Continuous { affected: creature[EnchantedBy], mods: [AddPower(+2), AddToughness(+2)] } ]
```

The `CantAttack` static is absent. In-game, Cagemail is a *downside* Aura: it makes a bigger creature that **cannot attack** (typically placed on an opponent's threat, or used with control-swapping). With the bug the enchanted creature gets +2/+2 but can **still attack normally** — the entire drawback is missing, making the card strictly better than printed.

(`CantAttack` is genuinely a parse drop, not a missing feature: it exists as a `StaticMode` and is runtime-enforced at declare-attackers in `game/combat.rs`. This is distinct from #1921/#1922's "can't attack **alone**", and from the scoped/directed "can't attack **you** or planeswalkers you control" restriction tracked separately under #2261 — that form needs a player-scoped attack mode and is not addressed here.)

## Steps to reproduce

1. `parse_static_line_multi("Enchanted creature gets +2/+2 and can't attack.")`.
2. Observe the result contains only the P/T `Continuous` def — no `CantAttack` static.

## Expected behavior

The line decomposes into two static definitions sharing the affected set: the +2/+2 grant **and** a `StaticMode::CantAttack` grant.

## Actual behavior

Only the P/T grant is produced; the can't-attack clause is dropped, so the enchanted creature can still attack.

## Suggested fix

Add a `try_split_and_cant_attack` splitter (in `oracle_static/evasion.rs`), mirroring `try_split_and_cant_block`:

- Use `scan_preceded` to locate the "and can't attack" conjunction at a word boundary (matching both the ASCII and U+2019 apostrophe), consuming an optional trailing duration.
- Apply a **terminal-phrase guard**: only split when nothing follows "can't attack" (after trimming a trailing period). This keeps it disjoint from "can't attack…

problems.title: Parser drops Condition_Unless clauses while coverage still marks affected cards supported
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`./scripts/gen-card-data.sh` reports `63` `Swallow:Condition_Unless` diagnostics across `63` cards. `62` of those cards are otherwise marked supported by coverage, so `unless` restrictions or alternative costs may be missing from exported AST while coverage stays green.

Related umbrella/context issue: #2229 (`Condition_If` swallowed clauses).

## Repro

```bash
./scripts/gen-card-data.sh
target/tool/coverage-report data --all --warning-detector Condition_Unless --warning-limit 5
```

Fresh drilldown:

```text
matched_cards: 63
supported_cards: 62
single_gap_cards: 0
examples: Arboria, Awesome Presence, Barbarian Bully, Blazing Salvo, Chained Throatseeker
```

## Example Patterns

- `can't attack ... unless that player cast a spell...`
- `can't be blocked unless defending player pays...`
- `gets +2/+2 ... unless a player has this creature deal damage...`
- `deals damage ... unless that creature's controller...`
- `can't attack unless defending player is poisoned`

## Expected

`unless` clauses should be represented as typed conditions, costs, restrictions, or branch alternatives. If unsupported, they should not be silently dropped from a supported card.

problems.title: Demonstrate keyword is parsed but has no runtime behavior (copy-on-cast unimplemented)
problems.issue_body:
### Summary
The **Demonstrate** keyword (CR 702.144a) is parsed and typed (so coverage reports it green) but has **no runtime behavior** — there is no `synthesize_*` pass for it, so casting a Demonstrate spell never copies it. ~9 cards.

### Impact (~9 cards)
The Strixhaven Demonstrate spells. On these cards the "you may copy it; if you do, an opponent also copies it" ability does nothing.

### Expected behavior (CR 702.144a)
"When you cast this spell, you may copy it and you may choose new targets for the copy. If you copy the spell, choose an opponent. That player copies the spell and may choose new targets for that copy."

### Actual behavior
`Keyword::Demonstrate` is parsed but no copy-on-cast trigger is installed; nothing happens when the spell is cast.

### Notes
The missing primitive is "another player copies the spell": `Effect::CopySpell` copies only for the effect controller (or, in the Chain cycle, a player named by an inherited `TargetRef::Player`). Demonstrate needs a *chosen opponent* to copy — a parameterization of the copier axis, not a new effect. Implement as a `SpellCast` self-copy trigger (mirroring Casualty/Replicate) whose sub-ability copies for the opponent, reusing the existing copy resolver + chain/`pending_continuation` sequencing.

### Component
- `crates/engine/src/types/ability.rs` (`Effect::CopySpell` copier axis)
- `crates/engine/src/game/effects/copy_spell.rs` (resolve the copier)
- `crates/engine/src/database/synthesis.rs` (new `synthesize_demonstrate` pass wired into `synthesize_all`)

## Summary

The compound **"can't attack/block, and activated abilities can't be activated"** (Arrest, Faith's Fetters) has a dedicated branch, and the **standalone** "its activated abilities can't be activated" is handled in `dispatch.rs`. But the **continuous-grant + activation-prohibition** compound has no owner — `CantBeActivated` is a struct `StaticMode`, not a `ContinuousModification`, so the continuous-grant default drops it.

(`CantBeActivated` is genuinely a parse drop, not a missing feature: it exists as a struct `StaticMode`, is produced by the standalone and Arrest-compound paths, and is runtime-enforced per CR 602.5.)

The line decomposes into the grant static(s) **and** a `CantBeActivated` static (self-reference: every player is prohibited from activating the affected permanent's own activated abilities), matching the standalone / Arrest-compound output.

Only the grant is produced; the activation-prohibition clause is dropped.

Add a `try_split_and_cant_activate_abilities` splitter (in `oracle_static/evasion.rs`), mirroring `try_split_and_cant_block`:

- Re-parse the first conjunct via `parse_static_line_multi`, then append a `CantBeActivated { who: AllPlayers, source_filter: SelfRef, exemption }` static built exactly like the standalone / Arrest-compound path (`parse_cant_be_activated_exemption_in_text` for any…

problems.title: [Bug]: Compound static `"… gets +X/+Y and can't be the target of spells"` silently drops the targeting restriction (Spec
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

A compound static ability that pairs a first clause (P/T change, keyword grant, or another restriction) with a **"can't be the target of …"** clause under one subject **drops the targeting restriction entirely**. Only the first conjunct survives; the `CantBeTargeted` static is never produced.

`parse_static_line_multi_inner` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/shared.rs`) has `try_split_and_*` splitters for every other compound shape — despite-defender, must-attack/block, can-block-additional, can't-be-blocked, can't-block, can't-attack, doesn't-untap, can't-activate-abilities, can't-be-sacrificed, and (added in #2452) **can't-be-enchanted/equipped** — but **none for "and can't be the target of …"**. Because `CantBeTargeted` is a `StaticMode` (not a `ContinuousModification`), the continuous-grant default path has no arm for it either, so the clause produces no modifications and is discarded.

This is the exact same root-cause pattern that #2452 fixed for attach prohibitions, applied to the targeting-restriction clause.

## Real card examples

- **Spectral Shield** — `Enchant creature` / *"Enchanted creature gets +0/+2 and can't be the target of spells."*
  The shroud-from-spells protection — the entire point of the card — is silently lost; the Aura behaves like a vanilla +0/+2.

The fix generalizes to the whole class of compound statics whose trailing conjunct is a targeting restriction (any first clause × any `can't be the target of {spells | abilities | spells and abilities | <color> spells | spells your opponents control}` tail), mirroring the eight existing `try_split_and_*` splitters.

## Steps to reproduce

```rust
use engine::parser::oracle_static::parse_static_line_multi;

// Spectral Shield
let defs = parse_static_line_multi(
    "Enchanted creature gets +0/+2 and can't be the target of spells.",
);
// Actual:   defs.len() == 1  -> [Continuous (+0/+2)]   <-- targeting restriction DROPPED
// Expected: defs.len() == 2  -> [Continuous (+0/+2), CantBeTargeted]
```

Diagnostic output (parser, current `main`):

```
"Enchanted creature gets +0/+2 and can't be the target of spells." => 1 defs
        mode=Continuous mods=[AddPower { value: 0 }, AddToughness { value: 2 }]

# standalone clause parses correctly on its own:
"Enchanted creature can't be the target of spells."               => 1 defs
        mode=CantBeTargeted mods=[]
```

The standalone clause is recognized as `StaticMode::CantBeTargeted`; only the **compound** form loses it — a clean splitter-drop.

## Expected behavior

`parse_static_line_multi` should decompose the compound into **two** `StaticDefinition`s:
1. the first conjunct (`Continuous` / `AddPower 0` / `AddToughness 2`), and
2. a `CantBeTargeted` static sharing the first conjunct's `affected` filter (`EnchantedBy`/`SelfRef`),

so the enchanted creature can't be targeted by spells (CR 702.18a Shroud for the unqualified form; CR 702.11a Hexproof for the "… your opponents control" variant, per the scope class…

problems.title: [Bug]: "During any turn you attacked with [a token / a commander / three or more creatures]" — filtered attack-history c
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The parser recognizes the bare attack-history condition ("you attacked this turn" → `ParsedCondition::YouAttackedThisTurn`, with `FilterProp::AttackedThisTurn` / `state.creatures_attacked_this_turn` runtime tracking). But the **filtered** form — *"During any turn you attacked with `<filter>`"* — is **not parsed**, so the gating clause is dropped and the dependent permission ("you may play that card") never functions.

This is a coherent class on recent, constructed/Commander-relevant cards, all using the same shape: *"… exile [card(s)]. During any turn you attacked with `<filter>`, you may play `<that/those>` card(s)."*

| Card | Clause | Filter |
|---|---|---|
| **Neyali, Suns' Vanguard** | "During any turn you attacked with a token, you may play that card." | attacked with a **token** |
| **Neriv, Crackling Vanguard** | "During any turn you attacked with a commander, you may play those cards." | attacked with a **commander** |
| **Boros Strike-Captain** | "During any turn you attacked with three or more creatures, you may play that card." | attacked with **≥3 creatures** |
| **Goblin Researcher** | "During any turn you attacked with ~ …" | attacked with **this creature** |
| **Rahilda, Feral Outlaw** | "During any turn you attacked with a Wolf or Werewolf …" | attacked with a **Wolf/Werewolf** |

Without the condition, Neyali/Neriv/Boros exile cards but the "you may play that card" permission is either always- or never-granted (the turn-gated, filtered condition is lost).

## Steps to reproduce

Parse any of the above; the trailing "During any turn you attacked with `<filter>` …" sentence is unrecognized (Unimplemented / dropped). The bare "if you attacked this turn" form parses; only the `with <filter>` qualifier (and the "three or more" count) is unhandled.

"During any turn you attacked with `<filter>`" (and the "N or more creatures" count form) should produce a condition that is true on a turn in which the controller declared one or more attackers matching `<filter>` (with the count threshold where present). The runtime can evaluate this directly against the existing `state.creatures_attacked_this_turn` set.

## Actual behavior

The filtered condition is unparsed → the clause is dropped, and the gated permission ("you may play that card") is not correctly conditioned.

problems.title: [Bug]: "Each [card] in your graveyard/hand has scavenge / foretell / encore. Its cost is equal to its mana cost" is unpa
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The engine already parses the graveyard keyword-grant family — `try_parse_graveyard_keyword_grant_clause` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/keyword_grant.rs`) recognizes *"Each `<filter>` card in your graveyard has `<keyword>`"* for **Flashback / Escape / Mayhem** (its `GraveyardGrantedKeywordKind` enum). But three real, coherent variants are unparsed, so the whole static is dropped (`Unimplemented`):

- **Scavenge** (graveyard) — "Each creature card in your graveyard has **scavenge**. The scavenge cost is equal to its mana cost." (Varolz, the Scar-Striped; Young Deathclaws; The Cave of Skulls)
- **Encore** (graveyard) — "Each artifact creature card in your graveyard has **encore**. Its encore cost is equal to its mana cost." (Wire Surgeons)
- **Foretell** (hand) — "Each nonland card in your hand without foretell has **foretell**. Its foretell cost is equal to its mana cost reduced by {2}." (Dream Devourer; Bohn, Beguiling Balladeer; Singing Towers of Darillium)

The granted keywords themselves are implemented (`Keyword::Scavenge(ManaCost)`, `Keyword::Foretell(ManaCost)`, `Keyword::Encore(ManaCost)`); what's missing is recognizing/wiring the **grant** of these keywords to a filtered set of cards in a zone, with a per-card cost derived from mana cost.

Two distinct gaps:
1. `GraveyardGrantedKeywordKind` covers only **cast-from-graveyard** keywords (Flashback/Escape/Mayhem). Scavenge and Encore are **activated abilities from the graveyard** (exile-and-pay), not casting — they need representation beyond the current enum/runtime.
2. The parser hard-requires the **graveyard** zone (`target_filter_is_your_graveyard`); Foretell is granted to cards in the **hand**, and its cost is "mana cost **reduced by {N}**", not a bare "equal to its mana cost".

## Real card examples (all currently dropped)

| Card | Clause |
|---|---|
| **Varolz, the Scar-Striped** | "Each creature card in your graveyard has scavenge. The scavenge cost is equal to its mana cost." |
| **Young Deathclaws** | (same scavenge grant) |

| **Bohn, Beguiling Balladeer / Singing Towers of Darillium** | (foretell grants) |

Varolz and Dream Devourer are Commander-played.

Each `<filter>` card in the named zone gains the keyword with the specified cost, so the keyword's existing runtime (scavenge exile-for-counters, encore exile-for-token-copies, foretell pay-and-exile-then-cast) functions from that card.

The static line fails the parser (`Static pattern matched but line failed`) → `Unimplemented`; the grant does nothing.

problems.title: `Effect::TimeTravel` is a no-op — the time travel keyword action does nothing (CR 701.56)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

**Time travel** (Doctor Who Universes Beyond, ~10 cards) is parsed into `Effect::TimeTravel` but the resolver is an explicit **no-op** — `effects/mod.rs:1865` is literally `Effect::TimeTravel => Ok(())`. Cards that say "time travel" (as a spell, a triggered ability, or an activated ability — all three forms are parsed and tested) do nothing: no time counters are ever added or removed, so suspended cards never advance, Vanishing/Fading permanents are never affected, and the strategic payoff (removing the last time counter from a suspended card to cast it early) never happens.

## Evidence

- **Parsed**: `Effect::TimeTravel` is produced for standalone spells, triggers, and activated abilities (parser tests `time_travel_standalone_spell` / `time_travel_in_trigger` / `time_travel_activated_ability`, `parser/oracle.rs:14220+`).
- **No runtime**: the effect dispatch is `Effect::TimeTravel => Ok(())` (`effects/mod.rs:1865`) — a documented no-op registered only so coverage marks the card as supported (the same pattern Forage had before #2559).
- ~10 cards reference it (`grep -oic "timetravel" data/mtgish-cards.json` → 10; the data's structured-rules form spells it `TimeTravel`).
- Time-counter infrastructure already exists and is widely used: 123 suspend references in the card data; `CounterType::Time`; the suspend / vanishing / fading counter machinery.
- Strictly novel: GitHub search (`repo:phase-rs/phase in:title time travel` / `timetravel`) returns **0** issues/PRs.

## Comprehensive Rules

**CR 701.56a** (verified in `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`): *"To time travel means to choose any number of permanents you control with one or more time counters on them and/or suspended cards you own in exile with one or more time counters on them and, for each of those objects, put a time counter on it or remove a time counter from it."*

So time travel is: choose any number of eligible objects (your time-countered permanents **and/or** your suspended exile cards with time counters), then **per object** decide to add or remove one time counter.

## Feasibility — the counters and all the downstream consequences already exist; the new piece is the interactive choice

This is **not** a new subsystem. Time counters and every consequence of changing them are already modeled — the only new work is the interactive selection that drives the existing primitives:

| CR 701.56a clause | Existing mechanism (reused) / new piece |
|---|---|
| "put a time counter on it or remove a time counter from it" | `CounterType::Time` + the existing `PutCounter` / `RemoveCounter` effects (used by Suspend, Vanishing, Fading). |
| consequence: removing the **last** time counter from a suspended card → cast it for free | **Already wired.** The suspend last-counter free-cast trigger is `CounterTriggerFilter { Time, threshold: Some(0) }` (`synthesis.rs:5833`); it fires on the `CounterRemoved` event that a time-travel removal produces — no new code. |
| consequence: removing the last ti…

problems.title: "Controls a [permanent]" condition checks count phased-out permanents (CR 702.26b)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Several "does this player control a [commander / speed permanent / Attraction]?" predicates scan `state.battlefield` with only a controller/owner filter and **no phased-out guard**. Per CR 702.26b a phased-out permanent "is treated as though it does not exist," so it must not satisfy these conditions — but today it does. This is the same bug class as the merged devotion (#2589/#2590) and condition (#2596, the activation/casting condition guards) fixes and the open domain report (#2591); these are additional unguarded outliers in the "controls a permanent" predicate family.

## Affected predicates (all in `crates/engine/src/game/`)

- **`commander.rs::controls_any_commander`** and **`commander.rs::controls_own_commander`** — `state.battlefield.iter().any(|…| controller == player && obj.is_commander …)`. Gate "as long as you control your commander"-style conditions; a phased-out commander (e.g. yours phased out by Teferi's Protection) wrongly keeps satisfying them.
- **`speed.rs::controls_start_your_engines`** (CR 702.179a) — "controls a permanent with [Start your engines]"; a phased-out such permanent wrongly satisfies it.
- **`attractions.rs::controls_attraction`** — "controls an Attraction"; same gap.

Each iterates the raw battlefield (which still holds phased-out permanents — phasing only flips `phase_status`, CR 702.26d) and excludes none.

## Evidence

- `grep -c "is_phased_in\|is_phased_out\|phase_status"` is **0** for `commander.rs` and `attractions.rs`; `speed.rs` has the guard only on its *other* scan (`speed.rs:182`, which routes through `active_static_definitions` and is explicitly commented "CR 702.26b + CR 604.1") — `controls_start_your_engines` at `speed.rs:112` is unguarded.
- The canonical guard already exists and is used by the filter path (`filter.rs:730/1047` → `if obj.is_phased_out() { return false; }`), the devotion fix, and the merged condition fix (#2596).
- Strictly novel: the open/closed CR 702.26b reports are devotion (#2589), domain (#2591), the activation/casting conditions (#2596, mine), mass phase-in (#1864), and aura re-apply (#2373) — none cover these commander/speed/attraction control predicates.

## Comprehensive Rules

**CR 702.26b** (verified in `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`): *"Except for rules and effects that specifically mention phased-out permanents, a phased-out permanent is treated as though it does not exist. It can't affect or be affected by anything else in the game."*

So a phased-out commander / speed permanent / Attraction must not satisfy a "you control a …" condition.

## Why this is valuable

- **Commander-relevant**: `controls_own_commander` / `controls_any_commander` gate real "control your commander" conditions in the format the engine centers on; a commander phased out by Teferi's Protection (a popular card) wrongly keeps those conditions satisfied.
- Covers a **family** of control predicates across three files, not a single card — the same predicate class the maintainer is actively …

problems.title: `Keyword::Assist` is parsed but inert — another player can never help pay the generic cost (CR 702.132)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`Keyword::Assist` is recognized by the parser (enum variant, `KeywordKind::Assist`, `FromStr`/deserialize) but has **zero runtime implementation** — `grep -rn "Assist" crates/engine/src/game/ crates/engine/src/database/` returns nothing (after excluding `persist`/`consist`/`assistant`). The keyword is read off the card and then silently dropped, so the "another player may pay the generic mana of this spell" mechanic never happens. On every card with Assist, the spell is paid for exactly as if it had no Assist at all.

This is the same inert-keyword class as the recently-implemented Surge / Forage / Read Ahead / Forecast gaps: a keyword whose `synthesize_*` / casting / game wiring was never written.

## Comprehensive Rules

**CR 702.132a** (verified in `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`): *"Assist is a static ability that modifies the rules of paying for the spell with assist (see rules 601.2g–h). If the total cost to cast a spell with assist includes a generic mana component, before you activate mana abilities while casting it, you may choose another player. That player has a chance to activate mana abilities. … Before you begin to pay the total cost of the spell, the player you chose may pay for any amount of the generic mana in the spell's total cost."*

So Assist inserts an optional, interactive payment step: after the total cost is locked but before the caster pays, the caster may choose another player who may contribute mana toward the **generic** portion only. The colored/hybrid/Phyrexian portions remain the caster's responsibility (CR 601.2g–h).

## Evidence (inert)

- Enum + plumbing only: `keywords.rs:196` / `:791` (`Keyword::Assist`), `:1059` (`KeywordKind::Assist`), `:2051` / `:2688` (`FromStr`), and parser display — and nothing else.
- **No** `CastingVariant::Assist`, **no** `synthesize_assist`, **no** reference in `casting.rs` / `casting_costs.rs` / `cost_payability.rs` / `ai_support/`.
- Contrast with the implemented "another resource pays generic" family: Convoke / Improvise / Waterbend are wired through `ConvokeMode` (`casting.rs:8665–8726`, `mana_payment_actions(.., Some(ConvokeMode::..))`) — but those tap the **caster's own** permanents. Assist is the **other-player mana** case and has no analogue.

Strictly novel: GitHub search `repo:phase-rs/phase Assist in:title` → **0 results**. (Delve #1322 and Spectacle #635 are the other big inert cost-keywords and are already filed; Assist is not.)

## Why this is valuable

- **~16 cards** carry Assist (e.g. **Bloodborn Scoundrels**, **Bring Down**, **Charging Binox** — the Battlebond cycle), and on every one the keyword is a complete no-op today.
- It is a **cost-payment** mechanic, so the gap is observable on the central casting path, not a fringe corner.
- Builds the general "another player contributes to a cost" interaction the engine doesn't yet have, complementing the existing caster-only `ConvokeMode` family.

## Feasibility / implementation sketch

Assist is the heaviest of th…

problems.title: feat(engine): implement Ripple keyword runtime (CR 702.60)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`Keyword::Ripple` is parsed but is a **unit variant that discards N** and has **zero runtime** — `grep "Keyword::Ripple" crates/engine/src/game/` returns nothing, and there is no `synthesize_ripple`. The parser even self-documents the gap (`oracle_keyword.rs:1279`: *"Keyword::Ripple is currently a unit variant (N is not yet tracked by the engine)"*). So on every card with ripple the keyword is a complete no-op: casting it never reveals the top N or casts the same-named copies.

This is the last inert keyword with real cards. It belongs to the same "reveal-from-top, cast-during-resolution" family the engine already implements end-to-end for **Cascade** and **Discover**, so the runtime is largely an assembly of existing building blocks.

## Comprehensive Rules

**CR 702.60a** (verified in `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`): *"Ripple N" means "When you cast this spell, you may reveal the top N cards of your library. You may cast any of those cards with the same name as this spell without paying their mana costs. Then put all revealed cards not cast this way on the bottom of your library in a random order."*

**CR 702.60b**: Multiple instances of ripple each trigger separately.

## Why this is valuable

- Covers the **class** of ripple cards (not one card): the Coldsnap "Surging" cycle — **Surging Aether, Surging Dementia, Surging Flame, Surging Might, Surging Sentinels** — plus **Thrumming Stone**, which grants "Ripple 4" to every spell you cast (a combo enabler). Card count: `grep -oc '"_Rule":"Ripple"' data/mtgish-cards.json` → 5, and Thrumming Stone makes it open-ended.
- It is the **final** parsed-but-inert keyword with cards; implementing it closes the keyword-runtime coverage gap that Convoke/Improvise/Assist/Delve/Spectacle/Splice/etc. have been filling.
- **High tractability** — it reuses the Cascade/Discover pipeline rather than introducing new machinery.

## Implementation plan (mirror Cascade)

1. **Carry N** — change `Keyword::Ripple` → `Keyword::Ripple(u32)`, exactly as `Dredge(u32)` does. Update the parser at `oracle_keyword.rs:1277-1289` to capture N (it currently parses then drops it), plus `FromStr`/display/`kind()` sites. (This is the small ripple already noted in the parser comment.)
2. **Synthesize the trigger** — add `synthesize_ripple` emitting a **"when you cast this spell"** triggered ability (the same SpellCast trigger shape Cascade uses, `triggers.rs:13478` / the Cascade synth path). CR 702.60b multiplicity falls out of the per-instance synthesis the engine already does for Cascade/Storm.
3. **Resolve via the existing cast-from-exile authority** — the effect reveals the top N (reuse the `exile_from_top` / `effects/exile_from_top_until.rs` "Cascade/Discover-shape" reveal), filters the revealed cards by **same name as the source spell**, and offers casting each match for free through the cast-during-resolution authority (`casting.rs:6595`, CR 608.2g) and the `CastOfferKind` / resolution-choice flow in `engine_resolution_c…

problems.title: [Bug]: static "… and can't attack or block" drops the combat lockout (CR 508.1a / 509.1b)
problems.issue_body:
## Description
When a permanent's static ability is a conjunction whose **trailing** clause is "**and can't attack or block**", the combat lockout is silently dropped. The leading clause (a type change, an ability-loss, a P/T modifier, etc.) parses, but the "and can't attack or block" half produces no static, so the affected creature can still attack and block.

This is the same drop-on-conjunction class already fixed for the sibling clauses:
- "… and can't be blocked" (#2167), "… and can't block" (#2251), "… and can't attack" (#2281),
- "… and doesn't untap during its controller's untap step" (#2293),
- "… and can't be sacrificed" (#2458), "… and can't be enchanted [or equipped]" (#2452),
- "… and can't be the target of …" (#2522), "… and its activated abilities can't be activated" (#2483).

The combined **"can't attack or block"** is the remaining gap in that family. The standalone form ("Enchanted creature can't attack or block.") already parses to `StaticMode::CantAttackOrBlock`, but the compound form does not: `try_split_and_cant_attack` matches "and can't attack" and then **deliberately declines** when a tail remains (its own comment: *"A remaining tail … is a different restriction owned by another branch — decline so we don't mis-split it"*), and there is no `try_split_and_cant_attack_or_block`. So the whole "and can't attack or block" clause falls through and is dropped.

Because the card still parses cleanly (the leading clause succeeds), these are counted as "supported" by the coverage metric — a silent no-op, not a parse failure.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Parse a permanent whose static reads "[some static] **and can't attack or block**" — e.g.:
   - **Observed Stasis** / **Fog on the Barrow-Downs** (enchanted creature is/becomes something **and can't attack or block**)
   - **Immovable Rod** ("another target permanent loses all abilities **and can't attack or block**")
   - Auras of the form "Enchanted creature is a [type] **and can't attack or block**." / "Enchanted creature loses all abilities **and can't attack or block**."
2. Resolve / inspect the resulting static abilities.
3. Only the leading static is present; there is no `CantAttackOrBlock` static — the affected creature can still be declared as an attacker and as a blocker.

## Expected behavior (CR 508.1a / CR 509.1b)
> A creature with "can't attack" can't be declared as an attacker (CR 508.1a); a creature with "can't block" can't be declared as a blocker (CR 509.1b). "Can't attack or block" imposes both.

The conjunction must be split: the leading clause parses to its own static(s), and "and can't attack or block" adds a companion `StaticMode::CantAttackOrBlock` over the same affected set (and any shared condition), exactly as the sibling split-static fixes do.

## Actual behavior
The trailing "and can't attack or block" is dropped entirely; no combat-lockout static is produced, so the affected creature can attack and block normally. Half the card does nothing.

## Impact

problems.title: [Feature]: Implement Epic keyword runtime (copy spell each upkeep and lock future spell casts)
problems.issue_body:
# [Feature]: Implement Epic keyword runtime (copy spell each upkeep and lock future spell casts)

## Description
The **Epic** keyword is parsed and typed (`Keyword::Epic`), but it has no runtime behavior. The only current references are keyword parsing/display/coverage entries:

- `types/keywords.rs` has `Keyword::Epic`.
- `parser/oracle_keyword.rs` can display it as `"epic"`.
- `game/coverage.rs` recognizes the keyword line.

There is no keyword synthesis, no resolution hook, no persistent "you can't cast spells for the rest of the game" state, and no beginning-of-upkeep copy trigger. As a result, an Epic spell resolves like an ordinary spell and then disappears; the defining rest-of-game effect never starts.

This is a good larger runtime feature because the engine already has pieces to reuse: spell-copy effects, target retargeting for copied spells, upkeep triggers, cast restrictions, and spell history/state plumbing. Epic needs those pieces connected through a persistent per-player runtime record.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Cast an Epic spell, for example **Enduring Ideal**.
2. Let it resolve.
3. Advance to that player's next upkeep.
4. No copy of the Epic spell is created.
5. The player can still cast spells after the Epic spell resolved.

## Expected behavior (CR 702.50)
Epic has two linked runtime effects:

- For the rest of the game, the spell's controller **can't cast spells**.
- At the beginning of each of that player's upkeeps, that player copies the Epic spell except for its Epic ability, and may choose new targets for the copy.

Key points:

- The copy engine should not create a fresh Epic loop from the copy; the copy excludes Epic.
- The copy is created at the beginning of each upkeep and is not cast, so ordinary "when you cast" triggers must not fire.
- The cast lock applies to spells, not activated abilities or triggered abilities.
- Multiple Epic spells can exist in unusual cases; each resolved Epic spell should create its own upkeep copy source, while the cast lock remains true for that player.

## Actual behavior
`Keyword::Epic` is inert:

- No trigger is synthesized for the Epic keyword in `database/synthesis.rs`.
- `stack.rs` resolution does not detect resolved Epic spells and does not register an ongoing Epic effect.
- `GameState` has no persistent Epic record for the resolved spell snapshot / controller.
- `game/restrictions.rs` does not block future spell casting after an Epic spell resolves.
- Upkeep trigger collection has no Epic source to place a spell copy on the stack.

## Impact
All printed Epic cards have their central mechanic missing:

- **Enduring Ideal**
- **Eternal Dominion**
- **Neverending Torment**
- **Undying Flames**
- **Endless Swarm**

These cards are unavoidably wrong without Epic runtime. The first resolution happens, but the rest-of-game lock and recurring upkeep copies are the whole point of the mechanic.

## Implementation
Implement Epic as a persistent runtime record installed when an Epic spell res…

problems.title: [Card Bug] Exile-base cumulative upkeep is parsed but never synthesized or payable
problems.issue_body:
## Card(s)
Thought Lash; any card whose cumulative upkeep cost is an exile cost, especially "Cumulative upkeep-Exile the top card of your library."

## Build/version
`phase-rs/phase` upstream `main` at `35d74b17`

## Game mode
AI / engine

## Actual behavior
`Cumulative upkeep` is implemented for several base cost shapes, but exile-base costs are still treated as unsupported:

- `parse_cumulative_upkeep_keyword` can produce `Keyword::CumulativeUpkeep(AbilityCost::Exile { ... })`.
- `AbilityCost::supports_cumulative_upkeep_payment` returns `false` for `AbilityCost::Exile`.
- `database::synthesis` only emits a `PayCumulativeUpkeep` trigger when the cost is supported, so these cards receive no cumulative-upkeep trigger at all.
- `game::coverage` has a regression test that intentionally reports `Keyword:CumulativeUpkeepUnsupportedCost` for an exile-base cumulative upkeep cost.

That means Thought Lash does not get the core upkeep trigger: it will not gain age counters, it will not ask the controller to exile the top card of their library once per age counter, and it will not sacrifice itself when that cost is declined or cannot be paid.

## Expected behavior
CR 702.24a says cumulative upkeep means:

1. At the beginning of the permanent's controller's upkeep, put an age counter on it.
2. Then that player may pay the listed upkeep cost for each age counter on it.
3. If the player does not pay, sacrifice the permanent.

For Thought Lash-style costs, the per-counter cost should expand from:

```rust
AbilityCost::PerCounter {
    counter: CounterType::Age,
    target: SelfRef,
    base: AbilityCost::Exile {
        count: 1,
        zone: Some(Zone::Library),
        filter: None,
    },
}
```

into an interactive payment of N top cards from the controller's library, where N is the number of age counters on the source at trigger resolution.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Build a face with:

```rust
Keyword::CumulativeUpkeep(AbilityCost::Exile {
    count: 1,
    zone: Some(Zone::Library),
    filter: None,
})
```

2. Run `database::synthesis::synthesize_face`.
3. Observe that no `TriggerMode::PayCumulativeUpkeep` trigger is installed because `supports_cumulative_upkeep_payment()` rejects the cost.
4. Alternatively, call `game::coverage::card_face_gaps`; it reports `Keyword:CumulativeUpkeepUnsupportedCost`.
5. Put a Thought Lash-like permanent onto the battlefield and advance to its controller's upkeep.

Expected:

- The upkeep trigger is created.
- One age counter is placed on the permanent.
- The controller can pay by exiling one top library card per age counter.
- Declining or being unable to pay sacrifices the permanent.

Actual:

- The exile-base cumulative upkeep ability is omitted before runtime, so no trigger or payment happens.

## Impact
This is a real card-behavior bug, not only a coverage-reporting gap. Thought Lash's main balancing cost is missing, and any future card data with exile-base cumulative upkeep will silently lose its upkeep obligation.

problems.title: Parser: optional 'as though' permission grants dropped (cast as flash / spend mana any color / damage as unblocked) (#22
problems.issue_body:
Sub-issue of #2231 (`Optional_YouMay` swallowed-clause cluster). One structural pattern per issue for clean building-block fixes.

`you may cast [type] spells as though they had flash`, `you may spend mana as though it were mana of any color [to cast this spell]`, `you may have this creature assign its combat damage as though it weren't blocked`

```bash
target/tool/coverage-report data --all --warning-detector Optional_YouMay --warning-limit 500 \

Represented as optional permission-granting continuous/applied effects (CR 609 "as though"; CR 702.8 flash timing; CR 609.4 mana-as-though-any-color; CR 509.1c combat-damage-as-though-unblocked). If unrepresentable, the ability must not stay fully supported.

problems.title: Replace Emissary Green aggregate vote-tally string-rewrite with QuantityRef::VoteCount
problems.issue_body:
Follow-up from #1440 (merged). The aggregate vote-tally parser (`rewrite_a_number_of` in `oracle_vote.rs`) currently lowers "create a number of X equal to [twice] the number of <choice> votes" by **rewriting the Oracle string** (`format!("{before}{count} {after}")`) and re-feeding it to the effect-chain parser with a fixed count + `repeat_for`. This is correct for Emissary Green's shipping interactions but is the wrong long-term representation:

- **String construction for matching** is a prohibited anti-pattern (CLAUDE.md).
- It serves exactly **one card** and does not generalize to the sibling "draw cards / deal damage equal to the number of X votes" forms (e.g. Truth or Consequences).
- The per-vote fan-out (`repeat_for = Fixed(votes)`) emits N single-token events rather than one aggregate event; harmless for linear doublers and batched token triggers, but diverges for non-linear count modifiers (Xorn).

**Correct seam:** add a `QuantityRef::VoteCount { choice_index }` variant resolved against the vote ballots in `game/quantity.rs`, and have `vote::resolve_tally` run each aggregate-tally per-choice effect ONCE with that dynamic count bound — emitting a single `CreateToken { count: N }` per CR 111.1 + CR 608.2c. This retires the string-rewrite and covers the draw/damage vote-tally variants in one move.

Refs: #1440, #888.

problems.title: CastPaymentMode: collapse 6 sibling *WithPaymentMode GameAction variants
problems.issue_body:
Surfaced by isolated post-fix review of f6d04779e (#531 + payment-mode plumbing).

The merged commit shipped 6 sibling `CastSpell*WithPaymentMode` GameAction variants instead of adding a `payment_mode: CastPaymentMode` field to the existing cast variants. This violates the **parameterize-don't-proliferate** principle:

- 6 duplicated GameAction variants (`CastSpellWithPaymentMode`, `CastSpellAsSneakWithPaymentMode`, `CastSpellAsWebSlingingWithPaymentMode`, `CastSpellForFreeWithPaymentMode`, `CastSpellAsMiracleWithPaymentMode`, `CastSpellAsMadnessWithPaymentMode`)
- 6 cloned `casting::handle_*_with_payment_mode` handler functions
- 6 cloned WaitingFor variants with double-default fields
- 30+ call sites pattern-matching both forms

## Fix (per implrev recommendation)
Replace with one field on each existing cast variant:
```rust
CastSpell {
    object_id: ObjectId,
    card_id: CardId,
    targets: Vec<ObjectId>,
    #[serde(default)]
    payment_mode: CastPaymentMode,
},
// ...same for the 5 other variants
```
`#[serde(default)]` with `Default = Auto` preserves wire compatibility. Remove all 6 `*WithPaymentMode` variants, fold the payment-mode parameter into the existing handlers, eliminate the dual pattern-match arms.

## Bonus required
- Add a Manual-path runtime test (every existing test constructs `CastPaymentMode::Auto`).
- Promote `triggers::is_valid_permutation` to `pub(crate)` and call it from `ai_support/mod.rs:108-128` instead of inlining identical logic.

## Why this matters
Compounds at every match site. Future maintenance cost grows linearly with adding new cast variants — every new variant requires a parallel `*WithPaymentMode` sibling. The right shape is one parameterization axis.

Refs: `feedback_parameterize_dont_proliferate.md`, `feedback_no_bool_flags.md`.
