problems.title: fix(parser): generalize "as long as enchanted creature is X, it gets…/has…" inverted-grant beyond Legendary (CR 613/611.
problems.issue_body:
Closes #2674 (Shield of the Oversoul does nothing on its enchanted creature).

## Summary

Auras (and Equipment) of the form **"As long as enchanted/equipped creature is `<characteristic>`, it gets `<P/T>` and has `<keyword>`"** only resolve correctly when the characteristic is the literal word **`legendary`**. For every other characteristic — a **color** ("is white" / "is green"), a card **type/subtype**, or the **basic** supertype — the buff silently lands on the **Aura itself** instead of the enchanted creature, so the creature gets nothing.

This is a single-card special case wearing a class handler's name: the inverted-grant parser calls `parse_attached_subject_is_legendary`, which hardcodes `tag("creature is legendary")`. The fix replaces that hardcoded qualifier with the parser's existing general predicate-tail building block so the whole class is covered.

## The card class (build for the class, not the card)

Pattern: **`As long as enchanted <subject> is <characteristic>, it gets <pt> and has <keyword>.`** (and the `equipped` / Equipment variant).

- **Shield of the Oversoul** — "As long as enchanted creature is **white**, it gets +1/+1 and has flying. / As long as enchanted creature is **green**, it gets +1/+1 and has indestructible." (the reported card; color-conditional)
- The general form covers any future Aura whose conditional grant keys on the host's color, type, subtype, or supertype — not just `legendary`.

CR references (verified against `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`):
- **CR 611.3a** — a continuous effect whose duration/condition is "as long as …" only applies while the condition holds.
- **CR 613.x** — layer system; the grant (P/T in layer 7c, abilities in layer 6) applies to the **enchanted creature**, the object named by "it".
- **CR 105.2b / 105.4** — a multicolored object *is* each of its colors, so a green-white creature satisfies both "is white" and "is green". (The runtime already honors this — `FilterProp::HasColor` uses `.contains(color)` in `game/filter.rs`; the bug is purely in the parser path, not color evaluation.)

## Root cause (verified in current `main`)

Parsing `"As long as enchanted creature is white, it gets +1/+1 and has flying."` today produces:

```text
StaticDefinition {
    affected: Some(SelfRef),                       // ← WRONG: the Aura, not the host
    modifications: [AddPower 1, AddToughness 1, AddKeyword Flying],
    condition: Some(IsPresent { filter: creature + EnchantedBy + HasColor{White} }),
}
```

`affected: SelfRef` is the Aura enchantment (not a creature), so the +1/+1/flying buff is applied to the Aura and the enchanted creature is unaffected — it "doesn't do anything, still gets destroyed, doesn't give flying" (exactly the #2674 report).

Compare the **working** `legendary` case, which yields the correct shape:

```text
StaticDefinition {
    affected: Some(Typed(creature + EnchantedBy + HasSupertype{Legendary})),  // ← buff lands on the host
    modifications: [AddPower 1, AddToughness…

problems.title: [Feature]: "Conjure a duplicate of <card>" is dropped to Unimplemented — Conjure parser only handles "conjure a card nam
problems.issue_body:
## Description
The Conjure keyword action has a working runtime (`Effect::Conjure { cards: Vec<ConjureCard> }` + `game/effects/conjure.rs`), but the **parser only recognizes the named-card form**. `try_parse_conjure` (`parser/oracle_effect/mod.rs`) parses:

> "conjure [N] card(s) **named {Name}** into/onto {zone}"

It has **no arm** for the far more common **"conjure a duplicate of `<referenced card>`"** form, so those cards fall to `Effect::Unimplemented`. `ConjureCard { name: String, count }` is name-only — it cannot express "a duplicate of the card resolved at runtime."

This is the single largest recognizable unimplemented subset in the corpus: **47 cards** carry "conjure a duplicate of …" and currently do nothing (the clause is dropped while the card still parses, so coverage counts it "supported").

## Steps to reproduce
1. Parse a card with a duplicate-conjure clause, e.g.:
   - "**conjure a duplicate of it** into your hand"
   - "**conjure a duplicate of that card** onto the battlefield"
   - "**conjure a duplicate of target creature card** exiled with ~ into your hand"
2. Inspect the parsed effect.
3. It is `Effect::Unimplemented` (the duplicate-conjure clause is dropped); the runtime `Effect::Conjure` is never produced.

## Expected behavior (Conjure keyword action; CR 707 copiable values)
"Conjure a duplicate of `<card>` into/onto `<zone>`" creates a **new real card** (not a token) that is a copy of the referenced card's copiable characteristics (CR 707.2), placed into the specified zone — exactly like the existing named-conjure, but with the card's identity taken from a runtime reference instead of a literal name.

## Actual behavior
The clause is dropped to `Effect::Unimplemented`; no card is conjured. ~47 cards (the Alchemy duplicate-conjure family) are inert.

## Implementation (parameterize `ConjureCard`'s source — don't add a parallel effect)
The runtime already creates conjured cards; the gap is (a) a source axis on `ConjureCard` and (b) a parser arm.

- **`types/ability.rs`** — give `ConjureCard` a typed *source* instead of a bare `name: String`: e.g. `source: ConjureSource` where `ConjureSource = Named(String) | DuplicateOf(<reference>)`. The reference reuses an existing object/zone-reference type (`TargetRef` / `ParentTarget` / `ExiledBySource`) so "it" / "that card" / "target … exiled with ~" all resolve through existing machinery. Run the `add-engine-variant` gate first; this is a leaf-level parameterization of `ConjureCard`, not a new `Effect` sibling.
- **`game/effects/conjure.rs`** — for `DuplicateOf`, resolve the reference, read its copiable values (reuse the existing copy machinery / `copiable_characteristics`, CR 707.2), and conjure a real card from them into the target zone (the named path's card-creation is otherwise unchanged).
- **`parser/oracle_effect/mod.rs`** — add a `try_parse_conjure` arm (or sibling) for "conjure a duplicate of `<reference>` into/onto `<zone>`", composing the existing zone + reference combin…

problems.title: Mutate/merged permanents over-trigger "dies" / "leaves the battlefield" (once per component card instead of once)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
When a merged permanent (a creature mutated via the **Mutate** keyword, CR 702.140 / 730) leaves the
battlefield, the engine fires "whenever a creature dies" / "whenever ~ leaves the battlefield"
triggers **once per component card** in the pile, instead of **once** for the single permanent. The
"creature died this turn" look-back is over-counted the same way. CR 730.3 says only **one**
permanent leaves the battlefield, so this over-triggers every death/leave payoff by the size of the
mutate stack.

## CR reference (verified against `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`)
- **CR 730.3:** "If a merged permanent leaves the battlefield, **one permanent leaves the
  battlefield** and each of the individual components are put into the appropriate zone."
- **CR 712.21** (the meld analogue of the same "single object represented by multiple cards" rule,
  with an explicit worked example):
  > "Chittering Host, a melded permanent, dies. An ability that triggers 'whenever a creature dies'
  > triggers **once**. An ability that triggers 'whenever a card is put into a graveyard from
  > anywhere' triggers **twice**."

So the correct behavior is asymmetric:
- "dies" / "leaves the battlefield" (battlefield-exit observers) → fire **once** (one permanent left).
- "put into a graveyard from anywhere" → fire **once per card** (N cards entered the graveyard).

## Root cause
`crates/engine/src/game/merge.rs` → `split_merged_permanent_on_leave` routes each non-survivor
component to the destination zone through the full `move_to_zone` flow:

```rust
for component_id in components {
    if component_id == merged_id {
        continue; // survivor rides the normal move_to_zone after this fn
    }
    // merge.rs:317
    crate::game::zones::move_to_zone(state, component_id, dest, events); // emits a battlefield-exit event
}
```

Each component has `zone = Battlefield` (set in `merge_object_onto`, `merge.rs:100`), so
`move_to_zone` takes the normal exit path and pushes
`GameEvent::ZoneChanged { object_id: <component>, from: Some(Battlefield), to: <dest> }`. The
survivor then emits its own exit event. Result: **N** battlefield-exit events for one departing
permanent.

The battlefield-exit observers all key on `from == Some(Battlefield)` with no de-duplication and no
"single merged permanent" guard, so each component matches:
- `match_leaves_battlefield` (`trigger_matchers.rs:2839`): `if *from != Some(Zone::Battlefield) { return false; }`
- the "dies" form (ChangesZone `Battlefield → Graveyard`) matches the same way
- `ParsedCondition::CreatureDiedThisTurn` (`restrictions.rs:1154`): `r.from_zone == Some(Zone::Battlefield)`

Each component is a creature card carrying the controller's characteristics, so each matches
"whenever a creature you control dies / leaves the battlefield."

Confirmed absent on current main:
- **No suppression** — no merge-component trigger guard exists in `trigger_matchers.rs` /
  `events.rs` / `zones.rs` (the only `merge` references near the matchers ar…

problems.title: [Bug]: `Effect::Animate` carries fixed `Option<i32>` power/toughness — "becomes a creature with power and toughness equa
problems.issue_body:
## Description
`Effect::Animate` (`crates/engine/src/types/ability.rs`) models the animated permanent's base power/toughness as **fixed integers**:

```rust
Animate {
    power: Option<i32>,
    toughness: Option<i32>,
    types: Vec<String>,
    remove_types: Vec<String>,
    target: TargetFilter,
    keywords: Vec<Keyword>,
}
```

So a one-shot / triggered / activated animation whose P/T is a **dynamic value** — "becomes a creature with power and toughness each equal to **its mana value** / **that spell's mana value** / **X** / **the result** / **the number of loyalty counters on it**" — cannot be represented. The parser (`parser/oracle_effect/animation.rs`) has nowhere to put the dynamic quantity, so the P/T is dropped (the permanent animates as a `0/0` / no-P/T creature) or the line falls to `Unimplemented`. Because the card still parses to *an* `Animate`, coverage counts it as "supported" while the defining size is silently wrong.

This is the engine side of #2398 (a land animated as `0/0` instead of its intended dynamic size) and the same root cause across the whole dynamic-P/T animation class.

Note: the **static** form ("Each noncreature artifact **is** an artifact creature with power and toughness each equal to its mana value" — March of the Machines) is already handled via the continuous-modification path (`oracle_static/anthem.rs` `parse_base_pt_dynamic` / `parse_base_pt_mana_value_dynamic`). The gap is specifically the **effect-based** `Effect::Animate` used by "becomes … until end of turn" and triggered/activated animations.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Resolve any effect of the form "[target] becomes a creature with power and toughness each equal to `<dynamic>`", e.g.:
   - "… becomes an artifact creature with power and toughness each equal to **its mana value** until end of turn" (Ensoul-/March-style temporary animate)
   - "… becomes an Illusion creature with power and toughness each equal to **that spell's mana value**"
   - "… becomes a creature with power and toughness each equal to **the number of loyalty counters on it**"
2. Inspect the animated permanent.
3. Its power/toughness is `0/0` (or unset) — the dynamic value was dropped.

## Expected behavior (CR 613.4 / CR 208.2)
> A characteristic-setting "becomes a creature with power and toughness equal to [value]" sets the permanent's base P/T to that value, recomputed continuously as the value changes (CR 613.4 layer 7b; CR 208.2 for `*`-style dynamic P/T).

The animated permanent's base power/toughness must reflect the dynamic quantity at all times, exactly as the static "is a creature with P/T equal to …" form already does.

## Actual behavior
The dynamic quantity is discarded at parse time (no slot on `Effect::Animate`); the permanent animates with `0/0` / no P/T. ~40 card-texts use "becomes … with power and toughness equal to <dynamic>" (P/T = mana value, that spell's mana value, X, a die result, loyalty-counter count, …).

problems.title: Merged Mutate permanent stays token-flagged when a card is mutated on top of a token (CR 730.2d)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
When a creature spell mutates **on top of** a non-Human creature **token**, the resulting permanent
keeps the surviving (token) object's `is_token = true`, even though its **topmost component is a
card**. CR 730.2d says a merged permanent is a token only if its *topmost* component is a token, so
this pile should be **nontoken** while merged. The engine wrongly continues to treat it as a token.

> Scope note: this is the **only** direction the rules can produce. Mutate is a way to *cast a
> creature spell* (CR 702.140a) and the *only* thing that merges permanents (CR 730.1); a token is
> never cast, so a token can only ever be a merge component as the **target/survivor**, never as a
> non-survivor on top of a card. A token-survivor is already `is_token = true` (correct), so there is
> no "token on top of a card" case to fix — the bug is strictly the card-on-top-of-a-token direction.

## CR reference (verified against `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`)
- **CR 730.2d:** "If a merged permanent contains a token, the resulting permanent is a token only if
  the topmost component is a token."
- **CR 730.2a:** the merged permanent's characteristics come from its topmost component.
- **CR 702.140a:** mutate "means 'You may pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost. … it
  becomes a mutating creature spell and targets a non-Human creature with the same owner as this
  spell.'" → the host can be a non-Human **token you own**; the mutating object is always a card.

## Root cause
`crates/engine/src/game/merge.rs` → `merge_object_onto` derives the merged permanent's display/art
from the topmost component (`display_source`, `token_image_ref`, `printed_ref`), but **never updates
`is_token`** (grep for `is_token` in `merge.rs` is empty on current `main`). The surviving object
(the token, when it is the mutate host) keeps its original `is_token = true`. At runtime token-ness
is read as a raw object field (e.g. `FilterProp::Token => obj.is_token` in `game/filter.rs`), so
nothing derives it from the topmost component.

## Current (wrong) behavior
Mutating a card on top of a creature token leaves the merged permanent flagged `is_token = true`,
even though the topmost component (the card) is not a token.

## Correct behavior (CR 730.2d)
While merged, the permanent is a token **iff** its topmost component is a token. With a card on top of
a token host, the merged permanent is **nontoken**. When the pile later leaves the battlefield, the
token component is once again a token (and ceases to exist per CR 111.7); the card component is put
into the graveyard.

## Concrete scenario
- You control a non-Human **creature token** you own (e.g. a 2/2 Zombie).
- You cast a creature spell with mutate, targeting the token, and choose **top** (the card supplies
  the copiable characteristics).
- **Correct:** the merged permanent is **nontoken** — not destroyed by "destroy all tokens", counted
  by "nontoken creatures you control get +1/+1", etc.
- **Actual:** it stays a **…

problems.title: [Feature]: "This ability costs {N} less to activate if [condition]" is dropped — only the "for each" form is parsed
problems.issue_body:
## Description
A growing family of activated abilities reduce their cost by a flat amount **conditionally**:

> "{cost}: {effect}. **This ability costs {N} less to activate if [condition].**"

The clause is dropped (an `Effect:this` gap), so these abilities always cost full price and the cards are unsupported. Affected (recent + classic):

- **Razorlash Transmogrant** — "costs {4} less to activate if an opponent controls four or more nonbasic lands"
- **Thaumaton Torpedo** — "costs {3} less to activate if you attacked with a Spacecraft this turn"
- **Starport Security** — "costs {2} less to activate if you control a creature with a +1/+1 counter on it"
- **Esquire of the King** — "costs {2} less to activate if you control a legendary creature"
- **A-Sewer Crocodile** — "costs {3} less to activate if there are five or more mana values among cards in your graveyard"
- **Imoen, Trickster Friend** — "costs {3} less to activate if there are two or more instant and/or sorcery cards in your graveyard"
- **Wayta, Trainer Prodigy** — "costs {2} less to activate if it targets two creatures you control"
- **Raft Security Officer** — "costs {1} less to activate if it targets a creature with power 3 or less"

This is a clean parameterization gap. The engine already models cost reduction on activated abilities — `CostReduction { amount_per, count }` (`types/ability.rs`), applied at `casting.rs` as `reduce_by = amount_per * count`. But `try_parse_cost_reduction` (`parser/oracle_cost.rs`) hard-requires the literal **"less to activate **for each** "** / "less to cast for each " — it has **no branch for the conditional "if [condition]"** flat-reduction form. `CostReduction` has no condition slot, so the conditional form cannot be represented and the clause falls to `Effect:this`.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Parse e.g. Esquire of the King's activated ability: "… This ability costs {2} less to activate if you control a legendary creature."
2. Inspect the parsed ability: `cost_reduction` is `None`; the clause is an `Effect:this` gap.
3. In play the ability always costs full price (the reduction never applies).
4. Contrast: the **"for each"** form ("costs {1} less to activate for each page counter on this artifact") is supported.

## Expected behavior (CR 601.2f)
"This ability costs {N} less to activate if [condition]" reduces the ability's generic activation cost by {N} **when the condition is met at activation time**, and not otherwise.

## Implementation (parameterize `CostReduction` + reuse the condition machinery)
- **`types/ability.rs`** — add `condition: Option<AbilityCondition>` to `CostReduction` (serde `default`/`skip_serializing_if` so existing card-data stays compatible; `None` = unconditional, current behavior). Run the `add-engine-variant` gate: this is a leaf-level **parameterization** of `CostReduction`, not a new variant. Update the `CostReduction` construction sites and **run a full `--workspace` check** (the struct is built in the parser; verify no cr…

problems.title: [Bug]: "Spells with the chosen name can't be cast" is dropped — Meddling Mage / Nevermore do nothing
problems.issue_body:
## Description
The classic name-lock hatebears — **Meddling Mage**, **Nevermore**, **Voidstone Gargoyle** — read:

> "As ~ enters, choose a nonland card name. **Spells with the chosen name can't be cast.**"

The "choose a nonland card name" half parses (the chosen name is persisted as `ChosenAttribute::CardName`), but the **"Spells with the chosen name can't be cast"** line is dropped (an `Effect:unknown` gap), so the lock never takes effect — the named spell can still be cast and the card does nothing.

This is purely a **parser** gap. Both the runtime and the supporting pieces already exist:

- `StaticMode::CantBeCast { who: ProhibitionScope }` + a `.affected(TargetFilter)` spell filter is the casting-prohibition static (Steel Golem "you can't cast creature spells", etc.).
- Its enforcement (`cant_cast_filter_matches`, `game/casting.rs`) **already handles `TargetFilter::HasChosenName`** — it matches the spell's name against the source's chosen `ChosenAttribute::CardName` (CR 201.2).
- The sibling activated-ability half ("Activated abilities of sources with the chosen name can't be activated", Voidstone/Pithing Needle) is already supported via `CantBeActivated` + `HasChosenName`.

The parser emits `CantBeCast` for many subjects but **has no arm for "spells with the chosen name"** — so the fully-wired runtime path is unreachable.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Parse Meddling Mage: "As this creature enters, choose a nonland card name. Spells with the chosen name can't be cast."
2. Inspect the parsed card: the "Spells with the chosen name can't be cast" line is an `Effect:unknown` gap; no `CantBeCast` static is produced.
3. In play, the chosen name is recorded but the named spell can still be cast.
4. Contrast: Voidstone Gargoyle's "Activated abilities of sources with the chosen name can't be activated" (the activated-ability half) is supported.

## Expected behavior (CR 101.2 + CR 201.2)
"Spells with the chosen name can't be cast" is a continuous casting prohibition affecting **all players**: any spell whose name matches the source's chosen card name can't be cast.

## Actual behavior
The clause is dropped (`Effect:unknown`). Affected (each unsupported on this line): **Meddling Mage**, **Nevermore**, **Voidstone Gargoyle**.

## Implementation (one parser arm — no engine/type/runtime change)
- **`parser/oracle_static/restriction.rs`** — in the `CantBeCast` parsing path (which already produces `StaticDefinition::new(CantBeCast { who: AllPlayers }).affected(<filter>)` for "[subject] spells can't be cast"), add the **"spells with the chosen name can't be cast"** subject, emitting `affected(TargetFilter::HasChosenName)`. Reuses the existing `who: ProhibitionScope::AllPlayers` shape and the `HasChosenName` filter the runtime already evaluates.
- No change to `StaticMode`, `cant_cast_filter_matches`, or the choose-a-name effect — all already present.
- **Tests** — build-the-class: "Spells with the chosen name can't be cast." parses to `CantBeCast { who: AllPl…

problems.title: fix(parser): parse "for each player who has lost the game" quantity (Rampant Frogantua)
problems.issue_body:
## Card(s)

- Rampant Frogantua — "This creature gets +10/+10 for each player who has lost the game."

(Related community report: #2930)

## Build/version

`main` @ `5eaba9c2`

## Game mode

Parser / static P/T inspection

## Actual behavior

`parse_for_each_clause` and `parse_quantity_ref` have no arm for `"player(s) who have/has lost the game"`, so the Rampant Frogantua static falls through to `Unimplemented` / drops the multiplier. At runtime, `resolve_player_count` has no `PlayerFilter` for eliminated players, so even a hand-built quantity would count zero.

## Expected behavior

Per CR 104.3 + CR 613.4c, `"for each player who has lost the game"` should parse to `QuantityRef::PlayerCount { filter: HasLostTheGame }` and resolve against `Player::is_eliminated`, giving +0/+0 in a two-player game with no eliminations and +10/+10 per eliminated player in multiplayer.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `parse_static_line("This creature gets +10/+10 for each player who has lost the game.")` → no `AddDynamicPower`/`AddDynamicToughness` keyed on lost-game count on current `main`.
2. `parse_for_each_clause("player who has lost the game")` → `None`.
3. In a 3-player state with one `is_eliminated` player, a `HasLostTheGame` quantity should resolve to `1` (currently unrepresentable).

## Component

- `crates/engine/src/types/ability.rs` — `PlayerFilter::HasLostTheGame`
- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_quantity.rs` — for-each / number-of parse arms
- `crates/engine/src/game/quantity.rs` — `resolve_player_count`

problems.title: [Card Bug] Harvest Pyre drops exile-X-from-graveyard additional cost — X unbound
problems.issue_body:
## Card(s)

- Harvest Pyre — "As an additional cost to cast this spell, exile X cards from your graveyard. Harvest Pyre deals X damage to target creature."

(Related maintainer report: #2934)

## Build/version

`main` @ `3c910199`

Parser / spell casting (additional cost payment)

## Actual behavior

`parse_single_cost` has no arm for `"exile X cards from your graveyard"`, so `parse_additional_cost_line` returns `None` and the clause is dropped during oracle parsing. Card-data ends up with `additional_costs: null` and `DealDamage{amount: Variable("X")}` with nothing to bind X to. At runtime, no graveyard card-selection prompt is offered.

## Expected behavior

Per CR 107.3a + CR 118.9 + CR 601.2b/601.2f, the additional cost should parse to `AbilityCost::Exile { count: u32::MAX, zone: Graveyard, filter: None }`, prompt for X (bounded by eligible graveyard cards), then require exiling exactly X cards before paying `{1}{R}` and dealing X damage.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `parse_additional_cost_line("as an additional cost to cast this spell, exile x cards from your graveyard.", …)` → `None` on current `main`.
2. `parse_oracle_cost("Exile X cards from your graveyard")` → does not return the graveyard exile cost shape.
3. Casting a synthetic Harvest Pyre with cards in graveyard never enters `ChooseXValue` or `PayCost::ExileFromZone`.

## Component

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_cost.rs` — exile-X-from-graveyard parse arm
- `crates/engine/src/game/casting_costs.rs` — `additional_cost_x_max` + concretize variable exile count after X is chosen

problems.title: Implement the Meld keyword action (CR 701.42 / CR 712.4)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
The **Meld** keyword action is not implemented at runtime. Meld cards are recognized only as a
**card layout** (`CardLayout::Meld(front, back)`, `types/card.rs:235`) — there is **no `Effect::Meld`,
no `perform_meld`, and no meld runtime** (`grep -r "Effect::Meld\|perform_meld" crates/` is empty).
As a result, meld pairs cannot meld into their combined permanent, and the instigator halves parse
to `Effect::Unimplemented`.

## What meld is (CR, verified against `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`)
- **CR 701.42a** — "To meld the two cards in a meld pair, put them onto the battlefield with their
  back faces up and combined. The resulting permanent is a single object represented by two cards."
- **CR 701.42b/c** — only two cards of the same meld pair can meld; if they can't (e.g. a token copy),
  they stay in their current zone.
- **CR 712.4a/b** — the back faces (exposed in card-data as the named *result* card) determine the
  melded permanent's characteristics.
- **CR 712.4c** — meld cards cannot transform.
- **CR 712.21** — when a melded permanent leaves, the two cards return to the appropriate zone (as
  their **front** faces).

## Affected cards (7 meld pairs — all 7 meld clauses confirmed in `card-data.json`)
Each pair has one **instigator** half carrying the meld ability that names the partner and the result.

| Instigator (ability form) | Partner | Melds into | Set |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gisela, the Broken Blade (**triggered**, end step) | Bruna, the Fading Light | Brisela, Voice of Nightmares | EMN |
| Graf Rats (**triggered**, begin combat) | Midnight Scavengers | Chittering Host | EMN |
| Hanweir Battlements (**activated**, mana+tap) | Hanweir Garrison | Hanweir, the Writhing Township | EMN |
| Urza, Lord Protector (**activated**, `{7}`, sorcery-speed) | The Mightstone and Weakstone | Urza, Planeswalker | BRO/MOM |
| Mishra, Claimed by Gix (**triggered**, combat + ETB rider) | Phyrexian Dragon Engine | Mishra, Lost to Phyrexia | MOM |
| Titania, Voice of Gaea (**triggered**, upkeep + extra condition) | Argoth, Sanctum of Nature | Titania, Gaea Incarnate | MOM |
| Vanille, Cheerful l'Cie (**triggered**, optional cost) | (FF partner) | Ragnarok, Divine Deliverance | FIN |

The instigator halves are currently **unsupported** because the meld effect cannot be expressed.

## Current behavior
The meld clause ("…exile them, then meld them into Z") has no typed effect and parses to
`Effect::Unimplemented`; the melded permanent (Brisela, Chittering Host, etc.) can never be created.

## Correct behavior
Resolving the meld ability — when its controller **both owns and controls** both pair halves
(CR 701.42b) — exiles both and puts a single melded permanent onto the battlefield, represented by
the two cards, with the **result card's** characteristics. Because the permanent **enters the
battlefield** (CR 701.42a), its **ETB abilities trigger** — this is the opposite of Mutate
(CR 730.2b, which explicitly does *not* enter). When the melded permanent le…

problems.title: [Feature]: "Turn the exiled card face up" is dropped — Imprint flip cards (Clone Shell, Summoner's Egg) do nothing
problems.issue_body:
## Description
The Imprint "exile a card face down, later flip it" family — **Clone Shell**, **Summoner's Egg**, **Compleated Clone Shell**, **The Creation of Avacyn** — exile a card face down and then later turn it face up with a follow-up:

> "Imprint — When this creature enters, you may exile a card from your hand face down. When this creature dies, **turn the exiled card face up. If it's a creature card, put it onto the battlefield under your control.**" (Summoner's Egg)

The face-down exile parses, but the **"Turn the exiled card face up …"** effect is dropped (an `Effect:turn` gap), so the imprinted card is never revealed/returned — the card's entire payoff is lost.

This is an engine gap, not just a parser one: `TurnFaceUp` exists only as an `EffectKind`/trigger-condition placeholder — there is **no `Effect` variant, resolver, or parser arm**. The supporting pieces, however, already exist and should be reused:
- **`TargetFilter::ExiledBySource`** — references "the exiled card" (the card this source exiled), the tracking handle these cards need.
- **`Effect::Manifest` / morph machinery (`game/morph.rs`)** — face-down card characteristics + turn-face-up logic to mirror.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Parse Summoner's Egg / Clone Shell.
2. Inspect the parse: the "Turn the exiled card face up. If it's a creature card, put it onto the battlefield under your control." clause is an `Effect:turn` gap; no turn-face-up effect is produced.
3. In play, the imprinted card stays face down in exile forever.

## Expected behavior (CR 707.2 + CR 711)
"Turn the exiled card face up" reveals the face-down card this source exiled (it gains its real characteristics in exile); the conditional follow-up then acts on it ("if it's a creature card, put it onto the battlefield under your control").

## Implementation (add the effect; reuse `ExiledBySource` + the face-down machinery)
- **`types/ability.rs`** — add an `Effect::TurnFaceUp { target: TargetFilter }` variant (default `target: ExiledBySource`). Run the **`add-engine-variant`** gate first (the `EffectKind::TurnFaceUp` placeholder already anticipates it; verify there is no existing slot to reuse — e.g. an unmorph/manifest-flip effect — before extending).
- **`game/effects/`** — resolver: resolve `ExiledBySource` to the face-down exiled object, restore its real characteristics (reuse `game/morph.rs` turn-face-up / `Manifest` face-down handling), and emit the `TurnFaceUp` event the `EffectKind` placeholder already reserves. The conditional follow-up ("if it's a creature card, put it onto the battlefield under your control" / "you lose life equal to …") chains via the existing condition + `ChangeZone`/`LoseLife` effects.
- **`parser/oracle_effect/`** — parse "turn the exiled card face up" (and "turn that card face up") → `Effect::TurnFaceUp { target: ExiledBySource }`, composing the existing if-creature conditional + put-onto-battlefield/lose-life follow-ups.
- **Tests** — build-the-class: Summoner's Egg / Clone Shel…

problems.title: Implement the Cloak keyword action (CR 702.170)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`Cloak` (Bloomburrow, CR 702.170) is unimplemented. Cards that cloak a card drop to an `Effect:cloak` gap, so none of them parse. Cloak is mechanically very close to the already-supported `Effect::Manifest` — put a card onto the battlefield **face down as a 2/2 creature**, which can be **turned face up any time for its mana cost if it's a creature card** — with two distinctions:

1. The cloaked permanent has **ward {2}** (Manifest grants no ward).
2. The card source varies (top of library, a card from hand, a searched/sought card, a face-down pile), whereas Manifest is always the top of the library.

Reminder text on the cards:
> *To cloak a card, put it onto the battlefield face down as a 2/2 creature with ward {2}. Turn it face up any time for its mana cost if it's a creature card.*

## Affected cards (`Effect:cloak` gap)

Single-card, controller-sourced forms (first-pass scope):
- **Cryptic Coat** — "cloak the top card of your library, then attach this Equipment to it"
- **Ransom Note** — "Cloak the top card of your library" (modal)
- **Vannifar, Evolved Enigma** — "Cloak a card from your hand" (modal)
- **Sleuth Instructor** — "seek a … creature card … and cloak it"
- **Veiled Ascension** — interacts with face-down/cloaked creatures (partial; also has an unrelated gap)

Deferred multi-card / relative-player forms (out of first-pass scope, noted below):
- **Become Anonymous**, **Expose the Culprit** — "cloak those cards / them" (cloak a whole face-down pile)
- **Unexplained Absence** — "its controller cloaks the top card of their library" (relative player)

## Proposed approach

1. **Engine variant — via the `add-engine-variant` gate.** Cloak shares Manifest's face-down-2/2 + turn-up-for-mana-cost-if-creature resolution, but differs on the **ward {2}** rider and the card **source**. Run the gate to decide between:
   - a new sibling `Effect::Cloak { target, count }` (CR 702.170), or
   - parameterizing `Effect::Manifest` with a `ward`/source axis.

   The ward {2} grant and the keyword-distinct source make a dedicated `Effect::Cloak` the likely outcome, but the gate is binding.

2. **Resolver** reuses the existing manifest face-down entry machinery (`ChangeZone` face-down profile / the 2/2-no-characteristics path) and additionally grants **ward {2}** to the cloaked object. The "turn face up for its mana cost if it's a creature card" permission is the same one Manifest/disguise already attach to face-down permanents, so no new turn-up path is required — and it composes with the existing `TurnedFaceUp` event/trigger plumbing.

3. **Parser arm** for `cloak the top card of your library` / `cloak a card from your hand` / `cloak it` (singular, controller source) → the new effect. Anchor it so any trailing follow-up sentence is left to the sentence splitter (same discipline as the recent `turn the exiled card face up` work).

## Scope

- **First pass:** the single-card, controller-sourced forms above (Cryptic Coat, Ransom Note, Vannifar, …

## Oracle text (verified from client/public/card-data.json)
First strike, trample, haste
Whenever this creature attacks, it gets +X/+0 until end of turn, where X is the number of creatures you control.
When this creature enters, if it's not a token, each opponent creates a token that's a copy of it. The tokens are goaded for the rest of the game. (They attack each combat if able and attack a player other than you if able.)

## Reported behavior
> Creating an infinite loop on the triggered ability.
> Was able to break the loop by deleting the new dropped copy.

## Expected vs actual
Expected: When Life of the Party enters AND IT IS NOT A TOKEN, each opponent creates one goaded token copy of it. Because the copies are tokens, the intervening-if 'if it's not a token' prevents those copies from re-triggering, so the effect resolves once.
Actual: The ETB trigger fires for the token copies too, each spawning more copies — an infinite loop. The player had to delete the newly created copy to break it.

Two parse defects in card-data.json: (1) the trigger's intervening-if 'if it's not a token' is missing (`condition: null`), so the recursion guard is gone — this is the infinite-loop root cause; (2) the chained 'The tokens are goaded for the rest of the game' sub-effect is parsed as `Effect::Unimplemented` (name 'the'), so the goad is also not applied.

problems.issue_body:

problems.title: Implement the Planechase subsystem (Planes + Phenomena, CR 901 / CR 701.31–701.33)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
**Plane** and **Phenomenon** cards are entirely unsupported. `CoreType` (`crates/engine/src/types/card_type.rs`) has **no `Plane` or `Phenomenon` variant**, so these cards parse with empty `core_types` and are 100% unsupported. There is no planar deck, no `planeswalk` action, no "chaos ensues" resolution, and no command-zone wiring for ongoing planar static/triggered abilities.

This is the closest remaining analogue to the merged Meld work: a recognized-but-unimplemented card class that needs a new runtime subsystem and lands in new, inline-test-free source files.

## What it is (CR, verified against `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`)
- **CR 901 (Planechase)** — multiplayer/variant rules. A player has a **planar deck**; the top card is face up in the command zone and is the active plane.
- **CR 701.31 (Planeswalk)** — move the top card of the planar deck to the bottom (or to the active position), changing the active plane; "leaves/enters" triggers fire.
- **CR 701.32 (Set in Motion)** — used by schemes; planes use the planar die.
- **CR 701.33 (Abandon)** — used by phenomena (put into the planar graveyard, then planeswalk).
- The **planar die** (six blank faces, one Planeswalk symbol, one Chaos symbol): rolling Chaos triggers the active plane's "Whenever chaos ensues" ability; rolling Planeswalk planeswalks.

## Current behavior
Plane/Phenomenon cards parse to a card with no core type; their ongoing static abilities, "whenever you planeswalk away from this plane" / "whenever chaos ensues" triggers, and the roll-the-planar-die action have no runtime. The cards cannot be played in any game mode.

## Correct behavior
A Planechase game maintains a per-game (or shared) planar deck; the active plane sits face up in the command zone and applies its continuous/triggered/replacement abilities while active. Rolling the planar die resolves Chaos/Planeswalk; planeswalking changes the active plane and fires the appropriate leave/enter triggers; phenomena are abandoned after resolving.

## Affected cards
~**130** Plane + Phenomenon cards (approximate — counted from regenerated card-data; the committed `data/card-data.json` is stale, see the separate data-staleness issue). Examples: Agyrem, Mirrored Depths, Kilnspire District, Spectrox Mines, Mondassian Colony Ship.
**Format note:** Planechase is a casual variant — **0 of these are constructed-legal.** Value here is game-mode/format completeness, not constructed play.

## Design (reuse existing command-zone + die-roll infrastructure)
- **`CoreType::Plane` + `CoreType::Phenomenon`** in `types/card_type.rs` (+ `FromStr`/`Display`/serde).
- **A new `game/planechase.rs` subsystem** mirroring the existing command-zone modules `game/dungeon.rs` and `game/commander.rs`: the planar deck zone, the active-plane slot, and the `planeswalk`/`abandon` actions.
- **Reuse `game/effects/roll_die.rs`** for the planar die (the d6/results-table die runtime already exists) — map the Chaos/Planeswalk faces onto the existing roll…

problems.title: "Enters under the control of an opponent" is dropped (Xantcha, Pendant of Prosperity, Abby, +1)
problems.issue_body:
## Affected cards (4)

Permanents that **enter under the control of an opponent**:

- **Xantcha, Sleeper Agent** — "Xantcha enters under the control of an opponent of your choice."
- **Captive Audience** — "When Captive Audience enters the battlefield under a player's control..." / it's given to an opponent.
- **Pendant of Prosperity** — "This artifact enters under the control of an opponent of your choice."
- **Abby, Merciless Soldier** — "Abby enters under the control of an opponent of your choice."

(Real Oracle text verified from `data/mtgjson/AtomicCards.json`.)

## Reported behavior

The "enters under the control of an opponent of your choice" clause is **dropped** — the permanent enters under its **caster's/owner's** control instead of an opponent's. For Xantcha this is the whole point of the card (you give it to an opponent who must attack with it); currently it just enters under your control.

## Expected vs actual (CR 110.2a)

- **Expected:** the permanent enters the battlefield directly under an opponent's control (the chosen opponent; the sole opponent in a 2-player game) — it never enters under the caster's control.
- **Actual:** the controller-override clause parses to `Unimplemented` and is ignored; the permanent enters under the caster's control.

## Root cause

There is already a correct replacement handler `parse_self_enters_under_opponent` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_replacement.rs`) and a complete runtime (`enters_under(ControllerRef::Opponent)` → `apply_battlefield_entry_controller_override`), but the line is **never routed to it**: `is_replacement_pattern` (`oracle_classifier.rs`, `REPLACEMENT_CONTAINS_PATTERNS`) does not list "enters under the control of", so the first line falls through to the effect parser and emits `Unimplemented{effect_structure}` (the single coverage gap on each of these 4 cards). The existing unit test passes only because it calls `parse_replacement_line` directly, bypassing the classifier gate.

problems.title: Implement the Archenemy Schemes subsystem (CR 904 / CR 701.32 Set in Motion)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
**Scheme** cards are unsupported. `CoreType` (`crates/engine/src/types/card_type.rs`) has **no `Scheme` variant**, and there is no scheme deck, no "set the top scheme in motion" turn step, and no ongoing-scheme / `abandon` runtime. Notably, the **set-in-motion trigger is already recognized** by the parser but has no resolver — the exact "stub, no runtime" shape that made Meld a clean coverage gap.

## Evidence the stub exists (verified)
`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_trigger.rs` already maps the scheme trigger text to a typed mode:
```rust
if matches!(lower,
    "when you set this scheme in motion" | "whenever you set this scheme in motion"
) {
    def.mode = TriggerMode::SetInMotion;
    return Some((TriggerMode::SetInMotion, def));
}
```
So `TriggerMode::SetInMotion` is recognized, but nothing **sets a scheme in motion** at runtime, and Scheme cards have no core type — so the trigger never fires and the cards are unsupported.

## What it is (CR, verified against `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`)
- **CR 904 (Archenemy)** — the archenemy has a **scheme deck**. At the start of the archenemy's turn (before the untap step), they **set the top scheme in motion** (turn it face up in the command zone).
- **Ongoing schemes** stay face up and apply their abilities until their condition abandons them; non-ongoing schemes are abandoned after they resolve.
- **CR 701.33 (Abandon)** — put an abandoned scheme on the bottom of its owner's scheme deck.

## Current behavior
Scheme cards parse with no core type; the recognized `TriggerMode::SetInMotion` never fires because no scheme is ever set in motion. The cards do nothing.

## Correct behavior
A scheme deck exists per archenemy. At the start of the archenemy's turn, the top scheme is set in motion (face up in the command zone), firing its `SetInMotion` trigger. Ongoing schemes apply their continuous/triggered abilities until abandoned; others abandon on resolution (CR 701.33).

## Affected cards
~**52** Scheme cards (approximate — from regenerated card-data; committed data is stale, see the data-staleness issue). Examples: Nature Demands an Offering, Fear My Authority, Your Nightmares Are Delicious.
**Format note:** Archenemy is a casual variant — **0 constructed-legal.** Value is format completeness.

## Design (reuse the dungeon/command-zone subsystem pattern)
- **`CoreType::Scheme`** (+ `Supertype::Ongoing`) in `types/card_type.rs` with parse/display/serde.
- **A new `game/archenemy.rs` (or `game/schemes.rs`) subsystem** mirroring `game/dungeon.rs`: the scheme deck zone, the command-zone active-scheme slot, the begin-turn "set in motion" step, and the `abandon` action.
- **Wire the existing `TriggerMode::SetInMotion`** so it fires when a scheme is set in motion (the parser side is already done).
- Reuse the layer/trigger systems for ongoing-scheme statics and abandon conditions.

### Proposed file plan
| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `crates/engine/src/types/card_type.rs` | add `CoreType::Scheme` (+ `Ong…

problems.title: Conditional keyword grant “has hexproof if it hasn’t dealt damage yet” is dropped
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
The conditional keyword-grant static **"[creature] has hexproof if it hasn't dealt damage yet"** is dropped. The line falls through the self-static parser to an `Unimplemented{static_structure}`, so the affected creatures never gain (or correctly lose) hexproof based on whether they have dealt damage.

## Affected cards
- **Palladia-Mors, the Ruiner** — "Flying, vigilance, trample / Palladia-Mors has hexproof if it hasn't dealt damage yet." (sole gap)
- **Karakyk Guardian** — "Flying, vigilance, trample / This creature has hexproof if it hasn't dealt damage yet." (sole gap)
- **Oyaminartok, Polar Werebear** — same hexproof line (plus an unrelated spellbook-draft gap, so it only partially benefits).

## Root cause
Two compounding gaps on the self-static path:
1. **Routing:** the ` has ` self arm (`parser/oracle_static/dispatch.rs`) routes to `parse_continuous_gets_has` (`oracle_static/anthem.rs`), which splits only on `" as long as "`, never `" if "`. So the trailing `" if it hasn't dealt damage yet"` is never separated from the keyword, `map_keyword("hexproof if it hasn't dealt damage yet")` fails, and the whole line gaps. (Contrast: `parse_conditional_keyword_list` already handles multi-keyword `has <kw> if <cond>` lists, but the single-keyword self line does not reach it.)
2. **Unmodeled condition:** there is no `StaticCondition` for "it hasn't dealt damage yet" — a per-object, sticky "has this creature dealt any damage since it entered" state (NOT the existing per-turn damage tracking). Once the creature deals damage it loses hexproof; the state resets when it leaves the battlefield.

## Expected
`[self] has <keyword> if <condition>` should route through the conditional-keyword machinery, and "it hasn't dealt damage yet" should map to a `StaticCondition` backed by a per-object damage-dealt flag (set at the single `deal_damage` site, cleared at the leave-battlefield hub — mirroring existing per-object sets like `commander_declined_zone_return`, and the existing `StaticCondition::SourceEnteredThisTurn` precedent for source-context evaluation). Palladia-Mors and Karakyk Guardian then parse fully.

CR 702.11a/702.11b (hexproof is a static ability / can't be targeted by opponents); CR 613.1f (Layer 6 ability-adding effects).

problems.title: Implement the Conspiracy card type + hidden agenda (CR 905 / CR 702.106)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
**Conspiracy** cards are unsupported. `CoreType` (`crates/engine/src/types/card_type.rs`) has **no `Conspiracy` variant** — the enum stops at the 14 types Artifact…Scheme. As a result every conspiracy card parses with empty `core_types` (verified: Hired Heist, Secret Summoning, Power Play, Worldknit, Backup Plan all have `core_types: []`) and is 100% unsupported. Conspiracies begin the game in the command zone — face up, or face down for **hidden agenda** — and apply their abilities from there.

## What it is (verified against `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`)
- **CR 905.4** — at the start of the game, before decks are shuffled, each player may put any number of conspiracy cards from their sideboard into the command zone.
- **CR 905.4a + CR 702.106** — conspiracy cards **with hidden agenda** are put into the command zone **face down** and name a card; any time a player has priority they may turn a face-down conspiracy they control face up.
- **CR 905.5** — the owner/controller of a conspiracy is the player who put it into the command zone.
- Most face-up conspiracies apply a **continuous or triggered effect from the command zone** for the rest of the game.

## Current behavior
Conspiracy cards parse with no core type and never enter the command zone, so their command-zone static/triggered abilities never apply. The cards do nothing.

## Correct behavior
A player may begin the game with conspiracies in the command zone; each applies its abilities from there. A face-up conspiracy's static affects the game immediately (e.g. Worldknit); a hidden-agenda conspiracy starts face down naming a card and can be turned face up (CR 702.106). Draft-time effects ("as you draft", CR 905.2) are out of scope — there is no draft engine.

## Affected cards (verified against committed `data/card-data.json`)
**~28–32** true Conspiracy-type cards parse with empty `core_types`. They fall into distinct value tiers:

- **Real runtime value — continuous statics / start-of-game triggers (~8–12 cards):** Worldknit, Command from the Shadows, Rule with an Even Hand, Weight Advantage, Hold the Perimeter, Sentinel Dispatch, Hymn of the Wilds.
- **Hidden-agenda (name-a-card) conspiracies:** Hired Heist, Secret Summoning, Adriana's Valor, Brago's Favor, Echoing Boon, etc. — real value but require the face-down + reveal mechanic.
- **Deck-construction / game-setup effects (low runtime value):** Advantageous Proclamation (min deck size −5), Sovereign's Realm (no max deck size), Power Play (you are the starting player), Backup Plan (extra opening hand). These do little or nothing in a normal game without a deckbuild/draft layer.

> **Note on legality:** conspiracies are **not legal in any tracked constructed/eternal format** (their committed `legalities` are empty — they're playable only in the Conspiracy Draft variant, which the engine does not model). This is a completeness/card-type gap, not a format-coverage win.

problems.title: Parser: “any player may <action>. If a player does / if no one does, …” (group bargain) not parsed
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
The group-bargain / punisher pattern **"any player may <action>. If a player does / if no one does, <consequence>"** is not parsed. The `"any player may "` optional-effect prefix is unrecognized, so the head action lowers to `Effect::Unimplemented` (or, for Browbeat, misparses to an UNCONDITIONAL `DealDamage` at the wrong scope — a silently-wrong parse).

## Affected cards (group-optional, controller included)
- **Browbeat** — "Any player may have Browbeat deal 5 damage to them. If no one does, target player draws three cards."
- **Book Burning** — "Any player may have Book Burning deal 6 damage to them. If no one does, target player mills six cards."
- **Breaking Point** — "Any player may have Breaking Point deal 6 damage to them. If no one does, destroy all creatures..."
- **Argothian Wurm** / **Shivan Wumpus** — "When this creature enters, any player may sacrifice a land of their choice. If a player does, put this creature on top of its owner's library."
- **Prowling Pangolin** — "When this creature enters, any player may sacrifice two creatures of their choice. If a player does, sacrifice this creature."
(~26 cards share the broader shape; the pay-a-cost punisher-counters like Dash Hopes/Temporal Extortion are a separate harder shape — cost-payment-on-accept — and out of scope here.)

## Root cause
`strip_optional_effect_prefix` (`parser/oracle_effect/lower.rs`) recognizes `"each opponent may "`, `"any opponent may "`, `"the first player may "`, `"target opponent may "`, but NOT `"any player may "`. And `OpponentMayScope` (`types/ability.rs`) has only `AnyOpponent` — there is no `AnyPlayer` scope that includes the controller. The interactive runtime that offers the optional to each player in APNAP order, resolves the accepted action, routes the `"If a player does"` sub-ability, and resolves the `"If no one does"` else-branch ALREADY EXISTS for the opponent scope (`game/effects/mod.rs` OpponentMayChoice loop + `engine_payment_choices.rs`). Only the `AnyPlayer` scope (including the controller) and the parser prefix are missing.

## Expected
Add an `OpponentMayScope::AnyPlayer` scope (offered to ALL players including the controller, APNAP order — CR 101.4) and the `"any player may "` parser prefix, reusing the existing opponent-may optional pipeline. Browbeat/Book Burning then correctly become "each player may choose to take the damage; if none do, the reward happens"; the ETB sacrifice cards offer the sacrifice to all players and apply the consequence only if a player accepts.

CR 101.4 (APNAP order for simultaneous multi-player choices); CR 608.2d (resolution-time choices announced as the effect applies).

problems.title: AI: add an Artifacts-matter deck-feature axis + policy
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
`phase-ai` models tribal, tokens-wide, +1/+1-counter and other synergy axes but has **no artifacts-matter axis**: it cannot recognize an artifact-synergy deck (affinity, metalcraft, improvise, "artifacts you control" payoffs, Treasure/Clue/Food engines) and so does not value deploying/holding artifacts to enable those payoffs. This adds the missing `ArtifactsFeature` + policy via the supported `add-ai-feature-policy` pattern.

## Current behavior
`DeckFeatures::analyze` (`features/mod.rs`) detects 9 axes; none detect artifact density or artifact-count payoffs. The AI treats artifacts as generic permanents, missing affinity/improvise cost discounts as a sequencing consideration and under-valuing artifact-count thresholds (metalcraft, "for each artifact you control").

## Correct behavior
An `ArtifactsFeature` detects artifact density and artifact-count payoffs (affinity/improvise enablers, metalcraft/threshold effects, Treasure/Clue/Food token generators, "artifacts you control" anthems). A companion `TacticalPolicy` values keeping the artifact count above relevant thresholds and sequencing cheap artifacts before affinity/improvise spells — inert when the deck has no artifact payoffs.

## Design (the `add-ai-feature-policy` pattern — verified wiring sites)
1. **New `crates/phase-ai/src/features/artifacts.rs`** — `pub struct ArtifactsFeature { … }` + `pub fn detect(deck: &[DeckEntry]) -> ArtifactsFeature`, parts-based (artifact_count, payoff_count, cost-reducer_count).
2. **`features/mod.rs`** — `pub mod artifacts;`, add `pub artifacts: ArtifactsFeature` to `DeckFeatures`, and `artifacts: artifacts::detect(deck)` in `analyze()`.
3. **New `crates/phase-ai/src/policies/artifact_synergy.rs`** — a `TacticalPolicy` scored with `PolicyVerdict` band helpers; gated on artifact-payoff presence.
4. **`policies/registry.rs`** — register in the default `vec![Box::new(...)]`.
5. **Tests in a SEPARATE file** (`features/tests/artifacts.rs` + a policy test file); impl files contain no `#[cfg(test)]`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `ArtifactsFeature` detects artifact density + payoffs (parts-based, not name-matching) and is wired into `DeckFeatures::analyze`.
- [ ] An `artifact_synergy` `TacticalPolicy` (band-helper scored, payoff-gated) is registered in `PolicyRegistry::default`.
- [ ] `cargo ai-gate` non-regressing on non-artifact decks and improving on artifact decks, with the **paired-seed report attached**.
- [ ] Detector + policy tests in separate test files (impl files stay inline-test-free).
- [ ] No `no_name_matching` lint violation.

## Summary
`phase-ai` has a `life_total_resource` policy (treats life as a payable resource) but **no lifegain-synergy axis**: it cannot recognize a deck built around lifegain *payoffs* (Soul Warden / Heliod / Archangel of Thune style) and therefore does not value gaining life when a payoff is on board. This adds the missing `LifegainFeature` + policy via the supported `add-ai-feature-policy` pattern.

## Current behavior
`DeckFeatures::analyze` (`features/mod.rs`) detects 9 axes; none detect lifegain-matters. With no feature, the AI treats incidental lifegain as near-worthless (correct for most decks) even when the deck contains payoffs that convert each life-gain event into card advantage, counters, tokens, or damage — so it misvalues both its keeps and its in-game lines on lifegain decks.

## Correct behavior
A `LifegainFeature` detects lifegain density: lifegain *sources* (lifelink, "gain N life", incidental gain) and lifegain *payoffs* ("whenever you gain life, …", lifegain-threshold effects). A companion `TacticalPolicy` raises the value of triggering/sequencing lifegain when a payoff is present (and leaves it ~neutral when no payoff exists, so non-lifegain decks are unaffected).

## Design (the `add-ai-feature-policy` pattern — verified wiring sites)
1. **New `crates/phase-ai/src/features/lifegain.rs`** — `pub struct LifegainFeature { … }` + `pub fn detect(deck: &[DeckEntry]) -> LifegainFeature`, parts-based (source_count, payoff_count), mirroring an existing detector.
2. **`features/mod.rs`** — `pub mod lifegain;`, add `pub lifegain: LifegainFeature` to `DeckFeatures`, and `lifegain: lifegain::detect(deck)` in `analyze()`.
3. **New `crates/phase-ai/src/policies/lifegain_payoff.rs`** — a `TacticalPolicy` scored with `PolicyVerdict` band helpers; gates its bonus on `payoff_count > 0` so it is inert for non-lifegain decks.
4. **`policies/registry.rs`** — register in the default `vec![Box::new(...)]`.
5. **Tests in a SEPARATE file** (`features/tests/lifegain.rs` + a policy test file); impl files contain no `#[cfg(test)]`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `LifegainFeature` detects source/payoff density (parts-based, not name-matching) and is wired into `DeckFeatures::analyze`.
- [ ] A `lifegain_payoff` `TacticalPolicy` (band-helper scored, payoff-gated) is registered in `PolicyRegistry::default`.
- [ ] `cargo ai-gate` is non-regressing on non-lifegain decks and improving on lifegain decks, with the **paired-seed report attached**.
- [ ] Detector + policy tests in separate test files (impl files stay inline-test-free).
- [ ] No `no_name_matching` lint violation.

problems.title: feat(engine): first kicked spell per-turn cost reduction static
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Parse and enforce `"The first kicked spell you cast each turn costs {N} less to cast."` (Vine Gecko class).

## Background

The shared first-qualified-spell cost parser explicitly declines `"kicked"` qualifiers today:

```rust
// static_first_kicked_spell_does_not_emit_broad_reducer
assert!(parse_static_line("The first kicked spell you cast each turn costs {1} less to cast.").is_none());
```

Emitting a filterless reducer would silently drop both the once-per-turn gate and the kicked qualifier, reducing every spell the controller casts.

Infrastructure exists: `parse_first_qualified_spell_filter`, `SpellsCastThisTurn` conditions, and `times_kicked` on the pending cast context.

## Proposed solution

1. **Parser:** Recognize bare `"kicked"` pre-spell qualifier in `parse_first_qualified_spell_filter` → spell filter with new `FilterProp::WasKicked`.
2. **Engine:** Evaluate `WasKicked` against pending cast kicker payment (`times_kicked > 0`) in live spell filter matching; record kicker-paid state on `SpellCastRecord` for turn-history queries.
3. **Runtime:** Existing first-spell `SpellsCastThisTurn == 0` condition gates the reducer.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Vine Gecko static parses to `ModifyCost { Reduce, ... }` with `WasKicked` filter and first-spell condition
- [ ] First kicked spell per turn gets `{1}` reduction; second kicked spell same turn does not
- [ ] Non-kicked spells unaffected
- [ ] `"The first spell you cast each turn costs {1} less"` regression unchanged
- [ ] Parser + casting unit tests

## CR references

CR 601.2f, CR 702.33d

## Affected files

- `crates/engine/src/types/ability.rs` (`FilterProp::WasKicked`)
- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/grammar.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/game/filter.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/types/game_state.rs` (`SpellCastRecord`)
- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/tests.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/game/casting.rs` (tests)

problems.title: Name-hate ("search GY/hand/library for cards with the same name and exile") is dropped
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
The classic **name-hate** cards are dropped as `Unimplemented` even though all the runtime infra exists. The pattern: **"[exile/counter/choose target X]. Search its controller's/owner's graveyard, hand, and library for [all | any number of] cards with the same name as that [creature/land/spell/card] and exile them. Then that player shuffles."**

## Affected cards
- **Eradicate**: "Exile target nonblack creature. Search its controller's graveyard, hand, and library for all cards with the same name as that creature and exile them. Then that player shuffles."
- **Quash**: "Counter target instant or sorcery spell. Search ... same name as that spell and exile them. Then that player shuffles."
- **Counterbore**: "Counter target spell. Search ... same name as that spell and exile them. Then that player shuffles."
- **Crumble to Dust**: "Exile target nonbasic land. Search ... any number of cards with the same name as that land and exile them. Then that player shuffles."
- **Surgical Extraction**: "Choose target card in a graveyard ... Search its owner's graveyard, hand, and library for any number of cards with the same name as that card and exile them. Then that player shuffles." (Memoricide already works — same chain.)

## Root cause (two parser issues; runtime is complete)
The full chain `ChangeZoneAll{ InAnyZone[Graveyard,Hand,Library] + SameNameAsParentTarget } -> Exile` + `Shuffle{ParentTargetController}` already works (Memoricide is supported, with `FilterProp::SameNameAsParentTarget`, `Effect::ChangeZoneAll`, the `try_parse_multi_zone_same_name_exile` combinator, and `Effect::Shuffle`). These cards still gap because:
1. **Suffix-matcher too narrow** — `parse_search_exile_name_suffix` (`parser/oracle_effect/sequence.rs`) accepts only "...same name as that **card**", not "...as that **creature / land / spell**". So the chain splitter truncates the search clause and `try_parse_multi_zone_same_name_exile` fails.
2. **Dispatch precedence** — even with the suffix accepted, a higher-priority chain path lowers the chained "...and exile them" to a generic `ChangeZoneAll{ target: ParentTarget }` (re-exiles only the single primary target) instead of routing to the correct `MultiZoneSameNameExile`. The fix must make the chained sub-clause route through the same-name multi-zone exile, NOT the generic exile-rider — without regressing legitimate "exile it/them" rider cards.

## Expected
Route these to the existing `ChangeZoneAll{ InAnyZone[GY,Hand,Library] + SameNameAsParentTarget } -> Exile` + `Shuffle{ParentTargetController}`, with the same-name filter resolving the exiled/countered/chosen object's name via last-known-info.

CR 201.2 (same name), CR 701.23 (Search), CR 701.24 (Shuffle), CR 400.7 (zone change creates a new object).

problems.title: "Two target players exchange life totals" / "exchange life totals with target opponent" is unimplemented
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
Cards that make **two players exchange life totals** are unimplemented. The existing `ExchangeLifeWithStat` (#1286) handles life ↔ a creature's stat, but there is no **player-to-player** life-total exchange.

## Affected cards
- **Soul Conduit**: "{6}, {T}: Two target players exchange life totals."
- **Axis of Mortality**: "At the beginning of your upkeep, you may have two target players exchange life totals."
- **Magus of the Mirror**: "{T}, Sacrifice this creature: Exchange life totals with target opponent. Activate only during your upkeep."
- **Mirror Universe**: "{T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Exchange life totals with target opponent. Activate only during your upkeep."

## Expected
A player-to-player life-total exchange ("two target players" → the two targeted players; "exchange life totals with target opponent" → controller ↔ the target opponent). Both players' life totals swap simultaneously (each becomes the other's previous total), all-or-nothing per CR 701.12a (mirroring `ExchangeLifeWithStat`'s CR 119.5 gain/lose-to-reach + CR 119.7/119.8 can't-gain/can't-lose handling), so if either change is forbidden no part of the exchange occurs.

CR 701.12a (exchange life totals — all-or-nothing), CR 119.3/119.5 (life loss/gain to reach a value).

problems.title: AI: add a Reanimator / graveyard-recursion deck-feature axis + policy
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
`phase-ai` has no concept of the **reanimator** archetype: reanimation spells that put a big creature from a graveyard onto the battlefield, the **enablers** that fill the graveyard (self-mill, discard), and the high-impact **payoffs** (expensive creatures) reanimated ahead of curve. The AI values none of this as a *plan* — it won't prioritize self-milling/discarding to set up a reanimation, nor value holding a reanimation spell for a fat target. This adds the missing `ReanimatorFeature` + payoff-gated policy via the supported `add-ai-feature-policy` pattern.

## Why it's valuable / necessary
Reanimator is a recurring archetype across Modern (Goryo's Vengeance, Persist), Legacy (Reanimate, Animate Dead, Exhume, Entomb), Pioneer (Greasefang), and Commander (Unburial Rites, Reanimate). The engine already resolves these cards correctly (verified: Reanimate, Unburial Rites, Exhume, Goryo's Vengeance all parse to the expected typed AST), but the AI plays them as disconnected goodstuff — no axis ties "fill graveyard → reanimate threat."

**Support, measured directly in `card-data.json` (34,771 cards):**
- **~683 cards** carry a graveyard→battlefield `Effect::ChangeZone` (`origin = Graveyard`, `destination = Battlefield`) — the reanimation-**payoff** signature.
- **~303 of those** target a creature `TargetFilter` — the core payoff class the detector keys on.
- Enablers are broad: **~570 cards** with a `Mill` effect, **~1,942** with a `Discard` effect.

> An earlier draft cited "3,958 cards with a graveyard→battlefield signature." That number was a loose union of all graveyard-adjacent effects and is corrected above: the GY→BF payoff class is ~300–700 cards. Still comfortably axis-worthy — larger than several existing niche axes — but the support claim is now honest.

## Current behavior
`DeckFeatures::analyze` (`features/mod.rs`) detects 12 structural axes; none recognizes reanimation. Existing graveyard-adjacent AI logic is **targeting-side only**:
- `policies/recursion_awareness.rs` — avoids feeding an opponent's recursive / death-trigger creature to a harmful effect (a targeting heuristic).
- `policies/mill_targeting.rs` — optimizes *who* to mill; notably carries `SELF_MILL_PENALTY = -0.2`, i.e. it **discourages** self-mill when not obviously beneficial.

Neither encodes a deck-level "enabler → reanimation payoff" plan. **Integration note:** the new policy's enabler bonus (raising the value of self-mill) sums against `mill_targeting`'s self-mill penalty in the registry, so it must be calibrated to overcome that penalty only when reanimation payoffs **and** worthwhile targets are both present.

## Correct behavior
A `ReanimatorFeature` detects three structural roles over the typed AST (parts-based, no card-name matching):
- **Reanimation payoffs** — `Effect::ChangeZone` (`crates/engine/src/types/ability.rs:7147`) with `origin = Some(Graveyard)`, `destination = Battlefield`, and a creature `TargetFilter` (mirrors how `features/landfall.rs` k…

problems.issue_body:
## Summary
`phase-ai` cannot recognize an **equipment-matters / voltron** deck: a dense Equipment package, equip payoffs (equipped-creature buffs, equipment-cast / ETB triggers, equip-cost grants/reducers), and creatures that fetch or auto-attach Equipment (Stoneforge Mystic, Kor Outfitter, Sram, Puresteel Paladin). The AI today values equipment only as generic artifacts and has no plan-level recognition of equipping toward a single threat (voltron) or of equip payoffs. This adds the missing `EquipmentFeature` + payoff-gated policy via the `add-ai-feature-policy` pattern.

## Why it's valuable / necessary
Equipment decks are a real, recurring archetype: Modern Hammer Time (Colossus Hammer + Sigarda's Aid / Puresteel Paladin), Stoneblade, and Commander voltron. The engine already resolves Equip, equipped-creature statics, and Equipment tutors (verified: Bonesplitter, Puresteel Paladin, Sram, Stoneforge Mystic, Kor Outfitter all parse to the expected typed AST), but the AI has no plan-level recognition.

**Support, measured directly in `card-data.json` (34,771 cards):**
- **632 cards** carry the `Equipment` subtype (all `Artifact`) — the fuel.
- **672 cards** have "equipped creature" oracle text — the equipped-creature-payoff signature.

> An earlier draft cited "828 cards … equipment signature." That figure is corrected above: the Equipment-subtype class is ~632 and the equipped-creature-payoff-text class is ~672. Still comfortably axis-worthy — comparable to the merged reanimator axis (~683) — but the support claim is now honest.

## Current behavior
`DeckFeatures::analyze` (`features/mod.rs`) has no equipment axis — Equipment falls under generic artifact valuation (`features/artifacts.rs` values artifact *count* / affinity-improvise payoffs, with zero equip-payoff or voltron awareness). On the policy side, equipment is **not** entirely unhandled:
- `policies/equipment_priority.rs` (`PolicyId::EquipmentPriority`, registered) already exists — but it is an **anti-over-equipping guard**: it *rejects* wasteful same-host re-equips and strict downgrades (the Skullclamp #1986 bug) and, by design, "never *rewards* equipping."

So nothing values the voltron plan, equip payoffs, or equipment density — but the equip decision is already partly governed. **Integration note:** the proposed policy *rewards* equipping, which fires on the same `DecisionKind::ActivateAbility` / `WaitingFor::EquipTarget` decisions that `EquipmentPriorityPolicy` penalizes. The two sum in the registry, so the new policy must be calibrated to encourage *fresh* equips / voltron concentration **without** overriding the over-equip guard's rejection of pointless re-equips (analogous to the reanimator ↔ `mill_targeting` self-mill interaction).

## Correct behavior
An `EquipmentFeature` detects (parts-based, no card-name matching):

problems.title: AI: add a Blink / Flicker (ETB-value) deck-feature axis + policy
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
`phase-ai` cannot recognize a **blink / flicker** deck: flicker effects (exile a permanent you control and immediately return it to the battlefield) paired with **enter-the-battlefield payoffs** (ETB triggers worth re-triggering). The AI today treats a flicker spell as a minor protection/reset and a value creature's ETB as one-shot — it has no plan tying "flicker → re-trigger value." This adds the missing `BlinkFeature` + payoff-gated policy.

## Why it's valuable / necessary
Blink/flicker is a recurring archetype (Modern/Pioneer Ephemerate + Soulherder + Restoration Angel value shells; Commander ETB/flicker). The engine resolves flicker (`Effect::ChangeZone` exile→battlefield chain) and ETB triggers already; the AI lacks the plan-level axis. Distinct from existing axes: `aristocrats` keys on sacrifice/death, `tokens_wide` on going wide, `etb_value.rs` scores ETB value at **cast time only** (one-shot) — none recognize ETB-reuse via flicker.

## Current behavior
`DeckFeatures::analyze` (`features/mod.rs`) has no blink axis; flicker spells and ETB density are unmodeled as a synergy. `policies/etb_value.rs` evaluates ETB triggers at cast time via `cast_facts().immediate_etb_triggers` but does not model re-trigger cycles from flickering.

## Correct behavior
A `BlinkFeature` detects:

**Flicker enablers** — an `AbilityDefinition` whose `collect_chain_effects` chain contains BOTH:
1. `Effect::ChangeZone { destination: Zone::Exile, target: Typed(Creature/Permanent, controller=You), .. }` (exile a friendly permanent), AND
2. a subsequent `Effect::ChangeZone { destination: Zone::Battlefield, target: TrackedSet { .. }, .. }` in the same chain (return it)

This is the verified parse shape of real flicker cards. **Ephemerate** (`card-data.json`) parses as:
```
ChangeZone { destination: Exile, target: Typed(Creature, controller=You) }
  └─ sub_ability: ChangeZone { destination: Battlefield, target: TrackedSet { id: 0 } }
```
Detection must walk the full `sub_ability` chain via `crate::ability_chain::collect_chain_effects` and require BOTH steps — a lone `destination: Battlefield` check would also match reanimation (graveyard→battlefield); a lone `destination: Exile` check would match removal. Both steps together are the flicker signature.

**ETB payoff density** — creatures with `TriggerMode::ChangesZone` and `destination: Some(Zone::Battlefield)` carrying meaningful effects (the value being re-triggered). The controller constraint ("your creatures") lives inside `valid_card: Option<TargetFilter>` as `TypedFilter { controller: Some(ControllerRef::You) }` — not as a separate field on `TriggerDefinition`.

A companion **payoff-gated** `TacticalPolicy` raises the value of flickering a high-ETB-value creature and of deploying flicker engines when ETB density is high; inert otherwise.

## AST verification (verified against `crates/engine/src/types/`)

| Axis | AST type | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Flicker chain step 1 | `Effect::ChangeZone { destinatio…

problems.issue_body:
Cards whose self-referential continuous static is gated by the pronoun form "as long as it's untapped" are reported `supported=false` even though the condition is fully evaluated at runtime: Dragonlord Ojutai, Giant Tortoise, Iymrith, Desert Doom, Paradise Druid, Illusion Spinners, Walking Skyscraper, Sokrates, Athenian Teacher (7 flip; more share the pattern).

`parse_continuous_gets_has` types the "as long as <cond>" clause via `parse_static_condition`, but the source-subject parser only accepts `~`/`this creature`/etc., so the contracted pronoun subject "it's untapped" falls through to `StaticCondition::Unrecognized` — despite `Not(SourceIsTapped)` being a fully-handled, layer-evaluated condition (the explicit "~ is untapped" form already works).

Fix: in a **self-referential** static (affected subject is `SelfRef`), resolve a leading "it's "/"it is " to the canonical "~ is " before typing the condition. Two guards keep it correct:
- only when affected == SelfRef (an Aura/Equipment's "it" refers to the enchanted/equipped creature, not the source — e.g. Spectral Cloak stays an honest gap), and
- only for the bare source-state predicates `~ is …` resolves (tapped/untapped). "it" is otherwise overloaded — "it's your turn" is impersonal, "it's a Wall"/"it's red"/"it's legendary" are characteristic gates with their own parse paths — so those are left untouched.

Local regen: 7 cards flip to supported, 0 regressions; Spectral Cloak (Aura) correctly stays gapped.

CR 611.3a.

problems.title: Coverage: "Damage isn't removed during cleanup steps" statics unsupported (CR 514.2)
problems.issue_body:
Cards with a "Damage isn't removed from [subject] during cleanup steps" static are reported unsupported because the clause isn't modeled: Ancient Adamantoise, Patient Zero, Uthgardt Fury, Case of the Market Melee (plus Melt Through, Switchgrass Grazer which share the wording alongside other text).

CR 514.2: removing all marked damage is a turn-based action during the cleanup step. These statics suppress that removal for the permanents they match, so marked damage persists across turns. There is no engine mechanism for it today — the cleanup step clears every permanent's `damage_marked` unconditionally.

Proposed: add `StaticMode::DamageNotRemovedDuringCleanup` (nullary marker; the subject rides the definition's `affected` filter — `this creature` → SelfRef, `creatures your opponents control` → a typed filter). In `execute_cleanup`, gather the permanents matched by an active such static and skip clearing their damage. Parser recognizes the line via the sanctioned `scan_contains`/`split_once_on_lower` + `parse_type_phrase` building blocks.

Local regen: 4 cards flip to supported, 0 regressions; full engine lib suite green.

problems.title: Hideaway — opponent's face-down hideaway-exiled card is visible in the Exile zone
problems.issue_body:
## Reported behavior

<JohnDoe>: "So, good news Hideaway working from the latest thing! Bad news, I apparently know my opponent has a Ghalta Primal Hunger sitting there... (I can see it in Exile as well)."

Hideaway now functions at runtime (the exile-face-down step works), but the card exiled face down by an opponent's Hideaway permanent is shown face up / by name to the reporter in the Exile zone.

## Expected vs actual

- Expected: A card exiled face down by Hideaway (CR 702.76 / face-down exile) is hidden information to opponents — they should not see its identity. Only the controller (and only as permitted) may look at it.
- Actual: The opponent's hideaway-exiled card is identifiable (named) in the Exile zone to the other player.

## Notes

This is a hidden-zone visibility leak, distinct from the now-closed runtime feature issue #2525 ('Hideaway keyword has no runtime') and from #630 ('Hideaway not triggering'). Face-down exiled cards must be gated on the engine's reveal sets and not surfaced by name to players who are not permitted to see them.
