problems.title: AI: add a Mill deck-feature axis + policy
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
`phase-ai` cannot recognize a **mill** deck — one whose win condition is emptying an opponent's library. The AI values milling incidentally via generic eval; it has no plan-level recognition of mill density, no awareness of how close the opponent is to decking, and no policy that raises the value of mill spells when the opponent's library is running low. This adds the missing `MillFeature` + payoff-gated policy.

## Why it's valuable / necessary
Mill is a real archetype (Pioneer/Historic Mill, Legacy, Commander). `Effect::Mill` is already resolved by the engine. The AI gap is plan recognition: treating high mill-effect density as a coherent win condition and shifting priority toward mill spells as the opponent's library shrinks.

## Current behavior
`DeckFeatures::analyze` (`features/mod.rs`) has no mill field. `FeatureKind` has 14 variants, none is Mill. Mill spells are valued incidentally; there is no recognition of mill-as-wincon or state-aware scaling based on opponent library size.

## Correct behavior

**Detection axis — single pillar.**
Mill is a one-dimensional axis: a deck either has enough mill-effect density to close out a game or it doesn't. There is no structurally distinct "payoff" class separate from enablers (unlike reanimator or blink, where enabler and payoff are clearly different AST shapes). The feature is therefore a single-pillar density commitment, matching the `AggroPressureFeature` pattern.

`MillFeature` detects **opponent-targeted mill enablers**: abilities/trigger chains containing `Effect::Mill { destination: Zone::Graveyard, target, .. }` where `target` is NOT `TargetFilter::Controller` or `TargetFilter::Any` (those are self-mill, already used by the reanimator axis). Opponent mill uses `TargetFilter::Player`, `TargetFilter::Opponent`, or a `Typed` filter with `controller: Some(ControllerRef::Opponent)`. The complement of `target_fills_own_graveyard` in `features/reanimator.rs` (line 258) is the exact predicate needed.

## AST verification (verified against `crates/engine/src/types/`)

| Axis | AST type | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Mill effect | `Effect::Mill { count: QuantityExpr, target: TargetFilter, destination: Zone }` | `ability.rs:7111` |
| Opponent mill target | `target` is NOT `TargetFilter::Controller` or `TargetFilter::Any` | complement of `reanimator.rs:258` |
| Self-mill (excluded) | `target: Controller \| Any`, already used by reanimator axis | `reanimator.rs:258` |
| Ability chain walk | `crate::ability_chain::collect_chain_effects(ability)` | `phase-ai` |
| Opponent library size | `state.players[opponent_id].library.len()` | `player.rs:96` |

## Design

1. **New `crates/phase-ai/src/features/mill.rs`** — `pub struct MillFeature { mill_count: u32, commitment: f32 }` + structural `detect()`. Single-pillar density commitment (mirrors `AggroPressureFeature` shape, not geometric-mean). `pub(crate) fn effect_is_opponent_mill(effect: &Effect) -> bool` is the shared predicate.

problems.title: AI: add an Energy-economy deck-feature axis + policy
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
`phase-ai` values a raw energy counter at a flat `energy * 0.1` (`eval.rs:402`) but has no energy-matters axis: it cannot recognize a deck built around energy **producers** feeding **sinks/payoffs**, so it never values *building* energy toward a payoff. This adds an `EnergyFeature` (energy-economy recognition) + a payoff-gated, reserve-aware `TacticalPolicy`.

## Verified facts (current `main` @ `02f5931b7`)
- **Gap confirmed:** no `features/energy.rs`, no `policies/energy_payoff.rs`, no `FeatureKind::Energy` (enum has 15 variants, ending at `Mill`).
- **Flat valuation:** `eval.rs:402` — `breakdown.hand_size += p.energy as f64 * 0.1;` (CR 122.1 comment). No producers/sinks recognition.
- **Producer primitive:** `Effect::GainEnergy { amount }` — `crates/engine/src/types/ability.rs:8717` (Effect enum).
- **Sink primitive:** `AbilityCost::PayEnergy { amount }` — `ability.rs:5888` (AbilityCost enum).
- **`Effect::Energy` is NOT a producer** — `Energy { amount }` (`ability.rs:6622`) is a **legacy cost** variant that converts to `AbilityCost::PayEnergy` (`ability.rs:6638`). Any detector that keys on `Effect::Energy` is wrong; use `Effect::GainEnergy`.
- **Card pool (structural, card-data.json):** ~122 unique producer cards, **~25 unique `PayEnergy`-sink cards** (the prior draft's "140 / 125" was inflated — producers ~right, sinks were ~5× over). The sink pool is small, so the feature's value hinges on a dense energy-engine deck, not breadth.
- **Pre-existing deck/matchup:** `duel_decks/modern/boros-energy.json` and the `boros-energy-mirror` matchup already exist, tagged `exercises: &[FeatureKind::AggroPressure]` (spec.rs:343). Boros Energy is an aggro deck where energy is incidental (~8–12 energy-relevant cards). **Do not retag it** — it belongs to AggroPressure. A new energy-engine snapshot is required instead.

## Correct behavior
`EnergyFeature` recognizes the full energy economy:
- **Producers** — any `Effect::GainEnergy` reachable through an ability chain **or** a trigger's `execute` chain (including sub-ability chains — e.g. Rogue Refiner's ETB `{E}`, which a flat walk misses).
- **Sinks/payoffs** — any `AbilityCost::PayEnergy`, including those nested in modal/choices structures (e.g. Harnessed Lightning, Confiscation Coup activations), not only top-level ability costs.
- **Commitment** — payoff-weighted density (producer∩sink density, not producer-count alone), so a deck must actually *spend* energy to score.

A payoff-gated `EnergyPayoffPolicy` values producing/holding energy when the deck has sinks (inert otherwise) and is **reserve-aware**: it scales with the live energy reserve vs. the deck's sink thresholds (analogous to MillPayoffPolicy's library-size urgency).

## Design (rich detector — the score lever)
1. **New `crates/phase-ai/src/features/energy.rs`** — `pub struct EnergyFeature { producer_count, sink_count, payoff_count, commitment }` + structural `detect()`.

problems.issue_body:

"Heist" is a card-defined action word from *Murders at Karlov Manor* (2024), a mainstream, heavily-played set (Commander / Modern / Legacy legal). > *"Look at three random nonland cards from target opponent's library. Exile one of them face down. You may cast that card for as long as it remains exiled, and you may spend mana as though it were mana of any type to cast that spell."*

It also commits a crime against the targeted opponent.

problems.title: Parser: leading-"If [condition], this spell costs {N} less to cast" drops the condition (Avatar cycle)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

A cost-reduction static written with a **leading** condition — `"If [condition], this spell costs {N} less to cast."` — silently drops the condition, so the reduction applies **unconditionally**. The cost-modifier condition extractor only looks for a **trailing** `if` / `as long as` clause (`lower.rfind(" as long as ")` / `rfind(" if ")` in `parse_static_line`'s cost-mod path, `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/static_helpers.rs`), so a condition that appears before the cost clause is never attached.

Affected real cards (all from the "Avatar" cycle plus others):

- **Avatar of Will** — "If an opponent has no cards in hand, this spell costs {6} less to cast."
- **Avatar of Fury** — "If an opponent controls seven or more lands, this spell costs {6} less to cast."
- **Avatar of Hope** — "If you have 3 or less life, this spell costs {6} less to cast."
- **Avatar of Might** — "If an opponent controls at least four more creatures than you, this spell costs {6} less to cast."
- **Avatar of Woe** — "If there are ten or more creature cards total in all graveyards, this spell costs {6} less to cast."
- **Phantasmal Extraction / Unforgiving Overtake / Unnatural Summons** — "If you weren't the starting player, this spell costs {1} less to cast."
- **Shadow of Mortality** — "If your life total is less than your starting life total, this spell costs {X} less to cast, where X is the difference."

## Current (wrong) parse

`parse_static_line("If an opponent has no cards in hand, this spell costs {6} less to cast.")` yields a `ModifyCost` static with `condition == None`. The reduction is treated as always-on, so every Avatar in the cycle costs {6} less regardless of its board condition.

## Root cause

The cost-mod condition extraction is trailing-only:

```rust
if let Some((cond_pos, marker)) = [" as long as ", " if "]
    .into_iter()
    .filter_map(|marker| lower.rfind(marker).map(|pos| (pos, marker)))
    .max_by_key(|(pos, _)| *pos)
{ ... parse_inner_condition(cond_text) ... }
```

A leading `"If …, this spell costs …"` has no preceding-space `" if "`, so nothing is extracted.

## Expected behavior

Recognize the leading `"If [condition], this spell costs {N} less to cast"` form: strip the leading `"if [condition], "` prefix, route `[condition]` through the existing `parse_inner_condition` (which already handles all the conditions above — "an opponent has no cards in hand", "you have 3 or less life", "an opponent controls at least four more creatures than you", etc.), and attach it as the static's `condition`. The cost-clause parse of the remainder is unchanged.

## Notes

Discovered while verifying #3843/#3844 (the condition-phrasing fix for "an opponent has no cards in hand" works through the static and trigger paths but not this cost-mod path). Parser-only; the conditions themselves are already supported. CR 601.2f / CR 608.2g (cost modification), CR 603.4 (intervening-if-style gate).

problems.title: Parser: multi-clause "spend this mana only to cast X or Y, or activate Z" restrictions are dropped (Maelstrom of the Spi
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Multi-clause mana-spend restrictions — "Spend this mana only to cast **X or Y**" (or "… to cast X, Y, **or** activate Z") — are silently dropped. `parse_mana_spend_restriction` only recognizes a *single* restriction clause, so a heterogeneous disjunction (different spell types, a keyword, and/or an ability activation) returns `None` and the produced mana carries **no** restriction — it can be spent on anything (CR 106.6 violated).

Affected real cards:

- **Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon** — "{T}: Add {R}{R}{R}. Spend this mana only to cast **a Dragon spell or an Omen spell**."
- **Brotherhood Headquarters** — "{T}: Add {B}. Spend this mana only to cast **an Assassin spell or a spell that has freerunning, or to activate an ability of an Assassin source**."
- **Chandra's Embercat** — "{T}: Add {R}{R}. Spend this mana only to cast **an Elemental spell or a Chandra planeswalker spell**."

(The single-clause forms — "creature spells", "spells with mana value N or greater", "a spell with flashback", "an artifact spell or activate an ability of an artifact source", etc. — already work; only the heterogeneous *disjunction* is dropped.)

## Current (wrong) parse

`parse_mana_spend_restriction("spend this mana only to cast a dragon spell or an omen spell")` returns `None`: the post-"to cast " remainder is parsed as one clause, and "a dragon spell or an omen spell" matches no single type-phrase. The restriction is dropped and the mana becomes unrestricted.

## Root cause

The runtime `ManaRestriction` enum has no disjunction variant, and the parser has no path that splits a remainder into multiple independent clauses. The existing `OnlyForSpellType` already handles a type *union* inside one clause ("instant or sorcery spells" → one `SpellType`), but cannot express a disjunction of *different kinds* of restriction (type vs. keyword vs. activation).

## Expected behavior

Add a composition combinator `ManaRestriction::OnlyForAny(Vec<ManaRestriction>)` — the mana may be spent on any payment satisfying at least one branch — and parse the disjunctive Oracle form into it. `allows_spell`/`allows_activation` short-circuit across the branches.

- "a Dragon spell or an Omen spell" → `OnlyForAny([OnlyForSpellType("Dragon"), OnlyForSpellType("Omen")])`.
- "an Assassin spell or a spell that has freerunning, or to activate an ability of an Assassin source" → `OnlyForAny([OnlyForSpellType("Assassin"), OnlyForSpellWithKeywordKind(Freerunning), OnlyForTypeSpellsOrAbilities { spell_type: "Assassin", ability: OfSpellType }])`.

## Notes

A general combinator ("parameterize, don't proliferate"): each branch is itself a full restriction, evaluated through the existing `allows`/`allows_spell`/`allows_activation` single-authority dispatch. Clauses that require call-site deferral ("pay a cost that contains {C}") are left as gaps rather than mismodeled. CR 106.6 (spending restrictions on produced mana).

problems.title: Parser: "up to two target creatures you control each deal damage equal to their power to target creature" is dropped (Al
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The "team-up" damage line — "**Up to two target creatures you control each deal damage equal to their power to target creature [filter]**" — is dropped to `Effect::Unimplemented`. The whole damage effect does nothing.

Affected real cards:

- **Allies at Last** — "Up to two target creatures you control each deal damage equal to their power to target creature an opponent controls."
- **Band Together** — "Up to two target creatures you control each deal damage equal to their power to another target creature."
- **Friendly Rivalry**, **Graceful Takedown** — "…to target creature you don't control."
- **Combo Attack** — "Two target creatures **your team** controls each deal damage equal to their power to target creature." (Two-Headed-Giant team scope — a separate axis)
- **Coordinated Clobbering** — "Tap one or two target untapped creatures you control. They each deal damage equal to their power to target creature an opponent controls." (tap variant)

All show `Effect::Unimplemented { name: "deal", description: "deal damage equal to their power to target creature…" }` in card-data.

## Current (wrong) parse

The effect chunk "(up to two target creatures you control) each deal damage equal to their power to (target creature …)" has no handler — it falls through to `Effect::unimplemented`. The engine has `Effect::DealDamage { amount, target, damage_source }` and `DamageSource` (Target / TriggeringSource) and `QuantityRef::Power { scope }`, but **no** mechanism for *each of a multi-target set of creatures* dealing damage equal to *its own* power.

## Expected behavior

Model "each of the [up to two] target source-creatures deals damage equal to its power to the target recipient-creature." At resolution, for each resolved source creature, deal damage equal to that creature's power, with that creature as the damage source, to the recipient.

## Notes

Two target slots: the sources ("up to two"/"two"/"one or two target creatures you control") and the recipient ("target creature [filter]"). Reuses the existing damage primitive per source; the new piece is the multi-source iteration. CR 120.3 (damage source), CR 601.2c / CR 115 (targeting). The tap variant (Coordinated Clobbering) may be scoped separately.

problems.title: Parser: "as long as this creature is enchanted" static applies permanently (condition parses to inert Unrecognized)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Static abilities gated on "as long as this creature is enchanted" apply **permanently** instead of only while an Aura is attached — the condition parses to an inert `StaticCondition::Unrecognized`, which the layer system evaluates as always-true.

Affected (5 statics):
- **Pillar of War** — "As long as this creature is enchanted, it can attack as though it didn't have defender." (attacks even with no Aura)
- **Thran Golem** — "As long as this creature is enchanted, it gets +2/+2 and has flying, first strike, and trample." (permanently buffed)
- **Gate Hound** — "Creatures you control have vigilance as long as this creature is enchanted." (anthem always on)
- **Freewind Equenaut** — "As long as this creature is enchanted, it has '{T}: …deals 2 damage…'."
- **Flaring Flame-Kin** — same idiom.

## Current (wrong) parse

The condition is `StaticCondition::Unrecognized { text: "~ is enchanted" }`. `Unrecognized` is treated as unconditionally true, so the granted P/T, keywords, anthem, or attack-despite-defender applies at all times.

## Root cause

The source-subject condition parser has arms for "is equipped" / "is monstrous" / "is saddled", but no arm for "is enchanted", so it falls through to the `Unrecognized` fallback. There was no `SourceIsEnchanted` condition at all.

## Expected

A `SourceIsEnchanted` condition — the Aura-twin of the existing `SourceIsEquipped` (an Aura is attached to the source) — evaluated by the layer system so the effect applies only while an Aura is attached.

## Notes

The "is enchanted by N Auras" count form is unaffected (it's matched first). "is enchanted or equipped" (Novice Knight) remains an honest gap. CR 303.4 / 301.5 / 611.3a.

problems.title: Parser: Conspiracy "Creatures you control are the chosen type" (SET form) unimplemented
problems.issue_body:
### Gap

Conspiracy's continuous type-changing static — "Creatures you control are the chosen type." (the **SET** form, replacing creature subtypes) — lowers to `Effect::Unimplemented`. The parallel **ADD** form, "Creatures you control are the chosen type **in addition to their other types**." (Arcane Adaptation), already parses; only the replace form is missing.

**Exemplar — Conspiracy** (verified gapped on current `main`):

> As this enchantment enters, choose a creature type. Creatures you control are the chosen type. The same is true for creature spells you control and creature cards you own that aren't on the battlefield.

Root cause: the chosen-creature-type static parser hard-requires the " ... the chosen type **in addition to** ... other types" suffix, so the bare "are the chosen type" (replace) sentence fails and falls through to the static fallback (`static_structure: line failed static parser`).

### Note on the trailing clause

"The same is true for creature spells you control and creature cards you own that aren't on the battlefield." applies a continuous type change to the stack and to hidden zones, which the engine does not currently model (same as Maskwood Nexus). That clause should remain an honest `Unimplemented` — only the battlefield SET form is the gap here.

### Repro

Parse Conspiracy's Oracle text via `parse_oracle_text`; the "Creatures you control are the chosen type." clause lowers to `Effect::Unimplemented` rather than a type-setting static.

problems.title: Counterspell zone-redirect silently dropped (Memory Lapse, Remand, Hinder, Spell Crumple) — countered spell goes to grav
problems.issue_body:
# fix(engine): counter target spell with a zone redirect — "put it [on top/bottom of its owner's library | into its owner's hand] instead of into that player's graveyard" is silently dropped

## Summary

A whole class of counterspells says **"Counter target spell. If that spell is countered this way, put it `<zone>` instead of into that player's graveyard."** The redirect clause is **silently swallowed**: the spell is countered but still goes to the graveyard (the CR default), so the intended destination — top of library, bottom of library, or the owner's hand — never happens. These cards are marked "supported" by coverage yet behave incorrectly (a silently-wrong card).

`Effect::Counter` (crates/engine/src/types/ability.rs ~7354) carries only `target` and `source_rider` (a rider for countered *abilities'* source permanents). It has **no field for the countered spell's destination zone**, so the parser drops the redirect.

## The card class (build for the class, not the card)

Verified silently-wrong on current `main` (the redirect clause is a `warning:swallowed-clause`):

- **Memory Lapse** — "...put it **on top of its owner's library** instead of into that player's graveyard." (Modern/Pauper staple)
- **Lapse of Certainty** — same (top of owner's library).
- **Remand** — "...put it **into its owner's hand** instead of into that player's graveyard. Draw a card." (Modern/Pauper staple)
- **Spell Crumple** — "...put it on the **bottom of its owner's library** instead..."
- **Hinder** — "...put that card on **your choice of the top or bottom** of its owner's library instead..." (adds a controller choice)
- **Transcendent Dragon** — "...**exile it** instead of putting it into its owner's graveyard, then you may cast it..." (adds a cast-from-exile rider)

The common, deterministic shape (top-of-library / bottom-of-library / hand) covers Memory Lapse, Lapse of Certainty, Remand, Spell Crumple. Hinder's top-or-bottom *choice* and Transcendent Dragon's exile-then-may-cast rider are the more complex tail.

## Root cause (current `main`)

Parsing e.g. Memory Lapse produces an `Effect::Counter { target, source_rider: None }` and the trailing "If that spell is countered this way, put it on top of its owner's library instead of into that player's graveyard." sentence is dropped (no destination to carry it). At resolution the countered spell follows the default — into the graveyard — so the card is wrong in play.

## Fix (sketch; final shape via the engine-implementer plan)

1. **Parameterize `Effect::Counter`** with an optional countered-spell destination (a typed zone+position, e.g. `Option<CounteredSpellZone>` covering `LibraryTop`, `LibraryBottom`, `Hand`, and `Exile`). No new sibling effect variant — extend the existing one (the `add-engine-variant` parameterize-don't-proliferate rule).
2. **Parser**: recognize the "If that spell is countered this way, put it `<zone>` instead of into that player's graveyard" rider and populate the new field. Reuse the ex…

problems.title: feat(engine): implement Stickers and sticker sheets (CR 123)
problems.issue_body:
## Motivation
Stickers are a fully-specified, CR-supported mechanic (Comprehensive Rules section 123). The engine currently handles only the *Ticket* player counter related to Unfinity; the actual sticker subsystem — sticker sheets, the four sticker kinds, and putting stickers on objects — is entirely missing.


## CR grounding (verified in `docs/MagicCompRules.txt`, section 123)
- **CR 123.1** — four kinds of stickers: name, ability, power/toughness, art.
- **CR 123.2** — sticker sheets (predetermined combinations on inserts).
- **CR 123.3** — putting a sticker: choose an unused sticker from accessible sheets and put it on the object.
- **CR 123.5** — stickers are retained into public zones (exception to 400.7);  not retained into hidden zones.
- **CR 123.6 / 123.7 / 123.8** — name sticker = text-changing effect; ability sticker = grants ability; P/T sticker = sets power/toughness (timestamp order, CR 613.4b / 613.7).
- Art stickers (CR 123.9) are cosmetic — out of scope for a rules engine.

## Scope
- Sticker-sheet data model (the 3 chosen sheets per player, each with its predetermined stickers).
- Object-side sticker tracking (a sticker is not a counter or token — CR 123.1).
- Three effect capabilities: put a **name** sticker, put an **ability** sticker, put a **power/toughness** sticker.
- Continuous-effect application via the existing layers system (text-change, ability-grant, P/T-set).

## Proposed approach (substantial, two-file)
1. New module `crates/engine/src/game/stickers.rs` — sticker sheet state, the  `Sticker` enum (`Name(String)` / `Ability(AbilityDef)` / `PowerToughness(i32,i32)`),  "choose an unused sticker" selection, and object sticker tracking.
2. New effect handler(s) for "put a [kind] sticker on [target]" — a new  `Effect::PutSticker { kind, target }` in `types/ability.rs`, resolved against the layer system (reuses existing text-change / ability-grant / P/T statics).
3. Sticker-sheet data seeded from MTGJSON/Scryfall sticker-sheet ids.
4. Tests in a separate `stickers_tests.rs` declared from the parent module.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Name/ability/P/T stickers modify object characteristics per CR 123.6–123.8.
- [ ] Stickers persist into public zones (CR 123.5) and are dropped in hidden zones.
- [ ] At least the ~31 put-sticker gap cards parse and resolve.


## Notes
- Art stickers (CR 123.9) are cosmetic — out of scope for a rules engine.
- `score_pr.py` harness is missing — Potential is an estimate from the validated
  table.

problems.title: Graveyard-scope Chroma 'number of <color> mana symbols in mana costs of cards in your graveyard' unparsed (Umbra Stalker
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The graveyard-scope **Chroma** quantity â€” "the number of \<color\> mana symbols in the mana costs of cards in your graveyard" â€” drops to `Unimplemented`. This is the graveyard-population sibling of devotion: devotion (CR 700.5) counts colored mana symbols among **permanents you control**, while this counts the same symbols among **cards in your graveyard**.

Affected card (Scryfall-verified):

- **Umbra Stalker** â€” "Chroma â€” Umbra Stalker's power and toughness are each equal to **the number of black mana symbols in the mana costs of cards in your graveyard**." (P/T CDA)

## Current parse

The quantity parser maps the permanents-population Chroma to `QuantityRef::Devotion` (recently added), but there is no quantity for the graveyard population, so Umbra Stalker's P/T CDA drops to `Unimplemented`. Devotion can't be reused directly â€” CR 700.5 defines it over permanents you control only, a different population than the graveyard.

## Proposed

Add a `QuantityRef::GraveyardChroma { color, player }` variant â€” the graveyard sibling of `Devotion`, kept distinct for that categorical boundary and parameterized by `player` (whose graveyard) so it is not card-specific. Resolution mirrors `count_devotion` but iterates the scoped player's graveyard cards' mana costs (hybrid symbols count toward each color, CR 700.5). Parser: "the number of \<color\> mana symbols in the mana costs of cards in your graveyard" â†’ `GraveyardChroma { color, player: Controller }`.

## Notes / scope

- Reuses the devotion symbol-counting idiom (`ManaCostShard::contributes_to`) and the per-player scalar resolver; new variant registered at all exhaustive `QuantityRef` match sites (resolver, the two leaf classifiers, entered-object perturbation, coverage describe + handled table).
- Permanents-population Chroma remains mapped to `Devotion`; single-object Chroma ("â€¦ in the sacrificed creature's mana cost", Fiery Bombardment) is a different shape and out of scope.
- CR 700.5 (devotion / colored mana symbol counting).

problems.title: feat(engine): Alchemy 'perpetually' keyword action — perpetual base power/toughness (High Fae Prankster)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The Alchemy **perpetually** keyword action is unimplemented across ~46 cards. "Perpetually" applies a modification to a card that **persists for the rest of the game and follows the card across all zones** (it permanently edits the card object, unlike until-end-of-turn or while-on-battlefield continuous effects). There is currently no engine support (only a `gap_analysis.rs` entry).

This issue tracks the first increment: **perpetual base power/toughness setting** â€” "[object] perpetually become(s)/has base power and toughness N/N".

Affected cards in this increment (Scryfall-verified):

- **High Fae Prankster** â€” "High Fae Prankster perpetually has base power and toughness 4/1."
- **Three Tree Battalion** â€” "The duplicate perpetually has base power and toughness 1/1."
- **Blood Age Muster** â€” "Its base power and toughness perpetually become 2/2."

## Design

Mirrors the existing Alchemy `intensity` model: `GameObject.intensity: u32` already persists across hand/library/stack/battlefield and serializes. The base P/T fields (`GameObject.base_power`/`base_toughness: Option<i32>`) are the persistent baseline the layer pass copies into live P/T each recalc, so a perpetual edit to them survives recalcs and zone changes â€” the correct "permanent card edit" semantics.

- `GameObject.perpetual_mods: Vec<PerpetualModification>` â€” the record of perpetual edits applied to this card (persists + serializes; basis for reapplication after copy).
- `enum PerpetualModification { SetBasePowerToughness { power, toughness } }` (extensible to ModifyPT / GrantAbility / Become in follow-ups).
- `Effect::ApplyPerpetual { target, modification }` + resolver: records the modification and applies it (sets `base_power`/`base_toughness`).
- Parser: "perpetually become(s)/has base power and toughness {p}/{t}" â†’ `Effect::ApplyPerpetual`.

## Scope

Increment 1 = base-P/T set only. Follow-ups: "perpetually gets +N/+N" (ModifyPT), "perpetually gain(s) [ability]" (the all-zones granted-ability form, the largest group), "perpetually become(s) [type]". No CR entry (digital-only Alchemy), consistent with the existing `Effect::Intensify` / `Effect::Conjure` treatment.

problems.title: Parser: "pay any amount of life" dropped to Unimplemented (Necrodominance, Plunge into Darkness)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

"Pay any amount of life" is dropped to `Effect::Unimplemented`, so the entire effect does nothing.

Affected real cards:
- **Necrodominance** — "At the beginning of your end step, you may pay any amount of life. If you do, draw that many cards." (draws nothing)
- **Plunge into Darkness** (mode) — "Pay any amount of life, then look at that many cards from the top of your library..." (looks at nothing)
- **Vizkopa Confessor** — ETB "pay any amount of life" (pay clause dropped)

## Current (wrong) parse

The clause lowers to `Effect::Unimplemented { name: "pay", description: "pay any amount of life" }`, taking the downstream "that many" effect with it.

## Root cause

The engine already implements the interactive "pay any amount" subsystem (`WaitingFor::PayAmountChoice` → `SubmitPayAmount` → `last_effect_count` → `QuantityRef::EventContextAmount`) for **Energy** and **generic mana** (`PayableResource::Energy` / `ManaGeneric`), but there is no `PayableResource::Life` — so "pay any amount of life" has no interactive path and falls through to `Unimplemented`.

## Expected

An interactive "pay any amount of life" payment: prompt for an amount (0..current life, clamped to 0 under a CantLoseLife lock), deduct it as life loss (CR 119.4), and bind the paid amount as the downstream "that many" quantity — so Necrodominance pays N and draws N, Plunge pays N and looks at N.

## Notes

The "As ~ enters, pay any amount of life" CDA cards (Phyrexian Processor, Minion of the Wastes, Nameless Race) are a separate as-enters/replacement seam, and Plague of Vermin's multi-player repeat loop is out of scope for this issue. CR 119.4 / 118.3 / 119.8 / 107.1c.

problems.title: Parser: "the next time you would draw a card this turn, [effect] instead" dropped to Unimplemented (Words of Worship, Wo
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The Odyssey "Words of" cards drop their entire activated ability to `Effect::Unimplemented`, so activating them does nothing.

- **Words of Worship** — `{1}: The next time you would draw a card this turn, you gain 5 life instead.`
- **Words of Wilding** — `{1}: The next time you would draw a card this turn, create a 2/2 green Bear creature token instead.`
- **Words of Wind** — `{1}: ... each player returns a permanent they control to its owner's hand instead.`
- **Words of Waste** — `{1}: ... each opponent discards a card instead.`

## Current (wrong) parse

The whole clause lowers to `Effect::Unimplemented { name: "the", description: "the next time you would draw a card this turn, ... instead" }` — the activated ability is a no-op.

## Root cause

The engine already *replaces* the draw event (Jace, the Mind Sculptor's "you win the game instead", Abundance) via `ReplacementDefinition` + the post-replacement continuation. But there is no resolution-time effect to **install** a one-shot, this-turn draw replacement that carries an arbitrary substitute effect — so "the next time you would draw a card this turn, [effect] instead" has no home and falls through to `Unimplemented`.

## Expected

Activating the ability installs a one-shot replacement: the controller's next draw this turn is replaced — the card is not drawn, and the substitute effect happens instead (Worship → gain 5 life; Wilding → create a 2/2 Bear). The replacement is consumed on use (a later draw the same turn is normal) and expires at end of turn if unused (CR 614.6 / 514.2).

## Notes

Words of Wind ("each player returns a permanent") and Words of Waste ("each opponent discards") use player-scoped payloads that the current effect parser mis-scopes to the controller, so they should remain honest gaps until that subject-scoping is handled. Aladdin's Lamp / Mangara's Tome use bespoke library payloads and are out of scope. CR 614.1a / 614.6 / 514.2 / 121.1.

problems.title: feat(engine): implement Augment casting and host-combine runtime semantics
problems.issue_body:
# Current state

The codebase already recognizes **Augment** as a keyword for card metadata and filtering, but it does **not** implement the actual gameplay mechanic.

What exists now:
- `Keyword::Augment` / `KeywordKind::Augment`
- parsing for `"augment"` in keyword/filter contexts
- support for queries like `"card with augment"`

What is still missing:
- casting an augment half for its augment cost
- targeting a legal host
- combining the augment half with that host at runtime
- support for host/combine effects that depend on the same mechanic

In current card data, augment cards still compile to `Unimplemented` spell effects for their `Augment {cost}` text.

# Motivation

Augment is still an engine gap for the Unstable host/augment card set.

There are **14 augment-half cards** in current data, and they are not playable using their augment mechanic. In addition, some support cards and effects refer to:
- cards with augment
- hosts
- combining with a host

So this is not only a parser gap. It is a missing runtime mechanic.

# Scope

Implement the **runtime** Augment mechanic, reusing existing merge infrastructure where appropriate.

Required behavior:
- parse and represent the augment cost as a real cast path, not an `Unimplemented` effect
- allow an augment half to be cast from hand for its augment cost
- require a legal host target
- combine the augment half with that host into a merged permanent
- apply merged characteristics per the Unstable host/augment rules
- support cards that instruct a player to combine a card with augment with a host outside the normal cast-for-augment flow

# Proposed approach

1. Reuse the existing merge/mutate infrastructure as the starting point for the merged-permanent representation.
2. Add Augment-specific cast handling:
   - alternative cast path
   - legality checks for host targeting
   - resolution path that combines onto the host
3. Add host/combine runtime support for non-cast effects that refer to cards with augment.
4. Add focused engine tests in a dedicated `augment_tests.rs`.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 14 augment-half cards can be cast for their augment cost.
- [ ] Casting for augment requires and targets a legal host.
- [ ] Resolution combines the augment half with the host into one merged permanent.
- [ ] The resulting permanent has the correct merged power/toughness, abilities, and combined characteristics per Unstable rules.
- [ ] Support cards/effects that refer to “card with augment” + “combine it with a host” function correctly.
- [ ] `cargo parser-gaps` no longer reports Augment as `F_new_mechanic`.

# Notes

- Do **not** frame this as “add the Augment keyword”; keyword recognition already exists.
- The real missing work is **runtime casting + host-combine semantics**.
- This is a legitimate feature request, but it is still a **low-to-medium priority** engine item because it mainly serves Un-set cards rather than mainstream format coverage.

problems.title: feat(engine): implement Contraption deck runtime and the Assemble action
problems.issue_body:
## Current state

The codebase has **partial Contraption scaffolding**, but not a working Contraption subsystem.

What already exists:
- `Contraption` is a recognized card type/subtype
- `Whenever you crank this Contraption` parses into `TriggerMode::CrankContraption`
- `ReplacementEvent::AssembleContraption` exists as a type-level enum case

What is still missing:
- no per-player Contraption deck model
- no sprocket / crank state tracking
- no runtime `Assemble` effect
- no event path that actually fires Contraption crank triggers
- many Contraption / assemble cards still export as `Unimplemented` or depend on unimplemented trigger/runtime paths

This is therefore **not** a parser-only issue. It is a missing gameplay subsystem.

## Motivation

Contraptions from **Unstable** are still not functionally supported.

Current card-data review shows:
- many cards still reference `assemble` / `Contraption`
- many of those still serialize with `Unimplemented` effects or rely on the unimplemented `CrankContraption` runtime path

Representative broken cards include:
- `Aerial Toastmaster`
- `Crafty Octopus`
- `First Pick`
- `Incite Insight`
- `Joyride Rigger`
- multiple Contraptions with `Whenever you crank this Contraption`

So while the parser can recognize some of the vocabulary, the engine still cannot actually support Contraption gameplay.

## Rules grounding

The bundled [docs/MagicCompRules.txt](docs/MagicCompRules.txt) includes the Assemble entry:

- **CR 701.45a**: Assemble is a keyword action in the Unstable set that puts Contraptions onto the battlefield.

However, the bundled rules also explicitly say Unstable cards/mechanics are otherwise not included there, so the implementation details for:
- Contraption deck handling
- sprockets
- crank progression
- firing Contraptions on the active sprocket

must be implemented from the **Unstable FAQ / Oracle behavior**, not inferred from the main CR file alone.

## Scope

Implement the missing Contraption runtime subsystem in the engine.

Required behavior:
- add a per-player Contraption supplementary deck model
- support assembling the top Contraption from that deck onto the battlefield
- assign assembled Contraptions to one of the three sprockets
- track sprocket/crank progression across turns
- fire Contraption abilities when their sprocket is cranked
- wire `assemble a Contraption` / `assemble N Contraptions` card text into real runtime effects
- make `Whenever you crank this Contraption` triggers actually functional

## Proposed approach

1. Add a dedicated Contraption runtime module, for example:
   - `crates/engine/src/game/contraptions.rs`
2. Follow the existing **Attractions** architecture as the closest local pattern:
   - per-player supplementary deck storage
   - object membership bookkeeping
   - explicit runtime events/effects
3. Add new engine effect wiring for:
   - `AssembleContraption`
   - crank/sprocket progression
4. Add explicit game events for Contraption assembly / cranking as ne…

problems.title: Import Deck silently fails when pasted content contains no valid cards
problems.issue_body: ### Summary The **Import Deck** flow provides no feedback when users paste text that does not contain any recognizable cards. Clicking **Parse** appears to succeed, but no cards are imported and the dialog closes without explanation. This creates a confusing user experience because it appears as though the Parse action did nothing or failed silently. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open **Deck Builder**. 2. Click **Import**. 3. Paste a deck in MTGA or .dck format."** * [ ] Import dialog remains open when parsing fails * [ ] Error message clears after the user edits the input * [ ] Valid deck lists continue to import successfully * [ ] Empty or unparseable imported files display the same validation message * [ ] Consistent validation behavior across all deck import entry points

problems.title: [Card Bug] Archon of Valor's Reach: "can't cast spells of the chosen type" never fires (Labeled vs CardType choice misma
problems.issue_body:
### Card(s)

Archon of Valor's Reach

### Actual behavior

The static "Players can't cast spells of the chosen type" never prevents any spell. The chosen card type is selected on ETB but the prohibition has no effect.

### Root cause (engine-authoritative parse, `card-data.json`)

Archon chooses from a **non-canonical subset** of card types:

> As ~ enters, choose artifact, enchantment, instant, sorcery, or planeswalker.
> Players can't cast spells of the chosen type.

Because the option list (`artifact/enchantment/instant/sorcery/planeswalker`) is **not** the full canonical card-type set, the parser routes it to `ChoiceType::Labeled { options: [...] }` rather than `ChoiceType::CardType`:

```json
"effect": { "type": "Choose",
  "choice_type": { "Labeled": { "options": ["Artifact","Enchantment","Instant","Sorcery","Planeswalker."] } },
  "persist": true }
```

At resolution, `ChosenAttribute::from_choice` maps a `Labeled` choice to `ChosenAttribute::Label(value)` — a string label — **not** `ChosenAttribute::CardType` (`crates/engine/src/types/ability.rs`, `from_choice`).

But the `CantBeCast` static carries `FilterProp::IsChosenCardType`:

```json
"CantBeCast": { "who": "AllPlayers" },
"affected": { "type": "Typed", "properties": [ { "type": "IsChosenCardType" } ] }
```

`IsChosenCardType` only reads `ChosenAttribute::CardType` (`crates/engine/src/game/filter.rs:2106`, `crates/engine/src/game/casting.rs:12245`). Archon stored a `Label`, so the filter returns `false` for every spell and the prohibition never applies.

This is distinct from #1654 (a creature-type-vs-card-type mismatch in cost reducers). Here it is a **Labeled-vs-CardType** mismatch: a restricted card-type enumeration is parsed as an anchor-word label instead of a card-type choice.

### Secondary parse artifact

The last option is captured as `"Planeswalker."` — the sentence-ending period is included in the option string.

### Suggested fix direction

A "choose [one of these card types]" enumeration that lists a *subset* of the canonical card types (Archon, and the broader class of "choose a card type from X, Y, or Z" cards) should resolve to a card-type choice that stores `ChosenAttribute::CardType`, so the linked `IsChosenCardType` prohibition resolves correctly — rather than `ChoiceType::Labeled`/`ChosenAttribute::Label`. CR 205.2a (card types) + CR 607.2d (linked abilities). Also strip the trailing period from the final enumerated option.

(Found during review of #1654 / PR #4197; analysis only — no code change yet.)

problems.title: Replace native folder name prompt with styled dialog on My Decks
problems.issue_body: ## Problem Creating or renaming a deck folder on **My Decks** currently uses the browser's native `window.prompt()`, which does not match the application's design system. This creates an inconsistent user experience compared to the rest of the app, which uses custom-styled dialogs, dark theme panels, cyan accent buttons, and standardized form controls. The native prompt appears when: * Clicking **New folder** from the My Decks toolbar * Selecting **New folder…** from a deck's actions menu * Renaming an existing folder from folder options ## Proposed Solution Create a reusable `TextPromptDialog` component that follows the styling and interaction patterns used by existing dialogs (e.g. `JoinErrorDialog`, `ImportDeckModal`) and replace all folder-related `prompt()` usages in `MyDecks.tsx`. The dialog should: * Match the application's dark theme and modal styling * Use existing button styles (`menuButtonClass` / primary action styling) * Provide inline validation instead of relying on browser prompts * Support keyboard shortcuts and accessibility expectations ## Scope ### UI Component * Add `TextPromptDialog` under: * `client/src/components/ui/` ### My Decks Integration Replace existing `prompt()` calls for: * Create folder (toolbar action) * Create folder and assign deck (deck actions menu) * Rename folder ### Validation & UX * Respect `MAX_FOLDER_NAME_LENGTH` * Auto-focus the input when the dialog opens * Submit on **Enter** * Cancel on **Escape** * Prevent submission of empty or whitespace-only names * Disable/guard confirm action when validation fails ### Localization * Add `folder.createButton` translation key across all supported locales ### Testing * Add unit tests covering: * Initial focus behavior * Enter to confirm * Escape to cancel * Validation of empty/whitespace input * Max length enforcement * Callback execution on confirm ## Out of Scope * Styling changes to existing **New folder**, **Collapse all**, or **Expand all** toolbar buttons * Replacing native `confirm()` used for folder deletion (can be addressed in a separate follow-up issue) ## Acceptance Criteria * No native browser prompt appears during folder creation or rename flows * Dialog matches existing application modal styling * Dark panel * Bordered text input * Cyan primary action button * Empty or whitespace-only folder names cannot be submitted * `MAX_FOLDER_NAME_LENGTH` is enforced * Enter/Escape keyboard shortcuts work as expected * Existing folder toolbar behavior remains unchanged * Existing collapse/expand functionality remains unchanged ## Screenshots

problems.title: [Card Bug] Visions of Ruin — flashback commander MV cost reduction dropped
problems.issue_body:

Visions of Ruin

Each opponent sacrifices an artifact. For each artifact sacrificed this way, you create a Treasure token.

problems.title: Drag to the Underworld devotion cost reduction not bound
problems.issue_body:
## Card

Drag to the Underworld

This spell costs {X} less to cast, where X is your devotion to black.

## Problem

problems.title: fix(parser): Bound by Moonsilver sacrifice-another attach activated
problems.issue_body:
## Card

Bound by Moonsilver

## Oracle

Enchant creature
Enchanted creature can't attack, block, or transform.
Sacrifice another permanent: Attach this Aura to target creature. Activate only as a sorcery and only once each turn.

## Problem

Cluster 34 misparse:

1. Sacrifice cost `another permanent` must carry `FilterProp::Another` (exclude the Aura source).
2. Activated `{cost}: Attach this Aura to target creature` must lower to `Effect::Attach` with `AsSorcery` + `OnlyOnceEachTurn` activation restrictions.
3. Compound enchanted-host static `can't attack, block, or transform` must bind to `EnchantedBy`, not fall through to SelfRef on the Aura.

## Expected

- One activated ability: `Sacrifice(Another permanent)` → `Attach(SelfRef → creature target)` with sorcery-speed + once-per-turn limits.
- Three enchanted-host statics: `CantAttack`, `CantBlock`, `CantTransform` on `FilterProp::EnchantedBy`.

## Fix

- `ensure_another_sacrifice_filter` in `oracle_cost.rs` for sacrifice costs.
- `parse_restriction_modes` dispatch in `parse_enchanted_equipped_predicate` for restriction-only Aura predicates.
- Parser + integration regression tests.

problems.title: feat(engine): perpetual type-change (Alchemy 'perpetually becomes a [type] with base P/T and gains [kw]') — Second Littl
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Follow-up to the Alchemy **perpetually** mechanic (`Effect::ApplyPerpetual` / `PerpetualModification`, added in #4104). This adds the **perpetual type-change** form:

> "[~] perpetually becomes a \<subtypes\> creature with base power and toughness N/N and gains \<keyword\>"

Card fixed (Scryfall-verified):

- **Second Little Pig** â€” "{2}{W/B}{W/B}: Second Little Pig perpetually becomes a Boar Spirit with base power and toughness 4/4 and gains flying."

## Design

Reuses the merged `perpetual_mods` / base-edit pattern (no new layer machinery). Adds `PerpetualModification::Become { creature_subtypes, power, toughness, keywords }`:

- **Resolver** (`apply_perpetual_modification`): replaces the card's **creature** subtypes (keeping any non-creature subtypes, identified via `state.all_creature_types`, CR 613.4), ensures it is a creature, sets base power/toughness, and grants the keywords â€” all on the persistent `base_*` fields, then `mark_layers_full` so live/public characteristics recompute at the next flush.
- **Parser** (`try_parse_perpetual_become`, tried before the bare base-P/T form): self-subjects only (no anaphoric "it"/"the duplicate"). The clause tail must be fully consumed, so compound riders that aren't modeled (e.g. Heir to Dragonfire's "gets +3/+3") fall through to `Unimplemented` rather than being silently dropped.

## Verification

- Parser unit test: the Second Little Pig phrasing â†’ `Become { [Boar, Spirit], 4/4, [Flying] }`; Heir to Dragonfire's "becomes a Dragon, gets +3/+3" does **not** parse as `Become`.
- Resolver runtime regression: after resolution + `flush_layers`, the live `card_types.subtypes` (Boar/Spirit, not Pig), `power`/`toughness` (4/4), and `keywords` (flying) reflect the change â€” not just the base fields.
- `cargo fmt`, the parser-combinator gate, and `clippy -D warnings` (engine + phase-ai) green.

## Scope

Self-subject "becomes a \<subtypes\> with base P/T N/N [and gains \<kw\>]" only. Deferred to follow-ups: the "gets +N/+N" perpetual P/T modifier (Heir to Dragonfire, Jaheira â€” needs P/T-modifier layer integration), referenced-object subjects ("the duplicate"/"its"), and the all-zones "perpetually gains [ability]" forms.

CR 613.4 (type-changing), CR 205.1b (subtypes).

problems.title: Add action-based game replay system (record, export, and scrub through past games)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Add a deterministic, action-based replay system: every local/AI game can be exported as a compact replay file (initial setup + the ordered sequence of submitted actions), and a new Replay Viewer can load that file, scrub through any point in the game, and step/play through it on the existing board UI in read-only mode.

## Motivation

- **Bug reports**: a player hitting a suspected engine bug can export the replay and attach it to an issue, letting maintainers reproduce the exact game deterministically instead of guessing from a description.
- **Sharing/highlights**: players can save and re-watch interesting games (a clutch top-deck, a big combo turn) without re-recording video.
- **Engine regression testing**: recorded replays from real games are a free source of regression fixtures — a replay that desyncs after an engine change is a real bug, not a synthetic test.

`GameLogEntry` (`crates/engine/src/types/log.rs`) already gives a human-readable text log, but it's display-only and not replayable. There's no way today to reconstruct or scrub through a past game.

## Design

The engine is already deterministic given a fixed RNG seed (`GameState::rng_seed` + `ChaCha20Rng`) and a fixed sequence of submitted `GameAction`s — `apply(state, actor, action)` is a pure reducer. This means a full game can be reconstructed from just:

1. A **header**: format/match config, player count, first player, RNG seed, and the resolved deck list (the same inputs `initialize_game` already takes).
2. The **ordered list of `(actor, GameAction)` pairs** that were actually submitted and accepted.

No per-turn state snapshots are required for correctness — only for fast scrubbing (see below).

### Engine (`crates/engine`)
- `types/replay.rs`: `ReplayHeader`, `RecordedAction`, `ReplayLog` (serde types).

problems.issue_body:
## Reported behavior

When Grenzo, Havoc Raiser's trigger fires after combat damage, both modes (Goad and Exile top card) affect the player who dealt the damage (Grenzo's controller) rather than the player who received the combat damage.

## Oracle text (verified from card-data.json)

```
Whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player, choose one —
• Goad target creature that player controls.
• Exile the top card of that player's library. Until end of turn, you may cast that card and you may spend mana as though it were mana of any color to cast that spell.
```

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected**: 'That player' refers to the player who received combat damage (the opponent). Goad targets a creature the damaged player controls; ExileTop exiles from the damaged player's library.
- **Actual**: The Goad mode targets a creature the controller (Grenzo's owner) controls (`controller: You` in parsed data). ExileTop targets `ParentTarget` which resolves to the controller's library.

Confirmed in card-data.json: `mode_abilities[0].effect.target.controller == "You"` (should be opponent/damaged player). The trigger mode is `DamageDone` and 'that player' should be bound to the event's damaged player, not the source's controller.

problems.title: [Card Bug] High Tide does not add additional blue mana from Islands
problems.issue_body:
## Card(s)

High Tide

## Build/version

Unknown

## Game mode

Unknown

## Actual behavior

After casting High Tide, Islands tapped for mana still produce only one blue mana.

## Expected behavior

After High Tide resolves, until end of turn, whenever any player taps an Island for mana, that player should add an additional `{U}`. An Island that normally produces `{U}` should effectively produce two blue mana for that tap.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Control an untapped Island.
2. Cast and resolve High Tide.
3. Tap the Island for mana before end of turn.
4. Observe the mana pool.

Actual: the mana pool increases by one blue mana.

Expected: the mana pool increases by two blue mana total: the Island's normal `{U}` plus High Tide's additional `{U}`.

## Oracle text verified from coverage data

> Until end of turn, whenever a player taps an Island for mana, that player adds an additional {U}.

## Classifier analysis

**Verdict**: `supported_aspect_defect`

**Matched clause**: `Until end of turn, whenever a player taps an Island for mana, that player adds an additional {U}.` (supported: true)

**Reasoning**: Live coverage marks High Tide as supported and parses the clause as `CreateDelayedTrigger` with `when = whenever event this turn` and `duration = until end of turn`. The AST claims to represent the delayed trigger, but runtime mana production still only applies the Island's base mana ability. This is therefore an actionable supported-aspect defect, likely in the runtime path for delayed triggers that watch mana taps / additional mana production.

problems.title: fix(parser): harden trailing if-gate combinator on static restrictions (as-if safe)
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

PR #4841 added `split_trailing_gate_condition` so trailing `if <condition>` gates work on `can't play lands` statics (Rock Jockey). The helper still uses `take_until(" if ")`, which anchors on the **first** ` if ` in the line. That mis-splits oracle text containing **as if** (e.g. permission riders like "cast as if it had flash if you control a Swamp") and would attach the wrong condition or drop the real trailing gate when this building block is reused on other restriction classes.

## Proposed fix

- Promote `split_trailing_gate_condition` to `oracle_static/shared.rs` as the shared trailing-gate building block (parity with `parse_if_static_condition` / `extract_cant_untap_condition`).
- Match the **last** valid trailing ` if ` (skip `as if` false positives) before falling back to `as long as`.
- Add regression coverage for an `as if` + trailing `if` line on `can't play lands`, and extend the full Rock Jockey oracle dispatch test to assert the gated `CantPlayLand` static on card-name-normalized text.

## CR

CR 611.3a (conditional statics) + CR 305.1 (land plays).

## Class

Parser building-block hardening in the same family as Rock Jockey / Wirecat trailing-gate fixes.

problems.title: fix(parser): parse parenthetical gate on cant-cast prohibitions (Alhammarret)
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Casting prohibitions like Alhammarret, High Arbiter:

> Your opponents can't cast spells with the chosen name **(as long as this creature is on the battlefield).**

`parse_cant_cast_type_spells` in `restriction.rs` currently **strips** trailing parenthetical riders via `rfind(" (")` instead of parsing them as `StaticCondition` gates. The prohibition is therefore enforced **unconditionally** — opponents cannot cast spells with the chosen name even after Alhammarret leaves the battlefield.

This is the same class of bug fixed for Rock Jockey in #4841 (trailing `if` / `as long as` gate swallowed → unconditional restriction), but on the **parenthetical** gate form used by cant-cast statics.

## Proposed fix

- Add a composable `split_parenthetical_gate_condition` helper (sibling of `split_trailing_gate_condition`) that accepts `(as long as <condition>)` and `(if <condition>)`.
- In `parse_cant_cast_type_spells`, peel the parenthetical gate **before** pattern dispatch; attach via `parse_static_condition`. If a parenthetical gate is present but its condition is unrecognized, leave the line unsupported (`None`) rather than enforcing unconditionally — parity with Limited Resources / Rock Jockey guards.
- Regression test on Alhammarret full Oracle text asserting `CantBeCast` + `SourceInZone { Battlefield }` gate.

## CR

CR 101.2 (who can cast) + CR 611.3a (conditional statics) + CR 113.6b (source zone).

## Related

- #4841 — trailing `if` gate on `CantPlayLand` (Rock Jockey)

problems.title: feat(parser+engine): continuous filter-scoped keyword-cost grants (Scavenge/Encore/Flashback/Embalm/Foretell) don't supp
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The engine already has the building blocks for granting a keyword ability whose cost is the recipient's own mana cost — `ManaCost::SelfManaCost` plus `ContinuousModification::AddKeyword` — used today for one-shot single-target grants like Snapcaster Mage's flashback trigger. It also has a *continuous, filter-scoped* variant of that same grant for a handful of graveyard keywords (`GraveyardGrantedKeywordKind` in `parser/oracle_static/keyword_grant.rs` + `oracle.rs`'s `parse_graveyard_keyword_continuation`), covering Flashback/Escape/Mayhem/Scavenge/Encore.

That continuous-grant class stops short of real, tournament-legal cards in three ways:

1. **No cost-delta support.** `ManaCost::SelfManaCost` only represents "equal to its mana cost" — there's no way to express "equal to its mana cost **reduced by {2}**", which several real cards need.
2. **Graveyard-only.** The combinator hard-requires the affected filter to be the controller's graveyard (`target_filter_is_your_graveyard`). Hand-zone grants (Foretell) aren't recognized at all.
3. **Missing keywords.** Embalm isn't in `GraveyardGrantedKeywordKind` even though the runtime resolver (`resolve_self_cost_graveyard_activated_keyword`) already handles it.

There's also a latent runtime gap: `foretell_cost`/`can_foretell_card` (`game/casting.rs`) read `obj.keywords` directly instead of going through the off-zone-aware `effective_off_zone_keyword` path that graveyard keywords already use — so even a correctly-parsed continuous Foretell grant on a hand card would silently never be castable.

## Real cards affected (verified against `data/mtgjson/AtomicCards.json`)

| Card | Legality | Zone | Keyword | Cost formula |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Varolz, the Scar-Striped | Commander/Legacy/Modern/Pioneer/Vintage | Graveyard | Scavenge | mana cost |
| Young Deathclaws | Commander/Legacy/Vintage | Graveyard | Scavenge | mana cost |
| Wire Surgeons | Commander/Legacy/Vintage | Graveyard | Encore | mana cost |
| Return the Past | Commander/Legacy/Vintage | Graveyard | Flashback | mana cost (during your turn only) |
| Bohn, Beguiling Balladeer | Commander/Legacy/Vintage | Hand | Foretell | mana cost **reduced by {2}** |
| Dream Devourer | Modern/Pioneer/Commander/Standard-legal formats | Hand | Foretell | mana cost **reduced by {2}** |
| Naktamun (Plane) | Planechase | Graveyard | Embalm | mana cost |
| The Cave of Skulls (Plane) | Planechase | Graveyard | Scavenge | mana cost |
| Singing Towers of Darillium (Plane) | Planechase | Hand | Foretell | mana cost reduced by {2} |

Varolz and Dream Devourer are real constructed/Commander staples — this isn't an edge-case cluster.

## Proposed fix (building-block, not per-card)

- Add `ManaCost::SelfManaCostAdjusted { delta: i32 }` alongside the existing `SelfManaCost`/`SelfManaValue` markers (CR 601.2f: generic mana adjusted, floored at `{0}`), resolved at the single existing choke point `resolve_keyword_mana_cost` (`game/keywords.rs`).
- Extend `GraveyardGra…

problems.title: fix(parser): "unless they're mana abilities" exemption dropped for U+2019 apostrophe, wrongly blocking mana abilities (P
problems.issue_body:
### Summary

The CR 605.1a mana-ability exemption suffix **"unless they're mana abilities"** is parsed with the straight ASCII apostrophe only. Since MTGJSON oracle text uses the typographic apostrophe (U+2019), a permanent whose text carries the U+2019 form silently loses the exemption: the static is built with `ActivationExemption::None`, and the runtime then **wrongly blocks the permanent's mana abilities** — a rules violation, not just a coverage miss.

### Affected cards (a class)

Every card templated `…activated abilities can't be activated unless they're mana abilities.` with the U+2019 apostrophe, e.g.:

- **Pithing Needle** — `Activated abilities of sources with the chosen name can't be activated unless they're mana abilities.`
- **Bound by Moonsilver** — `Enchanted permanent can't attack or block, and its activated abilities can't be activated unless they're mana abilities.`
- **Faith's Fetters / Kenrith's Transformation–shaped auras** — `…and its activated abilities can't be activated unless they're mana abilities.`

### Root cause

The asymmetry is internal and self-evident. The **predicate** half of the clause already accepts both apostrophes:

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/shared.rs:693-694` — `alt((tag("activated abilities can't be activated"), tag("activated abilities can\u{2019}t be activated")))`
- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/evasion.rs:1204-1205` — same dual-apostrophe pair.

But the **exemption suffix** half is straight-apostrophe only:

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/restriction.rs:292` — `tag(" unless they're ")`
- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/shared.rs:696` — `opt((tag(" unless they're "), tag("mana abilities")))`

There is no global apostrophe normalization in the pipeline (only `−`/`–` → `-`), which is exactly why the predicate carries dual-apostrophe branches. So a U+2019 printing parses the predicate but drops the suffix.

Trace: `parse_cant_be_activated_exemption_in_text` → `parse_activation_exemption_suffix` tries `tag(" unless they're ")` against ` unless they\u{2019}re mana abilities`, the `tag` fails, `opt` yields `None`, `unwrap_or_default()` returns `ActivationExemption::None`. The runtime gate then blocks mana abilities that CR 605.1a requires to remain activatable.

### Expected behavior (CR 605.1a)

Mana abilities remain activatable under a "can't be activated" static that carves them out with "unless they're mana abilities", regardless of which apostrophe glyph the oracle text uses.

### Proposed fix

Add the U+2019 branch to both exemption-suffix parse sites, mirroring the dual-apostrophe pattern already used for the adjacent predicate:

```rust
alt((tag(" unless they're "), tag(" unless they\u{2019}re ")))
```

Parser-only, no new enum variant, zero blast radius — both sites map to the existing `ActivationExemption::ManaAbilities`.

problems.title: feat(parser): compound-subject replacement animation static (CR 205.1a / CR 611.3)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

PR #5219 added `parse_compound_all_subjects_type_change` for **additive** compound-subject animation statics (`All <X> and all <Y> are … in addition to their other types`, e.g. Life and Limb). Review explicitly gated that handler to additive predicates only; non-additive compounds like `All Elves and all Goblins are 2/2 Zombie creatures` must use **replacement** semantics (CR 205.1a `SetCardTypes` / subtype wipe) instead of falling through silently.

## Proposed approach (mirror #5219 structure)

- Add `parse_compound_all_subjects_type_replacement` sibling in `oracle_static/type_change.rs`
- Reuse `parse_compound_all_subjects_filter` / `parse_compound_subject_conjunct` for `Or` subject distribution (CR 611.3)
- Parse predicate once via `parse_animation_spec` + `animation_modifications_with_replacement(&spec, false)`
- Dispatch immediately after the additive compound handler, before `parse_land_animation`
- Gate: require `creature` in predicate; decline when additive marker present

## CR references

- CR 611.3 — continuous effect applies to every object in the affected set
- CR 205.1a — non-additive type/subtype replacement
- CR 613.4b — base P/T setting (layer 7b)

## Test plan

- [ ] `All Elves and all Goblins are 2/2 Zombie creatures.` parses to one static with `Or(Elf, Goblin)` and replacement mods (SetPower/Toughness, RemoveAllSubtypes, AddSubtype Zombie)
- [ ] Life and Limb additive line still routes through additive handler only
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all`, parser combinator gate, `cargo test -p engine --lib parser::oracle_static`

problems.title: feat(parser): compound-subject land type-change static (CR 611.3 / CR 305.7)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

PR #5219 added compound-subject dispatch for **animation** statics (`All <X> and all <Y> are … creatures …`). The same structural gap exists for **land type-change** statics: `parse_land_type_change` splits on `" are "` and only resolves single-subject land filters, so a compound like `All Mountains and all Forests are Plains` would fall through with no static.

The additive animation handler already documents this predicate class as owned elsewhere (`type_change.rs`); this issue tracks the land-type sibling.

## Proposed approach (mirror #5219 structure)

- Add `parse_compound_all_subjects_land_type_change` in `oracle_static/type_change.rs`
- Reuse `parse_compound_all_subjects_filter` for `Or` subject distribution (CR 611.3)
- Factor shared predicate parsing from `parse_land_type_change` into a helper consumed by both handlers
- Dispatch after compound animation handlers, before `parse_land_animation` / `parse_land_type_change`; gate on absence of `"creature"` in the predicate so animation lines keep routing correctly
- Regression: Life and Limb and single-subject Conversion (`All Mountains are Plains`) unchanged

## CR references

- CR 611.3 — continuous effect applies to every object in the affected set
- CR 305.7 — basic land subtype changes
- CR 205.1b — additive land-type grants (`in addition to their other land types`)

## Test plan

- [ ] `All Mountains and all Forests are Plains.` → one static, `Or` subjects, `SetBasicLandType(Plains)`
- [ ] Additive compound `… are Islands in addition to their other land types` → `AddSubtype`

problems.title: feat(parser): factor animation+additive predicate merge into parse_land_animation (CR 205.1b / CR 613.4b)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

PR #5219 introduced compound-subject land/creature animation (`parse_compound_all_subjects_type_change`) by **merging two existing predicate parsers** — `parse_animation_spec` + `parse_additive_type_clause_modifications` — because neither single-subject sibling is complete for predicates of the form `"<P/T> <type> creatures and <type> lands in addition to their other types"`.

The same predicate-merge gap exists on the **single-subject** land-animation sibling: `parse_land_animation` delegates only to `parse_animation_spec` / `animation_modifications`, so it drops the trailing additive land-type grants when the predicate uses the CR 205.1b `"in addition to their other types"` marker instead of the confirmatory `"that are still lands"` retention tail (Living Plane / Nature's Revolt).

## Proposed approach (mirror #5219 predicate architecture)

- Factor `merge_creature_animation_with_additive_type_modifications` in `oracle_static/type_change.rs` — shared by `parse_compound_all_subjects_type_change` and `parse_land_animation`
- Gate the merge on `has_in_addition_to_other_types` so retention-form lines (`that are still lands`) keep routing through the existing path unchanged
- No new runtime — every modification remains an existing `ContinuousModification`
- Building-block regression: single-subject `"All lands are 1/1 … creatures and Forest lands in addition to their other types"` must emit animation mods **and** `AddType(Land)` / `AddSubtype(Forest)`; Living Plane unchanged

## CR references

- CR 611.3 — continuous effect applies uniformly to the affected set (single-subject here)
- CR 613.4b — layer 7b base P/T from animation spec
- CR 205.1b — additive type/subtype grants via `in addition to their other types`

## Test plan

- [ ] Single-subject additive-reciprocal land animation parses full modification set
- [ ] Living Plane / Nature's Revolt (`that are still lands`) unchanged
- [ ] Compound Life and Limb line unchanged (still owned by compound handler)
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all`, parser combinator gate, `cargo test -p engine --lib parser::oracle_static`

problems.title: feat(parser): Lignify-class enchanted subtype-only type-change with base P/T (CR 205.1a / CR 613.1d)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Auras in the **Lignify class** — `"Enchanted creature is a <creature subtype> with base power and toughness N/N and loses all abilities."` — strict-fail today. `parse_enchanted_is_type` requires at least one **core card type** word in the granted type phrase (`Insect artifact creature`, `blue Frog creature`, …). When the grammar names only a creature subtype before the base-P/T seam (`Treefolk`, `Wall`, …), `granted_core_types` stays empty and the handler returns `None`, so the line falls through to `Unimplemented` even though the runtime already supports every emitted modification (`SetCardTypes`, `RemoveAllSubtypes`, `AddSubtype`, `SetPower`/`SetToughness`, `RemoveAllAbilities`).

**Type specimen:** Lignify — `"Enchanted creature is a Treefolk with base power and toughness 0/4 and loses all abilities."`

Scryfall finds ~13 auras matching `is a` + `with base power and toughness` + `loses all abilities`; the subtype-only shape is the uncovered sibling of the Frogify/Darksteel Mutation family handled by `parse_enchanted_is_type`.

## Proposed approach (mirror #5142 / #4770 structure)

- Add `parse_enchanted_is_creature_subtype_with_base_pt` in `oracle_static/type_change.rs`
- Split on the existing ` with base power and toughness ` seam (same as `parse_enchanted_is_type`), parse leading creature subtype(s) via `parse_subtype`, **decline** if a core-type word appears (so `Insect artifact creature` stays on the general handler)
- Compose existing Layer-4/6/7b modifications in written order: optional leading `RemoveAllAbilities`, `SetCardTypes { Creature }` (CR 205.1a replacement), `RemoveAllSubtypes { Creature }`, `AddSubtype`, `SetPower`/`SetToughness`, trailing-clause mods from `parse_continuous_modifications`
- Dispatch after `parse_enchanted_becomes_type_with_ability`, **before** `parse_enchanted_is_type`
- No new engine variant, no new runtime

## CR references

- CR 205.1a — setting a creature subtype replaces existing creature subtypes
- CR 613.1d (Layer 4) — type-changing continuous effect
- CR 613.1f (Layer 6) — ability removal
- CR 613.4b (Layer 7b) — base power and toughness

## Test plan

- [ ] Lignify oracle line parses to `SetCardTypes(Creature)` + `RemoveAllSubtypes(Creature)` + `AddSubtype(Treefolk)` + `SetPower(0)` + `SetToughness(4)` + `RemoveAllAbilities`
- [ ] Prefix-order sibling: `"Enchanted creature loses all abilities and is a Treefolk with base power and toughness 0/4."`
- [ ] Darksteel Mutation / Frogify lines still route through `parse_enchanted_is_type` (regression)
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all`, parser combinator gate, `cargo test -p engine --lib parser::oracle_static`

problems.title: feat(parser): compound player+object hexproof/shroud static — generalise You-and-X grants (CR 702.11 / CR 702.18 / CR 61
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Generalize `parse_compound_subject_keyword_static` (currently Protection-only + hard-coded object subjects) into the full **player + object compound keyword-grant** class — the structural sibling of Serra's Emissary / #5219-style compound continuous statics.

Today the handler only claims:
- object subjects: `creatures you control` / `other creatures you control` / `permanents you control`
- player half: `StaticMode::PlayerProtection` only

Every other player+object grant falls through to a single incorrect `Continuous` that `Or`s the player filter with objects (empty typed + You), which layers interpret as granting the keyword to **every permanent you control** — including the wrong self-scope. That is the live Sigarda bug (Discord / #5322).

## Class (not a card)

`You and <object-subject> have <player-applicable keyword>` where the keyword has a player-scope `StaticMode`:

| Keyword | Object half | Player half |
|---|---|---|
| Protection from Q | `Continuous` + `AddKeyword(Protection(Q))` | `PlayerProtection(Q)` |
| Hexproof | `Continuous` + `AddKeyword(Hexproof)` | `StaticMode::Hexproof` |
| Shroud | `Continuous` + `AddKeyword(Shroud)` | `StaticMode::Shroud` |

Object subjects must reuse `parse_rule_static_subject_filter` (subtype scopes, `this creature` / `~`, `other Heroes you control`, etc.) — not a hard-coded `alt` of three phrases.

Gated forms of the same class:
- Leading turn window: `During your turn, you and this creature have hexproof.` (Gruul Spellbreaker)
- Inverted / trailing condition: `As long as <cond>, you and other Heroes you control have hexproof.` (Captain America, Super-Soldier)

## Anchored on

- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/evasion.rs` `parse_compound_subject_keyword_static` — existing Protection splitter (Serra's Emissary)
- `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/grammar.rs` `lower_rule_static` Hexproof/Shroud player-scope arms + `static_you_have_hexproof` / `static_you_have_shroud`
- Dispatch site: `shared.rs` `parse_static_line_multi_dispatch` (immediately before single-return fallback)

Same structural shape as #5219: dedicated compound handler before the incomplete single-subject sibling, reuse existing predicate/modification builders, Or/split scopes so one `StaticDefinition` is not forced to carry both player and object affected sets.

## Example Oracle (Scryfall-verified)

- **Sigarda, Heron's Grace**: `You and Humans you control have hexproof.`
- **I Am Untouchable**: `You and permanents you control have hexproof.`
- **Gruul Spellbreaker**: `During your turn, you and this creature have hexproof.`
- **Captain America, Super-Soldier**: `As long as Captain America has a shield counter on him, you and other Heroes you control have hexproof.`
- Regression: **Serra's Emissary** Protection compound must keep splitting unchanged

## Out of scope

Instant/sorcery until-EOT grants (`Dawn's Truce`, `Lazotep Plating`, `Veil of Summer`) — effect pipeline, not continuous statics.

## Related

- Disco…

problems.title: feat(parser): compound-quantified dual-subject become effect (Nightcreep class) (CR 611.3)
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

PR #5219 established the compound-subject static pattern for `All <X> and all <Y> are <predicate>` lines — distributing subjects into an `Or` filter and parsing the predicate once. A parallel **effect-layer** gap exists for the become-verb form:

```
Until end of turn, all creatures become black and all lands become Swamps.
```

(Nightcreep). Today the parser claims only the first conjunct (`Creature` → `SetColor(Black)`) and silently drops the second predicate into the static `description` field. The lands-never-become-Swamps half is lost.

## Proposed structural fix (mirror #5219)

Add `try_parse_compound_all_subjects_become_clause` in `oracle_effect/subject.rs`:

1. Peel conjuncts on the ` and all ` seam (same quantifier conjunction that distinguishes compound animation subjects in `parse_compound_all_subjects_filter`).
2. Per conjunct: split `subject become(s) predicate`; resolve subject via `parse_continuous_subject_filter`; lower predicate via existing `build_become_clause` building blocks.
3. Emit one `GenericEffect` carrying multiple `static_abilities` (same multi-static pattern as `build_defender_attack_continuous_compound`).
4. Dispatch immediately before `try_parse_subject_become_clause` so single-subject become lines fall through unchanged.

Factor the ` and all ` conjunct peeler into `oracle_static/static_helpers.rs` so `type_change.rs` and the effect handler share one authority.

## CR references

- CR 611.3 — a continuous effect applies to every object its text indicates (each conjunct is its own affected set).
- CR 105.2 / CR 613.1e — color-setting become (creatures → black).
- CR 305.7 — basic land type replacement (lands → Swamps).

## Acceptance

- Nightcreep parses to two `static_abilities`: `Creature → SetColor(Black)`, `Land → SetBasicLandType(Swamp)`.
- Single-subject `all creatures become black` unchanged.
- Shared-predicate compounds decline this handler.
- Regression tests for positive parse, per-conjunct mods, and decline guards.

## Track

Developer

problems.title: [Card Bug] Glaring Spotlight — hexproof bypass with "you control" qualifier doesn't parse
problems.issue_body:
### Card(s)

Glaring Spotlight

### Bug

Glaring Spotlight's static ability drops to `Unimplemented` and has no effect:

> Creatures your opponents control with hexproof can be the targets of spells and abilities you control as though they didn't have hexproof.

The engine already models the hexproof bypass (`StaticMode::IgnoreHexproof`) and parses the unqualified form (Nowhere to Run: "…targets of spells and abilities as though they didn't have hexproof"). The gap is purely the optional **"you control"** qualifier between "spells and abilities" and "as though" — `parse_ignore_hexproof_static` matches the phrase verbatim as "of spells and abilities as though", so the qualified form fails to parse and the bypass is never emitted. In actual play, Glaring Spotlight's hexproof-bypass does nothing.

### Expected

The line parses to a single `IgnoreHexproof` static scoped to creatures the opponents control (as it does for Nowhere to Run), so hexproof creatures your opponents control can be targeted by your spells and abilities.

### Notes

The compound player+permanent subject variants (Kaya, Bane of the Dead; Detection Tower — "your opponents and creatures your opponents control with hexproof …") additionally require player-subject hexproof bypass and are out of scope here.
