problems.title: parser: compound-subject chosen-type static strict-fails (Rukarumel, Biologist)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`Rukarumel, Biologist`'s chosen-creature-type static — `Slivers you control and nontoken creatures you control are the chosen type in addition to their other creature types.` — is a **compound-subject** sibling of the "chosen type" static class (Arcane Adaptation, Xenograft, Lifecraft Engine), and it currently strict-fails: no `StaticDefinition` is produced at all (verified against `data/card-data.json`: `static_abilities: []`, the whole line collapses into an `Unimplemented` ability).

This is the same *structural* gap shape as #5219 (Life and Limb's compound-subject animation static): two subject clauses joined by "and", each individually already resolvable via an existing building block, but the combination unhandled by any dispatcher.

## Root cause

`parse_arcane_adaptation_chosen_type_static` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/type_change.rs:94`) delegates subject-matching to `parse_chosen_creature_type_static_subject` (`type_change.rs:228-246`), which only recognizes three **fixed literal** single-subject forms:
- `"creatures you control are"`
- `"each creature you control is"`
- `"vehicle creatures you control are"`

Rukarumel's subject — `"Slivers you control and nontoken creatures you control"` — matches none of these, so the predicate parser is never reached.

Both conjuncts are independently well-supported elsewhere:
- `"Slivers you control"` → resolves via `parse_creature_subject_filter`/`parse_continuous_subject_filter` (subtype filter).
- `"nontoken creatures you control"` → already has a direct regression test at `oracle_static/tests.rs:12291-12296` (`parse_continuous_subject_filter("Nontoken creatures you control")`) confirming it resolves via `FilterProp::NonToken`.
- The general "`<X> you control and <Y> you control`" compounding is already handled generically by `parse_controlled_compound_continuous_subject_filter` (`oracle_static/anthem.rs:616`), which `parse_continuous_subject_filter` already calls — but the chosen-type dispatcher never reaches that generic path because its subject matcher short-circuits on the fixed three-arm list first.

There's a second, smaller gap in the *predicate*: the addition-suffix matcher (`parse_chosen_creature_type_static_scope_body`, `type_change.rs:211-226`) only accepts `"in addition to {their|its} other types"`. Rukarumel's actual predicate is `"in addition to their other **creature** types"` (verified verbatim against Scryfall) — an extra `"creature "` word the current suffix grammar doesn't accept.

## Verified card text (Scryfall, `oracleid: 84391c32-5bb7-4c36-be50-bbb5f8732156`)

```
As Rukarumel enters, choose a creature type.
Slivers you control and nontoken creatures you control are the chosen type in addition to their other creature types. The same is true for creature spells you control and creature cards you own that aren't on the battlefield.
{3}, {T}: Create a 1/1 colorless Sliver creature token.
```

- Sentence 1 (`As ~ enters, choose a creature type`) already …

problems.title: feat(parser): leading except-for exempt-list restriction static — Akron Legionnaire (CR 508.1c)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`parse_compound_subject_rule_static` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/evasion.rs:323`) is the single dispatcher for restriction-static lines of the form `"<subject> can't attack[/block/…]"`. Its subject extraction (`nom_primitives::scan_preceded(lower, parse_rule_static_predicate_nom)`) takes *everything before the first recognized predicate* as the subject and hands it whole to `parse_rule_static_subject_filter` (`shared.rs:3913`). Neither function has any grammar for a sentence-initial exception clause.

**Akron Legionnaire** (*Masters Edition III*, legal in Legacy/Vintage/Commander/Oathbreaker/Duel/Premodern/PreDH/Penny — verified via Scryfall `oracle_id: c5f50a78-9dc4-4f3c-aa11-b41c8278bc16`):

```
Except for creatures named Akron Legionnaire and artifact creatures, creatures you control can't attack.
```

Because the line opens with `"Except for "`, `parse_rule_static_subject_filter` is handed `"except for creatures named akron legionnaire and artifact creatures, creatures you control "` as a single subject phrase, which it has no grammar for, so the whole line strict-fails. `client/public/card-data.json` currently records:

```
"type":"Unimplemented","name":"static_structure",
"description":"Static pattern matched but line failed static parser: Except for creatures named Akron Legionnaire and artifact creatures, creatures you control can't attack."
```

So Akron Legionnaire's entire printed ability — a board-defining attack restriction with two carved-out exceptions — is silently dropped.

## Why this is a class, not a card

There IS an existing "except for" combinator, but it's the wrong grammatical slot: `parse_except_for_type_list_suffix` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_target.rs:6228`) only handles a **trailing** `"<type> except for <type-list>"` suffix (Scourglass: "Destroy all permanents except for artifacts and lands"), and its own doc comment explicitly declines named/designation exceptions as unsafe in that slot (an unrecognized word falls back to a silently-vacuous negated `Subtype`, so it must reject the whole clause rather than risk a no-op exclusion).

Akron Legionnaire's shape is different: `"Except for <A> and <B>, "` is a **sentence-initial** clause that scopes an entire restriction predicate, not a suffix on one type filter. This is the same shape of generalization as #5219 (compound-subject animation statics) and #5384 (Shalai's N-way keyword-grant compound subject): resolve each conjunct of a list independently through existing per-domain resolvers, then recombine generically — here, ANDing `Not{Or{exempt conjuncts}}` onto the `affected` filter the existing single-subject dispatcher already produces for the remainder, rather than hand-rolling an Akron-Legionnaire-specific branch.

Each exempt conjunct is itself a class-general shape already used elsewhere in the engine:
- `"artifact creatures"` — a bare type-phrase, handled by the existing `parse_type_phrase`.
- `"creatures named Akron Legionnaire"` …

problems.title: parser: compound-subject animation static strict-fails (Bello, Bard of the Brambles)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

**Bello, Bard of the Brambles** (Bloomburrow Commander)'s compound-subject animation static —

> "During your turn, each non-Equipment artifact and non-Aura enchantment you control with mana value 4 or greater is a 4/4 Elemental creature in addition to its other types and has indestructible, haste, and 'Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, draw a card.'"

(Oracle text verified against the Scryfall API) — currently **strict-fails** (verified against `data/coverage-data.json`: `supported: false`, single gap `"Effect:static_structure"` pointing at the entire line); the whole line collapses into an `Unimplemented` ability.

This is the same *structural* gap shape as #5219 (Life and Limb's compound-subject animation static) and #5392/#5406 (Rukarumel's compound-subject chosen-type static): a compound subject joined by "and" where each individual conjunct is already independently resolvable, and the animation+keyword+ability-grant predicate is already independently resolvable — but the *combination* of a two-conjunct compound subject with this predicate class is unreached.

## Proof the pieces are already independently correct

Two real, currently-`supported: true` cards confirm every constituent piece of Bello's line already works in isolation (verified against `data/coverage-data.json`):

- **Starfield of Nyx**: "each other non-Aura enchantment you control is a creature in addition to its other types" — proves the single negated-type conjunct ("non-Aura enchantment you control ... is a creature in addition to its other types") already resolves correctly, including the `non-` prefix and the CR 205.1b additive "in addition to its other types" marker.

problems.title: Granted-ability description loses case: Brightcap Badger renders "{t}: add {g}." instead of "{T}: Add {G}."
problems.issue_body:
## Symptom (CONFIRMED — full-pool `card-data.json` export diff)

**Brightcap Badger** — *"Each Fungus and Saproling you control has \"{T}: Add {G}.\""*

The granted ability's `description` — a **serialized, user-visible** field — is emitted lowercased:

```diff
-  "description": "{T}: Add {G}."
+  "description": "{t}: add {g}."
```

This string is rendered in the UI, so the card currently displays its granted ability as `{t}: add {g}.`

## Evidence

Found by a full-pool dual-run export (~35,396 faces) while validating an unrelated refactor. Two exports of
`card-data.json`, diffed structurally. The same card also *gained* a correct fix in the same window:

```diff
-  "Subtype": "Each Fungus"     # wrong (fabricated compound subtype)
+  "Subtype": "Fungus"          # correct
-  "description": "{T}: Add {G}."
+  "description": "{t}: add {g}."   # <-- the regression
```

So the subject-parse fix is right; the description built alongside it leaks the lowercased parse buffer.

**Blast radius:** descriptions containing a lowercase mana symbol (`{g}`, `{t}`, …) went **39 → 40** across the
pool. Note the 39 pre-existing hits suggest this leak class **predates** this card and is worth a sweep — the
40th is just the one a diff happened to surface.

## Suspected cause — NOT CONFIRMED, do not treat as diagnosis

Prime suspect is the `<Supertype> <Subtype>` subject peeling work (`oracle_static/grammar.rs`), which is what
fixed `"Each Fungus"` → `"Fungus"` on this same card in the same window. **But I could not confirm it:**
`split_leading_supertype` actually uses the correct case-preserving idiom
(`descriptor[descriptor.len() - rest_lower.len()..]`), and `"Each"` is not a supertype — so the peel that fixed
the subtype may not even live there.

**This needs a bisect, not a guess.** I am filing the *symptom* (which is proven) rather than the *cause*
(which is not).

## Likely shape of the fix

A code path building the granted-ability `description` from the **lowercased** parse buffer instead of the
original-case source text. Per `CLAUDE.md`, the intended pattern is `TextPair` (paired original/lowercase
slices) or the `descriptor.len() - rest_lower.len()` offset idiom — matching on lowercase while emitting the
original case. Grep for a `to_lowercase()` whose result reaches a `description` / `source_text` field.

## Why this matters beyond one card

`description` is a **serialized output surface** (`AbilityDefinition.description` → `ParsedItem.source_text` →
`card-data.json`), so a leak here is directly user-visible in the client and silently invisible to the test
suite — the fixture is ~7% of the card pool and does not contain this card.

problems.title: Saruman of Many Colors: CopySpell reads a stale tracked set (same-chain targeted exile never publishes one)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Saruman of Many Colors' "Copy the exiled card" copies the **wrong card** (or nothing) at runtime. This is a *distinct root cause* from #4792 (fixed by #5571) and was deliberately scoped out of that PR.

## Oracle text (verified from `client/public/card-data.json`)

> Ward—Discard an enchantment, instant, or sorcery card.
> Whenever you cast your second spell each turn, each opponent mills two cards. When one or more cards are milled this way, exile target enchantment, instant, or sorcery card with equal or lesser mana value than that spell from an opponent's graveyard. **Copy the exiled card.** You may cast the copy without paying its mana cost.

## Why this is NOT fixed by #5571

#5571 fixed the *cross-resolution* case, where "the exiled card" refers to an exile made by a **different, earlier** ability (Isochron Scepter's Imprint, Hideaway lands). It routes those to the durable `TargetFilter::ExiledBySource` link.

Saruman is **same-chain**: the exile (`exile target … card … from an opponent's graveyard`) and the `Copy the exiled card` live in the *same* triggered ability. #5571's exile-producer gate therefore (correctly) keeps Saruman's copy target as the chain-local `TrackedSet(0)` — it must not flip, or it would regress.

Parsed AST (current): `CopySpell { target: TrackedSet(0) }` — correct for a same-chain reference.

## Actual root cause (runtime)

`change_zone::resolve()` never calls `publish_tracked_set` for a **plain targeted** `Effect::ChangeZone { destination: Exile }` — every write to `chain_tracked_set_id` / `tracked_object_sets` in that file is under `#[cfg(test)]`. So when Saruman's `CopySpell { TrackedSet(0) }` sub-ability resolves, `TrackedSet(0)` is empty and `copy_source_from_tracked_set` (`game/effects/copy_spell.rs`) falls back to `latest_tracked_set_id` — a global scan for *any* non-empty tracked set — which by that point is some unrelated set (or empty). Result: wrong card copied, or silent no-op.

## Candidate fixes (from the #5571 plan, §3)

- **(a) Runtime — publish a tracked set for exile-destination `ChangeZone` in `change_zone::resolve()`.** NOT recommended: blast radius is *every* targeted `ChangeZone{Exile}` in the game (removal-exile, flicker, graveyard-exile — hundreds of cards), risking unrelated `TrackedSet` consumers / delayed-return snapshots.
- **(b) Narrow parser refinement — route same-chain *plain-targeted* `ChangeZone{Exile}`-then-copy to `ExiledBySource`.** Lower blast radius; reuses the `exile_links` path #5571 added (records via `should_track_exiled_by_source`, resolves via `copy_source_from_exiled_by_source`). **But** it also flips two other same-chain plain-targeted-exile cards whose runtime correctness under `ExiledBySource` is currently unverified and needs per-card runtime tests:
  - **Evolving Door** — `{1},{T}, Sacrifice a creature: … Exile that card, then shuffle. You may cast the exiled card.` (shuffle between exile and cast)
  - **Beseech the Mirror** — `Search your library for a …

problems.title: Nefarious Lich: damage-substitution replacement silently misparsed — defining mechanic never fires
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
**Confirmed silent misparse** (surfaced by Plan 03 unit P3-1b while pinning this card as a draw-replacement witness; verified against data/card-data.json: `replacements: 1`).

## Card (verified against the pool)
> If damage would be dealt to you, exile that many cards from your graveyard instead. If you can't, you lose the game.
> If you would gain life, draw that many cards instead.
> When this enchantment leaves the battlefield, you lose the game.

## Actual parse
Only the GainLife arm parses as a replacement. The damage clause — a textbook CR 614.1a substitution replacement — is lowered into a bare `abilities: [ChangeZone]` entry (inert), and the **"If you can't, you lose the game" rider is lost entirely**. Not Unimplemented — the card claims support while its defining mechanic never fires.

## Class (the discriminating evidence)
The same antecedent ("If damage would be dealt to you") parses CORRECTLY to a DamageDone replacement on 4 sibling cards — Angel of Suffering, Delaying Shield, Force Bubble, Immortal Coil — all of which use the PREVENTION form ("prevent that damage"). Nefarious Lich uses the SUBSTITUTION form ("<action> instead"). So the gap class is: **"If damage would be dealt to you, <non-prevention action> instead"** → antecedent dropped, body escapes as a standalone ability.

## Untriaged sibling leads (same probe: replacement-shaped lines > parsed replacements — flagged, NOT investigated)
- Pokey, the Scallywagg (2→0)
- Shaman en-Kor (2→0)
- Ugin's Nexus (2→1)
(Fisher's Talent from the same probe is already filed as #5636.)

## Fix shape
Extend the damage-replacement antecedent recognizer to accept a substitution body (route through the same DamageDone event with an execute action instead of Prevention), and thread the "If you can't, [consequence]" rider — CR 614.1a substitution + impossibility rider.

problems.title: The Dragon-Kami Reborn: Saga exiles ITSELF instead of a looked-at card (silent #1146-class misparse)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
**Silent misparse — coverage reports this card as SUPPORTED (zero `Unimplemented` nodes), but chapters I–II resolve wrong.** Surfaced by the U20 walk-back binding campaign (task #20 harvest, full-pool sweep of all 35,034 oracle texts).

## Card (verified against data/card-data.json)
> I, II — You gain 2 life. Look at the top three cards of your library. Exile one of them face down with a hatching counter on it, then put the rest on the bottom of your library in any order.

## Actual parse
```
Dig { keep_count: 0, reveal: false }            <- pure peek, keeps NOTHING
  └─ ChangeZone { destination: Exile, target: ParentTarget, enter_with_counters: [("hatching", 1)] }
```
This is verbatim the shape documented at `sequence.rs:4391` as the bug the Hideaway fusion exists to prevent (#1146): the Dig short-circuits as a keep_count:0 pure-peek and the sibling `ChangeZone { ParentTarget }` exiles **the trigger source itself** — the Saga exiles itself (with a hatching counter) instead of one of the three looked-at cards. #1146 is live on this card.

## Cause
The counter rider ("with a hatching counter on it") sits between "face down" and the sentence end, so the `ExileOneOfThemFaceDown` recognizer declines — honestly at the recognizer, but the fallback parse is silently wrong rather than a visible gap.

## Fix shape
Recognizer extension, not new engine work: `enter_with_counters` is already carried correctly on the ChangeZone. The recognizer needs to accept an optional counter rider between "face down" and clause end and thread it into the fused Hideaway-style exile.

## Why this matters beyond the card
This is the **supported-but-misparsed** class — invisible to every existing gate (no Unimplemented node, byte-identity gates can't see it). Full-pool sweep population: "exile one of them face down" matches 5 cards; 4 fire the recognizer correctly, this is the only decline.

problems.title: parser: compound-subject additive type static silently drops the 'spell' stack-scoping (Secret Arcade)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
`Secret Arcade`'s additive-type static — `Nonland permanents you control and permanent spells you control are enchantments in addition to their other types.` — silently **mis-parses**, not strict-fails. The compound-subject split itself already works (`parse_continuous_subject_filter` → `parse_shared_controller_compound_subject_filter` correctly produces an `Or` of the two `you control` conjuncts), but the second conjunct, `permanent spells you control`, loses its "spell" qualifier entirely and resolves to a bare `Typed{Permanent, controller: You}` filter — identical to `permanents you control`.

Verified Oracle text (Scryfall, `Secret Arcade // Dusty Parlor`, DSC #10):
> Nonland permanents you control and permanent spells you control are enchantments in addition to their other types.

## Root cause
`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_target.rs` already has a fully-built, tested mechanism for exactly this class of phrase — a bare "spell"/"spells" head noun means the filter targets an object **on the stack** (CR 109.2), not a permanent:
- `target_phrase_mentions_spell_word` / `target_phrase_uses_spell_suffix` detect the word.
- `scope_spell_targets_to_stack` / `stack_spell_filter` rewrite a `Typed` filter into `TargetFilter::StackSpell` (or `And{[StackSpell, Typed]}` when other type/controller constraints remain).
- `scope_target_spell_phrase` is the entry point, wired into `parse_target_with_ctx` at two call sites (`oracle_target.rs:984`, `:1671`) — this is why targeting grammar ("target artifact or enchantment **spell**") already resolves correctly to a stack-scoped filter.

`parse_type_phrase_with_ctx` (`oracle_target.rs:2038`) — the type-phrase grammar used by static-ability **subject** resolution — never calls `scope_target_spell_phrase`. `crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/shared.rs`'s `parse_continuous_subject_filter` falls through to `parse_type_phrase(subject)` at its generic fallback (`shared.rs:4305`) for any "you control"-suffixed conjunct not caught by an earlier special case. Since "permanent spells you control" hits that exact fallback, the "spells" head noun is silently swallowed by the bare type grammar instead of being scoped to the stack.

Net effect: the static's `affected` `Or` filter becomes `[NonlandPermanentsYouControl, PermanentsYouControl]`, which collapses to "permanents you control" — i.e. Secret Arcade incorrectly makes **lands** you control enchantments too (never intended), and never actually reaches permanent spells on the stack at all (its real, intended effect).

## Why this isn't new engine plumbing
The runtime side is already fully generic and stack-aware:
- `crates/engine/src/game/layers.rs`'s `apply_continuous_effect_filtered` scans `effect.affected_filter.extract_in_zone().unwrap_or(Zone::Battlefield)` via `zone_cache.ids_for(state, scan_zone)`.
- `crates/engine/src/game/targeting.rs:2172` — `zone_object_ids` already returns `state.stack.iter().map(|e| e.id)` for `Zone::Stack`.
- `crates/engine/sr…

problems.title: parser: N-way Oxford-comma "you control" anthem subject drops middle list items (Death-Priest of Myrkul, Blex)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

A continuous "get/have" static ability whose subject is a **3-or-more-item** comma list ending in `you control` silently **drops the middle list item(s)**. The subject filter comes out as an `Or` of only the **first** and **last** items; every item in between is lost, so the anthem buffs the wrong board.

This is the P/T-anthem sibling of the keyword-grant compound-subject path already fixed by #5383 (Shalai, Voice of Plenty). #5383 taught the *keyword* compound-subject splitter to handle N-item Oxford lists, but the **controller-scoped continuous-subject filter** (`parse_shared_controller_compound_subject_filter`) was left with a 2-item-only split, so P/T anthems with 3+ subtypes still regress.

## Repro (verified Oracle text)

| Card | Oracle text (static line) |
|------|---------------------------|
| Death-Priest of Myrkul | `Skeletons, Vampires, and Zombies you control get +1/+1.` |
| Blex, Vexing Pest | `Other Pests, Bats, Insects, Snakes, and Spiders you control get +1/+1.` |
| Raphael, Fiendish Savior | `Other Demons, Devils, Imps, and Tieflings you control get +1/+1 and have lifelink.` |
| Valley Questcaller | `Other Rabbits, Bats, Birds, and Mice you control get +1/+1.` |

### Actual (Death-Priest of Myrkul)

The parsed `affected` filter drops **Vampires**:

```
Or [
  Typed { Creature, Subtype("Skeleton"), controller: You },
  Typed { Creature, Subtype("Zombie"),   controller: You },
]
```

### Expected

```
Or [
  Typed { Creature, Subtype("Skeleton"), controller: You },
  Typed { Creature, Subtype("Vampire"),  controller: You },
  Typed { Creature, Subtype("Zombie"),   controller: You },
]
```

Blex/Raphael/Valley Questcaller lose 3 of their 4–5 listed subtypes the same way.

## Root cause

`parse_shared_controller_compound_subject_filter` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/shared.rs`) peels the shared `you control` / `your opponents control` suffix, then splits the remaining descriptor with a **single** `scan_preceded(tag("and "))` — a 2-item left/right split. For a 3+ item Oxford list `A, B, and C` the only `and ` sits at `, and C`, so it splits into:

* left = `A, B,` — which re-parses to just `A` (the trailing `, B,` is discarded by the single-subtype type-phrase parse), and
* right = `C`,

yielding `Or[A, C]` and silently dropping every middle item `B`.

## Proposed fix

Generalize the existing 2-item seam to an **N-way list split** (parameterize, don't add a sibling handler):

* Split the descriptor at **every** list connector (`", "`, `", and "`, `" and "`, `", or "`, `", and/or "`, `" and/or "`) via a small composable nom combinator, instead of the single `and `-only split. Bare `" or "` is deliberately excluded (it would over-split an intra-subject qualifier such as `with power 3 or greater`); only the comma-anchored `", or "` is a separator.
* Strip the leading distribution word (`Other`, `Each other`, `Each`) **once**, and re-attach `other ` to **each** item's subject so `Other`/`Each other` correctly dist…

problems.title: Ill-Gotten Gains: non-targeted "return up to N cards from graveyard" silently drops its count, bouncing the entire grave
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
**Confirmed silent misparse** (verified against `data/card-data.json` and cross-checked with the live parser output on `main`). Not `Unimplemented` — the clause parses as a *valid*-looking `Effect::Bounce`, but the defining quantity is gone.

## Card (verified against Scryfall)
> Exile Ill-Gotten Gains. Each player discards their hand, then returns up to three cards from their graveyard to their hand.

## Actual parse (current `main`)
The final clause lowers to:
```
Bounce { target: Typed<Card, Owned:ScopedPlayer, InZone:Graveyard>, destination: None, selection: AtResolution }
```
with **no `multi_target` at all**. There is nothing anywhere in the `AbilityDefinition` chain recording "three." At resolution, the `EffectZoneChoice` picker has no bound to enforce, so each player would return their **entire graveyard** to hand instead of up to three cards — the exact opposite of a "restraint" ability card text, and a significant rules violation (CR 601.2c "up to N" semantics never applied).

## Root cause
`TargetedImperativeAst::Return` (the non-targeted, at-resolution bounce variant — used whenever Oracle text omits the word "target", e.g. "return a card from your graveyard to your hand") has no count-carrying field at all, unlike its sibling `Tap`/`Untap`/`Fight`, which already carry `multi_target: Option<MultiTargetSpec>` for exactly this "up to N" shape.

Separately, the "return " clause dispatchers (`parse_targeted_action_ast` in `oracle_effect/imperative.rs` and `try_parse_verb_and_target` in `oracle_effect/mod.rs`) never call the existing `strip_any_number_quantifier` building block for this shape — even though `"return"` is already listed in its `MULTI_TARGET_VERBS` table and the helper is proven correct for the sibling `Tap`/`Untap` "up to N target creatures" pattern. Left unstripped, the leading "up to three " is silently absorbed as unrecognized filler by the downstream destination/target parser.

The *targeted* sibling shape ("return up to two **target** cards from your graveyard to your hand" — Seeds of Renewal, Restock) already works correctly today, via a completely different code path (`strip_optional_target_prefix`, gated on the literal word "target"). Only the non-targeted, "target"-keyword-less shape is affected.

## Runtime is unaffected
`Effect::Bounce`'s at-resolution `EffectZoneChoice` picker already correctly resolves a bounded `ability.multi_target` — this is exercised today by `game::effects::bounce::non_targeted_optional_bounce_still_prompts_at_resolution` and `targeted_up_to_two_graveyard_bounce_moves_chosen_creature` (Wrenn and Six / Macabre Waltz). This is a pure parser-side gap; no game-logic change is required.

## Scope — one confirmed card, a real architectural gap
Ill-Gotten Gains is the only card in the current pool matching this *exact* non-targeted numeric shape (`grep`'d against MTGJSON `AtomicCards.json` for `returns? (up to \w+|that many) cards? from (your|their) \w+ to (your|their) \w+` with no `tar…

problems.title: parser: multi-zone Oxford compound color static strict-fails (Painter's Servant / Mycosynth Lattice)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`Painter's Servant` and `Mycosynth Lattice` use a **multi-zone Oxford-compound color static** that the single-subject color path cannot reach:

- Painter's Servant: `All cards that aren't on the battlefield, spells, and permanents are the chosen color in addition to their other colors.`
- Mycosynth Lattice: `All cards that aren't on the battlefield, spells, and permanents are colorless.`

Verified against `client/public/card-data.json` on current upstream: both Oxford color lines collapse to `Unimplemented` (`static_abilities` empty for Painter's Servant; Lattice keeps only the unrelated artifact-addition line).

## Structural parallel to #5406 / #5219

This is the **color sibling** of [#5406](https://github.com/phase-rs/phase/pull/5406)'s compound-subject chosen-type static (Rukarumel):

| Axis | #5406 (chosen type) | This issue (chosen/fixed color) |
|---|---|---|
| Existing single-subject handler | `parse_arcane_adaptation_chosen_type_static` / `parse_subject_is_color` | `parse_subject_is_color` / `parse_all_subject_are_color` |
| Compound gap | `X you control and Y you control` | Oxford 3-leg `cards not on BF, spells, and permanents` |
| Shared additive suffix extract | `parse_chosen_type_additive_suffix` | `parse_chosen_color_additive_suffix` (`in addition to their other colors`, CR 105.3) |
| Decline unless genuine compound | Or of 2+ filters | Or of 2+ zone-scoped legs |
| Predicate ownership only | `AddChosenSubtype` | `AddChosenColor` / `SetColor { [] }` (colorless) |
| Runtime | already wired | already wired (`AddChosenColor`, `SetColor`) |

## Why it fails today

1. Subject: `parse_continuous_subject_filter` / `parse_all_subject_are_color` do not recognize the Oxford multi-zone enumeration as an `Or` of card / stack / battlefield legs.
2. Painter's predicate: `parse_subject_is_color` uses `all_consuming(tag("the chosen color"))`, which rejects the CR 105.3 additive retain-suffix `in addition to their other colors`.
3. Result: line never claims → strict-fail / `Unimplemented`.

## Proposed fix (mirror #5406)

- Add `parse_compound_multi_zone_color_static` that owns only the color predicate and resolves the subject via a dedicated Oxford peeler into `TargetFilter::Or` of zone-scoped filters (reuse `FilterProp::InAnyZone` / stack-spell scoping from #5744-class machinery).
- Extract shared `parse_chosen_color_additive_suffix`; teach the single-subject color path to accept the additive form where appropriate without stealing SET forms.
- Decline unless the subject is a genuine 2+ leg compound so Shifting Sky / Leyline-class single-subject lines stay on `parse_subject_is_color`.
- Wire in `dispatch.rs` beside the existing color branches; extensive parser shape + decline + no-regression tests.

## CR

- CR 105.2c (colorless)
- CR 105.3 (color change / additive colors)
- CR 105.4 (choose a color)
- CR 611.3 / CR 611.3a (static continuous)
- CR 613.1e (Layer 5 color)

Parser-first, class-level (`All cards that aren't …

problems.title: parser: color-defining static drops its color when composed with a keyword/pump (Onakke Catacomb)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

A continuous color-defining static of the form `<subject> are/is [color] and <keyword|pump>` **silently drops the color**, keeping only the keyword/pump.

- **Onakke Catacomb**: `All creatures are black and have deathtouch.`
  Verified against `client/public/card-data.json` on current upstream: the static parses to a single `AddKeyword { Deathtouch }` modification — the `SetColor { Black }` is gone, so every creature gains deathtouch but is **not** made black.

The color is only lost when it is *composed* with another modification: `All creatures are black.` (solo) parses correctly to `SetColor { Black }`.

## Root cause

`All creatures are black and have deathtouch` hits the `"all creatures "` fast path in `oracle_static/dispatch.rs`, which calls `parse_continuous_gets_has`. That handler matches the trailing `have deathtouch` and returns `AddKeyword { Deathtouch }`, claiming the whole line before the color path (`parse_all_subject_are_color`) is reached. The color functions themselves required the predicate to be a **pure** color expression (`parse_color_predicate(predicate)?`), so `black and have deathtouch` failed there and fell through to the keyword path.

The dispatch comment even asserts the ordering is safe because "`parse_continuous_gets_has`-driven branches … cleanly return None for `are black` predicates" — true for the solo color, but **false** for the `are black and have <keyword>` compound.

## Structural parallel

This is the color sibling of the anthem/type composition already handled elsewhere: `gets +N/+M and has flying` composes a pump with a keyword; `are black and have deathtouch` must compose a **color** (Layer 5, CR 613.1e) with a keyword (Layer 6, CR 613.1f) the same way.

## Proposed fix

Generalize the color-static predicate parse (`parse_all_subject_are_color` / `parse_subject_is_color` in `oracle_static/type_change.rs`):

- A shared `parse_color_and_trailing_modifications(predicate)` peels the leading color expression (itself possibly a multi-color `black and green` list) and parses the `and <keyword|pump>` tail via the existing `parse_continuous_modifications`, returning `(colors, extra_mods)`. A pure color predicate returns `(colors, [])` (unchanged); a non-color predicate returns `None` (routes elsewhere).
- The `"all creatures "` dispatch probes `parse_all_subject_are_color` before `parse_continuous_gets_has`, so a color-leading compound reaches the color path while a bare gets/has line (no leading color) still resolves there.

Result: `[SetColor { Black }, AddKeyword { Deathtouch }]`. Solo color statics and pure keyword/pump anthems are unchanged.

## CR

CR 105.2 (object color) + CR 613.1e (Layer 5, color-changing) + CR 613.1f (Layer 6, ability-adding) — a color-defining static applies the color and the granted ability simultaneously.

## Notes

No existing open issue covers this. #5798 (multi-zone Oxford *compound-subject* color, Painter's Servant/Mycosynth Lattice) is a different axis — that's about…

problems.title: parser: compound-subject additive land-type static drops off-battlefield conjunct (Dune Chanter)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`Dune Chanter`'s compound-subject land-type static — `Lands you control and land cards you own that aren't on the battlefield are Deserts in addition to their other types.` — silently drops the second conjunct. `parse_continuous_subject_filter` (the generic subject resolver) has no branch for the "`<type>` cards you own that aren't on the battlefield" shape, so `parse_controlled_compound_continuous_subject_filter`'s "X and Y" splitter can't resolve the second half, and the static ends up scoped to battlefield lands only — the off-battlefield land cards the printed text explicitly names are never affected.

Verified against Scryfall (`oracle_id: 7811b50d-af76-43cd-8753-43cf65fbefa3`):

```
Reach
Lands you control and land cards you own that aren't on the battlefield are Deserts in addition to their other types.
Lands you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color."
{T}: Mill two cards. You gain 1 life for each land card milled this way.
```

## Structural parallel to #5406 / #5219

Same structural gap shape as #5406 (Rukarumel's compound-subject chosen-type static): two subject clauses joined by "and", each individually resolvable via an existing building block, but the combination unreached because the shared resolver had no branch for one of the two shapes.

| Axis | #5406 (chosen type) | This issue (owned off-battlefield land type) |
|---|---|---|
| Predicate-owning dispatcher | `parse_arcane_adaptation_chosen_type_static` (bespoke 3-arm subject match) | `parse_subject_additive_type_static` (already delegates subject resolution to `parse_continuous_subject_filter`) |
| Missing conjunct shape | `X you control and Y you control` (each already resolvable) | `Y cards you own that aren't on the battlefield` (resolvable elsewhere, but only inside a keyword-grant-specific dispatcher, never reachable from the generic subject filter) |
| Fix shape | New compound-subject sibling dispatcher | One new branch inside the already-generic `parse_continuous_subject_filter`, reusing (via extraction) the keyword-grant family's existing off-battlefield-ownership grammar |
| Runtime | Already wired (`AddChosenSubtype`) | Already wired (`AddSubtype`, `FilterProp::InAnyZone`) |

## Root cause

1. `parse_subject_additive_type_static` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/anthem.rs`) is the general "`<subject>` are/is `<type>` in addition to its/their other types" dispatcher. It already delegates subject resolution *whole* to `parse_continuous_subject_filter` (`oracle_static/shared.rs`) — no bespoke subject matcher of its own.
2. `parse_continuous_subject_filter("Lands you control and land cards you own that aren't on the battlefield")` reaches `parse_controlled_compound_continuous_subject_filter`, which splits on `" and "` and recursively resolves each conjunct via `parse_continuous_subject_filter` itself:

   - `"land cards you own that aren't on the bat…

problems.title: parser: color-qualified keyword grant strict-fails — "has <keyword> if it's <color>" (Scion of Draco)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

A static that grants a keyword **qualified by the recipient's color** — `"<subject> has <keyword> if it's <color>[, …]"` — **strict-fails**: the line produces **zero statics**, so the ability does nothing at all.

**Scion of Draco** (verified against `client/public/card-data.json`):

> Each creature you control has vigilance if it's white, hexproof if it's blue, lifelink if it's black, first strike if it's red, and trample if it's green.

Live-parsed on current upstream: `statics = 0`. The card's **entire main ability is a no-op** — no creature gains any of the five keywords.

The failure is not about list length — even the minimal one-pair form is unhandled:

| Line | statics |
|---|---|
| `Each creature you control has vigilance if it's white, … trample if it's green.` (Scion) | **0** |
| `Each creature you control has vigilance if it's white and trample if it's green.` | **0** |
| `Each creature you control has vigilance if it's white.` | **0** |
| `Creatures you control have flying.` (control) | 1 ✅ |

## Root cause

`"has <keyword> if it's <color>"` has no handler. The single-sentence keyword-grant pipeline reads the keyword but cannot consume the trailing `if it's <color>` qualifier, so the whole line falls through unparsed.

## Proposed fix

Each `if it's <color>` qualifies **only the creature its own keyword lands on** — it is a *per-recipient* qualifier, **not** a shared `StaticCondition` (which would gate every listed keyword on one board check). So the color belongs in that branch's **affected filter**:

- Fold the color in as `FilterProp::HasColor`, exactly as `parse_continuous_subject_filter` already folds a color-named subject (`"White creatures you control"`).
- Read the `"<keyword> if it's <color>"` enumeration with the shared `parse_keyword_name` / `parse_color` atoms, and emit **one Continuous static per listed pair** — mirroring the per-keyword expansion `parse_keyword_grant_from_exiled_object_static` already performs for the Rayami class (#5257 / #5629).
- Decline unless the predicate is entirely such a list, so plain keyword grants and anthems keep their existing paths.

Result for Scion of Draco: 5 statics — `{Creature, You, HasColor(White)} → Vigilance`, `…HasColor(Blue) → Hexproof`, `…Black → Lifelink`, `…Red → FirstStrike`, `…Green → Trample`.

## CR

CR 613.1f (Layer 6, ability-adding effects) + CR 105.2 (an object's color) — the color selects which creatures receive each keyword.

## Notes

No existing open issue covers this. The runtime is already wired (`FilterProp::HasColor` is evaluated by `game::filter`), so this is a parser-only gap.

problems.title: parser: chosen-creature-type static strict-fails when scoped to the graveyard (Ashes of the Fallen)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

A chosen-creature-type static scoped to the **graveyard** strict-fails: the line produces **zero statics**, so the card does nothing after its ETB choice.

**Ashes of the Fallen** (verified against `client/public/card-data.json`):

> As this artifact enters, choose a creature type.
> **Each creature card in your graveyard has the chosen creature type in addition to its other types.**

Live-parsed on current upstream: `statics = 0`. The choice is made, but no graveyard card ever gains the type.

The battlefield sibling parses correctly, so this is purely a zone-scope gap:

| Line | statics |
|---|---|
| `Creatures you control are the chosen type in addition to their other types.` (Arcane Adaptation) | 1 ✅ |
| `Each creature card in your graveyard has the chosen creature type in addition to its other types.` (Ashes) | **0** ❌ |

## Root cause

`parse_arcane_adaptation_chosen_type_static` (`oracle_static/type_change.rs`) dispatches on `ChosenCreatureTypeStaticScope`, whose subject matcher has fixed arms for `creatures you control are`, `each creature you control is`, and `vehicle creatures you control are`. There is no arm for the graveyard-scoped subject — which also reads **"has"** (a single card) rather than "are" — so the whole line falls through unparsed.

## Proposed fix

Extend the existing scope axis rather than add a bolt-on handler:

- Add a `GraveyardCreatureCards` scope whose `target_filter()` is the same creature filter carrying `FilterProp::InAnyZone { zones: [Graveyard] }` — the identical zone fold `parse_hand_cards_have_derived_cost_keyword` already applies for its hand-scoped grant.
- Add the subject arm `"each creature card in your graveyard has"`, binding `"its"` as the retention pronoun.
- Group it with the creature-card subjects in the SET/replace arm (no SET printing exists today; Ashes is additive).

Result: `{Creature, controller: You, InAnyZone[Graveyard]} → AddChosenSubtype{CreatureType}`.

No new engine primitive is required — `AddChosenSubtype`, `InAnyZone`, and the additive/SET split are pre-existing and runtime-wired. Battlefield forms are unaffected.

## CR

CR 400.1 (zones) + CR 205.1b (in-addition retention) + CR 607.2d (chosen-value link) + CR 613.1d (Layer 4).

## Notes

No existing open issue covers this. Distinct from #5859, which is the *effect*-level `try_parse_become_choice` clause in `oracle_effect/subject.rs`.

problems.title: Seam: planeswalk replacement + planar-deck top-2 arrange (Susan Foreman) — requesting `accepted`
problems.issue_body:
## Seam: planeswalk replacement that arranges the top of the planar deck

**Requesting the `accepted` label** to authorize a protected-scope PR (adds a player-choice `WaitingFor` + frontend modal, and registers planar-deck manipulation) per the AI-contributor protected-architecture policy. Design below; I'll build to whatever shape you approve.

### Card
- **Susan Foreman** — *"If you would planeswalk, instead look at the top two cards of your planar deck, put one on the bottom of your planar deck and the other on top, then planeswalk."* ( + `{T}: Add {G}` and Doctor's companion, both already supported.)

### The seam (a class, not one card)
A **replacement of the planeswalk event** (CR 614 + CR 901.8) that performs a **planar-deck top-N look-and-arrange** (a scry-like reorder over the planar deck, CR 901.6) before proceeding to planeswalk. Generalizes to any "if you would planeswalk, instead … then planeswalk" and any planar-deck top-of-library manipulation.

Proposed building blocks:
- A planeswalk-event replacement carrier (reuse the existing replacement machinery; the planeswalk event already exists for Planechase).
- A planar-deck top-N arrange primitive + `WaitingFor::ArrangePlanarDeckTop { count }` (player chooses which of the two goes to bottom vs top). This mirrors the existing scry/surveil "arrange top N" interaction but scoped to the planar deck / command zone.

### Open design question for you
Susan is the first card to *manipulate the planar deck order* rather than just planeswalk. Two options — I'll take your call:
1. A dedicated `WaitingFor::ArrangePlanarDeckTop` + modal (most explicit, matches the card's "put one bottom / one top" wording), or
2. Reuse a generalized "arrange top N of zone Z" interaction if you'd rather I extend the existing scry-arrange rather than add a planar-specific one.

### CR grounding (to be grep-verified in the PR)
CR 901.6 (planar die / planeswalking), CR 901.8 (planeswalking away), CR 614 (replacement effects), CR 901.9–901.10 (planar deck / command zone), plus the scry-analogue reorder rules.

### Layers
types (replacement + WaitingFor/action/event) · game/replacement.rs + planar-deck handling (+ `game/mod.rs` if a new module) · parser/oracle_replacement.rs (nom combinator for "if you would planeswalk, instead …") · AI legal-actions · frontend arrange modal + i18n.

### Runtime proof
Registered card-test: trigger a planeswalk, assert the top two planar cards are revealed, the chosen arrangement is applied (one to bottom, one to top), and the planeswalk then proceeds.

Part of the Doctor Who set-completion effort. Not yet built — filing for acceptance first because it's protected scope and I want the design signed off before implementing.

problems.title: Ward of Bones: relative-quantity per-player cast prohibition + 'same is true' spell-type widening not parsed
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`Ward of Bones`'s per-player prohibitions —

```
Each opponent who controls more creatures than you can't cast creature spells. The same is true for artifacts and enchantments.
Each opponent who controls more lands than you can't play lands.
```

(Oracle text verified against the Scryfall API, `oracle_id: c3ea1497-63ac-46bb-95e9-d98b93a880b3`) — are not modeled by the parser today. No test or dispatch branch references the card, and it isn't in the "claimed parse impact" list of any merged PR.

Root cause: `parse_per_player_conditional_prohibition` (`crates/engine/src/parser/oracle_static/restriction.rs`) is the single handler for the CR 101.2 "Each [scope] who [did X] can't [Y]" class (Angelic Arbiter is the existing member), but its per-player predicate is a fixed 3-arm `alt()` of **turn-activity** predicates only (`attacked with a creature this turn`, `attacked you ... this turn`, `cast a spell this turn`). Ward of Bones's predicate is a **relative permanent-count comparison** ("controls more creatures than you") — a different axis the fixed `alt()` doesn't reach, so the whole line falls through to `Unimplemented`.

This is the same *class* of gap PR #5406 fixed for the chosen-type static family (a hardcoded fixed-arm matcher missing a reachable-but-unmodeled variant) — here the fixed arm is the per-player *condition*, and the same static also needs the "The same is true for X and Y" compound-clause widening PR #5789 generalized for type-changing statics, but applied to a spell-type-restriction static instead.

## Fix approach

- Add a `parse_controls_more_than_you_condition` per-player condition arm, built from **already-wired** primitives: `ParsedCondition::QuantityComparison` comparing `QuantityRef::ObjectCount` scoped via `ControllerRef::ScopedPlayer` (the affected candidate — CR 115.10) against the same count scoped via `ControllerRef::You` (the source's actual controller, per `game::quantity::resolve_quantity_scoped`'s documented split). No new `ParsedCondition` variant, no new evaluator arm — `QuantityComparison` is already generically evaluated by `game::restrictions::evaluate_condition`, and `per_player_condition` is already read at the one call site that matters here (`casting::is_blocked_by_cant_be_cast_for`).
- Add a `parse_cast_typed_spells_predicate` verb arm — the typed sibling of the existing bare "cast spells" arm — extended with an optional "the same is true for `<type>` and `<type>`" continuation (mirrors `same_is_true::parse_sentence`'s two-conjunct "and"-only grammar) that widens the restricted spell types into a single `Or`.

## Scope note

The third clause ("Each opponent who controls more lands than you can't play lands") reuses `StaticMode::Other("CantPlayLand")`, whose runtime check (`check_static_other_by_name`) does not currently read `per_player_condition` at all (only `StaticMode::CantBeCast`/`CantAttack` do, via a different call site). Wiring that up is a separate, slightly wider-blast-radius runtime …

problems.title: Kibo Banana tokens render as black squares because no official token art exists
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Banana tokens created by Kibo, Uktabi Prince currently render as black squares instead of a usable token/card visual.

This appears to be an art/data fallback problem, not a rules issue. Kibo's exported card data correctly creates a colorless artifact token named `Banana` with the expected activated mana/life ability, but `Banana` is not a normal `card-data.json` key and likely cannot be resolved through the generated Scryfall token-image data because Wizards does not appear to have produced an official paper Banana token/card image.

## Evidence

- Local exported card data for `kibo, uktabi prince` has the correct Oracle text and a `Token` effect named `Banana`.
- `jq -r 'keys[] | select(test("banana"; "i"))' client/public/card-data.json` only finds ordinary cards containing banana in the name, not a standalone `Banana` token entry.
- The frontend token image path expects either `obj.token_image_ref` via `client/public/scryfall-token-images.json` or a token/name lookup fallback.
- Public token references list Banana as a token without paper printing and note "No official art."

## Expected behavior

When Kibo creates Banana tokens, the UI should show a deliberate fallback representation instead of a black square. Possible resolutions to discuss:

- A generic artifact-token fallback frame/text tile for true tokens with no official art.
- A curated local fallback asset for non-paper tokens whose art cannot be sourced from Scryfall/MTGJSON.
- A generated or symbolic Banana token image, if that is acceptable for the project's asset policy.
- A specific engine/card-data token-image reference strategy for no-official-printing tokens.

## Repro

1. Start a game with Kibo, Uktabi Prince.
2. Activate Kibo's `{T}` ability.
3. Observe the created `Banana` tokens on the battlefield.

## Notes

This should be discussed before implementation because the right fix may affect the general policy for unofficial/no-paper tokens, not just Kibo.

problems.title: Quoted grants of replacement-shaped abilities ("if it would leave the battlefield, exile it instead") parse to an inert
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

A quoted ability grant of a **replacement-shaped** effect — e.g. `it gains "If this creature would leave the battlefield, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else"` — currently parses to an inert `ContinuousModification::GrantAbility`. The concretized ability body is pushed into `obj.abilities` (`crates/engine/src/game/layers.rs`), never into `replacement_definitions`, so the replacement **never fires** — the redirect is silently a no-op. Affected entries also carry a `SwallowedClause` / `Replacement_Instead` parse warning.

Surfaced during review of #6538 (unearth's standalone leave-battlefield exile rider); the granted variant is a distinct, pre-existing gap and was correctly held out of that PR.

## Affected cards (5 — verified against `card-data.json`)

Exactly the cards that carry the `Replacement_Instead` warning **and** an inert `GrantAbility` for this rider:

- **Elemental Expressionist** — grants it **until end of turn** (must lapse at cleanup, CR 611.2a / 514.2).
- **Geth, Thane of Contracts** — permanent grant on a reanimation ability. *(Correction: my initial draft named "Geth, Lord of the Vault" — that printing has no such rider; the matching card is Thane of Contracts.)*
- **Llanowar Greenwidow** — permanent (also has a separate unimplemented cost-reduction clause, out of scope).
- **Realmbreaker, the Invasion Tree** — permanent.
- **Spirit-Sister's Call** — permanent.

## Out of scope / separate gaps

- **Magar of the Magic Strings** and **The Eighth Doctor** — their whole granting clause is `Effect::Unimplemented` (a face-down-manifest body / a play-from-graveyard permission), so they never reach the `GrantAbility` seam; separate parser gaps.
- **Geth, Lord of the Vault** — no such rider on its current printing.

## Expected

A quoted grant of a replacement-shaped ability should install a **granted, duration-bound replacement effect** that (a) redirects the event while active, and (b) honors the grant's stated duration (lapses at cleanup for `until end of turn`; persists for permanent grants — CR 611.2a) via the layer system, **not** the object-lifetime host stamp used for standalone reanimation riders (#6538).

## Seam

`oracle_static::classify_quoted_inner` must recognize a quoted replacement clause and route it to a granted `ReplacementDefinition` (a new `ContinuousModification::GrantReplacement`) re-applied each layer pass (CR 613.1f), rather than collapsing it to an inert `GrantAbility`. Runtime install: the Layer-6 apply in `layers.rs`.

Repro (Elemental Expressionist): grant the rider to a creature, then destroy/sacrifice it **within the turn** → it should be exiled, not sent to the graveyard; after cleanup the rider should be gone.

problems.title: `prepare_body` stream detection regression
problems.issue_body:
<!-- Summary. -->
Requests 2.34.0 changed the stream detection in PreparedRequest.prepare_body() from `hasattr(data, "__iter__")` to `isinstance(data, Iterable)`. This breaks file-like wrappers that expose `__iter__/read/tell/seek` via `__getattr__ delegation` (e.g. tqdm.wrapattr), because `isinstance(..., Iterable)` only checks the class MRO, not dynamic attribute delegation. As a result, `_body_position` is never recorded and the body cannot be rewound on 307/308 redirects.
## Expected Result

Upload completes successfully through the redirect, as it did in 2.33.1.

## Actual Result

The redirected request sends an empty/consumed body. The server receives no data and the request times out:
```
requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: HTTPSConnectionPool(...): Read timed out. (read timeout=30)
```

## Reproduction Steps

```python
import os
import requests
from tqdm import tqdm

with open("testfile.txt", "wb") as f:
    f.write(b"hello world " * 1000)

with open("testfile.txt", "rb") as f:
    with tqdm.wrapattr(f, "read", total=os.path.getsize("testfile.txt")) as wrapped:
        # Any endpoint that 307 redirects to a presigned S3 URL
        requests.put("https://your-api.example.com/upload", data=wrapped, timeout=30)

```

problems.title: `--fixtures-per-test`: Exclude parametrizing pseudo fixtures?

With something like:

```python

problems.issue_body: ## pytest 8.2.2 breaks pytest-rerunfailures for tests that inherit unittest.TestCase The code: (placed in `new_file.py`) ```python from unittest import TestCase class MyTestClass(TestCase): def test_base(self): self.fail() ``` Run command: ```bash pytest new_file.py --reruns=1 ``` Expected output: (Using `pytest==8.2.1` / previous version) ``` self = def test_base(self): > self.fail() E AssertionError: None new_file.py:5: AssertionError ``` Regression output: (Using `pytest==8.2.2` / latest version) ``` self = def runtest(self) -> None: from _pytest.debugging import maybe_wrap_pytest_function_for_tracing testcase = self.instance > assert testcase is not None E AssertionError ``` The error occurs during the `rerun` of the test. The failure line should be `self.fail()`. Instead, it's `assert testcase is not None`. This causes the `rerun` to never happen. (The test only ran the first time) Tested on a Mac. Here's the `pip list`: ```bash Package Version -------------------- ------- iniconfig 2.0.0 packaging 24.0 pip 24.0 pluggy 1.5.0 pytest 8.2.2 pytest-rerunfailures 14.0 ```

problems.title: unittest: fix assertion errors on unittest reruns
problems.issue_body:
This fixes unittest test reruns when using plugins like pytest-rerunfailures.

The `instance` property uses AttributeError to check if the instance needs to be initialized, so `del` is the correct way to clear it, not setting to `None`.

Regressed in 8.2.2.

Fix #12424

problems.title: Improved the terminal colour formatting, Issue #11666
problems.issue_body:
Hello,

This PR resolves https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/11666.

This is my first time contributing to an open source project so please excuse any beginner mistakes. 

I used the pull request https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/pull/11700 as an initial guide as they started to implement this issue but then stopped. 

I also know that there are errors with my pull request. I believe that they are all due to do the testing of the terminal output, which I have now changed. I am not sure how to change these tests properly, so have left it for now. 

### What I did ###
My goal was to implement the use of the pygment classes `TerminalTrueColorFormatter` and `Terminal256Formatter` to get richer colours in the terminal . 

To do this I used the same logic as pygments use to get the formatter that is appropriate for the users computer.
https://github.com/pygments/pygments/blob/861fb9131b13241d7ea700fba8f6a38cf6f97285/pygments/cmdline.py#L448-L453C57

I set up the formatter in a way that the users can add their own style by setting the environmental variable `PYTEST_THEME `.  I also added in default styles which will be used if `PYTEST_THEME ` is not set. 

Both `TerminalTrueColorFormatter` and `Terminal256Formatter` do not have _light mode_ or _dark mode_ options. I therefore created two default styles, one for each. I tried to create the styles as close as I could to the default style of `TerminalFormatter`. The environmental variable `PYTEST_THEME_MODE` sets if the _light mode_ or _dark mode_ default style is used. If `PYTEST_THEME_MODE` is not set dark mode is the default style. 


To create the default styles. I made classes at the end of the terminalwiter.py file. If this is the wrong spot for them I am sorry. 



Thanks,
James

problems.title: Support marker keyword arguments in marker expression (test selection via `-m`)
problems.issue_body:
<!--
Thanks for suggesting a feature!

Quick check-list while suggesting features:
-->

#### What's the problem this feature will solve?
<!-- What are you trying to do, that you are unable to achieve with pytest as it currently stands? -->

It's possible to create custom markers like so:
```py
@pytest.mark.my_device_under_test
```

This marker can the be used to de/select tests via marker expressions, e.g.:
`pytest -m "not my_device_under_test"`

It is also possible to define keyword arguments for custom markers, e.g.:

```py
@pytest.mark.my_device_under_test(with_serial="1234")
```

Now, it would be amazing to select tests further depending on their keyword arguments + values, e.g.:

`pytest -m "my_device_under_test(with_serial="1234)"`

So only tests with that specific marker + that specific keyword argument+value would be run.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->

Marker keyword argument selection in pytest's marker expression.

<!-- Provide examples of real-world use cases that this would enable and how it solves the problem described above. -->

#### Alternative Solutions
<!-- Have you tried to workaround the problem using a pytest plugin or other tools? Or a different approach to solving this issue? Please elaborate here. -->

- There was a `nose` test plugin, which supported something similar [here](https://github.com/nose-devs/nose/blob/master/nose/plugins/attrib.py). This could be ported to pytest but comes with it's own `attr` decorator.

- A pytest plugin could probably do this in an extra step as well, but would somehow need to disable pytest's internal marker selection plugin [here](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/main/src/_pytest/mark/__init__.py#L261) as it would collide/fail otherwise.

#### Additional context
When skimming through the code I saw that @bluetech implemented a custom parsers some years ago. I'm not very familiar with the topic, as in how much effort it would be support such feature. I'd be interested to contribute though. 
<!-- Add any other context, links, etc. about the feature here. -->

problems.title: Support venv detection on Windows with mingw Python
problems.issue_body:
#### What's the problem this feature will solve?

Currently pytest checks platform depended paths in a directory to see if it might be a venv: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/0ed2d79457b499119693588b71233db957e972c0/src/_pytest/main.py#L370-L387

This works fine with the official CPython releases, but the mingw Python on Windows uses the Unix layout, which looks like this, despite being on Windows:

```console
$ tree -L 1 .venv
.venv
├── bin
├── include
├── lib
└── pyvenv.cfg
```

This results in pytest trying to collect tests in venv files by default.

#### Describe the solution you'd like

I can see three solutions to this:

1) Check for both bin/Scripts

2) First check for the existence of "pyvenv.cfg", which should be in every venv on every platform

3) Replace the current logic and just check for "pyvenv.cfg". "pyvenv.cfg" was introduced in Python 3.3 with the venv module, so it might be enough to assume it exists in every venv. Maybe I'm missing something though.

**Note:** I'm happy to create a PR for any of the above solutions.

problems.title: `pytest==8.3.1` collects tests from Python dependencies within `conda` environments (regression from `8.2.2`)
problems.issue_body:
<!--
Thanks for submitting an issue!

Quick check-list while reporting bugs:
-->

- [X] a detailed description of the bug or problem you are having
- [X] output of `pip list` from the virtual environment you are using
   - NB: Before and after failing CI runs: https://www.diffchecker.com/SReU8wCR/ 
- [X] pytest and operating system versions
   - 8.3.1, multiple different GitHub Actions runners (`windows-2019`, `ubuntu-2022`, etc.) 
- [X] minimal example if possible

----

We have the following `setup.cfg` file:

```ini
[tool:pytest]
addopts = --verbose --show-capture=stderr --tb=native
python_files = testing/**/test_*.py
# NB: norecursedirs is *not* set
```

When running `pytest` (with no additional options) in the [root of our repository](https://github.com/spinalcordtoolbox/spinalcordtoolbox), we see the following behavior:

- `pytest==8.2.2`: Only our tests are collected.
- `pytest==8.3.1`: Our tests _and_ the tests of our dependencies are collected, leading to many errors.
    - `collecting ... collected 367457 items / 408 errors / 100 skipped` (Woof!) 

----

Changing our `setup.cfg` to the following didn't fix the problem either:

```ini
[tool:pytest]
addopts = --verbose --show-capture=stderr --tb=native
testpaths = testing
python_files = test_*.py
```

The fix I used was adding `norecursedirs = {name_of_venv}`

----

Since this involves collection in virtual environments, the reason for the regression might be related to changes in:

- https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/pull/12545

Notably, we use a `conda` env with `pip` packages installed inside, which may subvert the expectations of the changes in the above PR.

problems.title: pytest.approx: Please improve repr readability
problems.issue_body:
It seems that pytest.approx repr is optimized for very high or very low tolerances, but is not as easily readable as it could be for values in between.
Some examples:

- `pytest.approx(42, abs=1)` repr is `42 ± 1.0e+00`, which could be just `42 ± 1`.
- `pytest.approx(5, rel=0.01)` repr is `5 ± 5.0e-02`, but could be `5 ± 0.05` or maybe even `5 ± 1%`
- `pytest.approx(24000, abs=500)` repr is `24000 ± 5.0e+02` and could be `24000 ± 500`
- removing accuracy example: `pytest.approx(1500, abs=555)` repr is `1500 ± 5.6e+02` and could be `1500 ± 555`

In these number ranges using the exact number instead of the exponential notation is both more accurate **and** easier readable for humans. Please adapt pytest.approx to switch it's repr style according to the input value ranges.

problems.title: Support navigating exceptions chains in pdb
problems.issue_body:
#### What's the problem this feature will solve?
If running pytest with `--pdb` and a chain of exceptions is raised, you can only navigate the bottom exception in the chain. You cannot hop between exceptions in the chain

#### Describe the solution you'd like
Python 3.13.0a1 added support for jumping between chained exception in Pdb (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/f75cefd402c4c830228d85ca3442377ebaf09454). `pdb.post_mortem` and `pdb.Pdb.interaction` must be passed an exception object for this to work. These functions used to accept only a traceback, so that's what pytest is passing currently. If pytest passes an exception instead then exception chains can be navigated. As a proof of concept:

```diff
diff --git a/src/_pytest/debugging.py b/src/_pytest/debugging.py
index 3e1463fff..578150f43 100644
--- a/src/_pytest/debugging.py
+++ b/src/_pytest/debugging.py
@@ -354,7 +354,7 @@ def _enter_pdb(
     tw.sep(">", "traceback")
     rep.toterminal(tw)
     tw.sep(">", "entering PDB")
-    tb = _postmortem_traceback(excinfo)
+    tb = excinfo.value #_postmortem_traceback(excinfo)
     rep._pdbshown = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
     post_mortem(tb)
     return rep
```

#### Alternative Solutions
I have not looked for alternate solutions.

#### Additional context
* CPython github issue for supporting jumping between chained exception in Pdb: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/106670

  Write sentences in the **past or present tense**, examples:

  * *Improved verbose diff output with sequences.*
  * *Terminal summary statistics now use multiple colors.*

- [ ] Add yourself to `AUTHORS` in alphabetical order.
-->

Fixes https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/pull/11916#issuecomment-2313758038

Importing `Self` from `typing` breaks the return type on Python 3.9 and under. You should be using `from typing_extension import Self` instead.

For example, the following code:
```py
def pytest_collect_file(file_path: pathlib.Path, parent: Node) -> CheckdocsItem | None:
    if file_path.name not in project_files:
        return None
    return CheckdocsItem.from_parent(parent, name='project')
```
Will error with `Returning Any from function declared to return "CheckdocsItem | None"  [no-any-return]` on 3.8 & 3.9, but pass on 3.10+ Which can only be worked around by disabling the error entirely in mypy, or doing:
```py
def pytest_collect_file(file_path: pathlib.Path, parent: Node) -> CheckdocsItem | None:
    if file_path.name not in project_files:
        return None
    if sys.version_info >= (3, 10):
        return CheckdocsItem.from_parent(parent, name='project')
    else:
        return cast(CheckdocsItem, CheckdocsItem.from_parent(parent, name='project'))
```

problems.title: Customisable truncation limits
problems.issue_body:
Hi! 
I've recently encountered a problem regarding basic truncation limits.

### What's the problem this feature will solve?
[Truncation method](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/main/src/_pytest/assertion/truncate.py#L36-L37) allows to set custom `max_lines`, `max_chars`, but this mechanism is not used in its only call [here](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/main/src/_pytest/assertion/truncate.py#L24), even when `max_length` (I guess it is used as a synonym to `max_chars`) can be specified in `truncate_if_required`.
However, `truncate_if_required` is not called with any length parameter (see [this invocation](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/main/src/_pytest/assertion/__init__.py#L156)).

In its basic form, it produces quite small diff, that may not be as intelligible as it is expected to be :(

#### Example
test.py file: 
```py

    print(10000) #comment
    do_something()

def b():

    do_something()
"""

string_b = """

problems.title: Don't auto-discover tests in particular folders
problems.issue_body:
<!--
Thanks for suggesting a feature!

Quick check-list while suggesting features:
-->

This inspired by a discussion: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/discussions/12748

#### What's the problem this feature will solve?

We have a project that's about a different kind of test. We have a lot of classes with "Test" in the name, including some that start with "Test". We would also like to organize some of our pytest tests in classes whose names start with "Test". We distinguish them by directory; all our pytest tests are in `tests`, and all our production code is in `src`. We'd like an easy way to set this up with no distortion to our production code and minimal shenanigans in the test code, while getting no warnings.

Naively one might think that limiting discovery to a particular directory, as with `pytest tests` or `testpaths=["tests"]`. However, if a production file called TestFoo is imported from production code into test code, it will still be discovered, resulting in a warning like:

```
src/pytest_collection_issue/domain.py:6
  src/pytest_collection_issue/domain.py:6: PytestCollectionWarning: cannot collect test class 'Testament' because it has a __init__ constructor (from: tests/test_domain.py)
    class Testament(object):
```


#### Describe the solution you'd like

For me, the best solution is just to by default disable discovery beyond the requested `testpaths`. Trying to run something just because it's included from wherever strikes me as counterintuitive behavior. If somebody needs that behavior, perhaps an option like `discover_imports` would be useful.

The second-best solution would be an option where we can specify paths to definitely not discover things in. E.g.:

```
testpaths = ["tests"]
excludepaths = ["src"]
```

#### Alternative Solutions

There are many ways to solve this, including manually adding a `__test__ = false` to each production class, using a marker mixin like NotAPytestTest to achieve the same end, importing production classes into the tests under different names, doing only local imports, or renaming our test classes. All of these are a little clunky, and require people to remember a ritual under certain circumstances.

The solution I went with is to put

```
for a_class in [i[1] for i in (globals().items()) if inspect.isclass(i[1])]:
    if a_class.__name__.startswith('Test'):
        a_class.__test__ = False
```

after my domain imports and before my test classes. It still seems clunky to me, but only has to happen once per file of tests. I think it would be better still if this could be fixed in one spot, or have it work by default.

#### Additional context

Please see [this GitHub discussion](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/discussions/12748) and [this example repository](https://github.com/wpietri/pytest-collection-issue) that demonstrates the problem.

problems.title: assertion rewriting ignores the original source positions
problems.issue_body:
The assertion rewriting in pytest changes the source position for all nodes in the assertion to the source range of the assertion.

https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/9515dfa58a144f3644fd29b256113d723c9c1955/src/_pytest/assertion/rewrite.py#L976-L978

This causes problems for tools like [executing](https://github.com/alexmojaki/executing) which uses these source ranges (since python 3.11) to provide a mapping back to the ast-node.

This causes the following problems.
- https://github.com/alexmojaki/executing/issues/2#issuecomment-553738141 executing does not work inside assertions.
- https://github.com/15r10nk/inline-snapshot/issues/57 I have to disable assertion rewriting to be able to find ast-nodes with executing.

problems.title: Capture: copy output when using readouterr() instead of consuming it
problems.issue_body:
## Issue
Currently pytest's capfd/capsys fixtures (CaptureFixture) that allow stdout capturing via readouterr() consume stdout, meaning that logs are no longer available in the "Captured stdout call" up to the point in the test where readouterr() was called. [The documentation](https://docs.pytest.org/en/7.1.x/reference/reference.html?highlight=capsys#pytest.CaptureFixture.readouterr) indicates that this is expected behaviour ("readouterr() : Read and return the captured output so far, **resetting the internal buffer**."), however the ["How to capture stdout/stderr output" tutorial](https://docs.pytest.org/en/7.1.x/how-to/capture-stdout-stderr.html#accessing-captured-output-from-a-test-function) seems to imply that the output is copied from the stdout/stderr streams instead of consumed and reset ("The readouterr() call **snapshots the output** so far - and capturing will be continued. After the test function finishes the original streams will be restored.")

### Example
Code:
```
def method_under_test():
    print("Hallo, Welt!")
    return 41

def test_result(capsys):
    result = method_under_test()
    out, err = capsys.readouterr()
    assert out.startswith("Hello")
    assert result == 42
```
Expected:
```
================================== FAILURES ===================================
______________________________ test_result _______________________________

...

pytestest.py:9: AssertionError
---------------------------- Captured stdout call -----------------------------
Hallo, Welt!
========================== 1 failed in 0.03 seconds ===========================
```
Actual (no captured stdout because it was consumed by `capsys.readouterr()`):
```
================================== FAILURES ===================================
___________________________ test_result ____________________________

...

pytestest.py:14: AssertionError
========================== 1 failed in 0.03 seconds ===========================
```

## Current workaround
Any tests requiring validation of stdout currently need to manually write-back the captured stdout and stderr immediately after capture in order to have them available for viewing under "Captured stdout call" in pytest results. It is not obvious that this is required from the documentation in order to both capture this output for test validation and have the output available for viewing to troubleshoot in the event of test failure.

### Example
Code:
```
def method_under_test():
    print("Hallo, Welt!")
    return 41

def test_result(capsys):
    result = method_under_test()
    out, err = capsys.readouterr()
    sys.stdout.write(out)
    sys.stderr.write(err)
    assert out.startswith("Hello")
    assert result == 42
```
Result:
```
================================== FAILURES ===================================
______________________________ test_result _______________________________

...

pytestest.py:9: AssertionError
----------------------…

problems.title: assertion rewriting ignores the original source positions
problems.issue_body:
The assertion rewriting in pytest changes the source position for all nodes in the assertion to the source range of the assertion.

https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/9515dfa58a144f3644fd29b256113d723c9c1955/src/_pytest/assertion/rewrite.py#L976-L978

This causes problems for tools like [executing](https://github.com/alexmojaki/executing) which uses these source ranges (since python 3.11) to provide a mapping back to the ast-node.

This causes the following problems.
- https://github.com/alexmojaki/executing/issues/2#issuecomment-553738141 executing does not work inside assertions.
- https://github.com/15r10nk/inline-snapshot/issues/57 I have to disable assertion rewriting to be able to find ast-nodes with executing.
- ... maybe more

I already created a pull-request to solve this problem #12815.

problems.title: Add a warning when setting up async fixtures
problems.issue_body:
#### What's the problem this feature will solve?
Pytest cannot evaluate fixture that are async functions or async generators. Users of async pytest plugins may unintentionally annotate those functions with `@pytest.fixture` rather than the async plugin's fixture function.

The fixture result ends up to be an unawaited async generator or coroutine, which is not what the user expected. Most of the time, the corresponding tests will fail. However, when the user defines an autouse fixture to perform setup or teardown, the fixture can silently fail.

##### Fixture results in async generator
```
import pytest

@pytest.fixture
async def async_fixture():
    yield 42

def test_this(async_fixture):
    assert async_fixture == 42  # fails
```

##### Fixture results in coroutine
```
import pytest

@pytest.fixture
async def async_fixture():
    return 42

def test_this(async_fixture):
    assert async_fixture == 42  # fails
```

##### Fixture silently does nothing
```
import pytest

@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
async def async_fixture():
    yield 42
   # perform teardown

def test_this():
    assert True  # succeeds but should fail
```

#### Describe the solution you'd like
Pytest emits the following warning when running async test functions without an async plugin (see #2224):
```
PytestUnhandledCoroutineWarning: async def functions are not natively supported and have been skipped.
  You need to install a suitable plugin for your async framework, for example:
    - anyio
    - pytest-asyncio
    - pytest-tornasync
    - pytest-trio
    - pytest-twisted
```

The warning is emitted as part of a *trylast* hook to `pytest_pyfunc_call`. That means async pytest plugins can create hook wrappers to synchronize the test function and prevent the warning from being emitted.

<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
I suggest to add the same behavior to the use of `@pytest.fixture` on async functions or async generators.

<!-- Provide examples of real-world use cases that this would enable and how it solves the problem described above. -->
Examples
* https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-asyncio/issues/518
* https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-asyncio/issues/286
* https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-asyncio/issues/390
* https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-asyncio/issues/386


#### Alternative Solutions
<!-- Have you tried to workaround the problem using a pytest plugin or other tools? Or a different approach to solving this issue? Please elaborate here. -->
#9962 proposes a mechanism to await results of awaitable tests and fixtures. It can potentially address the issue described here.

#### Additional context
<!-- Add any other context, links, etc. about the feature here. -->
From the above list of async plugins, only anyio, pytest-asyncio, and pytest-trio make use of *pytest_fixture_setup*.
