problems.issue_body:
### Issue Content

We have found at least 2 regression in the way forms are handled while trying to migrate to v0.115.11 from version v0.112.4. After investigation we were able to identify 2 commits that introduce 2 separate bugs that break the handling of default values in both `x-form-urlencoded` and `mutlipart` froms. Partial fixes have been proposed that also address a CVE, but the PR has been hanging since october 24.

# Breaking in the handling of default value in `x-url-encoded` forms

This bug has been introduced in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12134.

MRE:
```python
app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/")
def root(
    name: Annotated[Optional[str], Form(embed=True)] = None,
):
    print(name)
    return name
```

with the following request:
```
❯ http post -v --form localhost:8888 name=""
POST / HTTP/1.1
Accept: */*
Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd
Connection: keep-alive
Content-Length: 5
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Host: localhost:8888
User-Agent: xh/0.24.0

name=

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 2
Content-Type: application/json
Date: Sun, 23 Mar 2025 21:01:49 GMT
Server: uvicorn

""
```
The expected result is that `None` is printed, but instead `""` is printed.

this is the offending bit from the linked PR:
```
diff --git a/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py b/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py
index 6083b731..db7eedba 100644
--- a/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py
+++ b/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py
@@ -789,9 +789,9 @@ async def _extract_form_body(
             value = serialize_sequence_value(field=field, value=results)
         if value is not None:
             values[field.name] = value
-    for key, value in received_body.items():
-        if key not in values:
-            values[key] = value
+    # for key, value in received_body.items():
+    #     if key not in values:
+    #         values[key] = value
     return values
```
This patch solves the x-form-urlencoded  case. So we indeed have two different regressions.
This _get_multi_dict_value  gets called for all fields in the schema: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/4633b1bca933e68dac5c3bcce797ff5963debe2a/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L765-L765
we see here the special case for empty fields: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/4633b1bca933e68dac5c3bcce797ff5963debe2a/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L695-L700
This bit here just blindly re-adds all fields from the body:    https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/4633b1bca933e68dac5c3bcce797ff5963debe2a/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L794-L796

This would be partially fixed by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12502/files, but also requires that ignored fields are not re-added to the form.


# Breaking in the handling of default value in `multipart` forms

The breaking of multipart form originates from https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12117 where the check for empty field was dropped https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12117/files#diff-aef3dac481b68359f4edd6974fa3a047cfde595254a4567…

problems.issue_body:
### First Check

- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar issue and didn't find it.

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
# This needs to be in two files because the nature of the bug involves different globalns
# entries for a decorated function versus the module of the original function.
# If you put the code here into two files (func.py and main.py) in a directory, then the
# bug can be reproduced by running:
# PYTHONPATH=.:$PYTHONPATH python ./main.py
# This should cause an exception `NameError: name 'MyModel' is not defined`

# func.py
from pydantic import BaseModel


def foo(obj: "MyModel") -> "MyModel":
    return obj


class MyModel(BaseModel):
    x: int

# main.py
import functools, typing

from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel
from func import foo

app = FastAPI()


def deco(func):
    @functools.wraps(func)
    def passthrough(*args, **kwargs):
        return func(*args, **kwargs)
    return passthrough

decorated = deco(foo)

assert issubclass(typing.get_type_hints(decorated)["obj"], BaseModel)
assert decorated.__annotations__ == foo.__annotations__
assert isinstance(decorated.__annotations__["obj"], str)

method = app.post('/endpoint')(decorated)
```


### Description

Using a decorator employing `functools.wraps` or a similar causes a `NameError` in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py` in `get_typed_annotation`. The implementation there differs from the implementation in `typing`, which dereferences the `__wrapped__` attribute to find the namespace the original function was defined in. This allows forward references to be handled correctly:
https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/576dd901170af30fc50b0a7f07a388b38fd724a9/Lib/typing.py#L2314-L2315

In the "Example Code" section, my example includes assertions showing that `typing.get_type_hints` handles this situation correctly. I believe this can be fixed either by using the same implementation as typing uses, or by calling `typing.get_type_hints`, and only doing special FastAPI-specific logic if that fails.

### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

I first saw this on Ubuntu Linux with python 3.8, then later reproduced it on my Macbook in python 3.9. The example code was tested on the Mac.

I do not …

problems.title: Remove or change `impl FromRequest* for Option<impl FromRequest*>`?
problems.issue_body:
The possibility of using `Option<Extractor>` as an extractor has lead to a bunch of confusion because people have expected or wanted it to have different semantics for specific inner extractors. We should consider removing or altering the two implementations.

One option: We could have separate traits `OptionalFromRequest` and `OptionalFromRequestParts` and implement them only for a handful of types where it actually makes sense to discard the error. We could also implement different behavior, such as making `Option<Path<_>>` equivalent to the current `OptionalPath` from axum-extra. If you feel like this is worth exploring, I can open an issue.

This idea originally came up in https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/discussions/2281#discussioncomment-7434310.

My AsyncRead + AsyncWrite mock will panic if it sees unexpected bytes, and if this happens in the background task the test will hang. problems.title: Add a `CancellationToken` method for running a future until completion or cancellation
Vectored IO for `write_all_buf`
problems.issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The `AsyncWriteExt` trait provides the `write_all_buf` function to write the entire contents of a `Buf` type to the underlying writer. However, if the buf is fragmented (eg a VecDeque<u8> or Chain), then it can have potentially bad performance with the current implementation, writing many small buffers at a time. This is because the current impl only uses `chunk()` to get the first chunk slice only.

https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/blob/a02407171a3f1aeb86e7406bcac9dfb415278308/tokio/src/io/util/write_all_buf.rs#L47

**Describe the solution you'd like**

If the underlying writer `is_write_vectored()`, `write_all_buf` could make use of `Buf::chunks_vectored` to fill an IO slice to use with `poll_write_vectored`.

The vectored io-slice can use a fixed size array, eg 4 or 8. When advancing the io-slice, should a chunk be removed, it could call `chunks_vectored` again to fill the io-slice, considering that chunks_vectored should be a fairly cheap operation.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Similar implementation discussions have occurred in #3679.
Performance testing is needed, and real-world use cases of `write_all_buf` should be examined

make `broadcast::Receiver` cooperative
problems.issue_body:
Currently, `broadcast::Receiver` does not participate in the [coop budget](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/task/#cooperative-scheduling), so if there are a lot of messages available, a task will just keep receiving them and runtime may not be able to schedule other tasks.

So, it would make sense to have `broadcast::Receiver` participate in the coop budget as well.

problems.title: JoinHandle wakers are kept alive longer than necessary
problems.issue_body:
Currently, the waker registered with a `JoinHandle` is not dropped until the task allocation is dropped. This means that if two tasks await each other's `JoinHandle`, then they will form a reference cycle and the task allocation will never be freed.

The `JoinHandle` waker should be dropped eagerly once the task has completed and the `JoinHandle` is dropped.

problems.title: Add WeakSender for tokio::sync::broadcast
problems.issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

WeakSender is a useful abstraction which allows a "central spawner" to be able to hand out new Senders when needed, but not have the "central spawner" keep a channel alive after all the actual users shutdown.

This diff: https://github.com/RosLibRust/roslibrust/pull/208/files shows a real world application where I was relying on WeakSender for an mpsc channel, but when refactoring a chunk of code to use broadcast instead of mpsc had to do some gymnastics to work around broadcast lacking a WeakSender.

I also consider it "principle of least surprise" that if WeakSender exists for one channel type it would exist for all channel types.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
tokio::sync::broadcast to support WeakSender with an identical api to tokio::sync::mpsc

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
It is likely possible for users to emulate this behavior by passing Arc<Sender> to the various users of their channel, and having the central spawner hold a std::sync::Weak to that Arc. However it is non-obvious that this is the correct way to do things and refactoring code to hold Arc<Sender> in place of Sender is sub-optimal in both ergonomics and performance.

I think the biggest issue at play is the surprising difference between mpsc and broadcast. I can see a call for removing WeakSender from mpsc and pushing users for an externalized solution instead.

I'm unaware of the internal implementation details of mpsc vs. broadcast that make a WeakSender implementation applicable to one but not the other?

runtime hooks: expose spawn caller location in `on_task_spawn` hook
problems.issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

I'm using Tokio's unstable runtime hooks to integrate with an external diagnostics/observability system (DTrace). The function passed to [`runtime::Builder::on_task_spawn`](https://docs.rs/tokio/latest/tokio/runtime/struct.Builder.html#method.on_task_spawn) method is called with a `runtime::TaskMeta` type that contains the `task::Id` assigned by the runtime to that task. The task ID can be used to correlate the `on_before_task_poll`, `on_after_task_poll`, and `on_task_terminate` runtime hooks with when the task was spawned.

However, there isn't an easy way to determine _which_ task in the program's source code is being spawned. The runtime hooks can be used to track various events such as polls over the entire lifetime of the task, but there isn't an easy way to determine what those tasks *are*, limiting its use for debugging and profiling purposes.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

All of the functions involved in task spawning are annotated with the `#[track_caller]` attribute. This means that, within the call chain of `tokio::spawn` and similar APIs, `std::panic::Location::caller()` will return the source location in the *user's code* where the task was spawned, which basically tells you what it is and lets you associate task IDs with application source code. This is currently used by the `tokio_unstable` tracing events. However, it's not exposed to the `on_task_spawn` runtime hook. I'd like it to be passed to that hook.

There are a few different API designs for this, which have different tradeoffs around breaking changes and API niceness.

One option is to add the `std::panic::Location` to the `runtime::TaskMeta` struct. The advantage of this is that it doesn't change the signature of the `on_task_spawn` function, so no code currently using the runtime hooks will break. On the other hand, the spawn location is only cheaply available when the task is spawned, so this wouldn't be present in the `TaskMeta` passed to the `on_before_task_poll`, `on_after_task_poll`, and `on_task_terminate` hook functions. This means we'd have a `fn spawn_location(&self) -> Option<&std::panic::Location>` method on `TaskMeta` that would always be `Some` in `on_task_spawn` and `None` in the other hooks, and the user would have to `unwrap()` it in `on_task_spawn`. This is a bit unfortunate.

On the other hand, we could change the signature of `on_task_spawn` to include the spawn location as a separate argument, like `fn on_task_spawn(meta: &TaskMeta<'_>, spawn_location: &'static std::panic::Location)`. This would break existing code that uses the runtime hooks, since we're changing the signature of the function. However, the runtime hooks are unstable precisely *because* we want to reserve the ability to break them, but it could cause some annoyance for code that currently uses them. The benefit is that we have a much nicer API for the hook functions, where the additional data that's only provi…

problems.title: In `block_in_place`, deferred wakers are woken up after the blocking call and not before
problems.issue_body:
**Version**
1.49

**Description**
I could be missing something, but it seems that when `block_in_place` is called, deferred wakers are woken up after the blocking call finishes and not before.
This may lead to indefinite stalling in (relatively) innocent-looking code.

E.g. consider there is task1 like this:
```
let (action_tx, action_rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();
...
loop {
    select! {
        Some(action) = action_rx.recv() => {
            do stuff and send back the result via a one-shot channel that is part of `action`
        }
        ...
    }
}
```
and there is task2 that sends an action to task1 and waits for the result using `block_in_place`.

What may happen (e.g. under heavy load) is:
1) task1's budget gets exhausted, so the `select!`'s future returns `Pending` and the waker is deferred.
2) the last time that task1's action channel was checked, it was non-empty, so no waker was registered by the channel itself.
3) task2 switches to the same thread that task1 is on.
4) task2 sends an action to task1 and uses `block_in_place` to wait for the result. However there is no way for task1 to be woken up before `block_in_place` finishes.

problems.title: oneshot retains rx_task waker even after rx is closed, leads to RawTask 'leak'
problems.issue_body:
https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/blob/master/tokio/src/sync/oneshot.rs#L1301 

The rx_task waker is only used if the oneshot is not closed. Therefore, I think it would be reasonable to uninitialise the rx_task waker on close. Because we do not currently do this, we hold a reference to the receiving-end task waker for no reason, and this can lead to a RawTask memory leak; even after cancellation, the RawTask containing the receive-side future is kept around as long as the oneshot sender still exists. Obviously this can be fixed by dropping any closed senders, but it is very unintuitive that this can lead to a task leak on the receiving side (and tasks are quite large, while the oneshot inner is typically small, so the task leak would dominate).

If we agree this is a sensible change I would love to make the PR!

problems.title: Runtime identifier and name
problems.issue_body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

In certain circumstances, it would be useful for introspection of Tokio if it was possible to identify a runtime.

This would unlock new features and analyses in `tokio-console` (some described in [console#130](https://github.com/tokio-rs/console/issues/130), and another in [console#229](https://github.com/tokio-rs/console/issues/229)).

I believe it would also add value to `tokio-metrics`.

There are two different forms of identification that would be useful:
1. **Identifier**: unique identifier for the runtime per process. Ideally for the lifetime of the process (although guaranteed to be unique for all concurrently existing runtimes would be better than nothing).
2. **Name**: human readable (and probably human created) string which describes the runtime. No need for uniqueness.

In a sense these are two features, but to me it made more sense to present them together.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Foe the identifier, an opaque struct that can produce a `Sized` value would be ideal for the public API.

Internally a (thread-safe) counter could be used. Each new runtime is assigned the next value. A `u64` will provide more values than can be used during the lifetime of a process (or ever). This aligns with the task Id currently available in unstable.

The identifier would be available from the runtime `Handle`.

The runtime name could be optionally provided to the runtime builder.

It would then be available on the `Handle`.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Foe the `tokio-console` use-case alone, the `console-subscriber` could keep track of runtime creation and assign each an Id. However linking this back to the tasks executing on the runtime and the resources associated with the runtime would be much more complicated (maybe not possible?).

If an identifier is available in the tokio API, bit no name, then the `console-subscriber` or `tokio-console` could apply the mapping based on user input. However unless the runtime identifier would be stable, this mapping would need to be provided on every run of the final application.


**Additional context**

Both `tokio-console` (really `console-subscriber`) and `tokio-metrics` already require that tokio be built with the `tokio_unstable` cfg option set, as such it would be sense to put this feature in unstable as well, especially initially.

As well as use in `tokio-console` and `tokio-metrics`, a name or a way to distinguish Runtimes could be useful in other contexts.

Any application which runs multiple Runtimes, or frequently creates new runtimes (from memory `reqwest` does this for the sync API) may like to be able to distinguish between them at execution time.

tokio-util write_all_vectored can drop data after partial vectored writes
problems.issue_body:
### Description

`tokio_util::io::write_all_vectored` can advance the provided `IoSlice` list incorrectly after a partial `poll_write_vectored` result. The local `advance_slices` helper removes fully written buffers, then re-slices the new first buffer with `&first[..left]`. At that point, `left` is the number of bytes already consumed from that buffer, so the helper keeps the written prefix instead of the unwritten suffix.

### Example

For buffers `[b"ab", b"cd"]`, if `poll_write_vectored` returns `2`, the helper removes the first buffer and then replaces `b"cd"` with `b"cd"[..0]`. The future then sees no non-empty buffers and returns `Ok(())`, silently dropping `b"cd"`.

For buffers `[b"hello", b"world"]`, if `poll_write_vectored` returns `3`, the helper resumes from `b"hel"` instead of `b"lo"`, so subsequent writes can duplicate already-written bytes and skip unwritten bytes.

### Expected behavior

After a partial vectored write, `write_all_vectored` should continue from the unwritten suffix of the current buffer, and should continue with the next buffer when the write count lands exactly on a buffer boundary.

### Suggested fix

Change the helper to retain `&first[left..]`, and add regression coverage for a partial write inside a buffer and an exact buffer-boundary write.

tokio-stream: consider restoring cooperative budgeting in `iter`
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

`tokio_stream::iter` currently has an explicit `TODO: add coop back` and uses a local `yield_amt` counter to return `Poll::Pending` after every 32 yielded items.

Would it make sense to restore integration with Tokio's cooperative budgeting when the relevant Tokio runtime feature is available, while keeping the current simple fallback for configurations without it?

## Context

Current implementation:

- `tokio-stream/src/iter.rs` stores `yield_amt` on `Iter<I>`.
- `poll_next` increments the counter on each yielded item.
- Once the counter reaches 32, it resets the counter, wakes the current task, and returns `Poll::Pending`.
- The code has an explicit comment: `// TODO: add coop back`.

This is not necessarily a correctness bug: a `Stream` is allowed to return `Pending` and later produce more items. The concern is more about scheduler integration and maintainability.

## Motivation

The current implementation effectively gives `tokio_stream::iter` its own hard-coded cooperative-yield policy. That seems slightly separate from Tokio's broader cooperative scheduling machinery.

Using Tokio's cooperative budget where available could:

- keep fairness behavior aligned with the runtime's existing coop mechanisms;
- avoid a standalone magic number in this adapter;
- make behavior easier to reason about alongside other budget-aware Tokio primitives;
- potentially make runtime metrics and forced-yield behavior more consistent.

## Possible approach

One possible direction:

- under the appropriate Tokio `rt`/coop-enabled configuration, use Tokio's cooperative budget mechanism in `poll_next`;
- preserve the current lightweight fallback behavior where coop is not available;
- keep the public API and item semantics unchanged.

## Suggested tests

Before changing behavior, it would be useful to add focused tests for:

- a large finite iterator does not starve a sibling task under a Tokio runtime;
- `size_hint` continues to delegate to the underlying iterator;
- EOF behavior around the current 32-item boundary does not rely on an extra spurious pending poll;
- behavior remains sensible when Tokio runtime features are not enabled.

## Question

Is restoring coop integration for `tokio_stream::iter` still desirable, or is the current manual `yield_amt` behavior now the intended design?

If the former, I would be happy to work on a small PR following maintainer guidance.

problems.title: Inaccurate typing on HTTPHeaders
problems.issue_body:
`HTTPHeaders.get` should return `str | None`, but type checkers aren't able to infer that because it extends `MutableMapping` without type parameters:

```python
from typing_extensions import reveal_type
from tornado.httputil import HTTPHeaders

h = HTTPHeaders()
reveal_type(h.get('a-header'))
```

yields `Union[Any, None]` on mypy and `Unknown | None` on Pyright.

Adding the type parameters `[str, str]` to the extended `MutableMapping` would correct the type to `str | None`.

problems.title: run_sync raises TimeoutError on explicit event-loop stop
problems.issue_body:
When a coroutine passed to `run_sync` doesn't finish because the event loop is stopped explicitly, the error raised is a somewhat confusing:

> TimeoutError: Operation timed out after None seconds


Repro:

```python
import asyncio
from tornado.ioloop import IOLoop

async def main():
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    # ask the loop to stop
    IOLoop.current().stop()
    # coroutine doesn't finish
    await asyncio.sleep(10)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    IOLoop.current().run_sync(main)
```

I'm not even sure it needs to not be a TimeoutError, but the message should probably at least distinguish between the timeout having triggered and the loop stopping for other reasons. Right now, [this bit](https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/blob/385fd8823db043b787f2ca38c46628739deff6b4/tornado/ioloop.py#L534-L535) assumes a timeout is the only way the loop might stop before the given coroutine exits.

problems.title: Incorrect header validation
problems.issue_body:
# Header names

RFC 9110 says that HTTP header names are permitted to contain only the following characters:
> ```
> "!" / "#" / "$" / "%" / "&" / "'" / "*"
> / "+" / "-" / "." / "^" / "_" / "`" / "|" / "~"
> / DIGIT / ALPHA
> ```

Tornado allows the following invalid bytes inside of header names:
```
['\x00', '\x01', '\x02', '\x03', '\x04', '\x05', '\x06', '\x07', '\x08', '\x09', '\x0b', '\x0c', '\x0d', '\x0e', '\x0f', '\x10', '\x11', '\x12', '\x13', '\x14', '\x15', '\x16', '\x17', '\x18', '\x19', '\x1a', '\x1b', '\x1c', '\x1d', '\x1e', '\x1f', '\x20', '\x22', '\x28', '\x29', '\x2c', '\x2f', '\x3b', '\x3c', '\x3d', '\x3e', '\x3f', '\x40', '\x5b', '\x5c', '\x5d', '\x7b', '\x7d', '\x7f', '\x80', '\x81', '\x82', '\x83', '\x84', '\x85', '\x86', '\x87', '\x88', '\x89', '\x8a', '\x8b', '\x8c', '\x8d', '\x8e', '\x8f', '\x90', '\x91', '\x92', '\x93', '\x94', '\x95', '\x96', '\x97', '\x98', '\x99', '\x9a', '\x9b', '\x9c', '\x9d', '\x9e', '\x9f', '\xa0', '\xa1', '\xa2', '\xa3', '\xa4', '\xa5', '\xa6', '\xa7', '\xa8', '\xa9', '\xaa', '\xab', '\xac', '\xad', '\xae', '\xaf', '\xb0', '\xb1', '\xb2', '\xb3', '\xb4', '\xb5', '\xb6', '\xb7', '\xb8', '\xb9', '\xba', '\xbb', '\xbc', '\xbd', '\xbe', '\xbf', '\xc0', '\xc1', '\xc2', '\xc3', '\xc4', '\xc5', '\xc6', '\xc7', '\xc8', '\xc9', '\xca', '\xcb', '\xcc', '\xcd', '\xce', '\xcf', '\xd0', '\xd1', '\xd2', '\xd3', '\xd4', '\xd5', '\xd6', '\xd7', '\xd8', '\xd9', '\xda', '\xdb', '\xdc', '\xdd', '\xde', '\xdf', '\xe0', '\xe1', '\xe2', '\xe3', '\xe4', '\xe5', '\xe6', '\xe7', '\xe8', '\xe9', '\xea', '\xeb', '\xec', '\xed', '\xee', '\xef', '\xf0', '\xf1', '\xf2', '\xf3', '\xf4', '\xf5', '\xf6', '\xf7', '\xf8', '\xf9', '\xfa', '\xfb', '\xfc', '\xfd', '\xfe', '\xff']
```

This is nearly all of the invalid bytes (only `'\n'` and `':'` are handled correctly).

Of particular note is that `'\x00'`, `'\r'`, `'\t'`, and `' '` are allowed through.

I suggest that we start rejecting headers wtih names that contain any of these characters, as most web servers do.

# Header values

RFC 9110 says this:
> Field values containing CR, LF, or NUL characters are invalid and dangerous, due to the varying ways that implementations might parse and interpret those characters; a recipient of CR, LF, or NUL within a field value MUST either reject the message or replace each of those characters with SP before further processing or forwarding of that message.

Tornado allows null bytes in header values.

I suggest that we start rejecting headers with values that contain null, as most web servers do.

problems.title: Content-length validation does not handle spaces
Issues in Parsing HTTP Request "Host" Header
problems.issue_body:
Hello, I may find some bugs with the `Host` header where tornado parses HTTP requests.
RFC 9112 says this: 
> A server MUST respond with a `400 (Bad Request)` status code to any HTTP/1.1 request message that lacks a `Host` header field and to any request message that contains more than one `Host` header field line or a `Host` header field with an invalid field value.

This should imply that the HTTP server must reject requests with redundant `Host` headers or requests with missing `Host` headers. But in both cases, tornado did not reject.

Examples:
```
POST / HTTP/1.1\r\n
Host: victim1.com\r\n
Host: victim2.com\r\n
\r\n
```
```
$ echo -ne "POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: victim1.com\r\nHost: victim2.com\r\n\r\n" | nc 172.18.0.5 80
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: TornadoServer/6.5.dev1
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
Date: Wed, 19 Mar 2025 15:32:17 GMT
Content-Length: 145

{"headers":[["SG9zdA==","dmljdGltMS5jb20="],["SG9zdA==","dmljdGltMi5jb20="]],"body":"","method":"UE9TVA==","uri":"Lw==","version":"SFRUUC8xLjE="}
```
or
```
POST / HTTP/1.1\r\n
Content-Length: 0\r\n
\r\n
```
```
$ echo -ne "POST / HTTP/1.1\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n" | nc 172.18.0.5 80
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: TornadoServer/6.5.dev1
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
Date: Wed, 19 Mar 2025 15:32:40 GMT

{"headers":[["Q29udGVudC1MZW5ndGg=","MA=="]],"body":"","method":"UE9TVA==","uri":"Lw==","version":"SFRUUC8xLjE="}
```

The version I tested was f62afc3.

problems.title: obs-fold is implemented incorrectly
problems.issue_body:
The HTTP RFCs specify that when an HTTP/1.1 implementation receives a header line that begins with a space or horizontal tab, it has two choices:
1. Reject the request
2. Concatenate (fold) this line into the previous header line.

Tornado implements this incorrectly. In addition to folding header lines beginning with spaces and tabs, Tornado also folds header lines beginning with any of the following bytes:
- 0x0b
- 0x0c
- 0x0d
- 0x1c
- 0x1d
- 0x1e
- 0x1f
- 0x85
- 0xa0

problems.title: NUL and CR are incorrectly permitted within header values
problems.issue_body: The HTTP RFCs specify that NUL, CR, and LF bytes are not permitted within HTTP header values. Tornado does not enforce this rule for NUL and CR.

problems.title: Fix incorrect return type annotation for Locale.format_day
problems.issue_body:
`Locale.format_day` is annotated as returning `bool`, but it actually returns a formatted string (e.g. `"Monday, January 22"`).

This incorrect annotation causes type checkers to flag valid usage as errors and can mislead IDE autocompletion.

problems.title: Queue.get(timeout) waits indefinitly for timedelta of zero seconds
problems.issue_body:
The code snippet mentioned below will wait indefinitely until an element becomes available in the queue, while according to the documentation it should immediately raise a TimeoutError when the queue is empty.

```
from datetime import timedelta
from tornado import queues
q = queues.Queue()
q.get(timeout=timedelta(seconds=0))
```

This issue happens because `timedelta(seconds=0)` evaluates to a False value in a conditional expression. As such, the [queues._set_timeout()](https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/blob/f28b245306b204e5ff312973b994fba82a3af01c/tornado/queues.py#L62) method doesn't set the timeout when `timeout=timedelta(seconds=0)`.

problems.title: httputil: Clean up HTTPServerRequest uri and start_line
problems.issue_body:
HTTPServerRequest has two redundant arguments, `uri` and `start_line`. If `start_line` is given, it takes precedence. All production code paths specify `start_line`, but some of tornado's test cases use `uri` only, and some third party test cases (`jupyter_server`) specify neither. 

Prior to https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/pull/3542, both were kind of optional (depending on what you did with the request object); since that PR it has been mandatory to specify one of them. This will make the upgrade to Tornado 6.6 mildly disruptive to at least `jupyter_server`.

* Consider replacing the assertions added in #3542 with deprecation warnings (and giving method/uri/version hard-coded defaults instead of None, to avoid supressing type warnings?). If not, give `jupyter_server` a heads up about `start_line` becoming mandatory.
* In 6.6: Add deprecation warnings when `method`, `uri`, or `version` are given non-None values, or when `start_line` is None
* In 6.7: Remove `method`, `uri`, `version` arguments, make other constructor arguments keyword-only, and make start_line mandatory

problems.title: feature: add swipe tool
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #75

## Problem

TouchPilot has `scroll`, but it does not expose a general swipe primitive for horizontal pages, drawers, carousels, custom surfaces, and gesture-only controls.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `swipe` Android tool.

Supported modes should include:

- direction-based swipe: `left`, `right`, `up`, `down`,
- optional coordinate swipe: `start`, `end`, `duration_ms`,
- optional target/container selector after the resolver exists.

## User workflow

A user can ask TouchPilot to swipe left/right/up/down on a screen or specific area.

## Local-first impact

Swipe is a core Android control primitive and improves local automation on gesture-heavy screens.

## Safety and security considerations

Coordinate gestures are easy to misuse. Keep duration/distance bounded, validate coordinates, and log only safe gesture metadata.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `swipe` to the Android tool catalog.
- [ ] Support direction-based swipe first.
- [ ] Validate optional coordinate inputs if included.
- [ ] Return useful failures for invalid direction or out-of-range coordinates.
- [ ] Add tests for direction validation and execution request construction.
- [ ] Add manual emulator validation for horizontal and vertical swipe cases.

## Alternatives considered

Use `scroll` for all swipe-like behavior. Rejected because scroll and swipe have different semantics and verification needs.

problems.title: feature: add get_foreground_app tool
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #75

## Problem

Tool verification needs to know which app/window is currently foreground, but TouchPilot does not expose a dedicated foreground-app inspection tool.

This makes `open_app`, `press_back`, `press_home`, and future multi-step loops harder to verify.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `get_foreground_app` Android tool that returns current foreground package/window information where Android allows it.

The result should include, when available:

- package name,
- app label,
- window title,
- activity/class if accessible,
- whether TouchPilot AccessibilityService is connected.

## User workflow

A user or local agent can ask TouchPilot where it is before or after an action, and verification can use the result to confirm transitions.

## Local-first impact

Foreground state is local device context and is necessary for reliable local control.

## Safety and security considerations

Foreground app metadata can reveal private app usage. Keep logs concise, avoid sensitive text, and do not require broad new permissions unless clearly justified.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `get_foreground_app` to the Android tool catalog.
- [ ] Return package/window/app label where practical.
- [ ] Do not add unnecessary permissions.
- [ ] Use result in or prepare for post-action verification.
- [ ] Add unit tests for result shape and fallback behavior.
- [ ] Add live checklist coverage.

## Alternatives considered

Infer foreground app from raw screen dumps only. Rejected because verification needs a stable structured signal.

problems.title: feature: add clear_text tool
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #75

## Problem

TouchPilot can type text, but it does not have a reliable primitive for clearing or replacing existing field content.

This blocks common workflows such as editing search terms, replacing settings values, or retrying failed form entry.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `clear_text` Android tool that clears the focused or resolved input field.

Expected behavior:

- use a resolved input target when selector args are provided,
- otherwise operate on the currently focused editable field,
- return a clear failure when no editable target is available,
- avoid logging existing field contents.

## User workflow

A user can ask TouchPilot to clear a field before typing a new value.

## Local-first impact

Reliable local form control needs clear/replace behavior before Milestone 5 multi-step tasks.

## Safety and security considerations

Clearing text can delete user-entered data. The tool should use the normal policy/risk path and must not log previous field contents.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `clear_text` to the Android tool catalog.
- [ ] Support focused-field and resolved-target modes.
- [ ] Return actionable errors for no editable target or ambiguous target.
- [ ] Do not log raw field contents.
- [ ] Add unit tests and live-test checklist coverage.

## Alternatives considered

Use repeated delete key events through a generic key tool. Rejected for now because a focused clear primitive is easier to verify and constrain.

problems.title: feature: add find_element tool
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Current tool calls need reliable target resolution, but agents often need to inspect whether a specific element exists before choosing an action. Reusing raw observe output for this makes routing brittle and pushes too much parsing into the reasoning layer.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `find_element` Android tool that searches the current screen context and returns structured candidate nodes.

Expected arguments:

- `text`: optional visible text query.
- `content_description`: optional accessibility description query.
- `node_id`: optional stable node identifier.
- `class_name`: optional Android class filter.
- `match`: optional match mode such as `exact`, `contains`, or `semantic` when supported.
- `limit`: optional maximum candidates.

## User workflow

The agent can call `find_element({text=Settings})`, inspect the returned candidates, then call a target-aware action such as `tap` or future bounds-based action with the selected target.

## Local-first impact

This gives the local router and small model a structured lookup primitive instead of forcing them to parse full UI trees.

## Safety and security considerations

Results must preserve existing sensitive-text redaction and sensitivity flags. The tool should not return hidden/private fields beyond the existing accessibility observation boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tool is registered in the Android tool catalog.
- Returns structured candidates with stable id, display-safe text, content description, class, bounds, enabled/clickable flags, and sensitivity marker when available.
- Supports bounded candidate limits.
- Includes tests for matching modes and sensitive-text redaction.
- Live-test checklist covers exact text, partial text, content description, and no-match cases.

problems.title: feature: add wait_for_idle tool
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Many Android actions trigger short UI transitions, loading states, keyboard changes, or accessibility-tree churn. Current follow-up actions can run too early unless each caller hand-rolls delays or text waits.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `wait_for_idle` Android tool that waits until the observed screen context remains stable for a small window, or until a bounded timeout expires.

Expected arguments:

- `stable_ms`: optional duration the screen must remain stable.
- `timeout_ms`: optional maximum wait.
- `include_bounds`: optional flag if bounds changes should count as instability.

## User workflow

After `tap`, `swipe`, `open_app`, or `dismiss_keyboard`, the agent can call `wait_for_idle` before selecting the next target.

## Local-first impact

This improves reliability through deterministic synchronization rather than extra model reasoning.

## Safety and security considerations

The tool should be low-risk observation only. It should not expose raw sensitive text beyond the existing redacted screen-context path, and it should use strict timeout bounds to avoid stuck agent loops.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tool is registered in the Android tool catalog.
- Uses screen-context snapshots or accessibility-tree signatures to detect stability.
- Has bounded defaults and actionable timeout messages.
- Includes unit tests for idle/still-changing/timeout behavior where practical.
- Live-test checklist covers waiting after launch, tap, scroll/swipe, and keyboard dismissal.

problems.title: feature: add next-step context and clarification path
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

A multi-step local agent must use what happened in the previous step. It also needs a safe path when the next action is uncertain or multiple targets match. Without that, the loop will either guess or stop with vague errors.

## Proposed behavior

Add a next-step context object that carries recent screen summary, selected tool result, verification result, failure reason, and candidate targets into the next local decision. Add a clarification decision path when the local router cannot safely choose one action.

Clarification cases should include:

- multiple matching targets
- missing required target
- ambiguous user request
- low confidence local decision
- action would require user choice before continuing

## User workflow

When TouchPilot is unsure, it asks a direct question such as “Which Settings item should I open?” instead of executing a risky or random action.

## Local-first impact

This improves small local model reliability by giving it structured context and a non-execution fallback.

## Safety and security considerations

Clarification must not expose raw sensitive screen text. If policy blocks the action, the loop should stop or ask for approval only through the existing approval path, not through generic clarification.

## Acceptance criteria

- Adds a reusable next-step context structure.
- Carries tool result and verification result into the next decision.
- Adds clarification decision type and stop/continue behavior.
- Includes tests for ambiguous target and no-valid-action cases.
- Keeps blocked-policy behavior distinct from clarification behavior.

problems.title: feature: show tool call cards in chat
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Tool calls are central to TouchPilot, but chat users need a readable view of what tool was selected, why it ran, whether approval was needed, and what happened. Raw logs are too dense for normal use.

## Proposed behavior

Add compact tool call cards inside the chat step timeline. Cards should show tool name, redacted arguments, approval/policy status, result status, short message, and verification status when available.

## User workflow

During a task, the user can quickly scan each action TouchPilot took and see whether it succeeded.

## Local-first impact

Visible local tool calls make the local agent loop auditable without cloud traces.

## Safety and security considerations

All arguments and messages must use the existing redactor. High-risk or blocked policy outcomes should be clearly marked.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tool calls render as compact cards in chat.
- Cards include tool name, redacted args, result, and verification state.
- Approval-required and blocked states are easy to distinguish.
- Long args/messages wrap cleanly on mobile.
- No raw sensitive values are displayed.

problems.title: feature: add agent step model
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Milestone 5 needs a shared representation for each local agent step before the loop and UI can evolve cleanly. Today, agent events and tool results exist, but the observe-decide-act loop does not have a compact step model that can be reused by the runner, tests, chat timeline, and run detail UI.

## Proposed behavior

Add a structured agent step model for local runs. The model should represent step type, sequence number, status, input summary, output summary, tool call details when present, verification result when present, timestamps, and stop/clarification metadata.

Expected step types include:

- `observe`
- `decide`
- `act`
- `verify`
- `clarify`
- `stop`

## User workflow

A user starts a local task and every internal step can later be rendered in chat or inspected in a run detail view.

## Local-first impact

This makes the local agent loop observable without relying on cloud traces or external debugging tools.

## Safety and security considerations

Step fields must use existing redaction paths for tool args, screen text, and tool output. Sensitive data should not be persisted or rendered raw.

## Acceptance criteria

- Adds a reusable step data model for local agent runs.
- Covers observe, decide, act, verify, clarify, and stop steps.
- Includes status and stop reason fields.
- Keeps sensitive text redacted in display-facing fields.
- Includes focused unit tests for model construction/serialization where applicable.

problems.title: feature: add bounded local agent loop
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

TouchPilot needs to move from one-shot tool routing to short multi-step local tasks, but the loop must be bounded so it cannot run indefinitely or keep acting after repeated failures.

## Proposed behavior

Add a local observe-decide-act loop with strict run limits. The loop should observe the screen, choose the next local action, execute through the existing policy/tool path, verify the result, and either continue or stop.

Initial stop conditions should include:

- success verified
- max steps reached
- repeated tool failure
- policy blocked
- clarification needed
- no valid next action
- user cancelled

## User workflow

A user asks for a small local task such as opening an app or navigating to a settings subscreen. TouchPilot runs a few safe steps and stops with a clear reason.

## Local-first impact

The loop should use deterministic local routing and the existing local reasoning path. It must not require cloud/API provider configuration.

## Safety and security considerations

Every action must still pass through `DefaultActionPolicy` and existing approval behavior. The loop must stop on blocked or uncertain actions instead of bypassing policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- Adds a bounded local agent loop entry point.
- Supports configurable max steps with safe default.
- Emits structured step records.
- Stops with clear machine-readable and user-facing reasons.
- Includes unit tests for success, max-step, blocked, and failure stop paths.

problems.title: feature: add dismiss_keyboard tool
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The soft keyboard can cover controls and change the accessibility tree after typing. Agents currently have to guess whether pressing Back is meant to dismiss the keyboard or navigate away, which makes edit flows less reliable.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `dismiss_keyboard` Android tool that hides the soft keyboard when it is visible and reports whether the screen changed.

Expected arguments:

- `timeout_ms`: optional bounded wait for the keyboard to disappear.

## User workflow

After `focus_input` and `type_text`, the agent can call `dismiss_keyboard`, then `wait_for_idle`, then tap the next visible control without relying on a generic Back action.

## Local-first impact

This gives local command routing a precise editing primitive and reduces ambiguous use of `press_back`.

## Safety and security considerations

The tool should only hide input UI. It should not submit text, clear text, or navigate app state beyond keyboard dismissal. If implemented through Back fallback, the result should verify that the keyboard disappeared rather than silently navigating away.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tool is registered in the Android tool catalog.
- Detects keyboard visibility when possible.
- Hides the keyboard without submitting text.
- Returns clear success, already-hidden, and failure outcomes.
- Includes unit tests for result formatting/argument validation and live-test checklist coverage on focused input fields.

problems.title: feature: add agent run detail screen
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The chat timeline should stay compact, but maintainers and advanced users need a deeper view of a local agent run for debugging and live validation.

## Proposed behavior

Add an agent run detail screen that can be opened from a completed run or logs. It should show the full ordered step list, tool calls, redacted arguments, verification details, stop reason, and trace/export affordance if already supported.

## User workflow

A user or maintainer taps a run summary and inspects the full run details without digging through raw log text.

## Local-first impact

This supports on-device debugging and trust in the local observe-decide-act loop.

## Safety and security considerations

The detail screen must use display-safe/redacted fields and should not expose raw accessibility snapshots unless the user explicitly exports a redacted debug trace.

## Acceptance criteria

- Run detail screen is reachable from chat run summary or logs.
- Shows ordered steps with statuses and timestamps.
- Shows redacted tool args/results and verification details.
- Provides a clear empty/error state if run data is unavailable.
- Does not display raw sensitive screen text.

problems.title: feature: add running agent state controls
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Users need clear control while a local multi-step task is running. Without visible run state and cancellation, the app can feel stuck or unsafe during longer tasks.

## Proposed behavior

Add running-state UI for local agent runs. The chat screen should show whether the run is idle, running, waiting for approval, waiting for clarification, completed, failed, blocked, or cancelled. Add a cancel/stop control for active runs.

## User workflow

The user starts a task, sees that TouchPilot is running, and can stop it before more actions execute.

## Local-first impact

This keeps local automation user-directed and inspectable.

## Safety and security considerations

Cancel must stop future actions cleanly. It should not interrupt an already-dispatched Android action in a way that leaves internal state inconsistent.

## Acceptance criteria

- Chat screen shows clear run state.
- Active runs have a stop/cancel action.
- Completed, failed, blocked, and cancelled states are visually distinct.
- Cancelled runs emit a stop step/reason.
- Includes UI-level tests or focused state tests where practical.

problems.title: feature: show agent step timeline in chat
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

When a local task runs multiple steps, users need to see what TouchPilot is doing. A hidden loop makes the app feel unpredictable and makes debugging difficult.

## Proposed behavior

Render local agent steps as a compact timeline inside the chat-oriented agent screen. The timeline should show observe, decide, act, verify, clarify, and stop steps as they happen.

## User workflow

The user sends a task, then sees TouchPilot progress through each step without leaving chat.

## Local-first impact

A visible local timeline makes local reasoning inspectable and reinforces that the task is running on-device.

## Safety and security considerations

Timeline text must use redacted display fields. Sensitive args, screen text, or trace data must not be rendered raw.

## Acceptance criteria

- Chat screen renders agent step timeline items.
- Step status is visible: pending, running, success, failed, blocked, clarification needed.
- Timeline updates incrementally during a run.
- Empty and completed states look polished on mobile.
- Uses existing app Material styling conventions.

problems.title: feature: show clarification prompt in chat
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

When the local agent is uncertain, the user should see a clear question and respond in the same chat flow. A plain failure message is not enough for multi-step tasks.

## Proposed behavior

Render clarification requests as assistant chat messages. Where the backend provides options, show them as tappable choices; otherwise allow a normal text reply.

## User workflow

TouchPilot asks “Which item should I tap?” and the user can choose an option or type an answer. The run can then continue with the clarified context.

## Local-first impact

Clarification lets a small local model avoid unsafe guessing while still completing useful tasks.

## Safety and security considerations

Clarification options must be redacted and display-safe. User answers should go through the same policy path before actions resume.

## Acceptance criteria

- Chat renders clarification prompt messages.
- Optional answer choices are shown as tappable controls.
- Text reply path works when choices are absent.
- Clarification response is connected back to the active run state.
- Sensitive option text is redacted.

problems.title: feature: add wait_for_app tool
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

TouchPilot can open an app, but follow-up actions still need a reliable way to wait until the expected app is actually foreground. Without this, agent loops and tool chains can race Android launch transitions and act on the previous screen.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `wait_for_app` Android tool that waits until a target package name or launcher label becomes the foreground app, then returns a structured success/failure result.

Expected arguments:

- `package`: optional Android package name.
- `label`: optional launcher/app label.
- `timeout_ms`: optional bounded timeout with a safe default.

At least one of `package` or `label` should be required.

## User workflow

A local agent can call `open_app({target=Calculator})`, then `wait_for_app({label=Calculator})`, then observe or interact only after the app switch is confirmed.

## Local-first impact

This keeps app-switch synchronization local and deterministic, reducing the need for a larger model to guess whether Android has finished transitioning.

## Safety and security considerations

The tool should be observation/synchronization only. It must not launch apps itself, grant permissions, or bypass policy. Returned app identifiers should go through the normal logging/redaction path where applicable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tool is registered in the Android tool catalog.
- Supports package-name and label matching.
- Uses bounded timeout and clear failure messages.
- Includes unit tests for argument validation and success/failure result formatting.
- Live-test checklist is updated for open-app plus wait-for-app flow.

problems.title: AgentCommandParser mis-extracts the command from prose-wrapped or thought-then-action model output
problems.issue_body:
### What happened?

`AgentCommandParser.extractJsonObject` ([AgentCommandParser.kt:28-48](https://github.com/touchpilot/touchpilot/blob/bf1d817e35d694e22ff0ce82cbce17ecba0f556d/^Gpp/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/agent/AgentCommandParser.kt#L28-L48)) extracts the JSON command emitted by the model with `indexOf('{')` / `lastIndexOf('}')` and never walks the brace structure:

```kotlin
private fun extractJsonObject(raw: String): String {
    val trimmed = raw.trim()
    if (trimmed.startsWith("{") && trimmed.endsWith("}")) return trimmed   // Bug B trigger

    val fenced = Regex("```(?:json)?\\s*([\\s\\S]*?)```")
        .find(trimmed)?.groupValues?.getOrNull(1)?.trim()
    if (fenced != null && fenced.startsWith("{") && fenced.endsWith("}")) {
        return fenced
    }

    val start = trimmed.indexOf('{')
    val end = trimmed.lastIndexOf('}')                                      // Bug A trigger
    if (start >= 0 && end > start) {
        return trimmed.substring(start, end + 1)
    }
    error("Model did not return a JSON object: $raw")
}
```

That coarse extraction has two distinct failure modes, both reachable from the agent loop running on a stock build:

**Bug A â€” stray `{` in the prose before the JSON corrupts the substring and throws.**
When the model emits prose that contains an unrelated `{...}` snippet before the actual command, `indexOf('{')` lands inside the prose snippet and `lastIndexOf('}')` lands at the real end. The substring then spans both braces and the body in between, e.g.

```
User asked: "open {Settings} app". Here is the command: {"tool":"open_app","args":{"target":"Settings"}}
```

is sliced to

```
{Settings} app". Here is the command: {"tool":"open_app","args":{"target":"Settings"}}
```

which is not valid JSON. `JSONObject(jsonText)` on [AgentCommandParser.kt:8](https://github.com/touchpilot/touchpilot/blob/bf1d817e35d694e22ff0ce82cbce17ecba0f556d/^Gpp/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/agent/AgentCommandParser.kt#L8) throws `JSONException`. The exception is caught by the `runCatching { AgentCommandParser.parse(raw) }` block in [BoundedLocalAgentLoop.kt:45-51](https://github.com/touchpilot/touchpilot/blob/bf1d817e35d694e22ff0ce82cbce17ecba0f556d/^Gpp/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/agent/BoundedLocalAgentLoop.kt#L45-L51), which logs `Command parse error: ...` and emits an `invalidStep`, then stops the run with `NO_VALID_ACTION`. The agent burns a step on a response that contained a perfectly well-formed command at the end.

**Bug B â€” `{thought} {action}` output silently picks the wrong object.**
When the model emits two concatenated top-level objects â€” common for prompted "thought then action" patterns and for reasoning-style local models â€” e.g.

```
{"thought":"plan"} {"tool":"open_app","args":{"target":"Settings"}}
```

the trimmed string starts with `{` and ends with `}`, so the first branch of `extractJsonObject` returns the *entire* string verbatim. `org.json.JSONObject(String)` on Android leniently…

problems.title: feature: add task completion summary card
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

At the end of a local task, users need a concise summary of whether TouchPilot completed the task, stopped safely, failed, or needs more input. Without a final summary, the step timeline can be hard to interpret.

## Proposed behavior

Add a completion summary card at the end of each local agent run. It should show final status, stop reason, step count, last verified state, and a short next action if applicable.

## User workflow

After a task finishes, the user sees “Completed”, “Stopped”, “Blocked”, or “Needs clarification” with enough context to understand what happened.

## Local-first impact

This makes local execution outcomes transparent without requiring users to inspect debug logs.

## Safety and security considerations

Failure and blocked summaries should avoid exposing raw tool args or screen text. Policy-blocked runs should explain the safety reason clearly.

## Acceptance criteria

- Summary card renders after every run stop.
- Shows final status, stop reason, step count, and last verification outcome.
- Distinguishes completed, failed, blocked, cancelled, and clarification-needed states.
- Uses redacted display fields only.
- Looks correct on narrow mobile screens.

problems.title: IntentGate misroutes explicit `open`/`tap` phrases when target text contains a navigation keyword (back/home/scroll)
feature: add open_settings_panel tool
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #75

## Problem

Opening Android Settings by label works, but navigating to specific settings panels by tapping is brittle.

Many common workflows need direct access to Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Accessibility, app details, notification settings, or system settings screens.

## Proposed behavior

Add an `open_settings_panel` Android tool using Android Settings intents where available.

Supported panels can start small, for example:

- `wifi`
- `bluetooth`
- `accessibility`
- `app_info`
- `notifications`
- `system_settings`

The tool should return unsupported-panel errors instead of guessing.

## User workflow

A user can ask TouchPilot to open a specific Android settings panel directly, reducing brittle tap chains.

## Local-first impact

Direct local intents make common Android workflows more reliable without external services.

## Safety and security considerations

Settings panels can affect sensitive device state. Opening a panel is safer than toggling settings, but it should still be logged and may remain medium risk.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `open_settings_panel` to the Android tool catalog.
- [ ] Support an initial allowlist of safe panel names.
- [ ] Use Android Settings intents where available.
- [ ] Return clear failure for unsupported panel names.
- [ ] Do not toggle settings automatically.
- [ ] Add unit tests for panel mapping and live checklist coverage.

## Alternatives considered

Use `open_app` plus `tap` chains. Rejected because common settings navigation should be deterministic and less brittle.

problems.title: feature: add observe_screen_context tool
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #75

## Problem

TouchPilot exposes `observe_screen` as a raw Accessibility tree dump, but Milestone 3 added structured `ScreenContext` for local screen understanding.

Agents and debug tooling need a structured observation tool that returns the normalized context directly.

## Proposed behavior

Add an `observe_screen_context` Android tool that returns a redacted serialized `ScreenContext`.

The output should include:

- app/package/window metadata,
- visible nodes,
- roles,
- bounds,
- click/input/scroll flags,
- sensitive text redacted or marked safely.

## User workflow

The local agent can inspect structured screen context before choosing reliable tool actions.

## Local-first impact

Structured local context is the bridge between Milestone 3 understanding and Milestone 4 reliable control.

## Safety and security considerations

`ScreenContext` can contain sensitive visible text. Output must use display-safe/redacted text by default and avoid leaking raw sensitive values in logs or traces.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `observe_screen_context` to the Android tool catalog.
- [ ] Serialize `ScreenContext` in a stable JSON shape.
- [ ] Redact sensitive text by default.
- [ ] Keep `observe_screen` available for raw debug compatibility.
- [ ] Add tests for serialization, redaction, and empty context.
- [ ] Document when agents should prefer structured context over raw dumps.

## Alternatives considered

Only keep `observe_screen`. Rejected because raw text dumps are harder to rank, verify, and evolve safely.

problems.title: feature: add long_press tool
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #75

## Problem

Some Android workflows require long-press, such as opening launcher context menus, selecting text/items, or triggering app-specific overflow actions.

TouchPilot currently only supports normal tap.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `long_press` Android tool using the Milestone 4 target selector/resolver path.

Expected arguments should mirror `tap` where practical:

- `text`
- `node_id`
- `bounds`
- `view_id`

The tool should resolve one target and dispatch a long-press gesture on it.

## User workflow

A user can ask TouchPilot to long-press a visible item, such as an app icon or list item.

## Local-first impact

Long-press expands deterministic Android control without adding cloud dependencies.

## Safety and security considerations

Long-press can open destructive context menus or selection states. Ambiguous targets must fail safely, and the action should remain medium risk unless policy decides otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `long_press` to the Android tool catalog.
- [ ] Resolve targets through the selector/resolver path.
- [ ] Dispatch a bounded long-press gesture.
- [ ] Return clear failure for missing or ambiguous targets.
- [ ] Add unit tests and manual emulator checklist coverage.

## Alternatives considered

Overload `tap` with a duration argument. Rejected for now because a separate tool keeps risk, logging, and agent command parsing clearer.

problems.title: Bug: `LocalModelCommandProvider` and `LocalRouterCommandProvider` are stateful one-shot machines — every multi-step task
Stop button never cancels the agent run: cancellationSignal run() parameter shadows the constructor field
MCP SSE parsing returns the first event (a progress notification) instead of the JSON-RPC response, dropping tools/call
refactor: extract navigation state from MainActivity
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

`MainActivity.kt` currently owns app section navigation, bottom navigation state, settings panel state, pending settings transitions, and active run-detail navigation. As screens are extracted, this navigation state should be made explicit and easier to test.

## Goal

Extract app navigation state and section switching coordination from `MainActivity` into a small dedicated model/controller while preserving current navigation behavior.

## Proposed Location

```text
app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/navigation/
```

Possible files:

```text
AppSection.kt
SettingsPanel.kt
NavigationState.kt
NavigationController.kt
```

Exact names can change during implementation.

## Scope

- Move section state into an explicit navigation state object.
- Move settings panel navigation state where practical.
- Move active run detail navigation state where practical.
- Keep `MainActivity` responsible for attaching rendered views to the root container for now.
- Preserve bottom nav behavior and selected state.

## Non-Goals

- Do not introduce a navigation framework.
- Do not change screen order or labels.
- Do not redesign bottom navigation.
- Do not move full screen rendering in this PR unless already extracted.
- Do not change agent, tool, logging, or settings behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Navigation state is represented outside `MainActivity`.
- [ ] Bottom navigation still switches sections correctly.
- [ ] Settings panel navigation still works.
- [ ] Run detail open/close behavior still works.
- [ ] Current section is preserved across `onResume` as before.
- [ ] `MainActivity.kt` line count is reduced.
- [ ] `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` passes.
- [ ] CI passes.

problems.title: Bug: ScreenContextSummarizer drops the always-safe back/home suggestions on dense screens
problems.issue_body:
### Summary
`ScreenContextSummarizer` can silently drop its "always-safe" **Go back / Go home** suggestions on content-dense screens, violating its own documented invariant.

### Where
`app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/screen/ScreenContextSummarizer.kt`, `buildSuggestions`:
- Line 84: `visibleClickables.take(maxSuggestions - SafeNavigationSlots)` reserves the 2 nav slots **against taps only**.
- Lines 95–112: `type_text` and `scroll` are appended afterward with no slot accounting.
- Lines 117–128: `press_back` + `press_home` appended.
- Line 130: `suggestions.take(maxSuggestions)` truncates whatever overflowed — i.e. the navigation pair.

### Invariant it breaks
The class KDoc (lines 14–16) and the inline comment (lines 114–116) both state the back/home pair is *always* included while the screen has content. `SafeNavigationSlots = 2` exists precisely to reserve room for it — but the reservation is only subtracted from taps.

### Triggers (default `maxSuggestions = 6`)
- 4 clickables + 1 scrollable (no input): pre-cap `[tap×4, scroll, press_back, press_home]` → `take(6)` drops **press_home**.
- 4 clickables + 1 input + 1 scrollable: `[tap×4, type_text, scroll, press_back, press_home]` → `take(6)` drops **press_back and press_home**.

The first scenario is already produced by `OfflineMilestone3Test` (a Settings RecyclerView with 4 rows), which loses `press_home` today but never asserts on navigation, so it stays green.

### Impact
The screen-inquiry path surfaces these as the canonical always-safe way to navigate. On exactly the screens where a user is most likely stuck (a scrollable list, or a form with an input), the agent silently removes its documented escape hatch. Pure, JVM-testable logic; correctness regression against an explicit safety contract.

### Fix
Reserve the navigation pair first, reserve a slot each for the distinct `type_text`/`scroll` capabilities, give the remainder to taps from the front, and append navigation last so it can't be truncated. Preserves all existing assertions (first tap + 3..5 tap cap, scroll/type_text present). PR attached with a regression test.

problems.title: Bug: AgentCommandParser converts a null JSON argument into the string "null"
problems.issue_body:
### Summary
`AgentCommandParser` converts a JSON `null` argument into the literal string `"null"`, so a model emitting an explicit null arg produces a wrong tool argument instead of an absent one.

### Where
`app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/agent/AgentCommandParser.kt:16`:
```kotlin
for (key in argsJson.keys()) {
    put(key, argsJson.opt(key)?.toString().orEmpty())
}
```

### Root cause
`argsJson.opt(key)` returns `org.json.JSONObject.NULL` (a non-null sentinel object) for a JSON `null`. The Kotlin safe-call `?.toString()` therefore does NOT short-circuit — it calls `JSONObject.NULL.toString()`, which returns `"null"`. So `{"tool":"tap","args":{"text":null}}` parses to `args = {"text"="null"}`. The tap path (`TargetSelectorBuilder.fromLegacyArgs` → `TargetResolver`) then searches the screen for an element whose text literally equals/contains `null`, instead of treating the argument as absent.

This is internally inconsistent: the same parser reads `tool` and `final` with `optString(...)`, and org.json's `optString` special-cases `JSONObject.NULL` and returns the empty default — so top-level `null` → `""` but an arg `null` → `"null"`.

### Why it's a real bug (not intended)
An explicit `null` arg is a common LLM output shape; turning it into a literal `"null"` target is clearly wrong. No test asserts the `"null"` result (`AgentCommandParserTest` covers only a normal string arg and a fenced final answer; `LocalModelOutputParser`/contract tests delegate here and don't pin a `"null"` literal).

### Impact
A local model emitting a `null` arg causes a blind tap/type against a non-existent `"null"` target (or pollutes the redacted args log) — exactly the "no blind taps" invariant the selector layer exists to prevent.

### Fix
Map a JSON null arg to `""` via `argsJson.isNull(key)` (matching `optString`'s handling for `tool`/`final`). Regression test included. PR attached.

problems.title: Bug: ScreenSignalsExtractor over-counts clickable nodes from attribute text
problems.issue_body:
### Summary
`ScreenSignalsExtractor` over-counts clickable nodes: it counts a node as clickable whenever the substring `" clickable"` appears anywhere in the node line — including inside quoted attribute **values** like `text="Not clickable yet"`.

### Where
`app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/screen/ocr/ScreenSignalsExtractor.kt:52`:
```kotlin
if (" clickable" in " $body") clickable += 1
```
`body` is the full per-line node body, including quoted `text="..."`/`desc="..."` values (real dump format from `TouchPilotAccessibilityService.appendNode`).

### Root cause
The dump emits both attribute values and the bare flag token ` clickable`. The clickable detector scans the whole body, so a non-clickable node whose label contains the word — e.g. `- TextView node_id="0" text="Not clickable yet"` — matches and is counted. The two sibling extractors on the same node are correctly scoped (`TEXT_ATTR`/`DESC_ATTR` use anchored regexes; the input-field check uses `CLASS_NAME.find(body)` on the leading class token only). The clickable check is the lone one inspecting attribute values.

### Why it's a real bug (not intended)
`ScreenSignalsExtractorTest` exercises clickable counting only with the bare ` clickable` token and never feeds a label containing the word, so no test pins this false-positive path; the inconsistency with the correctly-scoped sibling extractors confirms it's unintended.

### Impact
Inflated `clickableNodeCount` feeds `ContextQualityDetector.classify`. A genuinely weak screen (no real affordances, just text mentioning "clickable") can be misclassified as `Strong`, suppressing the OCR/weak-context fallback the detector is documented to bias toward — so the agent guesses from insufficient data instead of degrading honestly.

### Fix
Strip quoted attribute values before scanning for the bare `clickable` flag token. Regression test included. PR attached.

problems.title: feat: add IntentGate for local routing
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

- Add `IntentGate` in the agent package. It classifies non-conversational tasks into one of the five Milestone-2 categories: `ExactCommand`, `KnownSkill`, `UnsafeRequest`, `ClarificationNeeded`, or `LocalModelNeeded`.
- Wire the gate into `DefaultLocalReasoningCore` after the conversational gate. Each decision routes deterministically:

| Decision               | Effect                                                                                |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `UnsafeRequest`        | Emit `UserMessage` + `PolicyBlocked` + `FinalAnswer`; runner not invoked.             |
| `ClarificationNeeded`  | Emit `UserMessage` + `AssistantMessage` asking the user to elaborate; runner not invoked. |
| `ExactCommand`         | Force `LOCAL_ROUTER` provider on this run so small local models cannot hallucinate an alternate tool call. |
| `KnownSkill`           | Pass through to the configured provider; existing skill allowlist / policy / approval still gate execution. |
| `LocalModelNeeded`     | Pass through unchanged.                                                               |

- Unsafe-keyword detection mirrors `DefaultActionPolicy.blockedWorkflow`. The gate fails closed against the same payment / secret / destructive-action vocabulary the policy layer already blocks — defence in depth, not a replacement.

Closes #34.

## Scope

- `app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/agent/IntentGate.kt` (new) — `sealed class IntentDecision` with 5 variants, `class IntentGate` with `classify(task, skills): IntentDecision`.
- `app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/agent/LocalReasoningCore.kt`
  - `DefaultLocalReasoningCore` now takes an `intentGate: IntentGate` (default-constructed) and an `availableSkills: () -> List<Skill>` callback.
  - `run(task)` consults the gate after the conversational gate; routes per the table above.
- `app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt` — passes `availableSkills = { skills }` into the core. One-line change.
- `app/src/test/java/dev/touchpilot/app/agent/IntentGateTest.kt` (new) — 16 cases covering every category, the precedence between them, blank input, skill-title matching, and a regression that unsafe wins over exact command when both could match.
- `app/src/test/java/dev/touchpilot/app/agent/LocalReasoningCoreTest.kt` — 4 new cases pinning the core's branch behavior for each non-fall-through intent.

## Testing

- [x] `./gradlew assembleDebug`
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleRelease`
- [x] `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` — 61 cases total green: `IntentGateTest` 16/16, `LocalReasoningCoreTest` 12/12 (8 existing + 4 new), `ConversationalGateTest` 14/14, `AgentEventTest` 6/6, `LocalModelApprovalGateTest` 3/3, plus the existing parser/policy/redactor/local-model suites.
- [x] `./gradlew lintDebug` — clean.
- [x] Manual emulator test (`TouchPilot_API_35`):

problems.title: Feature: parse Skills v2 metadata
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

`SkillStore` currently parses skills with ad hoc Markdown scanning. After the Skills v2 schema is documented, TouchPilot needs structured parsing and clear malformed-skill errors.

## Proposed behavior

Add richer skill models and update `SkillStore` to parse the v2 metadata fields. The parser should preserve Markdown instructions, expose structured metadata, and report invalid required fields or invalid tool names clearly.

## User workflow

When TouchPilot starts, bundled skills load into structured models. Broken skill files should be diagnosable from tests and developer logs instead of silently losing important metadata.

## Local-first impact

Structured local parsing gives the agent, UI, and policy layers a reliable on-device source of skill knowledge.

## Safety and security considerations

The parser must not silently accept malformed allowlists or unknown risk values. Invalid skill metadata should fail closed for policy-sensitive fields.

## Alternatives considered

Parsing only headings/lists would preserve current behavior, but it would not support Milestone 6 matching, examples, risk, or success criteria.

## Order note
