problems.title: dismiss_keyboard reports `still_visible_after = false` even when the IME re-shows after the show-mode restore
problems.issue_body:
### What happened?

`TouchPilotAccessibilityService.dismissKeyboard` ([TouchPilotAccessibilityService.kt:342-355](https://github.com/touchpilot/touchpilot/blob/a0ba5b0e14670645a07e3467ae84da36d2c42af9/^Gpp/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/androidcontrol/TouchPilotAccessibilityService.kt#L342-L355)) hides the soft keyboard, briefly waits, **restores the previous show mode**, and then unconditionally returns the `DismissKeyboardOutcome.Hidden` singleton. That singleton hard-codes `stillVisibleAfter = false`:

```kotlin
// TouchPilotAccessibilityService.kt:342-355
fun dismissKeyboard(timeoutMs: Long): DismissKeyboardOutcome {
    if (!isKeyboardVisible()) {
        return DismissKeyboardOutcome.AlreadyHidden
    }
    val controller = softKeyboardController
    val previousMode = controller.showMode
    controller.showMode = SHOW_MODE_HIDDEN
    val settle = timeoutMs.coerceIn(50L, 5_000L).coerceAtMost(500L)
    Thread.sleep(settle)
    controller.showMode = previousMode               // <-- can immediately re-show IME
    return DismissKeyboardOutcome.Hidden             // <-- stillVisibleAfter == false, hard-coded
}
```

```kotlin
// DismissKeyboardOutcome.kt:20-24
data object Hidden : DismissKeyboardOutcome() {
    override val wasVisibleBefore = true
    override val stillVisibleAfter = false           // <-- never measured
}
```

Two compounding problems:

**Problem 1 â€” restoring `previousMode` re-shows the IME, but the function returns before noticing.**
The previous mode is almost always `SHOW_MODE_AUTO` (the platform default). After hiding the keyboard for the ~50â€“500 ms settle window, `controller.showMode = previousMode` puts the IME back into auto-show mode while a focused editable field is still on the screen. The `InputMethodManagerService` immediately re-shows the IME. The function then returns without ever re-checking `isKeyboardVisible()`, so the agent and the user are told the dismissal succeeded even when the keyboard is visibly back.

**Problem 2 â€” `stillVisibleAfter` is a contract-level lie.**
`DismissKeyboardOutcome.Hidden` is a `data object` (singleton) with `stillVisibleAfter = false` baked into the override. No code path can construct a `Hidden` outcome that reports the keyboard is still visible, because there is no path that *measures* it. The field exists in the sealed-class contract â€” and the executor surfaces it as a tool-result field â€” but its value is determined by the source code, not by what the IME actually did.

That lie flows out to user-visible surfaces via the executor:

```kotlin
// AndroidToolExecutor.kt:783-803
private fun executeDismissKeyboard(args: Map<String, String>): ToolResult {
    val timeoutMs = args["timeout_ms"]?.toLongOrNull() ?: 500L
    val outcome = AccessibilityBridge.dismissKeyboard(timeoutMs)
    ...
    return ToolResult(
        ok = ok,
        message = message,
        data = mapOf(
            "was_visible_before" to outcome.wasVisibleBefore.toString(),
            "still_visi…

problems.title: Feature: improve skill matching with aliases and examples
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Current skill matching is mostly title-based. That is too weak for real Android tasks and can miss natural requests like “help me connect to wifi” or “draft a text”.

## Proposed behavior

Improve `IntentGate` skill matching using registry data such as aliases, examples, and task keywords. Matching should return a reason/confidence and must not override exact deterministic commands such as `back`, `home`, `scroll`, or direct tool phrases.

## User workflow

A user can ask for a task in natural language and TouchPilot can choose the relevant enabled skill when appropriate.

## Local-first impact

Better deterministic local matching reduces reliance on larger local models for simple skill selection.

## Safety and security considerations

Matching must be conservative for high-risk skills. It must not accidentally route generic or exact control commands into a skill scope.

## Alternatives considered

Model-only matching may eventually help, but deterministic matching is easier to audit and test for the first Skills v2 version.

## Order note

This is PR 4 of 9. It depends on the skill registry. It can land before or alongside agent prompt context work, but parser and registry should land first.

problems.title: Feature: add skill registry and enabled state
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Loaded skills are currently passed around as a simple list. Milestone 6 needs a registry that supports lookup, active skill selection, and enabled/disabled state.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `SkillRegistry` layer that can look up skills by ID, title, and alias. Persist enabled/disabled state locally, keep active-skill selection consistent with enabled skills, and expose deterministic lookup results for the agent and Settings UI.

## User workflow

A user can disable skills they do not want TouchPilot to use. The app should not match, select, or execute disabled skills.

## Local-first impact

Skill availability and preferences remain local device state, preserving the local-first execution model.

## Safety and security considerations

Disabled skills must fail closed. If the active skill becomes disabled or unavailable, the app should clear or ignore that active selection rather than continuing under stale scope.

## Alternatives considered

Keeping a raw list is enough for bundled demos, but it does not support user control or reliable matching.

## Order note

This is PR 3 of 9. It depends on the v2 parser. Matching, enable/disable UI, and skill detail UI should build on this registry.

problems.title: Feature: integrate skill risk metadata with approvals
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Skills v2 introduces risk metadata, but approval copy and policy decisions will not benefit from it until the security layer can see and use that metadata.

## Proposed behavior

Thread skill risk metadata into approval/policy context so approval prompts can mention when a tool call is happening under a higher-risk skill. Keep full Safety and Policy v2 work for Milestone 7, but make risk metadata available and visible now.

## User workflow

When a skill-scoped action needs approval, the user should see clearer context about why the action is sensitive and which skill is requesting it.

## Local-first impact

Risk-aware approvals keep local automation auditable and understandable without server-side policy checks.

## Safety and security considerations

Risk metadata must not lower existing tool risk or bypass approval. It may only preserve or increase caution in user-facing copy and policy context.

## Alternatives considered

Deferring all risk handling to Milestone 7 is possible, but Skills v2 would ship risk metadata that is not visible in the product.

## Order note

This is PR 9 of 9. It should land after schema, parser, registry, and agent context are stable.

problems.title: Feature: add skill detail UI
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Users and reviewers need to inspect what a skill can do before trusting it. The current Settings UI can show raw Markdown, but Skills v2 metadata should be presented in a clearer way.

## Proposed behavior

Add a skill detail view/card in Settings that shows description, aliases, risk, allowed tools, examples, success criteria, and the bundled Markdown instructions.

## User workflow

A user opens a skill from Settings and can see what the skill is for, what tools it can use, and what successful completion means.

## Local-first impact

Transparent local skill inspection helps users trust on-device automation without requiring external documentation.

## Safety and security considerations

Risk and allowed tools should be visible before a user enables or selects a skill.

## Alternatives considered

Showing only raw Markdown is low effort, but it is harder to scan and does not surface policy-relevant fields consistently.

## Order note

This is PR 7 of 9. It depends on parsed v2 metadata and should follow or parallel the enable/disable UI once the registry exists.

problems.title: Feature: Handle simple chat greetings before tool routing
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

When a user enters a simple greeting such as:

```text
Hello
```

TouchPilot currently treats it like an automation task and sends it into the command-routing flow.

For a chat-first UX, TouchPilot should answer simple conversational messages directly instead of observing the screen, selecting a tool, or producing an action timeline.

## Proposed behavior

If the user inputs:

```text
Hello
```

TouchPilot should respond:

```text
Hello, I am TouchPilot, how can I help you?
```

This should be returned as a final conversational response, not as an Android tool action.

## User workflow

1. User opens the Chat tab.
2. User types `Hello`.
3. TouchPilot appends the user message.
4. TouchPilot appends the assistant response:
   `Hello, I am TouchPilot, how can I help you?`
5. TouchPilot does not run `observe_screen`.
6. TouchPilot does not execute any Android tool.
7. TouchPilot does not show an action timeline for this greeting-only path.

For real automation requests, the existing provider, parser, skill, safety, approval, and tool execution flow should continue to work.

## Local-first impact

This should work without cloud fallback.

The local runtime should support a lightweight conversational `final` response path before tool routing. The behavior should be driven by TouchPilot agent/prompt policy, similar to the OpenClaw/PicoClaw pattern:

- identity/personality instructions
- agent behavior instructions
- tool capability instructions
- runtime/user-turn context
- provider/runtime execution

A future implementation may use an asset such as:

```text
app/src/main/assets/prompts/touchpilot_agent.md
```

or a dedicated Kotlin prompt module if that better fits the current Android app structure.

## Safety and security considerations

Greeting-only messages must not trigger Android control.

Specifically:

- Do not call `observe_screen`.
- Do not execute tools.
- Do not request approvals.
- Do not log screen state for this path.
- Keep automation tasks behind the existing parser, skill allowlist, safety policy, approval flow, and tool execution logs.

## Alternatives considered

One simple option is to hardcode `Hello` handling directly in `MainActivity`, but that would scatter agent behavior into UI code.

A better approach is to keep this behavior near the agent/provider boundary so TouchPilot can grow toward a maintainable prompt-driven local assistant model.

problems.title: Feature: implement central policy engine decisions
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Policy decisions need one central path so tool execution, local model output, local router output, skills, and MCP calls cannot drift into different safety behavior.

## Proposed behavior

Implement a central policy engine that produces consistent allow, ask approval, deny, and block decisions from tool risk, workflow class, app context, skill context, and source.

This should route existing policy behavior through the new model while preserving current safety guarantees.

## User workflow

When TouchPilot proposes a tool call, the policy engine returns a decision. Allowed actions run, approval-required actions show the approval UI, denied/blocked actions stop with a clear user-facing explanation.

## Local-first impact

The policy engine is local, deterministic, and testable. It should not depend on model judgment for final approval.

## Safety and security considerations

The local model can suggest actions, but only policy can approve execution. Unknown policy states should not execute by default.

## Alternatives considered

Leaving policy checks distributed across callers makes future app-aware and workflow-aware rules easier to bypass accidentally.

## Order note

Milestone 7 issue 3 of 6. Build after the rule model and workflow classifier. Keep compatibility with current approvals and blocked workflows.

problems.title: Feature: improve risk-specific approval copy
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Approval prompts should explain why an action needs approval, what data or app state may be affected, and exactly what TouchPilot will do if approved. Generic approval copy is not enough for sensitive workflows.

## Proposed behavior

Improve approval UI copy using policy decision metadata, workflow class, tool risk, app context, and skill context.

Approval text should be risk-specific and workflow-specific for message sending, payments/purchases, deletion, account changes, permissions, security settings, MCP calls, and high-risk skills.

## User workflow

Before approving a sensitive action, the user sees a concise explanation of the risk, affected data/action, tool arguments, and outcome if approved.

## Local-first impact

Approval copy is generated locally from policy metadata and redacted tool arguments.

## Safety and security considerations

Approval copy must not leak secrets. It should make high-risk actions harder to approve accidentally, not easier.

## Alternatives considered

A single generic approval message is simpler but gives users too little context for sensitive Android automation.

## Order note

Milestone 7 issue 5 of 6. Build after the central policy engine can provide structured decision metadata.

problems.title: Feature: Add real on-device command routing model
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

TouchPilot has a local router and an agent command-provider boundary, but it does not yet run a real on-device model. The project direction is local-first Android AI, so TouchPilot needs a real local inference path for command routing before expanding toward larger local LLMs.

The first local model runtime should be small, practical, and focused on structured command routing rather than general chat.

## Proposed Behavior

Add a real on-device model runtime for local command routing.

The runtime should take a user task plus relevant context and return a structured command compatible with the existing JSON command loop.

Example output:

```json
{
  "tool": "open_app",
  "args": {
    "target": "Settings"
  }
}
```

or:

```json
{
  "final": "I cannot do that safely."
}
```

## Scope

- Start with LiteRT for a small command-routing model.
- Define model asset loading and storage.
- Add local model status UI.
- Add runtime health/status checks.
- Add a local inference interface behind the existing command-provider boundary.
- Keep deterministic local router as fallback.
- Keep cloud provider optional and experimental.
- Ensure local model outputs go through:
  - JSON parsing
  - tool validation
  - skill allowlists
  - safety policy
  - approval flow
  - logs/traces
- Document future ExecuTorch and llama.cpp paths.
- Add tests or fixtures for local command output parsing.

## User Workflow

A user should be able to open TouchPilot and run simple tasks locally without configuring an API key.

Example tasks:

- open settings
- go back
- scroll down
- tap Wi-Fi
- observe the current screen

TouchPilot should show local model status and make it clear whether it is using:

- deterministic local router
- local model runtime
- cloud fallback

If the local model is unavailable, TouchPilot should fall back to the deterministic local router and explain that fallback in the UI.

## Local-First Impact

This is a core local-first milestone. It moves TouchPilot from deterministic local routing toward learned on-device command selection while preserving the existing safety/tool execution pipeline.

The goal is not full local chat yet. The goal is a small local command-routing model that can safely produce structured tool calls.

## Safety and Security Considerations

Local model output must be treated as untrusted.

Every local model command must pass through:

- schema parsing
- tool validation
- skill allowlists
- safety policy
- approval flow
- logging and trace redaction

The model must not directly execute Android actions. It only proposes commands.

The implementation should avoid:

- bypassing approval prompts
- bypassing skill allowlists
- logging sensitive screen text
- relying on model judgment for sensitive actions
- silently falling back to cloud without user visibility

## Alternatives Considered

- Keep deterministic local router only.
- Integrate ExecuTorch first.
- Integrate llama.cpp first.
- Use cloud provider until local LLM runti…

problems.title: Feature: Answer simple help requests before tool routing
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

TouchPilot can now answer simple greetings before tool routing, but users still need a lightweight way to discover what the local-first assistant can do.

If a user types `help`, TouchPilot should answer conversationally instead of treating it like an Android automation task.

## Proposed behavior

If the user inputs:

```text
help
```

TouchPilot should respond:

```text
I can help you control Android apps, open settings, tap visible text, scroll, go back or home, and use approved skills. What would you like to do?
```

Similar phrases should also work:

- `what can you do`
- `how can you help`

This should be returned as a final conversational response, not as an Android tool action.

## User workflow

1. User opens the Chat tab.
2. User types `help`.
3. TouchPilot appends the user message.
4. TouchPilot appends the assistant help response.
5. TouchPilot does not run `observe_screen`.
6. TouchPilot does not execute any Android tool.
7. TouchPilot does not show an action timeline for this help-only path.

Automation requests such as `open Settings`, `tap OK`, `scroll`, `go back`, and `go home` should continue through the existing provider, parser, skill, safety, approval, and tool execution flow.

## Local-first impact

This is a small Milestone 1 polish feature for the local-first chat experience.

The behavior should work offline and should not require cloud fallback. It can build on the existing `ConversationalGate` path introduced for greeting-only messages.

## Safety and security considerations

Help-only messages must not trigger Android control.

Specifically:

- Do not call `observe_screen`.
- Do not execute tools.
- Do not request approvals.
- Do not log screen state for this path.
- Keep real automation tasks behind the existing parser, skill allowlist, safety policy, approval flow, and tool execution logs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Typing `help` returns the expected help response.
- Typing `what can you do` returns the expected help response.
- Typing `how can you help` returns the expected help response.
- No tool call is made for help-only input.
- No action timeline is shown for help-only input.
- Existing automation commands still route normally.
- Unit tests cover positive help phrases and a mixed phrase such as `help me open Settings`, which should not be short-circuited.

problems.title: Feature: add local model manifest and version metadata
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
As local models improve, TouchPilot needs clear metadata for bundled model role, version, asset path, and input/output contract.

## Proposed behavior
Add or refine model manifest metadata so each local model role can be identified and validated consistently.

## Goal to reach
The app and tests can read model metadata that explains what model asset is bundled and what contract it supports.

## Minimal scope
- Define manifest fields for model role, version, asset path, runtime, and contract version.
- Validate the manifest in a focused unit test.
- Document the manifest fields.
- Keep compatibility with the current LiteRT command-router path.

## Out of scope
- Training or replacing model assets.
- Supporting every future runtime immediately.
- UI benchmark screens.

## User workflow
A maintainer can inspect the bundled local model metadata and know what model is active.

## Local-first impact
This makes local model deployment auditable and versioned inside the app package.

## Safety and security considerations
Manifest data should be local static metadata and must not fetch remote assets.

## Alternatives considered
Hard-coded asset assumptions will become brittle as more local model roles are added.

problems.title: Feature: add screen understanding cards
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
TouchPilot already has local screen summaries and suggested actions, but they are not surfaced as clear product UI cards. Users need to see what the app understood before trusting suggested actions.

## Proposed behavior
Add visible screen-understanding cards that present the current screen summary and suggested actions from existing local ScreenContext/Summary logic.

## Goal to reach
When the user asks about the current screen or opens the relevant UI surface, TouchPilot shows a clear card with what it sees and useful local actions.

## Minimal scope
- Reuse existing ScreenContext and ScreenSummary logic.
- Show summary text in a card.
- Show a small capped list of suggested actions.
- Keep suggestions descriptive unless the user explicitly chooses/runs one.
- Handle empty or weak context with a clear local-only fallback message.

## Out of scope
- New model training.
- New Android control tools.
- OCR/VLM implementation.
- Replacing existing chat/tool execution cards.

## User workflow
A user can ask what is on screen and see a structured local summary plus safe suggested next actions.

## Local-first impact
This makes existing local screen understanding visible without cloud inference.

## Safety and security considerations
Cards must use redacted/display-safe screen text and must not expose sensitive fields.

problems.title: Feature: add local model evaluation runner
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
After fixtures exist, TouchPilot needs a repeatable way to evaluate local model outputs without relying on manual review.

## Proposed behavior
Add a small evaluation runner that reads the committed fixtures and reports pass/fail counts for deterministic expectations.

## Goal to reach
A developer can run one command and see whether local model routing contracts still pass the minimal eval set.

## Minimal scope
- Read the fixture format added for Milestone 8.
- Evaluate current deterministic/local-model command output where supported.
- Print total cases, passed cases, failed cases, and failure details.
- Add a focused test or Gradle task hook if it fits the existing test style.

## Out of scope
- Training models.
- Accuracy dashboards.
- Device/emulator live tests.
- UI reporting.

## User workflow
A maintainer runs the eval before and after model/router changes to compare behavior.

## Local-first impact
This makes local model quality measurable inside the repository.

## Safety and security considerations
The runner must not call network services or execute Android actions. It should evaluate outputs only.

## Alternatives considered
Manual spot checks are too inconsistent for model-quality work.

problems.title: Feature: improve command routing model baseline
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
The current LiteRT command router is a proof baseline. Milestone 8 needs a small quality improvement that can be measured against fixtures/evals.

## Proposed behavior
Improve the command routing baseline for a narrow set of supported commands while preserving deterministic fallback behavior.

## Goal to reach
The eval runner shows improved or at least non-regressed routing results for supported command-routing cases.

## Minimal scope
- Focus only on command routing, not target ranking or screen summaries.
- Improve handling for simple supported commands such as open app, tap text, back, home, and scroll.
- Keep existing deterministic router fallback intact.
- Update model metadata or docs if the bundled model asset changes.

## Out of scope
- Multi-step planning.
- Cloud model fallback.
- New Android tools.
- UI redesign.

## User workflow
When a user gives a simple command, local routing should pick the expected tool more consistently.

## Local-first impact
This makes the on-device command route more useful without making basic control depend on it.

## Safety and security considerations
The router may suggest tools, but execution must still go through validation, skill allowlists, approvals, and policy.

## Alternatives considered
Keeping only the proof model blocks meaningful local-model quality measurement.

problems.title: Feature: add skill-use cards to agent runs
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
TouchPilot has active skills, skill detail UI, skill-aware prompts, and allowlists, but agent runs do not clearly show why a skill is active or what it permits during the run.

## Proposed behavior
Add a compact skill-use card in the chat/run flow when an agent run uses an active or matched skill.

## Goal to reach
During a skill-scoped run, the user can see the skill name, risk, allowed-tool scope, and why the skill is involved.

## Minimal scope
- Show skill title and risk.
- Show a concise allowed-tool count or short allowed-tool list.
- Show whether the skill was manually active or matched from the request.
- Link/tap through to existing skill detail UI if practical.
- Keep the card display-only; do not change skill selection logic.

## Out of scope
- New skill matching behavior.
- New skill metadata fields.
- Skill enable/disable controls.
- Policy engine changes.

## User workflow
A user starts a skill-scoped task and sees which skill is guiding the agent before or during tool execution.

## Local-first impact
This makes local skill context inspectable and easier to trust.

## Safety and security considerations
The card should reinforce that skill allowlists scope tools, but policy and approvals still decide execution.

problems.title: Feature: improve local and offline runtime indicators
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
TouchPilot has local router/model status text, but the product UI does not strongly communicate when work is local-only, when LiteRT is available, or when deterministic fallback is active.

## Proposed behavior
Improve runtime indicators across Chat and Settings so users can understand the current local/offline execution mode at a glance.

## Goal to reach
The user can tell whether TouchPilot is using local router, local model, fallback mode, and whether cloud services are involved.

## Minimal scope
- Improve the existing Chat runtime/skill strip or equivalent status surface.
- Improve Settings runtime status copy/card.
- Clearly show local router vs local model availability.
- Clearly show local-only/no-cloud behavior for core runtime.
- Reuse existing LocalModelStatus and AgentProviderMode data.

## Out of scope
- New runtime backends.
- Benchmark UI from Milestone 8.
- Cloud provider redesign.
- Model training or model asset changes.

## User workflow
A user opens Chat or Settings and can immediately understand the active runtime mode and locality.

## Local-first impact
This supports user trust by making local-first operation visible.

## Safety and security considerations
Runtime indicators should not claim cloud is impossible for optional integrations; they should distinguish core local runtime from separately configured integrations.

problems.title: Feature: polish in-app trace and run review UI
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
TouchPilot has logs, run detail, and trace export, but run review still needs a clearer product UI for understanding what happened during a task.

## Proposed behavior
Polish the in-app run review experience so users can inspect steps, tool results, policy decisions, failures, and exported trace context more easily.

## Goal to reach
After an agent run, the user can open one in-app review screen and understand the run timeline, important tool outcomes, and any blocked/failed policy decisions.

## Minimal scope
- Improve run detail layout using existing AgentRunRecord data.
- Highlight failed, blocked, approval, and completed steps clearly.
- Show concise tool result/policy details without raw sensitive data.
- Keep existing export trace action available.
- Add empty/error states for missing run data.

## Out of scope
- New log database schema unless unavoidable.
- Full trace file viewer/editor.
- New agent event types.
- Live automation replay.

## User workflow
A user taps a completed run summary and reviews what happened without needing to inspect exported text files first.

## Local-first impact
This makes local agent execution auditable inside the app.

## Safety and security considerations
All displayed trace details must use existing redaction/display-safe formatting.

problems.title: Feature: capture successful agent run traces as workflow recordings
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

When an agent run completes successfully, the full sequence of observed screens, decisions, and tool calls is discarded. There is no way to replay or reuse what worked.

## Proposed behavior

After a successful run, the agent serializes the trace — the sequence of observe/decide/act steps, tool calls, arguments, and verification results — into a structured local `WorkflowTrace` record that can serve as the raw input for a workflow definition.

## Goal to reach

A completed agent run produces a capturable trace that downstream workflow tooling can consume.

## Minimal scope

- Define a `WorkflowTrace` data model covering steps, tool calls, arguments, screen context signals, and verification outcomes.
- Serialize the trace at run completion (in the existing `AgentRunResult` or a parallel record).
- Store it locally in-memory for the session; SQLite persistence can follow.
- Redact sensitive screen text at capture time using the existing `SensitiveTextRedactor`.
- Emit a `TraceRecorded` agent event so the chat stream can surface it.

## Out of scope

- Replay engine.
- Workflow parameterization.
- Workflow review UI.
- Cross-session persistence (follow-on).

## User workflow

A user completes a task; the system captures what happened internally and signals that a workflow can be saved from this run.

## Local-first impact

All trace data stays on device. No cloud upload or sync is involved.

## Safety and security considerations

Sensitive screen text and typed arguments must be redacted at capture time, not at display time, so raw secrets never enter the stored trace.

problems.title: Feature: add per-step state verification in workflow replay
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Replay fires tool calls without confirming each step landed in the expected state before continuing. A missed tap or a wrong screen will silently cause all subsequent steps to act on the wrong context.

## Proposed behavior

After each tool call in a workflow replay, verify that the expected screen state described in the workflow definition is reached before proceeding to the next step. Abort replay and emit a failure event if verification does not pass within the step timeout.

## Goal to reach

Workflow replay stops at the first unverified step rather than continuing blindly into bad state.

## Minimal scope

- Evaluate each step's `expectedState` predicate using the existing `waitForText` / `isKeyboardVisible` / `observeScreenContext` primitives.
- Emit a verification-passed or verification-failed event per step.
- On failure: abort the remaining steps, surface a clear failure event with the expected vs observed context, and leave the device in whatever state the last tool left it.
- Respect the step-level timeout from the workflow definition; fall back to a sensible default.

## Out of scope

- Automatic repair or retry flows.
- Fuzzy/semantic state matching (use exact text or element presence for now).

## User workflow

A replay reaches a step where the expected screen text is not present; the user sees a verification-failed card explaining what was expected and what was observed.

## Local-first impact

Verification uses on-device Accessibility data exclusively via the existing `TouchPilotAccessibilityService`.

## Safety and security considerations

Verification failures must abort replay rather than continuing. Proceeding past an unverified step could execute destructive actions on the wrong screen.

problems.title: Feature: add deterministic workflow replay engine
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Captured workflow definitions have no execution path. There is no way to replay a saved workflow on a real device.

## Proposed behavior

A `WorkflowReplayEngine` takes a `WorkflowDefinition`, executes each step through the existing `AndroidToolExecutor`, and reports progress as agent events in the existing chat event stream.

## Goal to reach

A workflow can be replayed end-to-end and its progress is visible in the same step-based event stream as a live agent run.

## Minimal scope

- `WorkflowReplayEngine` iterates steps and dispatches each through `AndroidToolExecutor.execute()`.
- Stop on tool failure and surface a clear error event.
- Emit step-started / step-completed / replay-done events into the `AgentEvent` stream.
- Expose a `replayWorkflow(definition)` entry point from `LocalReasoningCore` or `AgentRunner`.
- Basic parameter substitution: fill parameter slots from a supplied argument map.

## Out of scope

- Per-step verification (separate issue).
- Policy integration (separate issue).
- Repair/retry flows.

## User workflow

A user triggers a known workflow and watches each step execute in the chat view, with the same tool-call cards as a live run.

## Local-first impact

All execution goes through the existing on-device `AndroidToolExecutor`. No cloud dependency added.

## Safety and security considerations

Every tool call must still pass through `AndroidToolExecutor.execute()` so the existing policy path is not bypassed, even in replay mode.

problems.title: Feature: define workflow file format with parameters and expected states
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

There is no structure for expressing a repeatable local workflow. A raw trace is a recording of what happened; a workflow needs to be a portable, parameterized, human-readable description of what should happen.

## Proposed behavior

Define a workflow file schema (JSON or Markdown front matter + steps) that captures the step sequence, expected intermediate screen states, parameterized value slots, and per-step policy requirements. Add a parser and serializer so the replay engine and trace-capture path share the same model.

## Goal to reach

A serializable, inspectable workflow file can represent a successful trace as a replayable workflow, and a developer can author one by hand.

## Minimal scope

- Design the schema: steps, tool name + arguments, expected state predicates (screen text, element presence), parameter slots, and optional skill/tool scope.
- Add `WorkflowDefinition` data class and a parser from JSON.
- Add a serializer so a `WorkflowTrace` can be converted into a `WorkflowDefinition`.
- Write schema documentation (add to `docs/`).

## Out of scope

- Replay engine.
- Capture path (separate issue).
- UI.

## User workflow

A developer inspects a saved workflow file and understands every step without needing to read source code.

## Local-first impact

Workflow files live entirely on device. The schema should be simple enough to hand-edit.

## Safety and security considerations

The schema must support expressing per-step policy requirements so the replay engine knows which steps need approval before execution.

problems.title: feat: expand redaction for logs and traces

problems.title: Feature: Add versioned plugin API manifest
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
Local extension tooling has no stable, versioned manifest, so plugin/runtime compatibility is ambiguous and version drift causes confusing runtime failures.

## Proposed behavior
Introduce a stable API manifest with semver for local extension tooling, enforce required fields and feature flags, and fail fast on unsupported versions with actionable guidance.

## User workflow
1. Extension author declares API version and required fields in the manifest.
2. On load, runtime checks compatibility deterministically.
3. If incompatible, runtime shows a clear error with the recommended action.

## Local-first impact
Local extensions get reproducible load behavior without depending on remote registries.

## Safety and security considerations
- Manifest must be validated locally to avoid pulling untrusted metadata.
- Feature flags must not silently enable privileged capabilities.

## Alternatives considered
- Free-form JSON with no schema: fragile, frequent breakage.
- Importer-only version check: too late, after install.

problems.title: Feature: separate MCP and local extension permissions with audit
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
MCP and local extension permissions are conflated with Android tool permissions, and their use is not easy to audit after the fact.

## Proposed behavior
Add explicit MCP and local extension permissions separate from Android tool permissions. Expand audit logs so every external capability invocation is recorded with action, target, parameters (redacted), and policy decision.

## User workflow
1. User installs an MCP server or local extension.
2. Reviews its permissions separately from Android tools.
3. Later inspects the audit log to see exactly what it did.

## Local-first impact
Permissions and audit logs are local.

## Safety and security considerations
- MCP and extension permissions must default to deny.
- Audit log must redact secrets in parameters.

## Alternatives considered
- Single permission surface: hides distinct trust boundaries.
- Cloud-based audit: violates local-first.

problems.title: Feature: Use page lists individual skills with example prompts
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
The Use page surfaces skill packs, but individual skills are not directly discoverable, and users cannot see example prompts to understand what each skill does.

## Proposed behavior
Surface individual skills on the Use page with example prompts, scope summary, and required permissions. Keep the page focused on discoverability of "what can I do here?" rather than pack-level management.

## User workflow
1. User opens the Use page.
2. Browses individual skills with example prompts.
3. Taps a skill card to start a run.

## Local-first impact
All examples are bundled with the app and skill files.

## Safety and security considerations
- Risk level and tool allowlist must be visible on each skill card.
- Example prompts must not require special permissions to display.

## Alternatives considered
- Pack-only listing: hides individual skill value.
- Long markdown index only: poor discoverability.

problems.title: Feature: skill cards as runnable entry points into chat
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
Users can read about skills but there is no direct entry point from a skill card into actually running it; the path to activation is unclear.

## Proposed behavior
Make each skill card on the Use page a runnable entry point. Tapping it activates the skill, optionally prefills a starter prompt, and takes the user into the chat with the skill active.

## User workflow
1. User taps a skill card on the Use page.
2. Skill is activated and a starter prompt is prefilled (or chat opens with the skill active).
3. User runs the skill in context.

## Local-first impact
Activation is local and immediate; no remote skill state.

## Safety and security considerations
- Activation must respect skill risk and tool allowlists.
- User must see that a skill is active in the chat header.

## Alternatives considered
- Manual skill enable from settings then chat: high friction.
- Deep-link only into chat: no skill context.

Let users demonstrate a task once and convert it into an inspectable local skill.

problems.title: Feature: freeze stable architecture and local model/tool/skill/workflow contracts
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
The architecture, tool, skill, workflow, and policy contracts have evolved through milestones 1–14 but have not been formally frozen and versioned. Without a stable contract surface, the 1.0 release cannot guarantee backward compatibility.

## Proposed behavior
Audit and freeze all contracts: tool API, skill SKILL.md schema, workflow schema, policy rule format, model manifest, and memory entry schema. Document each contract version with a changelog. Mark any remaining unstable fields as experimental or remove them before 1.0.

## User workflow
1. Maintainer runs the contract audit checklist.
2. Each contract is versioned and documented.
3. Release notes list the frozen contract versions and any breaking changes since M14.

## Local-first impact
All frozen contracts ship with the app; version validation is local.

## Safety and security considerations
- Policy contract freeze must not silently widen permissions.
- Experimental contracts must be clearly flagged.

## Alternatives considered
- Continue evolving past 1.0 without freezing: breaks external tool/skill authors.
- Freeze everything: blocks necessary iteration; experimental marker solves this.

problems.title: Feature: capture completed agent runs into workflow definitions
problems.issue_body:
## Problem
Successful agent runs are not captured into reusable workflows, so users repeat the same multi-step tasks manually each time.

## Proposed behavior
After a successful agent run, offer to capture it as a workflow definition with parameters, expected states, and step order. Provide a workflow editor to review and refine before saving.

## User workflow
1. User completes a task successfully.
2. App offers "Save as workflow" with suggested parameters.
3. User reviews, edits parameters and expected states, and saves.

## Local-first impact
Workflow definitions are stored locally; export/import is user-initiated.

## Safety and security considerations
- Captured workflows must respect existing policy decisions per step.
- Editor must warn if any step is sensitive.

## Alternatives considered
- Manual workflow authoring only: high friction.
- Auto-capture without review: risks saving broken or unsafe runs.

problems.title: Bug: IntentGate routes `press back` / `press home` to `tap` instead of system navigation
problems.issue_body:
### What happened?


`IntentGate.detectExactCommand` evaluates `TapPattern` before the bare navigation routes. `TapPattern` accepts both `tap` and `press`:

```kotlin
val TapPattern: Regex = Regex("(?:tap|press)\\s+([\\w .-]+)")
```

For common navigation phrasing, the gate captures the navigation word as a **tap target** instead of invoking the system back/home tools:

| User says | Current route | Expected |
|-----------|---------------|----------|
| `Go back` | `press_back` ✓ | `press_back` |
| `press back` | `tap {text: "back"}` ✗ | `press_back` |
| `press home` | `tap {text: "home"}` ✗ | `press_home` |

`press back` tries to tap a visible label named “back” (accessibility `tap`), not the Android system **Back** gesture. On many screens there is no such label, so the action fails; on others it triggers the wrong in-app control instead of system navigation.

Tests cover `Go back` and `tap back arrow`, but not `press back` / `press home`.

This is distinct from closed [#146](https://github.com/touchpilot/touchpilot/issues/146), which fixed `open`/`tap` losing to bare `back`/`home` **inside targets** (e.g. `tap home shortcut`).


### Expected behavior


- `press back` and `press home` route to `press_back` / `press_home` with empty args.
- `tap back arrow`, `tap home shortcut`, and `press OK` continue to route to `tap` with the captured target text.
- Bare `back` / `home` word-boundary routes (`Go back`, `go home`) remain unchanged.


### Steps to reproduce


1. From the project root, run:

```bash
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest --tests dev.touchpilot.app.agent.IntentGateTest
```

2. Add a temporary assertion (or run mentally against `main`):

```kotlin
val command = gate.classify("press back") as IntentDecision.ExactCommand
// main: tool == "tap", args["text"] == "back"
// expected: tool == "press_back", args.isEmpty()
```

3. On device: enable AccessibilityService, open chat, send `press back`. Observe the agent attempts `tap(text=back)` instead of system back.


### Device or emulator

TouchPilot_API_35

### Android version

15 / API 35

### TouchPilot commit

_No response_

### Accessibility service enabled?

Yes

### Areas involved

- [x] Android control
- [x] Agent loop
- [ ] Local router / local inference
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] MCP
- [ ] Security / approvals
- [ ] UI

problems.title: refactor: define local reasoning core boundary
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Milestone 2 needs a clean local reasoning core boundary. The app should clearly separate UI state, local command production, tool routing, policy checks, and Android execution.

Without this boundary, local model work, deterministic routing, skills, and safety policy will become tightly coupled and hard to test.

## Proposed behavior

Define and implement the local reasoning core boundary:

```text
user request + context
  -> local reasoning core
  -> agent events and/or structured tool request
  -> tool router + policy
  -> Android tool execution
```

This should be an architecture cleanup with minimal behavior change.

## User workflow

Existing flows such as `Hello`, `Help`, `Open Settings`, and `Go back` should continue working, but internally they should pass through a clearer runtime boundary.

## Local-first impact

This keeps the core product independent from cloud providers and makes local command routing, local model reasoning, skills, and policy pluggable behind one local runtime boundary.

## Safety and security considerations

The reasoning core must not execute tools directly. Tool execution must continue to go through validation, skill allowlists, policy, approvals, and logs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Define the local reasoning core interface or module boundary.
- [ ] UI does not directly own command production or Android tool execution.
- [ ] Local router output can pass through the reasoning core boundary.
- [ ] Tool execution remains behind tool router and policy checks.
- [ ] Existing core flows still work.
- [ ] Add focused unit tests for the boundary where practical.

problems.title: test: add offline validation checklist and tests
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Milestone 2 needs offline validation to prove the hybrid local core works without cloud models or hosted routing.

The milestone should not be considered complete until representative local-only flows pass.

## Proposed behavior

Add an offline validation checklist and tests for Milestone 2 flows:

- `Hello`
- `Help`
- `Open Settings`
- `Go back`
- one ambiguous request routed through the local-model-needed path

Validation should confirm intent gate behavior, event emission, deterministic fallback, and policy/tool routing where applicable.

## User workflow

A developer or tester should be able to run the app offline and validate the key Milestone 2 flows without configuring a cloud provider, API key, or backend service.

## Local-first impact

This proves the product direction: TouchPilot's core agent behavior works locally.

## Safety and security considerations

Offline validation should include at least one blocked or approval-related event path if practical, to confirm local policy remains active.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a Milestone 2 offline validation checklist.
- [ ] Validate `Hello` locally.
- [ ] Validate `Help` locally.
- [ ] Validate `Open Settings` locally.
- [ ] Validate `Go back` locally.
- [ ] Validate one ambiguous local-model-needed request.
- [ ] Confirm each flow emits expected agent events.
- [ ] Confirm no cloud provider/API key/backend is required.
- [ ] Add automated tests where practical and document any manual live-test steps.

problems.title: feature: add intent gate for local routing
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Milestone 2 needs an intent gate so TouchPilot does not ask the local model to solve every request. Small local models are limited, so exact commands, known skills, unsafe requests, and clarification cases should be routed deterministically first.

## Proposed behavior

Add an intent gate that classifies incoming user requests into:

- exact deterministic command
- known skill request
- unsafe or blocked request
- local-model-needed request
- clarification needed

The intent gate should run before local model reasoning.

## User workflow

Examples:

- `Hello` -> deterministic final answer
- `Help` -> deterministic/help skill response
- `Go back` -> exact command
- `Open Settings` -> exact command or known skill
- `Send this payment` -> unsafe or approval-required path
- `Do the thing I usually do here` -> clarification or local-model-needed path

## Local-first impact

The intent gate makes the local AI architecture practical. It uses deterministic logic where correctness matters and reserves local model reasoning for ambiguity.

## Safety and security considerations

Unsafe requests should be detected before tool execution. The intent gate should never approve risky actions by itself; it should only route to policy, clarification, or blocked outcomes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add an intent gate component.
- [ ] Route exact commands without invoking a local model.
- [ ] Route known skill candidates separately from exact commands.
- [ ] Route unsafe or unclear requests to policy/clarification paths.
- [ ] Route ambiguous requests to local-model-needed path.
- [ ] Unit tests cover representative routing decisions.

problems.title: feature: define OCR fallback boundary for weak screens
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #38

## Problem

Some Android screens expose weak or incomplete Accessibility data. TouchPilot needs a planned fallback boundary for OCR, without making OCR or local VLM required for Milestone 3 completion.

The project should know when Accessibility context is weak and how future OCR/VLM fallback will plug in.

## Proposed behavior

Add weak-tree detection and define the OCR fallback boundary:

```text
Accessibility observation
  -> screen context builder
  -> context quality check
  -> strong context: summarize/suggest directly
  -> weak context: mark OCR fallback needed
```

Milestone 3 can implement the interface/detection first. OCR execution can be added when the local OCR runtime is selected.

## User workflow

When TouchPilot cannot understand enough from Accessibility data, it should respond honestly:

```text
I can see this screen, but the app exposes limited readable UI data. OCR support is needed for better understanding here.
```

## Local-first impact

This keeps the primary path local and deterministic while preparing for future local OCR/VLM support.

## Safety and security considerations

- OCR output should be treated as untrusted and noisy.
- OCR text may include sensitive content and must go through redaction before logging.
- Weak context should not cause unsafe guessing or blind tapping.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add context quality or weak-tree detection logic.
- [ ] Define an OCR fallback interface/boundary or placeholder result type.
- [ ] Mark local VLM as future fallback, not a Milestone 3 dependency.
- [ ] Weak context produces conservative summary/suggestion behavior.
- [ ] Tests cover strong context, weak context, and empty context.
- [ ] Documentation or comments explain that OCR/VLM fallback remains local-only.

## References

- Parent issue: #38
- `docs/LOCAL_INFERENCE.md`
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`

problems.title: feature: define screen context model
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #38

## Problem

Milestone 3 needs a stable screen context model before TouchPilot can summarize screens, suggest actions, or feed useful local context into the reasoning core and future local models.

Current Android observation data is useful for debugging and tool execution, but it needs a normalized product-facing shape that is safe, testable, and independent from raw Accessibility implementation details.

## Proposed behavior

Define a structured screen context model that represents the current Android screen with enough information for local reasoning:

- current app label and package name when available
- screen/window title when available
- visible text
- clickable nodes
- input fields
- scrollable containers or scroll state
- node bounds
- enabled/focused/checked/clickable state
- stable node identifiers when available
- redaction-aware text fields

The model should be usable by:

- deterministic screen summaries
- suggested actions
- local model input contracts
- trace/log export
- future OCR/VLM fallback layers

## User workflow

When TouchPilot observes a screen, the runtime should be able to convert raw screen data into a stable context object before any summary or action suggestion is generated.

Example flow:

```text
Accessibility tree
  -> ScreenContext
  -> summary / suggested actions / local model input
```

## Local-first impact

A stable screen context model keeps screen understanding local and reusable. It lets TouchPilot improve local models later without changing the Android control layer or UI.

## Safety and security considerations

- Screen context may include sensitive text.
- Sensitive text fields should be marked or redacted before logs/traces.
- Raw Accessibility data should not be exposed directly to user-visible summaries without filtering.
- The model should support policy decisions later, such as sensitive app or sensitive field detection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a stable screen context data model.
- [ ] Model includes app/package, visible text, clickable nodes, input fields, bounds, and state flags where available.
- [ ] Model distinguishes raw text from redaction-safe display/log text where practical.
- [ ] Model is independent from UI components.
- [ ] Model can be used as input to local reasoning/model contracts.
- [ ] Unit tests cover construction of representative screen context objects.
- [ ] Documentation or code comments explain the role of the model boundary.

## References

- Parent issue: #38
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` Milestone 3
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`

problems.title: feature: build screen context from accessibility tree
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #38

## Problem

After defining the screen context model, TouchPilot needs a reliable builder that converts Android Accessibility observations into that model.

Raw Accessibility trees are noisy and inconsistent. The builder should normalize data into a smaller, useful context for local reasoning and suggested actions.

## Proposed behavior

Implement an Accessibility-to-screen-context builder:

```text
Accessibility observation
  -> normalize nodes
  -> extract visible text
  -> extract clickable targets
  -> extract input fields
  -> extract bounds/state
  -> produce ScreenContext
```

The builder should keep raw observation details available for debugging, but the reasoning core should use the normalized context.

## User workflow

When the user asks `What can you do here?`, TouchPilot should first build screen context from the active Android screen and then generate a local summary or suggestions from that context.

## Local-first impact

This is the primary screen-understanding path. It avoids requiring screenshot vision models for normal Android screens.

## Safety and security considerations

- Builder output should remain compatible with log redaction.
- Sensitive fields such as passwords, tokens, messages, and account data should be marked or redacted where possible.
- The builder should not create executable actions directly; it should only produce context.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Build screen context from current Accessibility observation data.
- [ ] Extract visible text nodes.
- [ ] Extract clickable targets with bounds and stable identifiers when available.
- [ ] Extract input fields and basic state.
- [ ] Extract scrollable state where available.
- [ ] Keep raw observation and normalized context separate.
- [ ] Add tests with fake/sample Accessibility data.
- [ ] Existing observe/tool behavior remains compatible.

## References

- Parent issue: #38
- Depends on: screen context model issue
- `docs/TOOL_SPEC.md`
- `docs/LIVE_TESTING.md`

problems.title: feature: hybrid local AI core (Milestone 2)
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Milestone 1 proved the local-first foundation, but TouchPilot still behaves mostly like a deterministic command router with a local model runtime path. Milestone 2 should turn the foundation into a real 100% local hybrid AI core.

The goal is not to make one small local model do everything. The goal is to combine deterministic routing, local model reasoning, skills, safety policy, and agent events into one clean runtime boundary.

## Proposed behavior

Implement the Hybrid Local AI Core:

```text
user message
    │
    ▼
┌────────────┐   ┌────────────┐   ┌──────────────┐
│ Intent     │ → │ Reasoning  │ → │ Agent Event  │
│ Gate       │   │ Core       │   │ Stream       │
└────────────┘   └─────┬──────┘   └──────┬───────┘
                       │                 │
      exact commands ◄─┼─► local model   ▼
      skill match      │          tool running / success /
      safety precheck  │          failure / approval / final
                       ▼
              deterministic fallback
```

Milestone 2 is complete when TouchPilot can route simple requests deterministically, use a local model path for ambiguous requests, and expose all work as local agent events.

## User workflow

A user sends a request such as:

- `Hello`
- `Help`
- `Open Settings`
- `Go back`
- `Open Wi-Fi settings`
- `What can you do on this screen?`

TouchPilot should:

1. Build local request context.
2. Run an intent gate.
3. Choose one of:
   - exact deterministic command
   - known skill match
   - local model reasoning path
   - clarification / blocked response
4. Emit structured agent events for the UI.
5. Route any tool request through validation, skill allowlists, and policy.
6. Return a final response or visible tool result.

## Required features and fixes

- Define a local reasoning core boundary separate from UI and Android tool execution.
- Add an intent gate for exact commands, known skills, unsafe requests, and model-needed requests.
- Remove cloud/provider fallback from the normal product path.
- Define local model input/output contracts for:
  - intent classification
  - tool selection
  - argument extraction
  - target ranking
  - final answer
- Build shared agent event types for:
  - user message
  - assistant message
  - tool requested
  - tool running
  - tool succeeded
  - tool failed
  - approval required
  - blocked by policy
  - final answer
- Keep deterministic router as fallback and test baseline.
- Ensure local model outputs are treated as untrusted and still pass through tool validation, skill allowlists, policy, and logging.
- Add offline-only validation for the main Milestone 2 flows.
- Add focused tests for routing decisions and event emission.

## Local-first impact

This milestone removes cloud/provider thinking from the core product path and makes TouchPilot's intelligence local by design:

```text
local deterministic router
  + local model reasoning
  + local skills
  + local policy
  + local logs
  = hybrid local Android AI core
``…

problems.title: feature: add local screen summary and suggested actions
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #38

## Problem

TouchPilot needs a visible local AI feature from screen context: it should be able to summarize the current screen and suggest useful actions without cloud inference.

This should start deterministic and context-driven. A local model hook can be added later, but Milestone 3 should not depend on a VLM or cloud model.

## Proposed behavior

Add local screen summary and suggested action generation from `ScreenContext`:

```text
ScreenContext
  -> screen summary
  -> suggested actions
  -> agent/UI event output
```

Example output:

```text
I see the Settings screen. Visible actions include Network & internet, Connected devices, Apps, Notifications, and Battery. I can open one of these sections, scroll, or go back.
```

Suggested actions should map to existing safe tool concepts where possible:

- tap visible item
- type into visible input
- scroll
- go back
- open app-specific visible section

## User workflow

User asks:

- `What screen am I on?`
- `What can you do here?`
- `What buttons are visible?`
- `Suggest actions for this screen`

TouchPilot replies locally using the current screen context.

## Local-first impact

This makes TouchPilot feel like a real local AI assistant while still using deterministic, inspectable local logic first.

## Safety and security considerations

- Summaries should avoid exposing sensitive details from password fields, private messages, tokens, or account screens.
- Suggested actions are not execution approval. Any selected action must still go through validation and policy.
- Suggestions should be conservative on sensitive screens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add local screen summary generation from screen context.
- [ ] Add suggested action generation from visible controls.
- [ ] Suggested actions reference existing tool concepts without executing automatically.
- [ ] UI or agent event path can display the summary and suggestions.
- [ ] Sensitive text is redacted or avoided in summaries where practical.
- [ ] Tests cover Settings-like screen, launcher-like screen, input-field screen, and empty/weak context.
- [ ] No cloud model/backend is required.

## References

- Parent issue: #38
- Depends on: screen context model and builder issues
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` Milestone 3

problems.title: test: add offline screen understanding validation
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #38

## Problem

Milestone 3 should not be considered complete until screen understanding works offline on representative screens and produces expected summaries, suggestions, and redacted logs.

## Proposed behavior

Add Milestone 3 offline validation covering screen context and understanding:

- TouchPilot screen
- Android Settings screen
- Launcher screen
- input-field screen
- weak/limited Accessibility screen if available

Validation should confirm:

- screen context is built locally
- summary is generated locally
- suggested actions are generated locally
- no cloud/backend is required
- sensitive text remains redacted in logs/traces

## User workflow

A tester should be able to run TouchPilot on emulator or real device, open common screens, ask what TouchPilot sees, and verify that the app responds with local summaries and possible actions.

## Local-first impact

This proves Milestone 3's core claim: TouchPilot can understand Android screens locally without relying on cloud vision/chat models.

## Safety and security considerations

- Include at least one text-entry or sensitive-looking screen in validation to confirm redaction behavior.
- Suggested actions should not execute automatically during validation unless explicitly selected.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a Milestone 3 offline validation checklist.
- [ ] Validate TouchPilot screen context.
- [ ] Validate Android Settings screen context.
- [ ] Validate launcher screen context.
- [ ] Validate an input-field screen.
- [ ] Validate weak/limited Accessibility behavior where practical.
- [ ] Confirm summaries and suggestions require no cloud/backend.

- [ ] Add automated tests where practical and document manual live-test steps.
