problems.title: Bug: Tools, MCP, and Logs tabs share a single `outputText` field, leaking tool results into unrelated section cards
problems.issue_body:
### What happened?

The MCP tab's "MCP result" card and the Logs tab's "Latest result" card display the output of the *most recent operation from any of the three tabs*, not the most recent operation from that tab.

The cause is a single `private var outputText: String` on `MainActivity` ([MainActivity.kt:733](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L733)):

```kotlin
private var outputText: String = "No result yet."
```

This same field is written from three places:

- `executeAndRender` on the **Tools** tab ([MainActivity.kt:737](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L737))
- Every **MCP** button click handler — List Tools, Call Tool, success and failure branches ([MainActivity.kt:640](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L640), [L664](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L664), [L677](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L677), [L688](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L688))
- The **Logs** tab's "Export Debug Trace" button ([MainActivity.kt:707](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L707))

…and read from three different cards:

- Tools — `timelineCard("Latest result", outputText)` ([MainActivity.kt:616](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L616))
- MCP — `timelineCard("MCP result", outputText)` ([MainActivity.kt:699](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L699))
- Logs — `timelineCard("Latest result", outputText)` ([MainActivity.kt:711](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/MainActivity.kt#L711))

Because every `showSection(...)` call wipes the view tree and re-runs the render function, the card always shows the **current global** `outputText`, regardless of which tab produced it.

Concrete leak directions observed on the running build:

1. **Tools → MCP / Logs**: Tapping `Observe Current Screen` on the Tools tab stores the snapshot result in `outputText`. Switching to the MCP tab shows `MCP result: observe_screen({}) -> false: TouchPilot Control is not enabled.`, and Logs shows the same string under `Latest result`. The user has no way to tell that the message originated in Tools and is unrelated to MCP.
2. **MCP → Tools / Logs**: Tapping `Call Tool` against an unreachable endpoint produces `MCP call failed: failed to connect to /10.0.2.2 (port 8000) ...`. Switching to Tools shows that same MCP-flavoured error under `Latest result`, suggesting the most recent tool execution failed when no tool was executed.
3. **Logs → Tools / MCP**: Tapping `Export Debug Trace` writes the export path into `outputText`. Switching to MCP shows `Debug trace exported: /storage/.../touchpilot-trace-...txt` under `MCP result`, which is nonsensical in MCP context.

The `ToolExecutionLog` shown lower on the Logs tab is correctly siloed — only the "Latest result" card leaks — which makes the bug particularly confusing: the user sees one card claiming `observe_screen(...)` was just run, while the audit-log card below correctly sho…

problems.title: Bug: `SensitiveTextRedactor` mangles `Authorization: Bearer` headers and its greedy token regex eats surrounding structu
problems.issue_body:
### What happened?

[`SensitiveTextRedactor.redact(text: String)`](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/security/SensitiveTextRedactor.kt#L15-L27) contains **two distinct bugs** that fire together whenever an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` substring is redacted as part of a larger log line — which is the exact case for tool-execution log strings written by `executeAndRender` and surfaced on the Tools tab and in `Export Debug Trace`.

### Bug A — `Authorization` header structure is destroyed

The second assignment pattern uses `(?i)(authorization:\s*bearer\s+)[^\s,;]+` and shares the same replacement lambda as the first pattern:

```kotlin
redacted = pattern.replace(redacted) { match ->
    val prefix = match.value.substringBeforeAny(listOf(":", "="))
    "$prefix=[REDACTED]"
}
```

For input `Authorization: Bearer abc123xyz`:

- `match.value` = `Authorization: Bearer abc123xyz`
- `substringBeforeAny(listOf(":", "="))` returns `Authorization` (split at the first `:`)
- replacement = `Authorization=[REDACTED]`

The output is `Authorization=[REDACTED]`. The `Bearer` keyword is dropped, and the HTTP-header `:` is rewritten to an assignment `=`. The first capture group (`(authorization:\s*bearer\s+)`) is captured but never used — the regex is written as if a `"$1[REDACTED]"`-style replacement were intended, and that is presumably the original intent.

### Bug B — the greedy `[^\s,;]+` token consumes trailing `}`, `)`, `]`, `>` etc.

`[^\s,;]+` is greedy and only excludes whitespace, comma, and semicolon. Closing brackets, parentheses, angle brackets, quotes, and any other structural character get eaten as part of the "token" and replaced along with the secret.

Concretely, the tool-execution log string produced by `MainActivity.executeAndRender` for a `type_text` call with `text=Authorization: Bearer abc123xyz` is:

```
type_text({text=Authorization: Bearer abc123xyz}) -> false: typeIntoFocusedField
```

After redaction, the actual output is:

```
type_text({text=Authorization=[REDACTED] -> false: typeIntoFocusedField
```

The `})` that closes the args dict and the tool-call parenthesis is **gone** — the regex matched `Authorization: Bearer abc123xyz})` (eating the closing `})`) and replaced the whole match with `Authorization=[REDACTED]`, throwing the brackets away.

Same class of structural damage happens with:

- `password=secret123}` inside an args dict — `password=[REDACTED]`, closing `}` deleted
- `api_key=sk-abc.def\nsomething` — the regex would also eat through anything not whitespace/comma/semicolon, although newlines do happen to count as whitespace so this particular case stops at end-of-line
- any JSON-ish args printout where the secret is the last value before `}` or `)`

The mangling is visible in the Tools tab's "Latest result" card after the [bug2 fix](touchpilot/bug2.md) (or in the unified card on `main`), in approval cards rendered by `buildApprovalMessage`, and in trace files written by `exportDebugTrace`.

The audit-log section on…

problems.title: Bug: `DefaultActionPolicy.blockedWorkflow` substring-matches against the active screen text, blocking unrelated benign a
problems.issue_body:
### What happened?

[`DefaultActionPolicy.evaluate`](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/security/ActionPolicy.kt#L54-L67) builds a `haystack` string that concatenates the tool name, the argument values, **and the entire `request.activeScreen` snapshot**, then runs [`blockedWorkflow`](app/src/main/java/dev/touchpilot/app/security/ActionPolicy.kt#L109-L131) which checks whether any of these substrings appear anywhere in the haystack:

```
payment, "pay ", password, passcode, account recovery, recover account,
factory reset, erase all, delete account, purchase, buy now, bank,
wire transfer, transfer money
```

Because `activeScreen` is the raw accessibility-tree text of whatever app the user is currently looking at, the policy returns `PolicyDecision.Block` **for every non-LOW-risk tool** the moment the foreground screen contains any of those tokens — even when the tool, its arguments, and the user's actual intent have nothing to do with the supposedly-blocked workflow.

The check runs before the message-send detector, before the MCP approval branch, and before the regular HIGH/MEDIUM approval branch (lines 67-91), so once a keyword appears on screen the agent loses its ability to take **any** medium- or high-risk action: `tap`, `open_app`, `type_text`, `scroll`, `press_back`, `press_home`, and any other MEDIUM/HIGH tool added in the future.

### Concrete examples that fire today

Every one of the following is a benign action whose arguments and tool name contain none of the blocked keywords, but the policy blocks it because the foreground screen contains an unrelated keyword:

| Tool | Args | Foreground screen text contains | Returned decision |
|------|------|--------------------------------|-------------------|
| `tap` | `text=Settings` | `"Banking app home screen"` | `Block("banking or financial actions are blocked")` |
| `open_app` | `target=Calculator` | `"Passwords saved earlier in this session"` | `Block("password workflows are blocked")` |
| `scroll` | `direction=forward` | `"Order history including past purchase totals"` | `Block("purchases are blocked")` |
| `press_back` | (none) | `"Help article: how to delete account permanently"` | `Block("destructive account changes are blocked")` |

Real-world consequences in normal Android usage:

- Browsing a news article that mentions "factory reset" anywhere on screen — every tap is blocked.
- Sitting on the Android system Settings → Passwords & accounts screen — every action is blocked, even pressing Home to leave the screen.
- Notification shade pulls in any banking, payment, or shopping notification text — every action is blocked until the notification is dismissed.
- A skill explicitly designed to navigate a banking app's read-only screens — entirely unable to act.

Crucially, the check provides **no actual security**: an attacker (or buggy model output) can perform the exact action the keyword is meant to discourage as long as the *foreground app currently on screen* does not happen to dis…

problems.title: feature: add Android target selector model
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #75

## Problem

TouchPilot tools currently pass target data as loose arguments such as `text`, `node_id`, or `bounds`. That makes tool behavior harder to validate, rank, debug, and extend.

## Proposed behavior

Add a stable target selector model for Android UI targets.

The selector should support:

- `text`
- `contentDescription`
- `nodeId`
- `bounds`
- `viewIdResourceName`
- optional role/package/window metadata
- confidence/source metadata for resolver output

## User workflow

When the agent or local router chooses a UI target, TouchPilot should represent the target in one structured shape before execution.

## Local-first impact

A local agent needs deterministic, inspectable target data. This selector model becomes the contract between screen understanding, routing, and Android tool execution.

## Safety and security considerations

Selectors must be redacted in logs when they contain sensitive text. The model should make ambiguity explicit rather than encouraging blind taps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a structured selector model for Android targets.
- [ ] Support current `tap` selectors: text, node id, and bounds.
- [ ] Include view id/content description fields for future resolver work.
- [ ] Add unit tests for selector construction and redaction-sensitive fields where practical.
- [ ] Do not change runtime tool behavior in this PR unless necessary.

## Alternatives considered

Keep loose string maps. Rejected because Milestone 4 needs stronger validation, ranking, and verification contracts.

problems.title: feature: add focus_input tool
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #75

## Problem

`type_text` currently depends on whichever field is already focused. That is unreliable for forms, search boxes, and settings screens where the intended field is visible but not focused.

## Proposed behavior

Add a `focus_input` Android tool that focuses a resolved editable target without typing text.

Expected arguments should support the Milestone 4 selector model, such as:

- `text`
- `node_id`
- `bounds`
- `view_id`

The tool should use the target resolver and only focus editable/input nodes.

## User workflow

A user or local agent can first focus a named input field, then call `type_text` with confidence that text will go to the intended place.

## Local-first impact

This strengthens deterministic local form control without needing a cloud model.

## Safety and security considerations

Focusing is lower risk than typing, but it can still prepare a sensitive workflow. The action should remain logged and should not bypass policy for the later text entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add `focus_input` to the Android tool catalog.
- [ ] Resolve target through the Milestone 4 selector/resolver path.
- [ ] Reject non-editable targets with a clear error.
- [ ] Preserve policy, approval, and log behavior.
- [ ] Add unit tests for successful focus, missing target, non-input target, and ambiguous target.

## Alternatives considered

Only add target handling inside `type_text`. That is still useful, but a separate focus primitive gives the agent a safer, inspectable step for multi-action form workflows.

problems.title: fix: harden scroll with target-aware container resolution
problems.issue_body:
Parent: #75

## Problem

The current `scroll` tool scrolls forward or backward on the active screen, but it does not resolve a specific scrollable container.

This can fail or scroll the wrong area on screens with nested lists, sheets, or panes.

## Proposed behavior

Make scroll target-aware where possible.

The hardened scroll flow should:

- resolve scrollable containers from `ScreenContext`,
- support current direction-only behavior as a fallback,
- return a clear failure when no scrollable target exists,
- record the selected scroll target in redacted debug data,
- avoid blind repeated scrolling when the screen does not change.

## User workflow

When a user asks TouchPilot to scroll a page or list, the app should scroll the relevant container or explain that no scrollable area is available.

## Local-first impact

Reliable local control depends on scroll behaving consistently across Android screens.

## Safety and security considerations

Do not use unbounded scrolling. Retry and verification must remain bounded and observable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Resolver can identify scrollable nodes.
- [ ] `scroll` can use a resolved scrollable target where possible.
- [ ] Direction-only scroll remains compatible.
- [ ] No-scrollable-target failure is explicit.
- [ ] Unit tests cover single container, multiple containers, no container, and unchanged-screen behavior where practical.

## Alternatives considered

Keep global scroll only. Rejected because nested scroll surfaces are common on Android.

problems.title: feat: Lazy load routers
problems.issue_body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Basically `next/dynamic` but for the backend. 

Recently our tRPC router has been growing significantly for many reasons but mostly due to heavy third party SDKs. The problem with this is that even if we're not calling that specific procedure we still load ALL the router dependencies when calling any procedure.

This impacts performance and cold boots significantly.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

Splitting big tRPC routers into lazy loadable chunks could help loading only what is needed when a procedure is called. I would imagine some pseudo code like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3504472/229645485-315a4d62-2044-49ef-b420-0b33bf7fd503.png)


### Describe alternate solutions

Other aternatives involve moving all the procedure code into a separate file a use imports for that [as done in here](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/7889/commits/6ce440851e172db3f4c7ae720e8396c9201eb316).

Also [lazy loading only third party libraries](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/7889/commits/a2ff4d9a0cac732af3cd842988feaad471187488) (like Stripe, Google, etc.) seems to help. But it would be a much nicer DX being able to simply lazy load full routers and support it natively.

### Additional information

_No response_

### 👨‍👧‍👦 Contributing

- [X] 🙋‍♂️ Yes, I'd be down to file a PR implementing this feature!

<sub>[TRP-19](https://linear.app/trpc/issue/TRP-19/feat-lazy-load-routers)</sub>

problems.title: Consider SSE to enable server->client http subscriptions
problems.issue_body:
Reading through the #532 PR it occurred to me that the JSON-RPC notification system only works one way, from client to server.  Most of the time you want it to be from server to client.  Although nothing about the spec says which side is which, in a browser this basically means the browser is the client.

One interesting approach could be to use [Server Sent Events](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Server-sent_events/Using_server-sent_events).  This would allow for stateless load balance-able subscriptions that could work with HTTP2.  From what I'm seeing though I'm not sure if it would technically fall under a JSON-RPC complaint spec; though you probably can treat as a server to client notification.  Nice thing is this is already built into browsers with [polyfills available for node](https://www.npmjs.com/package/eventsource) and most languages.

I think you'd create/cancel as you do currently but the client would also fetch on a new route /subscription/3nxu4ex234.  Know this is separate from the websocket implementation but SSE isn't a well known.  The major downside of the SSE spec as it stands is the text only protocol (compared to binary for websockets) but in a JSON-RPC context the point is moot.

<sub>[TRP-63](https://linear.app/trpc/issue/TRP-63/consider-sse-to-enable-server-client-http-subscriptions)</sub>

problems.title: feat: Add support for multiValueHeaders and cookies in aws-lambda adapter
problems.issue_body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

For the aws-lambda adapter, multiple cookies cannot be returned currently when using a Rest API - using a comma-separated `Set-Cookie` header returns the first cookie in the header, instead you should use either the `multiValueHeaders` or `cookies` property if using a V2-based API gateway (HTTP-API or WS API).

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

To add support for this, we will need to:

1. Replace the existing comma-separated array joining to instead return two objects: `headers` and `multiValueHeaders` if we are using a v1 response format (for v2 we can just return headers).
1. To support passing `cookies` back when using the V2 response spec, we will need to augment the `HTTPResponse` type by adding an optional `cookies?: string[]` type.

1. If using the v1 lambda response spec:
    1. The multi-value headers can then be passed into the existing response [here](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/main/packages/server/src/adapters/aws-lambda/index.ts#L59) as another field.

1. If using the v2 lambda response spec:
    1. V2-based APIs support comma-separated headers, so the current solution will work
    1. We should also pass `cookies` which can be returned via APIGateway [within this response](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/main/packages/server/src/adapters/aws-lambda/index.ts#L66)

### Describe alternate solutions

I have attempted to return a `Set-Cookie` header as an comma-separated string and an array however only one cookie is currently sent back.

    @trpc/server: next => 11.0.0-rc.436+fbb4a2fb4
    typescript: ^5.5.0 => 5.5.3
```

### Describe the bug

The AbortController signal seems ignored by Stream Links with async generators.

We'd expect an interruption on the server side, and on the client side, but packets continue to be produced by the async generator, flow to the client, and the client keeps awaiting and receiving them.

I don't know what the correct behavior would be, but right now the signal seems to be completely ignored on both ends.

### Link to reproduction

https://github.com/enricoros/trpc-repro-stream-unabort

### To reproduce

In summary:
1. The client creates a Stream Link, and queries with a `{signal: ac.signal}`, like this (minimal):
```typescript
const trpc = createTRPCClient<AppRouter>({
  links: [unstable_httpBatchStreamLink({url: 'http://localhost:3000',})],
});

const ac = new AbortController();

const iterable = await trpc.examples.iterable.query(undefined, { signal: ac.signal });
```

2. The server implements a procedure with an async generator, like this (minimal):
```typescript
    iterable: publicProcedure.query(async function* () {
      for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 500));
        yield i;
      }
    }),
```

3. We would expect both the server and the client to be aborted, but execution continues on both.
This is the output:
![image](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/assets/32999/b4175a3f-7e46-486f-81e4-7008a4014e86)

problems.issue_body: ### Provide environment information ``` System: OS: Linux 6.9 Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS CPU: (12) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9750H CPU @ 2.60GHz Memory: 8.56 GB / 15.26 GB Container: Yes Shell: 5.8.1 - /usr/bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 22.8.0 - ~/.volta/tools/image/node/22.8.0/bin/node Yarn: 1.22.19 - ~/.volta/tools/image/yarn/1.22.19/bin/yarn npm: 10.8.2 - ~/.volta/tools/image/node/22.8.0/bin/npm pnpm: 9.9.0 - ~/.local/share/pnpm/pnpm bun: 1.1.28 - ~/.bun/bin/bun npmPackages: @tanstack/react-query: ^5.56.2 => 5.56.2 @trpc/client: ^11.0.0-rc.502 => 11.0.0-rc.502+2a8c56027 @trpc/react-query: ^11.0.0-rc.502 => 11.0.0-rc.502+2a8c56027 @trpc/server: ^11.0.0-rc.502 => 11.0.0-rc.502+2a8c56027 react: 18.2.0 => 18.2.0 typescript: ^5.6.2 => 5.6.2 ``` ### Describe the bug I think I am seeing two bugs with `wsLink` specific on iOS on React Native - Active subscriptions do not resume when woken up from being locked 😴 - If `lazy` is enabled, an iOS device will not reconnect to the websocket server at all when woken up from being locked 😴 I get this error in the wsLink's `onError` whenever I wakeup my iOS device form being locked ### Link to reproduction https://github.com/bnussman/trpc-ws-issue ### To reproduce 1. Downlaod [Expo Go](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/expo-go/id982107779) on your iOS device 2. Clone the reproduction repository 3. Install dependencies with ``` bun install ``` 4. Start the dev servers with ``` bun start ``` 5. On your iOS device, open Expo Go and open this project 6. Observe the counter is counting up (meaning the subscription is working and connected) 7. Lock your iOS device's screen and wait for the server to register that the device disconnected 8. Unlock your iOS device and observe that the WS connections, but the tRPC subscription does not resume 9. Repeat steps 5-8 with lazy mode enabled. Observe that when your iOS device is woken up from sleep, the WS does not reconnect at all ### Additional information This also happens in my production iOS app, so I have confirmed that this is not specific to Expo Go. It might be a React Native bug, but I haven't found anything documenting if this is the case. It maybe me something tRPC needs to address for compatibility with React Native ### 👨‍👧‍👦 Contributing - [ ] 🙋‍♂️ Yes, I'd be down to file a PR fixing this bug!

  Browsers:
    Chrome: 111.0.5563.110
    Firefox: 109.0.1
    Safari: 16.1
    Safari Technology Preview: 16.4
```

### Describe the bug

After some time when tab is suspended on iOS safari, WS stops working on iOS safari. WebSocket doesn't emit `close` event, and it just hangs. No reconnect happen

### To reproduce

1. Open site with iOS Safari
2. Switch to other apps
3. Wait ~3-5 min
4. Return to safari browser
5. WS stops working, no reconnect happens

I also checked the "network" tab. The connection looks like is not closed, but not events are emitting.

### Additional information

I found a dirty workaround:

```ts
document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", () => {
  // Let's reconnect on visibility change,
  // Cause, for example, iOS safari connection may hang
  if (document.visibilityState === "visible") {
    wsClient.getConnection().dispatchEvent(new CloseEvent("close"));
  }
});
```

And, an interesting thing, is that I need to make `wsClient.getConnection().dispatchEvent(new CloseEvent("close"))`. If I do just `wsClient.close()` — nothing happens. I think `close` event just not emitting when WebSocket is hanged.

I found the same issue at `graphql-ws`, so it may help https://github.com/enisdenjo/graphql-ws/discussions/290 . They recommend using this solution — https://the-guild.dev/graphql/ws/recipes#client-usage-with-abrupt-termination-on-pong-timeout

problems.title: bug: TRPC may create an invalid URL that crashes the server
problems.issue_body:
### Provide environment information

Machine agnostic

### Describe the bug

Some bots or spammers might send invalid requests with URLs like:
```
hotmail-com.olc.protection.outlook.com%3A25... 
```
We've met the above, and here's a 3rd party library showcasing the same signature: https://github.com/sbordeyne/fastapi_spammer_protection/blob/fd4a3982c23cd4ab0f4761c9db603994c06fa19c/fastapi_spammer_protection/vulnerable_urls.py#L174

We've got some auxiliary servers, with exposed IPs, crashed by bots. Our main servers work behing Nginx which prevents the above from happening. 

Here's where it happens:

https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/next/packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/incomingMessageToRequest.ts#L70

```ts
const url = `http://${headers.get('host')}${req.url}`;
```

The above code is buggy because `req.url` might be invalid, in particular not starting with a slash! So `${headers.get('host')}${req.url}` becomes
something malformed of `{domain}{domain}` shape.

It leads to a **hard crash** of the server – it does not just return 400 or 500 or something, but completely stops to accept new connections, basically goes offline❗Some of this behavior might be NodeJS specific, but the issue starts in TRPC code. Couldn't investigate in more details due to the lack of time.

### Proposed Solution

Validate that `req.url` starts with `/`. 

### Link to reproduction

I don't have enough time to prepare a sandbox, sorry, maybe a bit later. 
It looks like a TRPC bug to me.

### To reproduce

Create a server with `http-node` adapter and send a GET/POST with an invalid  URL. E.g.

```
$ printf 'GET hotmail-com.olc.protection.outlook.com HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n' | nc localhost 2000
```

If anything – I'll contribute a sandbox next week.

### Additional information

problems.title: feat: Make React-Query integration less opaque
problems.issue_body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

As per [this discussion](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/discussions/4010), I found it confusing to integrate tRPC into NextJS SSG, when not adhering to the strict Prisma/Next/tRPC paradigm.

Ultimately, I would like it to be more straightforward to integrate React Query.

Currently, the way tRPC integrates with React Query is fairly opaque, and having both `@trpc/react-query` and `@trpc/next` packages adds more confusion than benefit IMO.

Considering packages like `react-query` do a good job of handling the fetching, caching and SSG - and have all the up-to-date docs around it - I think `tRPC` would do well to integrate with such tools in a less opinionated manner, plugging into these existing tools, instead of encapsulating, limiting their behaviour and then having to document and maintain what is effectively a third party interface.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

Both the `/react-query` and `/next` packages are relatively small. Given the recommendation against tree-resolving the queries, [here](https://trpc.io/docs/ssr), and the general consensus among client-side fetching libraries like Apollo and React Query away from such approached, I think the `/next` package can actually be deprecated. It's not clear that the NextJS integration (for fetching) is required, and adds more overhead for documentation and more opportunity for confusion.

Secondly, I think the `/react-query` package could integrate with `react-query` in a more lightweight manner. Instead of in-housing the creation of `QueryClient` and `QueryProvider`, instead it should integrate within the `/react-query` approach. In short, the `createTRPCReact` should return a bunch of type-safe helpers proxying the `some.query.here` to an object of pre-defined `useQuery, useInifiniteQuery` etc. wrappers. I don't think any fundamentally new functionality or different API pattern (to react query) should be added here.

## What might this look like?

Keep configuration of React Query entirely separate and up to the user. This maximises flexibility, transparency and minimizes `tRPC` maintenance + documentation.

```tsx
// _app.tsx
const myQueryClient = new QueryClient(myOptions)

return <QueryProvider queryClient={myQueryClient}>
  <Hydrate state={myDehydratedState}>
    <Component {...} />
  </Hydrate>
</QueryProvider>
```

And then `createTRPCReact` can just return a comprehensive object of helper queries and exposure of helpful internal functions like so:

```tsx
type AppRouter = { myProcedure: {...} }

const trpc = createTRRCReact<AppRouter>(trpcRelatedConfigHere)

// Using a procedure's helpers
trpc.myProcedure.useQuery(...)
trpc.myProcedure.useInfiniteQuery(...)
trpc.myProcedure.key(...) // <- useful for react-query idiomatic SSG
trpc.myProcedure.fetcher(...) // <- ^^

// Using TRPC helpers
```tsx
trpc.dehydrate() // <- Light wrapper over react query dehydrate, including appropriate seriali…

problems.title: feat: Maintainers wanted for `wsLink`
problems.issue_body:
# We need maintainers for `wsLink`

**Help us in revamping tRPC's WebSocket support!**

Since we introduced subscriptions using `httpSubscriptionLink`, the core team no longer relies on `wsLink` as we handle subscriptions over HTTP. Consequently, we've decided to deprecate `wsLink` and invite the community to take over its maintenance. 🙏

The current implementation is located [here](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/next/packages/client/src/links/wsLink.ts). As you might notice, it's not well-written; each modification has added complexity, and it urgently needs a rewrite.

We recognize the value of having tRPC support for WebSockets and would love to see it actively maintained by passionate developers like you. 🌟 **We'll happily guide you around the codebase to get you started!**

## What we'd like to see

We want a revamped version of `wsLink` and `createWSClient` that supports the existing features:

- ⏳ **Lazily closing/opening connections** when needed.
- 🔄 **Resumes subscriptions** if the server stops.
- 🔁 **Gracefully switches connections** to a new one if the server notifies it's about to close.
- 🚀 **Restarts with backoff** when it fails.
- ⚡ **Supports queries, subscriptions, and mutations**.
- 🔍 **Supports introspection of the current connection status of the active socket**.
- 🏓 **Ping/Pong support** to detect and close inactive connections.


Additionally, we'd want it to:

- ✍️ **Be well-written**.
- ✅ **Be thoroughly tested**. Existing tests should pass any implementation.
- 📚 **Include comprehensive documentation**.
- 🪝 **Have a React-hook** for introspecting the connection state - e.g. `useConnectionState(wsClient)`

## Alternatives we've considered 

- We're also considering **financial funding** as an option. We estimate that investing a few thousand dollars would enable us to dedicate the necessary time to rewrite it. 💰
- If we don't find maintainers, we'll likely delete the `wsLink` in v12 of tRPC. 🗑️

---

**If you're interested in contributing or taking over the maintenance of `wsLink`, please reach out! Your contributions can make a significant impact on the tRPC community.** 🙌

---

feat: Support `combine` option on `useQueries`
problems.issue_body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Tanstack Query has a `combine` option on `useQueries` that lets you process multiple results before passing them along.

This nice because the array that `useQueries` returns does not have a stable identity.

```ts
const flatten = <T>({ data }: { data: T[][] }): T[] => data.flat()

function Component() {
  const { data: books } = trpc.books.useQueries((t) =>
    decades.map((decade) => t.book.findInDecade({ decade })),
  )

  // Memo is invalidated every render
  const allBooks = useMemo(flatten, [books])
}
```

The `combine` solves this with some special handling of [memoization](https://tanstack.com/query/v5/docs/framework/react/reference/useQueries#memoization):

> The combine function will only re-run if:
>
> - the combine function itself changed referentially
> - any of the query results changed

Right now, though, tRPC cannot send a `combine` function to `useQueries`.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

Ideally I could just pass the `combine` option through:

```ts
const flatten = <T>({ data }: { data: T[][] }): T[] => data.flat()

function Component() {
  const { data: books } = trpc.books.useQueries(
    (t) => decades.map((decade) => t.book.findInDecade({ decade })),
    { combine: flatten },
  )

  // `books` has a stable identity, unless the combine function changes, decades changes,
  // or something is invalidated.
}
```

### Describe alternate solutions

The `callback, { combine }` api is maybe a little odd? Then maybe we support an overload signature that takes one object.

```ts
const { data: books } = trpc.books.useQueries({
  queries: (t) => decades.map((decade) => t.book.findInDecade({ decade })),
  combine: flatten,
})
```

### Additional information

### Prior Issues

This comment https://github.com/trpc/trpc/pull/4662#pullrequestreview-1559140858
Leads to this closed issue https://github.com/trpc/trpc/issues/4678
Which was closed as `not planned`, but with no explanation.

### Relevant Code

The handoff from tRPC to tanstack query happens here:
https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/next/packages/react-query/src/shared/hooks/createHooksInternal.tsx#L681-L709

And only takes one parameter: the queries.

### Existing Docs

But the [documentation site](https://trpc.io/docs/client/react/useQueries#context) says that you can pass a context as the second parameter, but I think this actually doesn't work at all, and is a type error to do so. If that is to be supported, that would need to be worked into the api as well. Perhaps by sticking close to how tanstack does it:

```ts
const { data: books } = trpc.books.useQueries({
  queries: (t) => decades.map((decade) => t.book.findInDecade({ decade })),
  combine: flatten,
}, customCtx)
```

### 👨‍👧‍👦 Contributing

- [X] 🙋‍♂️ Yes, I'd be down to file a PR implementing this feature!

    bun: 1.0.3 - ~/.bun/bin/bun

    @tanstack/react-query: ^5.64.2 => 5.64.2 
    @trpc/client: 11.0.0-rc.718 => 11.0.0-rc.718+2018e3914 
    @trpc/react-query: 11.0.0-rc.718 => 11.0.0-rc.718+2018e3914 
    @trpc/server: 11.0.0-rc.718 => 11.0.0-rc.718+2018e3914 
    react: ^18.3.1 => 18.3.1 
    typescript: 5.7.2 => 5.7.2
```

### Describe the bug

When using http2, the response body is always empty when the method is POST. I was able to trace the problem and discovered that the reason for this is that the request is being aborted in response to this event:

https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/776d07336bddd01ac2ad02da0360fb71aa734471/packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/incomingMessageToRequest.ts#L147

If I don't pass the abort signal in the stream pipe, it is able to write to the stream without any issue and everything works. Here is where I made that change:

https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/776d07336bddd01ac2ad02da0360fb71aa734471/packages/server/src/adapters/node-http/writeResponse.ts#L50-L52

I'll be honest, it doesn't make sense to me why the response close event fires and yet I can still write it to it just fine. I'm also not sure how to deal with this situation without breaking proper abort handling elsewhere.

### Link to reproduction

https://github.com/cseickel/trpc-http2-post-example

### To reproduce

Unfortunately it does not run in stakblitz for me, maybe because it requires an ssl connection. You can clone the linked repo and follow the readme.

https://github.com/cseickel/trpc-http2-post-example

### Additional information

I understand that no where does the project explicitly state that HTTP2 is supported, but I'm hoping it is within scope. The reason I want to use HTTP2 is that it is really important for using the SSE subscription feature. The reason for this is that each subscription opens a new connection, and with HTTP/1 the browser will not open more than 6 connections of any type to one server. This limit applies across multiple tabs as well, so it is really hard to stay under that limit. 

HTTP/2 removes this limit and makes SSE feasible.

Thank you for the awesome project!

problems.title: feat: add support for "ending" a subscription from the server
problems.issue_body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Right now subscriptions only work for endless streams, because the client will always reconnect if the connection breaks. There are some subscriptions that are not endless though:

- streaming a large amount of logs, for a job that finishes at some point
- waiting for a resource to go into a certain state, with status updates along the way

For these cases, it would be good if the server could say "this subscription is now done", for example by returning from the async generator / iterable.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

When the server ends the async iterable cleanly (using `return`, not because of an error), the client should stop trying to reconnect.

### Describe alternate solutions

Implement this manually in user code by sending a signal value to the client. The signal would then be processed on the client to abort the subscription.

problems.issue_body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

`httpBatchStreamLink` was implemented on this https://github.com/trpc/trpc/pull/4347

Currently, the built-in AWS Lambda Adapter for tRPC didn't provide support for AWS Lambda Response Streaming, so I'm opening this issue just to keep track of the future support of this functionality.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

The ideal solution should be something like this:

```js
import { CreateAWSLambdaContextOptions, awsLambdaRequestHandler } from '@trpc/server/adapters/aws-lambda-stream';
const appRouter = /* ... */;
// created for each request
const createContext = ({
  event,
  context,
}: CreateAWSLambdaContextOptions<APIGatewayProxyEventV2>) => ({}) // no context
type Context = trpc.inferAsyncReturnType<typeof createContext>;
export const handler = awsLambdaRequestStreamHandler({
  router: appRouter,
  createContext,
})
```

### Describe alternate solutions

I'm the maintainer of [Serverless Adapter](https://github.com/H4ad/serverless-adapter), a library to connect any serverless environment with any NodeJS Framework. 

I already added support for AWS Lambda Response Stream ([docs](https://serverless-adapter.viniciusl.com.br/docs/main/handlers/aws#aws-lambda-response-streaming)), and I also [support tRPC](https://serverless-adapter.viniciusl.com.br/docs/main/frameworks/trpc) (I still need to update my library to add support to the latest version) but I think it will work without any issue this new feature using my library.

If you want to add support for response streaming on the internal built-in, I suggest for who are interested in implementing, read the following files:
- [AwsStreamHandler](https://github.com/H4ad/serverless-adapter/blob/main/src/handlers/aws/aws-stream.handler.ts#L254-L316)
- [ResponseStream](https://github.com/H4ad/serverless-adapter/blob/main/src/network/response-stream.ts)
- [TrpcFramework](https://github.com/H4ad/serverless-adapter/blob/main/src/frameworks/trpc/trpc.framework.ts#L170-L186)

    @trpc/client: ^11.0.0 => 11.0.4 
    @trpc/server: ^11.0.0 => 11.0.4 
    next: ^15.0.0 => 15.3.0 
    react: ^19.0.0 => 19.1.0 
    typescript: ^5.8.2 => 5.8.3
```

### Describe the bug

When using the `useSubscription` hook from the new `@trpc/tanstack-react-query` integration, the `onConnectionStateChange` callback never fires. However, the `subscription.status` value does update as expected.

I believe this is happening because the `useSubscription` hook implementation does not appear to be calling the user-provided `onConnectionStateChange` callback. See [L202](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/main/packages/tanstack-react-query/src/internals/subscriptionOptions.ts#L202), where `updateState` is being called in a similar fashion as `onStarted` / `onData` / `onError`. However, in these other cases, there is a call to the user-provided callback in addition to `updateState`:

```ts
optsRef.current.onError?.(error);
updateState((prev) => {
  // ...
})
```

However, in the `onConnectionStateChange` block, it looks like we are missing this call, which should appear on line 203:

```ts
optsRef.current.onConnectionStateChange?.(result);
```

In fact, there does not appear to be any reference to `optsRef.current.onConnectionStateChange` anywhere in the hook implementation.

### Link to reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/github/trpc/examples-next-minimal-starter

### To reproduce

1. Provide a `onConnectionStateChange` callback to `subscriptionOptions` when creating a subscription.
2. Take any action that would normally trigger a connection state change, such as shutting down the local development server.
3. Observe that `subscription.status` (as returned from the `useSubscription` hook) will update to reflect this change (likely because the hook is calling `updateState`) but `onConnectionStateChange` is never called.

problems.issue_body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Hi there!

It would be great to have a `LocalLink` that allows me to do:
This would directly run the router in the same process as the client instead of transferring requests to a server.

### But why??

This is motivated mainly due to testing and fast prototyping:
1. This allows to test the client with the server code (with a small caveat, see below)
2. I can start writing a fully functional client that saves data in local storage instead of a database, and when I want to add a database, I don't need to rewrite the procedures, giving me significantly faster prototyping speed.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

```ts
import { createRouter } from '../path/to/server/trpc';
const client = createTRPCProxyClient<ReturnType<typeof createRouter>>({
  links: [
    localLink({ router: createRouter({ database }) }),
  ],
});```

For the feature itself it doesn't matter that the router is created by a function call, but this solves a problem I mentioned above: What if part of the code only runs on the server, e.g. database access? Well, just inject that dependency, and, in case you are running on the client, use a browser-based database.

### Describe alternate solutions

Not sure, to be honest.

problems.title: bug: httpBatchStreamLink loses buffered chunks on normal stream completion due to closeOrAbort using controller.error()
problems.issue_body:
### Provide environment information

```
System:
  OS: macOS 26.2
  CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M1 Max
  Memory: 78.77 MB / 32.00 GB
  Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh
Binaries:
  Node: 24.11.1
  pnpm: 10.9.0
npmPackages:
  @trpc/client: ^11.1.0 => 11.7.2
  @trpc/server: ^11.1.0 => 11.7.2
  @trpc/react-query: ^11.1.0 => 11.7.2
  @tanstack/react-query: ^5.74.4 => 5.90.12
  next: 15.2.8
  react: ^19.0.1 => 19.2.1
  typescript: ^5 => 5.9.3
```

### Describe the bug

When using `httpBatchStreamLink`, **normal stream completion causes all buffered (enqueued but unconsumed) chunks in the `ReadableStream` to be silently discarded**. This is because `closeOrAbort` calls `cancelAll()` → `controller.error(reason)` for **both** the `close` and `abort` handlers of the `WritableStream`.

Per the [WHATWG Streams specification](https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#rs-error), `controller.error()` immediately transitions the stream to the `"errored"` state and **discards all enqueued chunks** in the internal queue. In contrast, `controller.close()` transitions to `"closed"` and allows the consumer to drain all remaining buffered data.

#### Root cause

In [`src/unstable-core-do-not-import/stream/jsonl.ts`](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/main/packages/server/src/unstable-core-do-not-import/stream/jsonl.ts):

```typescript
// Line 588-591
const closeOrAbort = (reason?: unknown) => {
  headDeferred?.reject(reason);
  streamManager.cancelAll(reason);  // ← always calls controller.error()
};

// Line 615-616 — both handlers use the same function
close: closeOrAbort,
abort: closeOrAbort,
```

And in `cancelAll`:

```typescript
// Line 484-488
function cancelAll(reason: unknown) {
  for (const controller of controllerMap.values()) {
    controller.error(reason);  // ← discards buffered chunks per WHATWG spec
  }
}
```

On normal completion, the `WritableStream`'s `close` handler is called (not `abort`), meaning the server has successfully sent all data. However, `closeOrAbort` treats this identically to an abort — it calls `controller.error(undefined)`, which:

1. Discards all chunks that were `enqueue()`d but not yet `read()` by the consumer
2. Passes `undefined` as the error reason, which causes downstream issues (e.g., AI SDK's `makeRequest` catch block does `err.name` on `undefined`, throwing a `TypeError`)

#### Impact

This creates a **race condition** between the producer (HTTP response → JSONL parser → `controller.enqueue()`) and the consumer (`ReadableStream` → application code). For long streaming responses (e.g., 1500+ chunks from an LLM), the producer often finishes writing all chunks before the consumer has read them all. When `close` fires, the remaining buffered chunks are lost.

**Observed behavior:**
- Short responses: usually works (consumer keeps up with producer)
- Long responses: **truncated output** — the consumer receives only a portion of the data
- The stream ends with `error(undefined)` instead of `close()`, so consumers cannot distinguish between a normal compl…

bug: `httpBatchStreamLink` AbortController is created but never called on unsubscribe
problems.issue_body:
### Provide environment information

**Package:** `@trpc/client`
**File:** `packages/client/src/links/httpBatchStreamLink.ts` (lines 75, 139, 216)
**Version:** v11.17.0

### Describe the bug

In `httpBatchStreamLink`, an `AbortController` is created and passed to `jsonlStreamConsumer` to signal cancellation of the JSONL response stream. However, the observable's cleanup function is a noop:

```ts
return () => {
  // noop
};
```

`abortController.abort()` is never called when the observable is unsubscribed. As a result, the underlying response body stream continues consuming data from the server after the subscriber has disconnected — wasting bandwidth and holding the stream open unnecessarily. It can also cause `observer already completed` errors if the stream later resolves after the observer has been cleaned up.

### Link to reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/github/trpc/trpc/tree/main/examples/next-minimal-starter

### To reproduce

1. Set up a tRPC app using `httpBatchStreamLink`
2. Initiate a query that takes >1s to stream (e.g. a procedure returning an async iterable)
3. Unmount the component or navigate away before the stream completes
4. Open DevTools → Network tab
5. Observe the request continues streaming to completion despite the subscriber being gone

### Additional information

Root cause: In `packages/client/src/links/httpBatchStreamLink.ts`, an `AbortController` 
is created and passed to `jsonlStreamConsumer`, but the observable's cleanup function 
is a noop — `abortController.abort()` is never called on unsubscribe.

Suggested fix (one line):
// Before
return () => { // noop };

// After  
return () => { abortController.abort(); };

The AbortController is already wired into jsonlStreamConsumer — only the cleanup 
call is missing. Fix applies to all three batch paths in the file (~lines 75, 139, 216).

### 👨‍👧‍👦 Contributing

- [x] 🙋‍♂️ Yes, I'd be down to file a PR fixing this bug!

At [this line](https://github.com/twisted/twisted/blob/c465c460c68bec3cf481c2815d1039da6796eb03/src/twisted/web/http.py#L3324) Twisted is assuming that `logFile` has an encoding of `"utf8"` but that isn't always the case... problems.title: Add a context manager for calling `log.failure` when code fails
problems.issue_body:
Right now we have a pattern of doing this:

```python3
log = Logger()

try:
    applicationCode(parameter)
except BaseException:
    log.failure("while doing xyz with {parameter}", parameter=parameter)
else:
    proceed()
```

This is verbose, error-prone, and kinda reads backwards.  Instead, something like this would be nicer:

```python3
log = Logger()
with log.whenThereIsAnyProblemLogThis("while doing xyz with {parameter}", parameter=parameter) as operation:
    applicationCode(parameter)
if operation.succeeded:
    proceed()
```

problems.title: Stop including location exception was caught in Failure
problems.issue_body:
About 2/3rds of the time spent in creating `Failure` objects, and therefore in error handling in `Deferred`, is constructing `Deferred.stack`. I would argue this isn't necessary, insofar as Python doesn't include this info, and it's a huge performance hit.

## Comparing Python tracebacks to Failure tracebacks

Consider the following script:

```python
from twisted.python.failure import Failure
import sys
import traceback

def f():
    def h():
        1 / 0

    def g():
        h()

    g()

def a():
    try:
        f()
    except:
        if sys.argv[1] == "python":
            print("PYTHON")
            traceback.print_tb(sys.exc_info()[-1], file=sys.stdout)
        else:
            print("TWISTED")
            failure = Failure()
            failure.cleanFailure()
            failure.printTraceback(sys.stdout)

a()
```

When run:

```
(py311) itamarst@louverture:~/devel/twisted$ python 12227.py python
PYTHON
  File "/home/itamarst/devel/twisted/12227.py", line 16, in a
    f()
  File "/home/itamarst/devel/twisted/12227.py", line 12, in f
    g()
  File "/home/itamarst/devel/twisted/12227.py", line 10, in g
    h()
  File "/home/itamarst/devel/twisted/12227.py", line 7, in h
    1 / 0
    ~~^~~
(py311) itamarst@louverture:~/devel/twisted$ python 12227.py twisted
TWISTED
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/itamarst/devel/twisted/12227.py", line 26, in <module>    # <---- only Twisted has this bit!
    a()
--- <exception caught here> ---
  File "/home/itamarst/devel/twisted/12227.py", line 16, in a
    f()
  File "/home/itamarst/devel/twisted/12227.py", line 12, in f
    g()
  File "/home/itamarst/devel/twisted/12227.py", line 10, in g
    h()
  File "/home/itamarst/devel/twisted/12227.py", line 7, in h
    1 / 0
builtins.ZeroDivisionError: division by zero
```

Notice that Twisted includes where the Failure was created, whereas Python only includes the traceback.

## Why omit this? Performance

Two thirds of the time spent in `Deferred`  error handling of `Failure` (as measured by the relevant benchmark) is tied in creating `Deferred.stack`.

## A compromise

If we want to be extra nice, this extra info can be turned on when `Deferred.debug` is turned on. 

## A counterargument

It may be that the info of "where did we catch the exception" is super-helpful. I am not sure I have enough relevant experience in debugging production Twisted applications to have a good opinion.

problems.title: Twisted doesn't validate HTTP versions
problems.issue_body:
# Description

Twisted does no validation of received requests' HTTP versions.

# How to cause this behavior

1. Start a Twisted HTTP server that echos the received version, such as [this one](https://github.com/narfindustries/http-garden/blob/main/images/twisted/server.py).
2. Send Twisted an HTTP request with an invalid version, and extract the parsed version from the response:
```sh
(printf 'GET / This-is-totally-invalid!-It-even-contains-unprintable-bytes,-like-\x00-and\xff!!\r\nHost: a\r\n\r\n'; sleep 1) \
    | nc localhost 80 \
    | awk '{RS=""; FS="\r\n\r\n"} {print $2}' \
    | tail -n 1 \
    | jq '.["version"]' \
    | xargs echo \
    | base64 -d \
    | xxd
```
3. Observe that the version is unchanged, including the NUL and non-ASCII byte:
```
00000000: 5468 6973 2d69 732d 746f 7461 6c6c 792d  This-is-totally-
00000010: 696e 7661 6c69 6421 2d49 742d 6576 656e  invalid!-It-even
00000020: 2d63 6f6e 7461 696e 732d 756e 7072 696e  -contains-unprin
00000030: 7461 626c 652d 6279 7465 732c 2d6c 696b  table-bytes,-lik
00000040: 652d 002d 616e 64ff 2121                 e-.-and.!!
```

# The correct behavior
RFC 9112 specifies that HTTP versions have to match the following grammar rule:
```
  HTTP-version  = HTTP-name "/" DIGIT "." DIGIT
  HTTP-name     = %s"HTTP"
```
In other words, HTTP versions need to match the following regex: `HTTP/[0-9]\.[0-9]`.

**Testing environment**
 - Operating System and Version; paste the output of these commands:
   - `Linux e153e0bbe66c 6.9.7-arch1-1 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri, 28 Jun 2024 04:32:50 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
 - Twisted version [e.g. 22.2.0]

problems.title: Twisted incorrectly allows NUL in header values
problems.issue_body:
# The incorrect behavior
From RFC 9110:
> Field values containing CR, LF, or NUL characters are invalid and dangerous, due to the varying ways that implementations might parse and interpret those characters; a recipient of CR, LF, or NUL within a field value MUST either reject the message or replace each of those characters with SP before further processing or forwarding of that message.

# How to cause this behavior

0. Install Twisted
1. Run the following script (it just echos back the parsed components of each received request in base64, inside a JSON object):
```python3
from base64 import b64encode

from twisted.web import server, resource
from twisted.internet import reactor

class TheResource(resource.Resource):
    isLeaf = True
    def __getattribute__(self, key: str):
        if key.startswith("render_"):
            return self._respond
        return super().__getattribute__(key)

    def _respond(self, request) -> bytes:
        result: bytes = b'{"headers":['
        result += b",".join(b'["' + b64encode(name) + b'","' + b64encode(value) + b'"]' for name, value in request.getAllHeaders().items())
        result += b'],"method":"' + b64encode(request.method)
        result += b'","uri":"' + b64encode(request.uri)
        result += b'","version":"' + b64encode(request.clientproto)
        result += b'","body":"' + b64encode(request.content.read())
        result += b'"}'
        return result

site = server.Site(TheResource())
reactor.listenTCP(80, site)
reactor.run()
```
2. Send it a request with a NUL byte in a header value, and extract the parsed header value from the response:
```sh
(printf 'GET / HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: whatever\r\nTest: a\x00a\r\n\r\n'; sleep 1) \
    | nc localhost 80 \
    | grep '"headers"' \
    | jq '.["headers"][1][1]' \
    | xargs echo \
    | base64 -d \
    | xxd
```
```
00000000: 6100 61                                  a.a
```

# The correct behavior I'd like to see
Twisted should either reject the request with a 400, or replace the NUL with a SP before processing.

# Testing environment
 - Operating System and Version; paste the output of these commands:
   - `Linux cb97695853e1 6.9.7-arch1-1 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri, 28 Jun 2024 04:32:50 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
 - Twisted version [e.g. 22.2.0]
   - `24.3.0.post0`

problems.title: Replace Failure._findFailure dependency on bytecode with some mechanism that doesn't rely on bytecode
problems.issue_body:
The problem:

* As seen in #12061, changes to generated bytecode can break `Failure`'s special `inlineCallbacks` related code(and quite possibly async functions too).
* In a world where a CPython JIT is a possibility, it's not clear if any of this will work at all in the future.

It would be better to have a mechanism for finding the current failure that is less tied to obscure implementation details of Python. Perhaps contextvars might do the trick?

problems.title: Disable Nagle in HTTP client and server
problems.issue_body:
After spending a bunch of time trying to figure out why Tahoe-LAFS is spending a surprising amount of time idle while doing HTTP interactions, I discovered it was Nagle adding 40ms to small queries. 

The argument for disabling Nagle / enabling TCP_NODELAY:

* HTTP is often used for small, RPC-like queries, so delaying queries by 40ms is bad.
* Large bodies typically won't benefit Nagle anyway.
* HTTPS is all anyone uses in practice these days, and Twisted's TLS layer already does some minimal buffering to reduce small writes: https://github.com/twisted/twisted/blob/f0afc5eb9850eda242beefb178dd481e28926f08/src/twisted/protocols/tls.py#L818

problems.title: IMAP Server support is broken for iOS Mail.app and shorter messages
problems.issue_body:
**Describe the incorrect behavior you saw**

Using the IMAPServer class with the latest (at least, I've not tested on older versions) Mail.app on iOS appears to be broken. The client can load the folder structure, but will never load the body of the message if the message is less than 393216 bytes.

This appears to be due to iOS using `BODY.PEEK` with a very large partial window. The IMAP RFC (RFC3501) states:

>  Any partial fetch that attempts to read beyond the end of the
         text is truncated as appropriate.  A partial fetch that starts
         at octet 0 is returned as a partial fetch, even if this
         truncation happened.

> Note: This means that BODY[]<0.2048> of a 1500-octet message
    will return BODY[]<0> with a literal of size 1500, not
    BODY[].

Twisted [does not respect this](https://github.com/twisted/twisted/blob/trunk/src/twisted/mail/imap4.py#L5714) and returns the original partial window and the content of the message. This is then never displayed in mail.app and causes the app to go into a message retrieval loop.

iOS appears to always use the same partial range, with UID enabled:
```UID BODY.PEEK[]<0.393216>```
This taken from both debug output in twisted and a wireshark packet trace.

**Describe how to cause this behavior**

Create a test IMAP server using the IMAP4 support in Twisted and populate it with some messages. Attempt to connect to it using the iOS native mail.app.

This https://github.com/mistio/localmail/tree/master is an example of a server that exhibits the problem.

**Describe the correct behavior you'd like to see**

The mail should be viewable in mail.app, and the server should follow the RFC spec (as much as possible with the IMAP spec)

**Testing environment**
 - Operating System and Version; paste the output of these commands:
```
Linux SanctionedPartsOnly 6.11.0-8-generic #8-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon Sep 16 13:41:20 UTC 2024 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
DISTRIB_ID=Ubuntu
DISTRIB_RELEASE=24.10
DISTRIB_CODENAME=oracular
DISTRIB_DESCRIPTION="Ubuntu 24.10"
```

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

problems.issue_body:
Since 24.10.0 it is not possible to use HTTP server over `unix:` protocol. 

This bug has been initially reported in https://github.com/buildbot/buildbot/issues/8207.

Relevant log:

            protocol.makeConnection(transport)

            self.socket.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_TCP, socket.TCP_NODELAY, enabled)

problems.title: Allow opting out of parsing of MIME upload parsing in twisted.web
problems.issue_body:
Current file upload MIME parsing in Twisted Web requires, based on the interface, _requires_ parsing the whole thing into memory. So for large uploads this can result in very large memory usage. The API for users specifically involves accessing the mapping `request.args`.

How to solve this? 

1. Long term, one could do full-on async streaming parsing, but that is a large project. It also doesn't actually solve the problem in the short term, since for backwards compatibility `request.args` would still need to exist.
2. On-demand parsing only when `request.args` is accessed. This is not ideal since it makes it requires blocking, which can be meaningful for large uploads.
3. Allow users to opt-out so they can just do their own parsing (or use the streaming future API, if that ever happens). Tahoe-LAFS already wants to do this, for example, and right now overrides the parsing logic already in a pretty hacky way.

I propose to implement option 3.

problems.title: Regression handling multiple files in multipart/form-data with same name
problems.issue_body:
**Summary** 

We have found a regression with latest releases of Twisted in `twisted.web.http` due to replacement of `cgi.parse_multipart` in commit 4579398 which has resulted in our web server only being able to retrieve a single file from a request that contained multiple files.

**Environment**
 - Twisted version 24.x

**Description**

The web app has a file picker form where a user can select multiple files to upload to the web server.  Here is a sample snippet of request received by web server:

```
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="test1.torrent"
Content-Type: application/x-bittorrent
...
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="tes2.torrent"
Content-Type: application/x-bittorrent
```

The web server parses out the filenames as follows:

    files = request.args.get(b'file', [])

**Expected**

A list containing both files

**Actual**

A list containing only the first file

**Investigation notes**

The  content-disposition of the file upload form is using the same `name` parameter for both files. However the commit to replace `cgi` results in only a single file ever being assigned to a name:

```
        result[name.encode("utf8")] = [payload]
```

According to  [rfc7578](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7578) this is correct request

> To match widely deployed implementations, multiple files MUST be sent
   by supplying each file in a separate part but all with the same
   "name" parameter.

The solution to the problem is to assign result to a  `defaultdict(list)` then for the same key append payloads found to the list. I'll push a PR shortly...

problems.title: `ReconnectingClientFactory`: `initialDelay` is not the initial delay
problems.issue_body:
**Describe the incorrect behavior you saw**
With `initialDelay = 1.0` and `factor = 2.7`, the actual initial delay is 2.7.

**Describe how to cause this behavior**

Use `ReconnectingClientFactory` to try a connection to a port without a listening socket, refusing connections. If `initialDelay = x` and `factor = y`, reconnection delays are:

1. `x * y`
2. `x * y**2`
3. `x * y**3`

and so on.

**Describe the correct behavior you'd like to see**

`initialDelay` should specify the delay that is applied before the first reconnection, and only on subsequent retries should `factor` be applied. So the reconnection delays ought to be:

1. `x`
2. `x * y`
3. `x * y**2`

**Testing environment**
 - Operating System and Version; paste the output of these commands:
   - on Linux, `uname -a ; cat /etc/lsb-release`
       ```
       Linux kyle 6.1.0-37-amd64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Debian 6.1.140-1 (2025-05-22) x86_64 GNU/Linux
       PRETTY_NAME="Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm)"
       NAME="Debian GNU/Linux"
       VERSION_ID="12"
       VERSION="12 (bookworm)"
       VERSION_CODENAME=bookworm
       ID=debian
       HOME_URL="https://www.debian.org/"
       SUPPORT_URL="https://www.debian.org/support"
       BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugs.debian.org/"
       ```
 - Twisted version [e.g. 22.2.0]
   - please paste the output of `twist --version` and `pip --freeze`
       ```
       $ twist --version
       25.5.0
       $ pip freeze
       annotated-types==0.7.0
       attrs==25.3.0
       Automat==25.4.16
       constantly==23.10.4
       hyperlink==21.0.0
       idna==3.10
       incremental==24.7.2
       mypy==1.16.1
       mypy_extensions==1.1.0
       pathspec==0.12.1
       pydantic==2.11.7
       pydantic_core==2.33.2
       Twisted==25.5.0
       typing-inspection==0.4.1
       typing_extensions==4.14.1
       # Editable install with no version control (yate-buttons==0.1.dev1)
       -e /home/peter/src/yate-buttons
       yaypm3==3.1
       zope.interface==7.2
       ```

       (minor note: instructions say `pip --freeze` but really it's `pip freeze`)


 - Reactor [e.g. select, iocp]
     `twisted.internet.epollreactor.EPollReactor`


**Additional context**

While I was reading the source of `ReconnectingClientFactory` to take a look at the knobs available and the implementation, it stood out to me that the flow is as follows:

```python
class ReconnectingClientFactory(ClientFactory):

    initialDelay = 1.0
    factor = 2.7182818284590451  # (math.e)

    delay = initialDelay

    def retry(self, connector=None):

        self.delay = min(self.delay * self.factor, self.maxDelay)

        self._callID = self.clock.callLater(self.delay, reconnector)
```

The last two lines are in the wrong order; I believe to fix behaviour it should simply become
```python
        self._callID = self.clock.callLater(self.delay, reconnector)

        self.delay = min(self.delay * self.factor, self.maxDelay)
```

problems.title: Twisted should not mutate pyOpenSSL contexts after they've been used to create connections
problems.issue_body:
Currently twisted's various TLS interfaces will mutate a connection after it's been used to create a connection. While pyOpenSSL does not currently prohibit this, it does issue a warning, because this is unsound. In the near future this will be an error in pyOpenSSL: https://github.com/pyca/pyopenssl/pull/1429

You can see the failing tests on that PR.

Current issues I'm aware of:

- https://github.com/twisted/twisted/blob/trunk/src/twisted/protocols/tls.py#L910-L913 (self-evidently mutates the conext after creating a connection)
- https://github.com/twisted/twisted/blob/trunk/src/twisted/internet/_sslverify.py#L1129 (I believe this will happen any time you try to reuse a context for multiple connections)

Resolving the latter, without modifying twisted too much, may require https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/pull/13375

problems.issue_body:
|[](https://github.com/Jon-Work)| @Jon-Work reported| |-|-| |Trac ID|trac#10232| |Type|defect| |Created|2021-07-16 15:56:18Z| I'm trying to configure the supported SSL and TLS versions for a server. I am using the twisted.internet.ssl.CertificateOptions constructor's lowerMaximumSecurityTo parameter. But the configuration I get is not what the documentation says. The documentation says lowerMaximumSecurityTo is "The maximum TLS version to use." Which seems reasonable. The problem is line 78 of src/twisted/internet/_sslverify.py: excludedVersions = [x for x in versions[: versions.index(oldest)]] Since Python's list-slicing excludes the index specified, there is an off-by-one error there. problems.title: regression from 25.5.0: optionsForClientTLS no longer negotiates ALPN
problems.issue_body:
A big disclaimer: I used AI to investigate this, and while it looks plausible I'm lost in the `_sslverify.py` internals, so the reason may be a different one.

It looks like after #12506 passing `"h2"` in `acceptableProtocols` to `optionsForClientTLS()` is not enough to get your client connection negotiate HTTP/2, which can be reproduced using docs/core/examples/tls_alpn_client.py and docs/core/examples/tls_alpn_server.py. In trunk `set_alpn_protos()` is called in `twisted.internet._sslverify.OpenSSLCertificateOptions._makeTLSConnection()` on the *connection* while in 25.5.0 it's called in `twisted.internet._sslverify._setAcceptableProtocols()` on the *context* and `twisted.internet._sslverify.ClientTLSOptions.clientConnectionForTLS()` (in both versions) creates a connection directly, not via `_makeTLSConnection()`.

problems.title: Update typing annotations project wide using `pyupgrade --py39-plus`
problems.issue_body:
This issue tracks the work of applying `pyupgrade --py39-plus` across the Twisted codebase.

`pyupgrade --py39-plus` enables (among other things) the [PEP 585](https://peps.python.org/pep-0585/) typing rewrites (e.g. `List[str]` -> `list[str]`) in an automatic way such that human error by doing this work manually is eliminated.

The goal is to apply this conversion project wide mainly for consistency.

To limit the scope of changes, only `pyupgrade --py39-plus` will be run at first. Later we can also run `pyupgrade --py310-plus` when Python 3.9 support is dropped. But with the Python 3.9+ changes out of the way, then the Python 3.10+ changes will be much smaller and easier to review.

My plan is to focus on one module at a time unless the Git diff is small (less than ~100 lines changed).

Adding `from __future__ import annotations` also allows us to drop `Union` and `Optional`.

problems.title: `assertEquals` test helper was removed
problems.issue_body:
The `assertEquals` alias for unittest's `assertEqual` function was removed in https://github.com/twisted/twisted/pull/12450, specifically [this change](https://github.com/twisted/twisted/pull/12450/changes#diff-54b664956d68a20ebbdbdfad8fd9e742893c165bedca99b0f92c340edc0811daR449).

This was a breaking change, and requires downstream projects to change over to `self.assertEqual` from the plural variant. For example, our canary twisted `trunk` [CI began to fail](https://github.com/element-hq/synapse/actions/runs/20742182131/job/59551104266#step:8:6316).

Personally, updating the code is easy, especially as we caught this ahead of a twisted release. Though, the linked PR resulting in:

https://github.com/twisted/twisted/blob/dd86294dd27207f54d9e2c64b3cccbb6f8a75fd6/src/twisted/trial/_synctest.py#L449

makes me wonder whether this breaking change was intentional, or instead the result of an accidental find/replace.

If it was intentional, I suggest removing the redundant line and putting out a breaking change warning. If not, I'm highlighting the change in case you may wish to revert it. Cheers!

problems.title: Placeholder for future Twisted Names security fix
problems.issue_body:
We're going to disclose this through the normal development process because it's pretty low severity and is not urgent enough to skip the queue.

`twisted.names.dns.DNSDatagramProtocol`, the UDP transport used by twisted's DNS client (`twisted.names.client.Resolver`, `createResolver`, and anything built on it, including MX lookups in `twisted.mail`), accepts a DNS response for a pending query solely on the basis of the 16-bit transaction ID matching. It never checks that the response actually originated from the server the query was sent to. Any host that can deliver a UDP packet to the resolver's listening port with the correct transaction ID can inject a forged answer, independent of the real server's address. This is a materially weaker defense than standard DNS resolver practice (transaction ID plus source-address validation, typically also source-port rotation), and enables off-path DNS response spoofing / cache poisoning.

problems.title: twisted.conch.telnet: unbounded subnegotiation buffer (self.commands) leading to memory-exhaustion DoS
problems.issue_body:
### Summary
In `Telnet.dataReceived` (`src/twisted/conch/telnet.py`), after `IAC SB` opens a subnegotiation the parser enters the `subnegotiation` state and appends every non-`IAC` byte via `self.commands.append(b)` with no length cap. `self.commands` is an instance attribute, released only when `IAC SE` completes the subnegotiation. A peer that opens a subnegotiation and never sends `IAC SE` grows the buffer without bound. Negotiation runs at the transport layer before authentication.

The same unbounded pattern applies to the `subnegotiation-escaped` append path and, as you noted on the report, to `appDataBuffer.append(b)`.

### Reproduction
Send `IAC SB` (`0xFF 0xFA`), then stream any non-`0xFF` bytes and never send `IAC SE` (`0xFF 0xF0`). The buffer grows one element per byte (measured about 8x resident-memory amplification, since each byte is retained as a separate object).

### Impact
Unauthenticated remote memory-exhaustion denial of service. Contrast `NetstringReceiver.MAX_LENGTH`, which caps exactly this kind of buffer elsewhere in Twisted.

### Suggested fix
Add a configurable maximum length to the subnegotiation buffer (and to `appDataBuffer`); drop the oversized subnegotiation or close the connection when it is exceeded.

problems.title: twisted.words xish/domish: unbounded XML element tree (no depth/child/size limit) leading to memory-exhaustion DoS
problems.issue_body: ### Summary `ExpatElementStream._onStartElement` (`src/twisted/words/xish/domish.py`) appends each start tag to `self.currElem.children` and descends into it, with no limit on nesting depth or child count. An element is emitted and dropped only when it closes at top level (`_onEndElement`, `self.currElem.parent is None`). A peer that opens a container and never closes it retains every child, and everything nested inside them, for the life of the stream. `XmlStream.dataReceived` feeds `self.stream.parse(data)` with no size limit, and `addContent` appends character data uncapped. In XMPP the stream is parsed during negotiation before authentication. ### Reproduction Open ``, then stream `x` children and never close ``. Each 8-byte element becomes a full `Element` object (measured about 50x resident-memory amplification). ### Impact Unauthenticated remote memory-exhaustion denial of service on any XMPP or XML-stream service built on this stack. ### On your questions As far as I can see, sux/domish currently does **not** bound tag-name, attribute-name, or attribute-value lengths either. I am glad to help with the broader sux/domish security review you suggested and fold those limits in. ### Suggested fix Configurable limits on nesting depth, retained element count, unfinished-document size, and content length; tear down the stream when any is exceeded (in line with XEP-0205 guidance).

problems.title: twisted.web.http: bare CR or LF in a header value is not rejected (HTTP request smuggling)
problems.issue_body:
### Summary
`HTTPChannel.headerReceived` (`src/twisted/web/http.py`) rejects a NUL byte in a header value but not a bare CR or LF, though RFC 9110 section 5.5 requires all three to be rejected. Because the channel splits on CRLF, `Foo: x\nContent-Length: 39` arrives as one line: the `Content-Length` is folded into the `Foo` value and the request is framed with no body. A front-end that treats the bare LF as a line terminator instead reads the `Content-Length`, so the two disagree on where the request ends.

### Reproduction
Feed one connection `POST /public HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: v\r\nFoo: x\nContent-Length: 44\r\n\r\nGET /admin HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: internal\r\n\r\n`. Twisted parses and serves two requests, so the smuggled `GET /admin` is dispatched; a NUL in the value is rejected, isolating the missing CR/LF checks.

### Impact
HTTP request smuggling (CWE-444) behind a front-end that accepts a bare CR or LF: bypass of front-end access controls, connection/response poisoning, and cache poisoning. No code execution.

### Suggested fix
Reject CR and LF in the value alongside the existing NUL check, as RFC 9110 section 5.5 requires; the header name and request line already reject these characters.

problems.title: twisted.mail IMAP4: negative literal size in SEARCH hangs the reactor (authenticated DoS)
problems.issue_body:
`parseNestedParens` (`src/twisted/mail/imap4.py`) parses an IMAP literal size with `int()` and never rejects a negative value, so `{-100}` drives the cursor negative and the loop never terminates. It is reached from `select_SEARCH` in the selected state, so any authenticated user can send `a3 SEARCH {-100}zzz` and pin the single-threaded reactor forever, freezing every connection and every co-hosted service (e.g. SMTP/POP3 under `twistd mail`) until restart.

Fix: reject a negative literal size with the `ValueError` the parser already raises for a non-numeric literal.

problems.title: twisted.words IRC server: unbounded line buffer allows pre-auth memory-exhaustion DoS
problems.issue_body:
`IRC.dataReceived` (`src/twisted/words/protocols/irc.py`) appends received data to `self.buffer` up to the next line feed with no length limit, and `IRC` is not a `LineReceiver`, so an unauthenticated peer that sends data without a line delimiter grows the buffer until the server runs out of memory. The `twistd words` IRC server inherits this through `IRCUser`, so a single connection can OOM the process before authenticating.

Fix: mirror `twisted.protocols.basic.LineReceiver` with a `MAX_LENGTH` of 16384 and a `lineLengthExceeded` that drops the connection, enforced on the unterminated buffer and on each parsed line. Normal IRC traffic is well under the limit, and the bound also removes a quadratic buffer copy.
