problems.title: The template ref was not set to null correctly after the conditional rendering was updated
Star selectors leak scoped styles into children
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.13

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a component `Foo`
  - Add `class="foo"` on the root element
  - Add a scoped style `.foo * { border: 1px solid red; }`
- Create a component `Bar`
  - Create multiple nested elements (not just a root element)
- Add `<bar/>` into Foo's root

### What is expected?

The star selector should be scoped to inside `Foo`

### What is actually happening?

The star selector isn't being scoped, which causes the styles to leak into child elements

### System Info

```shell

```

### Any additional comments?

The example provided includes a `:first-child` pseudo-class, which makes the behavior (and use case) a bit clearer, however the scoping issues occur regardless of whether the pseudo-class is specified.

We ran into this issue while attempting to upgrade from Vue 2 to Vue 3, where certain selectors that used to be scoped to immediate children were suddenly applying to deep children. The usage sites themselves were flawed in other ways, and should have been using direct child combinators, but those are workarounds and shouldn't be necessary for scoping to apply correctly.

In the past Vue 3 used to mirror Vue 2's behavior, which scopes only the star selector. ([Vue 2 demo](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vue2-vite-starter-x67dqjku?file=src%2Fcomponents%2FHelloWorld.vue)). That behavior itself isn't ideal, which was reported in #10548 and then addressed in #10551, however in doing so it caused the styles to leak to children instead of from parents. More manageable, but still not ideal.

Here's a sample of different selectors and how they compile in Vue 2 vs Vue 3 (`[--]` represents the scoping attribute selector)
```
Source                Vue 2                     Vue 3
:active               [--]:active               [--]:active
*:active              *[--]:active              [--]:active
.foo :first-child     .foo[--] :first-child     .foo[--] :first-child
.foo *                .foo *[--]                .foo[--] *
.foo *:first-child    .foo *[--]:first-child    .foo[--] *:first-child
```

The solution for this would be to scope both the final class selector *and* the star selector:
```
Source                Vue 3 (fixed)
:active               [--]:active
*:active              [--]:active
.foo :first-child     .foo[--] :first-child
.foo *                .foo[--] [--]
.foo *:first-child    .foo[--] [--]:first-child
```

problems.title: Unable to set focus inside of Vue.js-based web components
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.13

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://github.com/padcom/vue-custom-element-delegates-focus

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
npm install
npm start
```


### What is expected?

Just the input is focused:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79290ae3-5005-495d-b371-e8e129e2357f)

### What is actually happening?


Observe that the whole element is focused instead of the input.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5c58bee-cce5-4548-b962-2f315322a43c)

### System Info

```shell
Google Chrome, Firefox - doesn't matter. It's a core deficiency of how Vue.js creates `shadowRoot`
```

### Any additional comments?

This is a critical issue for any type of web component that provides users with interactions. It blocks proper keyboard navigation and programmatic focusing of elements.

## More information

When creating custom web components that have focus-able parts (like inputs or buttons) the focus is first set to the custom element itself. That is why, in the example provided, the outline is showing for the entire element instead of the input.

To be able to focus elements inside the web component one needs to add the `delegatesFocus` to options alongside `mode: 'open'`. This, when the `focus()` method is called on the web component, will look for the first focus-able element and shift the focus there instead.

MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ShadowRoot/delegatesFocus

There are more options that can be set when creating the `shadowRoot` using `this.attachShadow()` call, but `delegatesFocus` is the key for focusing subelements.

problems.issue_body: ### Vue version 3.3.13 ### Link to minimal reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-gqtzmr?file=src%2FApp.vue ### Steps to reproduce - Create a new project with `npm create vue@latest -- --router` - Replace all the presence of `@` in the project with `#src` - Run either `npm run dev` or `npm run build && npm run preview` ### What is expected? The webpage correctly displays the Vue logo in both cases. ### What is actually happening? The `` `src` URL stays unchanged as `#src/assets/logo.svg`, fails to be transformed into an `import` from the `#src/assets/logo.svg` module, therefore can't be resolved. ### System Info ```shell System: OS: macOS 14.2.1 CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M1 Pro Memory: 275.08 MB / 32.00 GB Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 18.18.2 - ~/Library/Caches/fnm_multishells/1919_1703087524164/bin/node Yarn: 1.22.19 - ~/Library/Caches/fnm_multishells/1919_1703087524164/bin/yarn npm: 10.2.0 - ~/Library/Caches/fnm_multishells/1919_1703087524164/bin/npm pnpm: 8.12.1 - ~/Library/Caches/fnm_multishells/1919_1703087524164/bin/pnpm bun: 1.0.3 - ~/.bun/bin/bun Browsers: Chrome: 120.0.6099.109 Chrome Canary: 122.0.6206.0 Safari: 17.2.1 npmPackages: vue: ^3.3.11 => 3.3.13 ``` ### Any additional comments? **The Use Case** I want to change the default alias to `src/` in `create-vue` to `#src/`, replacing the current `@/`. Because: - Node.js supports subpath imports (the `imports` field in `package.json`) in all actively maintained versions (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v20.x/api/packages.html#subpath-imports) - Both [Vite](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/19e3c9a8a16847486fbad8a8cd48fc771b1538bb/playground/resolve/imports-path) and [webpack](https://github.com/webpack/webpack/issues/12928) can read this field from `package.json` directly. Considering the Vue.js documentation claims `src` imports follow the same path resolution rules as webpack module requests, it should be supported in Vue, too. - TypeScript is going to read from `imports` field automatically in 5.4 (https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/pull/55015) Therefore, using `#src` could reduce a lot of duplicate configurations in the templates. The only missing part is Vue's asset URL rewriting. **The Cause** The `transformAssetUrl` function skips attribute values starting with `#`. https://github.com/vuejs/core/blob/a8d0b1b38b092ec2d10b32bedcee2eea33b77657/packages/compiler-sfc/src/template/transformAssetUrl.ts#L110 But now that `#src` is a valid import specifier in Node.js, I think we can't skip such strings blindly. Actually, of all the default `transformAssetUrl.tags`, I find that only `use[href]` could possibly point to a URL fragment. In all the other tag and attribute combinations, when assigned a `#string`-style value, it can only be an aliased import path.

problems.title: Injection breaks when nesting Vue custom elements
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.0 - 3.5.13

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

Create two custom elements using Vue's `defineCustomElement` (`outer-component` and `inner-component`). In both `defineCustomElement` calls, use `configureApp` to `provide` a value. Then, nest `inner-component` within `outer-component`.

### What is expected?

I expect that both custom elements get their own isolated injection scope. Values that are provided on `inner-component` are not visible on `outer-component`, and vice versa.

Or, even if `inner-component` has access to the values provided by `outer-component`, I expect that it definitely has access to the values provided on `inner-component` and those have precedence.

### What is actually happening?

The injection scope of `outer-component` is applied to `inner-component`.

This means that when using `inject` in `inner-component`, only values that are provided on `outer-component` can be injected. Values provided on `inner-component` are not injectable within `inner-component`.

problems.title: Update of component prop before hydration causes hydration to fail
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.13

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-enjfxm8b?file=src%2FApp.vue,src%2FFoo.vue

### Steps to reproduce

I recommend to open browser dev console to see the errors when the "bug" is reproduced. As soon as the hydration fails we get an error, following this we get an error each time we update a prop to the component that failed hydration.

1. Build stackblitz minimal reproduction
2. Resize stackblitz preview to be larger than 100px wide
2. Reload stackblitz preview (If it wasnt already 100px+ wide)
3. Press toggle button one or more times
4. Resize stackblitz preview width to be less than 100px to hydrate the Foo component
5. Now the Foo component no longer reacts to prop updates

### What is expected?

I would expect the component to hydrate successfully and function correctly even if its reactive props are updated before hydration, perhaps with a hydration warning. Alternatively, it would be reasonable if updating a prop before hydration could automatically trigger that component's hydration process without needing a custom hydration function.

### What is actually happening?

If a reactive prop is updated before the component consuming it has finished hydrating, the hydration process for that component fails. Consequently, the component becomes unresponsive to any further updates of that prop after the failed hydration attempt.

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Linux 5.0 undefined
    CPU: (8) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9880H CPU @ 2.30GHz
    Memory: 0 Bytes / 0 Bytes
    Shell: 1.0 - /bin/jsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 20.19.1 - /usr/local/bin/node
    Yarn: 1.22.19 - /usr/local/bin/yarn
    npm: 10.8.2 - /usr/local/bin/npm
    pnpm: 8.15.6 - /usr/local/bin/pnpm
  npmPackages:
    vue: ^3.5.13 => 3.5.13
```

### Any additional comments?

It feels sub-optimal to not be able to use the build-in hydrate functions in combination with a reactive prop without having to worry about the hydration failing. Currently a custom hydrate function needs to be used as soon as we want a reactive property on a component that has delayed hydration or we need to make sure that the prop cant update before the component is hydrated. It would be very neat and less error prone to not have to worry about these problems, both with custom hydration functions and with built-in hydration functions. 

It is also worth noting that this behaviour occurs with all tested hydration methods. It can be mitigated by adding a once watcher that calls hydrate whenever a prop to that component is updated.

A version of this issue was originally reported as a [nuxt issue](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/31787)

problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

The issue disappears with any of these modifications:
- One of the nested `div`s in the child component receiving the fallthrough attr is removed
- The attribute of one of the `div`s is changed to an unknown HTML attribute or removed
- The comment in the child is removed

### What is expected?

The `style` attribute applied by the parent component should be applied to the root `div` of the child component

### What is actually happening?

The attribute is not applied

### System Info

```shell

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-pn21u36z?file=src%2Fcomponents%2FHelloWorld.vue,src%2Fcomponents%2FBox.vue,src%2FApp.vue,src%2Fmain-ce.js,index.html,vite.config.js,src%2FApp.ce.vue&terminal=dev

### Steps to reproduce

Open the page and wait until load.

### What is expected?

I would expect the first box to be red and the second box to be green.

### What is actually happening?

The first box is red, also second is red.

Generally speaking this is something that can potentially be avoided by using CSS selector specifity. But the issue here is that the behavior is inconsistent between standard Vue app and the app bundled as web component. 

Basically the issue here is that there is some "box" component which has its `class="box"` and some "nested" component which uses "box", but applies additional class and style. Like

```
Box.vue
<style scoped>
.box { background-color: red }
</style>

...
HelloWorld.vue
<style scoped>
.my-box{ background-color: green}
</style>

<template>
<Box class="my-box"></Box>
</template>
```

So, in normal Vue app (if you switch the mode in Vite config in example) the styles will get applied from deepest to most shallow, like `Box` styles will be injected into DOM and then `HelloWorld` styles. For CE that's not (always?) the case and styles get applied "in order", so `HelloWorld` gets injected before `Box`. 

I've been trying to find some info regarding this behavior, but I only found the general PR @11517 which adds some support to web component styles. Is it something that is anyhow achievable to behave like normal Vue app ? Or is there some oversight from my side here ?

I would gladly take a look at this if I'd been given a bit of a guidance here, where approximately should I look into, is it core, or maybe compiler etc. ?

problems.title: Using `watch` to observe a prop in a vue custom element, the other props accessed in the listener are the old values.
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.11

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add custom components in the `<template>` of the parent component with different prop orders.  
```html
<template>
  <test-el :prop1="value1" :prop2="value2"></test-el>
  <test-el :prop2="value2" :prop1="value1"></test-el>
</template>
```  
2. Use `watch` in the child component to monitor changes in a prop and record the value of another prop.  
```js
  watch: {
    prop1: {
      handler(val) {
        console.log('prop1 changed, prop2 is ', this.prop2)
        this.tempProp2 = this.prop2
      },
    },
    prop2: {
      handler(val) {
        console.log('prop2 changed, prop1 is', this.prop1)
        this.tempProp1 = this.prop1
      },
    },
  },
```
3. Update the prop value in the parent component.  
```js
const value1 = ref('old value1')
const value2 = ref('old value2')

setTimeout(() => {
  value1.value = 'new value1'
  value2.value = 'new value2'
}, 0)
```
4. Observe the results.


### What is expected?

The `watch` listener in a custom element can access the latest prop values.

### What is actually happening?

For a custom element, when using `watch` to observe a prop, accessing the values of other props defined later in the order within the listener will return their old values.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the minimal reproduction and observe the following compiler error:
```
[plugin:vite:vue] [@vue/compiler-sfc] Failed to resolve extends base type.
```
2. Open the `tsconfig.app.json` file and uncomment the following lines:
```
  // "compilerOptions": {
  //   "paths": {
  //     "@/*": ["src/*"]
  //   }
  // },
  // "include": ["src/**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx", "src/**/*.vue"],
```
3. In the terminal type `r` then press enter to reload the dev server
4. The compiler error should disappear

### What is expected?

There should not be a compiler error at any point, as the two versions of the tsconfig file are parsed identically by TypeScript.

### What is actually happening?

When using a tsconfig that extends another tsconfig, and the extended config uses the `${configDir}` magic string in the `include` or `compilerOptions.paths` settings, Vue fails to resolve imported base types for types passed to the `defineProps` macro.

problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

### Steps to reproduce

Add a `v-else` element right after it.

Add one or more additional `v-else` elements after that.

Only the last `v-else` is recognized. The rest are silently ignored.

### What is expected?

This syntax should either:

- throw a compile-time error, or
- 
- trigger a warning, or
- 
- at the very least, be caught by the Vue ESLint plugin as invalid usage.

Allowing multiple `v-else` blocks after a single `v-if` is logically invalid and likely always unintentional. It can lead to subtle bugs and confusion during development.



### What is actually happening?

No errors or warnings are shown. Only the last `v-else` is used, and the rest are ignored without any indication.

This makes it easy to introduce bugs, especially in larger templates or when components are modified over time.

### Steps to reproduce

When provide() is called, it creates a new Object with the prototype of the previous parent's providers, however when this is done in overlap like it is here, it skips one.

- Component 4 has Component 3's provides (which is Component 1's provides)

- Component 1 has Object.create(App.provides)
- Component 2 has Object.create(Component 1.provides)
- Component 3 has Component 2's provides
- Component 4 has Component 3's old provides (which is Component 1's provides) [Note: Here lies the issue.]

problems.title: [Regression 3.5.25] @vue/compat: Crash in warnDeprecation when processing COMPONENT_V_MODEL (instance.appContext is unde
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version 3.5.25 ### Link to minimal reproduction see below ### Steps to reproduce 1. Use `@vue/compat` with Vue 3.5.25. 2. Configure compat mode to Vue 2 (`MODE: 2`). 3. Create a component that accepts `v-model` (legacy usage). 4. Run the application. ```html Vue 3.5.25 Compat Crash Reproduction
``` [Reproduction.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24157211/Reproduction.html) ### What is expected? A deprecation warning (`COMPONENT_V_MODEL`) should be logged to the console, but the application should continue to run. ### What is actually happening? The application crashes with the following error in the browser console: ``` Uncaught TypeError: can't access property "components", instance.appContext is undefined VueJS 18 formatComponentName warnDeprecation$1 convertLegacyVModelProps createBaseVNode _createVNode createVNodeWithArgsTransform render renderComponentRoot componentUpdateFn run setupRenderEffect mountComponent processComponent patch render _compat_mount createCompatApp Vue2 ``` ### System Info ```shell ``` ### Any additional comments? It seems that `convertLegacyVModelProps` passes a pseudo-instance object (`{ type }`) to `warnDeprecation`. However, inside `warnDeprecation` (specifically when calling `formatComponentName`), it attempts to access `instance.appContext`, which is undefined on this pseudo-instance. This causes the app to crash instead of just emitting a warning. The current workaround is to suppress the warning: `Vue.configureCompat({ COMPONENT_V_MODEL: "suppress-warning" });`

problems.title: Slot Name Case Sensitivity Issue in DOM Templates（DOM 模板中插槽名称未转译）
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.26

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-xgjrdt9z?file=index.html&terminal=dev

### Steps to reproduce

1. 打开链接：https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-xgjrdt9z?file=index.html&terminal=dev
2. 点击 Select 组件，可以看到 dropdownRender 插槽未生效。

### What is expected?

在 DOM 模板中使用驼峰命名的插槽名称时，插槽内容应该能够正确渲染，就像在单文件组件（SFC）中一样。

### What is actually happening?

在 DOM 模板（HTML 文件）中使用驼峰命名（camelCase）的插槽名称时，插槽内容无法正常渲染。这是因为浏览器会将 HTML 属性名转换为小写，而 Vue 的插槽匹配需要完全匹配大小写。

### System Info

```shell

```

### Any additional comments?

When using camelCase slot names in DOM templates (HTML files), the slot content fails to render because the browser converts HTML attribute names to lowercase, but Vue's slot matching requires exact case matching.

Slot content should render correctly when using camelCase slot names in DOM templates, similar to how it works in Single File Components (SFC).

1. Open the following link:
https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-xgjrdt9z?file=index.html&terminal=dev
2. Click the Select component. You will see that the dropdownRender slot does not take effect.

problems.title: Transition enter-cancelled not called on asynchronous rendering
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.10

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

Render two components asynchronously after a short timeout.
The first component adds a tooltip with a transition. It is visible at first.
The second component then sets the visibility of the tooltip (via composable) to false.
If this action is not done with a `nextTick` the tooltip is still visible.

In the reproduction link the bug happens immediately, since it is caused by the transition.
The tooltip should not be visible at all.

The wrong behaviour can be viewed in the console.log. The `enter` is called after `leave`, although it should not be visible.
To view the correct behaviour you can comment out the according lines in Test.vue like this:

```javascript
// DOES NOT WORK
//setVisibility(false)

// WORKS
nextTick(() => setVisibility(false))
```

### What is expected?

It is expected that the tooltip is not visible and the order of events for the transitions should look like this:
```javascript
isVisible: true
"before-enter"
"enter"
isVisible: false
"enter-cancelled"
"before-leave"
"leave"
"after-leave"
```

### What is actually happening?

The tooltip is visible and the transition events look like this:
```javascript
isVisible: true
"before-enter"
isVisible: false
"before-leave"
"leave"
"enter"
"after-enter"
```

### System Info

_No response_

### Any additional comments?

It is also notable that the template of the tooltip is not reactive anymore.
Even though the watchEffect logs `isVisible: false`, the template still displays `true`.

problems.title: [Vapor] The prop `is` of Vapor components does not support dynamic binding via `v-bind`
problems.issue_body: ### Vue version 3.6.0-beta.7 ### Link to minimal reproduction https://play.vuejs.org/# ### Steps to reproduce 1. Define the prop for the Vapor component and use it in the template ```ts // Child.vue withDefaults(defineProps<{ is: string }>(), { is: 'Child' }) ``` ```html ``` 2. Use the Vapor component in the parent component and pass `:is="'Parent'"` via `v-bind` 3. At this point, the page displays `Child` and a warning is shown indicating that a required prop is missing. The `v-bind` passing method is supported in VDOM mode. ### What is expected? 1. When passing the `is` prop to a Vapor component via `v-bind` (e.g., `:is="'Parent'"`), the component should correctly receive and render the dynamically bound value (`Parent`), instead of falling back to the default value (`Child`). 2. No false warning about a "required prop missing" should be thrown when the `is` prop is passed via `v-bind` (consistent with the behavior in VDOM mode). ### What is actually happening? 1. When passing the `is` prop to the Vapor component via `v-bind` (i.e., `:is="'Parent'"`), the component **does not** receive the dynamically bound value `Parent` — instead, it renders the default value `Child` (defined via `withDefaults`). 2. A false warning is thrown in the console indicating that the required `is` prop is missing, even though the prop is explicitly passed via `v-bind`. 3. This behavior is inconsistent with VDOM mode (where `v-bind` for the `is` prop works as expected, with no false warnings). ### System Info ```shell ``` ### Any additional comments? _No response_

problems.title: Teleport + Suspense unmount crash during page navigation in Nuxt SSR (regression in 3.5.31)
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.31

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://github.com/Gabriel-SPassos/vue-teleport-regression

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Gabriel-SPassos/vue-teleport-regression
cd vue-teleport-regression
npm install
npm run dev
```

1. Open http://localhost:3000
2. Click **"Go"**
3. Check the browser console

### What is expected?

Navigation to Page B completes without errors. Teleported elements from the previous page are cleanly unmounted.

### What is actually happening?

**Dev mode** (`npm run dev`):

```
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at queuePostFlushCb
    at queueEffectWithSuspense
    at Object.process
    at flushPostFlushCbs
    at flushJobs
```

Infinite recursion in the scheduler — deferred Teleport post-flush callbacks create a loop between `queueEffectWithSuspense` and `flushJobs`.

**Production mode**  — observed in a real-world Nuxt app:

```
TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'bum' of 'y' as it is null.
    at unmountComponent
    at unmount
    at Object.remove (Teleport.remove)
```

The page freezes — URL updates but the UI does not re-render.

**Vue 3.5.30**: No errors in either dev or production mode. Navigation works as expected.

### System Info

```
System:
  OS: macOS 15.5
  Node: v20.19.0
Binaries:
  npm: 10.8.2
npmPackages:
  vue: 3.5.31
  nuxt: ^4.1.1
```

### Any additional comments?

**Scenario:**
- Nuxt 4 app with SSR enabled
- Page A (`index.vue`): `await useFetch()` in setup (triggers Suspense wrapping by `<NuxtPage>`), two `<teleport to="body">` blocks each containing a `<Transition>` wrapping `v-if` content with nested child components, reactive state changes after `navigateTo()` (clearing items array + resetting a flag in `finally`)
- Page B (`page-b.vue`): has async setup (`await useFetch(...)`) and its own `<teleport to="body">`
- The crash occurs during the Suspense branch swap — deferred Teleport post-flush callbacks create an infinite loop in the scheduler

**Candidate PRs merged between 3.5.30 and 3.5.31:**

| PR | Description | Suspicion |
|---|---|---|
| #9392 | fix(suspense): avoid unmount activeBranch twice if wrapped in transition | High |
| #8619 | fix(runtime-dom): defer teleport mount/update until suspense resolves | High |
| #12922 | fix(suspense): update suspense vnode's el during branch self-update | Medium |

The interaction between #8619 (deferring Teleport operations when `parentSuspense.pendingBranch` exists) and #9392 (changing Suspense unmount timing when wrapped in Transition) appears to create this issue during Nuxt's page navigation cycle (Suspense + Transition + Teleport).

**Workaround:** Pin `vue` to `3.5.30`:

```json
{
  "overrides": {
    "vue": "3.5.30"
  }
}
```

problems.title: [Teleport] TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'subTree') during Suspense resolve — regression in 3.5.32
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.32

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the reproduction link (Vue 3.5.32)
2. Open browser console
3. See `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'subTree')` on page load
4. Switch Vue version to 3.5.31 → error disappears

### What is expected?

No error. The page renders correctly (works in 3.5.31).

### What is actually happening?

Crash on page load:
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'subTree') at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8744:28) at Object.moveTeleport [as move] (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:3443:9) at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8752:12) at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8744:7) at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8758:9) at move (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:8744:7) at Object.resolve (runtime-dom.esm-browser.js:9498:11)

### System Info

```shell
...
```

### Any additional comments?

**Regression introduced by PR #14642.**

Root cause: `queuePendingMount()` in Teleport.ts defers mount when `parentSuspense.pendingBranch` exists (including for disabled Teleports). During `Suspense.resolve()`, `move(pendingBranch)` runs before the deferred mount job. When `moveTeleport` encounters a disabled Teleport in REORDER mode, it iterates children — but children's `vnode.component` is `null` because `mountChildren` was never called.

PR #14642's test cases only covered **element children** (`h('div', 'text')`) inside Teleport. This bug requires **component children** (`h(Comp)`) inside a disabled Teleport, inside a Suspense-wrapped async component with a multi-root (Fragment) template.

Trigger conditions (all required):
1. `<Suspense>` wrapping an async component (with `await` in setup)
2. Multi-root template (Fragment) in the async component
3. `<Teleport disabled>` as a root sibling
4. Component child (not element) inside the Teleport

- **3.5.30**: No error
- **3.5.31**: No error
- **3.5.32**: Crash

I'd like to submit a fix PR for this.

problems.title: defineProps runtime props inference misses Array from MaybeRef<T[]> in union type after upgrading to Vue 3.5.31
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.31

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://github.com/wuchunxu/vite-prop-runtime-repro

### Steps to reproduce

After upgrading Vue from `3.5.21` to `3.5.31`, runtime props inference from `defineProps<T>()` changed for a complex union type.

I have a prop type like this:

```ts
export type FormItemOptions<T = any, Context = any> =
  MaybeRef<OptionItem[]>
  | Promise<OptionItem[]>
  | ((row: T, context: Context) => Awaitable<OptionItem[]>)
```

In built output, Vue generates runtime prop type as:

```js
options: {
  type: [Promise, Function],
  default: () => []
}
```

`Array` is missing, so passing an array value triggers runtime warning:

```txt
[Vue warn]: Invalid prop: type check failed for prop "options". Expected Promise | Function, got Array
```

If I explicitly add `OptionItem[]` in the union (instead of relying only on `MaybeRef<OptionItem[]>`), the generated runtime type includes `Array` and warning disappears.


### What is expected?

Runtime props inference should include `Array` branch (or at least not narrow in a way that rejects valid array values from `MaybeRef<OptionItem[]>`).

For this case, expected generated runtime type should include:

```js
type: [Array, Promise, Function]
```

### What is actually happening?

Generated runtime type is:

```js
type: [Promise, Function]
```

which rejects array values at runtime.


### System Info

```shell

```

### Any additional comments?

This looks like a boundary case in SFC type-to-runtime props inference for complex union types involving `MaybeRef<T[]>`.

If this should be tracked in another Vue package (e.g. `compiler-sfc`), please let me know and I can move the issue with the same repro.

Sibling nodes in the same Fragment (e.g. an `<h4>`) are removed correctly - only the Transition/Suspense subtree leaks.

I came across this from (as a Member) nuxt/nuxt#34859 - it surfaces there because <NuxtPage> renders exactly this structure internally. - A descendant component with async setup (so Suspense actually suspends)
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
What I observed while debugging: the component lifecycle looks clean - `onUnmounted` fires for every leaving instance. But the DOM subtree stays attached to the container anyway. This points at the out-in leave path interacting badly with suspensible Suspense: the  `afterLeave` callback that should call `hostRemove(el)` never runs, because the surrounding <Transition> itself is torn down before it gets a chance to fire.

problems.title: Teleport + Suspense: unmount crashes on pending teleport with component child (regression since 3.5.31)
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.34

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://github.com/pont1s/vue-teleport-unmount-crashes

### Steps to reproduce

#### Option 1 — Browser (primary)

```bash
pnpm dev
```

1. Open the browser DevTools console.
2. Click **"Unmount Suspense"**.
3. Observe `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'type')` in the console

#### Option 2 — Tests (additional)

```bash
pnpm test
```

The repo also contains three Vitest tests in `tests/teleport-unmount.test.js`

### What is expected?

When a <Teleport> inside a <Suspense> is unmounted before its mount can run, Vue should remove it cleanly. This worked correctly in 3.5.30.

### What is actually happening?

In 3.5.31..3.5.34, unmounting such a teleport throws:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'type')
    at unmountComponent       (runtime-core.cjs.js)
    at unmount
    at Object.remove          (TeleportImpl.remove)
    at unmount
    at unmountChildren
    at unmount
    at unmountComponent
    at unmount
    at Object.resolve         (Suspense)
```

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: macOS 26.3.1
    CPU: (8) arm64 Apple M1
    Memory: 102.19 MB / 16.00 GB
    Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh
  Binaries:
    Node: 24.15.0 - /Users/user/.local/state/fnm_multishells/14407_1779493498078/bin/node
    npm: 11.12.1 - /Users/user/.local/state/fnm_multishells/14407_1779493498078/bin/npm
    pnpm: 11.1.3 - /Users/user/.local/state/fnm_multishells/14407_1779493498078/bin/pnpm
  Browsers:
    Chrome: 148.0.7778.179
    Safari: 26.3.1
  npmPackages:
    vue: 3.5.34 => 3.5.34
```

### Any additional comments?

This is a continuation of the regression chain that started in 3.5.31:

- **PR [#8619](https://github.com/vuejs/core/pull/8619)** (3.5.31) introduced `pendingMounts` so teleports defer their mount when `parentSuspense.pendingBranch` is set. This is what created the situation where a teleport's children can have `vnode.component === null`.
- **Issue [#14640](https://github.com/vuejs/core/issues/14640)** + **PR [#14642](https://github.com/vuejs/core/pull/14642)** (3.5.32) added the `pendingMount` check shown above. That gates DOM removal of *element* children, not the `unmountComponent(null, …)` call on *component* children.
- **Issue [#14699](https://github.com/vuejs/core/issues/14699)** (3.5.32)  reported the same crash with the same stack as this issue. Closed by the author with a note about re-filing with a more accurate reproduction.
- **Issue [#14701](https://github.com/vuejs/core/issues/14701)** + **PR [#14702](https://github.com/vuejs/core/pull/14702)** (3.5.33) added `pendingMounts.has(vnode)` guard, but only in `moveTeleport`. The `TeleportImpl.remove` path was not touched, so 3.5.33 and 3.5.34 still crash.

problems.title: compiler-core: :key expression not prefixed when element has v-memo without v-for (ReferenceError at runtime)
problems.issue_body:
### Version
3.5.35

### Reproduction link
[play.vuejs.org/](https://play.vuejs.org/#)







### Steps to reproduce
Open the playground link; it throws on load.
The trigger is v-memo + dynamic :key on a plain element without v-for, where the key references a prop

### What is expected?
:key expression is prefixed like any other (__props.updateKey / _ctx.updateKey), as in ≤3.5.12

### What is actually happening?
transformExpression skips the :key expression whenever the element has v-memo (the !(memo && arg.content === 'key') check added in 99009ee / PR #12014), assuming transformFor processed it eagerly — but that only happens when v-for is also present.

Plain elements fall through → unprefixed key → ReferenceError at runtime

---
This happened after vue version update.

We hit this in a component library's scroll-container component. It renders custom scrollbars, so its reactive scroll state changes on every scroll frame; to keep large slotted content (e.g. a table body with thousands of cells) from re-rendering on each frame, the content wrapper uses v-memo="[updateKey]" with :key="updateKey" on the same element — "freeze this subtree, and when the parent bumps updateKey (data reload, layout change), rebuild it from scratch instead of diffing."

This compiled and ran correctly up to compiler 3.5.12; from 3.5.13 the generated render function references the key as a bare identifier and every page using the component throws ReferenceError on first render.

Current workaround: v-bind="{ key: updateKey }" instead of :key="updateKey", which bypasses the skipped code path and produces a correctly prefixed expression.

The script renders 500 fresh SSR apps, which all get garbage-collected. Then renders **one** app whose slot content throws, then renders 500 more identical healthy apps, which will never be garbage collected afterwards.

A dynamic component `<component :is>` with a `<slot />` is needed for this to reproduce.

problems.title: EffectScope stop() causes runtime crash (Cannot read properties of undefined) when dynamic scope cleanup mutates parent.
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.28

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

Open the reproduction link.
Click the "Trigger сrash" button.
Observe the output status on the screen or check the browser console.

### What is expected?

The parent scope should stop all its children successfully. When a child scope stops a sibling scope during the cleanup phase, the parent traversal loop should handle the array mutation gracefully without throwing errors.

### What is actually happening?

The application crashes with the following error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'stop')

This happens because EffectScope.stop loops over this.scopes using a cached length l. During iteration, one child's onScopeDispose calls stop() on its sibling. The sibling removes itself from the parent's scopes array, reducing the array size. When the parent loop continues to the cached index l, it tries to access an element out of bounds (which is undefined), causing the runtime crash.

### System Info

```shell
System: OS: macOS, Browser: Chrome, Node: v20.19.5
```

### Any additional comments?

The bug lies in packages/reactivity/src/effectScope.ts.

Inside EffectScope, the methods pause(), resume(), and stop() loop over this.scopes using a cached length without accounting for array mutations. Creating a shallow copy of the array before iterating (e.g. const scopes = this.scopes.slice()) safely resolves the issue.

problems.title: hydrateOnVisible: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nodeType') when the SSR node is detached before the Intersect
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.33 

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-ktsycrrc?file=repro.mjs

### Steps to reproduce

1. SSR-render an async component that uses hydrate: hydrateOnVisible().
2. On the client, hydration is deferred and the strategy registers an IntersectionObserver on the component's SSR node.
3. The node gets detached from the document before the observer's callback executes (in production this is a route change / re-render while the intersection callback is already queued).
4. The observer callback runs and invokes hydrate() against the now-detached node.

### What is expected?

A node that is no longer connected to the document should simply not be hydrated (there's nothing to hydrate), no exception thrown.

### What is actually happening?

hydrate() reaches hydrateNode, which computes the container type from the node's parent:

```
// packages/runtime-core/src/hydration.ts — inside hydrateNode, async-component branch
nextNode = vnode.type.hydrate(
  node, vnode, parentComponent, parentSuspense,
  getContainerType(parentNode(node)),   // parentNode(node) === null for a detached node
  slotScopeIds, optimized, rendererInternals, hydrateNode,
)
```

```
// packages/runtime-core/src/hydration.ts
const getContainerType = (container) => {
  if (container.nodeType !== 1) return undefined   // <-- container is null -> throws
  ...
}
```

For a detached node parentNode(node) is null, so getContainerType(null) throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'nodeType').

The async-component hydration wrapper only guards against the patched case, never against disconnection:

```
// packages/runtime-core/src/apiAsyncComponent.ts — __asyncHydrate
const performHydrate = () => {
  if (patched) { /* warn + */ return }   // only guards `patched`
  hydrate()                              // no isConnected check
}
```
Because the strategy runs inside load().then(...), the throw surfaces as an unhandledrejection, so app-level try/catch around the component can't catch it.

### System Info

```shell
vue: 3.5.33
@vue/server-renderer: 3.5.33
Environment where it triggers: Android WebView (Chrome), production SSR + client hydration
```

### Any additional comments?

problems.title: Suspense: flushing buffered effects overflows the call stack when many effects accumulate while pending (RangeError: Max
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.5.39 (also reproduces on 3.5.40 / `@b5f8518` in the playground)

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the playground and show the **Preview** pane.
2. The app renders a `<Suspense>` whose default slot contains an async component (resolves after ~4s) plus a large tree (2000 rows, each with a few `flush: 'post'` watchers).
3. While the suspense is pending, a timer keeps mutating a ref, so the still-mounted tree re-renders repeatedly. Each re-render buffers its post effects into `suspense.effects` (via `queueEffectWithSuspense`).
4. When the async component resolves, the suspense flushes the buffered effects.

### What is expected?

The buffered effects flush and the app keeps working.

### What is actually happening?

`Uncaught (in promise): RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` — thrown from `queuePostFlushCb` called by `suspense.resolve()`:

```text
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at queuePostFlushCb (runtime-core.esm-bundler.js:331)
    at Object.resolve   (runtime-core.esm-bundler.js:7426)
```

The scheduler dies mid-flush, leaving the app permanently wedged (blank page).

### Root cause

`suspense.effects` is unbounded — every post effect of every component under a pending suspense boundary is buffered into it. On resolve, the whole array is flushed with a spread call:

- `scheduler.ts`: `pendingPostFlushCbs.push(...cb)`
- `scheduler.ts` (`flushPostFlushCbs` nested case): `activePostFlushCbs.push(...deduped)`
- `Suspense.ts` (merge into pending parent): `parent.effects.push(...effects)`

Spreading an array into a function call is limited by the engine's call stack (~100k–200k args in V8), so once enough effects accumulate the flush itself throws.

### Real-world impact

We hit this in production in a Nuxt app: a kanban board page with ~1000 mounted cards that re-renders once per second (elapsed-time ticker). Navigating to another page keeps the board mounted under `<NuxtPag…

problems.issue_body:
### Vue version 3.6.0-rc.2 (also reproduces on 3.6.0-rc.1) ### Link to minimal reproduction https://gist.github.com/doodlewind/894691dae0f8807dbfad7efbcb2bdd1e ### Steps to reproduce ```sh npm i vue@3.6.0-rc.2 happy-dom node repro.mjs ``` (happy-dom only supplies a spec-compliant `document` for Node — nothing else in the environment is custom.) The essence: a **functional** vapor component — a bare function, no props declaration — whose compiled template binds an attribute on its root element, while the parent passes a same-named attr: ```js // compiled shape of:
hello
const t0 = template("
hello
", true); const Functional = (props) => { const el = t0(); renderEffect(() => setProp(el, "title", props.title)); return el; }; Functional.__vapor = true; createVaporApp({ setup: () => createComponentWithFallback(Functional, { title: () => "from-props" }), }).mount(root); ``` ### What is expected? `
hello
` — matching both vdom functional components and vapor object components. Full matrix from the repro: | case | result | |---|---| | vapor object component (`defineVaporComponent`), no props declared | `
` ✅ | | vapor object component, `props: ["title"]` declared | `
` ✅ | | **vapor functional component (bare function)** | **`
` — attribute gone** ❌ | | vdom functional component (bare function), no props declared | `
` ✅ | ### What is actually happening? The attribute is written by nobody: 1. With no props declaration, `title` lands in `instance.attrs` and `hasFallthrough` is true. 2. The component's **own** `renderEffect(() => setProp(el, "title", …))` is suppressed by `shouldSkipFallthroughKey` (`runtime-vapor/src/dom/prop.ts`): it skips any root-element key present in `instance.attrs`, on the assumption that fallthrough will own that key. 3. But because `isFunction(component)`, fallthrough uses `getFunctionalFallthrough`, which forwards **only `class` / `style` / `on*`** — `title` is filtered out and never applied. Step 2's assumption ("fallthrough will re-apply this key") is broken exactly for functional components: any non-class/style/event key that is both passed by the parent and bound by the component's own template silently disappears. Object components take the same path safely because their `getFallthroughAttrs` is the unfiltered `() => instance.attrs`. A possible direction: `shouldSkipFallthroughKey` could skip only keys the fallthrough will actually re-apply — for function-typed components that's `class`/`style`/`isOn(key)` rather than `key in instance.attrs`. Workarounds we use meanwhile: declare props (or wrap with `defineVaporComponent(fn, { props })`), or avoid prop names that collide with attributes the component binds on its own root. ### Any additional comments? problems.title: [Vapor] <Transition> does not animate VDOM content passed through <slot> (vaporInteropPlugin)
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

`3.6.0-rc.2`

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://github.com/y-masuda-saraits/vue-vapor-transition-interop-repro

### Steps to reproduce

```
npm install --legacy-peer-deps
npm test        # 5 tests: 4 pass, 1 fails — the failing case (BUG A) is the bug
```

Or in a browser: `npm run dev`, click "toggle", and compare the two boxes.

### What is expected?

A Vapor `<Transition>` wrapping a `<slot />` should apply enter/leave transitions to the slotted child — the same as a VDOM `<Transition>` does, and the same as a Vapor `<Transition>` already does for Vapor children and for a **directly-rendered** VDOM child.

### What is actually happening?

When the slotted child is **VDOM content delivered through `<slot>`** (from a VDOM parent via `vaporInteropPlugin`), it is mounted/unmounted **instantly with no transition** — no `*-enter-*` / `*-leave-*` classes are applied.

The automated test verifies the **leave** transition: each case starts shown, toggles `show` `true` → `false`, and on the next tick checks whether the `.box` child is mid-leave (still in the DOM with a `fade-leave-*` class) or was removed instantly.

| Case | Wrapper | Child | rc.2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| CONTROL | vdom `<transition>` | vdom via `<slot>` | ✅ `fade-leave-from/active` applied |
| SANITY B | vapor `<transition>` | direct **vapor** child | ✅ animates |
| SANITY C | vapor `<transition>` | **vapor** child via `<slot>` | ✅ animates |
| SANITY D | vapor `<transition>` | direct **vdom** child component | ✅ animates |
| **BUG A** | **vapor `<transition>`** | **vdom child via `<slot>`** | ❌ `{stillPresent:false, classes:null}` |

**Isolation:** it is *not* that VDOM children can't live under a Vapor `<Transition>` — a directly-rendered VDOM child (D) transitions fine, and Vapor children work either way (B, C). The failure is specific to **VDOM content arriving through `<slot>`** (A).

### System Info

```shell
System:  OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200
Binaries: Node 24.18.0, npm 11.16.0
Browsers: Chrome 151, Edge 150
npmPackages: vue: 3.6.0-rc.2 => 3.6.0-rc.2
```

### Any additional comments?

Vapor `<Transition>` shipped in #12962 (merged), so this is a shipped feature rather than unimplemented, and the interop docs list `slots` as covered — so this looks like an uncovered edge of the slot path rather than unsupported usage. I searched open issues and didn't find this exact case (closest, #14192 "Modal with Transitions", was a different mechanism fixed via #14193 in alpha; the slot-boundary case still reproduces on rc.2). Reproduces on a clean, deduped install (unrelated to `@vue/shared` duplication).

problems.title: Vapor: optional chaining is dropped when the same optional member access is cached
problems.issue_body: ### Vue version 3.6.0-rc.2 ### Link to minimal reproduction https://play.vuejs.org/# ### Steps to reproduce Open the reproduction (it is pinned to 3.6.0-rc.2, which is the newest published version carrying Vapor). ```vue ``` ### What is expected? The same thing the VDOM compiler does: the optional chaining survives, so an `undefined` value simply yields `undefined` and nothing throws. VDOM output for the same template: ```js class: _normalizeClass({ x: _unref(maybe)?.id === 'k', y: _unref(maybe)?.id !== 'k' }) ``` ### What is actually happening? Vapor caches the repeated **member access** into a local and drops the `?.` while doing so, so the access becomes unconditional and throws: ``` TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'foo') ``` Compiled Vapor output (from `@vue/compiler-vapor` 3.6.0-rc.2): ```js const _obj = _ctx.obj const _obj_foo = _obj.foo // <-- source said obj?.foo _setClassName(n0, (_obj_foo === 'x' ? 1 : 0) | (_obj_foo !== 'x' ? 2 : 0), [" a", " b"]) ``` ### Additional comments The trigger is the **repetition of the optional access itself**, not `:class` and not props. Compiling four shapes with `@vue/compiler-vapor` 3.6.0-rc.2: | template | output | `?.` | | --- | --- | --- | | `:id="obj?.foo + obj?.bar"` | `const _obj = _ctx.obj` then `_obj?.foo + _obj?.bar` | preserved | | `:id="obj?.foo" :title="obj?.foo"` | `const _obj_foo = _ctx.obj.foo` | **dropped** | | `:id="obj?.foo === 'x' ? 'a' : obj?.foo"` | `const _obj_foo = _obj.foo` | **dropped** | | `:class="{ a: obj?.foo === 'x', b: obj?.foo !== 'x' }"` | `const _obj_foo = _obj.foo` | **dropped** | | `:id="obj?.foo"` (used once) | `_ctx.obj?.foo` | preserved | The first row is the shape #13519 fixed: there the cached value is the **object** (`_obj`), and the `?.` correctly stays on the access. The failing rows cache the **whole access** (`_obj_foo`), and that is where the `?.` is lost. So this looks like the adjacent case that fix did not cover rather than a regression of it. Note the caching is per render function, not per binding: in the two-element case the second element uses `_obj_foo` too, so a binding that reads `obj?.foo` exactly once still breaks when an earlier binding already caused the cache. Why this is easy to ship by accident: the source is correct, so `vue-tsc` and ESLint are…

problems.title: Vapor: class on a component is not normalized, so a declared class: String prop receives an Array
problems.issue_body: ### Vue version 3.6.0-rc.2 ### Link to minimal reproduction https://play.vuejs.org/# ### Steps to reproduce Open the reproduction (pinned to 3.6.0-rc.2). It is two files. `Child.vue` - a component that declares `class` as a prop, which is what a design system does when the root class is part of its public API: ```vue ``` `App.vue` - an ordinary call site with both a static and a dynamic class: ```vue ``` ### What is expected? The declared `class` prop receives a normalized **string**, the way it does under the VDOM renderer, so `class: { type: String }` stays a true declaration. ### What is actually happening? The prop receives the raw array and the runtime prop check fails: ``` [Vue warn]: Invalid prop: type check failed for prop "class". Expected String with value "a,b", got Array at ``` ### Additional comments Compiling the same template both ways with `@vue/compiler-sfc` 3.6.0-rc.2: ```js // vdom class: _normalizeClass(["a", skin]) // vapor _createComponent(Child, { class: () => (["a", skin]) }) ``` Under the VDOM renderer this is normalized regardless of whether the child declares `class` as a prop, because `createBaseVNode` normalizes `props.class` while building the vnode. Vapor has no vnode, so there is no equivalent normalization point and the array reaches the child as-is. The same template is emitted correctly for a plain element - `_setClass(n1, ["a", skin])` handles the array - so only the component-prop path is affected. Two things make this awkward to live with rather than merely noisy: - The declaration was TRUE under VDOM and silently became false at the flip. Nothing in the component or the call site changed; only what the renderer delivers did. - The call site is completely ordinary Vue. `class="a" :class="skin"` is the documented way to combine a static and a dynamic class, so every such site on a component with a declared `class` prop warns. We worked around it by widening the declared type to `ClassValue`, which is what our `cn()` helper already accepts. That is fine for us either way, but I wanted to check whether the array is the intended contract for Vapor or an oversight, since aligning with the VDOM behaviour would keep existing `class: String` declarations valid.

problems.title: [Vapor] compiler: custom directive with an inline object-literal value generates an arrow function with a bare `{ ... }`
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version 3.6.0-rc.2 ### Link to minimal reproduction https://play.vuejs.org/# ### Steps to reproduce A vapor SFC with a custom directive that receives an inline object literal, the way object options are typically passed to directives (e.g. PrimeVue's `v-tooltip="{ value: ..., pt: ... }"`): ```vue ``` Canonical repro of the codegen itself (node, `vue@3.6.0-rc.2`): ```js import { compileTemplate } from 'vue/compiler-sfc' const out = compileTemplate({ id: 'x', filename: 'App.vue', source: `
placeholder
p2
`, vapor: true, compilerOptions: { bindingMetadata: { vDemo: 'setup-const', description: 'setup-const' } }, }) console.log(out.code) ``` emits: ```js export function render(_ctx, $props, $emit, $attrs, $slots) { const n0 = t0() _withVaporDirectives(n0, [[_ctx.vDemo, () => { value: _ctx.description }]]) const n1 = t1() _withVaporDirectives(n1, [[_ctx.vDemo, () => { value: _ctx.description, other: 1 }]]) return [n0, n1] } ``` The directive value expression is wrapped in an arrow function without parenthesizing the object literal. ### What is expected? The getter should return the object: ```js _withVaporDirectives(n0, [[_ctx.vDemo, () => ({ value: _ctx.description })]]) ``` VDOM mode handles the same template correctly. ### What is actually happening? 1. **Single property, non-inline mode — silently wrong.** `() => { value: _ctx.description }` parses as an arrow with a *block body* containing a labeled statement, so the getter returns `undefined`. No compile error, no runtime error — the directive just receives `undefined` instead of the object. 2. **Two or more properties — SyntaxError.** `() => { value: _ctx.description, other: 1 }` is not valid JavaScript. problems.title: [Vapor] compiler: generated template HTML omits the space between quoted attributes (HTML parse error per spec)
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version 3.6.0-rc.2 ### Link to minimal reproduction https://play.vuejs.org/#eNqNkEFLBDEMhf9K6NmZEQUPwygs3rzuHgeWTve5U+y2tUm7K+J/t1YET+LtheR9ecm72sTYlww1qolNslGIITlS0TGkh9kPAz2uMC8kK+hpS6KXsekjPJIWHGgvOEVXJbEk64+0aiYfiKM2aIQFcgZ888k50GsOX0YtdX7JAh7bGNF0sIWM08z3s3p2uHQ+eJDJiUPqVrg4K7HiUNsbI7ZYeaOdPcFZj1nVvNPwfUaVtfhJVqv/wekv+mUaKqIt+QVWV2pfkNgGX79429/1110y/Y36+ATu63rf ### Steps to reproduce Any element with two quoted attributes where the first value contains a space: ```js import { compileTemplate } from 'vue/compiler-sfc' console.log(compileTemplate({ id: 'x', filename: 'A.vue', vapor: true, source: `
x
`, }).code) ``` emits: ```js const t0 = _template("
x", 3) ``` — no space between `"flex-none cursor-help"` and `title`. ### What is expected? Generated template HTML is spec-valid: ```html
x ``` (The compiler presumably drops the separator as size optimization — that is only safe when the preceding attribute value is *unquoted*; after a quoted value a space is required.) ### What is actually happening? The template string is a parse error per the HTML spec ("after attribute value (quoted) state" requires whitespace, `/` or `>`; anything else is a `missing-whitespace-between-attributes` parse error). Spec-compliant browsers *recover* — the error is reconsumed into "before attribute name" — so this happens to work in browsers today, but: - it relies on parser error recovery rather than valid HTML, - it breaks non-browser/strict HTML parsers that consume the generated code (SSR/hydration tooling, test DOM implementations, linters, anything that re-parses `_template` strings), - the equivalent VDOM codegen never produces this, so it is vapor-specific. ### System Info ```shell System: macOS 26.6 (arm64) Binaries: node v26.7.0, pnpm 11.18.0 npmPackages: vue 3.6.0-rc.2, @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.0.8, vite 8.2.1 ``` ### Any additional comments? Minor severity (browsers recover), filing for spec-correctness and non-browser parser compatibility. Attribute values that are unquoted in the output (e.g. `href=/inner`) do keep their following space, so the bug is specifically the quoted-value + following-attribute case.

problems.title: [Vapor] interop: props declared via `extends`/`mixins` resolve to `undefined` on a VDOM child of a vapor parent
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.6.0-rc.2

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

The playground has a vapor parent rendering two identical VDOM children with `v-model`. The only difference between the children is how the `modelValue` prop is declared:

`DirectChild.vue` (props declared directly on the component):

```js
export default {
  props: {
    modelValue: { type: Boolean, default: false },
  },
  emits: ['update:modelValue'],
}
```

`ExtendsChild.vue` (the exact same declaration, but via `extends`):

```js
const base = {
  props: {
    modelValue: { type: Boolean, default: false },
  },
  emits: ['update:modelValue'],
}

export default {
  extends: base,
}
```

Both children render `{{ typeof modelValue }}:{{ String(modelValue) }}`.

Outside the playground the same happens in a Vite app (vue 3.6.0-rc.2, @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.0.8): `createApp(...).use(vaporInteropPlugin)`, vapor parent, VDOM child with `extends`-declared props.

### What is expected?

Both children print `boolean:false`. Props declared through `extends`/`mixins` are part of the component's resolved props options and should behave identically to directly declared props, as they do under a VDOM parent.

### What is actually happening?

- `DirectChild` prints `boolean:false` — correct.
- `ExtendsChild` prints `undefined:undefined` — the prop is `undefined`, and its declared `default` is not applied either.

The same components under a VDOM parent both print `boolean:false`, so it is specific to the vapor→VDOM interop path.

Real-world impact: this silently breaks entire options-API component libraries whose props are declared through a base-component chain. E.g. every PrimeVue component declares props via `extends` (`BaseComponent`/`BaseEditableHolder`), so under a vapor parent a PrimeVue `ToggleSwitch` with `v-model="x"` where `x === false` renders as **checked**: all its props (`modelValue`, `trueValue`, …) are `undefined`, and its internal check `d_value === trueValue` becomes `undefined === undefined`. There is no warning of any kind.

### System Info

```shell
System: macOS 26.6 (arm64)
Binaries: node v26.7.0, pnpm 11.18.0
Browsers: reproduces in Chromium and happy-dom (vitest)
npmPackages: vue 3.6.0-rc.2, @vitejs/plugin-vue 6.0.8, vite 8.2.1

problems.title: Vapor: onUnmounted never fires on app.unmount(), while onBeforeUnmount and onScopeDispose do
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.6.0-rc.2

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

The reproduction mounts two sub-apps side by side from one host component: `VaporChild.vue` is `<script setup vapor>`, `VdomChild.vue` is the same file without the attribute. Each registers `onBeforeUnmount`, `onUnmounted` and `onScopeDispose`, and each pushes into a shared array.

1. Click **"call app.unmount() on both sub-apps"**.

The list under the button shows which hooks ran.

### What is expected?

Both renderers run all three hooks, which is what the vdom sub-app does:

```
vdom:  onBeforeUnmount
vdom:  onUnmounted
vdom:  onScopeDispose
```

### What is actually happening?

The vapor sub-app runs two of the three - `onUnmounted` never fires:

```
vapor: onBeforeUnmount
vapor: onScopeDispose
```

Measured against 3.6.0-rc.2, four cases, `<script setup lang="ts" vapor>` on every vapor fixture:

| teardown path | `onBeforeUnmount` | `onUnmounted` | `onScopeDispose` |
|---|---|---|---|
| vapor, `app.unmount()`, root component | fires | **never** | fires |
| vapor, `app.unmount()`, descendant component | fires | **never** | fires |
| vapor, `v-if` removing a child | fires | fires | fires |
| vdom, `app.unmount()`, root or descendant | fires | fires | fires |

So it is specific to `app.unmount()` under vapor: the same component's `onUnmounted` fires when it is removed by a `v-if`, and its siblings `onBeforeUnmount` and `onScopeDispose` fire on every path.

### Why it matters downstream

`onUnmounted` is where a component releases what it attached to something outside its own tree - a global listener, an observer, a timer, an entry in a shared registry. `app.unmount()` is the teardown path a test harness and an embedded widget use, and it is the one path where that release is skipped. Nothing warns: the app disappears from the DOM and the leak is silent until a later mount reads state the previous instance never cleaned up. problems.title: Vapor: two v-on listeners for the same event on a component are merged into an array and thrown at withModifiers
problems.issue_body:
### Vue version

3.6.0-rc.3

### Link to minimal reproduction

https://play.vuejs.org/#

### Steps to reproduce

Two SFCs, both `<script setup vapor>`. `App.vue` puts **two `v-on` listeners for the same event** on a component and the **identical pair** on a plain element:

```vue
<!-- on a COMPONENT -->
<Child
  @keydown.enter.prevent="hit('component enter')"
  @keydown.esc.prevent="hit('component esc')"
/>

<!-- the identical pair, on a plain ELEMENT -->
<input
  class="on-element"
  @keydown.enter.prevent="hit('element enter')"
  @keydown.esc.prevent="hit('element esc')"
>
```

Both keys are dispatched on mount, so no interaction is needed - open the link.

### What is expected?

`fired: ["component enter", "component esc", "element enter", "element esc"]`, and no error. Each listener handles its own key, on the component exactly as on the element.

### What is actually happening?

```
fired: [ "element enter", "element esc" ]
```

plus `TypeError: fn is not a function`.

The element fires **both** of its listeners. The component fires **neither** - including the one whose key was pressed, so this is not "the extra listener is ignored", it kills the branch that would have matched.

### Why

The compiler merges same-event listeners on a component into an **array** and hands that array to `runtime-dom`'s `withModifiers` / `withKeys`, which take a function. `compileTemplate({ vapor: true })` on the two bindings above shows it directly:

```js
// on the COMPONENT - one binding, an ARRAY, and the two key sets flattened together
_createAssetComponent("Child", {
  onKeydown: () => _withKeys(_withModifiers([_ctx.a, _ctx.b], ["prevent"]), ["enter"])
})

// on the ELEMENT - two separate calls, each with its own key
_on(n1, "keydown", _withKeys(_withModifiers(e => _ctx.a(e), ["prevent"]), ["enter"]))
_on(n1, "keydown", _withKeys(_withModifiers(e => _ctx.b(e), ["prevent"]), ["esc"]))
```

Note the modifiers are already wrong before the call throws: the component's single binding kept only `["enter"]`, so `esc` is gone outright.

Vapor's own `withVaporModifiers` / `withVaporKeys` guard with `typeof fn === "function"`; the `runtime-dom` pair the compiler reaches…

problems.title: Vapor: a declared style prop on a component receives an unmerged array, same bug as #15227 but for style
problems.issue_body: #15230 fixed #15227 ("Vapor: class on a component is not normalized, so a declared `class: String` prop receives an Array") by adding a `normalizeRawProp` guard in `packages/runtime-vapor/src/componentProps.ts`: ```ts const normalizeRawProp = (key: string, value: unknown) => key === 'class' && value && !isString(value) ? normalizeClass(value) : value ``` I checked the compiler side (`packages/compiler-vapor/src/transforms/transformElement.ts`, `dedupeProperties`/`mergePropValues`) and it treats `class` and `style` completely symmetrically: when a component receives both a static and a dynamic binding for either (``), both get merged into a raw array (`["color:red", dynamicObj]`). The runtime side mirrors this symmetry too — `getAttrFromRawProps` in the same `componentProps.ts` file explicitly special-cases `key === 'class' || key === 'style'` together for the fallthrough-attrs merge path (with the comment "need special merging behavior for class & style"). But `normalizeRawProp`, used when a component explicitly *declares* the prop (e.g. `defineProps({ style: Object })`), only unwraps `class` — there's no `key === 'style'` branch, and `normalizeStyle` isn't imported into this resolution path at all. So a declared `style` prop receives the raw unmerged array instead of the merged object/string VDOM would produce via `normalizeStyle` (`packages/runtime-core/src/vnode.ts`, `props.style = normalizeStyle(style)`). ### Reproduction ```vue ``` Expected (matches VDOM): `style` resolves to a merged object/string. Actual in Vapor: `style` is the raw array `["font-weight:bold", { color: "red" }]`.

The code example is written such that it has decent prop stability (i.e. modifying the selected prop only changes the props for the affected items, not all items in the list). To reproduce:

problems.title: Abstract `Assistant` class, in preparation for OpenClaw integration
problems.issue_body:
Move the current `Assistant` to a module - and current existing functionality to `Assistant:Builtin` as per this Claude Code architecture ... summary of the plan:

## Architecture Overview

### Before

`Assistant` was a single monolithic PORO class that handled everything: LLM provider lookup, configuration, function calling, response streaming, and broadcasting.

### After

`Assistant` is now a **module with a registry/factory pattern**:

```
Assistant (module)
  ├── .for_chat(chat)      → routes to the right implementation via Family preference
  ├── .config_for(chat)    → backward compat delegation to Builtin
  ├── .available_types     → ["builtin", "external"]
  │
  ├── Base                 → abstract class with shared Broadcastable concern
  ├── Builtin              → current behavior (zero changes), uses Provided + Configurable
  └── External             → stub for future WebSocket/OpenClaw assistants
```

### Key Design Decisions

1. **Module + Registry** — follows the existing `Provider::Registry` pattern. New assistant types just need a class and a REGISTRY entry.
    
2. **Family-level preference** — `families.assistant_type` column (default `"builtin"`) lets each family choose their assistant. `Chat#assistant` resolves through the factory transparently.
    
3. **Clean interface boundary** — `Base` only requires `for_chat(chat)` and `respond_to(message)`, plus shared `Broadcastable`. External assistants don't need local LLM providers, functions, or the Responder.
    
4. **Zero breaking changes** — all existing callers (`Chat#assistant`, `Assistant.config_for`, `Settings::AiPromptsController`) work unchanged.

problems.title: feat(statements): add account statement vault
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
- Add a web-only Account Statement Vault for uploading, storing, linking, reviewing, and deleting account statements.
- Add account-level statement coverage and balance-based reconciliation flags so users can see which months are backed by actual statements and where Sure's balance history appears mismatched.
- Keep V1 foundation-first: no transaction creation/update/import, no provider statement sync, no AI parsing requirement, and no public API/OpenAPI changes.

## Feature overview
This adds the core Statement Vault domain surface around `AccountStatement`. Users can upload PDF, CSV, or XLSX statement files into a general unmatched inbox, or directly from an account's Statements tab. Sure stores the original file through ActiveStorage, records file metadata and checksums, detects conservative statement metadata where deterministic signals exist, suggests obvious account matches, and lets users manually link, unlink, reject, edit metadata, download, or delete statements.

The account Statements tab shows month-by-month coverage states: covered, missing, duplicate, ambiguous, and mismatched. Reconciliation V1 is intentionally review-oriented: it compares statement opening/closing balances and derived period movement against Sure balance history when enough metadata exists, flags mismatches, and never mutates transactions.

## What changed
- Added `AccountStatement` with family ownership, optional account linkage, suggested account linkage, ActiveStorage original-file attachment, metadata fields, parser confidence, match confidence, review status, sanitized parser output, MD5 checksum, and SHA-256 content digest.
- Added secure upload preparation and validation for `.pdf`, `.csv`, and `.xlsx`, including extension + detected MIME checks, PDF magic-header checks, 25MB file limit, and duplicate detection with DB-level race protection.
- Added deterministic metadata detection for filenames and sampled CSV headers/date rows while avoiding raw statement text or raw transaction rows in stored parser output.
- Added deterministic account suggestions using institution/name/last-four/currency hints, with conservative manual review flows.
- Added Statement Vault inbox UI under settings plus an account Statements tab with upload, coverage timeline, linked statement table, and reconciliation badges.
- Added model/controller/ActiveStorage authorization so statement files remain family-scoped, linked statements follow account sharing, and unmatched statements require statement manager access.
- Added database constraints and indexes for statement ownership, statuses, byte size, checksums, SHA-256 digest format, period lookup, and suggested-account review lookup.

## Related prior work
Related: https://github.com/we-promise/sure/pull/1382

That earlier PR explored LLM-assisted PDF statement processing and reconciliation inside the PDF import flow. This PR does not merge that `PdfImport` job/UI behavior because V1 needs a smaller c…

problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Imported and synced data can leave a family with duplicate categories. Cleaning those up manually is risky because category assignments affect existing transaction history, and there is not a reviewed same-family merge flow that moves assignments and removes the duplicate source category atomically.

## Expected behavior

- A user can start a category merge from settings.
- The merge dialog makes the source and target categories explicit before applying changes.
- Only categories belonging to the current family can be merged.
- Self-merges and missing categories are rejected safely.
- Existing transaction assignments move to the selected target category before the duplicate source category is removed.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add a reviewed category merge flow from the categories settings page.
- Move category assignments and remove the source category inside a transaction.
- Validate missing, same-category, and cross-family targets.
- Cover successful merge and isolation behavior with model/controller tests.

problems.title: Add Kraken read-only crypto exchange provider
problems.issue_body:
## Before you start (required)

### Is this a bug?

No. This is not broken functionality in the current app.

### Is this a bug with _sensitive info_?

No sensitive user data, credentials, screenshots, logs, or account payloads are included here.

### Is this a feature request?

This is a provider implementation tracking issue for an incoming PR, not a request for issue assignment. I checked existing issues, PRs, and discussions before opening this:

- No existing Kraken provider issue or PR showed up.
- The closest related discussion I found is #1454, which references crypto security identifiers including Kraken/XKRA, but it does not track a Kraken provider connection/import implementation.

If maintainers would prefer this to live as a Feature Request discussion instead, I am fine with this issue being closed or moved and linking the PR to that discussion.

### Is this related to Docker and/or hosting for self hosting?

No.

---

## Issue description

Add Kraken as a family-scoped, read-only crypto exchange provider. The provider should support multiple Kraken API-key connections per family and require explicit connection selection when more than one connection exists.

## V1 scope

- Import one combined Crypto exchange account per Kraken connection.
- Sync balances and holdings from Kraken Spot `BalanceEx`.
- Sync spot trade fills from `TradesHistory` with stable external IDs.
- Validate credentials with `GetApiKeyInfo` and prove required read permissions through the private endpoints used by the sync.
- Keep holdings provider-scoped so Kraken imports cannot overwrite Binance, Coinbase, CoinStats, or other provider rows.
- Make the settings flow explicit that users should grant read-only permissions only.

## Out of scope for V1

- Deposits and withdrawals.
- Earn, staking, rewards, transfers, and ledger reconstruction.
- Tax-lot reconstruction beyond importing spot fills as provider entries.
- API-key OTP/2FA flows.
- Trading, cancellation, withdrawal, export, or ledger permissions.

## Implementation notes

- Model the multi-connection selection behavior after existing explicit-selection provider flows.
- Model the imported account shape after existing combined crypto exchange provider accounts.
- Normalize Kraken asset symbols using asset metadata first, with explicit fallbacks for common prefixed symbols such as XBT/XXBT and fiat Z-prefixed assets.
- Preserve Kraken suffix variants such as `.B`, `.F`, and `.T` in metadata instead of silently merging them into the base asset.
- Use increasing signed-request nonces that are safe across jobs/processes.

## References

- Kraken Spot REST auth: https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/guides/spot-rest-auth/
- GetApiKeyInfo: https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/rest-api/get-api-key-info/
- BalanceEx: https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/rest-api/get-extended-balance/
- TradesHistory: https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/rest-api/get-trade-history/
- Spot errors: https://docs.kraken.com/api/docs/guides/spot-errors/

problems.title: Bug: SimpleFIN cost_basis from Vanguard/Fidelity stored as per-share when it's actually total → ~-97% returns
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

After PR #1692 ("Fix avg_cost to return per-share cost basis"), SimpleFIN-imported holdings from brokerages that report `cost_basis` as a **total position cost** (Vanguard, and per #1182 also Fidelity) are stored as if the value were already per-share. Combined with `Holding#calculate_trend` doing `qty × avg_cost`, this produces a "previous" value `qty²` larger than truth and renders a return of roughly `-(1 − 1/qty)` per holding. Aggregated, an investment account ends up showing a near-total loss (~-97% to -99%).

## Reproduction

The exact field shape was already documented in the original Vanguard report — see [@kdknigga's payload in #1182](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/issues/1182):

```json
{
  "shares": "139.00",
  "symbol": "VDE",
  "cost_basis": "22004.40",
  "market_value": "22626.42",
  "purchase_price": "0.00"
}
```

Here `22004.40 / 139 ≈ $158.30/share` — i.e. `cost_basis` is the **total** position cost, not per-share. PR #1261 only addressed the related "value field misused as market_value" symptom; PR #1692 then introduced normalization for `total_cost`/`value` keys but explicitly left `cost_basis`/`basis` as per-share — see [`holdings_processor.rb#L130-L140`](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/blob/main/app/models/simplefin_account/investments/holdings_processor.rb#L130-L140).

## Walkthrough (synthetic numbers)

Hypothetical holding: 100 shares of an ETF, market price $50 (market_value $5,000), real per-share cost $45 (real total cost $4,500).

1. SimpleFIN payload from Vanguard contains `"cost_basis": "4500"` (the *total*).
2. `cost_basis_from` picks the `cost_basis` key.
3. `normalize_cost_basis` returns it unchanged (assumes per-share).
4. DB stores `holdings.cost_basis = 4500`.
5. `Holding#avg_cost` returns `Money.new(4500)`.
6. `Holding#calculate_trend` does `qty × avg_cost = 100 × 4500 = $450,000` as the "previous" value.
7. Trend is `($5,000 − $450,000) / $450,000 ≈ -98.9%`.

## Suggested fix

The `cost_basis`/`basis` keys can't be assumed per-share. Options:

- **Heuristic**: if the raw value is many multiples of the share price *and* `raw / qty` is plausible vs the share price, treat as total. Bounded, no allowlist maintenance.
- **Per-`org_domain` allowlist** for known-total brokerages (Vanguard, Fidelity) — more deterministic but requires plumbing org info through the processor.

## Affected versions

Branches/releases containing PR #1692.
