problems.title: Support resumable Sure NDJSON import sessions for split packages
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Large Sure NDJSON packages can exceed the practical single-upload import path. Splitting the package manually is unsafe because later files can reference accounts, categories, tags, merchants, transactions, and budgets created from earlier files, but the import flow does not preserve source-to-target mappings across separate uploads.

## Expected behavior

- Clients can create a Sure import session for one logical package.
- Ordered chunks can be uploaded and retried without duplicating imported rows.
- Source IDs created by earlier chunks can be referenced safely by later chunks.
- Chunk conflicts fail loudly when the same sequence is retried with different content.
- Existing single-file `POST /api/v1/imports` behavior remains unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add API endpoints for creating, inspecting, uploading to, and publishing an import session.
- Persist per-session chunk state and source-to-target mappings.
- Keep mappings scoped to the current family and import session.
- Make replay/idempotency behavior explicit in tests.
- Document the API contract in the generated OpenAPI output.

Related implementation: #1785

problems.title: Refactor `PdfImport` to build on` AccountStatement` as the canonical statement upload model
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
Follow up on the statement vault work in #1753: consider making `AccountStatement` the single canonical model for uploaded statements, and refactor the existing `PdfImport` statement-extraction flow to build on top of it instead of maintaining a parallel statement-upload path.

## Problem
Right now we have two overlapping concepts for uploaded statements:

- `AccountStatement` in PR #1753 for statement storage, metadata, account matching, coverage, and reconciliation
- `PdfImport` for uploading a statement-like PDF, extracting rows, and turning them into reviewable/importable transactions

This creates duplicated or potentially divergent logic around:

- file storage
- deduplication
- statement metadata
- account association / matching
- review workflows

## Proposed direction
Treat `AccountStatement` as the canonical uploaded-statement record, then layer optional downstream workflows on top of it.

Possible shape:

1. Upload/store a statement once as `AccountStatement`
2. Keep statement metadata, matching, coverage, and reconciliation on that model
3. For supported statement types, run an extraction step from the stored statement
4. Surface extracted rows as a reviewable import draft before publishing transactions

## Goals
- Avoid parallel statement-upload abstractions
- Reuse storage and metadata across vault + import flows
- Make future PDF/CSV/XLSX extraction work hang off a single domain model
- Preserve explicit review-before-import semantics

## Open questions
- Should `PdfImport` become a workflow/state on `AccountStatement`, or should it remain a separate import record that references an `AccountStatement`?
- What parts of the current `PdfImport` behavior should move first (upload, dedupe, metadata, extraction, mappings, publish flow)?
- How should non-statement document uploads continue to differ from statement uploads, if at all?

## Context
This came out of review discussion on #1753, where the current PR intentionally keeps statement vault storage separate from the older AI-assisted `PdfImport` path.

problems.title: Bug: Sure NDJSON publish needs strict preflight validation
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Sure NDJSON publish should validate package integrity before enqueueing or mutating data. Invalid packages can contain unsupported record types, missing required fields, invalid accountable types, duplicate source IDs, duplicate taxonomy names, duplicate valuations, broken split-line totals, or references that are not present in the package. Those failures should be reported before import work starts, not after partial mutation.

## Expected behavior

- Sure NDJSON preflight runs before publish and before background enqueue.
- Invalid packages fail with stable, client-safe API errors.
- Accountable types are resolved through an explicit allowlist.
- Split transactions, transfer decisions, and readback/revert bookkeeping continue to round trip through Sure NDJSON.
- Strict reference validation remains package-scoped unless a separate incremental-import mode is added.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add strict Sure NDJSON preflight validation for publish paths.
- Reject invalid accountable types/subtypes without dynamic constant lookup.
- Validate duplicate IDs, duplicate taxonomy names, duplicate valuations, missing references, and split-line totals.
- Preserve import/export behavior for split lines and transfer decision relationships.
- Keep rswag docs generated from docs-only specs and behavioral coverage in Minitest.

Related implementation: #1833

problems.title: Bug: Financial data reset can leave family-scoped records behind
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The financial data reset path and reset-status endpoint should describe and operate on the same family-scoped data surface. If the reset job only clears a narrow subset of records, family-owned financial, import, reference, provider, or attachment data can remain after reset, and reset status can report completion against a different surface than the destructive job actually deletes.

## Expected behavior

- Reset behavior is centralized in one service with an explicit family-scoped deletion surface.
- Reset status uses the same scope as the reset job.
- Provider cleanup only touches associations that are explicitly safe to reset.
- Reset work is idempotent and does not affect another family.
- API docs describe the reset-status response shape accurately.

## Acceptance criteria

- Replace the inline reset-job deletion list with a reusable family financial reset service.
- Include accounts, entries, transactions, transfers, holdings, balances, rules, budgets, taxonomies, imports, exports, statements, provider items, syncs, and related attachments where applicable.
- Keep destructive queries scoped through the current family or family-owned IDs.
- Update reset-status docs and regression coverage for idempotency and two-family isolation.

Related implementation: #1835

**Describe the bug**
When configuring a custom OpenAI endpoint (e.g., for Gemini or local LLMs) in Settings > General, entering the "Base URL" first causes the input field to aggressively reset/clear itself. The UI throws the error: `OpenAI model is required when custom URI base is configured`.

2. Type or paste a URL into the `Base URL` field.
3. Click away or press tab.

The URL field should retain its inputted string, allowing the user to subsequently fill in the `Model` field. Validation should ideally occur `onSubmit` or without resetting the inputted state `onChange`/`onBlur`.

**Workaround**
The user must manually input the `Model` string *before* pasting the `Base URL` to bypass the reactivity bug.

problems.title: Bug: existing user can lose access to original family/account after upgrade + family sharing flow
problems.issue_body:
## Bug description

A self-hosted user reported that after upgrading from `v0.6.7-alpha` to `v0.7.0-hotfix1`, adding an existing second user account (wife) into a family-sharing setup caused the wife's original account context to disappear and all visible accounts to become the husband's.

The user had **two separate users on the same instance** before the upgrade. After adding the wife's account into the husband's `Family`, the wife's prior data appears to have either:
- been reassigned into the husband's family,
- been orphaned under the previous family, or
- had the original user row destroyed while the historical family/account data may still remain.

There is concern that **~5 months of transactions** may now be inaccessible.

## Likely related history

This appears closely related to the long-standing bug where inviting a user who already belongs to another `Family` can move them into the new family and strand or destroy access to the original one.

Relevant prior work:
- #978 (closed, not merged): "Fix account destruction when user switches families via invitation"
- #1171: Check for pending invitations before creating new Family during SSO log in/sign up
- #1173: Enforce one pending invitation per email across all families
- #1272: Family sharing

During triage, we noticed PR #978 still contained a `@user.destroy` path, which raises the possibility that some flows may still destroy the original user record instead of safely preserving/restoring it.

## Reproduction outline

1. On a self-hosted instance, create user A with Family A.
2. Create user B with Family B.
3. Upgrade from `v0.6.7-alpha` to `v0.7.0-hotfix1`.
4. Add user B into user A's family-sharing setup, expecting B to see both A's and B's accounts.
5. Observe that B instead appears to lose access to B's original family/accounts and now sees only A's accounts.

## Expected behavior

If an existing user who already belongs to another family is added to a sharing/family flow:
- their original family and data should remain accessible,
- the app should not silently reassign or destroy their original account context,
- and any sharing flow should be explicit about whether access is additive vs. rehoming the user.

## Actual behavior

The invited/added user's visible account set becomes the inviter's/husband's family, while the original wife-owned family data becomes inaccessible.

## Recovery angle

In the reported case, recovery may still be possible if the prior `families` row and `accounts.family_id` records still exist and only the `users.family_id` link was changed. We suggested read-only SQL to inspect:
- matching `users` rows by email (including any `+family...` preserved-email variant),
- associated `family_id` values,
- whether the old family still has accounts,
- and related `invitations` rows.

If the old family still exists, recovery may be as simple as reassigning the correct user row back to the original `family_id`, but we should confirm whether the destructive path is …

problems.title: perf: N+1 syncing? queries on AccountsController#index
problems.issue_body:
**Sentry**: SURE-APP-2E (694 events, last seen today), SURE-APP-YA (129 events, 8 users, last seen today)

`AccountsController#index` fires one SQL query per account to check syncing status — 104 queries per page load for a large family. Two root causes:

**1. `Syncable#syncing?` bypasses preloaded syncs**

```ruby
def syncing?
  syncs.visible.any?  # fires SQL even when syncs are loaded in memory
end
```

`syncs.visible` creates a new scoped relation, ignoring any preloaded collection. Called once per account in `_account_groups.erb` (`accounts.any?(&:syncing?)`) and once per account in `_account.html.erb`.

**2. `item.family.accounts.listable_manual.exists?` per SimpleFIN item**

`build_sync_stats_maps` calls this inside the simplefin items loop. The answer is identical for all items (same family), so it fires N redundant queries.

**Fix**:
- Add `:syncs` to `@manual_accounts` includes and the view-level Preloader
- Change `syncing?` to check the loaded collection in-memory when available
- Compute `family.accounts.listable_manual.exists?` once before the SimpleFIN loop

  - [ ] Render
  - [x] Docker Compose
  - [ ] Umbrel
  - [ ] PikaPod
  - [ ] Other (please specify)

---

## Bug description

`IdentifyRecurringTransactionsJob#family_has_incomplete_syncs?` (`app/jobs/identify_recurring_transactions_job.rb:45-60`) is the debounce gate that delays `RecurringTransaction::Identifier` until the family's in-flight provider syncs have settled. The gate hand-rolls the list of provider `*_items` associations it polls, and the list is incomplete: it only checks `plaid_items`, `simplefin_items`, `lunchflow_items`, `enable_banking_items`, and `sophtron_items`. Nine other provider integrations that are also `Syncable` and have a `has_many :*_items` declaration on `Family` are silently missing from the gate: `coinbase_items`, `binance_items`, `kraken_items`, `coinstats_items`, `snaptrade_items`, `mercury_items`, `brex_items`, `indexa_capital_items`, `ibkr_items`.

When a sync on one of these nine providers is still in flight, the gate falls through, `RecurringTransaction::Identifier` runs against a partial dataset, and any recurring pattern that needs ≥ 3 occurrences silently misses the in-flight batch. When the late-arriving sync finishes it (correctly) re-schedules the job, but the previous run has already written a `RecurringTransaction` row with a stale `occurrence_count` / `last_occurrence_date`; the second run hits the `find_or_initialize_by` upsert path and the counts written reflect only the in-window entries seen at that moment, not the full set.

The maintainers' own `Sync.for_family` helper (`app/models/sync.rb:61-75`) already enumerates every `*_items` association via `Family.reflect_on_all_associations(:has_many)` filtered by inclusion of the `Syncable` module — that is exactly the helper this gate should delegate to so the list cannot drift again. The same drift pattern has already happened once: the file has had a single edit since creation (Apr 19, 2026, when Sophtron was bolted on as the 5th entry of the now-out-of-date hand-rolled list).

### Bypass / drift surface (current code)

```ruby
# app/jobs/identify_recurring_transactions_job.rb:45-60
def family_has_incomplete_syncs?(family)
  # Check family's own syncs
  return true if family.syncs.incomplete.exists?

  # Check all provider items' syncs
  return true if fami…

Additional currency cash positions aren't imported However, the account's "Current account value" will have the correct value. Example: A moomoo Canada account with $500 CAD and $1000 USD in cash only imports the $500 CAD. The USD cash is discarded entirely. ### To Reproduce Be as specific as possible so Sure contributors can quickly reproduce the bug you're experiencing. Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Observe in the Holdings tab only the primary currency's cash balance (CAD in my case) is imported. Other positions (in both currencies) are imported correctly. ### Expected behavior USD and CAD cash balances are imported under holdings ### Screenshots and/or recordings ------ ### From Dosu / Claude Code: Root cause: `SnaptradeAccount#upsert_balances!` selects a single cash entry from the SnapTrade balance response using a priority fallback (account currency → USD → first entry) and stores it in the single `cash_balance` field. Affected file: `app/models/snaptrade_account.rb` (lines 129-147) Related: #898 (multi-currency holdings) ------ I was able to "band-aid patch" this by storing the other currency as "synthetic cash holdings" here https://github.com/Badbird5907/sure/pull/1

problems.title: Bug: Surface actionable Plaid configuration/product-access errors in the UI
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

When Plaid fails during the link flow because the configured account is not enabled for the requested products, Sure currently logs the provider error but does not surface a useful explanation to the user in the UI.

In practice, the user clicks **Link with Plaid**, the modal closes, and nothing actionable appears. The real cause is only visible in logs, for example:

```json
"error_message": "Your account is not enabled for the following products: [\"investments\" \"liabilities\" \"transactions\"]. To request access, visit https://dashboard.plaid.com/overview/request-products or contact Sales or your Account Manager."
```

## Problem

This creates a bad failure mode for self-hosted users:
- the Plaid flow appears broken or silent
- the user cannot distinguish UI bugs from provider configuration problems
- maintainers have to diagnose from logs instead of the app giving an actionable error

## Expected behavior

If Plaid returns a known, user-actionable configuration or product-access error, Sure should surface that message (or a sanitized version of it) directly in the UI near the Plaid linking flow.

## Suggested course of action

### 1. Catch and classify Plaid provider errors
- Identify where Plaid link / token / exchange failures are rescued today
- Preserve structured Plaid error fields when available (`error_type`, `error_code`, `error_message`)
- Introduce a small mapper for known Plaid errors that are safe to show to users

### 2. Surface a user-facing error in the Plaid flow
- Show an inline flash/alert/toast when Plaid setup fails
- Include specific guidance for product-access failures, e.g.:
  - your Plaid account is not enabled for required products
  - request access in the Plaid dashboard
  - verify the app is using the expected Plaid environment/account

### 3. Keep raw errors out of the UI unless safe
- Avoid dumping arbitrary provider payloads directly to end users
- Prefer a sanitized message plus optional technical details in logs

### 4. Improve observability
- Log structured Plaid failure metadata with request/context IDs
- Consider storing the last sync/link error on the provider/item record for admin visibility

## Possible implementation direction

A reasonable first pass would be:
- rescue provider errors at the controller/service boundary for Plaid setup/linking
- map known product-access/configuration errors to a friendly message
- return/render that message in the account linking UI instead of failing silently

## Why this matters

This should reduce support/debug churn substantially because the current behavior makes a configuration problem look like a broken button or modal.

problems.issue_body:

---

## Bug description

`Family#tax_advantaged_account_ids` in `app/models/family.rb:243-263` is the ID set that the budget engine uses to **exclude** tax-advantaged account activity from income / expense / cashflow totals. PR #724 (`Exclude tax-advantaged account activity from budget & add provider data quality...`) originated this method and explicitly listed HSA as an in-scope account type ("401k, IRA, HSA, Roth IRA, etc."). The implementation correctly handles `Investment` (via `Investment::SUBTYPES`'s `tax_treatment` metadata) and `Crypto` (via the dedicated `tax_treatment` enum), but silently omits `Depository` — including the `Depository(subtype: "hsa")` variant.

Two facts make this matter in production:

- `Depository::SUBTYPES` at `app/models/depository.rb:9` already includes `"hsa" => { short: "HSA", long: "Health Savings Account" }`, so HSA depositories are constructable from the UI and from data importers today.
- `app/models/plaid_account/type_mappable.rb:35` routes Plaid-reported `depository.hsa` accounts to `Depository` (not `Investment`). A "Fidelity HSA cash" or similar Plaid-linked HSA cash account ends up as a `Depository`, not an `Investment`, which means it never enters the `tax_advantaged_account_ids` filter even though it semantically is one.

`Account#tax_advantaged?` (in the `TaxTreatable` concern) calls `accountable.respond_to?(:tax_treatment)` and reads the value if present. `Investment` and `Crypto` both implement `tax_treatment`; `Depository` does not, so `account.tax_advantaged?` returns `false` for every HSA depository in the system. This propagates symmetrically into `IncomeStatement::Totals`, `FamilyStats`, `CategoryStats`, and `Transaction::Search` — every analytics path that PR #724 was designed to suppress tax-advantaged activity from. HSA contributions and withdrawals show up in monthly expense totals, contaminating the household's actual non-tax-advantaged spending picture.

The fix is symmetric to the existing branches: surface `tax_treatment` on `Depository`, drive it from a class-level subtype list (so future expansion happens in one place), and join `depositories` in `Family#tax_advantaged_account_ids` alongside t…

problems.title: Categories settings index performs repeated category and transaction existence queries
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The categories settings page currently does repeated database work while rendering the category list. Sentry is grouping this under `CategoriesController#index` as an N+1 query issue: each rendered category can trigger its own subcategory lookup and its own transaction-existence check.

## Observed behavior

When a family has a larger category tree, rendering the index can repeatedly execute queries shaped like:

- look up subcategories for each parent category
- check whether each category has any transactions before choosing the delete flow

That makes the page cost grow with the number of categories instead of doing a small, bounded set of queries for the page.

## Expected behavior

The controller should prepare the data needed by the list once, scoped to the current family, and the view should render from that precomputed data without per-row database checks.

## Notes

This is a performance issue, not a data correctness issue. The fix should preserve the existing category hierarchy rendering and delete-menu behavior while avoiding the per-category query pattern.

Skylight reports slow and inconsistent response times for `CategoriesController#index` (HTML), with repeated SQL like:

```sql
SELECT 1 AS one FROM "categories" WHERE "categories"."parent_id" = ? LIMIT 1
```

and per-category transaction existence checks while rendering `categories/_category.html.erb`.

## Problem

The categories settings page renders one partial per category. When locals are missing or associations are checked in the view, each row can trigger:

- An EXISTS query for subcategories (`parent_id`)
- An EXISTS query for transactions (`category_id`)

This scales with the number of categories and shows up in Skylight as a repeated-query warning.

## Proposed solution

- [ ] Batch transaction lookups in one query (e.g. `Category.ids_with_transactions`)
- [ ] Pass explicit locals into `_category` (`subcategories`, `has_transactions`) and remove DB fallbacks from the partial
- [ ] Use `parent_id.present?` in the row partial instead of loading `parent` / `subcategories` associations
- [ ] Keep `Category::Group.for` for in-memory parent/child grouping

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CategoriesController#index` does not run per-category `categories.parent_id` or `transactions.category_id` existence queries
- [ ] Categories list UI unchanged: edit/delete behavior correct for categories with and without transactions
- [ ] Regression test(s) cover index query count or assert absence of N+1 patterns
- [ ] Skylight trace for `CategoriesController#index` no longer flags repeated `SELECT … FROM categories WHERE parent_id = ?`

## Context

- Skylight endpoint: `CategoriesController#index | html`
- Branch: `perf/categories-controller-index`
- Related PR: _(add link after opening PR)_

## Labels

`performance`, `bug`, `enhancement`

problems.title: Reduce query work on the new transaction form
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
Sentry has been pointing at slow requests on the new transaction form. The render path currently leaves several option lookups in the view layer, which makes the form more expensive to open for families with larger account/category/merchant/tag sets.

## Why it matters
Opening the add-transaction dialog should be bounded and predictable. Users should not pay repeated query work just to render the form options.

## Suggested scope
- Load the new-transaction form option data once from the controller.
- Keep account selection and account-currency metadata scoped to accounts the current user can access.
- Pass preloaded categories, merchants, tags, manual accounts, and account currencies into the form partial.
- Preserve transaction creation behavior and the failed-create render path.
- Add regression coverage for the rendered form and query shape.

problems.title: Reduce duplicate investment flow aggregate queries on reports index
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
Sentry has been pointing at slow database work around the reports index. One small source is InvestmentFlowStatement#period_totals, which builds the same filtered scope and then runs separate aggregate queries for contribution and withdrawal totals.

## Why it matters
The reports index is already doing several calculations, so duplicate aggregate queries add avoidable latency on a page that should stay responsive.

## Suggested scope
- Compute contribution and withdrawal totals in one aggregate query.
- Preserve existing family/user visibility and account-finance scoping.
- Preserve the current ABS(SUM(amount)) semantics so correction/reversal rows do not change totals.
- Add regression coverage for the single-query path and offsetting entry behavior.
- Keep the change limited to investment-flow totals rather than broad reports refactoring.

problems.title: Reduce sensitive data in mobile diagnostic logs
problems.issue_body:
## Summary
Mobile diagnostic logs are useful for support and debugging, but some current log paths can include raw authentication responses, user payload details, transaction names, amounts, merchant labels, account identifiers, backend URLs, or custom proxy header details.

## Why
These logs can be viewed in-app, printed during development, and exported from the log viewer. They should stay operationally useful without carrying credentials or personal financial data.

## Scope
- Redact sensitive values before mobile logs are stored, printed, or exported.
- Replace clearly risky log messages with flow, status, count, and outcome diagnostics.
- Keep the existing LogService and log viewer behavior intact.
- Avoid adding telemetry, Sentry, or a new logging framework in this change.

problems.title: Add privacy-safe Flutter Sentry crash and performance instrumentation
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

The Flutter mobile client currently has useful local diagnostic logging, but it does not have an opt-in client observability path for native crashes, handled startup/auth/sync failures, or basic performance spans.

After the diagnostic log privacy baseline in #2199, the mobile app can safely add Sentry instrumentation behind configuration so maintainers can see mobile crash and performance signals without collecting financial details or raw support logs.

## Current behavior

- Mobile crash and handled-exception visibility depends mostly on local/device logs.
- Auth, SSO/deep-link, sync replay, transaction fetch, and local database failures are hard to correlate across releases.
- There is no configured no-op path for client Sentry builds, so enabling telemetry would require app code changes instead of build-time configuration.

## Desired behavior

- Keep telemetry disabled by default when no mobile Sentry DSN is provided.
- Allow mobile builds to opt in with compile-time configuration.
- Capture low-cardinality breadcrumbs/spans for app startup, backend configuration, auth/SSO, sync replay/fetch, and local database failures.
- Avoid sending emails, backend URLs, auth headers, custom proxy headers, transaction names, amounts, merchant names, account IDs, request/response bodies, local support logs, or SQLite query details.

## Acceptance criteria

- App startup behaves the same with no Sentry DSN configured.
- Sentry options disable PII, screenshots, request bodies, and response bodies.
- Event, transaction, breadcrumb, request, tag, user, and extra data are filtered before send.
- Tests cover no-DSN startup and privacy filtering for sensitive telemetry payloads.
- Flutter analyzer and mobile tests pass.

## Related

- Builds on the diagnostic privacy baseline in #2199.

problems.title: Bug: ActiveRecord::InvalidForeignKey when deleting a withdrawal/deposit trade — rejected_transfers not cascade-deleted
problems.issue_body:
**Describe the bug**
When a manually created withdrawal (or deposit) trade is proposed as a transfer match by Sure's auto-matching logic and the user rejects that match, Sure records the rejection in the rejected_transfers table. If the user subsequently tries to delete the original trade from the UI, the deletion fails silently for the user and raises an ActiveRecord::InvalidForeignKey exception in the server logs, because the rejected_transfers rows still reference the transaction and the foreign key has no ON DELETE CASCADE.

**Steps to reproduce**
Manually create a withdrawal (or deposit) trade on an investment account via the UI
Sure's transfer auto-matching logic runs and proposes matches between the new transaction and existing transactions in other accounts
The user rejects those proposed matches
Sure records the rejections in the rejected_transfers table, referencing the withdrawal as outflow_transaction_id
Attempt to delete the original withdrawal trade from the UI
Deletion fails with the FK violation above

**Root cause**
When a user rejects a proposed transfer match, Sure creates rows in rejected_transfers to remember not to propose that match again. These rows hold a foreign key reference to the original transaction. When the user later tries to delete that transaction, the rejected_transfers rows block deletion because the foreign key has no ON DELETE CASCADE. The deletion controller makes no attempt to clean them up first.

**Workaround**
Manually delete the blocking rejected_transfers rows before deleting the transaction:
sqlDELETE FROM rejected_transfers 
WHERE outflow_transaction_id = '<transaction_id>';
-- or inflow_transaction_id if applicable

**Expected behaviour**
Deleting a trade should cascade-delete any associated rejected_transfers rows, or the BulkDeletionsController should clean them up before deleting the transaction.
Fix suggestion
Add ON DELETE CASCADE to the fk_rails_2da6f89959 foreign key constraint on rejected_transfers, or add explicit cleanup in the deletion logic.

problems.title: Limit transfer auto-matching work after account sync
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

Account sync currently asks the family transfer matcher to scan eligible transfer candidates across the family after each account refresh. On larger families, this can repeat unrelated transfer matching work for accounts that were not touched by the current sync.

There is also a query/index mismatch risk if excluded entries are indexed out of the lookup path but the matching query does not explicitly filter them out.

## Expected behavior

- Post-sync transfer matching should only consider candidate pairs that touch the account that was just synced.
- Manual or family-wide transfer matching should remain available for full-family repair flows.
- Excluded entries should not participate in transfer candidate matching.
- Query predicates and supporting indexes should stay aligned so the database can use the intended lookup path.

## Acceptance criteria

- Account sync passes the synced account into transfer auto-matching.
- Transfer candidate SQL can scope to pairs involving that account without broadening family access.
- Excluded inflow and outflow entries are filtered out explicitly.
- Regression tests cover account-scoped matching, preserved family-wide matching, and excluded-entry behavior.

problems.title: Show richer account context in the mobile transaction list
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The Flutter account transaction screen currently has much less account context than the web/API surfaces. Users can open an account and review its transactions, but the screen does not show nearby account detail such as status, subtype, institution context, recent balance movement, cash balance, or investment holdings where the existing API already exposes that data.

That makes the mobile account screen feel disconnected from the richer account surfaces available elsewhere in Sure.

## Expected behavior

- The mobile transaction list for an account should include a compact account-detail header.
- The header should use existing API endpoints rather than requiring new backend endpoints.
- Recent balance history should be shown where available.
- Investment and crypto accounts should be able to show a small top-holdings summary where available.
- Auth expiry and malformed/failed API responses should fail cleanly without exposing internal errors to users.

## Acceptance criteria

- Mobile account detail, balance history, and holdings are loaded through existing authenticated API calls.
- Account IDs are encoded safely when used in API paths.
- Unauthorized responses log the user out consistently with existing mobile behavior.
- Malformed API payloads return generic mobile errors instead of crashing.
- Tests cover account detail, scoped balances, scoped holdings, auth expiry, encoded account IDs, and malformed payload handling.

problems.title: Make mobile offline transaction replay idempotent
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The Flutter app can queue locally-created transactions while offline and replay them when connectivity returns. If a create request succeeds on the server but the client loses the response or fails before recording the synced state, a later replay can submit the same locally-created transaction again.

That creates a duplicate-risk path for offline mobile transaction entry.

## Expected behavior

- Mobile-created offline transactions should replay with stable idempotency metadata.
- Regular online transaction creates should keep their existing request shape.
- Partial idempotency metadata should be omitted rather than sending only one half of a key.

## Acceptance criteria

- Offline replay sends a stable `source` and `external_id` pair derived from the local pending transaction.
- The create payload includes idempotency metadata only when both values are present and non-empty.
- Regular creates omit the idempotency fields.
- Regression tests cover idempotent replay payloads, normal create payloads, empty values, and partial-key omission.

problems.title: Add Flutter theme foundation from Sure design tokens
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Add the first Flutter design-system foundation layer by deriving mobile theme values from Sure's canonical design tokens.

## Problem

The Flutter app currently defines light and dark `ThemeData` inline in `mobile/lib/main.dart` using a Material seed color. That makes the mobile app easy to drift away from the web app's design-system tokens, especially as the design system continues to evolve around `design/tokens/sure.tokens.json`.

## Proposed scope

- Add a small generator that reads `design/tokens/sure.tokens.json`.
- Generate typed Flutter token constants under `mobile/lib/theme/`.
- Add a shared `SureTheme` for light and dark `ThemeData`.
- Replace the duplicated inline `ThemeData` blocks in `mobile/lib/main.dart`.
- Add focused tests for token generation and theme wiring.

## Out of scope

- No full screen restyle.
- No screenshot/mockup CSS copied into Dart.
- No native font asset registration until mobile-ready font assets are available.
- No redesign of navigation, forms, cards, dashboard, settings, or transaction screens in this issue.

## Validation target

- Generator check proves generated tokens are current.
- Flutter analyze/test pass.
- iOS simulator debug build passes.
- Follow-up visible screen work can use the same token/theme foundation instead of inventing mobile-only palettes.

problems.title: Remove N+1 queries from recurring transaction identification
Reports page still performs residual category lookups
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Sentry is still reporting residual `ReportsController#index` N+1 query spans for category lookups on the reports page. The repeated SQL shape is:

```sql
SELECT "categories".* FROM "categories" WHERE "categories"."id" = $1 LIMIT $2
```

This appears in reports traces after the investment-flow aggregate work, so it looks like a separate residual category-loading path rather than the same issue.

## Current behavior

The reports page can still trigger per-category lazy loads while building report totals:

- `Category#subcategory?` checks `parent.present?`, which loads the parent category when only `parent_id` is needed.
- `Budget#sync_budget_categories` creates missing budget categories from `category_id`, which can cause belongs-to validation to load each category row individually.

Those paths become visible when reports render families with several categories/subcategories and budget category sync work happens during report setup.

## Expected behavior

`ReportsController#index` should not need one category lookup per category row while building totals. The model paths should use already-known foreign keys or loaded family category records where possible.

## Suggested fix

- Make `Category#subcategory?` use `parent_id.present?`.
- Build missing budget categories from a loaded family category map rather than passing only `category_id`.
- Add regression coverage around `reports_path(period_type: :monthly)` that captures SQL and asserts the Sentry-shaped category lookup is not emitted.

## Validation target

A fix should include a bounded-query regression test for the reports page and pass the existing reports/category/budget model tests.

problems.title: Improve dashboard investment totals query performance
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Recent dashboard performance traces show `PagesController#dashboard` spending most of its time rendering the investment summary. In the slow samples I checked, the dashboard request took a little over 2s, the dashboard view render took about 1.9s, and the largest database span was the investment activity totals query at roughly 1.17-1.20s.

## Root cause

The dashboard investment summary calls `InvestmentStatement#totals`, which currently builds a `family.trades.joins(:entry)` relation and passes that relation into `InvestmentStatement::Totals`.

`InvestmentStatement::Totals` then wraps that relation as a subquery and joins `entries` again to calculate contributions and withdrawals. For all-time dashboard periods, that creates a heavier nested query than the report needs.

The query still needs to preserve:

- family scoping
- active/draft investment account status
- `included_in_finances_for(user)` account visibility
- excluded-entry filtering
- existing 1:1 missing-FX fallback behavior

## Proposed fix

Rework the investment totals aggregate so it starts from scoped trade entries directly instead of wrapping a pre-joined trades relation and joining entries a second time.

Add a matching partial index for trade-entry activity lookups, and add regression coverage that proves the dashboard totals use one direct aggregate query while excluding unshared accounts for a shared user.

## Acceptance criteria

- Dashboard investment activity totals aggregate directly from `entries JOIN trades`.
- The query keeps family, account visibility, active/draft status, date range, and excluded-entry guards.
- A partial index supports the trade-entry lookup shape.
- Regression coverage proves both the totals and the query shape.

problems.title: Bug: Actual Budget CSV import fails entirely when a row has a blank payee
problems.issue_body:
## Before you start (required)

### General checklist

- [x] I have removed personal / sensitive data from screenshots and logs
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/issues?q=is:issue) and [discussions](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/discussions) to ensure this is not a duplicate issue

### How are you using Sure?

- [x] I am a self-hosted user (local only)

### Self hoster checklist

- Self hosted app commit SHA: reproducible on current `main` (`f25fe30a4`) and on every version since `ActualImport` was introduced in #1830.
  - [x] I have confirmed that my app's commit is the latest version of Sure
- Where are you hosting?
  - [x] Docker Compose

---

## Bug description

Importing an **Actual Budget** transaction CSV fails with a generic "Import failed" when the file contains a row with a **blank Payee**. Actual exports such rows for reconciliation balance adjustments and starting balances, e.g.:

```csv
Account,Date,Payee,Notes,Category_Group,Category,Amount,Split_Amount,Cleared
account1,2026-05-14,,Reconciliation balance adjustment,Income,Income,0.43,0,Reconciled
```

A single blank-payee row aborts the **entire** import (not just that row). The UI shows only:

> Import failed
> Please check that your file format, for any errors and that all required fields are filled, then come back and try again.

…and the worker log shows the job completing normally (`ImportJob ... done`) with no error, which makes it hard to diagnose. Selecting only rows that have a payee imports successfully, which is how the blank payee was identified as the trigger.

### Root cause

`ActualImport#generate_rows_from_csv` maps the row name directly from the Payee column with no fallback:

```ruby
# app/models/actual_import.rb
name: row[name_col_label].to_s,   # "Payee" → "" when blank
```

This differs from the base importer and `MintImport`, which both fall back to `default_row_name`:

- `app/models/import.rb`: `name: (csv_value(row, name_col_label, "name") || default_row_name).to_s`
- `app/models/mint_import.rb`: `name: (row[name_col_label] || default_row_name).to_s`

`Entry` requires a name (`app/models/entry.rb`: `validates :date, :name, :amount, :currency, presence: true`). Because `ActualImport#import!` wraps all rows in a single `transaction do ... entry.save! ... end`, the blank name raises `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid` and rolls back every row. `Import#publish` rescues the error and stores it on `import.error` while marking the import `failed`, so the Sidekiq job exits cleanly and logs `done`.

The preflight ("clean your data") step does not catch this because `ActualImport#required_column_keys` is only `%i[date amount]`, so a blank-payee row is considered valid at preflight but still fails at `entry.save!`.

### To Reproduce

1. Go to **Import** → **Financial Tools** → **Import from Actual Budget**.
2. Paste/upload an Actual CSV that includes at least one row with an empty `Payee` (e.g. a reconciliation balance adjustment …

problems.title: Upgrade Rails 7.2 → 8.1
problems.issue_body:
### Summary

Rails **7.2 reaches end of life on 2026-08-09**. The application should move to the
current **8.1.x** line before then. This issue tracks upgrading the framework and
fully landing on Rails 8.1: bumping the gem, adopting the 8.1 framework defaults,
and the small application/config adjustments the upgrade requires.

### Why now

- Rails 7.2 EOL (2026-08-09) means no further security/bug fixes after that date;
  brakeman's `CheckEOLRails` already flags it on every branch.
- Ruby 3.4.7 already satisfies Rails 8's `>= 3.2` requirement.
- Assets are Propshaft + importmap (no Sprockets migration) and jobs run on
  Sidekiq, so the upgrade is a contained dependency bump rather than a stack change.

### Scope

1. **Framework gem → Rails 8.1** (`Gemfile` `rails "~> 8.1.0"`, `bundle update
   rails`). This carries the Rails 8 framework gems plus the bumps they require
   (notably ViewComponent 3.x → 4.x for Rails 8 support, rails-i18n 7 → 8).
2. **Application/test adjustments the bump requires:**
   - `Transfer#date` nil-safety — Rails 8's `date_field` evaluates the default on a
     new/unpersisted `Transfer`.
   - `StyledFormBuilder` — Rails 8 renamed `field_helpers` (`:text_area`→`:textarea`,
     `:check_box`→`:checkbox`), which dropped styling on `form.text_area`.
   - Make the property edit-modal system test deterministic against a Turbo morph
     refresh.
3. **Adopt Rails 8.1 framework defaults** (`config.load_defaults 8.1`). Rails 8.0
   introduced no new framework defaults, so 7.2 → 8.1 is the single meaningful step.
4. **Restore brakeman's `CheckEOLRails`** by removing the temporary skip added for
   the 7.2 EOL window.

### Acceptance

- Full unit/integration and system suites green on Rails 8.1 with `load_defaults
  8.1`.
- `bin/rubocop`, `bin/brakeman` (EOL checks restored), and `zeitwerk:check` clean.
- ViewComponent 4 previews verified in Lookbook (`/design-system`).

problems.title: Standardize mobile money typography and semantic amount color
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Second implementation step under the mobile design-system coordination issue #2235
(after the theme foundation in #2237): **standardize how the Flutter app renders
monetary values** — consistent money typography (tabular figures) and semantic
amount color sourced from the Sure design-system tokens, instead of raw
`Colors.green` / `Colors.red` / `Colors.grey`.

## Scope

- Add a brightness-aware `SureColors` `ThemeExtension` so widgets resolve the active
  light/dark Sure palette (`success` / `destructive` / `textSubdued`).
- Add a reusable `MoneyText` / `SureMoney` primitive: directional semantic color via a
  `MoneyTrend`, plus tabular figures for column-aligned digits.
- Migrate the money surfaces to the primitive: recent transactions, account transaction
  list, net-worth card, account cards.

Primitive-first: no layout changes, just tokenized color + typography. Broader screen
redesign remains later steps of #2235.

## Acceptance

- Reusable `SureColors` extension + `MoneyText`/`SureMoney` primitive with tests.
- Migrated screens render via the primitive (no raw `Colors.green/red/grey` for amounts).
- `flutter analyze` clean, `flutter test` green, `flutter build ios --simulator --debug` builds.
- Before/after iOS-simulator screenshots (light + dark).

Part of #2235.

problems.title: Introduce SureIcon (Lucide) and migrate the dashboard off Material icons
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Part of the mobile design-system sequence (#2235), continuing the off-Material facelift. The Flutter app draws every glyph with Material `Icons.*`, which don't match Sure's design system — the web uses **Lucide** via the `icon` helper / `DS::FilledIcon`. This introduces a `SureIcon` primitive and migrates the dashboard surface onto it.

It's self-contained and **adds no dependency** — `flutter_svg` is already in the project.

## Scope

- **`SureIcon` primitive** — renders bundled Lucide SVGs (2px stroke, `currentColor`) via `flutter_svg`, mirroring the web `icon` helper: tokenized size (`SureIconSize` xs–2xl = 12–32), color inherited from the ambient `IconTheme` by default (Material-icon parity), and accessibility that distinguishes decorative icons (excluded from the semantics tree) from meaningful ones (`semanticLabel`). A `SureIcons` registry keeps call sites typo-safe and limited to bundled assets.
- **Migrate the dashboard surface** off Material `Icons.*` — `net_worth_card`, `account_card`, `dashboard_screen` — onto `SureIcon` (account-type glyphs, asset/liability trend icons, sync/empty/error states, refresh, collapsible section headers, expand chevrons).
- **Bundle** the Lucide SVGs the surface needs under `assets/icons/lucide/` with the SIL/ISC license.
- Out of scope (own later slices): the bottom navigation bar (`SureBottomNav`), and the remaining screens (settings, login, transactions, chat) — the rest of the ~95-icon long tail.

## Why

Mobile should render the same Lucide iconography as the web/PWA design system. A single `SureIcon` primitive (tokenized size/color + a11y) replaces ad-hoc Material icons and gives later screens a drop-in path off Material.

## Acceptance

- Lucide icons render on device (before/after screenshots, light + dark).
- `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` clean (no new issues), `flutter test` green, and `flutter build ios --simulator --debug` + `flutter build apk --debug` pass with the SVGs bundled.

Part of #2235.

problems.title: Extend the mobile token generator with the shadow scale + focus-ring/bg-inverse
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Part of the mobile design-system sequence (#2235) — the remaining Phase‑0 foundation item. The mobile token generator (`mobile/tool/generate_sure_tokens.mjs`) emits font families, radii (`md`/`lg`), and the color palette, but not the canonical **shadow scale** or the **focus-ring** / **bg-inverse** colors. Primitives like `SureCard` need a token-driven elevation rather than hardcoded shadows, so this extends the generator to emit them from `design/tokens/sure.tokens.json`.

Codegen + tokens only — no visible UI change in this PR.

## Scope

- Emit a **mode-aware box-shadow scale** `shadowXs..shadowXl` (from `shadow.xs..xl`) as `List<BoxShadow>` on `SureTokenPalette` (light/dark differ — `black 6%` vs `white 8%`).
- Emit **`focusRing`** (`color.focus-ring`) and **`bgInverse`** (`utility.bg-inverse`) colors.
- Regenerate `mobile/lib/theme/sure_tokens.dart`; keep the `--check` parity gate; add token tests for the new values.
- Out of scope (intentional): **radii** (the source only defines `md`/`lg` — already generated), a **type-scale** (not present in the token source), and the **shadow-border** composites (derivable in-widget as a shadow + a 1px border from existing border tokens).

## Why

Token-driven elevation + focus keeps mobile in lockstep with the canonical tokens and unblocks `SureCard` / elevated surfaces without hardcoding shadow values.

## Acceptance

- Generator emits the new tokens; `node mobile/tool/generate_sure_tokens.mjs --check` parity passes.
- `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` clean (no new issues), `flutter test` green, and `flutter build ios --simulator --debug` + `flutter build apk --debug` pass.

Part of #2235.

problems.title: SyncJob silently discarded after Rails 8.1 upgrade (enqueue_after_transaction_commit race)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Two latent regressions introduced by the alpha.6 Rails 7.2 → 8.1 upgrade share a single root cause: ActiveJob's `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` default changed from "defer until the transaction commits" to "enqueue immediately". Any job enqueued inside a DB transaction can now be dequeued by a Sidekiq worker before `COMMIT`, on a separate connection that cannot see the uncommitted rows. This manifests as (1) silently discarded `SyncJob`s / stuck syncs, and (2) leaked SnapTrade brokerage connections on disconnect.

## Shared root cause

`enqueue_after_transaction_commit` controls whether a `perform_later` issued inside an Active Record transaction is deferred until that transaction commits.

- Rails 7.2: `config.load_defaults 7.2` set `config.active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = :default`, and the Sidekiq adapter (`AbstractAdapter#enqueue_after_transaction_commit?`) returned `true`, so in-transaction enqueues were deferred until commit. The race was covered by the default.
- Rails 8.0: the `:always`/`:never`/`:default` enum was collapsed to a boolean `class_attribute` defaulting to `false` (`activejob/lib/active_job/enqueuing.rb`), and the global config toggle was deprecated.
- Rails 8.1 (current): the global `config.active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit` toggle is non-functional — the Active Job railtie explicitly excludes the key from global application ("This config can't be applied globally"). Only the per-class `class_attribute` is honored, and it defaults to `false` (enqueue immediately). `raw_enqueue` defers via `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit` only when the attribute is truthy (`active_job/enqueue_after_transaction_commit.rb`).
- Rails 8.2: the default flips back to `true`; the Active Job changelog states the reason directly — "jobs would surprisingly run against uncommitted and rolled-back records."

## Bug 1 — `SyncJob` silently discarded (stuck syncs)

`Syncable#sync_later` (`app/models/concerns/syncable.rb:18`) opens `Sync.transaction` (`:19`), creates a `Sync` row, and calls `SyncJob.perform_later(sync)` (`:38`) inside that transaction. The job carries only a GlobalID reference to the not-yet-committed `Sync`.

Under the 8.1 default the enqueue is immediate, so a Sidekiq worker on another connection can dequeue before `COMMIT`, fail to resolve the `Sync` GlobalID, and raise `ActiveJob::DeserializationError`. `ApplicationJob` declares `discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError`, so the job is dropped without a trace — which is why the symptom is a silently stuck / never-completing sync rather than a visible error.

Reported in Discord by Alessio (the `SyncJob` discard with `ActiveJob::DeserializationError`) and Murphy (a stuck Enable Banking sync).

## Bug 2 — SnapTrade / Indexa connection-cleanup leak

`SnaptradeAccount` declares `after_destroy :enqueue_connection_cleanup` (`app/models/snaptrade_account.rb:24`), which enqueues `SnaptradeConnectionCleanupJob.perform_later(...)` (`:196`) from i…

problems.title: Add a SureButton design-system primitive (off Material)
problems.issue_body:
## Summary

Part of the mobile design-system sequence (#2235) — the first Phase-1 primitive. The app draws CTAs with Material `ElevatedButton`/`OutlinedButton`/`TextButton`, which carry Material styling (ripple, accent-colored outline/text foregrounds) rather than the Sure design system. Introduce a custom `SureButton` mirroring the web `DS::Button`, off Material.

This is **independent** of the in-review foundation PRs — it uses only tokens already on `main`.

## Scope

- **`SureButton` primitive** mirroring `DS::Button` / `DS::Buttonish`: variants (`primary`, `secondary`, `destructive`, `outline`, `ghost`), sizes (`sm`/`md`/`lg` ≈ 28/36/48), optional leading widget, `fullWidth`, `loading`, and disabled. Colors resolve from the `SureColors` palette; the shape from `radiusMd`/`radiusLg` tokens; flat custom press feedback (no Material ripple).
- **Migrate the 3 main-view login buttons** as the showcase: Sign In (primary, lg, loading), Sign in with Google (outline + SVG leading), API-Key Login (ghost).
- Out of scope (follow-ups): the 2 buttons inside the API-key **modal dialog**, and the remaining button call sites across settings / transactions / chat / etc.

## Why

One consistent, off-Material button matching the web DS — neutral (not Material-accent) outline/ghost foregrounds, tokenized colors, DS shape — and the foundational primitive that dialogs, forms, empty states, and CTAs all build on.

## Acceptance

- `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` clean (no new issues), `flutter test` green, and `flutter build ios --simulator --debug` + `flutter build apk --debug` pass.
- Before/after login screenshots (light + dark) show the migration.

Part of #2235.

problems.title: Mobile: Material colorScheme maps primary to link-blue, so primary surfaces render off-brand
problems.issue_body:
### Problem

The mobile theme (`SureTheme._build`) maps Flutter's Material `colorScheme.primary` to the **`link`** token (blue `#1570EF` / `#2E90FA`) and leaves the primary/secondary *container* roles unset. Material uses those roles for FABs, unread badges, avatar circles, and selection — so any screen not yet redesigned with `SureColors` (e.g. the **Chats** list) renders those surfaces in link-blue / Material defaults instead of Sure's neutral brand.

Sure's primary *action* color is `buttonPrimary` (near-black in light, white in dark — mirroring the web DS primary button); `link` is for hyperlinks. The Material role mapping should reflect that.

Separately, the mobile `logomark.svg` hardcodes `fill="grey"` for the wordmark's muted strokes, which is too dim to read on the dark surface.

### Notes

Surfaced on the Chats screen. Pre-existing — introduced with the theme foundation (#2237), not a specific recent PR. Part of the mobile design-system alignment (#2235).

problems.title: design-system(mobile): SureCard primitive (tokenized card surface)
problems.issue_body:
Part of the mobile design-system sequence (#2235). Now that the foundation (tokens, typography, iconography, shadow scale) and `SureButton` have landed, the next primitive is the **card surface**.

Card chrome — `bg-container` + a hairline border + rounded corners + the subtle DS shadow — is currently duplicated across the mobile app via Material `Card` and ad-hoc `BoxDecoration`s (account rows, dashboard, etc.), so it drifts from the web design system and the `sure.tokens.json` source of truth.

**Scope:** add a `SureCard` primitive that resolves its chrome from the active `SureColors` palette (brightness-aware) using the shadow scale shipped in #2349, with an optional tappable mode. Migrate `AccountCard` off the Material `Card` as proof. Tests + before/after screenshots.

`SureListGroup` / `SureListRow` (grouped inset lists) will follow as a separate PR, building on `SureCard`.

problems.title: design-system(mobile): SureListGroup / SureListRow primitives (grouped inset lists)
problems.issue_body:
Part of the mobile design-system sequence (#2235), following `SureCard` (#2369). With the card surface landed, the next primitives are the **grouped inset list** and its **rows**.

Grouped-list chrome — a rounded `bg-container` surface with a hairline border, the subtle DS shadow, and inset dividers between rows — is currently hand-rolled across the mobile app via raw Material `ListTile` + `Divider` on `colorScheme.*` defaults (the More menu, settings, etc.), so it drifts from the web design system (`DS::*` grouped lists) and the `sure.tokens.json` source of truth.

**Scope:** add `SureListGroup` (tokenized grouped container: `bg-container` + `borderSecondary` hairline + `radiusLg` corners + `shadowXs`, with clipped inset dividers and an optional section header) and `SureListRow` (leading / title / subtitle / trailing slots, a DS chevron disclosure affordance, and a destructive variant), both resolving from the active `SureColors` palette so they're brightness-aware and stay in lockstep with `sure.tokens.json`. Migrate the More menu off raw `ListTile` / `Divider` as proof. Tests + before/after screenshots.

problems.title: design-system(mobile): SureTextField primitive (tokenized form field)
problems.issue_body:
Part of the mobile design-system sequence (#2235), continuing the form-control primitives after `SureButton`. The next control is the **text field**.

Form-field chrome — a labeled, filled `bg-container` input with a hairline border, rounded corners, a `textSubdued` placeholder, a stronger border on focus, and the destructive token for errors — is currently hand-rolled across the app: ~18 `TextField`/`TextFormField` call sites lean on Material's `labelText` + default decoration, so labels float inside the border and placeholder/error styling drifts from the web DS (`styled_form_builder` / `form-field`) and `sure.tokens.json`.

**Scope:** add a `SureTextField` primitive that builds a complete, brightness-aware `InputDecoration` from the active `SureColors` palette (filled container, `borderSecondary` hairline → `borderPrimary` on focus, `destructive` error border, `textSubdued` placeholder, `radiusLg` corners) with a DS-style label rendered above the field and associated to it for screen readers (Material `labelText` parity). Migrate the custom proxy-headers editor off raw `TextFormField` as proof. Tests + before/after screenshots.

Filter chips and a segmented control will follow as separate PRs to complete the form-control set.

problems.title: design-system(mobile): SureChip primitive (tokenized filter chip)
problems.issue_body:
Part of the mobile design-system sequence (#2235), continuing the form-control primitives after `SureTextField` (#2377). The next control is the **filter chip**.

Filter chips today use Material `FilterChip` on `colorScheme.*` (e.g. `category_filter` / `currency_filter`): a `primaryContainer` selected tint + a checkmark + a `primary` (blue) border that drift from the web DS pill and `sure.tokens.json`.

**Scope:** add a `SureChip` primitive — a tokenized selectable pill resolving from the active `SureColors` palette (bordered/transparent when unselected, filled neutral `buttonPrimary` + inverse label when selected), with `selected` button semantics and a comfortable min tap target. Migrate the currency filter off Material `FilterChip` as proof. Tests + before/after screenshots.

The segmented control will follow as a separate PR to complete the form-control set.

problems.title: design-system(mobile): SureSegmentedControl primitive (tokenized segmented control)
problems.issue_body:
Part of the mobile design-system sequence (#2235), completing the form-control primitives after `SureChip` (#2379). The last control is the **segmented control**.

Segmented selectors today use Material `SegmentedButton` (e.g. the transaction Type, settings theme, calendar view): the M3 outlined-stadium look with a `secondaryContainer` selection + checkmark, which drifts from the web DS `segmented-control` and `sure.tokens.json`.

**Scope:** add a `SureSegmentedControl<T>` primitive — an inset track holding equal-width segments where the selected segment is a raised surface (container fill + the subtle DS shadow) and unselected segments are flat `textSecondary` labels — resolving from the active `SureColors` palette (brightness-aware), with per-segment button/selected semantics and keyboard/switch focus. Migrate the transaction-form Type selector off Material `SegmentedButton` as proof. Tests + before/after screenshots.

This completes the mobile form-control primitive set (text field, chip, segmented control).

problems.title: feat(mobile): migrate the Flutter app to gen_l10n i18n (full ARB migration)
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The Flutter mobile app shipped ~330 hardcoded English strings with no localisation infrastructure. Nothing could be translated, and there was no `gen_l10n` pipeline to migrate strings into.

## Solution

Stand up the `gen_l10n` + ARB pipeline and migrate **every** user-facing string in the app onto it, so the app can be translated into any language without touching Dart source.

### Foundation
- `flutter_localizations` SDK dep + `generate: true` in `pubspec.yaml`; `intl: any` so `flutter_localizations` selects the SDK-pinned version across all supported Flutter floors.
- `l10n.yaml` pointing gen_l10n at `lib/l10n/app_en.arb`; generated `AppLocalizations` wired into `MaterialApp` (`onGenerateTitle` + `localizationsDelegates` + `supportedLocales`).

### Full string migration
- Migrate all user-facing strings across the 21 screens/widgets (titles, buttons, labels, hints, helper texts, tooltips, validators, dialogs, snackbars, empty states).
- ICU plurals for counts (pending-sync, multi-delete, relative time); parameterised keys for interpolated copy (greeting, version, amount, names).
- Locale-aware **display** dates (calendar, chat list, recent transactions) and localized weekday labels; internal `yyyy-MM-dd` map keys left fixed.
- `AppLocalizations` captured before async gaps and re-obtained inside dialog builders; `const` adjusted only where a localisation getter is introduced.

## Acceptance
- Zero hardcoded user-facing strings remain (grep-verified).
- `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` — 0 errors (only pre-existing infos in untouched files).
- `flutter test` — 116/116 pass.
- ARB has no unused keys.

## Out of scope (tracked separately)
- Shipping a second locale / actual translations.
- Provider error-code enum refactor (stringly-typed server errors → typed, localisable enum).

Implemented by #2384.

problems.title: feat(mobile): privacy mode to mask money values
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

The Flutter app always renders monetary amounts in the clear — net worth, account balances, and transaction amounts. There's no quick way to hide them from over-the-shoulder view (on a train, in a meeting, sharing a screen). Most finance apps offer a one-tap "hide balances" mode.

## Solution

Add an app-wide privacy mode that masks every money value, persisted across launches.

- A `PrivacyProvider` (ChangeNotifier) backed by the existing `PreferencesService`, so the choice survives relaunch and every money widget rebuilds instantly on toggle.
- A `MoneyMasker` util that replaces each digit with a bullet while preserving the currency symbol, separators, and sign — masked values keep their shape (e.g. `CA$1,234.56` → `CA$•,•••.••`). Currency- and locale-agnostic, since it operates on already-formatted strings.
- Masking applied at every money render site: net worth + per-currency totals + breakdown sheet, account balances, and transaction amounts (list, recent, calendar).
- Two entry points: a **Hide amounts** switch in Settings → Security, and a quick **eye toggle** in the top bar (visible on every tab).

## Acceptance

- Toggle hides/shows all amounts app-wide and persists across launches.
- Non-amount text (account names, labels, the `--` empty placeholder) is unaffected.
- Unit tests for the masker + a widget test asserting masking flips with the provider.
- `flutter analyze` introduces no new issues; full suite green.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- Tap-to-reveal a single masked value.
- Auto-hide on app background / biometric-gated reveal.

problems.title: fix(mobile): API-key dialog controller leaks on barrier/back dismissal
problems.issue_body:
## Problem

In `mobile/lib/screens/login_screen.dart`, `_showApiKeyDialog()` creates a `TextEditingController` but only disposes it inside the **Cancel** and **Sign-In** button handlers. If the dialog is dismissed any other way — tapping outside the barrier, or the Android system back button — neither handler runs and the controller is leaked.

## Fix

Make `_showApiKeyDialog` async, `await showDialog(...)`, and dispose the controller once after it returns, so disposal happens regardless of how the dialog closes. Remove the two in-handler `dispose()` calls to avoid double disposal.

## Acceptance

- Controller is disposed on every dismissal path (button, barrier tap, system back).
- No double-disposal.
- `flutter analyze` — no new issues; `flutter test` — green.

problems.title: design-system(mobile): SureFontWeights tokens (named weight tiers)

The web design system expresses these as **named** Tailwind utilities (`font-medium`, `font-semibold`), so a named token is more faithful and keeps weight choices centralized as the design-system migration continues.

Weight-only; other screens adopt the tokens in their own polish PRs.

## Acceptance
